title: [Whisper] Enable CUDA graph support and timestamp for whisper model
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

Previously, Whisper used a custom `bmm + mask` cross-attention implementation with a Python-side `_encoder_cache` dict, which was incompatible with CUDA graph capture/replay. This PR enables CUDA graph for Whisper, achieving **36% throughput improvement** with **identical accuracy**.

Related: #21161

## Modifications

- **Cross-attention → RadixAttention**: Replaced manual BMM cross-attention with native `RadixAttention` path. During prefill, encoder KV is projected and saved to the KV pool; during decode, `k=None, v=None` triggers cached KV read from the pool.
- **Removed `_encoder_cache` dict**: Encoder outputs now flow through the native encoder-decoder cache managed by scheduler/attention backends.
- **Auto-select flashinfer backend**: Encoder-decoder models require `flashinfer` for cross-attention support (trtllm_mha/fa3 lack `encoder_out_cache_loc` handling).
- **Auto-disable radix cache**: Encoder token padding conflicts with prefix caching, causing `assert len(req.prefix_indices) == 0` failures.
- **Fixed CUDA graph capture**: Set `encoder_len_fill_value` to `max_source_positions` (1500 for Whisper) so cross-attention kernels are included in the captured graph. Previously was 0, causing cross-attention to be skipped during capture.
- **Fixed FlashInfer decode cross-attention planning**: `update_cross_attention` was passing decoder `seq_lens_cpu` for cross-attention wrapper, causing `global_override_indptr_cpu` to override KV length from 1500 to ~5. Now correctly uses `encoder_lens` for cross-attention.
- **Position embedding OOB protection**: Clamp `position_ids` to `max_target_positions - 1` to prevent warmup from exceeding the 448-entry position embedding table.
- **Added `encoder_out_cache_loc` to trtllm_mha backend**: For forward compatibility.

## Accuracy Tests

```bash
# launch server (no manual flags needed - auto-configured)
sglang serve --model-path openai/whisper-large-v3

# benchmark
python benchmark/asr/bench_sglang.py \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:30000 \
    --model openai/whisper-large-v3 \
    --api-type transcription \
    --language en \
    --concurrency 1
```

| Config | WER | Avg Latency | Throughput |
|--------|-----|-------------|------------|
| **CUDA graph (ours)** | **12.77%** | **0.297s** | **3.26 req/s** |
| No CUDA graph (baseline) | 12.77% | 0.406s | 2.40 req/s |

WER is identical between CUDA graph and non-CUDA-graph modes (12.7690% on earnings22 dataset, 511 samples).

## Benchmarking

| Metric | No CUDA Graph | CUDA Graph | Improvement |
|--------|---------------|------------|-------------|
| WER | 12.77% | 12.77% | identical |
| Avg Latency | 0.406s | 0.297s | **-27%** |
| Median Latency | 0.376s | 0.267s | **-29%** |
| P95 Latency | 0.837s | 0.601s | **-28%** |
| Throughput | 2.40 req/s | 3.26 req/s | **+36%** |
| Token Throughput | 44.71 tok/s | 60.72 tok/s | **+36%** |

Dataset: `D4nt3/esb-datasets-earnings22-validation-tiny-filtered` (511 samples), concurrency=1, model=`openai/whisper-large-v3`.

title: [Perf] Optimize CUDA IPC for multimodal transfer by caching IPC pool handles
author: saatwiknagpal
body:
## Motivation

When CUDA IPC transport is enabled for multimodal models (`SGLANG_USE_CUDA_IPC_TRANSPORT=1`), every scheduler iteration re-opens IPC handles for the same long-lived memory pool via `torch.UntypedStorage._new_shared_cuda()`. While the underlying `cuIpcOpenMemHandle` driver call does reference-count repeated opens, the PyTorch wrapper (`_new_shared_cuda`) adds significant per-call overhead from storage object creation, event management, and Python-level bookkeeping ([pytorch/pytorch#161481](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/161481)). Since the pool is allocated once at startup, these repeated calls are redundant.

This overhead is on the scheduler's critical path (`mm_loop`) and blocks both prefill and decode iterations for all in-flight requests.

## Modifications

- Pre-compute the pool's IPC handle once at `MmItemMemoryPool` init instead of per-slice
- Add a process-global `_pool_storage_cache` dict that caches the opened `UntypedStorage` per pool handle (thread-safe via double-checked locking)
- On cache miss or stale entry: invalidate and retry uncached
- Pass pool handle + byte offset through `CudaIpcTensorTransportProxy` so the consumer can slice into the cached pool storage directly
- Gate behind `SGLANG_USE_IPC_POOL_HANDLE_CACHE` env var (default: disabled)

## Benchmarking

**Setup:** Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct, 1×H100, 16 tokenizer workers, mixed-chunk ON, CUDA IPC transport ON

**Reproduce:**
```bash
# Set SGLANG_USE_IPC_POOL_HANDLE_CACHE=1 or 0 before launching
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct \
  --enable-multimodal --enable-mixed-chunk \
  --tokenizer-worker-num 16 \
  --max-running-requests 128 --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000

python -m sglang.bench_serving \
  --backend sglang-oai-chat --port 30000 \
  --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct \
  --dataset-name image --num-prompts 3000 \
  --image-count 1 --image-resolution 360p \
  --random-input-len 128 --random-output-len 32 \
  --max-concurrency 50 --seed 2710
```

**Results (median of 10 runs per configuration):**

| Metric | Cache OFF | Cache ON | Improvement |
|--------|----------|---------|-------------|
| Request throughput | 22.2 req/s | 25.7 req/s | **+16.2%** |
| TTFT mean (p50 / p99) | 965 ms (1020 / 2058) | 838 ms (930 / 1819) | **-13.2%** |
| TPOT mean | 72 ms | 60 ms | **-17.2%** |
| ITL mean (p99) | 67 ms (627) | 56 ms (556) | **-16.2%** |
| E2E latency mean (p50 / p90 / p99) | 1979 ms (1901 / 3329 / 4309) | 1768 ms (1720 / 2831 / 3666) | **-10.6%** |
| Errors | 2-3 / 3000 | 2-3 / 3000 | Similar |

Throughput improves by ~16% and latency drops 10-17% across all percentiles. TPOT and ITL also improve because `mm_loop` is on the scheduler's critical path — a slower `mm_loop` delays decode iterations for all in-flight requests, not just the prefilling one.

## Correctness

Output comparison on 3000 requests with identical inputs (`--seed 2710`):
- 52% of outputs are byte-identical between cache ON and OFF
- Remaining differences are due to non-deterministic batch scheduling at c=50
- Output length distributions are identical (mean=63, median=59 chars)
- No corrupted or garbled outputs

The optimization only changes how the scheduler opens the pool's GPU memory mapping — the same feature tensors reach the scheduler in both configurations.

## Tests

`test/registered/utils/test_cuda_ipc_transport_utils.py`:

- **Cache reuse**: two proxies from the same pool trigger only one `_new_shared_cuda()` call
- **Stale entry recovery**: poisoned cache entry is invalidated and retried uncached
- **Cross-pool isolation**: separate pools maintain independent cache entries; poisoning one doesn't affect the other

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with [pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit)
- [x] Add unit tests
- [x] Benchmark results (10 runs per configuration, median reported)
- [x] Correctness verified

title: [Diffusion] Add qknorm rope fuse kernel
author: BBuf
body: ## Summary Made with Codex and this skills: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/tree/main/python/sglang/multimodal_gen/.claude/skills/sglang-diffusion-ako4all-kernel ```prompt $Radixark03 SGLang $SGLang AKO4ALL Kernel $Sglang Diffusion Benchmark Profile 帮我在sglang diffusion里面基于AKO4ALL框架继续优化diffusion kernel，运行任何模型和benchmark之前都需要保证使用的gpu是完全空闲的。现在需要你帮我优化diffusion模型里面的一个常见pattern，qk norm+rope fuse，你可以看看diffusion models实现，里面已经有大量这种pattern，只不过目前是分别调用了jit_kernel的qk norm和flashinfer的rope实现，并没有实现fuse的效果，现在我需要你帮我在jit_kernel里面实现这个fuse kernel。 ``` This PR adds a new JIT CUDA kernel that fuses QK RMSNorm and RoPE into a single in-place kernel for diffusion models. It also wires the fused path into the main diffusion DiT implementations that already use the QK norm + RoPE pattern, while keeping the existing split path as a fallback. ## What Changed - Added a new fused JIT kernel for QK RMSNorm + RoPE: - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/elementwise/qknorm_rope.cuh` - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/qknorm_rope.py` - Added a shared runtime helper: - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/layernorm.py` - `apply_qk_norm_rope(...)` uses the fused kernel when the shape/dtype/layout is supported, and falls back to split QK norm + FlashInfer RoPE otherwise. - Integrated the fused path into diffusion model implementations: - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/qwen_image.py` - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux.py` - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/flux_2.py` - `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/zimage.py` - Added correctness coverage and a dedicated micro benchmark: - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_qknorm_rope.py` - `python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_qknorm_rope.py` ## Key Optimization Points - Fuse QK RMSNorm and RoPE into a single kernel to remove an extra read/write pass over Q and K. - Keep the operation fully in-place on supported CUDA paths. - Reuse a shared runtime entry point so model code does not need model-specific kernel handling. - Add segmented position offset support so the fused path also works for FLUX / FLUX.2 dual-stream attention blocks, where text and image tokens use different RoPE position ranges. - Keep a safe fallback to the existing split implementation for unsupported cases. ## Fused QKNorm+RoPE Kernel Design The new kernel fuses Q/K RMSNorm and RoPE into a single warp-level in-place CUDA kernel. Implementation highlights: - Each warp processes one `(token, head)` work item. - Input values and RMSNorm weights are loaded with vectorized packed loads. - RMSNorm is computed fully within a warp using warp-level reduction, without shared memory. - The normalized values stay in registers and are immediately consumed by RoPE. - RoPE is applied in-register: - pairwise rotation for the standard layout - `__shfl_xor_sync`-based lane exchange for the Neox layout - Results are packed back and written in place. Key optimizations: - Eliminates the extra global memory round trip between split QKNorm and RoPE. - Merges Q and K processing into one kernel launch. - Uses vectorized loads/stores to reduce memory instructions. - Uses fp32 accumulation for RMSNorm for numerical stability. - Uses occupancy-aware launch sizing and JIT specialization on `head_dim`, `rope_dim`, `is_neox`, and `dtype`. This PR also adds `position_offset` support in the shared runtime helper so the fused path can be used for segmented RoPE ranges in FLUX / FLUX.2 dual-stream attention blocks. ## Micro Benchmark All numbers below compare the split path (`jit qknorm + flashinfer rope`) vs the new fused JIT kernel. Shape notation: - `q/k shape = [B*T, H, D]` - `rope_dim` is the applied rotary dimension | Case | Shape | Split (ms) | Fused (ms) | Speedup | | :--- | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `flux_1024` | `B=1, T=4096, H=24, D=128, rope_dim=128` | 0.059520 | 0.043072 | 1.3819x | | `qwen_image_1024` | `B=1, T=4096, H=32, D=128, rope_dim=128` | 0.081152 | 0.055008 | 1.4753x | | `qwen_image_partial` | `B=1, T=4096, H=32, D=128, rope_dim=64` | 0.079680 | 0.054560 | 1.4604x | | `zimage_1024` | `B=1, T=4096, H=30, D=128, rope_dim=128` | 0.074112 | 0.051008 | 1.4529x | | `batch2_medium` | `B=2, T=2048, H=24, D=128, rope_dim=128` | 0.059488 | 0.043232 | 1.3760x | Weighted micro benchmark speedup: `1.4387x` ## End-to-End Denoise Stage | Model | Split Denoise (s) | Fused Denoise (s) | Delta | Speedup | | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | `qwen` | 14.43 | 12.36 | -14.35% | 1.1675x | | `qwen-edit` | 28.62 | 28.26 | -1.26% | 1.0127x | | `flux` | 6.495 | 6.421 | -1.14% | 1.0116x | | `flux2` | 22.314 | 22.311 | -0.01% | 1.0001x | | `zimage` | 0.723 | 0.712 | -1.47% | 1.0149x | Commands used for the end-to-end denoise benchmark: ```bash # title: [AMD] Enable FP8 KV cache and FP8 attention kernel for NSA on MI300/MI355 with TileLang backend
author: 1am9trash
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Enable FP8 KV cache and FP8 attention kernel for NSA on MI300/MI355 with TileLang backend.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- Upgraded TileLang to [a55a823](https://github.com/tile-ai/tilelang/commit/a55a82302bf7f3c5af635b5c9146f728185cc900) to enable FP8 gemm support on AMD GPUs.
- Added an FP8 attention kernel, `sparse_mla_fwd_decode_partial_fp8`, while reusing the existing reduce kernel.
- Fused quantization path:
  - On MI355, reused `fused_qk_rope_cat_and_cache_mla` for both Q and KV quantization.
  - On MI300, added a Triton kernel, `set_mla_kv_buffer_fp8_quant`, for KV cache quantization.

To enable this feature, set `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3` in the server launch command:
DSV32 server cmd:
```
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --tp 8 \
  --port 9000 --trust-remote-code \
  --nsa-prefill-backend tilelang --nsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --disable-radix-cache --mem-fraction-static 0.85 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```
GLM5 server cmd:
```
export SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0 
export ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4 
export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1 
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path GLM-5-FP8 \
  --tp 8 \
  --port 9000 --trust-remote-code \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' \
  --nsa-prefill-backend tilelang --nsa-decode-backend tilelang \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

No accuracy regression (gsm8k) is observed for either DSV32 or GLM5.

| GLM5  | 0.946 | 0.950 |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

On MI300, throughput improves by more than 10%, while on MI355, throughput improves by more than 5%.
The gain becomes larger at higher concurrency levels.

Benchmark cmd:

```
  --model DeepSeek-V3.2 \
  --dataset-name random --random-input 8192 --random-output 1024 --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
```

title: [Feature] Add FP4 KV Cache Design and support SM120 GPUs
author: samuellees
body:
- [x] Roadmap: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/29913
- [x] Rebased from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/18314

 ## Summary
  Add NVFP4 (FP4 E2M1) KV cache quantization support for SM120 GPUs, reducing KV cache memory by ~2x compared to FP8 with no accuracy loss on GSM8K/GPQA/LongBenchV2-128k.

  ### Usage

  ```bash
# server
  python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
      --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8 \
      --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4 \
      --prefill-attention-backend flashinfer \
      --decode-attention-backend trtllm_mha \
      --disable-radix-cache \
      --port 8005

# client gsm8k
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 8001 --eval-name gsm8k \
--num-examples 1319 --max-tokens 10240 --repeat 1 \
--num-threads 1319 --num-shots 8 --temperature 0.6 \
--top-p 0.95 --top-k 20

# client gpqa
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval \
    --base-url http://127.0.0.1:8005 \
    --eval-name gpqa \
    --num-examples 198 \
    --max-tokens 81920 \
    --repeat 2 \
    --temperature 0.6 \
    --top-p 0.95 \
    --top-k 20
```

### Accuracy
Qwen3.5-35B NVFP4 KV Cache shows no accuracy drop across different dataset
| Benchmark                | BF16 KV | FP8 E4M3 KV | NVFP4 KV |
|--------------------------|---------|-------------|----------|
| GSM8K 1319        | 97.10%  | 96.95%      | 97.18%   |
| GPQA 8 round avg         | 82.26%  | 83.08%      | 83.33%   |
| LongBench V2 128K subset | 52.03%  | Not measured   | 52.70%   |

LLaMA-3.1-8B NVFP4 KV Cache
| Benchmark                | FP8 E4M3 KV | NVFP4 KV |
|--------------------------|-------------|----------|
| GSM8K 1319        | 64.6%      | 63.85%   |


### Throughput
|                          | FP8 KV Cache | NVFP4 KV Cache | Speedup (NVFP4 vs FP8) |
|--------------------------|--------------|----------------|------------------------|
| Prefill Latency (160K)   | 8757 ms      | 8792 ms        | 0.996x                 |
| Prefill Latency (1M)     | 142143 ms    | 142325 ms      | 0.998x                 |
| Decode Latency (1M)      | 8.4 ms       | 7.1 ms         | 1.18x                  |

## Reviewer Guide
Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`

### Minimal pseudocode

```python
# Pass nvfp4 kv cli parameters
quant_method = resolve_kv_cache_quant(server_args.kv_cache_dtype)
quant_method.load_scales_from_model(model)
token_to_kv_pool = MHATokenToKVPool(..., quant_method=quant_method)

# KV quant and write 
token_to_kv_pool.set_kv_buffer(layer, loc, k, v, k_scale=None, v_scale=None)

# FlashInfer extend/prefill
#   for prefix cache, dequant fp4 kv into fp8 kv
#   for current input, use bf16-> fp8 kv.
dq_k, dq_v = token_to_kv_pool.prepare_fp8_extend_workspace(layer_id, ...)
flashinfer_prefill(kv_cache=(dq_k, dq_v), kv_cache_dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)

# TRT-LLM MHA decode
#   attention kernel use fp4 kv directly
raw_kv, block_scales = token_to_kv_pool.get_raw_fp4_kv_buffer(layer_id)
k_scale, v_scale = quant_method.get_bmm_scales(layer_id)
trtllm_batch_decode_with_kv_cache(
    kv_cache=raw_kv,
    kv_cache_sf=block_scales,
    bmm1_scale=q_scale * k_scale * layer.scaling,
    bmm2_scale=v_scale,
    out_dtype=model_runner.dtype,
)
```

### Data/Module Flow

```text
CLI / ServerArgs
  --kv-cache-dtype nvfp4
        |
        v
model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py
  resolve_kv_cache_quant("nvfp4")
  load_scales_from_model(model weights)
        |
        v
fp4_kv_cache_quant_method.py
  NVFP4KVCacheMethod
    - owns per-layer global scales
    - keeps GPU tensor scales for quant/dequant
    - keeps Python float scales for TRT-LLM BMM args
    - applies the SM100 scale bridge inside the recipe
        |
        v
memory_pool.py / pool_configurator.py
  MHATokenToKVPool(quant_method=NVFP4KVCacheMethod)
    - packed FP4 K/V buffers
    - per-block FP8 scale buffers
    - FP8 extend/prefill workspace
    - slot movement for data and scales
        |
        +-----------------------------+
        |                             |
        v                             v
flashinfer_backend.py            trtllm_mha_backend.py
  extend/prefill                  decode only
    - build page metadata           - view raw FP4 cache for XQA
    - dequant prefix to FP8         - pass kv_cache_sf block scales
    - copy current chunk FP8        - pass BMM scales from quant method
    - run FlashInfer FP8 prefill    - output dtype follows model dtype
```

title: [Feature] DCP: A2A + FlashInfer-MNNVL comm backends and q-replicate (Helix)
author: thanhhao98
body:
## Summary

Adds pluggable communication backends and q-replicate (Helix) to the DeepSeek-MLA
**decode context-parallel (DCP)** path, on top of the merged DCP base (#14194):

```
--dcp-comm-backend {ag_rs, a2a, fi_a2a}    --dcp-replicate-q-proj
```

## What's added

- **`a2a`** (NCCL All-to-All): exchanges packed *(attention output + fp32 LSE)* in a
  **single collective per layer**, then a one-shot Triton LSE combine (base-2). Adds a
  CUDA-graph-capturable `pynccl.all_to_all_single`. **fp8 KV** supported via uint8
  byte-transport (NCCL has no fp8 dtype).
- **`fi_a2a`** (FlashInfer MNNVL, flashinfer#2951): delegates only the cross-rank
  exchange to the MNNVL `decode_cp_a2a_alltoall` kernel (GB200), reusing the same Triton
  combine; hardware-gated to MNNVL fabric.
- **q-replicate / Helix** (`--dcp-replicate-q-proj`): each DCP rank projects the
  full-head Q locally (weights gathered once pre-capture) and **skips the per-layer Q
  head-dim all-gather**.
- All DCP a2a code consolidated under `python/sglang/srt/layers/dcp/` (comm.py + kernels.py).


## Tests (registered CI)

- `test/registered/dcp/test_dcp_fi_a2a_reshape.py` — fi_a2a pack/unpack layout **==** NCCL
  a2a **==** ground-truth DCP combine (CPU; the fi_a2a backend's top correctness risk).
- `test/registered/kernels/test_dcp_lse_combine.py` — Triton combine vs CPU reference
  (base-e/base-2, NaN/inf, cuda-graph buffers).
- `test/registered/unit/server_args/test_dcp_config.py` — backend / q-replicate validation.

## Results — DeepSeek-V2-Lite (MLA, BF16)

title: perf: optimize PCG inductor path for FP8 models
author: jasperjiaguo
body:
Three changes that reduce GPU kernel overhead under PCG with inductor compiler:

1. **models/utils** (`apply_qk_norm`): Skip `fused_inplace_qknorm` when `piecewise_cuda_graph_compiler == "inductor"`; fix reshape pattern from `reshape(-1, head_dim)` to `view(*shape[:-1], -1, head_dim)`. The old 2D reshape forced inductor to emit separate `as_strided`/`clone`/`split_with_sizes` kernels; the new 3D view is stride-preserving and fuses cleanly with RMSNorm.
2. **fp8_utils** (`apply_fp8_linear`): For static per-tensor FP8 quantization, use pure PyTorch ops (`reciprocal` + `clamp` + `cast`) instead of the opaque `sgl_kernel.per_tensor_quant_fp8` kernel when `piecewise_cuda_graph_compiler == "inductor"`. Inductor fuses these with surrounding RMSNorm and GEMM dispatch, eliminating a separate kernel launch per linear layer. Eager PCG and decode both continue to use the faster custom kernel.

The inductor check is done locally at each call site via `get_global_server_args().piecewise_cuda_graph_compiler` rather than modifying the global `SGLANG_ENABLE_TORCH_COMPILE` env var, avoiding potential side effects on other code paths.

## Embedding Benchmarks

Qwen3-0.6B embeddings on H200, PCG inductor, production traffic distribution, 60 RPS:

| Config | Items/sec | vs baseline |
|--------|:---------:|:-----------:|
| **This PR (FP8)** | **34.38** | **+24%** |
| main (non-fp8, baseline) | 27.68 | — |

## Generation Benchmarks

Qwen3-0.6B FP8 on H200, PCG inductor, 100 in / 30k out, 10 prompts, request rate 2:

| Server | Output tok/s |
|--------|:------------:|
| **This PR** | **1,025** |
| main | 1,021 |

No regression in decode.

## Per-request GPU profile (FP8 embedding, 7k tokens)

| Metric | main | This PR | Change |
|--------|:----:|:-------:|:------:|
| GPU time/req | 9.8ms | 7.8ms | **-20%** |
| Kernel launches/req | 581 | 441 | **-24%** |

Eliminated kernels per request:
- `fused_qknorm_warp` (28x) — now fused into triton RMSNorm kernels
- `triton_poi_fused_as_strided_clone_split_with_sizes_view` (54x) — eliminated by stride-preserving reshape
- `triton_poi_fused_as_strided_view` (27x) — eliminated by stride-preserving reshape
- `per_tensor_quant_fp8_kernel` (112x) — fused into triton RMSNorm+quant kernels

title: [GDN] Remove FlashInfer GDN decode + no_buffer guard and default to FlashInfer on SM100+
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation

The FlashInfer GDN decode kernel was previously blocked from being used with `--mamba-scheduler-strategy no_buffer` due to accuracy degradation caused by OOB memory access from negative padding indices in the bf16 decode kernel (see #20791).

The root cause was fixed in FlashInfer v0.6.7 via flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2810 (padding index guard for bf16 decode kernel). Thanks to @kaixih!

With PR #21422 merged (upgrading FlashInfer to v0.6.7), we are able to remove this guard and proceed with further benchmarking.

## Modifications

1. **Remove the `raise ValueError` guard** that blocked `--linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer` with `--mamba-scheduler-strategy no_buffer`.
2. **Default to FlashInfer GDN decode on SM100+** when `mamba-ssm-dtype=bfloat16` and no explicit decode backend is specified. This is excluded when MTP speculative decoding is active, since FlashInfer GDN MTP verify is not yet supported on SM100+.

## Benchmarking

### Accuracy Validation

Verified on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B (4×GB200), GSM8K (1319 examples, 8-shot, temp=0.6):

| Scenario              | Quantization | Scheduler    | MTP   | conc=128 | conc=512 |
|----------------------|--------------|--------------|-------|----------|----------|
| NVFP4 + no_buffer    | modelopt_fp4 | no_buffer    | -     | **0.977** | **0.977** |
| NVFP4 + extra_buffer | modelopt_fp4 | extra_buffer | -     | **0.979** | **0.977** |
| FP8 + no_buffer      | fp8          | no_buffer    | -     | **0.978** | **0.977** |
| FP8 + extra_buffer   | fp8          | extra_buffer | -     | **0.979** | **0.979** |
| NVFP4 + MTP          | modelopt_fp4 | extra_buffer | NEXTN | N/A      | N/A      |

> MTP is excluded because `FlashInfer GDN MTP verify is not yet supported on SM100+`.

### Performance

sa-bench, ISL=1024, OSL=1024, NVFP4, 4×GB200  
Comparison: `--linear-attn-decode-backend flashinfer` vs default (`triton`)

| Concurrency | Baseline Mean TPOT | LADFI Mean TPOT | Difference | Output tok/s Improvement |
|------------|--------------------|-----------------|------------|--------------------------|
| 2          | 5.68 ms            | 5.61 ms         | **-1.3%**  | +1.3%                    |
| 4          | 6.43 ms            | 6.35 ms         | **-1.2%**  | +0.5%                    |
| 8          | 7.33 ms            | 7.29 ms         | **-0.6%**  | +1.2%                    |
| 16         | 8.58 ms            | 8.54 ms         | **-0.5%**  | +0.5%                    |
| 32         | 10.86 ms           | 10.77 ms        | **-0.8%**  | +0.7%                    |
| 64         | 13.61 ms           | 13.43 ms        | **-1.3%**  | +1.6%                    |
| 128        | 17.36 ms           | 17.16 ms        | **-1.2%**  | +1.2%                    |
| 256        | 23.60 ms           | 23.04 ms        | **-2.4%**  | +2.3%                    |
| 512        | 33.70 ms           | 32.47 ms        | **-3.7%**  | +3.6%                    |
| 1024       | 53.50 ms           | 51.08 ms        | **-4.5%**  | +4.7%                    |

TPOT improves across all concurrency levels, with gains increasing at higher concurrencies, reaching up to **4.5% TPOT reduction** and **4.7% throughput improvement** at `conc=1024`.

Closes #20791

title: [HiSparse] Optimize the scheduling of decode backup.
author: huangtingwei9988
body:
## Motivation In overlap scheduling, the backup of decode tokens within the `prepare_for_decode` method currently requires waiting for the forward stream to complete, resulting in significant CPU bubbles. This PR shifts the timing of the backup operation to occur at the conclusion of the forward pass, and verifies whether the backup is complete just prior to the commencement of the next forward iteration. ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant S as Scheduler participant C as HiSparseCoordinator participant P as Decode Producer Stream participant B as Decode Backup Stream S->>C: map_last_loc_to_buffer(...) C->>C: prepare previous-token backup metadata C->>B: enqueue backup work Note over B: Backup is queued immediately
but waits on forward_done_event C->>C: grow device buffer / remap reserved slot P->>C: wait_for_pending_backup() Note over P,C: Before each decode pass,
wait for the previous backup to finish C-->>P: clear pending_backup_done_event P->>P: run decode forward P->>C: note_decode_forward_done() C->>C: record decode_forward_done_event B->>B: wait(decode_forward_done_event) B->>B: host_locs = alloc(...) B->>B: req_to_host_pool[...] = host_locs B->>B: backup_from_device_all_layer(...) B->>C: record backup_done_event C->>C: publish pending_backup_done_event Note over C: The next decode pass

title: perf: skip KV cache in FA backend for embedding mode
author: jasperjiaguo
body:
## Summary

Skip KV cache read/write in the FlashAttention backend when serving embedding models, eliminating `store_kvcache` and `flash::prepare_varlen_num_blocks` kernel overhead per decoder layer.

### Motivation

In embedding mode with `--chunked-prefill-size -1` and `--disable-radix-cache`, every request is a single prefill with no decode step. The KV cache is written to and read from but never reused. This wastes ~19µs per layer (`store_kvcache` ~15µs + `prepare_varlen` ~4µs).

### Changes
 **`flashattention_backend.py`**:
   - Skip `set_kv_buffer` (KV cache write) when `layer.fa_skip_kv_cache` is true
   - Use `flash_attn_varlen_func` with raw K/V tensors instead of `flash_attn_with_kvcache` (bypasses KV cache read + paged attention)
   - Uses `cu_seqlens_q` for both Q and K sequence lengths (no prefix cache in this mode)

### Why `fa_skip_kv_cache` requires `disable_radix_cache`

If radix cache is enabled, prefix KV entries could be shared across requests. Skipping the KV cache write would leave the cache unpopulated, causing radix cache lookups to read garbage. The `disable_radix_cache` guard ensures we only skip when caching is fully disabled.

### Why other backends are unaffected

The `save_kv_cache=False` override was previously applied in `radix_attention.forward()`, which broke `torch_native` and `triton` backends — they skip the write but still read K/V from the (now empty) cache. The fix moves the skip logic entirely into `flashattention_backend.py`, which has its own varlen path that uses raw K/V directly.

## Test plan
- [x] Embedding correctness: cosine similarity > 0.99 vs baseline
- [x] Cross-encoder test: torch_native/triton backends unaffected (no `save_kv_cache` override)
- [ ] CI tests pass

title: perf: enable inductor combo_kernels for horizontal fusion
author: jasperjiaguo
body: Enable `combo_kernels` and `benchmark_combo_kernel` in inductor config to allow horizontal fusion of sibling ops with different shapes. This fuses operations like q_norm + k_norm (QK normalization) into a single triton kernel instead of generating separate kernels for each. Requires torch >= 2.9.0. ## Profile Results Qwen3-0.6B FP8 embeddings on H200, PCG inductor, 7k tokens: | Metric | Before | After | |--------|:------:|:-----:| | GPU kernels per forward | 413 | **357** (-14%) | | QK norm kernels per layer | 4 | **2** | | `split_with_sizes` / `clone` in kernel names | Present | **Gone** | The QK norm reduction + pointwise kernels for q and k are now horizontally fused into single kernels. Throughput impact is neutral at 60 RPS (kernel launch overhead is not the bottleneck at this load), but the reduced kernel count should help at higher concurrency or with smaller models where launch overhead is proportionally larger.

title: [AMD] Simplify fused allreduce + RMSNorm and remove hidden_dim allowlist
author: hubertlu-tw
body:
Two changes to the `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` path:

1. **`communicator.py`** (commit `449f7c293`): Fix an off-by-one (`<` → `<=`) in  `apply_aiter_all_reduce_fusion` so the fused kernel activates at the exact boundary size, matching AITER's internal `should_custom_ar` (`inp_size <= max_size/2`).

2. **`parallel_state.py`** (this PR): Remove the hardcoded `hidden_dim ∈ {512, 1024, 2048, 4096}` allowlist for 1-stage vs 2-stage selection. Keep the 128 KB byte-size threshold (the 1-stage kernel is capped at 80 tokens via `kMaxBlocks`) but let AITER's C++ dispatch decide which hidden_dims are supported.

Together these eliminate the per-model maintenance burden (no more manual hidden_dim additions for new models) and ensure AITER's own heuristics are respected.

**Depends on:**
- [ROCm/aiter#2586](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2586) — fixes numerical
  accuracy in the 1-stage fused kernel (bf16 round-trip before residual addition).
- [ROCm/aiter#2453](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2453) — refactors the fused allreduce dispatch so the 1-stage kernel accepts any `hidden_dim` divisible by `pack_size` (no more hardcoded template set), and the 2-stage kernel uses `n_packs`-based dispatch (no more `n_bytes % 1024` alignment requirement).

**Subsumes:** [#21947](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21947) — that PR adds `2880` to the Python-side allowlist. With this change, the allowlist is removed entirely, so all AITER-supported hidden_dims work automatically.

## Motivation

### Problem 1: Off-by-one in outer gate

The activation gate in `communicator.py` used `<` for the byte-size threshold while AITER uses `<=`. For `hidden_size=4096` with bf16 at 8192 tokens, `total_bytes` exactly equals the threshold (67,108,864), so `<` rejected it.

### Problem 2: Redundant hidden_dim allowlist

The 1-stage vs 2-stage decision in `parallel_state.py` gated on `hidden_dim ∈ {512, 1024, 2048, 4096}`. This was redundant at three levels:

| Layer | Where | What it checked |
|-------|-------|----------------|
| Python (SGLang) | `parallel_state.py` | `hidden_dim ∈ {512, 1024, 2048, 4096}` |
| C++ (old AITER) | `custom_all_reduce.cuh` | `n == 4096 \|\| n == 2048 \|\| ...` |
| C++ (new AITER, #2453) | `custom_all_reduce.cuh` | `n % pack_size == 0 && n/pack_size <= 1024` |

AITER's C++ dispatch **already enforces** which hidden_dims have 1-stage support. Passing `use_1stage=True` for an unsupported dim is safe — AITER overrides it to `false` and falls through to 2-stage. The Python-side allowlist only created a maintenance burden (cf. PR #21947).

### The 128 KB threshold is kept (but the allowlist is not)

The 1-stage fused kernel launches one CTA per token and is hard-capped at
`kMaxBlocks = 80` tokens. For `hidden_dim=4096` with bf16:
`80 × 4096 × 2 = 655,360 bytes`.  The 128 KB threshold safely ensures only
small decode-like batches take the 1-stage path; larger prefill batches
automatically fall through to the 2-stage kernel.

## Modifications

### File 1: `python/sglang/srt/layers/communicator.py`

```diff
 def apply_aiter_all_reduce_fusion(input_tensor: torch.Tensor):
     n = input_tensor.shape[-1]
     total_bytes = input_tensor.numel() * input_tensor.element_size()
+    # Aiter's should_custom_ar uses <= max_size/2 (64 MB); match that boundary.
     return (
         _use_aiter
         and total_bytes > 0
         and n <= 16384
-        and total_bytes < 8 * 1024 * 8192
+        and total_bytes <= 8 * 1024 * 8192
         and get_tensor_model_parallel_world_size() != 6
         and not is_dp_attention_enabled()
         and get_global_server_args().enable_aiter_allreduce_fusion
     )
```

### File 2: `python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`

```diff
-        # 1-stage policy for fused AR+RMSNorm:
-        # 1) Explicit env override wins.
-        # 2) Deterministic inference forces 1-stage for reproducibility.
-        # 3) Otherwise follow AITER's heuristic (small payloads only).
+        # 1-stage vs 2-stage selection for fused AR+RMSNorm:
+        # The 1-stage kernel launches one block per token and is capped at
+        # 80 tokens (kMaxBlocks).  Guard with a byte threshold so large
+        # prefill batches fall through to the 2-stage kernel instead of
+        # hitting a runtime error.  AITER's C++ dispatch already gates
+        # which hidden_dims have valid 1-stage support.
         if envs.SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE.is_set():
             use_1stage_ar = envs.SGLANG_USE_1STAGE_ALLREDUCE.get()
-        elif envs.SGLANG_ENABLE_DETERMINISTIC_INFERENCE.get():
-            use_1stage_ar = True
         else:
             total_bytes = input_.numel() * input_.element_size()
-            hidden_dim = input_.shape[-1]
-            use_1stage_ar = total_bytes <= 128 * 1024 and hidden_dim in {
-                512,
-                1024,
-                2048,
-                4096,
-            }
+            use_1stage_ar = total_bytes <= 128 * 1024
```

## Accuracy Tests

### Setup

- **Model:** Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 (60 layers, hidden=4096, 512 experts, MoE)
- **Hardware:** 4× AMD MI355X / gfx950 (TP=4, XGMI fully connected)
- **Backend:** `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, `--attention-backend aiter`
- **AITER version:** `main` branch (`a530b92bf`), includes both
  [ROCm/aiter#2586](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2586) (1-stage accuracy fix) and
  [ROCm/aiter#2453](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2453) (allreduce refactor).
  Full rebuild with `GPU_ARCHS=gfx950 MAX_JOBS=192 PREBUILD_KERNELS=1`.

### GSM8K (1319 questions, 5-shot, parallel=1319)

Three rounds per configuration, with full PID/GPU cleanup between cases.

| Round | A: `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` | B: Baseline (no flag) |
|---|--:|--:|
| 1 | 95.0% | 92.8% |
| 2 | 94.2% | 91.7% |
| 3 | 94.9% | 92.6% |
| **Mean** | **94.7%** | **92.4%** |

No accuracy regression. Fusion ON is **+2.3pp above baseline**, confirming the AITER accuracy fix (#2586) is correctly integrated and the fused path produces numerically sound results.

### Commands

```bash
# Server (Case A — fusion ON)
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /data2/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8/ \
  --tp 4 --attention-backend aiter --trust-remote-code \
  --watchdog-timeout 1200 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000 \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion

# Server (Case B — fusion OFF)
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /data2/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8/ \
  --tp 4 --attention-backend aiter --trust-remote-code \
  --watchdog-timeout 1200 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 9000

# GSM8K benchmark (run 3 rounds per case)
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \
  --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319 --num-shots 5 --port 9000

# Serving benchmark
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
  --host localhost --port 9000 \
  --model /data2/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8/ \
  --dataset-name random \
  --random-input 8192 --random-output 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
  --max-concurrency 1 --num-prompt 8
```

## Benchmarking

### Serving Benchmark (random, 8 × 8192-in / 1024-out, concurrency=1)

| Metric | A: Fusion ON | B: Fusion OFF | Delta |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| Total token throughput (tok/s) | 766.4 | 739.1 | **+3.7%** |
| Output token throughput (tok/s) | 85.2 | 82.1 | **+3.7%** |
| Peak output throughput (tok/s) | 88.0 | 85.0 | +3.5% |
| Median E2E Latency (ms) | 12,019 | 12,476 | **−3.7%** |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 297.5 | 295.2 | +0.8% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 11.46 | 11.90 | **−3.7%** |
| Median ITL (ms) | 11.46 | 11.89 | **−3.6%** |

### Kernel Microbenchmark (TP=4, bf16)

The fused kernel is faster across **all** tested shapes and hidden_dims:

```bash
torchrun --nproc_per_node=4 \
  benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_fused_ar_rms_amd.py \
  --dtype bf16 \
  --decode-shapes 1x4096,4x4096,16x4096,32x4096,1x5120,16x5120,1x7168,16x7168,1x8192,1x14336,4x16384 \
  --prefill-shapes 128x4096,128x5120,128x7168,128x16384,8192x4096 \
  --warmup 10 --iters 30 --repeats 5
```

#### Decode (graph-captured)

With AITER [#2453](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2453) applied, all hidden_dims
work — including GPT-OSS's `hidden_dim=2880`:

| Shape | Unfused p50 (µs) | Fused p50 (µs) | Speedup |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 1×2880 | 20.4 | 10.4 | **1.96×** |
| 4×2880 | 21.7 | 10.5 | **2.07×** |
| 16×2880 | 22.8 | 10.8 | **2.10×** |
| 1×4096 | 20.6 | 11.7 | **1.76×** |
| 4×4096 | 21.4 | 10.3 | **2.08×** |
| 16×4096 | 23.2 | 11.6 | **2.00×** |
| 1×5120 | 22.2 | 10.4 | **2.13×** |
| 16×5120 | 22.8 | 14.2 | **1.61×** |
| 1×6144 | 21.9 | 10.9 | **2.00×** |
| 16×6144 | 23.9 | 14.5 | **1.65×** |
| 1×7168 | 23.7 | 10.6 | **2.24×** |
| 16×7168 | 24.4 | 14.8 | **1.64×** |
| 1×8192 | 23.2 | 10.8 | **2.14×** |
| 16×8192 | 25.4 | 14.8 | **1.72×** |

#### Prefill (eager)

| Shape | Unfused p50 (µs) | Fused p50 (µs) | Speedup |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| 128×2880 | 36.0 | 25.4 | **1.42×** |
| 128×4096 | 36.8 | 25.5 | **1.44×** |
| 128×5120 | 37.8 | 25.5 | **1.49×** |
| 128×6144 | 37.9 | 28.2 | **1.34×** |
| 128×7168 | 38.8 | 30.3 | **1.28×** |
| 128×8192 | 41.3 | 32.5 | **1.27×** |

All hidden_dims benefit — confirming that the allowlist was unnecessarily restrictive.
GPT-OSS (`hidden_dim=2880`) gets up to **2.10× speedup** on decode.

### Trace Verification

After the threshold fix, the EXTEND (prefill) trace on TP-0 confirms fused
kernel activation:

| Kernel | Before fix | After fix | Change |
|---|--:|--:|---|
| `cross_device_reduce_2stage` (unfused AR) | 121 | 2 | Replaced by fused |
| `add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel` (256-wide) | 120 | 1 | Replaced by fused |
| `reduce_scatter_cross_device_store` (fused step 1) | 0 | **119** | NEW |
| `local_device_load_rmsnorm_naive` (fused step 2) | 0 | **119** | NEW |

119 out of 121 allreduce sites now use the fused path. The remaining 2 are
smaller-hidden-dim layers (64-wide) that fall below AITER's internal threshold.

## Summary

| Aspect | Result |
|---|---|
| Accuracy (GSM8K) | No regression (94.7% vs 92.4% baseline, **+2.3pp**) |
| Throughput | **+3.7%** total tok/s |
| Decode latency (TPOT) | **−3.7%** (11.46ms vs 11.90ms) |
| Prefill latency (TTFT) | Neutral |
| Kernel speedup (decode) | **1.3–2.2×** across all decode shapes and hidden_dims |
| Maintenance | No more per-model hidden_dim additions needed |

title: Allow piecewise CUDA graph with speculative decoding
author: narutolhy
body:
## Summary

- Allow `--enable-piecewise-cuda-graph` to coexist with all speculative decoding algorithms (EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN/STANDALONE/NGRAM)
- Previously all speculative algorithms disabled PCG (#16331 added this as a safety measure when PCG became default, without testing spec decode compatibility)

## Motivation

PCG and speculative decoding operate on **independent forward paths**:
- **PCG**: captures/replays graphs for prefill/extend (`ForwardMode.EXTEND`) with `spec_info=None`
- **Speculative**: draft/verify uses decode CUDA graphs (`ForwardMode.TARGET_VERIFY`)

The restriction was added in #16331 as a conservative safety measure when PCG became default-enabled. The original PCG implementation (#10062) had no speculative restriction.

## Accuracy Verification (GSM8K, 50 questions per config)

| Algorithm | Model | PCG Score | No-PCG Score | Acceptance | Status |
|-----------|-------|-----------|-------------|-----------|--------|
| **EAGLE/NEXTN** | Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8 TP2 | **0.980** | 0.980 | 3.46 | ✅ Identical |
| **EAGLE3** | Qwen3-30B-A3B TP2 | **1.000** | — | 4.23 | ✅ |
| **STANDALONE** | Qwen3-8B FP8 TP2 | **0.380** | 0.400 | 3.11 | ✅ Within noise |

STANDALONE's lower score (0.56→0.40) is from the weak draft model (Qwen3-0.6B), equally present with and without PCG.

## Benchmark (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B FP8, TP2, H100)

`--mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer` for all configs.

| Config | rate=1 ITL | rate=5 TTFT | rate=5 ITL |
|--------|----------|-----------|----------|
| Baseline (no overlap, no PCG, no MTP) | 21.95ms | — | — |
| extra_buffer + MTP | 3.00ms | 253ms | 6.06ms |
| **extra_buffer + PCG + MTP (this PR)** | **2.89ms** | **147ms** | **5.56ms** |

PCG adds prefill acceleration on top of MTP's decode speedup:
- **TTFT (rate=5): 253ms → 147ms (-42%)**

## Modification

`server_args.py`: Removed the blanket disable of PCG for speculative decoding. Added comments explaining why PCG and speculative decoding are compatible (independent forward paths).

## Test plan
- [x] EAGLE/NEXTN (MTP) + PCG: accuracy 0.980 (= baseline)
- [x] EAGLE3 + PCG: accuracy 1.000
- [x] STANDALONE + PCG: accuracy 0.380 (= no-PCG 0.400, within noise)
- [x] Added test: `test/registered/piecewise_cuda_graph/test_pcg_with_mtp.py`
  - TestPCGWithMTP: Qwen3.5-35B-A3B + NEXTN + PCG
  - TestPCGWithEAGLE3: Qwen3-30B-A3B + EAGLE3 + PCG
  - TestPCGWithSTANDALONE: Qwen3-8B + STANDALONE + PCG
- [ ] CI tests

title: [Spec][Ngram] Followup fixes for `MatchState` incremental advance
author: hnyls2002
body:
Followup fixes for #21243.

## Summary
- Eliminate per-token heap allocation in `advanceMatchState_()` — reuse a single `vector<NodeRef>` across loop iterations
- Access `root_` directly instead of going through `resolve(state, rootRef())` which was a tautological check on a freshly-created ref
- Move `test_ngram_corpus.py` from `spec/utils/` to `unit/spec/` and switch from `register_cuda_ci` to `register_cpu_ci` (ngram corpus is pure C++, no GPU needed)
- Add `TestNgramCorpusMatchBenchmark` — measures incremental advance vs full rebuild per-step latency with `max_trie_depth=18`
- Add clarifying comments: `TrieNode::version` / `NodeRef::version` invariant, `reset()` epoch-based invalidation, match state lifecycle in `ngram_worker.py`
- Add `x/N` progress tracking and timing to `rerun-test.yml` (both CUDA and CPU jobs)

## Benchmark (CPU, `max_trie_depth=18`)

```
Incremental: 32.4 us/step
Rebuild:     45.3 us/step
Speedup:     1.40x
```

`match()` is O(D) incremental vs O(D²) rebuild, but only accounts for a fraction of total `batch_get` latency (FFI + `buildRecency` + `fillResult` dominate). The 1.40x end-to-end speedup is consistent with expectations at D=18.

title: [AMD] Enable Piecewise CUDA Graph for AMD GPUs
author: hubertlu-tw
body:
## Motivation

Enable Piecewise CUDA Graph (PCG) on AMD/ROCm with the aiter backend, while keeping the existing CUDA path unchanged. The PR also fixes a Dynamo recompilation fallback crash when batches exceed `piecewise_cuda_graph_max_tokens`.

### Tested configurations

- **DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4-Preview** — TP=4, EP=4, EAGLE speculative decoding, FP8 KV cache, aiter backend
- **DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4-Preview** — TP=8, registered AMD PCG test
- **Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4** — TP=4, aiter backend
- **1-GPU models** — Qwen2.5-VL-7B, InternVL2.5-8B, Qwen2.5-VL-3B

## Modifications

- Add eager fallback in `cuda_piecewise_backend.py` when Dynamo recompilation happens outside PCG capture.
- Add AMD-only PCG fixes for aiter MXFP4 custom-op wrapping, MLA dual-attention lookup, aiter chip-info prewarm, single-pass warmup compile, and oversized-batch fallback context. PCG init on DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 drops from ~6 min to ~1 min 40 sec (3.6x faster).
- Fix padded-token correctness under PCG by zeroing attention output / MoE routing weights and using `raw_num_tokens` for EAGLE verify batches.
- Update registered AMD coverage for DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 with local model path support and the correct `--piecewise-cuda-graph-max-tokens` flag.
- Fix `_use_aiter` initialization in `piecewise_cuda_graph_runner.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K benchmark (5-shot, 1319 questions, `--parallel 1319`):

| Model | Config | Accuracy | Threshold |
|-------|--------|----------|-----------|
| DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 | TP=4, EP=4, PCG, fp8 KV | **0.941** | >= 0.94 |
| DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 + EAGLE | TP=4, EP=4, PCG, EAGLE, fp8 KV | **0.954** | >= 0.94 |
| DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 | TP=8, PCG, registered AMD test | **0.946** | >= 0.94 |

Additional models (registered CI tests):

| Model | Config | Metric | Result |
|-------|--------|--------|--------|
| Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4 | TP=4, PCG | Serving OK | Pass |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct | TP=1, PCG | GSM8K | 0.820 (>= 0.80) |
| InternVL2.5-8B | TP=1, PCG | MGSM | 0.704 (>= 0.70) |
| Qwen2.5-VL-3B (embedding) | TP=1, PCG | diff | 0.0 (atol=1e-2) |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

**Baseline** (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4 + EAGLE, TP=4, EP=4, no PCG):
- Accuracy: 0.950, Output throughput: 1642 token/s

**With PCG + EAGLE** (`--piecewise-cuda-graph-max-tokens 8192`, recommended):
- Accuracy: 0.954, Output throughput: 2657-2677 token/s (**+63% throughput**)
- bench_serving (random 3500in/1500out, 768 prompts, 448 concurrency):
  Output throughput 4222 tok/s, Total 14070 tok/s, TPOT 78.74ms

**Without EAGLE** (PCG only):
- No PCG: Accuracy 0.947, Throughput 2019 tok/s
- With PCG (max-tokens 2048): Accuracy 0.945, Throughput 1898 tok/s

**Registered AMD PCG test** (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4, TP=8, local model path):
- `test/registered/amd/test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_8gpu.py::TestDeepseekR1MXFP4`
- GSM8K accuracy: 0.946
- GSM8K output throughput: 3096.887 token/s
- Single-request speed: 159.49 token/s
- Result: `2 passed, 6 warnings in 404.79s`

**Registered 1-GPU PCG test** (Qwen2.5-VL):
- `test/registered/piecewise_cuda_graph/test_piecewise_cuda_graph_support_1_gpu.py`
- GSM8K accuracy: 0.820
- Output throughput: 7550.009 token/s
- Embedding parity: max_abs=0.0, max_rel=0.0
- Result: `2 passed, 8 warnings in 190.27s`

Note: Without EAGLE, the default MLA cap of 2048 means PCG only covers small
decode batches. Raising `--piecewise-cuda-graph-max-tokens` to 8192 is
recommended for MLA models to also capture prefill/verify batches.

### Qwen3.5-MXFP4 PCG A/B on gfx950

Setup:
- Model: `/data2/amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4/`
- TP=2, aiter backend, FP8 KV cache, page size 16, radix cache disabled
- Baseline launch: Qwen3.5 without PCG flags
- PCG launch: same command plus `--enforce-piecewise-cuda-graph --piecewise-cuda-graph-compiler eager --piecewise-cuda-graph-max-tokens 8192`
- GSM8K warmup/sanity: 1319 questions, parallel 1319, 5-shot, threshold >= 0.92
- Serving runs: random dataset, `--random-range-ratio 1.0`, `--num-prompt 32`

#### 1k/1k/cc=8

| Metric | without PCG | with PCG | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| GSM8K accuracy | 0.927 | 0.931 | +0.43% |

#### 8k/1k/cc=4

#### 1k/1k/cc=64

Serving command shape: random input 1024, random output 1024, max concurrency

|---|---:|---:|---:|

Serving command shape: random input 8192, random output 1024, max concurrency
64, num prompts 256.

| Metric | without PCG | with PCG | Improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 10670.35 | 11183.88 | +4.81% |

Note: Improvement is higher-is-better for accuracy/throughput and lower-is-better for TTFT/TPOT latency.

## Commands Used

### Qwen3.5-MXFP4

```bash
env -u ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION \
    SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
```

title: [AMD] Use aiter CK layernorm2d for LayerNorm to reduce NSA indexer kernel launches
author: 1am9trash
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

cc @Jacob0226

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

The current `LayerNorm` on HIP uses the torch implementation and triggers an extra dtype cast at both entry and exit. This results in 3 kernels per `LayerNorm` call (cast -> layernorm -> cast), hurting the performance of operations like `k_norm()` in the GLM-5-FP8 NSA indexer.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

- In `LayerNorm.forward_hip()`, use the aiter CK kernel `layernorm2d_fwd()` when the dtype is `bf16` or `fp16`. For other dtypes, fall back to the original torch code path.
- Change `k_norm` dtype in the NSA indexer from `fp32` to `bf16` when aiter is enabled, so it can take the CK kernel path.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

**LayerNorm unit test:**
- Command: `python -m pytest python/sglang/test/test_layernorm.py::TestLayerNorm -v`
- Result: all 384 subtests passed

**Model test:**
- GLM-5-FP8 on MI355 GSM8k (TP8): 0.946

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

GLM-5-FP8 server command on MI355:
```bash
export SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0
export ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
export SAFETENSORS_FAST_GPU=1
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path GLM-5-FP8 \
  --tp 8 --port 9000 --trust-remote-code \
  --tool-call-parser glm47 --reasoning-parser glm45 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 8}' \
  --nsa-prefill-backend tilelang --nsa-decode-backend tilelang --disable-radix-cache \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

Benchmark on MI355X TP8, concurrency 4/8/16/32/64 averaged (baseline: sglang PR #22258 + aiter PR #2575):
- ISL/OSL 1k/1k: Throughput +1.4%, TPOT -0.9%
- ISL/OSL 8k/1k: Throughput +1.2%, TPOT -2.8%

Per-layer profiling:
- Time: ~12us -> ~4us
- Kernel: 3 -> 1

title: [EPD] Optimize the Mooncake backend
author: LucQueen
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

The current EPD (Encoder-Prefill-Decode) disaggregation architecture with the Mooncake backend transfers vision embeddings from the Encoder server to the Prefill server through a **CPU-staged** path: after ViT forward on the Encoder GPU, the embedding tensor is moved to CPU (`new_embeddings.cpu()`), then transferred via Mooncake to a CPU buffer on the Prefill side, and finally copied back to GPU for LLM prefill. This CPU round-trip (D2H → RDMA → H2D) introduces unnecessary latency and memory bandwidth overhead, especially for large multimodal inputs (e.g., multi-image MMMU tasks).

This PR optimizes the Mooncake backend to enable **GPU-to-GPU zero-copy RDMA transfer** by:
1. Keeping ViT embeddings on GPU after forward pass (no `.cpu()` call).
2. Pre-allocating GPU-side receive buffers on the Prefill server and registering them with the Mooncake engine.
3. Using GPUDirect RDMA to transfer embeddings directly from Encoder GPU memory to Prefill GPU memory.
4. This approach decouples VIT inference from metadata return, enabling overlapped computation and communication for better end-to-end performance.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

### `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_receiver.py`
- **New class `WaitingImageRDMARequest`**: Extends `WaitingImageRequest` to support GPU-to-GPU RDMA transfers. Implements:
  - A two-phase encode flow: `POST /encode` (returns metadata incl. `embedding_size`) → pre-allocate GPU buffer → `POST /send` (triggers RDMA write).
  - GPU buffer lifecycle management: allocation on `cuda:<gpu_id>`, Mooncake engine registration/deregistration, and cleanup on error/timeout.
  - `_try_recv_mm_data()` override that reconstructs embedding tensors directly from the GPU buffer (zero-copy, no deserialization of ZMQ data parts).
- **`MMReceiverBase.__init__`**: For `mooncake` backend, initializes scheduler-side properties (pp_rank, tp_rank, hostname, mm_processor, waiting_list, etc.) previously only set for `zmq_to_scheduler`.
- **`_send_encode_request`**: For `mooncake` backend, saves `mm_data` (extracted URL list) onto the request object as `mm_data_mooncake` and returns early — no tokenizer-side encoding thread is spawned.
- **`_process_waiting_requests`**: Accepts `**extra_kwargs` to forward `embeddings_engine`, `dtype`, and `gpu_id` to `WaitingImageRDMARequest` constructor.
- **`process_waiting_requests`** in `MMReceiverHTTP`: Routes to `WaitingImageRDMARequest` class (with RDMA kwargs) instead of base `WaitingImageRequest`.
- **`allocate_embedding_buffer`**: Changed from CPU tensor to GPU tensor (`device=self.scheduler.gpu_id`) for zero-copy RDMA receive.
- **Timeout handling**: Added `_cleanup_gpu_buffer()` and socket close on timeout for RDMA requests.

### `python/sglang/srt/disaggregation/encode_server.py`
- **Pre-computed embedding metadata**: On init, Mooncake backend pre-computes `_embedding_dims`, `_embedding_dtype`, and `_element_size` so metadata can be returned before VIT forward completes.
- **New async encode methods**:
  - `encode_with_mooncake()`: For non-cache mode — returns metadata immediately, launches VIT forward as a background `asyncio.Task`.
  - `encode_with_global_cache_mooncake()`: For global-cache mode — same async pattern with cache check, VIT forward, prefetch, and fallback all running as background tasks.
- **Async forward synchronization**: Added `_forward_ready_events` (dict of `asyncio.Event`) and `_forward_results` (dict storing embedding or error) to coordinate between `/encode` (returns metadata) and `/send` (waits for forward completion before RDMA transfer).
- **`_send` method**: Before RDMA transfer, waits for VIT forward completion via the event mechanism; validates embedding availability.
- **`run_encoder` / `launch_server`**: Routes to the appropriate encode method based on `encoder_transfer_backend == "mooncake"`.
- **Logger configuration**: Added `configure_logger(server_args)` call in `launch_server`.

### `python/sglang/srt/managers/scheduler.py`
- Extended `init_disaggregation` and `recv_requests` to handle `mooncake` backend alongside `zmq_to_scheduler` (previously only `zmq_to_scheduler` triggered mm_receiver initialization and waiting request processing).
- Passes `dtype=self.model_config.dtype` to `create_mm_receiver` for GPU buffer allocation.

### `python/sglang/srt/managers/tokenizer_manager.py`
- Removed `mooncake` from the tokenizer-side mm_data receiving path — Mooncake now uses the scheduler-side path (`zmq_to_scheduler` style) instead of the tokenizer-side path.
- Forwards `mm_data_mooncake` attribute through `TokenizedGenerateReqInput` so the scheduler-side `WaitingImageRDMARequest` can access the original image URLs.
- Updated `_handle_epd_disaggregation_encode_request` to route `mooncake` backend through the scheduler-side dispatch path.

### `test/registered/distributed/test_epd_disaggregation.py`
- **New test class `TestEPDDisaggregationMooncake`**: End-to-end test for the Mooncake GPU RDMA zero-copy pipeline.
  - Skipped in CI (requires RDMA hardware).
  - Launches encode, prefill, and decode servers with `--encoder-transfer-backend mooncake`.
  - Runs MMMU evaluation (50 samples) and asserts accuracy > 0.40 (matching baseline for Qwen2.5-VL-3B-Instruct).

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Expected improvements:
- Elimination of D2H + H2D memory copies per embedding transfer
- Overlapped VIT forward computation with metadata return and GPU buffer allocation
- Lower end-to-end latency for multimodal EPD disaggregation requests

Model: Qwen3-VL-4B-Instruct
Deployment topology: 1E3PD on H20
Workload: 8 images per request

Throughput increased by 2.48x: Request throughput surged from 0.29 req/s to 0.72 req/s.
End-to-End Latency reduced by 7.6x: Mean E2E latency dropped from ~54.5 seconds to ~7.1 seconds.
TTFT (Time to First Token) slashed by 8.35x: Mean TTFT dropped dramatically from ~51.9 seconds down to just ~6.2 seconds.

title: [Bugfix] Fix flashinfer_cutlass MoE crash when intermediate_size_per_partition is not 16-aligned
author: vguduruTT
body:
## Summary

- Fix crash in `flashinfer_cutlass MoE backend ` when `intermediate_size_per_partition` is not a multiple of 16 (e.g., NemotronH FP8 at TP=8: 7688 / 8 = 961)
- Add 16-byte alignment padding for flashinfer_cutlass in` ModelOptFp8MoEMethod.process_weights_after_loading`, following the same post-load padding pattern as `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod` for flashinfer_trtllm
- Move moe_runner_backend auto-resolution (`AUTO` → `FLASHINFER_CUTLASS`) from `server_args.py` into `ModelOptFp8MoEMethod.create_moe_runner,` following the fp8.py pattern so user `--moe-runner-backend` overrides are still respected

## Motivation

- The flashinfer_cutlass MoE kernel requires intermediate_size_per_partition to be a multiple of 16. For models like NemotronH FP8 (Nemotron Nano 30B A3B), moe_intermediate_size = 7688. At TP=8, this gives 7688 / 8 = 961, which is not 16-aligned, causing a hard crash during server launch on flashinfer 0.6.3+.
- On older flashinfer versions, this silently fell back to a slower kernel path. This bug was discovered while investigating the performance characteristics reported in #21307.

## Changes

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/modelopt_quant.py `(ModelOptFp8MoEMethod)

create_moe_runner: Resolve AUTO → FLASHINFER_CUTLASS and store as self._resolved_backend (user overrides via --moe-runner-backend are respected; only instantiate MoeRunner for TRITON)
process_weights_after_loading: Use self._resolved_backend instead of global get_moe_runner_backend(); pad w13_weight and w2_weight with F.pad when intermediate_size_per_partition % 16 != 0 (same post-load padding approach as ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod for trtllm 128-alignment)
apply: Use self._resolved_backend for backend dispatch

- `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py`
Remove the NemotronH-specific moe_runner_backend = "flashinfer_cutlass" override entirely (now handled in the quant method per reviewer feedback)


- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/fused_moe_triton/layer.py` (FusedMoE)

Remove use_flashinfer_cutlass_padded flag and pre-allocation padding from __init__ (padding is now post-load in the quant method)
Remove use_flashinfer_cutlass_padded from use_padded_loading in _load_w13 and _load_w2

## Impact

Benchmarked on **NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Nano-30B-A3B-FP8**, TP=8, 8xH100:

| Metric | Before (triton MoE fallback) | After (flashinfer_cutlass + fix) | Improvement |
|--------|------------------------------|----------------------------------|-------------|
| Output tok/s | 140.14 | **207.18** | **+47.8%** |
| ITL (ms) | 7.14 | **4.83** | **-32.4%** |

No accuracy impact -- the fix only pads weight tensors with zeros (same approach as `flashinfer_trtllm` 128-alignment).

## Test plan

- [x] TP=1: No alignment needed (7688 / 1 = 7688, divisible by 16) -- verified no regression
- [x] TP=8: Alignment fix applied (961 -> 976) -- verified crash resolved, +47.8% throughput
- [x] Accuracy validation: lm_eval gsm8k matches baseline
- [ ] CI: Existing MoE tests should pass (fix only activates when `intermediate_size_per_partition % 16 != 0`)

Related: #21307 (discovered this bug while investigating Nemotron TP=8 performance)


- Attaching Summary and Benchmarking Results for reference- [TP8_BENCHMARKING_RESULTS.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26824000/TP8_BENCHMARKING_RESULTS.md), [ACC_VALIDATION.md](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26823995/ACC_VALIDATION.md), [nemotron_benchmarks_acc_validation.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/26823997/nemotron_benchmarks_acc_validation.zip)

title: MSCCL++ Integration
author: caiocbr
body:
## Motivation

This PR migrates the MSCCL++ integration from a statically-linked C++/CUDA kernel bundled inside `sgl-kernel` to the upstream **MSCCL++ Python package** (`mscclpp`). The new approach:

- **Supports the latest MSCCL++ version** — uses `mscclpp`'s Python-level `Executor`, DSL compiler, and native algorithm collection instead of the old hand-written CUDA kernels.
- **Provides a flexible algorithm interface** — algorithms are configured via `AlgorithmCollectionBuilder` (native) and `mscclpp.language` (DSL), making it easy to add new collective algorithms for different scales (currently TP=8 single-node and TP=16 two-node).
- **Adds auto-tuning** — at initialization, the communicator benchmarks all candidate algorithms × block/thread configurations using CUDA graph capture and selects the best per message size.
- **Integrates correctly with piecewise CUDA graph compilation** — prevents MSCCL++ from being used during compile/capture/replay phases, avoiding `torch.compile` guard invalidation and recompilation.
- **Supports symmetric memory (NVLS)** — enables `default_allreduce_nvls_zero_copy` when `--enable-symm-mem` is active.

## Modifications

### Rewritten `PyMscclppCommunicator` (`python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/pymscclpp.py`)
- **Complete rewrite**: Replaced the old `sgl-kernel` C++ op-based communicator with a pure-Python implementation using `mscclpp`, `mscclpp.ext`, and `mscclpp.default_algos`.
- Removed old dependencies: `bisect`, `math`, `os`, `IntEnum`, `custom_all_reduce_ops`, `MscclContextSelection`, `mscclpp_convert_to_bytes`, `mscclpp_bench_time`, `SGLANG_MSCCLPP_MAX_BYTES` env var.
- Added `_create_native_algorithms()` with four algorithm types: `nvls_packet`, `packet`, `rsag_zero_copy`, `nvls_zero_copy`.
- Added `_create_dsl_algorithms()` for TP=16 two-node allreduce via the MSCCL++ DSL compiler.
- Added `_tune()` and `_get_time()` for CUDA-graph-based auto-tuning with synchronized timing across ranks.
- `should_mscclpp_allreduce()` now checks piecewise CUDA graph state (`is_in_piecewise_cuda_graph()`, `is_in_pcg_torch_compile()`, `get_pcg_capture_stream()`) to avoid use during graph compilation/capture.
- `all_reduce()` is now in-place (returns the input tensor) and uses the tuned algorithm config.
- Added `destroy()` for proper cleanup of executor, buffers, and algorithm configs.

### Removed MSCCL++ C++/CUDA code from `sgl-kernel`
- **Deleted** `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/mscclpp_allreduce.cu` (~140 lines) and `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/mscclpp_allreduce.cuh` (~779 lines) — the old hand-written allreduce kernels.
- **Deleted** `sgl-kernel/csrc/allreduce/test_mscclpp_allreduce.cu` (~153 lines).
- **Removed** `mscclpp` FetchContent dependency from `sgl-kernel/CMakeLists.txt` and all `mscclpp_static` link targets.
- **Removed** `mscclpp_generate_unique_id`, `mscclpp_init_context`, `mscclpp_allreduce` from `sgl_kernel_ops.h`, `common_extension.cc`, and `sgl_kernel/allreduce.py`.
- **Removed** `IS_MSCCLPP_AR_AVAILABLE` and the MSCCL++ ops region from `custom_all_reduce_ops.py`.

### Removed old MSCCL++ tests
- **Deleted** `sgl-kernel/tests/test_mscclpp.py` (~146 lines) and `test/manual/test_mscclpp.py` (~196 lines).

### Piecewise context manager (`python/sglang/srt/compilation/piecewise_context_manager.py`)
- Added `_piecewise_compiled` flag and `is_piecewise_compiled()` to track whether piecewise compilation has completed, used to prevent enabling MSCCL++ during CUDA graph capture.

### Allreduce dispatch (`python/sglang/srt/distributed/parallel_state.py`)
- In `graph_capture()`: disabled `pymscclpp_comm` after piecewise compilation to avoid invalidating `torch.compile` guards.
- In `all_reduce()`: replaced symmetric memory dispatch condition to use `should_mscclpp_allreduce(input_)` instead of checking `pymscclpp_comm.disabled`, giving MSCCL++ proper per-message-size control.
- Added MSCCL++ fallback guard to the custom allreduce (`ca_comm`) dispatch path.
- Simplified piecewise CUDA graph pynccl fallback condition.
- Added `pymscclpp_comm.destroy()` in `GroupCoordinator.destroy()`.

### Custom allreduce (`python/sglang/srt/distributed/device_communicators/custom_all_reduce.py`)
- Added `None` guard for `ops` in `close()` to prevent errors during shutdown when the module has been garbage-collected.

### Benchmark (`benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/`)
- Added `README.md` with setup/usage instructions for MSCCL++ benchmarking and inference.
- Updated `benchmark_mscclpp.py`: added input snapshot for graph correctness, proper cleanup (`destroy()`, `dist.barrier()`, `cleanup_dist_env_and_memory()`).

### `bench_one_batch.py`
- Added `destroy_model_parallel()` call before `destroy_distributed_environment()`.
- Replaced `maybe_reindex_device_id` with direct local rank calculation for multi-node support.

## Accuracy Tests

Allreduce correctness was validated using the existing `benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py` microbenchmark, which compares the MSCCL++ output element-wise against torch/NCCL allreduce across power-of-two message sizes (`bfloat16`).

### Single-node (H100, TP=8)

```bash
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 torchrun --nproc_per_node 8 --nnodes 1 --node_rank 0 \
    benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py
```

Kernel-level latency comparison (all times in µs):

| msg_size  | torch eager | msccl eager | msccl graph | pynccl graph |
|-----------|-------------|-------------|-------------|--------------|
| 2.0 KiB  | 19.77       | 11.70       | **5.86**    | 16.84        |
| 4.0 KiB  | 17.24       | 11.04       | **5.98**    | 16.99        |
| 8.0 KiB  | 18.60       | 10.72       | **6.00**    | 17.23        |
| 16.0 KiB | 22.43       | 11.09       | **6.37**    | 17.75        |
| 32.0 KiB | 18.87       | 11.12       | **7.21**    | 19.63        |
| 64.0 KiB | 18.81       | 10.54       | **8.20**    | 19.92        |
| 128.0 KiB| 19.33       | 10.95       | **8.80**    | 20.13        |
| 256.0 KiB| 19.50       | 10.31       | **10.56**   | 20.31        |
| 512.0 KiB| 19.81       | 505.39      | **11.96**   | 20.86        |
| 1.0 MiB  | 25.88       | 512.41      | **14.01**   | 27.00        |

MSCCL++ graph-captured allreduce is **1.9–2.9× faster** than pynccl graph for messages up to 256 KiB.

---

### Two-node (H200, TP=16)

```bash
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 torchrun --nproc_per_node 8 --nnodes 2 --node_rank <rank> \
    benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py
```

Kernel-level latency comparison (all times in µs):

| msg_size   | torch eager time | msccl eager time | msccl graph time | pynccl graph time |
|------------|------------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|------------------:|
| 2.0 KiB    | 56.7552 | 151.11  | **16.3434** | 32.3386 |
| 4.0 KiB    | 34.2752 | 168.131 | **15.9667** | 37.2829 |
| 8.0 KiB    | 67.1872 | 168.496 | **16.2461** | 39.0819 |
| 16.0 KiB   | 68.2112 | 150.739 | **16.1210** | 43.8541 |
| 32.0 KiB   | 79.1712 | 171.094 | **16.6038** | 43.5085 |
| 64.0 KiB   | 40.8672 | 193.594 | **17.7155** | 42.5562 |
| 128.0 KiB  | 43.1520 | 405.661 | **22.7440** | 48.9597 |
| 256.0 KiB  | 98.9984 | 591.226 | **20.6394** | 101.745 |
| 512.0 KiB  | 108.278 | 738.973 | **25.2358** | 76.0314 |
| 1.0 MiB    | 75.2992 | 814.592 | **31.8493** | 80.9184 |

MSCCL++ graph-captured allreduce remains significantly faster than pynccl graph execution in the multi-node configuration, particularly for small and medium message sizes.

---

### Four-node (H200, TP=32)

```bash
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 torchrun --nproc_per_node 8 --nnodes 4 --node_rank <rank> \
    benchmark/kernels/all_reduce/benchmark_mscclpp.py
```

Kernel-level latency comparison (all times in µs):

| msg_size   | torch eager time | msccl eager time | msccl graph time | pynccl graph time |
|------------|------------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|------------------:|
| 2.0 KiB    | 197.162  | 160.390 | **19.2624** | 51.6115 |
| 4.0 KiB    | 58.1792  | 178.003 | **20.9779** | 56.1440 |
| 8.0 KiB    | 93.7312  | 265.206 | **20.6093** | 60.9440 |
| 16.0 KiB   | 90.3808  | 408.336 | **19.9437** | 63.1962 |
| 32.0 KiB   | 92.5504  | 161.139 | **21.2691** | 62.5667 |
| 64.0 KiB   | 61.1104  | 162.051 | **23.1878** | 66.8675 |
| 128.0 KiB  | 71.8304  | 416.426 | **25.5725** | 79.5904 |
| 256.0 KiB  | 178.355  | 462.093 | **26.4970** | 136.921 |
| 512.0 KiB  | 155.773  | 531.478 | **33.2646** | 137.177 |
| 1.0 MiB    | 136.717  | 763.683 | **45.0688** | 139.499 |

Even at 4 nodes, graph-captured MSCCL++ maintains substantially lower latency than pynccl graph execution across all tested message sizes.

---

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End-to-end inference throughput was measured using `bench_one_batch` with **Qwen/Qwen3-8B** (`input-len=256`, `output-len=256`, `bfloat16`).

### Single-node (H100, TP=8)

**MSCCL++ vs. native SGLang (NCCL + custom allreduce)**

```bash
# MSCCL++
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
    --batch <bs> --input-len 256 --output-len 256 --tp-size 8 --enable-mscclpp

# Native SGLang baseline (NCCL + custom allreduce)
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
    --batch <bs> --input-len 256 --output-len 256 --tp-size 8
```

| Batch Size | MSCCL++ (tok/s) | Native SGLang (tok/s) | Speedup |

| 256        | 37,945.59       | 36,490.37             | 1.04×   |
| 512        | 50,978.09       | 49,442.72             | 1.03×   |

```bash
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
    --load-format auto \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \

```

**MSCCL++ vs. native SGLang**

At 2 nodes, MSCCL++ provides substantial throughput improvements over native SGLang, reaching up to **2.7× higher throughput** at medium batch sizes.

---

### Four-node (H200, TP=32)

```bash
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch \
    --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-8B \
    --load-format auto \
```

At 4 nodes, MSCCL++ achieves up to **3.4× throughput improvement** over NCCL, with the largest gains appearing at medium-to-large batch sizes where communication overhead becomes dominant.

**2. MSCCL++ with symmetric memory (NVLS) vs. NCCL with symmetric memory**

title: [AMD] Reduce NSA indexer kernels (weights_proj,  k-cache store kernel fusion)
author: 1am9trash
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

Redundant kernels in the NSA indexer on HIP:

weights_proj: 
- The ReplicatedLinear layer uses fp32 params_dtype, preventing tgemm from dispatching to the tuned bf16 fused kernel and falling back to torch GEMM instead. An additional x.to(fp32) cast is also required before the GEMM. 
- Total: 3 kernels (dtype cast + fp32 GEMM + reduction).

Indexer k-cache store: 
- Key quantization (act_quant) and cache write (set_index_k_scale_buffer) are two separate kernel launches.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

weights_proj:
- Switch params_dtype to bf16 (aligned with the CUDA path) and remove the redundant input dtype cast. The GEMM now dispatches to aiter::wv_splitk_small_fp16_bf16_kernel in a single kernel.
- Perf impact: 3 -> 1 kernel, ~10 µs saved per layer.

Indexer k-cache store:
- Replace the two-step quant + store with the fused indexer_k_quant_and_cache kernel from AITER.
- Perf impact: 2 -> 1 kernel, ~4 µs saved per layer.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

TP8, GSM8k:
- MI300 (GLM-5-fp8): 0.950
- MI355 (GLM-5.1-fp8): 0.951

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

GLM-5.1-FP8 server command on MI355:
```bash
export SGLANG_ROCM_FUSED_DECODE_MLA=0
export ROCM_QUICK_REDUCE_QUANTIZATION=INT4
```
