title: [Apple Silicon] Add custom Metal RoPE kernel with fused KV cache store
author: adityavaid
body:
## Motivation

This PR adds the first AOT-compiled Metal kernel to SGLang's Apple Silicon backend: a fused **NeoX RoPE + KV pool scatter** that replaces two `mx.fast.rope` calls and the per-request KV-pool scatter in batched decode with a single C++ entry that emits one Metal command buffer.

On Apple Silicon, each kernel dispatch incurs ~1-4ms of GPU idle time due to Metal command buffer overhead ([profiled in #22114](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/22114)). Reducing dispatch count directly improves decode latency. This kernel consolidates the Q and K rotation into one dispatch, cutting the RoPE step from ~224us (2 × 112us) to ~127us — a **1.8x speedup** for the RoPE operation.
Part of the **Apple Device Support roadmap** ([#19137](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/19137))

**NOTE : this builds on #23449's scaffolding**

## Kernel logic
A single `.metallib` produced at build time by Apple's `xcrun metal` +
`xcrun metallib` (same pipeline MLX itself uses), exporting three
specialised kernels per dtype (f16, bf16, f32). All three are dispatched
into one Metal command buffer per batched-decode forward, per layer:

| Kernel | Work |
|---|---|
| `rope_q` | NeoX RoPE on Q |
| `rope_k_pool` | NeoX RoPE on K **and** scatter rotated K to `k_pool[slot]` |
| `v_to_pool` | Scatter V to `v_pool[slot]` |

Loaded once at import via `register_library(path)`. Per-shape pipelines
are specialised through Metal function constants so a single `.metallib`
serves every model configuration.

## Optimisations over a naïve fused-RoPE kernel
( Inspired by [MLX's own rope.metal](https://github.com/ml-explore/mlx/blob/main/mlx/backend/metal/kernels/rope.metal) )
Baseline : single 1-D-grid kernel that recovers `(token, head, dim)` via div/mod and branches on `is_q`. 

Layered on top of that:

1. **AOT `.metallib`** instead of runtime JIT — Apple's full compiler-optimisation pass at build time.
2.. **3D thread-grid** (`pos.x = dim`, `pos.y = token`, `pos.z = head`) — eliminates the div/mod hot path.
4. **Smart threadgroup sizing** — fills 4–8 SIMD groups per threadgroup instead of the naïve `(32, 1, 1)` that uses 1.
5. **Function-constant specialisation** of shape parameters `(`HEAD_DIM`, `NUM_QO_HEADS`, `NUM_KV_HEADS`, `INV_DIM_LOG2_BASE`, `HEADS_PER_THREAD`) `— compiler folds constants per pipeline.
6. **Inline trig** (`metal::exp2` + `metal::fast::cos/sin`) — no precomputed cos/sin cache.
7. **Heads-per-thread amortisation infra** (`HEADS_PER_THREAD` fn-const, `SGLANG_RPF_N` env override). Default N=1 — kernel is launch-overhead-bound at our shapes; N>1 left for future hardware.
8. **`mlx::core::Primitive` integration** — required for kernel writes to be visible to MLX's lazy graph and downstream ops.
9. **Fused KV-pool write** — rotated K + V land in `kv_pool[slot]` in the same command buffer, eliminating the separate `pool[slots] = …` scatters that would otherwise be needed after RoPE.
10. **Zero-copy pool donation** — `copy_shared_buffer` returns the  input pool buffer as the output; the user-side handle is rebound, GPU memory is the same allocation.

### Accuracy Tests

( Adding Unit Tests ) 

E2E server test with `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B`:

| Check | Result |
|-------|--------|
| Startup log: `Custom RoPE kernel enabled` | Present |
| Single-request inference | Correct text output |
| KV pool initialized | 42165 slots × 28 layers |

### Benchmarking and Profiling

#### Kernel microbenchmark on Apple M4 Pro (48GB), Qwen3-0.6B dimensions (32 tokens, 16 Q heads, 2 KV heads, head_dim=64)

Focused local profile timing:

| Case | MLX baseline | AOT fused | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| LLaMA-like bf16 BS=512 (`nq=32`, `nk=8`, `hd=128`) | 88.13 us | 64.23 us | 1.37x |
| Qwen-like bf16 BS=512 (`nq=16`, `nk=2`, `hd=64`) | 28.22 us | 39.96 us | 0.71x |

Large-batch bf16 sweep:

| Config | MLX median | AOT fused median | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Qwen3 bf16 BS=128 | 14.56 us | 17.65 us | 0.82x |
| Qwen3 bf16 BS=256 | 16.88 us | 24.78 us | 0.68x |
| Qwen3 bf16 BS=512 | 21.40 us | 33.22 us | 0.64x |
| Qwen3 bf16 BS=1024 | 32.85 us | 38.40 us | 0.86x |
| LLaMA bf16 BS=128 | 29.21 us | 33.46 us | 0.87x |
| LLaMA bf16 BS=256 | 45.73 us | 41.07 us | 1.11x |
| LLaMA bf16 BS=512 | 79.57 us | 57.74 us | 1.38x |
| LLaMA bf16 BS=1024 | 156.89 us | 115.72 us | 1.36x |

Takeaway: this is not a universal speedup. The fused AOT path helps on larger
LLaMA-like shapes, especially larger bf16 batches, but regresses on Qwen-like
small-KV-head shapes. The PR keeps the implementation guarded and easy to A/B.

### How to Run Tests

```bash
cd /path/to/sglang
source .venv-mlx-dev/bin/activate

# Full server E2E (downloads Qwen3-0.6B on first run)
SGLANG_USE_MLX=1 python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B --port 43440 --mem-fraction-static 0.5
# Look for "Custom RoPE kernel enabled" in logs
```

title: [Diffusion] Add Qwen Image ModelOpt FP8 support
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Add ModelOpt FP8 support for Qwen Image diffusion transformers in the SGLang runtime and FP8 converter.

- make Qwen Image attention, MLP, and top-level projections quant-aware with full checkpoint prefixes
- add a Qwen Image / Qwen Image Edit BF16 fallback profile, including `transformer_blocks.*.img_mlp.net.2` after image-quality ablation
- fix the FP8 converter so explicit BF16 fallback tensors are written before ModelOpt ignore-preservation skips the source tensor
- publish clean SGLang-native ModelOpt FP8 transformer overrides under the `lmsys` Hugging Face org
- document the validated Qwen Image and Qwen Image Edit ModelOpt FP8 checkpoint flow in `docs/diffusion/quantization.md`
- update the diffusion ModelOpt quant skill with the Qwen Image FP8 fallback and converter-ordering notes
- add Qwen Image and Qwen Image Edit ModelOpt FP8 cases to the B200 diffusion CI set

- Qwen Image Edit: https://huggingface.co/lmsys/qwen-image-edit-modelopt-fp8-sglang-transformer

Both repos are intentionally clean transformer override repos: `README.md`, `config.json`, and `.safetensors` shards only.

title: Reenable MNNVL backend for FlashInfer allreduce fusion
author: wenscarl
body:
## Summary
Reintroduces FlashInfer **unified** fused allreduce + residual + RMSNorm with an explicit backend flag **`--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend`** (`auto` \| `trtllm` \| `mnnvl`), and fixes interaction with **piecewise CUDA graph** when the **MNNVL** path is used.
## Background
- Original integration: [PR #12787](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/12787).
- Reverted due to hangs (e.g. some models / CI): [PR #20792](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20792).
- Related report (fused AR + RMSNorm + piecewise graph): [vLLM #35772](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/35772).
## Problem
Hangs were correlated with **piecewise CUDA graph** capture/replay while MNNVL-style allreduce fusion was active, including configurations where the fused op was already a **torch.compile split op** relative to PCG. Reducing the number of piecewise graphs made the hang much rarer. **Eager** execution and the **decode** (non–piecewise) CUDA graph path did not reproduce the issue in our testing.
When stuck, stacks pointed to lack of progress in the Lamport-style wait loop in FlashInfer’s MNNVL allreduce implementation, e.g. [`trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh` (lines ~557–573)](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/main/include/flashinfer/comm/trtllm_mnnvl_allreduce.cuh#L557-L573), consistent with **oneshot/twoshot** progress assumptions conflicting with PCG replay.

## What this PR does
- Adds **`--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend`** and gates fusion on `flashinfer_allreduce_fusion_backend is not None` (see `communicator.py`, `server_args.py`).
- **`mnnvl`** or **`auto`** on SM100 (where MNNVL may be selected): **disables piecewise CUDA graph** in `model_runner.py` so MNNVL fusion is not replayed inside PCG; keeps `flashinfer_allreduce_residual_rmsnorm` registered as a **split op** so it runs eagerly between graph pieces.
- **`trtllm`**: removes that split-op name from PCG `split_ops` when MNNVL split is not required, so fusion can stay **in-graph** for piecewise compile.
- **Layernorm**: if FlashInfer fusion returns `(None, None)`, always performs `tensor_model_parallel_all_reduce` before RMSNorm (fixes missing allreduce on fallback).
- Deprecates **`--enable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion`**: if set with no backend, maps to `--flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend=auto` and logs a warning.
- Workspace creation uses FlashInfer **`create_allreduce_fusion_workspace`** with `backend=…`, optional `gpus_per_node`, and preserves the existing **NCCL device + GLOO cpu** `TorchDistBackend` workaround where applicable.
## Benchmarks (Gb200 4GPUs)
**Server**:
```bash
sglang serve \
  --model-path openai/gpt-oss-120b \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 \
  --reasoning-parser gpt-oss \
  --tool-call-parser gpt-oss \
  --flashinfer-allreduce-fusion-backend mnnvl or trtllm \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune
```
**Client** (`bench_serving`):
```bash
  python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --dataset-name random \
    --random-input-len 1024 \
    --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 1.0 \
    --num-prompts 128 \
    --max-concurrency ${BS} \
    --request-rate inf \
    --disable-ignore-eos
```

| Max request concurrency | MNNVL TPOT (ms) | TRT-LLM TPOT (ms) (piecewise CUDA graph) | Speedup vs TRT-LLM (piecewise CUDA graph) | TRT-LLM TPOT (ms) (without piecewise CUDA graph) | Speedup vs TRT-LLM (without piecewise CUDA graph) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 3.30 | 3.79 | 1.15x | 3.79 | 1.15x |
| 4 | 4.25 | 4.75 | 1.12x | 4.83 | 1.14x |

| 32 | 7.16 | 8.34 | 1.17x | 8.57 | 1.20x |
| 64 | 8.93 | 10.60 | 1.19x | 10.83 | 1.21x |
## Notes for reviewers
- MNNVL + PCG is treated as **unsafe** (similar policy to other non–graph-safe comm); TRT-LLM path remains the default for single-node `auto` where applicable.
- FlashInfer / topology details are documented in comments in `flashinfer_comm_fusion.py`.

```
python3 -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200

Accuracy: 0.875
Invalid: 0.020
Latency: 27.135 s
Output throughput: 2344.613 token/s
```

## How to reproduce the hang
1. Goal
You want both:

FlashInfer MNNVL (or auto on SM100 where MNNVL is chosen) for fused allreduce + residual + RMSNorm, and
Piecewise CUDA graph capture/replay still enabled (the path this PR disables in model_runner.py).
On this PR’s default code, piecewise CUDA graph is skipped when flashinfer_ar_needs_piecewise_cuda_graph_split(server_args) is true, so you will not see the hang until you relax that guard.

2. Code change (force the bad combination)
Option A — turn piecewise CUDA graph back on (most direct)

In python/sglang/srt/model_executor/model_runner.py, comment out or remove the early return that runs when flashinfer_ar_needs_piecewise_cuda_graph_split is true (the block that logs “Disable piecewise CUDA graph because MNNVL allreduce fusion is enabled”).

Option B — make the “disable PCG” helper always false

In python/sglang/srt/layers/flashinfer_comm_fusion.py, change flashinfer_ar_needs_piecewise_cuda_graph_split so it always returns False (or only returns False for your MNNVL / auto case). Then model_runner will not skip piecewise CUDA graph, while piecewise_cuda_graph_runner can still treat the fused op as a split op for MNNVL when your branch logic keeps it in split_ops.

You reported that even Option B still hung; that is why the shipped fix disables PCG entirely for MNNVL instead of relying on split-op alone.

title: perf: add --prefill-only-disable-kv-cache to skip KV pool allocation
author: jasperjiaguo
body:
## Summary

Adds an opt-in flag `--prefill-only-disable-kv-cache` that skips the physical KV cache pool allocation for prefill-only workloads. In those modes no layer ever reads or writes the KV cache — attention uses raw K/V via `flash_attn_varlen_func` — so the tens of GB of auto-sized KV buffers are pure waste.

**What "prefill-only" covers today:**
- `--is-embedding` (CausalLM-as-embedding via FA3 `fa_skip_kv_cache`)
- SequenceClassification / RewardModel / cross-encoder scoring routed through `/v1/score`'s `EmbeddingReqInput` path (which sets `is_embedding=True` internally)

**Doesn't cover yet** (writes will go to the no-op pool and `set_kv_buffer` raises): CausalLM scoring with `sampling_params.max_new_tokens=0`. That's a one-line `fa_skip_kv_cache` extension in the FA backend — a separate PR.

A new `NoOpMHATokenToKVPool(MHATokenToKVPool)` subclass:
- `_create_buffers` allocates `(page_size, head_num, head_dim)` placeholder tensors per layer (~hundreds of KB total) instead of full `(size+page_size, head_num, head_dim)` buffers. The per-page-size shape ensures the FA backend's unconditional `key_cache.view(-1, page_size, head_num, head_dim)` at the top of `forward_extend` succeeds for any `--page-size`, not just 1.
- `_finalize_allocation_log` / `get_kv_size_bytes` report zero.
- `set_kv_buffer` / `move_kv_cache` raise / no-op — they should never be reached with `fa_skip_kv_cache` active; loud failures make silent correctness bugs visible if a user enables this flag in a mode that still does decode.
- `get_key_buffer` / `get_value_buffer` / `get_kv_buffer` return the placeholder so the FA backend's read at the top of `forward_extend` (which happens before the `fa_skip_kv_cache` branch) succeeds. The returned tensor is immediately discarded because the branch below switches to raw K/V.

`__post_init__` enforces the two structural preconditions for `fa_skip_kv_cache`: `chunked_prefill_size == -1` and `disable_radix_cache`. We **deliberately don't gate on `is_embedding`** so the same skip path naturally applies to scoring and any other prefill-only workload. Misuse (e.g. enabling the flag in a mode that still decodes) surfaces loudly at the first cache write rather than corrupting outputs.

Scheduler admission is unchanged (`self.size` still reflects logical pool capacity).

## Numbers

H200 + Qwen3-0.6B FP8 embedding + production traffic distribution, `--is-embedding --chunked-prefill-size=-1 --max-prefill-tokens=32768 --enable-piecewise-cuda-graph --piecewise-cuda-graph-compiler=inductor`, RPS=45, 1 item/req, CONSTANT pace, 60s × 3 runs each:

| Config | Mean items/s | Free GPU mem |
|---|---|---|
| without flag | 37.61 | 46.8 GB |
| **with** flag | **39.97** | **135.7 GB** |

+6.3% throughput, +88.9 GB freed device memory. The throughput lift is presumably cuda allocator fragmentation / caching-allocator headroom effects; the KV pool was never hot in either config.

## Testing Done

- [x] Engine boots cleanly with the flag
- [x] `KV Cache skipped (no-op pool). ... physical K/V size: ~112.0 KB placeholder` in the log, `avail mem=135.73 GB` (vs 46.81 GB baseline)
- [x] `POST /v1/embeddings` returns valid embeddings
- [x] 3× 60s production-distribution bench completes at 38.70 / 40.21 / 41.01 items/s, no scheduler exceptions
- [x] `__post_init__` validation rejects: `--chunked-prefill-size != -1` or missing `--disable-radix-cache`
- [x] Placeholder size scales with `--page-size` so the FA backend's view operation works for any page configuration

title: [MoE] Deprecate act_and_mul_triton; fold filter_expert into JIT silu/gelu_and_mul
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

`act_and_mul_triton` (in `fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`) duplicates `silu_and_mul` / `gelu_and_mul`. The only difference is that it skips rows whose routed expert id is `-1` (the `filter_expert=True` MoE path used under EP). The JIT CUDA `silu_and_mul` / `gelu_and_mul` kernels already exist and are faster — the consolidation removes ~100 lines of Triton and a redundant kernel.

## Modifications

**JIT activation kernel (CUDA)**
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/elementwise/activation.cuh`: added `expert_ids` (`const int32_t*`) and `expert_step` (`uint32_t`) to `ActivationParams`; added a compile-time `kFilterExpert` template bool to `act_and_mul_kernel` (zero overhead when off — `if constexpr` skips the load); exposed `run_activation_filtered` host method.
- `python/sglang/jit_kernel/activation.py`: `silu_and_mul` / `gelu_and_mul` / `gelu_tanh_and_mul` / `run_activation` now accept optional `expert_ids` and `expert_step` kwargs. Existing call sites are unchanged.

**MoE call sites (`triton_utils/fused_moe.py`)**
- Replaced both `act_and_mul_triton(...)` calls with `silu_and_mul` / `gelu_and_mul` passing `expert_ids` and `expert_step`.
- **CUDA**: filter_expert path → JIT kernel with `expert_ids` (skips filtered rows).
- **HIP / XPU**: filter_expert path → AOT `sgl_kernel.silu_and_mul/gelu_and_mul` (unfiltered). The downstream fused MoE down kernel writes zeros for filtered experts and `return`s before reading the activation input (`fused_moe_triton_kernels.py:192–208`), so writing real output to those rows is harmless. This avoids exposing the JIT activation kernel to AMD users for the first time in this PR.

**Removed**
- `act_and_mul_kernel` (Triton) and `act_and_mul_triton` wrapper, plus the now-unused `_apply_activation` and `tanh` helpers in `fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`.

**Tests** (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_activation.py`)
- Added `test_activation_filter_expert` parametrized over op × dtype × shape × `expert_step ∈ {1, 16}` (per-token and sorted/TMA routing).
- Added `test_activation_filter_expert_all_skipped` and `test_activation_filter_expert_none_skipped` edge cases (the latter asserts bit-exact equality with the unfiltered path).

**Benchmark** (`python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/bench_activation.py`)
- Added `benchmark_filter` comparing the filtered JIT path vs the unfiltered baseline across batch × dim × skip ratio.

## Accuracy Tests

`pytest python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/test_activation.py` — **348 passed in 23s** (135 pre-existing + 213 new filter_expert).

The `none_skipped` test asserts bit-exact equality between the filtered kernel (with all expert_ids = 0) and the unfiltered kernel, so the filter machinery does not perturb the math.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The new filter benchmark (`bench_activation.py::benchmark_filter`, bf16):

| op   | dim  | bs    | skip | Unfiltered (μs) | Filtered (μs) |
|------|------|-------|------|----------------:|--------------:|
| silu | 8192 | 1024  | 0.00 | 30.26           | 29.85         |
| silu | 8192 | 1024  | 0.25 | 30.27           | 23.87         |
| silu | 8192 | 1024  | 0.50 | 30.26           | 16.13         |
| silu | 4096 | 16384 | 0.00 | 213.89          | 213.63        |
| silu | 4096 | 16384 | 0.25 | 213.86          | 162.16        |
| silu | 4096 | 16384 | 0.50 | 213.83          | 110.20        |
| gelu | 8192 | 1024  | 0.50 | 29.96           | 16.63         |
| gelu | 4096 | 16384 | 0.50 | 214.03          | 116.92        |

- At `skip_ratio=0`: filter overhead is bounded (≤ ~0.3μs absolute, negligible at large shapes — e.g. 213.89 → 213.63μs).
- At `skip_ratio>0`: work scales linearly with skipped rows, exactly as expected.

Compared to the deleted Triton `act_and_mul_triton` kernel (measured against a local copy before removal), the JIT path is ~2–3× faster in the launch-bound regime (small/medium batches, the regime MoE expert tiles hit during decode) and within ±5% at HBM-bandwidth-bound shapes.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Notes for reviewers

- **AMD/HIP coverage**: The JIT activation kernel still has no AMD CI suite (the `pr-test-jit-kernel.yml` workflow runs only `--hw cuda`). To avoid making this PR a "first run on AMD" gamble, the HIP filter_expert path falls back to the unfiltered AOT `sgl_kernel` kernel and accepts the small wasted compute on filtered rows. A follow-up PR registering `test_activation.py` on AMD CI would let us route HIP filter_expert through the JIT kernel too.
- The PR deletes `_apply_activation` and `tanh` from `fused_moe_triton_kernels.py` — these had no other callers (verified via grep across the repo).

title: :sparkles: [llm][npu][quant] Add W4A4 MXFP4 quantization support for Qwen3 Dense on Ascend NPU
author: TallMessiWu
body:
# Summary

Adds **MXFP4 W4A4** quantization (4-bit weights + 4-bit activations) for Qwen3 / Qwen3.5 **dense** LLM models on Ascend NPU, continuing the NPU quantization work tracked in #21584. The **online** path uses **dual-level** MXFP4; the **offline** msmodelslim path is single-level.

> **Rebased onto latest `main`.** The two prerequisite PRs this built on — #22352 (W8A8 MXFP8) and #23650 (W4A8 MXFP4) — are now **merged**, so this PR contains only the W4A4 delta and reuses their merged infrastructure (`_NPULinearMethodBase`, the lazy `_get_float4_e2m1fn_x2_dtype()` helper, `npu_format_cast`, `ModelSlimLinearScheme`, `ModelSlimConfig.get_linear_scheme`).

Two modes are supported:

**Online quantization (`--quantization mxfp4`)**

- On the **Ascend NPU** backend, `mxfp4` dispatches to the new `Mxfp4W4A4Config` → `NPUDualLevelMXFP4LinearMethod`. On GPU/CPU the same flag still resolves to the upstream OCP `Mxfp4Config` (MoE) — the split is done purely at registration time (the NPU config is registered only inside the `is_npu()` block of `layers/quantization/__init__.py`, mirroring `GPTQAscendConfig`), so there is no collision and the upstream config is untouched.
- The online path uses **dual-level** MXFP4: at load, BF16/FP16 weights are quantised via `npu_dynamic_dual_level_mx_quant` to packed FP4 plus a fine FP8 (E4M3) **L0** block scale and a coarser **L1** scale, and the weight is cast to `FRACTAL_NZ`. At inference, activations are dynamically quantised the same way and the matmul runs via `npu_dual_level_quant_matmul`.
- **Why dual-level:** an earlier single-level online path (RTN with UE8M0 power-of-2 block scales) lost enough precision that greedy long-form decoding could degenerate into loops that never emit EOS. The dual-level FP8 L0 scale captures per-block dynamic range far more accurately, which removes that failure and lands online accuracy on par with (slightly ahead of) the calibrated offline checkpoint. Requires Ascend 950 (A5) — the `DualLevelQuantBatchMatmul` op is unavailable on A2/A3.

**Offline quantization (msmodelslim pre-quantized weights, `--quantization modelslim`)**

- `W4A4_MXFP4` checkpoints are auto-detected (via `quant_model_description.json`) and handled by `ModelSlimMXFP4Scheme`, which delegates weight post-processing + matmul to `NPUSingleLevelMXFP4OfflineLinearMethod` (`self.kernel`).
- The checkpoint stores weights as `float8_e4m3fn [out, in]` (one FP4 value per byte, fp8 as container) + `uint8` E8M0 scales `[out, in/32]`. At load they are re-packed to `float4_e2m1fn_x2` (2 FP4/byte, `[out, in//2]`) and transposed; the single-level scale is reshaped to 3D and the matmul runs via `npu_quant_matmul(x1_dtype = x2_dtype = float4_e2m1fn_x2, group_sizes=[1, 1, 32])`. Because the checkpoint ships single-level UE8M0 scales, the offline path is single-level and uses a **different matmul kernel** from the dual-level online path.

# Benchmark Results

Validated end-to-end on Ascend A5 hardware. Both W4A4 modes (online dual-level and offline msmodelslim single-level) are compared against the BF16 baseline.

## Performance

Online W4A4 delivers **~+41% throughput** and **~-29% latency** over BF16; the offline single-level path is a bit faster (**~+49% / ~-32%**), since dual-level trades some throughput for the finer L0 scales.

| Metric | BF16 (avg, min–max) | Online W4A4 (avg, min–max) | vs BF16 | Offline W4A4 (avg, min–max) | vs BF16 |
|--------|---------------------|-----------------------------|---------|-----------------------------|---------|
| **Request Throughput (req/s)** | 5.29 (4.61–5.63) | 7.45 (7.37–7.55) | **↑ +40.8%** | 7.87 (7.50–8.08) | **↑ +48.8%** |
| **Total Token Throughput (tok/s)** | 3195.54 (2785.43–3402.36) | 4507.91 (4460.16–4566.13) | **↑ +41.1%** | 4758.92 (4536.85–4887.02) | **↑ +48.9%** |
| **Output Token Throughput (tok/s)** | 1117.66 (974.22–1189.99) | 1576.66 (1559.96–1597.02) | **↑ +41.1%** | 1664.45 (1586.78–1709.25) | **↑ +48.9%** |
| **Mean E2E Latency (ms)** | 5753.31 (5333.75–6581.71) | 4104.58 (4045.68–4152.14) | **↓ -28.7%** | 3893.88 (3783.73–4088.84) | **↓ -32.3%** |
| **Median E2E Latency (ms)** | 4190.66 (3750.52–4973.08) | 2898.55 (2868.76–2931.64) | **↓ -30.8%** | 2744.72 (2684.69–2795.60) | **↓ -34.5%** |
| **P99 E2E Latency (ms)** | 21615.96 (19830.34–25060.68) | 15540.93 (15110.64–15855.10) | **↓ -28.1%** | 14908.88 (14483.17–15642.32) | **↓ -31.0%** |
| **Mean TTFT (ms)** | 231.42 (162.34–367.42) | 157.01 (156.28–158.33) | **↓ -32.2%** | 150.76 (138.94–172.86) | **↓ -34.9%** |
| **Median TTFT (ms)** | 97.57 (96.47–98.57) | 91.80 (91.00–93.25) | **↓ -5.9%** | 92.93 (92.40–93.50) | **↓ -4.8%** |
| **Mean TPOT (ms)** | 26.62 (24.68–30.47) | 18.88 (18.53–19.27) | **↓ -29.1%** | 17.83 (17.44–18.38) | **↓ -33.0%** |
| **Median TPOT (ms)** | 25.13 (24.70–25.96) | 18.93 (18.70–19.29) | **↓ -24.7%** | 17.67 (17.49–17.86) | **↓ -29.7%** |

## Accuracy (GSM8K)

Three runs per configuration. Both W4A4 modes stay within ~1.6–1.9 points of the BF16 baseline; online dual-level is marginally ahead of the offline single-level path.

| Config | Run 1 | Run 2 | Run 3 | Avg | vs BF16 |
|--------|-------|-------|-------|-----|---------|
| **BF16 (baseline)** | 95.53 | 95.22 | 95.22 | **95.32** | — |
| **Online W4A4** | 94.16 | 93.40 | 93.71 | **93.76** | **-1.56 (-1.6%)** |
| **Offline W4A4** | 93.33 | 93.48 | 93.63 | **93.48** | **-1.84 (-1.9%)** |

# Style / consistency with #23650

This PR follows the same refactored conventions as the merged W4A8 PR:

- All NPU ops go through `torch.ops.npu.*`; **no top-level `import torch_npu`**, no `current_platform` guards (module stays importable on CUDA/CPU/AMD/XPU CI).
- The packed-FP4 dtype is resolved from the shared lazy `_get_float4_e2m1fn_x2_dtype()` helper — the `torch_npu.float4_e2m1fn_x2` int enum, **not** the `torch.float4_e2m1fn_x2` dtype object, which recent op-plugin builds reject.
- Device-agnostic config with per-device dispatch (`is_npu()` branch + `NotImplementedError` elsewhere); the offline scheme subclasses `ModelSlimLinearScheme` and delegates to a `self.kernel` kernel, registered in `get_linear_scheme`'s `linear_quant_schemes` list.

# Files Changed

**New**

| ---- | ------ |
| `srt/layers/quantization/npu_mxfp4_w4a4.py` | `Mxfp4W4A4Config` (online W4A4, `get_name() == "mxfp4"`, NPU-dispatched to the dual-level method) |
| `srt/layers/quantization/modelslim/schemes/modelslim_mxfp4.py` | offline `ModelSlimMXFP4Scheme` for `W4A4_MXFP4` |

**Modified**

| ---- | ------ |
| `srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/linear_method_npu.py` | add `NPUDualLevelMXFP4LinearMethod` (online, dual-level), `NPUSingleLevelMXFP4LinearMethod` (single-level base) + `NPUSingleLevelMXFP4OfflineLinearMethod` (offline, subclasses the single-level base) |

| `docs_new/docs/advanced_features/quantization.mdx`, `docs_new/docs/hardware-platforms/ascend-npus/ascend_npu_quantization.mdx` | document W4A4 (Ascend row + prose) |

# Status

Implementation complete, lint-clean, and **validated end-to-end on Ascend A5 hardware** (see Benchmark Results above). Both online (`--quantization mxfp4`) and offline (`--quantization modelslim`) paths were run against a BF16 baseline for throughput/latency and GSM8K accuracy.

# Related Issues

Part of #21584 (MXFP8/MXFP4 support on Ascend NPU for Qwen3 dense LLM). Builds on #22352 and #23650 (both merged).

title: [NPU] Support shared expert dual stream optimization
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

On NPU, the shared expert and routed expert in MoE models are executed sequentially on the same stream, leaving compute resources underutilized. This PR introduces a dual stream optimization that overlaps shared expert computation with routed expert computation on independent NPU streams.

## Modifications

- Added `shared_expert_on_independent_stream` in `cmo.py` to offload shared expert computation to independent NPU streams with dedicated core allocation (8 cores).
- Modified `Qwen2MoeModel._forward_deepep` to execute shared expert and routed expert on separate streams in parallel when `SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM` is enabled during CUDA graph mode.

## Accuracy Tests

```
# shared expert stream
export SGLANG_NPU_USE_MULTI_STREAM=1

MODEL_PATH=/home/weights/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
        --model-path ${MODEL_PATH} \
        --attention-backend ascend \
        --device npu \
        --tp-size 4 --nnodes 1 --node-rank 0 \
        --chunked-prefill-size -1 --max-prefill-tokens 16384 \
        --trust-remote-code \
        --host 127.0.0.1 --max-running-requests 128 \
        --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
        --port 9903 \
        --mm-attention-backend ascend_attn --max-total-tokens 800000 \
        --dtype bfloat16 --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \
        --base-gpu-id 4 \
        --enable-multimodal \
        --disable-radix-cache \
        --dp-size 2 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
        --speculative-algorithm NEXTN --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
        --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \
        --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode auto \
        --cuda-graph-bs 8 12 16 20 24 32 40 48 56 64 \
```

```
+-----------------+-----------+----------+----------+-------+---------+---------+
| Model           | Dataset   | Metric   | Subset   |   Num |   Score | Cat.0   |
+=================+===========+==========+==========+=======+=========+=========+
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | gsm8k     | mean_acc | main     |   256 |  0.9766 | default |
+-----------------+-----------+----------+----------+-------+---------+---------+
+-----------------+-----------+----------+------------------------------------------+-------+---------+----------------+
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B | ceval     | mean_acc | OVERALL                                  |  1346 |  0.893  | -              |
+-----------------+-----------+----------+------------------------------------------+-------+---------+----------------+
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Benchmarked on Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, 128 concurrent requests:

throughput (req/s) | 1.72 | 1.91 | +11.0%

Mean E2E Latency (ms) | 57695 | 52973 | -8.2%

title: [perf] cherry-pick #22911: support return_routed_experts with overlap scheduling
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Motivation

Cherry-pick of upstream PR #22911 ([perf] support return_routed_experts with overlap scheduling, commit `c5603268`) onto the `sglang-miles` branch.

Previously, the routed-experts capture path issued a synchronous device-to-host copy inside the forward step (`out_cache_loc.cpu()` + `device_cache.buffer[...].cpu()`), which forced the GPU to drain and broke the overlap scheduler. This made `--return-routed-experts` unusable in overlap mode.

## Modifications

- Add `RoutedExpertsOutput` dataclass that holds GPU tensors plus a reference to the host cache, with `copy_to_cpu()` (called inside the forward stream before `copy_done.record()`) and `finalize()` (called after `copy_done.synchronize()`).
- Refactor `_RoutedExpertsCapturerReal` to extract `_get_local_range` and add `_prepare_routed_experts_output`; `on_forward_end` now takes `no_copy_to_cpu=False` and returns an `Optional[RoutedExpertsOutput]`.
- In `model_runner.py`, set `no_copy_to_cpu = not server_args.disable_overlap_schedule` so the deferred path is used whenever overlap is enabled, and surface the result on `ModelRunnerOutput.routed_experts_output`.
- Plumb `routed_experts_output` through `GenerationBatchResult`, `TpModelWorker`, and both `EAGLEWorkerV2` / `MultiLayerEagleWorkerV2`.
- In `SchedulerOutputProcessorMixin`, after `copy_done.synchronize()`, call `routed_experts_output.finalize()` and clear the field.

### Conflict resolution

Resolved conflicts in `routed_experts_capturer.py` and `model_runner.py` to keep the following miles-side changes on top of upstream's `_get_local_range` / `no_copy_to_cpu` refactor:
- Draft-worker guard around `on_forward_end` (`if not self.is_draft_worker:`).
- `bs * num_tokens_per_bs` cuda_graph token-count fix for spec decoding.
- DeepEP all-gather path: skip DP-rank slicing when DeepEP is enabled (the `is_dp_attention_enabled() and not get_moe_a2a_backend().is_deepep()` guard).

## Accuracy Tests

Router replay accuracy test (`test_return_routed_experts`) passes 3/3 with **0 mismatches across ~26.7M expert IDs**.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

H200 TP=4, Qwen3-30B-A3B, batch=64, in=1024, out=512:

| Mode | Output throughput |
|---|---|
| Before (sync DtoH inside forward) | 7453.48 tok/s |
| After (deferred copy via `RoutedExpertsOutput`) | **8609.21 tok/s** |

→ **+15.5%** end-to-end output throughput with `--return-routed-experts` enabled in overlap mode.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Refactor] Cuda Graph Runner/Backend Refactor
author: Oasis-Git
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/23004 

## Modifications

### Runner ↔ CudaGraphBackend Interaction (cg-refactor)

Two layers are in scope:

- **Phase runner** — `PrefillCudaGraphRunner` / `DecodeCudaGraphRunner`
  - Both subclass `BaseCudaGraphRunner`
  - Exactly one runner per phase
  - Fixed implementation

- **CG backend** — `BaseCudaGraphBackend` and its subclasses:
  - `FullCudaGraphBackend`
  - `BreakableCudaGraphBackend`
  - `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend`
  - Pluggable per phase
  - Selected at initialization by:
    - `resolve_prefill_backend(model_runner)`
    - `resolve_decode_backend(model_runner)`
  - Backend type comes from:
    - `cuda_graph_config[phase].backend`

---

### Phase Runner API (`BaseCudaGraphRunner`)

Exposed upward to `ModelRunner`.

Each method delegates strategy-specific behavior to `self.backend`.

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `can_run(forward_batch) -> bool` | Determine whether the current batch can use a captured graph. Performs runner-level filtering before consulting the backend. |
| `capture()` | One-time capture entrypoint. Enumerates all capture shapes and invokes `capture_one_shape()` for each. |
| `capture_one_shape(size, ...)` | Captures a single shape. Builds a dummy forward batch and delegates actual capture to `self.backend.capture_one(...)`. |
| `replay_prepare(forward_batch, **kwargs) -> ForwardBatch` | Pads or reshapes inputs to match a captured shape and returns the static batch used during replay. |
| `replay(forward_batch, ...) -> ModelOutput` | Executes the captured graph via `self.backend.replay(...)`. |

---

### CG Backend API (`BaseCudaGraphBackend`)

Exposed downward to the phase runner.

| Method | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `prepare(runner)` | One-time setup against the owning runner. Wires static buffers, patches the model module, and installs forward hooks. |
| `setup_prefill_state(runner)` *(prefill only)* | Additional one-time initialization for prefill-specific state. |
| `can_run(forward_batch) -> bool` | Strategy-specific runtime gate. Examples: BCG rejects sparse-DP batches; TcPiecewise checks `torch.compile` state. |
| `capture_session(stream)` *(context manager)* | Wraps the entire capture phase. Sets graph-pool ID, capture flags, allocator hints, etc. |
| `capture_one(num_tokens, ...)` | Captures a single shape. The runner provides the dummy batch; the backend performs warmup and recorded forward execution. |
| `has_shape(shape_key) -> bool` | Returns whether a recorded graph exists for the given shape. Used by `runner.can_run()`. |
| `runtime_session()` *(context manager)* | Wraps a replay execution. Sets replay flags, locks caches, and scopes graph resources. |
| `replay(shape_key, forward_batch) -> ModelOutput` | Executes the recorded graph corresponding to the shape key. |
| `populate_prefill_dummy_inputs(...)` *(prefill only)* | Fills capture-time placeholders so recorded graphs observe stable input addresses. |
| `commit_prefill_serving_inputs(forward_batch)` *(prefill only)* | Copies real serving inputs into static buffers immediately before replay. |
| `cleanup()` | Releases graph pools and removes any model patching. |

---

### Runner → Backend Interaction

#### Initialization

Once per runner:

    runner.init
    └─ self.backend = resolve_{prefill,decode}_backend(model_runner)
       ├─ self.backend.prepare(self)
       └─ prefill only:
          └─ self.backend.setup_prefill_state(self)

---

#### Capture

Once, across all capture shapes:

    runner.capture()
    └─ with backend.capture_session(stream):
       └─ for size in capture_shapes:
          └─ runner.capture_one_shape(size)
             ├─ build dummy forward_batch
             │  └─ runner-owned logic
             ├─ prefill only:
             │  └─ backend.populate_prefill_dummy_inputs(...)
             └─ backend.capture_one(num_tokens, ...)
                └─ warmup + recorded forward

---

#### Replay

Per forward, on the hot path:

    ModelRunner.forward(batch)
    ├─ if not runner.can_run(batch):
    │  └─ fall back to eager
    │
    │     runner.can_run() internally consults:
    │     - backend.has_shape(...)
    │     - backend.can_run(...)
    │
    ├─ static_batch = runner.replay_prepare(batch)
    │  └─ prefill only:
    │     └─ backend.commit_prefill_serving_inputs(batch)
    │
    └─ with backend.runtime_session():
       └─ output = backend.replay(shape_key, static_batch)

---

### Backend-Specific Overrides

| Backend | Capture mechanism | Distinct overrides |
|---|---|---|
| `FullCudaGraphBackend` | `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` over the entire model forward | `capture_session()`, `capture_one()`, `replay()` |
| `BreakableCudaGraphBackend` | Multiple `torch.cuda.CUDAGraph` segments stitched at `eager_on_graph` breakpoints | `capture_one()`, `replay()`, plus per-segment metadata in `attn_metadata_buffers` |
| `TcPiecewiseCudaGraphBackend` | `torch.compile(mode="reduce-overhead")` with FX-level piecewise splits | `prepare()` installs compile hooks; `capture_one()` drives `torch.compile` warmup; no direct graph replay recording because `torch.compile` owns execution |

---

### Where the Seam Matters

The runner/backend boundary is the extensibility point.

Adding a new CUDA Graph strategy requires:

1. Creating a new `BaseCudaGraphBackend` subclass.
2. Registering it in the backend factory.

The phase runner code should remain unchanged.

This refactor replaces the previous design where each strategy required its own runner implementation.

The strict API contract is the runner call points listed above. If a new strategy requires additional coordination, the corresponding hook should be added to `BaseCudaGraphBackend` so that all runners can drive the strategy uniformly.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

2. `cuda graph runner` to `runner`

title: [AMD] Replace fp8 mla with fp8 mha kernel for diffusion model aiter backend
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation
Dependency: https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/2911 (merged)
The original FP8 prefill path in the AITer backend temporarily used the MLA prefill ASM kernel to get FP8 attention running on MI350 series for Wan 2.2. Switching to the proper FP8 FMHA ASM kernel fmha_fwd_hd128_fp8_gfx950 removes extra padding, the head-divisibility constraint, and the whole metadata-building scaffolding. That FMHA path natively supports MHA with q/k/v head_dim == 128 and applies to Wan 2.2 as well as other diffusion models’ self- and cross-attention shapes.

| Aspect | Before — MLA prefill ASM (`mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`) | After — FMHA FP8 ASM (`aiter.flash_attn_fp8_pertensor_func`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Q/K head dim | `qk_head_dim = 192` hard-coded in the binary; Wan's 128 had to be **zero-padded 128 → 192** on every call (extra memory + bandwidth) | `q_head_dim = k_head_dim = 128` natively; **no padding** |
| Head-tiling constraint | Tiles 8 heads at a time (`m32x8`); `num_heads` **must be divisible by 8**, so Ulysses SP degree=4 on 40 heads (→ 10/rank) crashed with OOB reads | No head-divisibility constraint; **Ulysses SP=4 on 40-head models works** |
| `torch.compile` compatibility | `@torch.compiler.disable` required on the wrapper (Python-side metadata construction breaks Dynamo) | Decorator removed; **path is Dynamo-friendly** |

## Modifications

`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/layers/attention/backends/aiter.py`:

- **Removed** the MLA prefill code path:
  - `_can_use_mla_prefill(...)`
  - `_build_mla_prefill_metadata(...)` (persistent-scheduling metadata builder for `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd`)
  - `_mla_prefill_ps_attention(...)` (varlen reshape + Q/K zero-pad-to-192 + `mla_prefill_ps_asm_fwd` + `mla_reduce_v1`)
- **Added** the FMHA FP8 prefill code path:
  - `_FMHA_FP8_HEAD_DIM = 128` constant.
  - `_can_use_fmha_fp8_prefill(q_head_dim, k_head_dim, v_head_dim, num_heads, num_kv_heads)` — gates on `_use_aiter_gfx95`, full MHA (`num_kv_heads == num_heads`), and `q == k == v == 128`.
- **Restriction Update**:
   - Drops the `num_heads % 8 == 0` constraint, unblocking Ulysses SP degree=4 for 40-head models.
   - No more `F.pad` of Q/K on the hot path.
   - The `@torch.compiler.disable` decorator on `AITerImpl.forward` (no longer needed since the new path doesn't go through Python-side metadata construction that breaks Dynamo).

## Accuracy Tests
Kernel unit test pass

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Image: rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.10.post1-rocm700-mi35x-20260426
Wan 2.2 T2V, 1MI355

### Per-kernel
| Path | Kernel | Time (us) | Subtotal (us) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** (MLA prefill + reduce) | `aiter::mla_pfl_qh192_vh128_m32x8_n128x1_causal0` | 87,409.1 | |
|                                   | `_Z19kn_mla_reduce_v1_...` (`mla_reduce_v1`)      | 4.4      | **87,413.5** |
| **After** (this PR, FMHA FP8)     | `_ZN5aiter24fmha_fwd_hd128_fp8_gfx950E`           | 78,006.2 | **78,006.2** |


### End-to-end
Stage-level wallclock for one full Wan 2.2 T2V run, FP8 attention path:
| Path | Encoding (s) | Denoising (s) | Decoding (s) | Total (s) |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Before** (FP8 MLA prefill, with 128→192 pad + `mla_reduce_v1`) | 4.34 | 96.90 | 11.80 | **113.04** |
| **After**  (this PR, FP8 FMHA `hd128` pertensor)                 | 4.41 | 81.28 | 11.79 | **97.48**  |

title: support asymmetric pd-mtp via mock spec hidden
author: hnyls2002
body:
Always size the PD MetadataBuffers hidden_states buffer to model_config.spec_hidden_size on both prefill and decode (instead of conditional on local --speculative-algorithm). This unblocks asymmetric P/D configs where prefill runs no spec module but decode runs EAGLE/MTP: prefill ships a zero-initialized buffer that decode consumes as mock conditioning for the first draft step. Verified spec decoding keeps the output token correct -- only the first decode iteration's accept length is affected (~ < 1% throughput hit on long generations).

Cost: when neither side runs spec, the buffer is allocated but unused (~few MB). The alternative is a wire-protocol size mismatch on asymmetric configs.

Test: test_dsv4_pd_disagg_nixl.py uses asymmetric config (prefill TP-only, decode TP+DP+EAGLE), no new server arg required. Follow-up to #23918.

title: (1/n - prefill optimize)feat(lora): enable csgmv backend with virtual experts for MoE LoRA
author: yushengsu-thu
body:
## Summary

- Remove the assertion that restricted `--lora-use-virtual-experts` to triton-only. The virtual experts path uses its own triton kernel (`merged_experts_fused_moe_lora_add`) independent of the dense-LoRA backend, so csgmv is fully compatible.
- Fix CUDA graph crash when using `--lora-backend csgmv --lora-use-virtual-experts` by adding per-request segment info (`req_seg_indptr`, `req_weight_indices`) to `LoRABatchInfo`. The csgmv backend's chunked-segment semantics differ from what MoE virtual experts expect (per-request), causing garbage token-to-adapter mappings and device-side asserts.

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `server_args.py` | Remove triton-only assertion for `--lora-use-virtual-experts` |
| `lora/utils.py` | Add `req_seg_indptr` and `req_weight_indices` fields to `LoRABatchInfo` |
| `lora/backend/chunked_backend.py` | csgmv backend computes and stores per-request segment info (incl. CUDA graph pre-allocation) |
| `lora/layers.py` | MoE LoRA `_get_lora_info` uses per-request fields when available |

## Benchmark Results (Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP=4, GB300, in=1024, out=2048)

| BS | triton (e2e tps) | csgmv (e2e tps) | csgmv vs triton |
|----|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|
| 1 | 201.0/s | 205.5/s | **102.2%** |
| 128 | 2753.3/s | 2800.3/s | **101.7%** |
| 512 | 2758.7/s | 2807.6/s | **101.8%** |

csgmv matches triton throughput (~1.7-2.2% faster) since MoE LoRA uses the same virtual experts triton kernel regardless of the dense-LoRA backend.

## Accuracy

| Metric | Value |
|--------|-------|
| KL(sglang, trainer) | 0.00392 |
| KL(orig_sampler, trainer) | 0.00424 |
| KL(sglang, orig_sampler) | 0.00497 |

Accuracy verified — sglang csgmv+virtual_experts output closely matches the training reference (lower KL than the original sampler).

## Test plan

- [x] CUDA graph capture succeeds with csgmv + virtual experts

title: [core/loader] Add presharded load format
author: ch-wan
body:
## Motivation

Initial weight loading + quantization processing for large MoE models (e.g., DeepSeek-V2 family with `--quantization fp8`, DeepSeek-V3, DeepSeek-V4-Pro with mxfp4) is expensive and re-runs every time the engine starts with the same parallelism + quantization config. This PR introduces a `presharded` load format that caches the post-`process_weights_after_loading` state on disk so subsequent runs skip the source-shard iteration, the model-specific `post_load_weights` conversion, and the quant-method `process_weights_after_loading` reshape on real data.

## Modifications

New `--load-format presharded` (`LoadFormat.PRESHARDED`). Behavior:

- **First run (dump)**: each rank loads weights normally, runs `post_load_weights`, runs `process_weights_after_loading` to materialize the inference-ready layout, then ranks coordinate to dump a per-rank deduplicated safetensors set under `<model_path>/presharded/<config subfolder>/`.
- **Subsequent runs (reload)** with the same config: each rank initializes the model, runs `process_weights_after_loading` once on uninitialized parameters purely to materialize post-process shapes, then multi-thread reads only the files it needs and `copy_`s dumped values in. Source ckpt is not iterated; `post_load_weights` is not re-run on real data.

Subfolder name is derived from a structural signature over TP/DP/EP/PP, quantization, dtype, EPLB, expert location, and related knobs (e.g. `TP-8-sig-…`).

### Algorithm (rank-coordinated dump)

1. Each rank hashes every tensor in its post-process state with **xxh3-128** over `(shape, dtype, raw little-endian bytes)` and writes a small JSON manifest. CUDA tensors use pinned streaming D2H so multi-GB weights never need a single contiguous host allocation. Hashing is multi-threaded (`hash_num_threads`, default 8); xxhash releases the GIL.
2. Rank 0 reads all manifests, deduplicates by content digest, groups by rank-list signature, and bin-packs into files of at most 20 GiB (balanced across writers). Rank 0 also computes a **per-rank aggregate checksum**: sum (mod 2^64) of per-tensor 64-bit folds of `xxh3(name + ":" + content_digest)`. The plan is published as `checksum.json`.
3. Each rank writes the files it owns (`model-…-common.safetensors` / `model-…-rank-….safetensors`).
4. After a final barrier, rank 0 writes a **`READY`** sentinel last so concurrent readers never observe a half-written dump.

### Reload path (efficiency)

- **Default `verify_on_load=false`**: pure multi-thread safetensors → device `copy_` (no content re-hash).
- **`verify_on_load=true`**: re-hash loaded tensors with xxh3 and compare the rank aggregate against `rank_checksums`.
- **Multi-thread I/O**: same knobs as the HF path — `enable_multithread_load` (default true) and `num_threads` (default 8). Workers only do disk→CPU reads; GPU apply stays on the main thread. Sliding window bounds host RAM to ~`num_threads` in-flight files.
- **No mid-load `empty_cache`**: params are filled with in-place `copy_`, so the caching allocator does not grow file-by-file. One sync + `empty_cache` at end of load matches `DefaultModelLoader`. Per-file `empty_cache` previously dominated large MoE reloads (hundreds of shards).

### Capture timing — why post-process

State is captured **after** both `model.load_weights` (so model-specific `post_load_weights` has run) **and** layer-level `quant_method.process_weights_after_loading` (so e.g. mxfp4 expert weights are already packed).

Reload reproduces the layout by running `process_weights_after_loading` on the initialized model *before* copying dumped values. The transform depends only on shape, not values. Non-`nn.Parameter` Tensor attributes installed by `post_load_weights` (`w_kc`, `w_vc`, `compressor.freqs_cis`, …) are persisted as extras and reinstalled via `setattr`. GemmaRMSNorm non-persistent `gemma_weight` and GDN Parameter aliases are refreshed/rebound after copy.

Post-process capture also avoids memory doubling on large quant models (e.g. DeepSeek-V4-Pro mxfp4: pre-process ~283 GB vs post-process ~223 GB per rank).

### Optional extra-config knobs (`--model-loader-extra-config`)

| Key | Default | Meaning |
|-----|---------|---------|
| `presharded_path` | under model path | Override dump/load directory |
| `max_file_bytes` | 20 GiB | Per-file cap |
| `hash_num_threads` | 8 | Parallel hash workers (dump / optional verify) |
| `verify_on_load` | **false** | Re-hash and check rank checksums |
| `enable_multithread_load` | true | Multi-thread file I/O on reload (and first-time HF load) |
| `num_threads` | 8 | Worker count for multi-thread load |

## Accuracy Tests

**DeepSeek-V4-Pro mxfp4, TP=4 EP=4 DP-attn, 4×GB300**: full param-hash diff between baseline (`--load-format auto`) and presharded reload with `verify_on_load=true`, hashing every `state_dict` entry **and** every non-`nn.Parameter` Tensor attr installed by `post_load_weights`. Result: **9288/9288 params bit-identical across all 4 ranks**.

Also verified on DeepSeek-Coder-V2-Lite-Instruct across TP/quant configs and on Qwen3.5 (including GDN / GemmaRMSNorm rebind) with matching generation text after reload.

Plan corruption (flipping one byte of `rank_checksums["0"]`) is correctly detected when `verify_on_load=true`.

## Speed Tests

Method (unless noted): **weight-load only** — no warmup generate, `disable_cuda_graph=True`, `max_total_tokens=10000`. Metric: scheduler `Load weight end. elapsed=` (max across ranks). Hardware: 8×H200. Reload uses default `verify_on_load=false`. Dump is one-time (source load + hash + write).

### DeepSeek-V3-0324 FP8, TP=8 (~642 GB source, 632 GB presharded)

| Phase | Weight (s) | vs auto |
|-------|----------:|--------:|
| auto (source) | 53.9 | 1.0× |
| **presharded reload** | **16.0** | **3.4× faster** |
| first-time dump (earlier run) | ~501 | one-time |

Rank spread on reload: 15.0–16.0 s (tight). Earlier serial + per-file `empty_cache` path was ~160 s on the same dump — multi-thread I/O + dropping mid-load `empty_cache` recover the win.

### Main matrix (12/12 OK)

| Case | Dump wt (s) | Reload wt (s) | Auto wt (s) | Auto/Reload |
|------|------------:|--------------:|------------:|------------:|
| llama32-tp1 | 4.22 | **0.60** | 1.09 | **1.82×** |
| llama32-tp2 | 2.92 | **0.41** | 0.76 | **1.85×** |
| llama32-tp1-fp32lm | 4.05 | **0.59** | 1.11 | **1.88×** |

| dsv2-tp2-dense1 | 24.29 | **3.04** | 6.33 | **2.08×** |

All reloads hit the presharded cache.

### Additional configs (13/18 full OK)

|------|-----:|-------:|-----:|------------:|
| llama32-tp4 | 2.13 | **0.32** | 0.50 | **1.56×** |

Cold-cache ~2.6–3.0× vs baseline on that setup.

title: (3/n - prefill optimize)[LoRA][MoE] Optimize virtual experts: remove CPU-GPU sync & multi-block CUDA JIT histogram
author: yushengsu-thu
body:
## Summary

based on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24246

I add the jit but also keep the original in case our hardware can fall back to torch if fail on jit.

  ### Hidden side-benefit: ~68% drop in `AllReduce` kernel time on prefill-heavy LoRA workloads

  While cross-checking optimize-2 against pre-opt-2 traces (Qwen3-30B-A3B + LoRA, TP=4, GB300,
  input=65536 / output=32, 10 prompts, `--max-concurrency 4`), I noticed a much larger drop in
  `ncclDevKernel_AllReduce_Sum_bf16` than the PR's micro-benchmark numbers would suggest:

  | metric | pre-opt-2 (merged 4-TP) | post-opt-2 (TP-0 × 4 estimate) | Δ |
  |---|---:|---:|---:|
  | `AllReduce` kernel total | 6,778 ms | ~2,192 ms | **−4,586 ms (−68%)** |

  #### Mechanism

  NCCL collectives are CUDA kernels that **spin-wait inside the kernel** until all ranks
  arrive. Pre-opt-2 had a recurring per-layer CPU stall on each TP rank coming from the PyTorch
   align fallback:

  | pre-opt-2 CPU stall source | time (ms) | removed by |
  |---|---:|---|
  | `Torch-Compiled Region: 4/0` (`_align_block_size_torch` + `torch.compile`) | 3,851 | **this
   PR** |
  | `aten::sort` (`torch.argsort` in the fallback) | 790 | **this PR** |
  | `aten::item` / `_local_scalar_dense` (`.any().item()` ×4,728 in `_add_lora_gate_up_delta`)
  | ~2,000 | #24246 |

  Whichever rank is currently stalled forces the other three ranks' AllReduce kernels to keep
  spinning until it catches up. After this PR (combined with #24246) no rank stalls, all four
  ranks reach AllReduce together, and the kernel duration collapses to roughly just the actual
  data transfer.

  #### Attribution to this PR

  The two stall sources that this PR removes (`Torch-Compiled Region` + `aten::sort`) sum to
  **~4,640 ms**, which closely matches the observed −4,586 ms AllReduce drop. #24246
  contributes another ~2 sec on a separate path (likely partially overlapping in the same
  stream).

  Long stalls hurt NCCL more than frequent short ones: the `.any().item()` calls in #24246 are
  4,728 × ~291 µs (often amortizable), whereas one `Torch-Compiled Region` call is hundreds of
  µs continuous, which the other ranks cannot work around.

  #### Caveats

  - No incremental traces were taken — only `pre-opt-2` vs `post-opt-2`. The per-PR attribution
   above is by stall-source matching, not direct per-PR measurement.
  - The post side uses **TP-0 × 4** as a rough proxy for merged 4-TP; a full merged 4-TP
  post-opt-2 trace would tighten the number.
  - The `4,640 + 2,000 = 6,640 ms` total estimated stall removal exceeds the observed `−4,586
  ms` AllReduce drop, which is consistent with overlap (the two PRs' stalls partially share the
   same GPU-stream window).

  **TL;DR:** the headline 8× speedup of `_align_block_size` is real, but on prefill-heavy
  multi-TP workloads the bigger end-to-end win is **NCCL un-stalling**, which only shows up
  when you diff `AllReduce` kernel time across pre-vs-post traces.

## Accuracy Tests

Verified on 3 models with LoRA adapters (TP=4, NVIDIA GB300):

| Model | KL(sglang, trainer) | KL(sglang, orig_sampler) | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 | 0.00392 | 0.00497 | ✅ PASS |
| Qwen3-VL-30B-A3B-Instruct | 0.00072 | 0.00162 | ✅ PASS |
| gpt-oss-20b | 0.00094 | 0.00110 | ✅ PASS |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Micro-benchmark: `_align_block_size` kernel (50 repeats)

| Config | JIT (new) | PyTorch (old) | Speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8E×128L, 64 tokens | 0.048ms | 0.384ms | **8.0×** |
| 8E×256L, 256 tokens | 0.038ms | 0.320ms | **8.5×** |
| 64E×64L, 256 tokens | 0.038ms | 0.322ms | **8.6×** |
| 8E×256L, 1 token (decode) | 0.037ms | 0.327ms | **8.8×** |



## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [KDA] Optimize prefill kernels with diagonal and recompute fuse
author: yuan-luo
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Improve KDA prefill kernel performance for hybrid linear-attention models such as `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` on Hopper-class GPUs. Profiling shows KDA accounts for ~13 % of prefill GPU time on a 4-GPU TP setup; the two dominant KDA kernels (`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` and `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused`) had restrictive autotune configs and were leaving SM utilization on the table: `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64`'s grid `(V/BV, B·H_per_rank)` produces only 16 CTAs at TP=8 H=4, far below Hopper's per-GPU SM count, so most SMs sit idle.

## Modifications

KDA (Kimi Delta Attention) is a chunked linear-attention variant. For each chunk t of size BT=64, the per-layer forward decomposes into four stages:

1. **`cumsum`** — chunk-local cumulative gate `gk`
2. **`chunk_kda_fwd_intra`** — three sub-kernels that compute, per chunk, the gated qk attention `Aqk`, the lower-triangular gated kk matrix `Akk`, its inverse via in-chunk forward substitution, and finally the delta-rule helpers `w =
β·k·Akk⁻¹`, `u = β·v·Akk⁻¹`, `kg = k·exp(gn − gk)`. Each step is parallelizable over `(chunk, head, batch)`.
3. **`chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h`** — the recurrence: `h_{t+1} = h_t ⊙ exp(gk_last_t) + k_t.T @ (u_t − w_t @ h_t.T)`. **Serial across the NT chunk axis**; only parallelizable over `(head, batch, V-slice)`.
4. **`chunk_gla_fwd_o_gk`** — output `o = q·g·h.T + Aqk·v_new`. Parallel over `(chunk, head, V-slice)`.

This PR's improvement comes from the following perspectives:

### 1. h-recurrence kernel: SM under-utilization at small per-rank H
- **Expand the BV sweep to include 16 and num_warps to include 8** so triton can pick a wider grid (`V/BV = 8`) when small per-rank H starves SMs. The smaller per-CTA tile also reduces register pressure on the `b_h₁..b_h₄` accumulators (each `[BV, 64]` fp32), which raises occupancy per SM.
- **Add `NT_BUCKET` to the autotune key** (3 buckets: NT ≤ 32, ≤ 128, > 128). The optimal config genuinely differs by chunk count: short prefills favor larger BV (more work amortized over launch), long prefills favor smaller BV (more parallelism to fill SMs). Without bucketing, whichever shape autotunes first locks the choice for all subsequent shapes.
- **Add `restore_value=["h", "v_new", "initial_state"]`** to the autotune decorator. Triton's autotune benchmarks each config by repeatedly invoking the kernel; without this, the post-autotune output tensor reflects whichever config ran last in the benchmark sequence rather than the chosen config, which can produce transient precision drift on the first call. Save+restore makes the cold-cache output identical to the steady-state output.

### 2. chunk_intra: kernel-launch and HBM round-trip overhead

The intra stage was three separate kernels (`token_parallel` for diagonal Akk blocks, `inter_solve_fused` for off-diagonal blocks + lower-triangular solve, `recompute_w_u_fwd` for w/u/kg). Each boundary materializes an intermediate tensor in HBM:
- `Akkd` (diagonal blocks, fp32, ~T·H·16·4 bytes) between kernels 1 and 2
- `Akk_inv` (full triangular inverse, ~T·H·64·4 bytes) between kernels 2 and 3

The PR introduces two `tl.constexpr` modes inside `chunk_kda_fwd_kernel_inter_solve_fused`:
- **`FUSE_DIAGONAL`** — folds the diagonal Akk computation into the same kernel. Diagonal blocks live in registers and are consumed immediately by the forward-substitution; the Akkd round-trip is eliminated.
- **`FUSE_RECOMPUTE`** — additionally folds the w/u/kg recompute. The Akk_inv sub-blocks stay in registers after solve and are immediately used to construct `w = β·k·Akk_inv` etc.; the Akk_inv round-trip is eliminated.

### 3. Off-diagonal MMA in bf16

Off-diagonal `tl.dot` inputs were upcast to fp32 before the matmul; cast the per-block products `b_q·b_gqn`, `b_k·b_gqn`, and the transposed key tile to bf16 before MMA so the Hopper tensor cores run at bf16 rate (2× throughput vs the fp32 path). Accumulator stays fp32. Validated against `test_chunk_gated_delta_rule.py` (ATOL=2e-2).

### 4. Grid-aware fuse gate (kda.py dispatcher)

Compute `_small_grid = (B · NT_pr · H_per_rank ≤ 256)` and pass `fuse_diagonal=_small_grid, fuse_recompute=_small_grid` to `chunk_kda_fwd_intra`. Fusion saves launch overhead at small grid where the kernel is launch-bound; falls back to the
unfused path at large grid where the extra register footprint would spill.

For varlen (packed) tensors `NT_pr` uses `chunk_indices.shape[0]` to correctly count per-sequence chunks (chunks don't cross sequence boundaries, so `cdiv(total_tokens, chunk_size)` undercounts for typical short-sequence packs).

---

All the modified files are in `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/`:

**`chunk_delta_h.py`** — thread `chunk_indices` through the wrapper for varlen, keep autotune at a single config.

**`chunk_intra.py`** — fuse diagonal-block compute and `recompute_w_u_fwd` into the inter+solve kernel (`FUSE_DIAGONAL`, `FUSE_RECOMPUTE`); cast off-diagonal MMA inputs to bf16; keep the autotune sweep narrow (`BK ∈ {32, 64} × num_warps ∈ {1, 2, 4}`) since wider sweeps caused triton 3.6 to pick suboptimal configs at large grids.

**`kda.py`** — grid-aware dispatcher (`_small_grid`) with varlen-correct `NT_pr`; `chunk_gla_fwd_kernel_o` autotune restricted to `BK=64, BV=64` (matches pre-PR hardcoded values; wider sweeps on triton 3.6+ either crash or pick suboptimal configs).

**`cumsum.py`** — minor: add `num_stages` to the existing autotune sweep so longer prefills can benefit from deeper pipelining.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct GSM8K accuracy: **90.0 %** (no drops vs main).

| Metric          | Value         |
| --------------- | ------------: |
| Accuracy        | **90.0 %**    |
| Invalid outputs | 0.0 %         |
| Output throughput | 356 tok/s   |

```
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path moonshotai/Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct \
  --tp 4 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7 --attention-backend triton \
  --port 30000
python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-shots 8 --num-questions 200 --port 30000
```

Registered correctness tests:

title: LPLB: linear-programming load balancer for MoE expert parallelism
author: feliang-git
body:
## Summary

Adds LPLB (Linear Programming Load Balancer), a new MoE expert-dispatch algorithm that solves a per-layer LP to balance token routing across redundant expert replicas. Opt-in via `--ep-dispatch-algorithm=lp`; default behavior unchanged.

- New `lp` choice for `--ep-dispatch-algorithm` (complements `static`, `dynamic`, `fake`).
- 4 JIT-compiled CUDA kernels under `python/sglang/jit_kernel/csrc/lplb/`: a single-block IPM (`ipm.cuh`) using cuBLASDx for GEMMs and a hand-written block Cholesky for POSV (no `-rdc=true` device linking required), plus three more (`lp_prep`, `lp_post`, `dispatch_probability`) that fuse 8/5/7 torch ops into single launches.
- Math-DX is the only new dependency. Resolved via `MATHDX_HOME` env var, the `nvidia-mathdx` PyPI package, or the bundled `python/sglang/jit_kernel/lplb/resources/download-mathdx.sh`.
- Strict failure semantics: the server raises at startup if the fused backend isn't available (no CUDA, SM < 9.0, missing Math-DX); no silent fallback to torch IPM or to dynamic dispatch.

## Performance

Measured on 2× H20 nodes, DeepSeek-R1, EP=16 with DP-attention, DeepEP backend, `--max-concurrency 2048`, 4096-prompt timed runs × 3 reps each, counterbalanced order:

| Dataset  | dynamic tput | lp tput | Δ% | TTFT p50 Δ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **GSM8K**   | 19,715 | **20,779** | **+5.40%** | -5.99% |
| MMLU     | 22,949 | 22,825 | -0.54% | -2.58% |
| ShareGPT | 2,114  | 2,104  | -0.48% | **-9.18%** |

GSM8K is the routing-skewed workload LPLB targets. MMLU and ShareGPT are nulls on throughput (LPLB doesn't regress on uniform-routing or prefill-bound workloads). ShareGPT's TTFT p50 is -9.2% — the median-user TTFT improvement, which is the load-balance signal on long-context chat workloads. n = 3 reps; all p > 0.05, but effects are directionally consistent across all metrics on GSM8K (5/5 favor LP).

## Reproducing the benchmark

### 0. One-time: install Math-DX

```bash
# Either via PyPI:
pip install nvidia-mathdx
# or via the bundled script (idempotent — safe to re-run):
bash python/sglang/jit_kernel/lplb/resources/download-mathdx.sh
```

### 1. Launch the server (run on both nodes; `--node-rank` differs)

```bash
# Required to keep the JIT path off the legacy default CUDA stream
# under DP-attention all-reduce.
export NVSHMEM_IB_GID_INDEX=3
export NVSHMEM_IBGDA_NIC_HANDLER=cpu
export NVSHMEM_BOOTSTRAP_UID_SOCK_IFNAME=bond0

python3 -u -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path /path/to/DeepSeek-R1 \
    --tokenizer-path /path/to/DeepSeek-R1 \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000 \
    --tp-size 16 --dp-size 16 --ep-size 16 \
    --enable-dp-attention \
    --moe-a2a-backend deepep --deepep-mode normal \
    --ep-num-redundant-experts 16 \
    --ep-dispatch-algorithm lp \
    --init-expert-location /path/to/expert_stats.pt \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.8 \
    --max-running-requests 1024 \
    --max-prefill-tokens 65536 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
    --schedule-conservativeness 0.3 \
    --disable-radix-cache \
    --nnodes 2 --node-rank 0 \
    --dist-init-addr <head-node-ip>:29500
```

`expert_stats.pt` is a per-dataset routing-statistics file produced by a 1000-prompt run with `--ep-dispatch-algorithm=dynamic --expert-distribution-recorder-mode=stat` and dumped via `/dump_expert_distribution_record`. The file must exist on every node (the cluster /raid is non-shared in our setup).

### 2. Run the benchmark

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang-oai \
    --base-url http://localhost:30000 \
    --dataset-name custom \
    --dataset-path /path/to/dataset.jsonl \
    --num-prompts 4096 \
    --max-concurrency 2048 \
    --sharegpt-output-len 4 \
    --output-file lp.json
```

Re-run with `--ep-dispatch-algorithm=dynamic` for the baseline. We counterbalanced 3 reps × 2 algorithms with kill-and-relaunch between every rep to control for JIT-cache and NIC-heat drift.

## Scope

**DeepSeek-v2 only.** Other MoE forward paths (Qwen3, GLM4, SDAR-MoE, …) return `empty_topk_output` directly without participating in the EP all-reduce; with LP active they would deadlock under DP-attention. Out of scope for this PR; future work to enable.

LP additionally requires:
- `--enable-dp-attention`
- `--moe-a2a-backend=deepep`
- Hopper-class GPU (SM ≥ 9.0)
- Math-DX cuBLASDx headers reachable

`check_lplb_server_args` validates the first two at startup with clear errors. The model-arch check fires at `LPLBSolver.__init__`.

## Notes for reviewers

- Default behavior (no LP flags) is byte-identical to pre-PR upstream — LP code paths are inert imports.
- This PR also includes a small worker-node startup fix in `entrypoints/http_server.py` and `entrypoints/openai/serving_{base,chat}.py` (guard against `tokenizer_manager is None` for `node_rank >= 1` in multi-node serving). Happy to split into a separate PR if preferred — it's unrelated to LPLB but came up during multi-node bring-up.
- `download-mathdx.sh` is idempotent (skips if `mathdx/include` and `mathdx/lib` are present).
- No NCCL or NVSHMEM changes; LP runs over existing all-reduce primitives.

## Test plan

- [x] Multi-rank smoke test on 2× H20 with DeepSeek-R1: server boots, `/server_info` reports `ep_dispatch_algorithm=lp`, single + 8-parallel completions return valid text.
- [x] End-to-end 3-dataset benchmark sweep (3 datasets × 6 reps each, 18 timed runs): no errors, numbers match the table above.
- [x] Codex review + rescue passes against the diff (P0 clean; P1 findings addressed in the last two commits).
- [ ] CI: `pytest test/registered/eplb/test_lplb_distributed.py` under `torchrun --nproc-per-node 2` (to be triggered in CI).

title: [AMD] Add fused all-reduce RMSNorm per-group quant for Qwen3.5 FP8
author: hubertlu-tw
body:
Co-author: @mqhc2020, @yichiche  
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR adds a fused aiter path for the Qwen3.5 FP8 attention/GDN input normalization path on AMD. The baseline path around `prepare_attn` runs all-reduce, RMSNorm, and per-group activation quant as separate work before the FP8 projection consumes `(fp8, scale)`.

The new path lets `LayerCommunicator.prepare_attn` request fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group FP8 quant. Standard attention receives `(fp8, scale)` directly for `qkv_proj`. GDN receives `(bf16, fp8, scale)` so `in_proj_qkvz` can skip its internal activation quant while `in_proj_ba` still reads the bf16 activation it needs.

The fused-quant path is scoped to ROCm/aiter. The aiter single-kernel dispatch is gated to gfx95 / gfx950-class GPUs through `is_gfx95_supported()`, and plain `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` AR+RMSNorm behavior remains separate. If the fused-quant path is unavailable, callers fall back to fused AR+RMSNorm or the existing generic path.

## Modifications


- Added a tensor-parallel API for fused all-reduce + RMSNorm + per-group FP8
  quant:
  - `tensor_model_parallel_fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group(...)`
  - `GroupCoordinator.fused_allreduce_rmsnorm_quant_per_group(...)`
- Added layernorm helpers that return tuple activations for FP8 consumers:
  - `((fp8, scale), residual)` for standard attention.
  - `((bf16, fp8, scale), residual)` for GDN, where bf16 is required by `in_proj_ba`.
- Wired `LayerCommunicator.prepare_attn` to prefer the fused-quant helper when `_sglang_needs_allreduce_fusion` is set and the layer opts in with `enable_fused_ar_quant=True`.
- Wired Qwen3.5 standard attention with `keep_bf16=False` and GDN with `keep_bf16=True`.
- Updated Qwen3.5 GDN input projection to consume the `(bf16, fp8, scale)` tuple without dequantizing fp8 back to bf16.
- Added `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT=1` as the operator opt-out for this quantized handoff while keeping the existing AR+RMSNorm fusion eligible.

Fallback order:

1. aiter single-kernel AR + RMSNorm + per-group FP8 quant, optionally with bf16 side-output.
2. aiter fused AR + RMSNorm plus separate aiter per-1x128 quant.
3. Generic caller fallback.

The single-kernel dispatch is intentionally limited to ROCm + aiter + gfx95.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K was run on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 with TP=8 and
`--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`.

| Config | GSM8K command | Accuracy |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Baseline | `python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319 --num-shots 5 --port 9000` | 0.946 |
| Fused AR+RMSNorm+per-group quant | `python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319 --num-shots 5 --port 9000` | 0.955 |

The fused path is above the 0.94 accuracy gate used for this model.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<details>
<summary>Server command</summary>

```bash
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001 --tensor-parallel-size 4 \
  --attention-backend aiter --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 16 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --watchdog-timeout 1200 \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion
```

</details>

<details>
<summary>Serving benchmark command</summary>

```bash
for cc in 2 8 32; do
  python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30001 \
    --model /data2/Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 \
    --dataset-name random --random-input 8192 --random-output 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.8 --max-concurrency $cc \
    --num-prompts $((cc*10)) --seed 0
done
```

</details>

Case A: baseline without `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion` 
Case B: with `--enable-aiter-allreduce-fusion`
| cc | Output tok/s A -> B | Delta | Mean TPOT A -> B | Delta | Mean TTFT A -> B |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 186.42 -> 197.21 | +5.8% | 10.46 ms -> 9.88 ms | +5.5% | 222.27 ms -> 225.39 ms |
| 8 | 598.54 -> 625.89 | +4.6% | 12.82 ms -> 12.23 ms | +4.6% | 292.07 ms -> 305.96 ms |
| 32 | 1332.17 -> 1328.84 | -0.2% | 22.81 ms -> 22.90 ms | -0.4% | 571.93 ms -> 560.36 ms |

Improvement formula:

- Throughput: `(candidate - baseline) / baseline * 100`.
- TPOT: `(baseline - candidate) / baseline * 100`.

Kernel-count profile, per decode pass on Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 / TP=8 with 60
decoder layers:

| Kernel | Baseline | Fused path | Delta |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| `cross_device_reduce_*stage` (plain AR) | 60 | 0 | -60 |
| `add_rmsnorm_quant_kernel` (RMSNorm+add) | 60 | 0 | -60 |
| `dynamic_per_group_scaled_quant_kernel` | 60 | 0 | -60 |
| `allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage` (AR+RMSNorm) | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| `allreduce_fusion_kernel_1stage_per_group` | 0 | 60 | +60 |
| Comm-side separate quant for GDN keep-bf16 path | 45 | 0 | -45 |
| Total kernels saved on `prepare_attn` | | | -165 |

title: Feat: Support newer EAGLE-3 drafters
author: Dogacel
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

We will have a paper-release soon and we would like our models to have day-0 support with the paper/model release. 

We will release checkpoints for gpt-oss-20b and gpt-oss-120b.

## Modifications

1) Multi-layer EAGLE-3: backwards compatible as we rename midlayer -> layers.0, this gives flexibility for users to run more models including vLLM supported ones.

2) Alternate norm positioning: this is about our upcoming paper release and new models.

3) Support EAGLE-3 backbones that take other than 3 aux hidden states: current models only use 3 hidden states but our models benefit from more hidden states.

## Accuracy Tests, Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware GH200, VRAM 96 GB, vCPU: 64, RAM: 432 GiB hosted on lambda.ai

### vs. D-Flash

depth=5 seems to be the sweet-spot for GPT-oss for both models.

| Metric | d-flash | Ours | Δ |

title: feat: SM120 (Blackwell Desktop) support for DeepSeek-V4 inference
author: AliceChenyy
body:
## Summary

Adds full **SM120** (RTX PRO 6000 / RTX 5090 / DGX Spark, compute 12.0) support for DeepSeek-V4/V3 on SGLang. SM120 desktop Blackwell GPUs lack TMEM, tcgen05, and DeepGEMM support — this PR provides Triton-based fallback kernels for all critical paths and enables CUDA graph capture.

### Key changes

**New kernels (7 files):**
- `mxfp4_moe_sm120_triton.py` — Triton fused MXFP4 dequant + GEMM for MoE experts (4.1x vs PyTorch per-GEMM)
- `flash_mla_sm120_triton.py` — Triton FlashMLA sparse decode kernel (3.2–5.4x vs FlashInfer fallback)
- `sm120_mqa_triton.py` — FP8 paged MQA with wq-precompute + vectorized batch (CUDA graph compatible)
- `flash_mla_sm120_fallback.py` / `sm120_mqa_fallback.py` / `mxfp4_moe_fallback.py` — PyTorch fallback paths
- `test_sm120_mqa_fallback.py` — Unit tests for MQA fallback correctness

**SM120 guards (10 modified files):**
- DeepGEMM / tilelang MHC disabled on SM120 (no TMEM/tcgen05)
- NSA backend: tilelang default, skip DeepGEMM metadata allocation
- FlashMLA: SM120 adapter in `deepseek_v4_backend.py`
- MoE: auto-select `marlin` backend on SM120
- 3 CUDA-graph-breaking paths fixed (`.unique()/.item()/.nonzero()` → vectorized)

**Bug fix (found during latest-image validation):**
- FlashMLA Triton kernel: handle KV cache `uint8` dtype (upstream changed from `float8_e4m3fn`)

### Results (8× RTX PRO 6000, TP=8, CUDA graph)

**On `sglang:dev-cu13` (sgl-kernel 0.4.2.post1, PyTorch 2.11+cu130):**

| Metric | Value |

| GSM8K 5-shot (200q) | **99.0%** accuracy |
| Decode (BS=1) | **11.40 tok/s** (TPOT = 87.7ms) |

**On older nightly-dev-20260430 (sgl-kernel 0.4.1, PyTorch 2.9.1+cu129):**

### Motivation

- SM120 is desktop Blackwell (RTX 5090, RTX PRO 6000) — no server-class features (TMEM, tcgen05, NVSwitch)
