title: [Gemma4] Optimize Gemm4 with fused Q/K/V RMSNorm + per-expert FP8 ckpt loader
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Motivation

The original motivation is to speedup Gemm4 model. Two unrelated issues on the Gemma4 FP8-MoE path:

1. **Attention RMSNorm is launch-bound.** Each Gemma4 attention layer issues three separate sgl-kernel `rmsnorm` launches (q/k/v). At small token counts the per-launch host overhead dominates — three back-to-back launches cost ~60μs regardless of M, even though the actual compute is trivial.

2. **compressed-tensors per-expert FP8 checkpoints fail silently.** Models like `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic` store one weight per expert (`experts.<id>.{gate,up,down}_proj.{weight,weight_scale}`). The existing loader only recognizes the stacked `experts.gate_up_proj` / `experts.down_proj` layout, so every routed expert is silently skipped → zero-init expert weights → server launches fine but generation collapses to all-`<pad>` and GSM8K = 0.0.

## Design

### 1. Fused Q/K/V RMSNorm (`gemma_qkv_rmsnorm`)

- One Triton kernel computes `x · rsqrt(mean(x²) + eps) · w` for all q/k/v heads in a single launch, in-place into the qkv buffer.
- Grid `(M,)`, `BLOCK = next_pow2(head_dim)`, with `tl.static_range` over heads.
- Operates on `qkv.split(...)` strided views via `stride_*_m` — no `.contiguous()` copy.
- V path skips the weight multiply (V uses `with_scale=False` → weight is identically 1).
- Conservative fallback in `Gemma4Attention.forward`: only takes the fused path when CUDA + `q_norm.scale_shift == 0 == k_norm.scale_shift` + `not v_norm.with_scale`. Non-standard configs and KV-shared layers retain the original three-norm
path.

### 2. Per-expert FP8 loader

- New regex branch in `Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` for `^.*\.moe\.experts\.<id>\.(gate|up|down)_proj\.(weight|weight_scale)$`.
- Maps each per-expert key to the fused FusedMoE param + shard id + expert id, then dispatches via `param.weight_loader` (standard FusedMoE signature).
- If the regex matches but the fused param is absent (e.g. ckpt-format drift), emit `logger.warning` instead of silently skipping — this prevents reproducing the very failure mode the patch fixes.

### 3. Test

- `test/registered/models/test_gemma4_fp8_per_expert_loading.py` (CI: `stage-c-test-4-gpu-h100`, est 120s) launches the FP8 model with TP=4 and asserts: server health, non-`<pad>` chat output, and GSM8K-20 ≥ 0.80 (BF16 baseline ~0.95). All three checks fail pre-fix.

## Accuracy

MMLU 500 examples
BF16 （500 examples, TP=4）：0.878

RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic
| Category | Score |
|---|---|
| Overall | 0.885 |
| STEM | 0.952 |
| Social sciences | 0.918 |
| Other | 0.872 |
| Humanities | 0.823 |

## Benchmark

H100 ×4, TP=4, `RedHatAI/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it-FP8-Dynamic`, batch=1, in=2048, out=64.

**Microbench (single H100, bf16, Q=8h, KV=2h, head_dim=128):**

| M | unfused (μs) | fused (μs) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 44.4 | 19.8 | 2.25x |
| 8 | 59.4 | 20.3 | 2.93x |
| 64 | 59.4 | 20.4 | 2.91x |
| 256 | 59.7 | 20.1 | 2.96x |
| 1024 | 60.1 | 20.2 | 2.97x |
| 4096 | 58.4 | 18.6 | 3.14x |
| 8192 | 59.3 | 32.3 | 1.83x |
| 16384 | 108.0 | 75.0 | 1.44x |

Bit-exact vs unfused at M=1/8/128 (max abs diff = 0).

**End-to-end (4-GPU, RedHatAI FP8):**

| Metric | Unfused (baseline) | Fused (this PR) | Δ |
|---|---|---|---|
| Prefill 2048 tok | 47.0 ms | 46.0 ms | **-2.1%** |
| Decode median | 5.47 ms/tok | 5.45 ms/tok | -0.4% |
| Total | 0.393 s | 0.390 s | -0.8% |

Decode benefit is muted because the SGLang decode path runs inside CUDA Graph, which amortizes the launch overhead the fused kernel saves. Prefill (no graph) realizes the full 2% win. Net change is neutral-to-positive across regimes; never negative within the tested M range.

The per-expert FP8 loader is a correctness fix: pre-fix GSM8K-20 = 0.00, post-fix ≈ 0.95 — gated at ≥ 0.80 in the new test.

## Test plan

- [x] Microbench: fused vs unfused bit-exact, 1.4–3.1x faster across M ∈ [1, 16384]
- [x] E2E prefill/decode latency comparison (above)
- [x] New CI test `test_gemma4_fp8_per_expert_loading.py` exercises the loader fix end-to-end on 4 GPUs
- [ ] Existing Gemma4 tests still pass (need full CI run)

title: Add FlashInfer SM90 cutlass MXFP4 MoE backend (W4A16) for GPT-OSS + DeepSeek-V4
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Summary Wires FlashInfer's SM90 mixed-input `cutlass_fused_moe(use_w4_group_scaling=True)` path ([FlashInfer PR #3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084)) into both SGLang MXFP4 entry points as an **opt-in** backend on Hopper: - **GPT-OSS** path: `Mxfp4MoEMethod` in `mxfp4.py`, dispatched from `Mxfp4Config`. - **DeepSeek-V4** path: new `Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod`, sibling of `Mxfp4MarlinMoEMethod` / `Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod`, dispatched from `Fp8MoEConfig.get_quant_method` when `is_fp4_experts=True`. Both are triggered by `--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4` on H100/H200. Today that flag auto-selects only on SM100; on SM90 users still default to Marlin, so this PR is purely additive. **PD-disaggregation is the killer use case: prefill workers run FlashInfer (+24–36% at M ≥ 1024), decode workers stay on Marlin (+12–15% at M ≤ 64), each phase picks the kernel that wins its regime.** See benchmark below. No default behavior changes. Marlin remains the SM90 default for both models. ## What FlashInfer PR [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084) ships PR #3084 ports TensorRT-LLM PR [#12451](https://github.com/NVIDIA/TensorRT-LLM/pull/12451) into FlashInfer's existing `cutlass_fused_moe` kernel: - **LDSM + LUT FP4 / INT4 → BF16 weight load pipeline** in `mixed_input_utils.hpp` and `sm90_mma_array_tma_gmma_rs_warpspecialized_mixed_input_*.hpp` — replaces the previous bit-shuffle path on Hopper for 4-bit weights × 16/8-bit activations. - **Tactic-list pruning** in `cutlass_heuristic.cpp`: skip `CtaShape128x128x128B + COOPERATIVE` for `has_w4afp8` (register overflow on SM90), pick `COOPERATIVE` / `PINGPONG` per tile. - **Scheduler tweaks** in `moe_gemm_tma_ws_mixed_input_launcher.inl`: `max_swizzle_size=2`, `raster_order=Heuristic`. - **Two new Python helpers** that the kernel layout requires: - `interleave_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm(weight, "fp4"|"int4")` — C++ byte-level interleave of packed 4-bit weights. - `interleave_moe_scales_for_sm90_mixed_gemm(scales, group_size=32)` — pure-PyTorch reshape + permute of E8M0 block scales (factor `128 // group_size`). Both helpers must run once at weight-load time. They live in `flashinfer.fused_moe.core` and ship in FlashInfer ≥ 0.6.11. Depends on https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24452 ## What changes in SGLang ### GPT-OSS path — `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py` 1. **`Mxfp4MoEMethod.__init__`** — new `self._fi_kernel` discriminator (`"trtllm_sm100"` / `"cutlass_sm90"` / `None`). Imports of the new helpers are guarded with `try/except` so older FlashInfer builds still load. 2. **`create_weights`** — adds an SM90 cutlass branch that pads `intermediate_size` and `hidden_size` to multiples of 128 (mixed-input GEMM contraction-dim constraint: `K % 128 == 0` because the scale interleave factor is `128 // group_size = 4`). 3. **`process_weights_after_loading`** — early-dispatch into `_process_weights_for_sm90_cutlass`, which: - byte-interleaves `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` with the FP4 helper, - reshape+permute interleaves `w13_weight_scale` / `w2_weight_scale`, - builds per-expert SwiGLU scalars (α=1.702, β=1.0, limit=7.0; matches the existing SM100 trtllm-gen path's GPT-OSS hardcoded defaults). 4. **`apply`** — early-dispatch into `_apply_sm90_cutlass`, which pads input, calls `flashinfer_cutlass_fused_moe(use_w4_group_scaling=True, …)` with per-expert SwiGLU scalars and bias, and trims the output back to the original hidden width. ### DeepSeek-V4 path — `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_cutlass_moe.py` (new) New sibling class `Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod` paralleling `Mxfp4MarlinMoEMethod` / `Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod`: 1. **Dispatch** — `fp8.py:get_quant_method` checks SM at runtime: SM100 continues to route to `Mxfp4FlashinferTrtllmMoEMethod` (trtllm-gen), SM90 routes to the new class. 2. **`process_weights_after_loading`** — - calls the FP8 base hook (ROCm normalization etc), - reorders `[w1; w3] → [w3; w1]` via `reorder_w1w3_to_w3w1` (cutlass expects `[up; gate]`, matching the trtllm-gen convention), - converts the fp32-stored E8M0 scales to raw uint8 bytes via `.to(float8_e8m0fnu).view(uint8)`, - byte-interleaves weights, reshape+permute interleaves scales. 3. **`apply`** — `cutlass_fused_moe(use_w4_group_scaling=True)` with biases `None` (DSv4 has no MoE bias), `swiglu_alpha`/`swiglu_beta` `None` (kernel defaults give standard SwiGLU), and `swiglu_limit` from `moe_runner_config.swiglu_limit` (per-expert tensor). 4. **Routed-scale fusion** — extends the `isinstance` check in `mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.maybe_fuse_routed_scale_and_shared_add` so the new class participates in the same shared-add fusion as Marlin / trtllm-gen. Padding is asserted rather than applied: DSv4's standard config (hidden=7168, intermediate=2048) is already a multiple of 128. Variants with non-aligned shapes will raise a clear error. ## Tests ### Unit tests `python/sglang/test/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py` — 12 cases, all PASSED on H100: GPT-OSS path (5 + 4): - `test_process_weights_matches_direct_interleave` × 5 — verifies that `_process_weights_for_sm90_cutlass` (de-interleave + pad + halved swap + byte/scale interleave) produces **bit-exact** the same bytes as a hand-rolled reference that performs the same transform sequence. Cases include the GPT-OSS-20B production shape (2880 × 2880) and the 192 × 192 boundary case to exercise the pad path. - `test_apply_sm90_cutlass_matches_flashinfer_direct` × 4 — end-to-end on random MXFP4 inputs: SGLang's `_apply_sm90_cutlass` output is **bit-exact** equal to a direct `cutlass_fused_moe(use_w4_group_scaling=True, …)` call fed with the layer's processed tensors (with manual pad x + trim out for the unaligned shape). Confirms bias / SwiGLU scalar / `quant_scales` plumbing + input-pad / output-trim is correct. DeepSeek-V4 path (3): - `test_dsv4_apply_matches_flashinfer_direct` × 3 — end-to-end on random DSv4-style MXFP4 inputs (int8-packed weights, fp32 E8M0 scales). `Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod.apply` output is **bit-exact** equal to a reference path that manually applies `reorder_w1w3_to_w3w1` + the fp32→uint8 E8M0 cast + the FlashInfer interleave helpers + a direct `cutlass_fused_moe(use_w4_group_scaling=True, biases=None, swiglu_*=None)` call. Confirms the DSv4-specific reorder + scale-cast plumbing is correct. ### End-to-end accuracy Both paths exercised on real production checkpoints with chat-API GSM8K (200 questions, T=0, on H100): **GPT-OSS-20B** — `Mxfp4MoEMethod` (mxfp4.py) ``` $ python -m sglang.launch_server --model openai/gpt-oss-20b \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --attention-backend triton \ --port 30011 --tp 1 $ python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30011 --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 --api chat --max-tokens 1024 --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 ``` | backend | GSM8K score | latency | throughput | |---|---:|---:|---:| | FlashInfer cutlass (this PR) | **0.940** | 20.25 s | 3338 tok/s | | `triton_kernel` baseline | 0.945 | 17.44 s | 3926 tok/s | It matches the published GPT-OSS-20B GSM8K range (≈ 91–94 %). **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** — `Mxfp4FlashinferCutlassMoEMethod` (new) ``` $ python -m sglang.launch_server --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \ --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 --port 30000 --tp 4 \ --trust-remote-code $ python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 200 --api chat --max-tokens 1024 --num-threads 32 \ --temperature 0 ``` | metric | value | |---|---:| | GSM8K score (200 q, chat API, T=0) | **0.985** | | Total latency | 49.21 s | | Output throughput | 469 tok/s | 98.5 % is consistent with DSv4-Flash's published GSM8K range. ## Benchmark `python/sglang/test/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py` — kernel-level perf on H100 (80 GB HBM3, cap 9.0). Both paths use the same random MXFP4 weights; `autotune(True)` is active for FlashInfer; bias-on and bias-off are autotuned independently. Body fixed at the GPT-OSS-like config (hidden=4096, inter=2048, E=256, top_k=6) and tokens swept across the decode → prefill range. | tokens | Marlin | FI cutlass (AT, bias) | FI cutlass (AT, no bias) | Winner | Margin | |------:|-------------:|----------------------:|-------------------------:|:----------|------:| | 4 | **0.174 ms** | 0.195 ms | 0.190 ms | Marlin | +12 % | | 16 | **0.484 ms** | 0.549 ms | 0.549 ms | Marlin | +13 % | | 64 | **1.046 ms** | 1.204 ms | 1.204 ms | Marlin | +15 % | | 256 | 1.549 ms | 1.587 ms | 1.583 ms | tie | +2 % | | 1024 | 2.084 ms | **1.943 ms** | 1.954 ms | FlashInfer | +7 % | | 2048 | 3.420 ms | **2.663 ms** | 2.624 ms | FlashInfer | +28 % | | 4096 | 7.011 ms | **5.149 ms** | 5.134 ms | FlashInfer | +36 % | | 8192 | 12.541 ms | **10.085 ms** | 10.176 ms | FlashInfer | +24 % | Each row is the median of 30 timed iterations after 5 warmups. **Bias overhead** (FI bias-on vs FI bias-off) is consistently within ±2 %, i.e. essentially free. ### Interpretation The two backends have clearly distinct sweet spots: - **Decode regime (m ≤ 64).** Marlin is 12–15 % faster. Marlin's tile policy and native E8M0 scale path squeeze more out of small-M grouped GEMM where the kernel is launch-bound and per-CTA work matters more than aggregate throughput. - **Tie zone (m ≈ 256).** Both within 2 % of each other. - **Prefill / chunked-prefill regime (m ≥ 1024).** FlashInfer cutlass is **24–36 % faster**. At large M the kernel becomes GEMM-bound, the SM90 TMA-warp-specialized cooperative scheduler from PR #3084 fully populates the H100 SM array, and Marlin's per-CTA overhead dominates instead. Sanity check: FlashInfer's m=4 number (0.195 ms) matches PR #3084's H200 table (0.193 ms), so the integration is correct. PR #3084's reported 2.66–3.11× speedup is vs FlashInfer's *own* previous SM90 path (~0.79 ms at m=4), not vs Marlin — Marlin wasn't in that comparison. ### Conclusion - **Default unchanged for decode-heavy serving.** Marlin remains the SM90 MXFP4 default; it dominates the small-M region typical of pure decode. - **FlashInfer cutlass is the right pick for prefill.** Long context, large chunked-prefill (≥ 1024 tokens/forward), or PD-disaggregation prefill workers all benefit by 24–36 %. - **PD-disaggregation natural fit:** prefill workers (`--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4`) and decode workers (Marlin default) can pick the best kernel for their phase. - Mixed-batch deployments: pick by expected average M; an end-to-end throughput benchmark on a target workload is the next step before flipping any default. ## Caveats / known issues - Requires FlashInfer ≥ 0.6.11 (PR #3084 landed after 0.6.10). Bumping `flashinfer_python` is a separate change; for now the import is gated and raises a clear error if the user picks `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90 without the helpers. - Padding to 128 is required on SM90 cutlass; small models (e.g. GPT-OSS hidden=2880 → padded 2944) pay a ~2 % memory overhead in the MoE weights. - SwiGLU per-expert scalars are hardcoded to GPT-OSS defaults (α=1.702, β=1.0, limit=7.0), mirroring the existing SM100 trtllm-gen path. When other models adopt this backend, they should be plumbed from `moe_runner_config.gemm1_alpha` / `.gemm1_clamp_limit`. - FlashInfer's autotuner does not key tactics on bias presence; if a deployment toggles bias on/off through the same MoE method, run autotune for each configuration. (Affects only autotune cache hit-rate, not correctness.) ## Files changed - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4.py` (+~140 lines, GPT-OSS path) - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_cutlass_moe.py` (new, ~230 lines, DSv4 path) - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/fp8.py` (+~15 lines, SM-aware dispatch) - `python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/mxfp4_flashinfer_trtllm_moe.py` (+~5 lines, fuse-check) - `python/sglang/test/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py` (new, ~370 lines, 9 cases) - `python/sglang/test/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py` (new, ~280 lines)

title: [AMD] support fp8 blockwise quantization combine for mori ep
author: billishyahao
body: ## Motivation This patch is to add FP8 blockwise quantization support for the combine in Mori EP dispatcher, complementing the existing FP8/FP4 dispatch quantization. Fix issue https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/24866 Work with https://github.com/ROCm/mori/pull/311 cc @Duyi-Wang @HaiShaw ## Modifications - Introduce `DispatchDtype` and `CombineDtype` enums to replace boolean flags (`fp8_dispatch`, `fp4_dispatch`), making the dtype configuration more extensible and type-safe. - Add `CombineDtype.fp8` (`fp8_blockwise`) as a new combine quantization mode alongside the existing `fp8_direct_cast`. - Add new env var `SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE` (`auto|bf16|fp8|fp8_direct_cast`) for explicit combine dtype control. - Unify dispatch dtype env var: `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE` (`auto|bf16|fp8|fp4`) replaces deprecated `SGLANG_MORI_FP8_DISP` / `SGLANG_MORI_FP4_DISP`. - Deprecated env vars (`SGLANG_MORI_FP8_DISP`, `SGLANG_MORI_FP4_DISP`, `SGLANG_MORI_FP8_COMB`) are still supported with deprecation warnings. - Auto-detect default combine dtype from model weight type: FP4 models default to `fp8_blockwise` combine, FP8 models default to `bf16` combine. - Pass `dispatch_dtype` / `combine_dtype` enums (instead of booleans) through `init_mori_op()` and `_MoriEPDispatcherImplBase`. ## Accuracy Tests Model: amd/DeepSeek-R1-0528-MXFP4, DEP8, GSM8K All 16 combinations of `SGLANG_MORI_DISPATCH_DTYPE` x `SGLANG_MORI_COMBINE_DTYPE` tested: | dispatch \ combine | bf16 | fp8 (blockwise) | fp8_direct_cast | auto | |--------------------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------|-----------------| | **auto** (→fp4) | 93.9% / 846 tps | 93.8% / 786 tps | 92.2% / 825 tps | 93.8% / 771 tps | | **bf16** | 93.9% / 788 tps | 93.8% / 739 tps | 91.5% / 774 tps | 93.6% / 752 tps | | **fp8** | 93.7% / 536 tps | 94.2% / 525 tps | 91.8% / 518 tps | 93.1% / 524 tps | | **fp4** | 93.7% / 848 tps | 94.5% / 784 tps | 91.2% / 829 tps | 93.8% / 777 tps | Key findings: 1. **No regression:** All 16 combinations produce accuracy in the 91.2%–94.5% range, within normal variance. 2. **`fp8_blockwise` combine outperforms `fp8_direct_cast`:** ~2% higher accuracy across all dispatch types (e.g., fp4+fp8_blockwise: 94.5% vs fp4+fp8_direct_cast: 91.2%). 3. **Default auto/auto path (fp4 dispatch + fp8 blockwise combine) is optimal** for MXFP4 models: 93.8% accuracy, 771 tps. ## Checklist - title: Support Nemotron DP attention and MTP
author: Zhichenzzz
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enable **data-parallel (DP) attention** for Nemotron-H. Nemotron-H is a hybrid model (Mamba2 + full attention + MoE), and DP attention previously only supported standard attention + MLP transformers. So Nemotron-H ran attention and Mamba in **global TP** with no path for the DP layout — there was no gather/scatter between the DP-local (attn-TP) layout and the full-TP MoE layout, and the per-rank token padding that DP attention adds for collective alignment was not handled in the Mamba recurrent path (padding rows would write KV cache, update Mamba states, and corrupt residuals).

This PR makes attention **and** Mamba run data-parallel across attention-TP subgroups (cutting KV / Mamba-state duplication) while MoE/MLP stay in full TP.

## Modifications

- Run `MambaMixer2` and attention on the **attention-TP group** (`attn_tp_rank/size`) instead of the global TP group when DP attention is enabled; the gated RMSNorm variance reduction uses the attn-TP group too.
- Add a per-layer `LayerCommunicator` that gathers the DP-local, attn-TP-partial output into the full-TP layout for MoE/MLP and scatters it back (`TP_ATTN_FULL` ↔ `FULL`).
- Handle DP padding rows end-to-end: trim / zero the padding so it never writes KV cache, updates Mamba recurrent state, or leaks into residuals; thread the real (unpadded) batch size and prefill-token count through the Mamba metadata and the CUDA-graph replay.
- `o_proj` / `out_proj` run with `reduce_results=False` plus chunked, global-TP-emulated fp32 accumulation so the deferred reduction matches the non-DP numerics.

## Accuracy Tests

gsm8k smoke test on a Nemotron model (tp=8, eager, `parallel=32`, 200 questions):

| config             | accuracy | invalid |
| ------------------ | -------- | ------- |
| no DP, no MTP      | 0.955    | 0.000   |
| DP attention only  | 0.970    | 0.000   |
| MTP only           | 0.955    | 0.000   |
| DP attention + MTP | 0.955    | 0.000   |

DP attention + MTP matches the no-DP/no-MTP and single-feature baselines (no accuracy regression, no hangs).

title: [AMD] Support triton backend decode context parallel for Qwen3.5
author: At1a8
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->
co-author: @IzacharyI 

## Motivation
- support decode context parallel(DCP) for Qwen3.5 models, use zigzag format to save kv on different kv rank
- this pr following https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/14982 and https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/34018

## Modifications

### DCP Group and Runtime Arguments
- `server_args.py` adds the `dcp_size` field and exposes `--decode-context-parallel-size` / `--dcp-size`.
- `distributed/parallel_state.py` adds `_DCP` and `get_dcp_group()`, and splits each TP group into DCP groups according to `dcp_size`.
- The `graph_capture()` group stack in `parallel_state.py` includes the DCP group, so DCP collectives can participate in CUDA graph capture.
- `model_executor/model_runner.py` stores `dcp_size` / `dcp_rank` and passes `decode_context_parallel_size` into model-parallel initialization.

### KV Cache, Allocator, and Owner Mask

The DCP KV ownership rule is:

```text
owner(abs_pos) = abs_pos % dcp_size
```

- `model_executor/forward_batch_info.py` adds `ForwardBatch.dcp_kv_mask`. In the eager path, the owner mask can be generated from `positions % dcp_size == dcp_rank`.
- `model_executor/cuda_graph_runner.py` adds `DecodeInputBuffers.dcp_kv_mask` as a fallback input for graph replay.
- `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer()` in `mem_cache/memory_pool.py` supports `dcp_kv_mask`, and uses `masked_set_kv_buffer_kernel` to write only the tokens KV cache owned by the current DCP rank.
- `HybridLinearKVPool.set_kv_buffer()` in `mem_cache/memory_pool.py` forwards `dcp_kv_mask`, preventing the Qwen3.5 hybrid full/linear attention path from breaking.
- `models/utils.py` disables fused KV writes when `forward_batch.dcp_kv_mask` exists, so the write path does not bypass masked KV writes.
- `model_executor/model_runner_kv_cache_mixin.py` uses enlarged physical page allocation under DCP, allowing the full KV cache physical pages to hold DCP owner shards.
- `mem_cache/common.py` selects paged allocation according to the actual allocator page size, avoiding mismatches between the tree-cache page size and the real allocator page size.
- `managers/scheduler_components/invariant_checker.py` accounts for DCP physical-page slack, avoiding false positives caused by differences between logical token counts and physical page counts.

### Triton Attention DCP

#### Core utilities(layers/attention/utils.py):
- `create_triton_kv_indices_for_dcp_triton()` in `utils.py` builds local KV indices for the current rank from `req_to_token` according to the DCP owner rule. Regular attention reads a contiguous KV range; under DCP, each rank only reads absolute positions satisfying `abs_pos % dcp_size == dcp_rank`. For example, when `dcp_size=2`, rank 0 reads `0,2,4,...`, while rank 1 reads `1,3,5,...`.
- `get_dcp_lens()` in `utils.py` computes the local KV length visible to the current rank for each request. It supports both `start=None` and tensor `start` paths. `start` usually has shape `[batch_size]`, with one KV start offset per request; the actual KV range for request `i` is `[start[i], start[i] + lens[i])`.
- In `utils.py`, the `cp_lse_ag_out_rs()` pipeline is: LSE all-gather -> output rescale -> output all-reduce -> local head slice.

#### Changes in `triton_backend.py`:
- During initialization, the backend stores `dcp_size` / `dcp_rank` and sets `self.num_head` to the number of query heads actually seen by the Triton kernel after all-gather: `local_num_heads * dcp_size`.
- Decode metadata is split by `dcp_size`. Non-DCP continues to use `create_flashinfer_kv_indices_triton()` to generate full contiguous KV indices. Under DCP, `get_dcp_lens()` and `create_triton_kv_indices_for_dcp_triton()` generate only the current rank's KV-shard `kv_indptr` / `kv_indices`.
- `get_num_kv_splits()` uses the local KV-shard length under DCP decode rather than the full global `seq_lens`. 
- Add `_kv_cache_loc()` and `_set_kv_buffer()`. Under DCP, global `out_cache_loc` is mapped to local physical locations with `out_cache_loc // dcp_size`, and the owner mask is generated by `positions % dcp_size == dcp_rank`, so each rank only writes the tokens it owns. When DCP is disabled, `_kv_cache_loc()` returns `out_cache_loc` unchanged.
- KV writes in `forward_extend()` are isolated by DCP. Non-DCP continues to use the main-branch default `token_to_kv_pool.set_kv_buffer()` path. DCP uses `_set_kv_buffer()` so it can apply local locations and owner masks. The MLA path keeps the original manual-scale + direct-write logic; the current DCP changes are mainly for non-MLA models.
- KV writes in `forward_decode()` are similarly isolated. Non-DCP writes directly to `out_cache_loc`; DCP uses `_set_kv_buffer()`. This keeps regular Triton decode away from the DCP masked-write path.

#### Decode path:

- DCP decode first reshapes the current rank's Q to `[tokens, local_heads, head_dim]`, then performs an all-gather along the head dimension within the DCP group so every DCP rank has the full set of Q heads.
- Each rank calls the original Triton decode kernel with its local `kv_indices`, computing partial output and split-dimension partial LSE over the current rank's KV shard.
- The decode kernel's `attn_lse` includes a split dimension, so DCP first applies `torch.logsumexp(..., dim=-1)` over the split dimension to obtain the local LSE for the current rank's KV shard.
- Finally, `cp_lse_ag_out_rs()` performs LSE all-gather, global-LSE rescaling, output all-reduce, and local-head slicing. The final output shape remains the same as regular TP decode.

#### Extend path:

- `triton_ops/extend_attention.py` adds optional LSE output to the existing Triton extend kernel. `_fwd_kernel()` adds `LSE_Extend`, `stride_lse_bs`, `stride_lse_h`, and `STORE_LSE`. When `STORE_LSE=True`, the kernel writes the online-softmax `log(sum(exp(logits)))` value to `LSE_Extend`, which is needed to merge DCP partial outputs across ranks.
- `triton_ops/extend_attention.py` adds two switches to `_fwd_kernel()`: `SKIP_PREFIX` and `SKIP_EXTEND`. When `SKIP_PREFIX=True`, the prefix-KV loop is skipped and only current-chunk causal attention is computed. When `SKIP_EXTEND=True`, the current-chunk loop is skipped and only prefix-KV attention is computed.
- `extend_attention_fwd_with_lse()` is added as a wrapper. It takes `lse_extend`, calls `_fwd_kernel()` with `STORE_LSE=True`, and exposes `skip_prefix` / `skip_extend`. Regular non-DCP extend still uses the original `extend_attention_fwd()` / unified path and passes `STORE_LSE=False`, `SKIP_PREFIX=False`, and `SKIP_EXTEND=False`, preserving the original semantics.
- `forward_extend()` enters `_forward_extend_dcp()` when `dcp_size > 1`, avoiding the Python dense-attention fallback and preventing long-context OOM from constructing dense score tensors with shape similar to `[extend_tokens, heads, context_tokens]`.
- `_forward_extend_dcp()` splits extend attention into current chunk and prefix KV:
  - All DCP ranks first compute the current chunk. The current chunk's K/V still comes from the local tensors produced by this forward pass, so each rank uses its local query heads and calls `extend_attention_fwd_with_lse(..., skip_prefix=True)` to compute its own `current_out/current_lse`. `skip_prefix=True` is not rank-specific; all DCP ranks use it during the current stage.
  - All DCP ranks then compute the prefix shard. Prefix KV has already been sharded in KV cache according to the DCP owner rule, so the prefix stage first all-gathers query heads and then calls `extend_attention_fwd_with_lse(..., skip_extend=True)`. Each rank computes only its own prefix-KV shard's `prefix_out/prefix_lse`.
- Prefix partial output/LSE is merged across DCP ranks through `cp_lse_ag_out_rs(..., return_lse=True)`. The prefix and current parts are then merged with `logaddexp` over LSE and output rescaling with `exp(part_lse - final_lse)`, ensuring the softmax denominator is equivalent to full prefix+current attention.
- If prefix KV is empty, `_forward_extend_dcp()` directly returns the current-chunk result and skips prefix all-gather and cross-rank merge, reducing redundant communication during initial prefill.
- DCP extend currently explicitly rejects `sinks`, custom masks, and sliding-window paths to avoid silently running unverified combinations.

title: Fix EPLB redundant experts with shared expert fusion and Waterfill
author: xutizhou
body:
## Summary
- pass the physical routed expert count (logical routed + redundant) to DeepEP Waterfill
- detect fused shared checkpoint weights using the logical expert boundary when EPLB metadata is active
- map those shared weights back to the physical shared slot layout used by FusedMoE

title: integrate flash_mla_sparse_fwd
author: zcnrex

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
- `flash_mla_with_kvcache` is slow because of complicated loading logic. Switching to `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` see 1.35x speedup compared to the `flash_mla_with_kvcache` kernel
   - total cuda wall 1.1x speedup
- Chunk prefill only works for <=8192, fails for 32768. (https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25502 has more details on this motivation)
<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

## Modifications
- Use `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` for prefill instead of `flash_mla_with_kvcache`. This is faster because it directly uses TMA load and avoid complicated loading logic.
- A few small kernels to make `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` work.
- Also route (cherry picked from https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25502) long input seq to the `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` kernel to avoid a bug https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/25484.

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->

title: [fp8] SM90 swap-AB scaled_mm dispatch (~1.16x kernel geomean, +5.8-18.5% end-to-end)
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Summary

Replace the in-file SM90 FP8 W8A8 GEMM dispatch in `fp8_gemm_kernel.cu` with a modular swap-AB dispatch in `cutlass_extensions/`. Adds two new dispatch buckets (`M32_N8192` and `M128_smallN`) that close the regression zones a naive swap-AB dispatch would leave behind.

Net result on H200:
- **1.156x geomean** vs main on M ≤ 128 kernel-level (58W / 4L / 84 shapes), no net regression in any M bucket
- **+5.8 – 18.5% end-to-end decode throughput** on Llama-3.1 8B/70B FP8-dynamic

## Motivation

Main's SM90 FP8 dispatch uses tile `<_64, _64, _128>` for all small-M paths. For M_orig ≪ 64 (decode batch=1..16) this wastes a large fraction of the M-tile every iteration — e.g. for M=1 only 1/64 of the M dim is real work, the rest is padding-compute.

Swap-AB transposes the GEMM at the kernel level (D^T = B^T · A^T) so that "kernel M" maps to the much larger N_orig dimension and "kernel N" maps to the small M_orig. Pairing this with smaller kernel-N tiles (16, 32) lets us sit just above M_orig with minimal padding waste, which is the dominant overhead in small-batch decode.

This affects every dense linear in FP8-W8A8 quantized models (Llama / Qwen / Mistral / DeepSeek dense layers / Mixtral etc. with `*-FP8-dynamic` or per-token + per-channel scaled checkpoints), via `apply_fp8_linear → fp8_scaled_mm`. DeepSeek V3 / R1 use blockwise FP8 (separate kernel `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm`) and are **not** affected.

## Changes

### New files (`sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/`)

- `epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_c3x.hpp` (450 lines) — SM90 col/row broadcast loads with runtime per-tensor-or-per-channel selection
- `epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_array_c3x.hpp` (460 lines) — array variant for grouped GEMM
- `epilogue/scaled_mm_epilogues_c3x.hpp` (416 lines) — `ScaledEpilogue`, `ScaledEpilogueBias`, `ScaledEpilogueColumnBias` EVT trees
- `gemm/fp8_gemm_sm90_dispatch.cuh` (~480 lines) — bucketed dispatch:

  | bucket | M | N | tile | cluster | swap |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | M16_N1280 | [1, 16] | ≤ 1280 | `<_64, _16, _256>` | `<_1, _2, _1>` | ✓ |
  | M16_N8192 | [1, 16] | > 1280 | `<_64, _16, _256>` | `<_1, _1, _1>` | ✓ |
  | **M32_N8192** | **(16, 32]** | **> 1280** | **`<_64, _32, _256>`** | **`<_1, _1, _1>`** | ✓ |
  | M64_N1280 | (16, 64] | ≤ 1280 | `<_64, _16, _256>` | `<_1, _4, _1>` | ✓ |
  | M64_N8192 | (32, 64] | > 1280 | `<_64, _64, _256>` | `<_1, _1, _1>` | ✓ |
  | **M128_smallN** | **(64, 128]** | **≤ 4096** | **`<_64, _64, _128>`** | **`<_1, _1, _1>`** | |
  | M128 | (64, 128] | > 4096 | `<_64, _128, _128>` | `<_2, _1, _1>` | |
  | default | > 128 | * | `<_128, _128, _128>` | `<_2, _1, _1>` | |

  The two bolded buckets close regressions the naïve M-only split leaves behind:

  - **M32_N8192**: with kernel-N=64, M_orig=32 wastes 50% of the N-tile (kernel-N = M_orig in swap mode). kernel-N=32 fits M_orig=32 exactly. Recovers M=32 from −9% geomean (vs main) to **+19%**.
  - **M128_smallN**: the larger M128 tile (`<_64, _128, _128>` + cluster `<_2, _1, _1>`) regresses 20-25% vs main on N ≤ 4096; falling back to a smaller tile in that sub-region recovers it.

### Modified

- `csrc/gemm/fp8_gemm_kernel.cu`:
  - 6-line dispatch site change → call `cutlass_scaled_mm_sm90_fp8`
  - **Remove 355 lines of dead code**: the old inline SM90 dispatch (`DeviceGemmFp8RowwiseSm90`, `prepare_sm90_fp8_args`, `launch_sm90_fp8_scaled_mm`, `sm90_fp8_dispatch_bias`, `sm90_fp8_dispatch_shape`) is no longer reachable after the dispatch swap.

### Tests

- `sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py::test_accuracy_sm90_swap_ab` — 60 cases covering each dispatch bucket boundary (15 shapes × bf16/fp16 × bias/no-bias)
- Existing `test_accuracy` (500 cases) still passes — no behavior change for shapes the new dispatch wasn't intended to touch

## Kernel-level benchmark

H200 (SM90), `fp8_e4m3 × bf16`, per-token A scale + per-channel B scale, no bias. `triton.testing.do_bench_cudagraph(rep=200, median)`.

### Geomean speedup vs main (M ≤ 128)

| M | geomean | W / L / total | typical workload |
|---|---:|---|---|
| 1   | **1.13x** | 9W 1L / 12 | chat completion / autocomplete (bs=1) |
| 8   | **1.22x** | 12W 0L / 12 | small-batch decode |
| 16  | **1.24x** | 10W 0L / 12 | EAGLE/MTP draft verify (bs × k_draft) |
| 32  | **1.19x** | 10W 0L / 12 | continuous batching bs=32 |
| 64  | 1.09x | 5W 3L / 12 | |
| 96  | **1.19x** | 6W 0L / 12 | |
| 128 | 1.05x | 6W 0L / 12 | |
| **ALL** | **1.156x** | **58W 4L / 84** | |

Every M bucket has geomean ≥ 1.05x. No bucket regresses on net.

### Largest wins (selected)

| M | N | K | speedup |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 16 | 8192 | 4096 | 2.02x |
| 8 | 8192 | 4096 | 1.90x |
| 32 | 8192 | 4096 | 1.80x |
| 64 | 8192 | 4096 | 1.50x |
| 16 | 4096 | 8192 | 1.31x |

### Remaining individual-shape regressions (4 losses, all ≤ 10%)

| M | N | K | speedup | cause |
|---|---|---|---:|---|
| 1 | 4096 | 4096 | 0.97x | main has `<_1, _8, _1>` cluster A-multicast at this M=1 sweet spot; swap-AB structurally cannot use that direction. Sub-noise. |
| 64 | 14336 | 4096 | 0.94x | similar — medium-M swap-AB loses small N-cluster multicast advantage |
| 64 | 28672 | 4096 | 0.90x | same |
| 64 | 14336 | 8192 | 0.98x | same, smaller magnitude |

Bucket geomeans still net positive everywhere.

### M > 128 (prefill / large-batch)

Dispatch path for M > 128 is unchanged from main. Verified geomean = 1.000x ± noise on M ∈ {256, 512, 1024, 2048, 4096} bench. No regression introduced.

## End-to-end decode benchmark

H200, `sglang.bench_one_batch`, input_len=32, output_len=64, TP=1, `--mem-fraction-static 0.75` for 70B. Toggle pattern: bench this PR → `git stash + checkout main + pip install -e .` → bench main → restore. Same GPU, same Python interpreter, same model snapshot.

### Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct-FP8-dynamic

| bs | main tok/s | this PR tok/s | speedup | main ms/tok | this PR ms/tok |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
|  1 |   42.31 |   49.03 | **+15.9%** | 23.64 | 20.40 |
|  8 |  321.75 |  381.29 | **+18.5%** | 24.86 | 20.98 |
| 16 |  655.29 |  755.56 | **+15.3%** | 24.42 | 21.18 |
| 32 | 1279.80 | 1457.20 | **+13.9%** | 25.00 | 21.96 |

70B amplifies the gain 2.7-5× vs 8B because the per-layer linear time dominates decode latency more strongly at the larger hidden size (8192 vs 4096), more layers (80 vs 32), and stronger HBM-bandwidth-bound regime.

For 70B chat completion at bs=1: 23.64 → 20.40 ms/token saves ~640 ms on a 200-token reply.

## Non-goals / explored-but-rejected

The following were tried during development and reverted; documenting here so future contributors don't repeat them:

- **Stream-K scheduler on small-M paths**: structurally blocked — CUTLASS static_asserts that only `KernelTmaWarpSpecializedCooperative*` supports Stream-K, and Cooperative requires TileM ≥ 128, which conflicts with the swap-AB small-M tile design (TileM=64).
- **`KernelTmaWarpSpecializedCooperativeFP8FastAccum` on the M > 128 default config**: measured −8% geomean vs Pingpong baseline (41 losses, 2 wins on M ∈ [256, 4096]). The existing Pingpong + PersistentScheduler is already at the sweet spot for these tiles.
- **`max_swizzle_size = 4/8` on default / M128 configs**: measured −50%+ on several mid-M shapes. Suspected interaction with `RasterOrderOptions::Heuristic` or scheduler/tile mismatch; not pursued further.

## Test plan

- [x] `pytest sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py::test_accuracy` (500 cases) — all pass
- [x] `pytest sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py::test_accuracy_sm90_swap_ab` (60 cases) — all pass
- [x] Kernel-level benchmark on H200 (above)
- [x] End-to-end Llama-3.1-8B FP8-dynamic decode bs=1..32 (above)
- [x] End-to-end Llama-3.1-70B FP8-dynamic decode bs=1..32 (above)
- [ ] CI passes (existing `test_fp8_gemm.py` exercises the new dispatch automatically; new `test_accuracy_sm90_swap_ab` is picked up by pytest collection)

## Files changed

```
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_array_c3x.hpp | 460 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/epilogue/broadcast_load_epilogue_c3x.hpp       | 450 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/epilogue/scaled_mm_epilogues_c3x.hpp           | 416 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/cutlass_extensions/gemm/fp8_gemm_sm90_dispatch.cuh                | 480 +++++
sgl-kernel/csrc/gemm/fp8_gemm_kernel.cu                                           |   7 +- (and −355 dead code)
sgl-kernel/tests/test_fp8_gemm.py                                                 |  30 +
sgl-kernel/benchmark/bench_fp8_gemm_swap_ab.py                                    | 100 +
```

title: Use DeepGEMM BF16 for unquantized DeepEP LL MoE
author: YAMY1234
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This is a follow-up to #24906. The merged implementation enabled BF16 DeepEP dispatch for every `quant_config=None` MoE layer, which is too broad. This PR narrows the behavior to the target case: unquantized DeepEP low-latency MoE on CUDA, used by the Qwen3.5 NVFP4 MTP/NextN draft MoE path.

The Qwen3.5 NVFP4 main decode MoE can use `flashinfer_cutedsl + DeepEP`, but the MTP/NextN draft MoE is unquantized (`quant_config=None`). For this draft path, DeepEP low-latency dispatch should keep BF16 activations and let the existing unquantized `FusedMoE` path run the DeepGEMM BF16 masked runner.

This branch now includes #25525, where `flashinfer_cutedsl + DeepEP` is already migrated to `MoeRunner`, and #22822, which adds the DeepEP dispatcher output dtype mechanism. The narrow unquantized DeepEP LL case now uses `dispatcher_output_dtype=bf16` rather than the previous temporary `bf16_dispatch` key.

## Modifications

- Restrict BF16 DeepEP dispatch to unquantized low-latency DeepEP LL MoE on non-NPU/non-HIP backends, and only when the active MoE runner is `deep_gemm`, using #22822 `dispatcher_output_dtype=bf16`.
- Set `deprecate_flag=True` for that narrow case so execution delegates to the generic `FusedMoE` path: dispatch, `quant_method.apply`, DeepGEMM runner, and combine.
- Remove the local PyTorch `forward_unquantized_deepep_ll` fallback.
- Keep the #25525 `flashinfer_cutedsl + DeepEP` MoeRunner path intact; this PR does not reintroduce the old `forward_flashinfer_cutedsl` path.

## Accuracy Tests

Accuracy was checked with GSM8K using the matched harness: 5-shot, `max_tokens=16384`, `temperature=0.0`.

| job | model / path | harness | score | latency s | output tok/s | note |

title: [MoE Refactor] [NPU] Refactor Ascend MoE implementation to reduce code duplication and align with community design
author: OrangeRedeng
body: ## Overview This PR addresses two major issues in the current Ascend MoE (Mixture of Experts) implementation: 1. **High code duplication** – Many places required changes whenever the MoE logic was updated, leading to high maintenance overhead and inconsistency risks. 2. **Deviation from community design** – dispatching and grouped-GEMM were hard‑coded in a monolithic `apply` flow and scattered across multiple files to handle different quantization formats, blocking integration with the standard **All‑to‑All backend** and **MoE Runner** pattern defined in [#8715](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8715). This PR solves both issues with a clean **issue → solution** approach: - **5‑component decomposition** eliminates duplication and makes each piece independently testable and swappable which allow, for example independent quantization **for each matmul**. - **New Ascend MoE Runner** and **Ascend A2A Backend** fully align with the community routing architecture and separate computation from communication. The result is a maintainable, extensible NPU MoE stack that works uniformly across all quantization schemes (Unquant, AWQ, GPTQ, ModelSlim, CompressedTensors, GGUF) and all dispatchers (NPU native, DeepEP normal/low‑latency, FuseEP). ## Issue 1: Code Duplication → 5‑Component Decomposition ### The problem Before this PR, the MoE forward pass was duplicated in multiple places. Each copy repeated the same sequence of steps: ```tokens routing```, ```first w13 gate_up_proj grouped matmul```, ```activation```, ```second w2 down_proj grouped matmul```, and ```finalize routing```. When a new kernel arrived or a bug was found, developers had to track down **every** copy and apply the same fix. This was error‑prone and discouraged experimentation. ### Legacy Code Disunity Map ```text LEGACY FRAGMENTED FILESYSTEM python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/ │ ├── 📄 unquant.py ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu, Gelu, Swiglu_oai] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] ├── 📄 gguf.py ──► [Routing V1] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ ‎python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/fused_moe_method_npu.py │ ├── 📄 w4a4 apply() ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ │ │ └── 📄 w4a4 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ ├── 📄 w4a8 apply() ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Unpermute] │ │ │ └── 📄 w4a8 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ ├── 📄 w8a8 apply_prefill() ──► [Routing V1] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [dequant_swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ │ │ 📄 w8a8 apply_decode() ──► [Routing V2] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [dequant_swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Unpermute] │ │ │ └── 📄 w8a8 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [dequant_swiglu_quant] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ └── 📄 w4a16 apply() ──► [Routing V1] ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] ──► [Finalize] │ └── 📄 w4a16 apply_without_routing() ──► [w13 MatMul] ──► [Swiglu] ──► [w2 MatMul] │ 🚨 Maintenance Bottleneck: ─────────┘ Updating any kernel or fixing a bug required updating identical code logic across ALL 10 isolated places. ``` ### The solution: 5 reusable components We split the pipeline into five abstract components and just call each of them when they are needed, each with a clear `Base*` interface: | Component | Responsibility | File path | |-----------|----------------|----------------| | **Initial Routing** | Maps tokens to target experts (top-k processing and token permutation) | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/init_routing.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-f02f1521aae576082ebb67fce7f43977bfbfc95395cd80266167d91696a08d78) | | **Hidden States Quant** | Optional dynamic/static quantisation of activations before matmul | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/hidden_states_quant.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-2cc1b30a86e9efba3c06e5bd2c7d6d4e8cfbfecbcc130a16d9fdc856fbe45126) | | **Grouped Matmul** | Coordinates expert-parallel matrix multiplications across arbitrary precision variants (FP16, W4A4, W8A8, etc.) | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/matmul.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-a1fa2ce9efcc44edc1fa3f19f3e2183227da34602667cee2b8cee2c724150908) | | **Activation** | Processes non-linear operations (SwiGLU, GELU) along with integrated dequantization or/and quantization steps | [‎python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/activation.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-ba4346a5deb6a84d17b721af656d30bf50c1164e16b21db349e2ffaf142fdc7c) | | **Finalize Routing** | Reassembles expert outputs into original token order | [python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/finalize_routing.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-9045dc3acd5ac53496c175a744aa85c0137cbb1ee5d1779a0d1b4704188c37c5) | Every component has NPU‑specific implementations (e.g., `NPUMoEInitRouting_v1`, `NPUSwigluQuant`, `GroupedMatmul`). The runner selects the right set at runtime based on the model config and quantization scheme. Example of [‎python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/activation.py](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/25663/changes#diff-ba4346a5deb6a84d17b721af656d30bf50c1164e16b21db349e2ffaf142fdc7c) scheme ```text Activation.py Orchestration Layer ├── BaseActivation (Abstract Base Interface) │ └── Unified execution signature: forward(x, *args, **kwargs) │ ├── Standard Precision Kernels │ ├── NPUSwiglu -> Traditional SwiGLU operation │ ├── NPUGeluAndMul -> GELU-based gated linear unit variations │ └── NPUSwigluOAI -> Open AI style compatible SwiGLU formulation │ ├── Quantization & Specialized Kernels │ ├── NPUSwigluQuant -> SwiGLU with integrated INT8 quantization processing │ ├── NPUSwigluQuantWithScales -> SwiGLU with precision-aware scaling factor handling │ └── NPUSwigluStepAndMul -> Multi-step fused activation logic │ └── Dispatcher Integrations └── NPUSwigluDeepEPKernel -> Low-latency communication-fused activation for DeepEP ``` ## Issue 2: Community Design → Ascend MoE Runner & A2A Backend The legacy codebase lacked alignment with the standardized SGLang community routing model laid out in [issue #8715](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8715). Multi-NPU Tensor Parallelism (TP) was implemented via fragmented, ad-hoc routines. Functions like ```apply()``` and ```apply_without_routing()``` mixed core mathematical calculations with distributed communication primitives, preventing proper support for optimized dispatches like DeepEP. ### The solution: Unified AscendRunnerCore & Ascend A2A Backend We designed a unified MoE Runner (AscendRunnerCore) to manage the centralized execution block, completely deprecating legacy apply_without_routing routines. Alongside this, we implemented a dedicated NPU All-to-All (A2A) backend leveraging and follow community scheme: ```text [input_hidden_states] | v TopK.forward -> `select_experts` / `triton_kernels.routing` / bypass | V [TopKOutput] | v FusedMoE.forward -> Dispatcher.dispatch -> DeepEP / AscendTP <-- NEW A2A Backend | | | v | [DispatchOutput] | | | v | quant_method.apply -> AscendMoeRunner.run <-- NEW MoE Runner | | | | | v | | pre-permute + grouped_gemm + post-permute | | | | |-------------------------------- | v | [CombineInput] | | | v | Dispatcher.combine -> DeepEP / AscendTP / bypass | | |--------------------- v [final_hidden_states] ``` ### AscendMoERunner and – from monolithic `apply` to composable stages Structural Evolution: Old vs. New Execution Flow The mathematical operations (matmul1, activation, matmul2) have been extracted from monolithic wrapper configurations into separate sequential execution stages managed cleanly by the new runner core: - Matmul, activation, and the second matmul have been moved out of the old `apply` blob into **independent, swappable stages**. - The runner can now support **any** quantisation (unquant, W4A4, W8A8, etc.) by simply picking the right component implementations. - It fully supports DeepEP normal and low‑latency modes through pre/post‑permute hooks, without duplicating the core pipeline. ### Mapping the old monolithic file to the new composable structure The diff in `fused_moe_method_npu.py` looks large because we **deleted all the duplicated kernel‑calling logic** and replaced it with thin method wrappers. The actual computation was moved into five reusable components (listed in the table and picture above) and a new file that holds the `AscendMoERunner` orchestration. | Old location (`fused_moe_method_npu.py`) | New location(s) | |-------------------------------------------------------|----------------------------------------------------------------------------------| | `npu_fused_experts_w4a4()` | Removed – handled by `AscendMoERunner` + `AscendTPDispatcher` | | `npu_fused_experts()` | Removed – same pattern as above, now in `AscendMoERunner` + `AscendTPDispatcher`, bf16 code is separated into new `NPUUnquantMoEMethod` in new `moe_methods.py` file | | `npu_fused_experts_w8a8_decode()` | Removed – decode‑specific path merged with `npu_fused_experts()` prefill‑specific path (The measurements did not show the advantages of separation) | | `npu_fused_moe_without_routing_weights_bf16()` | Removed – logic moved to `AscendMoERunner` pre/post-permute DeepEP hooks | | `fused_moe_npu()` (deprecated) | Kept with deprecation warning to ensure backward compatibility with models that do not use the FusedMoE class yet | | `maybe_apply_deepep_npu()` | Removed – logic moved to `AscendMoERunner` pre/post-permute DeepEP hooks | | `maybe_apply_fuseep_weights()` | The logic is preserved and adapted to the existing structure in new `moe_methods.py`, does not use Runner infrastructure | | `NPUW4A4Int4DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUW4A4Int4MoEMethod` in new `moe_methods.py` – now it is used for each MatMul separately | | `NPUW8A8Int8DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUW8A8Int8MoEMethod` – same way | | `NPUW4A8Int8DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUW4A8Int8MoEMethod` – same way | | `NPUW4A16Int4DynamicMoEMethod` | Rewritten as `NPUWNA16Int4MoEMethod` – same way | | `_NPUFusedMoEMethodBase` | Replaced by `_NPUMoEMethodBase` in new `moe_methods.py` file | The **new file** (`python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/quantization/moe_methods.py`) now contains **only** the configuration and lightweight delegation code; the heavy logic lives in: - `AscendMoERunner` – `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/ascend.py` - `AscendTPDispatcher` – `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/token_dispatcher/ascend_tp.py` - `InitRouting` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/init_routing.py` - `HiddenStatesQuant` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/hidden_states_quant.py` - `GroupedMatmul` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/matmul.py` - `Activation` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/activation.py` - `FinalizeRouting` – `python/sglang/srt/hardware_backend/npu/moe/finalize_routing.py` ### AscendA2ABackend – clean separation of TP communication Tensor‑parallel expert routing (All‑to‑All) used to be buried inside the old `apply` functions. The new **AscendA2ABackend** extracts this into a dedicated communication module that implements: - `init_routing` – dispatches tokens to the correct expert shards across NPUs. - `finalize_routing` – collects sharded expert outputs and reassembles them in the original token order. **Advantages:** 1. **Testability** – the routing logic can be unit‑tested in isolation (no real computation needed). 2. **Portability** – different hardware backends (e.g., NVIDIA NCCL, Ascend HCCL) can provide their own A2A implementations while the MoE runner stays unchanged. 3. **Extensibility** – upcoming communication backends (DeepEP, FuseEP) can be integrated without touching the core MoE logic. By moving TP init/finalize routing out of the monolithic `apply` and into this backend, the architecture now mirrors exactly the community pattern from [#8715](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/8715), enabling future shared improvements across all backends. --- ## Additional Improvements (Side Effects of the Refactor) - **AWQ**, **GGUF**, **GPTQ**, **Auto-round** now can be used with DeepEP (previously it didn't work for this quantization frameworks). - **AWQ** models compatibility were improved by implementing new unquant path for Linear to to circumvent ```torch_npu.npu_weight_quant_batchmatmul``` kernel limitations. - **AWQ** MoE now uses 2x times less memory after ```process_weights_after_loading``` redesign. - **Modelslim** now supports mix-bits quantized MoE models (with different w13/w2 quant schemes). - **GGUF** performance were improved by adding npu_format_cast to enable NZ weights format. - **GPTQ** performance and accuracy were improved by using new kernels versions. - **GPTQ** add scales expanded size does not match K_shard warning and support negative-scale correction skipping. - **W4A4 NZ format fix** – the NPU kernel now correctly uses the native NZ memory layout (instead of forced ND), giving up to **5-10% speedup**. - **Improved int4 packing** – support improved int4 packing using ```SGLANG_NPU_W4A4_NEW_PACKING=True``` env variable, two int4 values are now stored in one int8, halving the memory footprint during weight loading. - **def fused_moe_npu()** now deprecated and will be removed in future releases. Reverts https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/29503 to avoid performance drops --- ## Accuracy Tests ## Speed Tests and Profiling ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 4. title: [EPD][Perf] Async image preprocessing and cross-request ViT batching for encode_server
author: ntgiang71096
body:
## Motivation

The EPD encoder server (`encode_server.py`) processes image preprocessing
(PIL resize + normalize via `image_processor()`) synchronously on the asyncio
event loop. Under N concurrent requests, all preprocessing is serialized —
each request waits for the previous one to finish. Additionally, after
preprocessing completes, each request triggers its own individual ViT forward
pass rather than batching across concurrent requests arriving at the same time.

## Modifications

### 1. Async image preprocessing (`preproc_executor`)

Moves `image_processor()` calls off the asyncio event loop into a dedicated
`ThreadPoolExecutor` via `run_in_executor`. N concurrent requests now
preprocess images in parallel without blocking request acceptance or each other.

A separate executor (`preproc_executor`) is used instead of the existing
`self.executor` (which handles ZMQ sends) to prevent contention under high
concurrency.

Configurable via `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS` (default: 8).

### 2. Cross-request ViT batching (`_vit_batch_loop`)

Adds an asyncio queue (`_vit_queue`) and a background coroutine
(`_vit_batch_loop`) that collects concurrently preprocessed images and runs
them as a single batched ViT forward pass instead of N separate ones.

**Adaptive sleep:** when the queue already has items the loop yields
immediately (`asyncio.sleep(0)`); it only waits `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`
(default: 20 ms) when the queue is empty, avoiding unnecessary latency for
staggered arrivals while still allowing batch accumulation.

Configurable via:
- `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE` (default: 8) — max requests per ViT batch
- `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` (default: 20) — batch accumulation window

Unit tests added in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encode_server_perf.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

No change to model outputs. Preprocessing and ViT inference are unchanged;
only the scheduling of when they execute changes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Benchmarked with `sglang.bench_serving` on AMD MI355X, Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B, EPD 1E1P.
`output_len=1` isolates the encoder path (preprocessing + ViT + ZMQ + PD prefill); no decode pressure — metric is end-to-end request latency.

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
    --backend sglang \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port <pd_port> \
    --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B \
    --dataset-name image \
    --image-count 8 \
    --image-resolution 720p \
    --num-prompts 100 \
    --random-input-len 128 \
    --random-output-len 1 \
    --max-concurrency 16
```

Encoder env (as measured): `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE=16`. Note: `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS` was at its then-default of 32, but `--max-concurrency 16` caps in-flight requests, so effective preproc parallelism is 16 — any value ≥16 reproduces these numbers. The default is now **8** (per @ShangmingCai review): for this workload that means ~2 preprocessing waves instead of 1, still well clear of stock's 16-wide event-loop serialization (the source of the gain). Tunable via the env var.

| Config | Median E2E Latency | Throughput | vs Stock |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Stock (no patch) | 5,820 ms | 2.59 req/s | — |
| This PR | 4,705 ms | 3.19 req/s | **−19% latency, +23% tput** |

Both changes are platform-agnostic (standard Python asyncio + `concurrent.futures`).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). — ran `pre-commit run --all-files`, all hooks passed.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). — added 5 tests in `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encode_server_perf.py` covering async preprocessing concurrency and ViT batch queue correctness.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). — no existing docs page for `encode_server` configuration; the three new env vars (`SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS`) are documented in the Modifications section above.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). — accuracy unaffected (no change to model outputs); speed results provided in Speed Tests section.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). — covered by pre-commit (Black, Ruff, isort, codespell).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

cc @ShangmingCai @liusy58 @ZhengWG @gty111 @ByronHsu @hnyls2002 @mickqian

---

## Update 2026-05-26: Scope narrowed to async preprocessing only

Per reviewer feedback from @liusy58, this PR is narrowed to keep only the
async preprocessing change. Cross-request ViT batching is dropped because
PR #25964 covers it at a coarser layer (its `EncoderScheduler` +
`batch_encode` fuses the HF processor call too). The two changes compose:
async preprocessing keeps the event loop free so #25964's batch worker
actually sees concurrent requests, instead of seeing them arrive
one-at-a-time after each blocking processor call.

**Removed:** `_vit_queue` / `_vit_task` / `_vit_batch_loop` /
`_ensure_vit_batch_loop`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_SIZE` and
`SGLANG_ENCODER_BATCH_TIMEOUT_MS` env vars, `TestViTBatchQueue` test class
(4 tests).

**Kept:** `preproc_executor`, `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS`
(now in `sglang.srt.environ`, default 8), `run_in_executor` wrapping for
image / video / audio preprocessing.

### Performance note

The narrowed scope does **not** lose measurable perf on this benchmark.
The "This PR" row was measured with ViT batching included. Re-measuring
the same workload with ViT batching removed (async preprocessing only)
gives −18% lat / +26% tput — essentially the same as the table row,
within run-to-run noise. The current benchmark setup doesn't exercise
the ViT-batching improvement enough to show a distinguishable delta.

### Inline review threads
- @ZhengWG: apply `run_in_executor` to video/audio paths — **kept** in this PR.
- @ZhengWG: switch to grouped batched ViT call (`fn(group_items)`) — **moot**,
  the batching block is removed entirely.
- @liusy58: add comments / extract helpers on `_vit_batch_loop` lines
  1128–1161 — **resolved by deletion**.

## Update 2026-05-29: code-owner review (@ShangmingCai)

- `SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS` default lowered **32 → 8**.
- Moved it into `sglang.srt.environ` (`EnvInt(8)`, EPD group); `encode_server.py` now reads it via `envs.SGLANG_ENCODER_PREPROC_WORKERS.get()`.
- Removed `test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_encode_server_perf.py` (it exercised asyncio/ThreadPoolExecutor on mocks rather than the encoder path, so it wasn't protecting much).

title: loader: yield filtered MTP weights lazily to avoid OOM hang on multi-layer EAGLE
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Summary

`DefaultModelLoader._filter_mtp_weights` was materializing the entire filtered checkpoint into a `tuple` before returning, which defeated the bounded sliding-window in `buffered_multi_thread_safetensors_weights_iterator` (`buffer_size = max_workers + 1`).

With multi-layer EAGLE on large MoE checkpoints (e.g. MiMo-V2.5-Pro, ~963 GiB fp8), each TP rank instantiates `speculative_num_steps` draft runners (each with its own `draft_model_idx`), and every runner independently re-scans the full checkpoint. The eager `tuple(filtered_weights)` held the full prefix-renamed payload resident on CPU per runner — at TP=8 with 3 draft runners that's enough live tensors per host to push it into page reclaim. The visible symptom was:

- All scheduler threads stuck on `futex_do_wait`
- `/proc/<pid>/io read_bytes = 0`, no `rchar` growth
- No progress past `Found local HF snapshot ... skipping download.`
- Identical on virtiofs and local NVMe (rules out storage)

Switching to a generator preserves behavior (callers already iterate the result; sibling `_get_weights_iterator` paths already return generators) while letting the buffered upstream actually bound CPU memory.

## Test plan

Tested on 8× B200 with MiMo-V2.5-Pro (~963 GiB fp8) and the default `enable_multithread_load=True`:

| | before (default `enable_multithread_load=True`) | after (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Server ready | **hangs indefinitely** (all sched in `futex_do_wait`) | ~2.5 min |
| GSM8K (200, parallel=4) | n/a (hung) | score 0.97 |
| avg accept_rate | n/a | 0.755 (over 307 batches) |
| avg accept_length | n/a | 3.27 (max 4) |
| gen throughput | n/a | ~700 tok/s |

Behaviour with the previous `--model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load":false}'` workaround is unchanged: same accept_rate (0.753 → 0.755), same GSM8K score (0.975 → 0.97 — within noise), but server is now ~30 % faster to ready because the multi-thread loader is actually live.

Launch:
\`\`\`bash
export SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2=1
sglang serve --trust-remote-code --model-path XiaomiMiMo/MiMo-V2.5-Pro --tp 8 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_trtllm --attention-backend fa4 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --max-running-requests 128 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.1 \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
  --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --enable-multi-layer-eagle \
  --reasoning-parser mimo --tool-call-parser mimo \
  --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
\`\`\`

title: [DeepSeek-V4] Add mhc_fused_post_pre kernel
author: JoeLee314
body: # [DeepSeek-V4] Add fused mHC post/pre kernel ## Motivation This PR optimizes the DeepSeek-V4 mHC path by fusing the boundary between one mHC post step and the next mHC pre step. The approach is adapted from TRTLLM. The main idea is to avoid launching separate kernels for the latency-sensitive decode path: ```text mhc_post -> pre-norm GEMM -> mhc_pre finalization ``` The fused path keeps the existing numerically sensitive `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization stage, but removes the separate post/pre scheduling boundary. For small token batches, a TileLang scalar-FMA kernel computes the following work in one launch: ```text previous hc_post + bf16 residual materialization + pre-norm GEMM partials + RMS square-sum partials ``` For larger token batches, the implementation keeps the existing high-throughput TileLang `mhc_post` + DeepGEMM decomposition. The optimization is guarded by a new env var: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE=1 ``` It intentionally depends on the existing TileLang mHC switches: ```bash SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_PRE=1 SGLANG_OPT_USE_TILELANG_MHC_POST=1 ``` because the fused implementation directly reuses the TileLang mHC tensor layouts and the `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization kernels. ## Performance Test total_throughput increased by 3.35% ### Performance summary ## Accuracy / Correctness Tests GSM8K score: 0.975 ## Modifications ### `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` Add: ```python SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE = EnvBool(False) ``` ### `python/sglang/srt/layers/mhc.py` - Add `mhc_fused_post_pre_fma_tilelang`, a small-token fused TileLang kernel. - Add `mhc_fused_post_pre`, which dispatches: - small batches to the fused FMA kernel; - larger batches to the existing TileLang `mhc_post` + DeepGEMM path. - Preserve the existing `mhc_pre_big_fuse(_with_norm)` finalization stage. - Handle zero-token DP/EP ranks with correctly typed empty tensors. ### `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py` - Add fused mHC enable check cached in `__init__`. - Fuse: - cross-layer previous FFN `hc_post` + next attention `hc_pre`; - within-layer attention `hc_post` + FFN `hc_pre`. - Defer the final FFN `hc_post` and close it at model tail. - Cache bf16 RMSNorm weights for the fused path to avoid per-forward casts. ### `python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4_nextn.py` - Adapt NextN decoder usage to the decoder layer returning deferred fused state. ### `tests/kernels/test_mhc_kernels.py` - Add coverage for `mhc_fused_post_pre` vs the unfused reference sequence. ## Checklist - [x] Added fused mHC post/pre boundary optimization. - [x] Added env guard `SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_MHC_POST_PRE`. - [x] Kept the fused path dependent on TileLang mHC pre/post kernels. - [x] Added kernel unit test for fused vs unfused mHC. - [x] Verified operator-level precision. - [x] Verified short deterministic sanity prompts. - [x] Verified GSM8K-200 end-to-end accuracy. - [x] Verified `bench_serving` performance improvement on DeepSeek-V4-Flash. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26549213709](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26549213709) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26549213622](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26549213622)
