title: Apply apply_group_norm_silu to LTX-2 latent upsampler
author: pengdurice
body:
## Motivation The LTX-2 spatial **`LatentUpsampler`** (`runtime/models/upsampler/latent_upsampler.py`) is auto-loaded as the `spatial_upsampler` component of every LTX-2 two-stage pipeline — Lightricks generates latents at lower spatial resolution and uses this module to upscale them by 2× before VAE decode, so it sits on the critical path of every LTX-2 generation. Its `LatentUpsampler` and `ResBlock` modules use `torch.nn.GroupNorm(32, ...) + torch.nn.SiLU()` at multiple sites, but the existing inline `silu(norm(x))` pattern bypasses the Triton-fused `apply_group_norm_silu` helper that HunyuanVAE already routes through. This PR plumbs the helper into the three eligible direct-`silu(norm(x))` sites in `latent_upsampler.py`, picking up a **6.5×–14× kernel speedup on H100** (vs eager `silu(group_norm(x))`) without changing model outputs. The speedup factors into a ~1.55× SiLU+GroupNorm fusion win (constant across shapes) and a 4×–9× parallelization win that scales with per-group size; see [Speed Tests and Profiling](#speed-tests-and-profiling) for the decomposition. This also addresses the "kernel fusion instead of compiler-driven fusion" line under Performance Improvements in [Roadmap] SGLang-Diffusion (26 Q2) (#23035). ## Modifications - **`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/upsampler/latent_upsampler.py`** — route three `silu(norm(x))` sites through `apply_group_norm_silu`: | Site | Class | Hit per `LatentUpsampler.forward` | |---|---|---| | `initial_norm` + `initial_activation` | `LatentUpsampler.forward` (both 2D and 3D paths) | 1 | | `norm1` + `activation` | `ResBlock.forward` (one per ResBlock) | `2 * num_blocks_per_stage` | At the default `num_blocks_per_stage=4` this is **9 fused sites per upsampler call** (1 initial + 4 pre-upsample ResBlocks + 4 post-upsample ResBlocks). The second norm site inside `ResBlock` (`silu(norm2(x) + residual)` at line 118) is deliberately left on the eager path with an inline comment — the current `apply_group_norm_silu` helper only covers `silu(norm(x))`, not the `silu(norm(x) + residual)` pattern. A follow-up `apply_group_norm_add_silu` kernel would catch those remaining 8 sites per generation (doubling fusion coverage on this module); it's out of scope here. - **`python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/diffusion/bench_group_norm_silu.py`** — add three LTX-2 latent upsampler shape cases (`ltx2_upsampler_small`, `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p`, `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p`) at `num_groups=32`, bracketing the production shape range that Lightricks ships in the LTX-2.3 spatial upscaler checkpoints. The `post_720p` case is ~471M bf16 elements (~940 MB), making the kernel asymptotically HBM-bandwidth-bound. This bench is registered with `disabled="standalone benchmark"`, so it never appears in the regular CI memory budget. - **`python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_latent_upsampler_group_norm_silu.py`** (new file) — 19 unit tests (10 CPU-fp32 wiring + 9 CUDA bf16/fp16 production-path parity, the CUDA tests gated on `torch.cuda.is_available()`). ## Accuracy Tests Zero-tolerance parity vs the original eager `silu(norm(x))` chain on CPU plus CUDA-tolerance parity on the production fast path: ```bash $ PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider \ python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_latent_upsampler_group_norm_silu.py -v ... ================ 19 passed, 16 warnings in 8.89s ================ ``` **Coverage:** | Test | Tier | What it pins | |---|---|---| | `test_resblock_forward_parity` (3 parametrized) | CPU fp32 | `ResBlock.forward` output bit-identical (`atol=0.0, rtol=0.0`) to an explicit `activation(norm(x))` reference. CPU helper fallback path. | | `test_latent_upsampler_forward_parity` (2 parametrized) | CPU fp32 | Same for `LatentUpsampler.forward` across 2D + 3D conv paths. | | `test_resblock_fuses_exactly_one_site` | CPU fp32 | Patches `apply_group_norm_silu` and asserts exactly 1 call per `ResBlock.forward` (the residual-add `norm2` site must stay eager). | | `test_latent_upsampler_fuses_expected_sites` (3 parametrized) | CPU fp32 | Asserts call count equals `1 + 2 * num_blocks_per_stage` (i.e., 5, 9 across configs). | | `test_latent_upsampler_module_wires_fused_helper` | CPU fp32 | Smoke test: module imports `apply_group_norm_silu` at top level. | | **`test_resblock_forward_parity_cuda`** (4 parametrized) | **CUDA bf16/fp16** | `ResBlock.forward` on CUDA actually fires `triton_group_norm_silu`; output matches eager reference within kernel-side tolerance (bf16: `atol=7e-2, rtol=2e-2`; fp16: `atol=3e-3, rtol=3e-3`). | | **`test_latent_upsampler_forward_parity_cuda`** (4 parametrized) | **CUDA bf16/fp16** | Full `LatentUpsampler.forward` end-to-end parity. fp16 tolerance is intentionally looser (`atol=2e-2, rtol=1e-1`) to absorb the multi-layer fp16 quantization drift through the 8+ downstream conv layers; bf16 stays at kernel-side tolerance because bf16 has fp32-equivalent exponent range. | | **`test_resblock_actually_uses_triton_kernel_cuda`** | **CUDA bf16** | Patches `triton_group_norm_silu` and asserts `call_count >= 1` — explicit proof the production path doesn't silently fall back to eager. | The Triton kernel itself is already covered by `python/sglang/jit_kernel/tests/diffusion/test_group_norm_silu.py` (parametrized over `(shape, num_groups, dtype)`, registered via `register_cuda_ci`). ## Speed Tests and Profiling Measured on H100 SXM5 (`p5.48xlarge`, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0`) via the bench script added in this PR: ```bash PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 .venv/bin/python \ python/sglang/jit_kernel/benchmark/diffusion/bench_group_norm_silu.py \ --cases ltx2_upsampler_small,ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p,ltx2_upsampler_post_720p \ --dtypes bf16,fp16 --rounds 3 --warmup 25 --rep 100 ``` | case | dtype | shape | native (µs) | fused (µs) | speedup | |---|---|---|---:|---:|---:| | `ltx2_upsampler_small` | bf16 | 1×512×8×45×80 | 452.00 | 70.05 | **6.45×** | | `ltx2_upsampler_small` | fp16 | 1×512×8×45×80 | 451.49 | 69.22 | 6.52× | | `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p` | bf16 | 1×512×16×90×160 | 3 468.27 | 261.87 | **13.24×** | | `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p` | fp16 | 1×512×16×90×160 | 3 468.50 | 260.26 | 13.33× | | `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p` | bf16 | 1×512×16×180×320 | 13 710.72 | 987.52 | **13.88×** | | `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p` | fp16 | 1×512×16×180×320 | 13 717.54 | 984.90 | 13.93× | Geomean kernel speedup on LTX-2 upsampler shapes: **~10.7×**. **Where the speedup comes from.** A 13.9× speedup deserves scrutiny, so I forced the kernel onto its non-chunked one-pass path (same parallelism as PyTorch's `native_group_norm` CUDA kernel — one block per `(batch, group)` pair) and re-measured. The headline decomposes cleanly into two roughly multiplicative factors: | case | fusion-only
`native / one-pass` | parallelization
`one-pass / chunked` | total
`native / chunked` | |---|---:|---:|---:| | `ltx2_upsampler_small` | 1.56× | 3.94× | 6.13× | | `ltx2_upsampler_pre_720p` | 1.56× | 8.57× | 13.34× | | `ltx2_upsampler_post_720p` | 1.55× | 8.96× | 13.91× | 1. **Fusion contributes a flat ~1.55×**, constant across shapes — exactly what's expected for collapsing `F.silu(...)` into the apply pass: one full-tensor read + write saved per call, theoretical ceiling 2×. 2. **Chunked Welford parallelization contributes 4× → 9×**, scaling with per-group size. PyTorch's `native_group_norm` CUDA kernel (and Triton's own one-pass fallback) both launch one block per `(batch, group)` pair → **32 blocks on a 132-SM H100, ~24% SM occupancy**, with per-block work serialized across the entire `group_size` (461 K → 14.7 M elements as shape grows). The production `_launch_chunked` path splits each group into 8 192-element chunks reduced in parallel → **~57 600 programs for `post_720p`**, achieving **~2.87 TB/s = 86% of H100 HBM peak**. PyTorch's path tops out at ~12% of HBM peak on the same workload — not a memory-traffic problem, a parallelism problem. To reproduce the decomposition, override the threshold at runtime: ```python from sglang.jit_kernel.diffusion.triton import group_norm_silu as gns gns._LARGE_GROUP_THRESHOLD = 10**10 # force one-pass path ``` **Where this generalizes.** Smaller DiT-side `group_norm` call sites will see only the fusion-only **~1.5×** factor; the 6×+ headline numbers are specific to **large VAE/upsampler-style shapes** where per-group size is large enough that PyTorch's per-group kernel is severely under-parallelized on Hopper. The existing HunyuanVAE wiring that this PR follows has similar (large per-group) shapes, which is why the same kernel pays off there too. **E2E translation.** Each `LatentUpsampler.forward` call fires the helper 9 times — 5 sites at the pre-upsample resolution (1 initial + 4 pre-upsample ResBlocks) and 4 sites at the post-upsample resolution (4 post-upsample ResBlocks). For a 720p clip, naive multi-site savings: | Sites | Per-call saved (bf16) | × count | Subtotal | |---|---:|---:|---:| | Pre-upsample (initial + 4 pre ResBlocks) | ~3.2 ms | × 5 | ~16 ms | | Post-upsample (4 post ResBlocks) | ~12.7 ms | × 4 | ~51 ms | **Total saved per generation: ~67 ms** of `LatentUpsampler.forward` wall time on H100. The latent upsampler is one bounded subsystem of a multi-second LTX-2 generation, so relative E2E gain is small in absolute terms — but it represents 20–45% of the upsampler's own runtime budget, and every LTX-2 generation pays it. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #26735497021](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26735497021) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #26735496918](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26735496918)

title: [GDN] Support SM100 CuTeDSL GDN Prefill Kernel
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Summary - Port the SM100 (Blackwell) CuTeDSL chunkwise GDN prefill kernel from vLLM PR [#43273](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273) into SGLang as a new option for `--linear-attn-prefill-backend cutedsl`. - Three CuTeDSL kernels (`kkt_inv_uw`, `h`, `o`) plus shared Blackwell helpers (`cute_utils/`: tcgen05 / tmem / TMA bulk-swizzle / PTX BF16 wrappers). - 1.7x geomean kernel speedup over Triton FLA baseline on Qwen3-Next prefill shapes (B200, bfloat16). - +12.7% total throughput and -17% mean TTFT on Qwen3.6-27B TP=1 end-to-end (input=4096, output=256, 64 concurrent prompts). - SM90 path is unchanged: when the user picks `cutedsl` on Hopper, the dispatcher transparently falls back to Triton for prefill (decode keeps the existing CuTeDSL fused recurrent kernel). ## Motivation vLLM PR [#43273](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273) introduces a Blackwell-specific CuTeDSL GDN prefill kernel that beats both Triton FLA and FlashInfer's GDN Blackwell path in the multi-request / mixed-length / lower-head-count workloads that production serving actually sees. SGLang's existing `gdn_cutedsl.py` only wired the decode path; prefill on Blackwell was stuck on Triton. This PR closes that gap by porting the upstream kernel byte-for-byte under `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/gdn_blackwell/`, with the integration cost limited to a new `extend()` method on `CuteDSLGDNKernel` and an additional dispatch branch in `GDNKernelDispatcher`. The kernels follow the design of FLA: kkt_inv_uw_kernel: fusion of FLA's chunk_scaled_dot_kkt_fwd(), solve_tril(), and recompute_w_u_fwd() h_kernel: FLA's chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_h() o_kernel: FLA's chunk_fwd_o() This kernel also provides native support for BF16 state (no extra BF16->FP32 casting) Kernel timeline (just to illustrate the pipeline, not drawn correct to relative latencies) **Note** The following diagrams are extracted from https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273. ## Modifications - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/cute_utils/` — shared Blackwell helpers (3 files: tcgen05 / tmem / TMA-bulk-swizzle wrappers and PTX BF16 SIMD ops). Sourced from `vllm/cute_utils/` (Apache-2.0). - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/gdn_blackwell/` — 4 files: `kernel_kkt_inv_uw.py`, `kernel_h.py`, `kernel_o.py`, and the top-level `chunk_gated_delta_rule_cutedsl` + `prepare_metadata_cutedsl` entry. Sourced from `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/gdn_chunk_cutedsl/`. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/gdn_cutedsl.py` — `CuteDSLGDNKernel.extend()` added; `decode()` unchanged. Adapts to the existing SGLang contract: l2norm Q/K outside the kernel, gather initial state from the pool, build `chunk_indices` / `chunk_offsets` via `prepare_metadata_cutedsl`, scatter final state back. Lazy import keeps SM90 boxes able to construct the kernel for decode only. - `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py` — `GDNKernelDispatcher` learns to route prefill through the CuTeDSL kernel when `prefill_backend=cutedsl` and `cutedsl_kernel.supports_prefill` is True (SM>=10); else it logs a one-line warning and falls back to Triton. - `test/registered/attention/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py` — correctness test (6 cases: `num_seqs in {1,5,257}` x `state_dtype in {bf16, fp32}`) against `fused_recurrent_gated_delta_rule` as ground truth. Registered for CI via `register_cuda_ci(est_time=60, stage="base-b", runner_config="4-gpu-b200")` and module-level `pytest.skip` on SM<10. - `benchmark/bench_linear_attention/bench_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py` — Triton-vs-CuteDSL correctness sweep (19 shapes) plus `do_bench_cudagraph` perf table. ## Benchmarks ### Kernel microbench NVIDIA B200, bfloat16, `do_bench_cudagraph`, Qwen3-Next preset (K=V=128, pool_size=256). | B | H | T/seq | T_tot | triton (ms) | TFLOPS | TB/s | cutedsl (ms) | TFLOPS | TB/s | speedup | |----:|----:|------:|-------:|------------:|-------:|-------:|-------------:|-------:|-------:|--------:| | 4 | 16 | 256 | 1024 | 0.656 | 1.64 | 0.04 | 0.367 | 2.92 | 0.07 | 1.79x | | 4 | 32 | 256 | 1024 | 1.267 | 1.70 | 0.04 | 0.696 | 3.08 | 0.07 | 1.82x | | 16 | 16 | 256 | 4096 | 0.750 | 5.72 | 0.13 | 0.427 | 10.07 | 0.24 | 1.76x | | 16 | 32 | 256 | 4096 | 1.472 | 5.84 | 0.14 | 0.831 | 10.34 | 0.24 | 1.77x | | 32 | 16 | 256 | 8192 | 0.888 | 9.67 | 0.23 | 0.516 | 16.63 | 0.39 | 1.72x | | 32 | 32 | 256 | 8192 | 1.742 | 9.86 | 0.23 | 1.000 | 17.18 | 0.40 | 1.74x | | 64 | 16 | 256 | 16384 | 1.155 | 14.87 | 0.35 | 0.683 | 25.17 | 0.59 | 1.69x | | 64 | 32 | 256 | 16384 | 2.283 | 15.05 | 0.35 | 1.335 | 25.74 | 0.61 | 1.71x | | 128 | 16 | 256 | 32768 | 1.693 | 20.29 | 0.48 | 1.012 | 33.94 | 0.80 | 1.67x | | 128 | 32 | 256 | 32768 | 3.371 | 20.39 | 0.48 | 2.002 | 34.33 | 0.81 | 1.68x | | 4 | 16 | 1024 | 4096 | 0.751 | 5.72 | 0.10 | 0.414 | 10.38 | 0.18 | 1.82x | | 4 | 32 | 1024 | 4096 | 1.482 | 5.80 | 0.10 | 0.791 | 10.86 | 0.19 | 1.87x | | 32 | 16 | 1024 | 32768 | 1.657 | 20.74 | 0.37 | 0.876 | 39.22 | 0.69 | 1.89x | | 32 | 32 | 1024 | 32768 | 3.301 | 20.82 | 0.37 | 1.719 | 39.97 | 0.71 | 1.92x | Geomean speedup across all 14 shapes: **~1.78x**. Range: 1.67x to 1.92x. No regression on any shape. ### End-to-end Qwen3.6-27B (`Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B`), B200 TP=1, `sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name random --num-prompts 64 --random-input-len 4096 --random-output-len 256 --random-range-ratio 1.0`. Both backends use `--linear-attn-decode-backend triton` (decode unchanged); only `--linear-attn-prefill-backend` differs. | Metric | Triton | CuteDSL | Delta | |------------------------------|--------:|--------:|---------:| | Bench duration (s) | 20.55 | 18.24 | -11.2% | | Total token throughput (t/s) | 13,557 | 15,273 | +12.7% | | Input throughput (t/s) | 12,759 | 14,375 | +12.7% | | Output throughput (t/s) | 797 | 898 | +12.7% | | Mean TTFT (ms) | 8,243 | 6,842 | -17.0% | | P99 TTFT (ms) | 14,890 | 12,681 | -14.8% | | Mean TPOT (ms) | 48.0 | 44.5 | -7.4% | | Mean E2E latency (ms) | 20,489 | 18,181 | -11.3% | Server log for the CuteDSL run confirms `Using CuTe DSL GDN prefill (Blackwell)`. ### Accuracy (GSM8K) `python -m sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k --num-questions 200 --port 30000` (5-shot, temperature=0, greedy decode, same prompts). | Backend | Accuracy | Invalid | Latency (s) | |------------------|---------:|--------:|------------:| | Triton (run 1) | 0.620 | 0.235 | 14.81 | | Triton (run 2) | 0.640 | 0.240 | 13.87 | | CuteDSL | 0.725 | 0.120 | 14.62 | No regression. The +9 pp accuracy delta on this 200-question subset is driven by a lower invalid (unparseable answer) rate from CuteDSL: with greedy decode at temperature=0, the chunked accumulation order differs between the two backends, which propagates into different reasoning trajectories. Both backends sit in the expected range for a 27B model on 5-shot GSM8K; treat the gap as run-to-run numerical variance rather than a quality claim. ## How to use ``` python -m sglang.launch_server \ --model Qwen/Qwen3.6-27B \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp 1 \ --linear-attn-prefill-backend cutedsl \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port 30000 ``` The flag is also accepted on SM90 (Hopper); the dispatcher transparently falls back to Triton for prefill and prints one info-level line. This means users can pick `cutedsl` uniformly across hardware without per-host configuration. ## Requirements - CUDA runtime >= 13. - `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.5.0` — **the `[cu13]` extra matters**. The base `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.5.0` wheel does not pull in the matching `cuda-bindings 13.2.0` / `cuda-pathfinder` / `numpy 2.4.x` set, and the kernel fails to compile inside `cute.copy` (asserts in `_ods_common._get_value`) without them. Consider updating `requirements/cuda.txt` accordingly. - `quack-kernels>=0.3.3`. ## Limitations and future work - The ported kernel hard-codes `BT=64` and `K_dim=V_dim=128`. The wrapper asserts `head_k_dim==128` at first call; a clearer error path may be added later. - KDA (Kimi Delta Attention, used by Kimi-Linear) cannot reuse this kernel: GDN's forget gate is per-head scalar `[T, Hv]`, while KDA's is per-K-dim `[T, H, K]`. The kernel's `Gamma[i,j] = exp(g_cu[i] - g_cu[j])` is structurally per-head. A KDA-specific Blackwell kernel would need to add a K dim to `Gamma` and to the H/state-evolution and output kernels; this is left as follow-up. - Two reviewer flags from the upstream Gemini bot on the source PR are not yet addressed there (TMEM hardcoded base addresses; an H-kernel TMEM dealloc race). These carry over to this port; we should re-sync once upstream lands fixes. - Decode path is unchanged. Existing `cutedsl_fused_sigmoid_gating_delta_rule_update` continues to serve decode on SM90+ via the unmodified `CuteDSLGDNKernel.decode()`. ## Test plan - [x] Correctness: `pytest test/registered/attention/test_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py -v` on B200 — 6/6 pass. - [x] Regression: `pytest test/registered/attention/test_kda_kernels.py -v` on B200 — 6/6 pass (KDA path unaffected). - [x] Standalone kernel sweep: `bench_gdn_prefill_cutedsl.py --mode correctness` — 19/19 PASS across varying B, T_per_seq, H, sparse vs sequential pool indices. - [x] SM90 fallback: `--linear-attn-prefill-backend cutedsl` on H200 logs the fallback and uses Triton for extend (decode keeps CuteDSL). - [x] End-to-end correctness: GSM8K 5-shot @ 200 questions on Qwen3.6-27B — no regression. - [x] End-to-end perf: Qwen3.6-27B TP=1 random workload — measured throughput / TTFT / TPOT. - [ ] Update `requirements/cuda.txt` to pin `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]==4.5.0` (follow-up). - [ ] CLI flag plumbing: ensure `linear_attn_prefill_backend` is wired through any model-specific entry points (Qwen3-Next, Kimi-Linear) — verified for the dispatcher; spot-check other call sites in review. ## Credits The CuTeDSL kernel code under `gdn_blackwell/` and `cute_utils/` is a near-byte-identical port from [vllm-project/vllm#43273](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/43273) by [@gau-nernst](https://github.com/gau-nernst), originally written in CUDA C++ by team CUDA_ERROR_UNKNOWN for the MLSys 2026 FlashInfer Kernel competition and rewritten in CuTeDSL by the vLLM PR author. The only changes here are import paths (`vllm.cute_utils` -> `sglang.srt.layers.attention.cute_utils`; `vllm.triton_utils` -> `triton`). License preserved as Apache-2.0. Many thanks to the upstream authors. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #26396897793](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26396897793) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #26396897621](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/26396897621)

title: Optimize Qwen3 Next FP8 MoE on H200
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Enable guarded CUDA shared-expert fusion for Qwen3-Next FP8 MoE on H200.
- Remap `mlp.shared_expert.*` checkpoint weights into the fused MoE expert slot for Qwen3-Next.
- Add H200 FP8 Triton MoE configs for fused `E=513,N=512` normal and down projections.
- Keep the fusion opt-in for Qwen3-Next so existing Qwen2-MoE paths keep their default behavior.

## Performance

title: [GDN] Optimize prefill QKV split dispatch
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

This patch reduces Qwen3.6 GDN prefill QKV split overhead observed during profiling:

- add a Triton `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` to split post-conv GDN Q/K/V into contiguous FLA prefill tensors in one launch;
- route CUDA GDN prefill tensors, including strided post-conv views, through that fused split path with a guarded fallback to the previous `torch.split(...).view(...)` path;
- add a focused `bench_gdn_qkv_split.py` benchmark for contiguous and strided inputs;
- tune the single safe `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` config to `BV=32`, `num_warps=4`, `num_stages=4`, while keeping env overrides for validation.

The chunk-h autotune remains single-config because this kernel updates the state pool in place; multi-config autotune can corrupt the state pool during benchmarking.

## Benchmark

Model: `Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8`  
Hardware: single NVIDIA B200, `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=1`  
Workload: default SOTA serving workload, 80 random prompts, `--disable-radix-cache` for the winning SGLang lane.

| Framework / candidate | Chat 1000/1000 out tok/s | Chat TTFT ms | Chat TPOT ms | Long 8000/1000 out tok/s | Long TTFT ms | Long TPOT ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SGLang baseline best | 7205.38 | 858.08 | 10.20 | 4243.72 | 4014.37 | 14.55 |
| vLLM latest best | 6480.19 | 1975.60 | 10.33 | 3993.22 | 4275.92 | 15.35 |
| SGLang patched GDN fused split + w4/s4 | 7396.73 | 709.25 | 10.07 | 4353.39 | 3820.19 | 14.28 |
| TensorRT-LLM latest | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A | N/A |

TensorRT-LLM latest could not serve this checkpoint because the bundled Transformers stack does not recognize `model_type=qwen3_5_moe`.

## Kernel Profile

| Row | Baseline SGLang | Patched SGLang |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `chunk_gated_delta_rule_fwd_kernel_h_blockdim64` | 24.21 ms / 90 = 269.00 us | 19.69 ms / 90 = 218.78 us |
| FLA/GDN prep copy | 18.97 ms | removed; replaced by 3.33 ms fused split |
| `fused_qkv_split_gdn_prefill_kernel` | N/A | 3.33 ms / 90 = 37.00 us |

## QKV Split Microbenchmark

H200 smoke benchmark for the new split path, `seq_len=8192`, `qkv_dim=6144`, bf16:

| Layout | Baseline us | Fused us | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| contiguous | 124.54 | 52.41 | 2.38x |
| strided | 349.45 | 338.48 | 1.03x |

## Accuracy

Full-dataset regression runs used the same model and 1x B200 setup. The eval command used `--chat-template-kwargs '{"enable_thinking": false}'`; MMLU used `--max-tokens 512`, and GSM8K used `--max-tokens 1024 --num-shots 5`.

| Variant | MMLU full | GSM8K full | Delta vs baseline |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline SGLang | 0.436761 | 0.954338 | - |
| SGLang patched GDN fused split + w4/s4 | 0.437687 | 0.955860 | +0.000926 MMLU / +0.001522 GSM8K |

## Validation

- `python3 -m py_compile python/sglang/jit_kernel/triton/gdn_fused_proj.py python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/fla/chunk_delta_h.py python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/linear/gdn_backend.py`
- `python3 benchmark/bench_linear_attention/bench_gdn_qkv_split.py --seq-len 8192 --warmup 10 --iters 50` on `ion8-h200`, GPU 0.
- Real-model serving benchmark on `ion-b200`, single B200.
- Torch profiler comparison against the strongest vLLM latest-image candidate.
- Full MMLU and GSM8K regression runs for baseline and patched SGLang.

title: amd/deepseek_v4 33/N remove BF16-to-FP32 elementwise cast from compressor GEMM on HIP
author: yichiche
body:
Update amd/deepseek_v4 integration branch

Merging to main is WIP, we use this PR and upstream amd/deepseek_v4 branch to integrate in parallel.

Original PRs at Day-0:
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23600
https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23608


## Motivation

On MI355/HIP, `Compressor.forward()` calls `linear_bf16_fp32()` which does:
```python
return tgemm.mm(x, y, otype=x.dtype).float()
```
The `.float()` triggers a separate `bfloat16tofloat32_copy_kernel_cuda` elementwise kernel (~4.2 us each). This fires once per compressor GEMM call:
- C-type layers (compress_ratio=4): 2 compressor GEMMs -> 2 cast kernels
- B-type layers (compress_ratio=128): 1 compressor GEMM -> 1 cast kernel
- A-type layers (compress_ratio=0): no compressor -> 0 cast kernels

Total: 30x2 + 30x1 = 90 cast kernels per iteration, ~384 us (~1.87% of ITL).

### Why B200 doesn't have this problem

`linear_bf16_fp32()` dispatches to different GEMM backends depending on the platform:

| Path | Method | FP32 output? |
|------|--------|-------------|
| B200 `deep_gemm` | `bf16_gemm_nt(x, y, z)` — output tensor `z` is pre-allocated as FP32, GEMM writes FP32 directly | Native, no extra kernel |
| B200 `cublas` | JIT CUDA module outputs FP32 directly | Native, no extra kernel |
| MI355 `aiter` | `tgemm.mm(x, y, otype=x.dtype)` — tuned flydsl configs only support BF16 output | Requires separate `.float()` cast |

B200's GEMM kernels natively support FP32 output in a single kernel launch. MI355's tuned flydsl kernels only support BF16 output, so the FP32 cast requires a separate elementwise kernel.

### Why removing the cast is safe on HIP

`linear_bf16_fp32()` has an FP32-output contract used by multiple paths (cublas, deep_gemm, torch fallback). Rather than breaking this contract, the compressor call site on HIP/aiter bypasses it and calls `tgemm.mm()` directly to get BF16 output.

This is safe because all downstream fused Triton compress kernels (`_c4_decode_kernel`, `_c128_decode_kernel`, `_compress_norm_rope_kernel`) already promote to FP32 internally via `.to(tl.float32)`. The GEMM itself uses FP32 accumulators internally -- the BF16 output simply avoids the unnecessary BF16->FP32->BF16->FP32 round-trip (GEMM accumulates in FP32, truncates to BF16 output, `.float()` casts back to FP32, then Triton loads and promotes to FP32 again).

The `CompressStatePool` buffer remains FP32 (`pool_configurator.py` sets `state_dtype=torch.float32`). Triton handles the mixed-dtype scenario (BF16 input stored into FP32 buffer) correctly via automatic type promotion.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**:
  - In `Compressor.forward()`, the aiter/HIP path now calls `_tgemm.mm()` directly (returns BF16), bypassing `linear_bf16_fp32()` and its `.float()` cast. The non-aiter path is unchanged.
  - Added `from aiter.tuned_gemm import tgemm as _tgemm` under the `if _use_aiter:` gate.

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/compressed/fused_compress_triton.py`**:
  - Relaxed FP32-only assertions in `_check_common()` to accept BF16 input (`kv_score_input` and `out`), since BF16 `kv_score` now flows through `compress_dispatch()` into the fused Triton kernels. The `kv_score_buffer` assertion remains FP32-only (state pool is always FP32).

## Accuracy Tests

| Benchmark | Score | Threshold | Status |
|-----------|-------|-----------|--------|
| GSM8K (2000 questions, 5-shot, parallel=1000) | 0.908 | 0.88 | PASS |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel Replacement (per C-type layer, decode)

| Before | Time (us) | After | Time (us) |
|--------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| `hgemm_bf16` (C4 GEMM) | 8.8 | `hgemm_bf16` (C4 GEMM) | 8.8 |
| `bfloat16tofloat32_copy` | 4.4 | *(eliminated)* | -- |
| `hgemm_bf16` (C128 GEMM) | 9.3 | `hgemm_bf16` (C128 GEMM) | 9.3 |
| `bfloat16tofloat32_copy` | 4.2 | *(eliminated)* | -- |
| **Total** | **26.7** | **Total** | **18.1** |

### Kernel-to-E2E Impact Analysis

| Layer Type | Layers/iter | Kernel Savings/Layer | Total Savings |
|------------|-------------|---------------------|---------------|
| C-type (MLA+Compressor+MoE) | 30 | 8.6 us | 258 us |
| B-type (MoE) | 30 | 4.2 us | 126 us |
| A-type (MLA+Dense) | 61 | 0 us | 0 us |
| **Total** | | | **384 us** |

Expected ITL improvement: 384 us / 20,590 us = **1.87%** (~0.38 ms).

TTFT impact: Negligible -- prefill is dominated by large GEMMs.

### End-to-End Benchmark (il8k_ol1k, concurrency=4, 32 prompts)

| Metric | Baseline | After | Delta |
|--------|----------|-------|-------|
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 1,558.2 | 1,591.2 | +2.1% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 173.1 | 176.8 | +2.1% |
| Median E2E Latency (ms) | 23,109.0 | 22,969.5 | -0.6% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 1,546.1 | 1,535.9 | -0.7% |
| Median ITL (ms) | 20.59 | 20.46 | -0.6% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 21.54 | 20.99 | -2.6% |

### Configuration

- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP=8, MI355
- Attention backend: compressed
- Page size: 256, chunked prefill: 8192

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review Process

title: [mtp] add rejection sampling for speculative decoding
author: liyucheng09
body:
## Motivation

Add classic reject sampling (RS) in Eagle speculative decoding.

The current pipeline of Eagle speculative decoding employ greedy sampling in both predicting draft tokens and target verification.

Use classic reject sampling means to use actual draft prob distribution for sampling draft tokens and for acceptance criterion.

Experimental results show using classic rs can largely improve accept length across various tasks.

## Modifications

We change how tokens are drafted: from argmax to sample on draft distribution. And we provide a reject sample triton kernel to update accept criterion from `p` to `min(1, p\q)`.

title: API Perf: Replace pydantic per-element validation with C loop validation
author: Jialin

Introduce a C-loop validation, and wire up via PlainValidator

title: Optimize Gemma4 H200 MoE and extend attention
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- Add H200 Triton fused MoE configs for Gemma4 `E=128,N=704` normal and down projections.
- Tune Hopper extend-attention block sizes for `Lq=129..256` to reduce TTFT/TPOT on Gemma4 prefill-heavy serving.
- Add a small-batch (M ≤ 256) per-head Triton kernel for Gemma4 QKV RMSNorm to lower MTP draft latency.
- ~~Add a Gemma4-specific Triton routing kernel that fuses top-k selection, top-k softmax, and per-expert scale into `gemma4_topk_softmax_scale`.~~ Reverted (commit `27cb94c45`) due to BF16 precision regression on MoE routing — see "Reverted optimizations" below.
- ~~Replace `Gemma4Router.norm(x) * fused_scale` with a single fused `rmsnorm(x, fused_scale, eps)` call on the CUDA fast path.~~ Reverted (commit `0d3c9c694`) for the same reason.
- Keep the optimization scoped to Gemma4/Hopper paths so existing model families keep their current behavior.

## Performance

Re-measured on `ion8-h200`, `sglang_bbuf`, single NVIDIA H200, TP=1, `google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, BF16, `--attention-backend triton`, random `1024/256`, request rate 8, max concurrency 64, 80 prompts. Baseline = latest `origin/main` (`376635c1e`); patched = PR head (`27cb94c45`, with c2/c3 reverted).

| Workload | Build | Output tok/s | p50 TTFT ms | p50 TPOT ms | Median E2E ms | Result |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- |
| Random `1024/256`, 80 prompts | SGLang baseline (`376635c1e`) | 1670.72 | 96.56 | 20.30 | 5295.91 | Baseline |
| Random `1024/256`, 80 prompts | SGLang patched (`27cb94c45`) | **1725.50** | **74.04** | **16.62** | **4338.60** | **+3.28% output tok/s, -23.3% TTFT, -18.2% TPOT, -18.1% E2E** |

Full benchmark details:

| Build | Completed | Duration s | Request throughput req/s | Total tok/s | Median E2E ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| SGLang baseline (`376635c1e`) | 80 | 12.26 | 6.526 | 8353.59 | 5295.91 |
| SGLang patched (`27cb94c45`) | 80 | 11.87 | 6.740 | 8627.50 | 4338.60 |

The remaining speedup comes from the H200 MoE Triton configs + Hopper extend-attention block-size tuning + small-batch QKV RMSNorm; the heavier routing-fusion optimizations were dropped to keep accuracy on the MTP path.

## Accuracy

Validated on `ion8-h200` via the registered Gemma4 MTP CI test (`test_gemma4_mtp_26b_a4b_extra::test_gsm8k_mtp`, TP=2, `--enable-deterministic-inference`, NEXTN spec decode, 200 GSM8K examples, 5-shot). With the two reverted commits, GSM8K MTP score is back to baseline:

| Build (TP=2, deterministic) | GSM8K MTP topk=1 | avg accept length | Threshold 0.41 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| SGLang baseline (`376635c1e`, all reverts = main) | 0.445 | 4.494 | ✓ pass |
| SGLang patched (`27cb94c45`, c1+c4 kept, c2+c3 reverted) | 0.445 | 4.494 | ✓ pass |
| ~~PR head before revert (`10ab189e3`, all 4 commits)~~ | ~~0.360~~ | ~~4.475~~ | ✗ fail (-5pp) |

Standalone GSM8K (TP=1, no MTP, 8-shot, 200 questions, no deterministic mode) shows the typical run-to-run variance (~5pp swing) but no systematic regression — patched and baseline land within noise of each other (patched: 0.41 / 0.495 across two runs; baseline: 0.465 / 0.445).

## Reverted optimizations

Bisecting `test_gemma4_mtp_26b_a4b_extra` on `ion8-h200` (TP=2, deterministic):

| Configuration | GSM8K topk=1 | Δ vs PR head |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PR head (all 4 commits) | 0.360 | 0 |
| Revert only `fabb5b5ee` (QKV RMSNorm small batch) | 0.360 | 0 — innocuous |
| Revert only `d72d246a3` (Router RMSNorm fuse) | 0.395 | +0.035 |
| Revert only `03826cdd9` (MoE topk fuse) | 0.380 | +0.020 |
| Revert only `3398cb7af` (extend-attn + MoE configs) | 0.360 | 0 — innocuous |
| **Revert `d72d246a3` + `03826cdd9` together** | **0.445** | **+0.085 (pass)** |
| Revert all 4 (= origin/main) | 0.445 | identical to c2+c3 revert |

Both reverted commits modify the Gemma4 MoE routing path in `gemma4_causal.py`:
- `d72d246a3`: `rmsnorm(x, fused_scale, eps)` fast path in `Gemma4Router.forward`. The math is equivalent to `(self.norm(x) with weight=1) * fused_scale`, but BF16 accumulation order in the fused kernel diverges from the two-step path when `fused_scale ≈ hidden_size**-0.5 ≈ 0.022`.
- `03826cdd9`: `_gemma4_topk_softmax_scale_kernel` doing topk + stable-softmax + per-expert scale in one pass. Equivalent to `softmax(topk_logits) * scale[topk_ids]` for `topk ≤ 8`, but its FP32-internal `exp(top_logit - top1) / sum_top_exp` ordering doesn't match `torch.nn.functional.softmax` bit-for-bit.

Either alone causes a ~0.02-0.035 GSM8K drop; together the routing logits drift enough to flip enough expert selections that the MTP draft/target distribution gap widens (MTP `avg_accept_length` still looks healthy at 4.48, masking the underlying quality regression).

If you want to recover these speedups, the kernels need to be made bit-equivalent to the eager paths — e.g. accept `weight=ones` in the fused router RMSNorm and apply `fused_scale` as a separate elementwise op, and have `_gemma4_topk_softmax_scale_kernel` mirror PyTorch's exact softmax floating-point order (compute max, subtract, exp, sum, divide — all in fp32 with the same reduction tree).

## Validation

- Bisect, perf re-measurement, and Gemma4 MTP accuracy validation all completed on `ion8-h200`, container `sglang_bbuf`.
- Python syntax check passed for the changed Python files.
- New H200 Triton config JSON files (`E=128,N=704`) parse successfully.
- Extend-attention block-size sanity checked for `Lq=128,192,256,288`.
- Server benchmark + Gemma4 MTP CI test (TP=2, deterministic, 200-question GSM8K) confirm patched ≡ baseline accuracy (both 0.445).

title: [core] Make overlap-schedule WAR barrier CUDA-only
author: bingxche
body:
Started as a revert of #26380; instead this keeps #26380's data-race fix on CUDA and reverts it on other platforms, where the barrier caused regressions.

## Summary
- Gate the overlap-schedule WAR barrier (`schedule_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)`) and its D2H-stream occupancy compensation behind `is_cuda()`. CUDA keeps #26380; other platforms (HIP / NPU / CPU) fall back to pre-#26380 behavior.

## Background
- #26380 added a global WAR barrier to fix an overlap-scheduling data race. It is free on CUDA but regressed AMD/HIP:
  - `test_deepseek_r1_mxfp4_8gpu` (MTP): all 8 TP ranks hit the scheduler watchdog timeout (hang).
  - `test_priority_scheduling`: `test_priority_scheduling_request_ordering_validation` assertion failure.
  - DSv4 non-MTP: ~20% throughput drop.
- CUDA shows no measurable throughput change across Llama-3 + EAGLE3 (MTP), DSv4 MTP, and DSv4 non-MTP — data in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26380#issuecomment-4571064550.

## Changes
- `scheduler.py` / `disaggregation/decode.py` / `disaggregation/prefill.py`: guard the three `schedule_stream.wait_stream(forward_stream)` barriers with `self._war_barrier_enabled = is_cuda()`.
- `managers/overlap_utils.py`: narrow the `fwd_prepare_d2h_stream` + pinned-buffer compensation from `_is_cuda or _is_hip` to `_is_cuda`.

Reference #26380.

body: Update amd/deepseek_v4 integration branch Merging to main is WIP, we use this PR and upstream amd/deepseek_v4 branch to integrate in parallel. Original PRs at Day-0: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23600 https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23608 Co-author: @yichiche, @Raiden-Makoto ## Motivation The Triton sparse MLA decode kernel dispatch logic previously had a fallback path to a 2-phase (separate gather + attention) implementation for decode batch sizes in [33, 255] from kernel-level benchmarking. But for real E2E test, this 2-phase path caused significant performance degradation at high concurrency (8k/1k, TP=8, cc=64/128) due to: - Extra intermediate buffer allocation (gathered_kv) - Additional kernel launch overhead - Inability to fuse gather and attention operations For example, at bs=64, `_unified_sparse_decode_kernel` alone takes ~65% of decode attention time, whereas at bs=4, the fused `_fused_gather_attn_dsv4_dual_scope_kernel `only takes ~29.6%. We should try forcing the fused kernel path even at high concurrency. ## Modifications - **Remove 2-phase implementation**: Delete 3 files containing the separate gather+attention path since won't be called anymore. (`triton_mla_kernels_decode_common.py`, `triton_mla_kernels_decode_dsv4.py`, `triton_mla_kernels_decode_splitk.py`) - **Simplify kernel dispatch**: All dual-scope cases now use fused kernels: - Small batches: fused split-K kernel (better GPU utilization) - Large batches / extend / prefill: fused no-splitk kernel - Previously 2-phase [33, 255] range: now uses fused no-splitk - **Code cleanup**: Inline `_bucket_total_tokens`, extract `_decide_splitk_dual_scope` as shared function, remove dead code ## Accuracy Tests gsm8k accuracy ~0.939/0.942 (2 rounds confirmation) ## Speed Tests and Profiling This opt should benefit those cases where the batch size locates in [33, 255] that will fall back to the 2phase implementation, and now they will be forced to run into the fused kernel. title: [DeepSeek-V4] Fuse UE8M0 scale rounding into FP8 group quantization
author: JoeLee314
body: ## Motivation This PR optimizes the DeepSeek-V4 `wo_a` FP8 path by removing the separate `deep_gemm.ceil_to_ue8m0` call after activation quantization. The original path launches quantization first, then rounds the generated FP8 scales to UE8M0/power-of-two format: ```text sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8 -> deep_gemm.ceil_to_ue8m0 -> deep_gemm.fp8_einsum ``` The optimized path emits the rounded power-of-two scale directly from the per-token group quantization kernel: ```text sglang_per_token_group_quant_fp8(scale_ue8m0=True) -> deep_gemm.fp8_einsum ``` ## Performance Test DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP=4, 32K input / 1K output, 128 requests, max concurrency 4. Output token throughput increased by 7.8%. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8K score: 0.928 ## Update: precision fix on Blackwell (B300/B200) The initial fused kernel in this PR had a precision issue on Blackwell: in the `SCALE_UE8M0 && !IS_COLUMN_MAJOR` branch, activations were quantized with the exact FP32 scale while only the *output* scale was rounded to UE8M0 (power-of-2). Since quantization and dequantization then used mismatched scales, EAGLE speculative decoding accept_length dropped from 2.76 to 2.69 on B300/B200. Thanks to @yhyang201 for catching this and providing the fix. The special branch is removed and all UE8M0 paths now go through `calculate_fp8_scales`, which computes the rounded (power-of-2) scale first and quantizes with it — matching the official DeepSeek-V4 `kernel.py` `act_quant(scale_fmt="ue8m0")`. The row-major UE8M0 test now asserts the scales are exact powers of 2 and the fp8 codes match the `ceil_to_ue8m0` reference. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #27789934317](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27789934317) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #27791183010](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/27791183010)

title: [JIT Kernel] DeepSeek-V4 DSA indexer: faster top-k + page-table transform (runtime k <= 2048)
author: DarkSharpness
body:
Note: after this PR, the v1 should be deprecated. v2 is now a superset of v1. (this line is written by human)
 
(auto-generated by claude)

## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4 DSA indexer selects the top-k KV positions per query for sparse
attention and maps the selected indices through a page table. This fused top-k +
page-table transform sits on the decode critical path, especially for long context.
This PR provides an optimized JIT kernel for it.

## Feature

- **Runtime top-k — `k = 512`, `1024`, and `2048` are all supported** (`k` is a
  runtime argument, so a single module serves every `k`).
- Ragged per-batch sequence lengths.
- Arbitrary (power-of-two) page size.
- Optional raw (pre-transform) top-k index output.

## Performance

Benchmarked on B200 against flashinfer's `top_k_page_table_transform`
(apples-to-apples: both do top-k **and** the page-table transform), `k=512`:

- Faster in nearly all `(batch, seq)` configurations; up to ~1.5× at large batch /
  long context.
- Sustains ~3.0–3.6 TB/s (near HBM peak) for `batch ≥ 2048` at `seq ≥ 64K`.

Correctness is validated against `torch.topk` across all dispatch paths
(172 unit-test cases).

title: [AMD]Reuse fused FP8 KV cache write on standard aiter prefill/decode
author: IzacharyI
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
The fused bf16→fp8 KV cache write kernel (launch_reshape_and_cache_flash) was only enabled on the unified-attention path (use_triton_unified_attention). On the standard aiter path (read via paged_attention_ragged), FP8 KV writes fell back to set_kv_buffer, which performs a separate divide + cast + store_kvcache — i.e. extra elementwise kernels and intermediate DRAM traffic per K/V per attention layer.

The KV write only produces the fp8 cache and is independent of the attention read path, so the fused kernel can be reused for the standard path as well. This PR broadens the fused write to the standard aiter prefill/decode FP8 path and fixes a latent scale-correctness gap.

## Modifications
python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py:

Decode (forward_decode): relax the fused-write gating from use_triton_unified_attention and kv_cache_dtype == fp8 to kv_cache_dtype == fp8 and not use_mla, so the standard (non-unified) aiter path also uses launch_reshape_and_cache_flash instead of set_kv_buffer.
Prefill (forward_extend): add the same fused write for the non-SWA, non-MLA FP8 case (previously this path used the naive set_kv_buffer).
Correctness: pass k_scale/v_scale to launch_reshape_and_cache_flash. The existing decode FP8 branch (#23620) omitted them, which is only correct when the KV descale is 1.0; passing them keeps non-unit descales correct.
MLA is explicitly excluded (not use_mla) and keeps its own KV write path.

## Accuracy Tests

### Kernel-level (fused write vs naive set_kv_buffer)
Compared the reused fused write against the naive set_kv_buffer path (per-tensor descale = amax/fp8_max), checking both the written cache slots and fp8 contents:

| Case                   | fused vs fp32-divide ref | fused vs naive-bf16 mismatch | mean abs err vs fp32 ref (fused / naive) |
| ---------------------- | ------------------------ | ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| decode  [32, 1, 256]   | 0.0000% (bit-identical)  | ~1.7%                        | fused ≤ naive                            |
| prefill [8000, 1, 256] | 0.0000% (bit-identical)  | ~2.5%                        | fused ≤ naive (fused slightly closer)    |

### End-to-end (before vs after, standard aiter FP8 path)
To isolate "FP8 KV quantization itself" from "this change", I compared the pre-change naive `set_kv_buffer` write against the fused write on the same standard aiter path. The pre-change naive FP8 write is not directly runnable on ROCm (`set_kv_buffer` → `store_cache` raises `BufferError: float8 types are not supported by dlpack`), so for the baseline I bypassed `store_cache` to use the naive scatter write — identical numerics, only a different store mechanism.

GSM8K, Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, TP8, full 1319 questions, 5-shot, greedy:

KV / FP8 write | gsm8k (1319) | invalid
-- | -- | --
naive set_kv_buffer FP8 (before) | 93.1% | 3.4%
fused FP8 write (this PR)         | 92.9% | 3.7%
bf16 KV (full-precision ref)      | 94.2% | 2.1%

naive vs fused differ by 0.2pp, and fp8 vs full-precision bf16 by ~1.3pp
(decode is bit-identical at the kernel level). So the small gap comes from FP8 KV
quantization itself, not from this change.

### Kernel speed (fused write vs naive)
case | naive (before) | fused (after) | speedUp
-- | -- | -- | --
decode bs=1 nkv=1 | 39.75us | 37.51us | 1.06x
decode bs=16 nkv=1 | 39.40us | 37.49us | 1.05x
decode bs=32 nkv=1 | 37.90us | 36.49us | 1.04x
decode bs=32 nkv=4 | 37.37us | 35.30us | 1.06x
prefill q=8000 nkv=1 | 100.41us | 41.32us | 2.43x
prefill q=8000 nkv=4 | 271.33us | 42.38us | 6.40x

## Speed Tests and Profiling
e2e: fp8-KV (this PR) vs bf16-KV (reference) — Qwen3.5-397B-A17B, TP8, bs=1, out=128
```log

Mean TTFT (ms):                          528.10

Mean TPOT (ms):                          8.58
```

title: [AMD] Fuse compress norm+rope+hadamard into single Triton kernel
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

In the DSV4 compressor decode path on MI355, the post-compression pipeline runs two separate kernels back-to-back on the same `kv_compressed` tensor `[num_tokens, 512]`:

1. `_compress_norm_rope_kernel` (RMSNorm + RoPE) -- ~4.0 us
2. `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` (Hadamard rotation) -- ~4.1 us

Since both operate on the same data and the full head_dim (512) fits in registers, fusing them eliminates one kernel launch and one global memory round-trip.

This fusion fires for every C4 compressor call with `rotate=True` (C-type layers have 2 such calls, A-type layers have 1). The C128 compressor has `rotate=False` and is unaffected.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/compressed/fused_compress_triton.py`**:
  - Added `_compress_norm_rope_hadamard_kernel`: Triton kernel that performs RMSNorm + RoPE + Walsh-Hadamard butterfly transform (9 stages for dim=512) in a single kernel launch. The butterfly uses a store-reload pattern through L1 cache (2KB per row).
  - Added `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_hadamard_inplace()`: Python wrapper that launches the fused kernel with the hadamard scale factor (`head_dim^-0.5`).

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/compressed/compressor.py`**:
  - When `rotate=True` (C4 compressor), dispatch to the new fused `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_hadamard_inplace()` instead of separate `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_inplace()` + `rotate_activation()`.
  - When `rotate=False` (C128 compressor), unchanged -- still uses `hip_compress_fused_norm_rope_inplace()`.

## Accuracy Tests

| Benchmark | Score | Threshold | Status |
|-----------|-------|-----------|--------|
| GSM8K (2000 questions, 5-shot, parallel=1000) | 0.950 | 0.94 | PASS |

## Benchmarking and Profiling

### Kernel Replacement (C-type layer, decode)

| Before | Time (us) | After | Time (us) |
|--------|-----------|-------|-----------|
| `_compress_norm_rope_kernel` (×2) | 8.3 | `_compress_norm_rope_hadamard_kernel` (×1) | 4.1 |
| `fast_hadamard_transform_kernel` (×2) | 8.3 | *(eliminated)* | -- |
| **Total** | **16.6** | `_compress_norm_rope_kernel` (×1, C128 rotate=False) | 4.0 |
| | | **Total** | **8.1** |

### Kernel-to-E2E Impact Analysis

| Layer Type | Layers/iter | Kernel Savings/Layer | Total Savings |
|------------|-------------|---------------------|---------------|
| C-type (MLA+Compressor+MoE) | 30 | 6.3 us | 189 us |
| A-type (MLA+Dense) | 61 | 0 us | 0 us |
| B-type (MoE) | 30 | 0 us | 0 us |
| **Total** | | | **189 us** |

Expected ITL improvement: 189 us / 20,570 us = **0.92%** (~0.19 ms). This is within typical run-to-run benchmark noise (1-2%), so the improvement is real at the kernel level but not distinguishable in e2e benchmarks at this precision.

TTFT impact: Negligible — prefill is dominated by large GEMMs; compressor norm+rope+hadamard is a tiny fraction.

### End-to-End Benchmark (il8k_ol1k, concurrency=4, 32 prompts)

| Metric | Baseline | After | Delta |
|--------|----------|-------|-------|
| Total throughput (tok/s) | 1,560.0 | 1,583.5 | +1.5% |
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 173.3 | 175.9 | +1.5% |
| Median E2E Latency (ms) | 23,080.4 | 23,078.8 | -0.0% |
| Median TTFT (ms) | 1,542.7 | 1,542.0 | -0.0% |
| Median ITL (ms) | 20.57 | 20.56 | -0.0% |
| Median TPOT (ms) | 21.51 | 21.10 | -1.9% |

### Configuration

- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Pro, TP=8, MI355
- Attention backend: compressed
- Page size: 256, chunked prefill: 8192

title: [HiCache] Fix PP inconsistency with HiCache L3 (#22607)
author: stepinto
body:
## Motivation

When deploying HiCache and PP, multiple PP ranks go diverge and eventually cause sglang crash.  The detailed reason was discussed in issue #22607.

## Modifications

This patch introduces two kinds of synchronization mechanisms to fix the issue.  I will illustrate this idea with an example of pp_size=2 and tp_size=1.

1. **pp_sync** across scheduler threads.  pp_sync is a new name introduced by this patch.  PP0's scheduler thread determine the number of completion events in its local queues (ack_load_queue, ack_prefetch_queue, etc). Then, PP1 must consume the **exact** same number of events from its queues.  This prevents divergence.

2. **all_reduce** across prefetch threads.  Consider a case that PP0 and PP1 have different lengths on their L3 storage for a given sequence. They have to reach an agreement on the length, by perform all_reduce(MIN).  This behavior is consistent with TP.

This patch also changes how `check_prefetch_progress` works.  Before this patch, it simply does all_reduce(MIN) to determine the final tokens prefetchted.  However, this would not work on PP, as we cannot do that in the scheduler thread.  This patch adds a new background thread `prefetch_sync_thread`, which does the all_reduce work instead.

## Accuracy Tests

Added `test_unified_radix_cache_hicache_pp_kl.py`.

I have also tested SWE-bench verified with DSv4 flash model.

I ran two groups:

- Group A: The baseline, commit 5747ed3b, without this PR, TP=8, L3 enabled.  Resolved 356/500.
- Group B: This PR, PP=4, TP=2, L3 enabled.  Resolved 353/500.

I analyzed the difference, and found 351 cases successful in both group, 5 are successful only in group A, and 2 are successful only in group B.  The 7 cases that are successfuly in one group but failed in another, are due to container exits after a long time. 

Here are commands for anyone has interested in reproducing this test.  Hints to make L3 are in-use:
- Use large number of workers (128), leading to large number of running requests.
- Limit number of tokens in L1 and L2.

```sh
# Group A
sglang serve \
    --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --tp-size 8 \
    --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
    --disable-cuda-graph \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 30000 \
    --max-total-tokens=500000 \
    --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \
    --enable-metrics \
    --enable-hierarchical-cache \
    --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \
    --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}'

# Group B
sglang serve \
    --model=deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
    --pp-size 4 \
    --tp-size 2 \
    --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
    --disable-cuda-graph \
    --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
    --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 \
    --port 30000 \
    --max-total-tokens=500000 \
    --swa-full-tokens-ratio=0.4 \
    --enable-metrics \
    --enable-hierarchical-cache \
    --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \
    --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "512gb", "protocol": "tcp"}'

# SWE bench agent
python -m minisweagent.run.benchmarks.swebench \
    --subset verified \
    --split test \
    -c swebench.yaml -c environment.container_timeout=24h \
    -o /root/swe_test/result \
    -m "openai/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash" \
    -w 128

# SWE evaluation
python -m swebench.harness.run_evaluation \
    --predictions_path /root/swe_test/result/preds.json \
    --dataset_name princeton-nlp/SWE-Bench_Verified \
    --split test \
    --max_workers 32 \
    --run_id test-mini-swe-agent \
    --timeout 1200
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

I tested with L1 only, L1+L2 and L1+L2+L3.  The size of L1 and L2 are configured not to hold all tokens.  L3 is large enough to hold all tokens.  `request-rate` is set to `1` so that L3 prefetch are performed and not limited by budget.


```sh

sglang serve \
  --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \
  --tp-size=2 \
  --pp-size=4 \
  --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --tool-call-parser qwen25 \
  --page-size=64 \
  --enable-metrics

# L2
sglang serve \
  --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \
  --tp-size=2 \
  --pp-size=4 \
  --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --tool-call-parser qwen25 \
  --page-size=64 \
  --enable-metrics \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache \
  --hicache-mem-layout=page_first 

# L3
sglang serve \
  --model=Qwen/Qwen3-32B \
  --tp-size=2 \
  --pp-size=4 \
  --max-total-tokens=$((256*1024)) \
  --reasoning-parser qwen3 \
  --tool-call-parser qwen25 \
  --page-size=64 \
  --enable-metrics \
  --enable-hierarchical-cache \
  --hicache-mem-layout=page_first \
  --hicache-storage-backend=mooncake \
  --hicache-storage-backend-extra-config '{"master_server_address": "127.0.0.1:50051", "local_hostname": "localhost", "metadata_server": "http://127.0.0.1:8080/metadata", "global_segment_size": "256gb", "protocol": "tcp"}'

# Benchmark
python benchmark/hicache/bench_multiturn.py  \
    --num-clients=128 \

```

title: [BCG][GLM5] perf: BCG support and prefill enhancements
author: mattteochen
body: ## Motivation https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23351 introduced PCG for GLM5 (`nsa_indexer`). As the current implementation runs the full indexer path, which is not fully captured by a CUDA graph, we found that running the fast indexer in eager mode yields better performance. Moreover, the current PCG split creates a CUDA graph island with only 1 kernel, introducing unnecessary overhead during dispatch. After `2048` tokens, PCG is disabled; the full path is being run eagerly in any case. ## Modifications - BCG support for NSA models - Run the fast nsa idexer (only k) in eager mode, marking it as a split op (opt in with env variable) - Registered another custom op with `bmm` + `unified_attention_with_output` to avoid single cuda graph with only `bmm` (opt in with env variable) - Updated the breakable cuda graph handler to merge adjacent eager Modules (this optimisation was also implemented for PCG, but then removed to reduce this PR code changes, as PCG is planned to be deprecated) ## Accuracy Tests PCG: ```bash gpqa: ==================== Repeat: 6, mean: 0.863 Scores: ['0.833', '0.854', '0.884', '0.879', '0.869', '0.859'] Mean latency: 14037.766 s ==================== ``` BCG: ```bash ==================== Repeat: 6, mean: 0.854 Scores: ['0.848', '0.854', '0.869', '0.869', '0.838', '0.848'] Mean latency: 15453.834 s ==================== ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested on B200 and INTEL(R) XEON(R) PLATINUM 8570. ### 1k1k Pareto for 1k1k on B200 TP8: ~4% speedup over the PCG solution at max concurrency: Median TTFT for 1k1k sees 10% improvement at max conc (not in pareto). title: Add FP4 Indexer for DeepSeek V4 on SM120
author: liz-badada
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #26209, extends the FP4 Indexer to SM120 (depends on https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/56). 

## Accuracy

DeepSeek V4 Flash GSM8K
|                                 | Accuracy |
|-------------------|----------|
| Default FP8            |    95.5% |
| FP4 indexer            |    93.0% |

## Performance

Two sets of results are reported because they were collected on different SGLang software stacks. They use the same model, workload, and FP8-versus-FP4 indexer comparison, but different SM120 main-attention backends. Therefore, each table is a valid within-stack A/B comparison, while the absolute numbers across the two tables are not directly comparable as a regression test.

### Test configurations

| Setting | Original PR measurement | Latest validation |
|---|---|---|
| SGLang source | `5453e93c50` | Tested at `245a47444c`; tree identical to current squashed PR head `9f100e6e27` |
| DeepGEMM source | https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepGEMM/pull/324 | https://github.com/sgl-project/DeepGEMM/pull/55 |
| Hardware | 4x SM120 | 4x SM120 |
| FlashInfer | Not used for SM120 attention | 0.6.14 |
| SM120 attention backend | **Triton** | **FlashInfer** |
| Baseline indexer | **Torch FP8** | **Torch FP8** |
| Optimized indexer | **DeepGEMM FP4** | **DeepGEMM FP4** |
| Model | DeepSeek-V4-Flash | DeepSeek-V4-Flash |
| Tensor parallelism | TP4 | TP4 |
| Workload | 8 prompts, 8192 input tokens, 256 output tokens, concurrency 8, seed 3 | Same |
| MoE backend | Marlin | Marlin |
| Chunked prefill | 4096 | 4096 |
| Radix cache | Disabled | Disabled |
| CUDA Graph | Maximum decode batch size 16 | Maximum decode batch size 16 |

The latest validation explicitly selected the supported SM120 FlashInfer paged-attention path:

```bash
export SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer
export SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_NONPAGED_INDEXER=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0
```

`SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_NONPAGED_INDEXER=0` ensures that the paged indexer path covered by DeepGEMM PR #55 is exercised. Sparse prefill was disabled to isolate the supported FlashInfer paged path on SM120.


### Latest validation: FlashInfer attention

SGLang tested commit: `245a47444c`  
Current PR head: `9f100e6e27`  
Both commits have the same Git tree: `dce05ad8fc61e17e0062bbafa376fc54cd8f95ae`.

Both cases completed all 8 requests successfully.

| Metric | Default FP8 Indexer | FP4 Indexer | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Successful requests | 8/8 | 8/8 | - |
| Request throughput | 0.155116 req/s | 0.389084 req/s | +150.83% |
| Input throughput | 1270.710 tok/s | 3187.374 tok/s | +150.83% |
| Output throughput | 39.7097 tok/s | 99.6054 tok/s | +150.83% |
| Mean E2E latency | 51.447145 s | 20.533064 s | -60.09% |
| Mean TTFT | 12.946906 s | 9.395233 s | -27.43% |
| Mean TPOT | 150.981 ms | 43.678 ms | -71.07% |

The latest server command was:

```bash
export SGLANG_SM120_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=flashinfer
export SGLANG_OPT_DSV4_NONPAGED_INDEXER=0
export SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL=0

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 31720 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --skip-server-warmup \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 16
```

For the FP4 case, the same command was used with:

```bash
--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer
```

The current benchmark entry point has moved from `sglang.bench_serving` to `sglang.benchmark.serving`:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 31720 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tokenizer /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name random-ids \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --num-prompts 8 \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --seed 3 \
  --output-file benchmark.jsonl
```

Although `--skip-server-warmup` was used in the latest run, the benchmark client performed its default warmup request before starting the timed region.

### Original measurement: Triton attention

SGLang commit: `5453e93c50`

At this revision, the SM120 attention implementation selected Triton by default through `SGLANG_SM120_TRITON_FLASHMLA=1`.

| Metric | Default FP8 Indexer | FP4 Indexer | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Input throughput | 148.52 tok/s | 159.58 tok/s | +7.45% |
| Output throughput | 4.641 tok/s | 4.987 tok/s | +7.45% |
| Mean E2E latency | 440.97 s | 410.49 s | -6.91% |
| Mean TTFT | 237.20 s | 233.58 s | -1.53% |
| Mean TPOT | 799.11 ms | 693.75 ms | -13.19% |

The original server command was:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 31720 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend marlin \
  --chunked-prefill-size 4096 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.70 \
  --disable-flashinfer-autotune \
  --disable-radix-cache \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 16
```

For the FP4 case, the same command was used with:

```bash
--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer
```

The benchmark command was:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving \
  --backend sglang \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port 31720 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --tokenizer /models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --dataset-name random-ids \
  --random-input-len 8192 \
  --random-output-len 256 \
  --random-range-ratio 1 \
  --num-prompts 8 \
  --max-concurrency 8 \
  --seed 3
```

## Why the percentage improvement changed

The two result sets are not contradictory. The following decomposition shows what changed:

| Stack | FP4 E2E | Additional time observed with the FP8 indexer (`FP8 - FP4`) | FP8 E2E | E2E reduction from FP4 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Original Triton stack | 410.49 s | +30.48 s | 440.97 s | 6.91% |
| Latest FlashInfer stack | 20.53 s | +30.91 s | 51.45 s | 60.09% |

The FP8 indexer adds approximately 31 seconds in both measurements. The major change is that the FP4 path, which represents the rest of the model plus the faster indexer, decreased from 410.49 seconds to 20.53 seconds on the newer stack.

On the original stack, the approximately 30.48-second saving was small relative to the 440.97-second total, so E2E latency improved by only 6.91%. On the latest stack, the surrounding model path became much faster while the FP8-indexer overhead remained approximately 31 seconds. Removing that overhead reduced E2E latency from 51.45 seconds to 20.53 seconds, or 60.09%.

For the fixed-concurrency workload, benchmark duration decreased from approximately 51.57 seconds to 20.56 seconds. Throughput is inversely proportional to duration for a fixed amount of work, so this is a `51.57 / 20.56 = 2.508x` throughput ratio, reported as a 150.83% increase.

Therefore, the larger percentage does not mean that the FP4 indexer itself suddenly became several times faster. Its absolute E2E benefit remained approximately 31 seconds. The newer SGLang stack made the surrounding SM120 attention and model-execution path much faster, exposing the FP8 indexer as the dominant remaining bottleneck.

The full cross-run speedup should not be attributed solely to FlashInfer because the SGLang revisions also differ by roughly six weeks of development. A backend-only experiment on one fixed SGLang revision would be required to isolate the exact contribution of the attention backend.

title: [AMD] Optimize gpt-oss-120B performance
author: kkHuang-amd
body:
## Motivation

Integrate Atom's `pa_decode_gluon` paged-attention decode kernel into
SGLang's AITER backend to accelerate gpt-oss-120b decode on ROCm
(MI300 / MI355).  The kernel requires a SHUFFLE 5D vectorized KV
cache layout that aiter's `mha_batch_prefill_func` also consumes
natively, so we add the layout as a new opt-in pool format
(`SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`) and route the AITER backend
through it on both prefill and decode.

End result on gpt-oss-120b @ MI300, TP=1, page=64, c=128:

- **+14 % TPOT** and **+15 % output throughput** vs the NHD baseline
  on 8K/1K decode; pa_decode_gluon itself is ~46 % faster than the
  legacy `unified_attention` decode kernel.
- GSM8K (lm_eval, 3-shot, chat template) stays within seed noise of
  baseline for both bf16 and fp8 KV cache.

The layout is fully opt-in — when `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` is unset
(default `"nhd"`) every code path is bit-for-bit identical to current
`main`.

## Modifications

### New env var
- `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT` (`environ.py`) selects the physical KV pool
  layout. `"nhd"` (default) keeps today's behaviour; `"vectorized_5d"`
  enables the SHUFFLE 5D layout.

### Memory pool (`mem_cache/`)
- `MHATokenToKVPool` allocates the 5D layout when the flag is set:
  - K: `(num_blocks, H_kv, head_dim/X, page_size, X)`
  - V: `(num_blocks, H_kv, page_size/X, head_dim, X)`,
    where `X = 16 / store_dtype.itemsize` (8 for bf16, 16 for fp8).
- `SWAKVPool` propagates the layout to both full-attn and SWA sub-pools
  so SWA decode can also go through `pa_decode_gluon`.
- `set_kv_buffer` already does per-tensor fp8 quant on the host before
  the writer kernel, so the kernel just byte-copies into the cache —
  no scale plumbing needed on the writer side.

### Writer kernel (`layers/attention/utils.py`)
- `reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d` / `launch_reshape_and_cache_shuffle_5d`:
  Triton scatter from per-token `(num_tokens, num_heads, head_size)`
  K/V into the 5D SHUFFLE layout. Used by `MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer`
  when the fused QKV+RoPE+set_kv writer is unavailable.

### Reader kernel (`layers/attention/utils.py`)
- `gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear` / `launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear`:
  bit-exact triton inverse of the writer. Materialises per-token
  `(T, num_heads, head_size)` K/V from a list of pool slot ids. Used
  by the chunked-prefill gather-and-linearize fallback (see below).

### AITER backend wiring (`layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` + new
`layers/attention/aiter_utils.py`)

Two 5D-specific entry points live in `aiter_utils.py` and are called
from `forward_extend` / `forward_decode` only when the active pool is
5D, keeping the backend file focused on dispatch and the legacy NHD
path:

- `forward_extend_vectorized_5d`
  - **Fresh-prompt shortcut**: when every request in the batch has
    `extend_prefix_lens == 0` (first prefill chunk, no prefix reuse)
    skip pool reads entirely and feed the raw `(k, v)` to
    `mha_batch_prefill_func` in 3D LINEAR mode (page_size=1) on bf16.
  - **Gather-and-linearize**: otherwise gather the full per-request
    K/V from the SHUFFLE 5D pool via `launch_gather_shuffle_5d_to_linear`
    into a contiguous `(T, H, D)` buffer in `store_dtype`, then run
    the same LINEAR prefill. fp8-store layers forward the raw fp8
    tensors with per-tensor descales — aiter's LINEAR-mode prefill
    supports fp8 K/V/Q natively, no host-side dequant needed.
  - Without this path aiter's paged `mha_batch_prefill_func` aborts
    with `"no matching kernel found"` for our
    `(page_size=64, bf16/fp8, SHUFFLE 5D)` configuration whenever the
    scheduler produces a non-first chunked-prefill batch.

- `forward_decode_vectorized_5d`
  - Routes BOTH full-attn and SWA layers through `pa_decode_gluon`
    (SWA sub-pool is also allocated 5D). Full layers pass
    `kv_indices` + `sliding_window=0`; SWA layers pass
    `swa_page_table` + `sliding_window=layer.sliding_window_size`.
    fp8 KV cache forwards `layer.k_scale` / `layer.v_scale` as
    `key_scale` / `value_scale` so the kernel dequantises correctly.

### Fused RoPE + KV write (`layers/rotary_embedding/base.py`, `models/utils.py`)
- The HIP fused `fused_qk_rope_reshape_and_cache` kernel already
  supports the 5D SHUFFLE layout (`flash_layout=False`). Re-enable
  `enable_fused_set_kv_buffer` for the 5D pool and have the arg
  builder pass the raw 5D buffer when `k_buffer.ndim == 5`. This
  collapses RoPE + KV write into a single launch per layer per step.

### UX
- `server_args._handle_page_size` defaults `page_size=64` when
  `SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d`, since that is the page size
  the 5D kernels are tuned for.

## Accuracy Tests

All numbers below are GSM8K (3-shot, chat template) on gpt-oss-120b @
MI300, **TP=1**, run with the following commands:

```bash
# Server (vary --kv-cache-dtype between auto / fp8_e4m3; drop the
# SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT env for the NHD baseline rows).
SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d \
SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=False \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/gpt-oss-120b/ \
  --tp 1 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --chunked-prefill-size 131072 --max-running-requests 256 \
  --page-size 64 --disable-radix-cache --port 8000 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3   # or `auto` for bf16

# Client
lm_eval --model local-chat-completions --apply_chat_template \
  --model_args model=/path/to/gpt-oss-120b/,base_url=http://localhost:8000/v1/chat/completions,num_concurrent=65,max_retries=3,max_gen_toks=2048,tokenized_requests=False \
  --tasks gsm8k --num_fewshot 3
```

| Layout              | KV dtype  | flexible-extract | strict-match |
|---------------------|-----------|-----------------:|-------------:|
| NHD (baseline)      | bf16      | 0.8855           | 0.3647       |
| NHD                 | fp8_e4m3  | 0.8893           | 0.3381       |
| **SHUFFLE 5D (this PR)** | bf16 | **0.8870**       | **0.3389**   |
| **SHUFFLE 5D (this PR)** | fp8_e4m3 | **0.8848** | **0.3374**   |

Specific path coverage:
- Chunked-prefill gather-and-linearize path (forced by the repro in
  the bugfix commit): bf16 → 0.8863 / 0.3442, fp8 → 0.8848 / 0.3374.
- fp8 with the fused write path disabled (forces the standalone 5D
  writer): 0.8848 / 0.3480 — confirms `set_kv_buffer`'s host-side
  per-tensor quant feeds the writer correctly.

> **TP > 1 caveat:** GSM8K at TP=2 / TP=4 fails on this branch *and*
> on pre-Plan-A `main` (the NHD baseline also drops to ~0.32 / 0.16 at
> TP=2). Suspected upstream MoE FlyDSL kernel dispatch bug at
> per-rank shapes. TP=1 and TP=8 are unaffected. Tracked in
> `KNOWN_ISSUES.md` (A1, local doc) — not introduced by this PR.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

InferenceX-style sweep on 8K/1K decode (256 prompts, MI300, TP=1,
`--page-size 64 --kv-cache-dtype auto --disable-radix-cache`):

| Concurrency | Layout | Median TPOT (ms) | Output throughput (tok/s) |
|--:|---|--:|--:|
|  4 | NHD baseline       | ~4.75 |   780 |
|  4 | SHUFFLE 5D (this)  | **~4.17 (-12 %)** | **~920 (+18 %)** |
|  8 | NHD baseline       | ~6.06 | 1220  |
|  8 | SHUFFLE 5D (this)  | **~4.88 (-19 %)** | **~1530 (+26 %)** |
| 128 | NHD baseline      | ~7.05 | 2007  |
| 128 | SHUFFLE 5D (this) | **~6.06 (-14 %)** | **~2307 (+15 %)** |

For full-context fp8 + 8K c=64 we re-verified single-run noise: the
SHUFFLE 5D + `pa_decode_gluon` path matches ATOM throughput within
±6 % across the sweep and beats it by 18-26 % at low concurrency.

`pa_decode_gluon` itself is ~46 % faster than `unified_attention` on
the same `(bs, num_kv_heads, head_dim, ctx_len)` for our gpt-oss
shapes.

## Known issues / how to use

```bash
SGLANG_AITER_KV_CACHE_LAYOUT=vectorized_5d \
SGLANG_USE_AITER_MOE_GU_ITLV=False \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /path/to/gpt-oss-120b/ \
  --tp 1 --trust-remote-code \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --prefill-attention-backend aiter --decode-attention-backend aiter \
  --page-size 64 --disable-radix-cache \
  --max-running-requests 256 \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3
```

- `--max-running-requests 256` (or omit; auto-tuned default is
  >= 256) is **required** for full accuracy on gpt-oss-120b. With
  `--max-running-requests < 256` the AITER MoE dispatch in
  `aiter/fused_moe.py` selects a bf16-activation path (governed by
  `GPTOSS_SWIGLU_MXFP4_BF16_BOUND`, default 256) that produces
  measurably wrong logits on gpt-oss MXFP4 — independently of this
  PR. Workaround for smaller batches:
  `export GPTOSS_SWIGLU_MXFP4_BF16_BOUND=128` (don't set to 0 — that
  crashes the server at init since warmup hits tiny `M`).

## Checklist

* [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
* [ ] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
* [x] Update documentation according to Write documentations.
* [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to Test
      the accuracy and Benchmark the speed.
* [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
