title: [MTP] Cut spec-v2 host-seam overhead in hybrid-linear MTP decode
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation With MTP (NEXTN) speculative decoding under spec-v2 overlap scheduling, each decode step consists of three CUDA graphs: ``` [draft graph] NEXTN draft model, k autoregressive passes -> draft-token chain [verify graph] target model, one forward over the draft tokens (TARGET_VERIFY) [extend graph] draft model backfills KV for the accepted tokens (DRAFT_EXTEND) ``` Between the graphs live eager "seams": accept sampling, cache-slot assignment, attention-metadata rebuild, next-step draft input preparation. At low concurrency (bs=1 to small batches) these seams, host-side Python dispatch and per-step synchronization the GPU cannot overlap, become GPU idle time. ### Host run-ahead, and what pins it sglang's `event_loop_overlap` is designed so that while the GPU executes step N, the host is already assembling and enqueuing step N+1; the host stays off the critical path iff **host loop time < GPU step time**. The `FutureMap` keeps cross-step data (next tokens, new_seq_lens, draft seeds) GPU-resident, relayed by pool index between graphs, so the host can launch the next step without ever seeing accept results, launch-queue depth grows to ~1 full step of run-ahead: Several per-step host costs, however, still pin the host to the GPU's progress and shrink that run-ahead back toward lockstep: 1. **A blocking per-step seq_lens D2H stream sync for KDA hybrids.** `KDAAttnBackend` never declared `needs_cpu_seq_lens`, inheriting the base-class `True`, which forces `FutureMap.resolve_seq_lens_cpu` onto the blocking path (`fwd_prepare_d2h_stream.synchronize()` every step). In bs=1 MTP traces of a KDA-hybrid model this stall measured ~0.5 ms/step median — the host waits for the previous verify to finish on GPU, zeroing run-ahead. GDN / Mamba2 / ShortConv siblings already declare `False` and run the same base-class metadata code. 2. **Hybrid wrappers drop the verify-buffer hooks.** `HybridLinearAttnBackend` never forwarded `get/update_verify_buffers_to_fill_after_draft`, so every hybrid-linear MTP model takes the `[None, None]` fallback: the draft stage cannot write the tree mask / positions straight into the full-attn child's captured verify buffers and instead allocates a fresh `custom_mask` each step — sized `bs * max_context_len` once the GPU-only seq_lens path nulls `seq_lens_sum`. 3. **An eager end-offset add in verify prep.** `eagle_prepare_for_verify` extends every row by exactly `draft_token_num` tokens, yet materialized `seq_lens + draft_token_num` on the host (a fresh tensor + a dispatch per step) for the generic cache-locs kernel, which then re-derived per-row output offsets with O(bs) cross-row prefix-sum loads. 4. **A 5-7 dispatch replay-prep chain.** `_replay_metadata` refreshed `state_indices_list` via separate aten ops (zero padded `req_pool_indices` rows → mapping gather → v2p translate → `-1` padding sentinel → `copy_` into the static buffer) on every mamba-backend CUDA-graph replay. **The host seam is a serial chain** — single-point savings do not add up: remove A and the CPU immediately hits B. What ultimately hides the host is the combination plus the overlap scheduling itself, not any single item. The latency payoff therefore lands as a bundle; each fix is nonetheless independently correct and independently revertible. ### Effects Before PR, GPU bubbles between draft_extend/draft/target_verify are significant: After PR, GPU bubbles between these tree APIs are almost gone: Whole picture before PR, no overlap, CUDA graph launch is sync: After PR, the verify CUDA graph launch can be overlapped in the next draft_extend: ### Provenance These items were developed and measured in a bs=1 MTP decode optimization campaign on a KDA-hybrid MoE model (4× B200, TP4, NEXTN speculative decoding), whose end state reached **~90% GPU busy per step** with the host fully hidden behind the GPU — the per-item trace measurements quoted in this PR (the ~0.5 ms/step D2H stall) come from that campaign. This PR upstreams the model-agnostic host-seam subset; every item passed the campaign's correctness gate (byte-exact 256-token greedy output + accept length invariance) before it stayed. ## Modifications One commit per item, bit-identical by construction (scheduling / fusion only — no numerical path changes): - **`Opt KDA backend out of the per-step seq_lens_cpu D2H sync`** — `KDAAttnBackend` declares `needs_cpu_seq_lens = False`, matching GDN/Mamba2/ShortConv. Safety: the shared `MambaAttnBackendBase` metadata never reads the spec-v2 CPU mirror for KDA — replay padding always comes from `forward_batch.num_padding`, and the replayssm track-flush mask reads are `not is_kda`-gated. With the full-attn siblings (trtllm_mla / fa3 / flashmla / triton) already `False`, the OR over spec-v2 backends can now stay `False` for KDA hybrids and the per-step stream sync disappears. - **`Forward verify-buffer hooks through HybridLinearAttnBackend`** — `get` delegates to the full-attn child (the linear side consumes no mask); the draft stage now writes directly into the captured verify buffers and the per-step mask allocation disappears. `update` forwards to both children with an explicit no-op on `MambaAttnBackendBase` (mamba plan-time metadata is draft-output independent); children without an implementation keep the fail-loud `NotImplementedError`, so an unvetted plan-stream combination fails loudly instead of silently reading stale buffers. - **`Fuse the uniform verify-prep cache-locs end offsets into the kernel`** — new `assign_extend_cache_locs_uniform`: end offset computed in-kernel (`start + draft_token_num`), output offset a direct `pid * draft_token_num`. NPU / CPU fall back to the end_offset-tensor reference path unchanged; the non-uniform call site (`move_accept_tokens`) keeps the reference kernel. - **`Fuse the mamba replay-prep state-indices chain into one launch`** — `_fused_state_indices_kernel` does the gather + sentinel + store in a single triton launch, preserving the reference chain's side effect of zeroing padded `req_pool_indices` rows (captured kernels gather with that buffer). Gated to CUDA + the static hybrid pool whose v2p translate is the identity + replayssm off; unified-pool / replayssm configs keep the reference chain. - **`Add bit-exact reference test for _fused_state_indices_kernel`** — see Accuracy Tests. Compatibility: no API / flag changes; NPU, CPU, unified-memory pool, and replayssm behavior unchanged (explicit gates / fallbacks); plan-stream fail-loud contract preserved. ## Accuracy Tests - **New unit test** `test/registered/attention/unittests/hybrid_linear/test_fused_state_indices_kernel.py`: fused kernel vs the reference aten chain on guard-padded buffers, bs ∈ {1, 2, 7, 32, 33} × num_padding sweep × 3 seeds + a non-injective-mapping case — asserts bit-identical state indices (incl. `-1` sentinels), the `req_pool_indices` zeroing side effect, and untouched guard tails (out-of-range write protection for `BS_UPPER > bs`). Result on H20-3e: **2 tests, 45 subtests, all pass (8.8s)**. - **e2e greedy byte-identity, branch vs base (`b98a577f`), H20-3e, tp=4** (greedy, 8 fixed prompts, 256 tokens each, `ignore_eos`): - `Qwen3.5-35B-A3B` + **NEXTN MTP** (`--speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4`) — a GDN-hybrid spec-v2 config exercising items 2-4: output text **byte-identical**; per-prompt `spec_verify_ct` **identical** (113/91/71/83/84/83/85/80) — acceptance behavior unchanged. - `Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct` plain CUDA-graph decode — a KDA config exercising item 4's fused replay path: output **byte-identical**. ## Speed Tests and Profiling These changes remove host-side work whose payoff is latency at low concurrency and compounds with sibling optimizations (serial chain): - Item 1 removes a measured ~0.5 ms/step median blocking stream sync (bs=1 MTP trace, KDA-hybrid lineage) once a KDA-hybrid spec-v2 config is active; it is inert (flag read only by `decide_needs_cpu_seq_lens`) for all other configs. - Item 2 removes a per-step `bs * max_context_len` bool-mask allocation for every hybrid-linear MTP model. - Items 3-4 replace 6-8 per-step host dispatches with 2 kernel launches. Byte-identical outputs above double as the no-regression evidence. A bundle-level TPOT A/B on Blackwell for the KDA-hybrid MTP target is part of the follow-up series and will be reported there. This is one part of hybrid-linear model optimazations, with which GPU utils increase from 67% to 95% in MTP. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :no_entry_sign: [Run #30326134766](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30326134766) Latest PR Test (Extra): :white_check_mark: [Run #30889987619](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/30889987619)

title: [AMD][DSV4]perf: shared experts fusion top6
author: karverma-amd
body:
# [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: fix shared-experts fusion for top-6

## Summary

Enabling shared-experts fusion (`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`) for
DeepSeek-V4 on MI355X (gfx950) crashed at startup. Two independent issues in the
fused topk / append path assume DeepSeek-V3 conventions (fp32 correction bias,
power-of-two topk) that DeepSeek-V4 (bf16 correction bias, **top-6** routing)
violates. This PR fixes both so the fused path runs, and shows it is a
**~+8–11% output-throughput win at low concurrency with accuracy preserved**.

## What changed

- **`python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`** — in `biased_topk_jit_kernel_impl`,
  cast `correction_bias` to `float32` before calling `moe_fused_gate`.
  DeepSeek-V4 stores `e_score_correction_bias` in bf16 (for the aiter
  sqrtsoftplus topk path), but `moe_fused_gate` asserts a float32 bias
  (`AssertionError: bias must be float32`). Only the fused-gate branch (taken
  when `num_fused_shared_experts > 0`) is touched.
- **`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/fused_moe_triton_kernels.py`** —
  `_fused_append_shared_experts_kernel` indexed the routed/shared lanes with
  `tl.arange(0, K)` / `tl.arange(0, S)`, which Triton only accepts for
  power-of-two ranges. DeepSeek-V4 routes top-6 (`K=6`), so it failed with
  `ValueError: arange's range must be a power of 2`. The kernel now iterates over
  `next_power_of_2(K)` / `next_power_of_2(S)` blocks with masking, mirroring the
  existing `_fused_append_shared_experts_with_weights_kernel` sibling. Behavior
  is unchanged for power-of-two `K`.
- **`test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py`** — new unit
  test covering non-power-of-two `K`/`S` (incl. the DSV4 `K=6` case) against a
  pure-torch golden reference.

## Validation

Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4.
Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`.
Baseline = `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, Fusion = `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`.

### Unit test

```
$ python3 -m pytest test/registered/moe/test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py -q
3 passed, 7 subtests passed
```

### Accuracy (GSM8K, 2000 questions × 3 runs)

| run | baseline | fusion |
|----:|:--------:|:------:|
| 1   | 0.942    | 0.943  |
| 2   | 0.939    | 0.937  |
| 3   | 0.936    | 0.940  |
| **avg** | **0.939** | **0.940** |

Invalid ≈ 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy is preserved (within run-to-run noise).

### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput)

| concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | fusion (tok/s) | Δ |
|------------:|:----------------:|:--------------:|:-----:|
| 1   | 69.59  | 77.06  | **+10.7%** |
| 2   | 122.31 | 135.33 | **+10.6%** |
| 4   | 216.26 | 238.91 | **+10.5%** |
| 8   | 366.29 | 403.37 | **+10.1%** |
| 16  | 569.47 | 613.60 | **+7.7%**  |

### Commands used

Server (per config; `$FLAG` = `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` or `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`):

```bash
export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton
sglang serve --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 4 --attention-backend dsv4 --trust-remote-code \
  --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs 16 --max-running-requests 16 \
  --context-length 10240 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 $FLAG
```

Accuracy:

```bash
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200
```

Performance (per concurrency `C` in 1 2 4 8 16):

```bash
python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency $C --ignore-eos
```

## Test plan / Checklist

- [x] `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` no longer crashes for DeepSeek-V4 (top-6) on gfx950.
- [x] New unit test `test_fused_append_shared_experts_top6.py` passes (non-pow2 K/S incl. K=6).
- [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.940 vs 0.939).
- [x] Output throughput improves ~+8–11% at concurrency 1–16 (TP4, 8k/1k).
- [x] Power-of-two `K` behavior unchanged (regression guard in the unit test).

body:
Day-0 support for the Kimi K3 model.

#### Nvidia Support
Day 0 Cuda 13 image: `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3`
Day 0 Cuda 12 image: `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang:kimi-k3-cu12`

#### AMD Support
Day 0 image: `docker pull lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:rocm720-mi35x-k3-20260727`
More details: #32548

#### Links

Cookbook: https://docs.sglang.io/cookbook/autoregressive/Moonshotai/Kimi-K3
Blog: https://www.lmsys.org/blog/2026-07-27-kimi-k3-day0-support
DSpark: https://huggingface.co/RadixArk/Kimi-K3-DSpark

#### Consolidated VLM follow-ups

This branch now absorbs #31318, #31581, #31587, #31637, #31638, and #31944. #31932 is superseded by the stronger `any(...)` assertion already present on this branch.

- avoid redundant Kimi vision projection split/cat copies
- make seeded random-image benchmark requests reproducible across processes
- default the CUDA IPC pool-handle cache on only when CUDA IPC transport is selected; this reuses the existing bounded pool mapping and does not reserve another pool
- keep packed MoonViT grid metadata on CPU and reuse host-precomputed attention metadata
- share the vision RoPE component while selecting the fastest layout-specific path: in-place JIT for contiguous K2.5/K2.7 Q/K and the existing strided-QKV Triton path for K3
- preserve invalid media input as `ValueError` so the serving layer returns HTTP 400 without logging an expected traceback

#### PR-before vs PR-after performance

Projection packing microbenchmark, RTX 5090 BF16: 1/2/4/8 image chunks improved from 0.0242/0.0222/0.0231/0.0274 ms to 0.0140/0.0126/0.0126/0.0134 ms (**1.73x-2.05x**). This isolates the post-projector packing path.

CUDA IPC handle-cache A/B, 4x H100 TP4, Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8 with four seeded random images per request:

| Workload | Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| output=1, burst | Request throughput | 7.55 req/s | 20.43 req/s | **+170.6%** |
| output=1, rate=4 | Mean TTFT | 496.30 ms | 97.70 ms | **-80.3%** |
| output=64, burst | Request throughput | 5.59 req/s | 17.17 req/s | **+207.2%** |
| output=64, burst | Mean E2E | 2007.29 ms | 560.14 ms | **-72.1%** |

The cache-off/cache-on runs used the same 512 MiB producer pool and had identical per-GPU memory after warmup (`69534 / 68076 / 68058 / 67578 MiB`). CUDA IPC transport itself remains opt-in because its configured pool consumes HBM.

Packed-grid metadata profiling on H200 TP8 removed all 12 `Memcpy DtoH` events and reduced `cudaStreamSynchronize` from 60 to 48 for the measured request set. End-to-end `bench_serving` stayed within run-to-run noise, so this is a synchronization cleanup rather than a standalone throughput claim.

MoonViT RoPE microbenchmark on NVIDIA B300 BF16 (16 heads, head dim 72); preparation is performed once per encoder forward and the table measures the per-layer Q/K operation:

| Vision tokens | Before: portable | After: shared in-place | Speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 47.58 us | 7.60 us | **6.26x** |
| 1,024 | 48.14 us | 7.53 us | **6.39x** |
| 4,096 | 63.55 us | 7.84 us | **8.10x** |
| 8,192 | 116.23 us | 14.52 us | **8.01x** |

The earlier H200 TP8 profile measured launch count **648 -> 108** and relevant GPU time **-5.802 ms** for the random-image request set; end-to-end serving remained within noise at that workload size.

#### Validation

- NVIDIA B300: **260 passed, 32 skipped, 18 subtests passed** across the affected Kimi K2.5/K3, multimodal transport, media error, dataset, server-args, vision metadata, and vision RoPE tests
- B300 fused RoPE coverage includes 1/480/5660/8360 random-token shapes, BF16/FP16, CUDA graph replay, and K2.5 head-dim 72 parity
- all changed-file pre-commit hooks and `git diff --check` pass

title: Autotune flashinfer extend buckets at warmup
author: sshleifer
body:
## Problem

The warmup flashinfer autotune runs a **decode-shaped** dummy forward (`BaseRunner.warmup` → `_autotune_buffers()`, 1 token/req), so tuned buckets only cover token counts up to the decode batch size. Larger prefill/extend batches fall outside the tuned buckets at serving time and run flashinfer's slow default heuristic:

```
[AutoTuner]: No tuned config covers flashinfer::trtllm_fp4_block_scale_moe input_shapes=(torch.Size([16384, 7168]), ...);
falling back to runner=MoERunner tactic=-1. This shape is outside the tuning bucket range ...
```

With flashinfer **0.6.15.post1**, the default heuristic for `trtllm_fp4_block_scale_routed_moe` is **~30% slower than the tuned tactic at >=8192 tokens** on sm100 (GB300) — flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4190. Microbench at Kimi-K2-architecture shapes (384 experts, top-8, hidden 7168, intermediate 512/rank at tp4), same GPU, µs/call:

| tokens | 0.6.13 heuristic | 0.6.15.post1 heuristic | 0.6.13 autotuned | 0.6.15.post1 autotuned |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 567 | **443 (−22%)** | 550 | **402 (−27%)** |
| 4096 | 607 | 593 | 554 | 545 |
| 8192 | 840 | **1074 (+28%)** | 839 | 825 |
| 16384 | 1319 | **1713 (+30%)** | 1313 | 1304 |

End-to-end: **−7…−9% extend throughput** on TP-only NVFP4 MoE serving at >=8k-token extend batches (dp-attention configs stay under the bucket per rank and are unaffected).

## Fix

One **EXTEND-shaped** autotune dummy forward at warmup:

- **Sized to `max_prefill_tokens`** (÷ `dp_size` under dp-attention) — the scheduler's per-forward-batch extend-token budget, i.e. the largest shape the kernels see; tuning there covers every smaller bucket. `chunked_prefill_size` would under-cover (it caps per-request chunks; chunks batch together up to `max_prefill_tokens`). Deliberately unbounded, no new knob: serving must survive a real forward at that exact shape, buffers are freed after the pass, and large-context configs are the ones whose workload lives in the big buckets. Disable via `--disable_flashinfer_autotune`.
- **Packed within the req pool**: the dummy batch is at most `req_to_token_pool.size` seqs × N tokens (e.g. 1024×16) via `_dummy_run(extend_num_tokens_per_req=...)` — per-seq attention metadata (e.g. triton `kv_indptr`) is sized to the req pool, so num_tokens 1-token seqs would crash configs with `max_prefill_tokens > max_num_seqs`. Also matches real chunked-prefill shapes. Autotune buckets key on num_tokens, so tuning results are unchanged.
- The dummy buffer set skips the `(num_tokens, vocab)` fp32 logits buffer (>10 GB at 16k tokens) since autotune runs with `skip_logits`.
- Speculative-decoding runners are skipped for now (`_dummy_run` forces TARGET_VERIFY shapes there); spec configs are a follow-up.

## Verification (GB300, Kimi-K2-arch NVFP4 MoE, tp4, flashinfer 0.6.15.post1, `batch_full` bench)

prefill extend tok/s (bs=1, n=3, IQR≈0):

| input_len | 0.6.13 | 0.6.15.post1 unfixed | 0.6.15.post1 + this PR |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4096 | 47,270 | 47,357 | 48,473 |
| 8192 | **53,155** | **48,957 (−7.9%)** | **53,401 (+0.7% vs 0.6.13)** |
| 16384 | **51,946** | **47,877 (−7.8%)** | **51,349 (+0.4%)** |

decode_long@8192 +9.6%, saturated-throughput +9.3% (ttft −17%) vs unfixed; numerics unchanged (wikitext / long-decode ppl identical to 4 digits across versions). The packed dummy (1024×16) validated end-to-end on a config with `max_num_seqs=1024, max_prefill_tokens=16384` that crashed with the unpacked shape.

title: [AMD] DeepSeek-V4: add aiter fused mHC post+pre with cross-layer boundary dispatch
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Summary

Add a HIP/aiter fused `mhc_post` + next-layer `mhc_pre` path for DeepSeek-V4 on
gfx95, dispatched across the attention/MoE boundary alongside the existing TileLang
and Triton fused paths. On MI355X (gfx950) this is a **+0.8%–1.8% output-throughput
win across concurrency 4–64 with accuracy preserved**.

## What changed

- **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_common/amd/deepseek_v4_fused_mhc.py`**
  - `try_aiter_fused_mhc_post_pre()`: wraps `aiter.ops.mhc.mhc_fused_post_pre`. The
    aiter kernel self-gates fused-vs-unfused per arch/token-count, so no token
    threshold is duplicated here; import/runtime failures fall back and warn once.
  - `try_mhc_fused_post_pre_boundary()`: aiter → Triton dispatch. The two kernels
    expect opposite fn orientations (Triton transposed, aiter native).
  - `is_cross_layer_mhc_fusion_enabled()` / `_is_production_mhc_enabled()`: enable
    cross-layer fusion when either the TileLang path or the aiter gfx95 path is
    available. `_is_fused_mhc_post_pre_enabled()` is consolidated here (previously
    duplicated in `deepseek_v4.py`).
- **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`**: route the attn-side, FFN-side, and
  `op_mhc_post_attn_pre_mlp` boundaries through `_apply_mhc_post_pre_boundary()`,
  falling back to the unfused `hc_post` + `hc_pre` sequence when no fused kernel
  fires. In the operation/batch-overlap path (DP attention) `state` is a
  `_StateDict` (attribute access, no `__getitem__`), so read it via `state.<field>`.
- **`test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py`**: gating/dispatch
  unit tests plus a gfx95-gated numerical test asserting `next_residual` (bit-exact)
  and `layer_input`/`post_mix` (bf16 tolerance) vs the unfused reference.

## Validation

Model: `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`. Hardware: MI355X (gfx950), TP4.
Image: `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.15.post1-rocm720-mi35x-20260724`.

### Unit test

$ python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py -q
8 passed
```

### Accuracy (GSM8K, 1319 questions × 3 runs)

| 2   | 0.943    | 0.943   |
| 3   | 0.937    | 0.944   |

Invalid = 0.000 for all runs. Accuracy preserved (within run-to-run noise).

### Performance (ISL=8192, OSL=1024, output token throughput)

| concurrency | baseline (tok/s) | patched (tok/s) | Δ | baseline TPOT (ms) | patched TPOT (ms) |
|------------:|:----------------:|:---------------:|:-----:|:---:|:---:|
| 4   | 216.38  | 219.66  | **+1.5%** | 17.507 | 17.242 |
| 8   | 367.65  | 372.98  | **+1.4%** | 20.715 | 20.423 |
| 16  | 568.64  | 579.04  | **+1.8%** | 26.460 | 25.960 |

### Commands used

# Accuracy
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 2000 --parallel 1200

# Performance (per concurrency C in 4 8 16 32 64)
python3 benchmark_serving.py --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro --backend sglang \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((C*10)) --max-concurrency C --ignore-eos
```

## Test plan / Checklist
- [x] New unit test `test_deepseek_v4_amd_fused_mhc.py` passes (8 passed; gfx95 numerical).
- [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved vs baseline (0.945 vs 0.941, invalid 0.000).
- [x] Output throughput improves +0.8%–1.8% at concurrency 4–64 (TP4, 8k/1k), TPOT reduced.

title: [Kernel] Enable Helion backend for Kimi Delta-Attention
author: ethche
body:
## Motivation

Add an opt-in Helion backend (e.g. used for Inkling [silu_mul fusion](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/inkling_moe.py)) for Kimi Delta Attention packed decode and prefill while preserving the existing default backends, public contracts, state mutations, and fallback behavior. 

The decode kernel delivers a **1.1x speedup** over Triton default. The prefill kernel delivers a **1.6x speedup** over Triton default. For Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct (TP=2, 2xGB200), we observe geomean **5.04%-5.27%** improvement in tok/s with **4.06%-5.22%** reduction in TTFT compared to default kernels.

This enables helion==1.4.0 as an optional dependency that is required only for the helion backend, matching what is done for some of the other KDA backends.

## Modifications

- Add Helion implementations for packed recurrent decode and fixed/packed-varlen prefill.
- Support FP32, BF16, and FP16 recurrent states, padded cache indices, bounded gates, intermediate states, and an opt-in Newton-Schulz research path.
- Register helion for KDA decode and prefill selection:
  ```bash
  sglang serve MODEL_PATH --linear-attn-backend helion
  ```
  Phases can also be selected independently:
  ```bash
  sglang serve MODEL_PATH \
    --linear-attn-decode-backend helion \
    --linear-attn-prefill-backend triton
  ```
- Keep generic decode, speculative verification, and ReplaySSM on the existing Triton fallback.
- Add registered CUDA kernel tests, CPU dispatcher tests, benchmark coverage, and backend documentation.
- Use fixed Helion configurations and static shapes, with no runtime autotuning on the model hot path.

## Accuracy Tests

- Decode comparisons against packed Triton:
  - FP32 state: maximum output difference: 7.63e-6; maximum state difference: 2.24e-8.
  - BF16 state: maximum output difference: 7.63e-6; maximum state difference: 1.22e-4.
- Prefill comparisons against recurrent Triton:
  - Maximum output difference: 7.32e-4.
  - Maximum state difference: 4.90e-3.
- Covered fixed and packed-varlen prefill, FP32/BF16/FP16 state, padded `-1` cache indices, partial chunks, safe gates with `lower_bound=-5.0`, and stable sub-chunk normalization.
- End-to-end Kimi-Linear GSM8K smoke test with Helion decode passed with score 0.915.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Measured on NVIDIA 2xGB200 GPUs. 

End-to-End benchmarks:
- Kimi-Linear-48B-A3B-Instruct
- TP=2
- input length 8192, batches 1/4/16, and output lengths 64/256. 
- Geomeans cover all six shapes for each state dtype.
- We compare against default prefill/decode for KDA.

| State dtype | Activation dtype | Overall throughput gain | TTFT reduction | TPOT reduction |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FP32 | BF16 | 5.04% | 5.22% | 4.83% |
| BF16 | BF16 | 5.27% | 4.06% | 5.68% |

Microbenchmark summary:
| Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Decode | FP32 | FP32 | Packed Triton | 1.134x |
| Decode | BF16 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.067x |
| Decode | FP32 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.118x |
| Decode | BF16 | BF16 | FlashInfer | 1.393x |
| Prefill | FP32 | BF16 | Triton | 1.603x |
| Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton | 1.595x |

H = 12, lower_bound=-5.0

| Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Decode | FP32 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.552x |
| Decode | FP32 | BF16 | CUDA decode | 0.721x |
| Decode | BF16 | BF16 | Packed Triton | 1.130x |
| Prefill | FP32 | BF16 | Triton | 1.385x |
| Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton | 1.390x |
| Prefill| FP32 | BF16 | Triton ReplaySSM | 1.707x |
| Prefill | BF16 | BF16 | Triton ReplaySSM | 1.225x |

Currently Helion decode under performs the custom cuda KDA decode kernel, as the CUDA kernel fuses convolution, recurrence, and RMSNorm. A follow up PR will evaluate Helion under the same fusions.

Note that the`bench_kda_prefill_cutedsl.py` script precomputes CuTe metadata and scratch buffers outside the timed region and bypasses the production adapters, so this is not a super faithful representation of performance (helion has a 0.86x speedup compared to cute on this benchmark).

If we benchmark the entire KDA wrapper, we observe:
| Benchmark | State dtype | Activation dtype | Baseline | Geomean speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---:|
| Helion | FP32 | BF16 | CuTe DSL | 2.031x |

title: [JIT] Restore the previous division behavior in per-token group quantization
author: 1e4ves
body:
## Motivation

  #30924 changed the FP32-scale quantization multiplier from direct division to an explicit reciprocal multiplication. This introduces small FP8 rounding differences on Hopper.

  The exact mechanism is still unclear, and this change may not fully resolve the GLM-5.2 decode regression reported in #32582.

  ## Modifications

  Restore `kMaxValue / amax` in the shared per-token-group quantization path, matching the previous v2 kernel behavior.


  ## Accuracy Tests
  - FP32-scale CUDA tests on H20: 8 passed.
  - Bitwise comparison with the previous v2 kernel: zero FP8 code and scale mismatches.
  - With #30393, the DeepSeek-V3.2 MTP L3 replay accept length recovered from `2.462` to `3.368`, compared with a cold-run accept length of `3.459`.

CC @BBuf @whybeyoung @DarkSharpness

title: [Perf] Occupancy tuning for DSA indexer fp8-quant Q kernel
author: Rainchar9119
body:
Optimize fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant scheduling: 8 warps/block
  (256 threads) + lane-0-only weights_out write. The math path (RoPE /
  128-pt Hadamard / fp8 quant) is unchanged, so output is bitwise-identical
  for both the V4 (kRopeFirst=false, kHadamard=true) and V3.2
  (kRopeFirst=true, kHadamard=false) template configs. Block size / cap
  default to 8 / 16 (tuned for sm_100 / B200), overridable via
  -DQ_BLOCK_SIZE / -DQ_MIN_BLOCKS_PER_SM.

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`fused_q_indexer_rope_hadamard_quant` (the DSA C4 indexer fp8-quant Q kernel,
shared by the V4 rope-hadamard path and the V3.2/GLM rope-first path) is
latency-bound with low occupancy: the baseline launches 4-warp blocks
(128 threads, `__launch_bounds__(128,16)`), which run the schedulers at only
~38% achieved warp occupancy. NCU shows the top stall is `long_scoreboard`
(warps waiting on global loads) with compute pipelines under 35% utilized — so
the lever is scheduling (more warps in flight to hide the load latency), not the
math.

## Modifications

Pure launch-config changes to the quant kernel; the math path (RoPE, 128-pt
Hadamard, dynamic fp8-e4m3 quant, weight scaling) is **untouched**:

1. **8 warps/block (256 threads) + `__launch_bounds__(256,16)`** — the kernel
   gains `kNumWarps` / `kMinBlocksPerSM` template params (defaulting to 8 / 16),
   doubling the warps resident per block so more work is in flight to cover the
   `long_scoreboard` stall. Occupancy goes ~38% → ~86%. Overridable at compile
   time via `-DQ_BLOCK_SIZE` / `-DQ_MIN_BLOCKS_PER_SM`.
2. **lane-0-only `weights_out` write** — the scale/weight are warp-uniform, so
   the other 31 same-address stores were pure waste.

Each (token, head) row is a fully self-contained warp work-item (no cross-row
state), so which SM / warp / order runs it does not change its 128 output bits.
Output is therefore **bitwise-identical** to the previous kernel for both
template configs — V4 (`kRopeFirst=false, kHadamard=true`) and V3.2/GLM
(`kRopeFirst=true, kHadamard=false`).

> Note: an earlier revision of this PR also added a single-wave grid cap +
> persistent grid-stride loop. Ablation (below) showed the CTA change carries
> essentially all of the speedup, while the persistent path was perf-neutral at
> mid batch and ~3% *slower* at B≥2048 (extra loop bookkeeping once occupancy is
> saturated). It has been dropped; this PR is now just the two changes above.

## Accuracy Tests

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsv4_indexer_quant.py` — checks
both template paths against a torch reference (dequantized q within fp8-e4m3
precision; `weights_out` to atol/rtol 1e-3), plus a strided-weight test.
Batch sizes span small (latency-bound) through large (occupancy-saturated).

```
19 passed
```
(V4: B in {1,8,64,256,512,2048} x {int32,int64}; V3.2: same batches; strided weight.)

Additionally verified byte-exact against the pre-change kernel across
B in {1,8,64,128,256,512,1024,2048,4096,8192,16384} for both configs: q_fp8
0 bytes differ, weights_out 0 elements differ, all finite.


## Speed Tests and Profiling


NCU pure-kernel time on B200 (sm_100), interleaved baseline/candidate to cancel
clock drift:

| B      | baseline (ns) | this PR (ns) | ratio |
|-------:|--------------:|-------------:|:-----:|
| 1      | 3104          | 3216         | 1.04  |
| 8      | 3440          | 3360         | 0.98  |
| 64     | 3968          | 3792         | 0.96  |
| 128    | 5184          | 4400         | 0.85  |
| 256    | 7392          | 6544         | 0.89  |
| 512    | 11616         | 10176        | 0.88  |
| 1024   | 20208         | 17312        | 0.86  |
| 2048   | 37552         | 30784        | 0.82  |
| 4096   | 71952         | 57344        | 0.80  |
| 8192   | 141072        | 110512       | 0.78  |
| 16384  | 279296        | 216352       | 0.78  |

Small batch (≤64) is launch-bound and stays at parity (the grid can't fill the
SMs); the benefit appears once work fills the GPU and grows to ~22% at large
batch. Wall-clock cross-check (CUDA-event HOT) matches: B=256 0.95, B=2048 0.81,
B=16384 0.79 — not a profiler artifact.

**CTA-size sweep** (why 256 threads), ncu duration / achieved occupancy /
registers-per-thread:

| config     | B=256 dur / occ / regs | B=2048 dur / occ / regs |
|------------|------------------------|-------------------------|
| 4w / 128t  | 8704ns / 66% / 21      | 38896ns / 53% / 21      |
| **8w / 256t** | **7728ns / 79% / 21** | **32320ns / 87% / 21** |
| 12w / 384t | 7936ns / 77% / 21      | 32912ns / 81% / 21      |
| 16w / 512t | 7792ns / 80% / 21      | 32880ns / 87% / 21      |

256 threads is the knee: registers stay at 21 (not register-bound; the limiter
is the resident-block cap), occupancy is already saturated, and 384/512 give no
further speedup.

title: [SM120&90] Add CUDA fused Triton sparse-MLA prefill backend for DSA
author: yunyang1999
body:
## Motivation

DSA prefill on CUDA has no fused Triton path, and the kernels it does dispatch to are a poor fit for the head count the model actually has after TP.

`flash_mla_sparse_fwd` requires `num_heads % 64` on SM90 and `% 128` on SM100+, so `_forward_flashmla_sparse` zero-pads the head dim before calling it. GLM-5.x at TP8 has **8 real heads**, so 7/8 of the tensor-core work on SM90 — 15/16 on SM100+ — is spent on padding, and the split form then writes `O(tokens x splits)` partials to HBM for a second kernel to merge. What main selects on its own for an FP8 KV cache on SM90 today is `flashmla_kv`, which is slower still from 4096 tokens up; both are columns in the tables below.

Neither cost is necessary at this size. The attention tile is small enough that one Triton program per query token, holding the online softmax in registers, beats a wide cooperative block, and it lets the head dim be padded into a 16-row MMA tile (8 -> 16) instead of into the grid (8 -> 128) — no partials, no merge.

## Modifications

Adds `--dsa-prefill-backend triton_sparse_mla`, **default off**, plus one opt-in fast path. The fast path is an algebraic rewrite rather than an approximation, and it is gated against an fp32 reference in the tests.

### `--dsa-triton-union {2,4}`

In DSA prefill the indexer's scores drift slowly in `t`, so neighbouring query tokens select nearly the same KV rows. Measured on captured GLM-5.1 traces:

| capture | valid rows/token | union of 2 tokens | union of 4 tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| bs1 x 2048 | 1024 | 1.00x one token's set | 1.01x |
| bs1 x 4096 | 1536 | 1.05x | 1.09x |
| bs1 x 8192 | 1792 | 1.12x | 1.23x |
| bs2 x 4096 | 1536 | 1.05x | 1.09x |
| bs4 x 2048 | 1024 | 1.00x | 1.01x |

One gather can therefore serve `G` tokens for ~1.1x the rows. `G` adjacent tokens share a single gathered index set, and a `G * num_heads`-row MMA tile then carries real work instead of padding. A per-row ownership bitmask restores each token's own softmax support, so the result is identical to the per-token path.

The union set is built per group, on the device, with nothing that depends on the KV span: each token's `topk` rows are sorted on their own (a `K`-wide segment, which torch sorts in shared memory), then one Triton program per group runs a vectorised `lower_bound` of every row against the other tokens' sorted lists. A token emits a row if no earlier token of the group selected it, and ORs in the bit of every token that did. Cost is `O(G * K * log K)` gathers per group from lists that stay in L1, so there is no bytemap, no workspace that outlives the call, and no device-to-host read. The union tile must be a power of two in [16, 32] rows (`tl.arange` needs a power of two, `tl.dot` needs `M >= 16`), which the validator enforces at startup: with 8 heads both group sizes are legal, at 16 heads only `G=2`; on SM90 real indices `G=2` is also the better setting (below).

**Recommended setting: `--dsa-triton-union 2`.** On SM90 it is the faster of the two at every real-index shape and end to end; on SM120 the two are within 3% of each other at kernel level, and 4 is the one measured end to end there.

One measurement note, because it is easy to get wrong: uniformly random indices have none of that structure and understate this path by about 2x. The benchmark added here builds indices as a calibrated random walk instead — token `t+1` is token `t` with ~2% of rows swapped, plus the `-1` padding real prefill has for `t < topk` — so the synthetic union sizes match the captured ones.

### Robustness

- Token offsets inside the kernel are int64, so a large extend batch at 64 or 128 heads cannot wrap into another token's rows.
- The launcher steps the shared-memory tile down rather than propagating `OutOfResources` to the request, and remembers the tile that fit per `(num_heads, G, device)`, so the retry runs once per shape rather than on every layer.
- The startup validator rejects what cannot work or exceeds what was measured: ROCm, SM < 90, more than 32 query heads per rank, `index_kpool > 1` (the pooled indexer tail is only rerouted for `flashmla_sparse`), and union tiles outside the power-of-two [16, 32] window. Tiles are tuned on SM90 and SM120; other SM90+ architectures run an untuned default tile and log a warning at startup (the SM100 CI lane exercises this path).
- Union is forced off under `--enable-deterministic-inference` (a token's output would depend on which tokens share its group) and whenever the stream itself is capturing (the FULL prefill graph); the per-token path gives the same result there. Inside the breakable prefill graph, where attention runs eagerly between the graph segments, union stays on.
- The wrapper refuses a non-bf16 KV cache with a clear error instead of reading packed FP8 bytes at a bf16 stride, and takes `topk_length` from the metadata the backend already holds rather than recomputing it per layer.
- Known follow-up, not in this PR: `get_topk_transform_method` keeps MIXED batches on the PAGED transform, so `--enable-mixed-chunk` with an FP8 KV cache reaches this backend with the packed pool and hits that error on the first mixed batch. `flashmla_sparse` has the same routing gap on main, so both will be fixed together in a separate change.

### Files

New kernel module (no environment variables); the dispatch is folded into the existing `flashmla_sparse` branch of `dsa_backend.py` (the input preparation is identical; only the final kernel call differs), with a startup validator and the option read at construction; one server arg (`--dsa-triton-union`) in `arg_groups/fields/exec_.py`; the SM120 GLM-FP8 allowlist in `flash_mla_sm120.py` admits `triton_sparse_mla` for prefill, backed by the end-to-end launch below; and registration in the DSA variant matrix so `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsa/test_dsa.py` exercises this backend too; and the `triton_sparse_mla` row plus the `--dsa-triton-union` entry in `docs/docs/advanced_features/attention_backend.mdx` and `server_arguments.mdx`.

## Accuracy Tests

**Kernel** — `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_triton_sparse_mla_prefill.py`, against an fp32 reference: base path at three shapes, `-1`/ragged padding, union exactness on overlapping-but-unequal selections at `G=2` and `G=4` including a `T % G != 0` tail (T=1023, G=4), the union dedup contract on its own (each row once, ownership bits equal to the OR of its owners, `-1` dropped — a duplicated row is weighted twice, which can hide under the cosine gate), the fall-back to the per-token path when the union tile is illegal (`h=4, G=2`), int32-vs-int64 gather addressing equivalence, determinism, two forced shared-memory step-downs (an oversized tile, so the retry path runs on the CI GPU too; the recorded fit must differ from the requested tile), and the backend method itself driving the real kernel with the `[tokens, heads, d_v]` contract. **CPU** — `test/registered/unit/attention/test_triton_sparse_mla_prefill.py`, 20 cases: the validator's boundaries (including the new power-of-two, head-cap and `index_kpool` rejections), the deterministic, stream-capture and breakable-graph gates, `topk_length` plumbing and its row-count guard, the RAGGED top-k routing regression, CLI registration, and that the SM120 GLM FP8 auto-selection still resolves to `flashinfer_sparse_mla` with this backend registered.

**Every timed point below is correctness-gated** against the same fp32 reference before it is timed — 5/5 real-index shapes PASS at cosine 1.0000 on each architecture.

Two independent model-level checks, at different tolerances, because they answer different questions.

**(a) The kernel's own output tensor** — GLM-5.2 config, TP8 on SM120, `--load-format dummy` (fixed per-parameter seed, so both runs get identical weights) and a seeded prompt at 4096 tokens. The reference is `flashinfer_sparse_mla`, the backend SM120 selects on its own (`flashmla_sparse` is not admitted on that platform). Comparing the layer-0 prefill attention output — the tensor this backend actually computes — in fp64, against a control of the reference rerun against itself:

| comparison | cosine | rel L2 | max abs |
|---|---|---|---|
| control: `flashinfer_sparse_mla` vs itself (rerun) | 0.9999998258 | 5.90e-04 | 3.05e-05 |
| `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9996746051 | 2.55e-02 | 4.39e-03 |
| + `--dsa-triton-union 4` | 0.9996746126 | 2.55e-02 | 4.39e-03 |
| `--dsa-triton-union 4` vs the per-token path | 0.9999994603 | 1.04e-03 | 6.10e-05 |

Two readings. The union path sits on top of the per-token path at the control's own noise level (rel L2 1.0e-03 against 5.9e-04, max abs 6.1e-05 against 3.1e-05): it is the same computation with the rows accumulated in a different order. The 2.5% between this kernel and `flashinfer_sparse_mla` is the distance between an FP8-native kernel and a bf16 one, not an error in either: against the bf16 `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` on SM90 (same config, same seed) this kernel is within 1.5x of rerun noise, and against an fp32 reference on the five real captures it scores cosine 1.0000 on every path.

| SM90, GLM-5.2 config, reference `flashmla_sparse` | cosine | rel L2 | max abs |
|---|---|---|---|
| control: `flashmla_sparse` vs itself (rerun) | 0.9999999134 | 4.16e-04 | 3.05e-05 |
| `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9999998054 | 6.24e-04 | 6.10e-05 |
| + `--dsa-triton-union 4` | 0.9999996655 | 8.18e-04 | 6.10e-05 |
| + `--dsa-triton-union 2` | 0.9999996657 | 8.18e-04 | 6.10e-05 |
| `--dsa-triton-union 4` vs the per-token path | 0.9999997687 | 6.80e-04 | 3.05e-05 |

Against the bf16 reference the per-token path sits within 1.5x of the rerun noise and the union paths within 2x. The pre-review revision measured the per-token row at 0.9999997999 / 6.33e-04 on the same seed, which is what an unchanged kernel should look like; the union rows are the new per-group dedup.

This is the tight measurement: it reads the kernel's output directly, before 78 layers of MoE can amplify anything. GLM-5.1 shares every attention dimension and reproduces these figures.

**(b) What the model actually emits, on real weights** — GLM-5.2 (78 layers, FP8, TP8 on SM90), seeded prompt, next-token logits over the full 154880-wide vocabulary in fp64, against a rerun control and against main's own default for this platform:

| tokens | comparison | cosine | rel L2 | argmax |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | every pair | 1.0000000 | 0 | same |
| 4096 | control: `flashmla_sparse` vs itself | 0.9985622 | 7.49e-02 | same |
| 4096 | `auto` (`flashmla_kv`, main's pick) | 0.9987185 | 6.46e-02 | same |
| 4096 | `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9987416 | 5.02e-02 | same |
| 4096 | + `--dsa-triton-union 4` | 0.9984925 | 5.87e-02 | same |
| 4096 | + `--dsa-triton-union 2` | 0.9990947 | 4.25e-02 | same |
| 8192 | control: `flashmla_sparse` vs itself | 0.9995941 | 2.85e-02 | same |
| 8192 | `auto` (`flashmla_kv`, main's pick) | 0.9993871 | 3.53e-02 | differs |
| 8192 | `triton_sparse_mla` | 0.9994118 | 3.53e-02 | same |
| 8192 | + `--dsa-triton-union 4` | 0.9990762 | 5.36e-02 | same |
| 8192 | + `--dsa-triton-union 2` | 0.9991140 | 4.72e-02 | differs |

At 2048 tokens every backend emits bit-identical logits: SM90 routes that length to the dense one-shot path and the stack is deterministic there. From 4096 up the tolerances are three orders looser than in (a) — that is 78 layers of 256-expert FP8 MoE, not the kernel, and the control shows it: the reference rerun against itself moves by 3-7% in rel L2. The per-token path sits inside the control's own band at both lengths. The union paths are inside it at 4096 and within 2x of it at 8192, the same order as main's own alternative kernel, which also flips the argmax at 8192. A greedy-token match is therefore not a usable metric on this stack; the layer-0 tensor in (a) is the measurement that isolates the kernel.

**(c) SM120, real weights, first-token agreement** — GLM-5.2-NVFP4, TP8, greedy, one generated token, comparing the argmax token and its logprob across the three prefill backends on otherwise identical servers. Each row of the control is a separate server instance, so it measures run-to-run noise of the stack itself:

| prompts | comparison | argmax agreement | mean \|Δ logprob\| (agreeing) | max |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 50 natural-language | control: `flashinfer_sparse_mla` vs its own rerun | 50/50 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| 50 natural-language | `triton_sparse_mla` vs `flashinfer_sparse_mla` | **47/50** | 0.090 | 0.255 |
| 50 natural-language | `+ --dsa-triton-union 4` vs `triton_sparse_mla` | **50/50** | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| 50 random-word strings | control: `flashinfer_sparse_mla` vs its own rerun | 50/50 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |
| 50 random-word strings | `triton_sparse_mla` vs `flashinfer_sparse_mla` | 28/50 | 0.358 | 0.854 |
| 50 random-word strings | `+ --dsa-triton-union 4` vs `triton_sparse_mla` | 50/50 | 0.0000 | 0.0000 |

Unlike the SM90 FP8 stack in (b), this deployment is bit-reproducible across server instances (the controls are exact), so the differences against `flashinfer_sparse_mla` are real and come from the arithmetic: that kernel consumes the FP8 pool with its scales directly, while this one takes the dequantized bf16 rows the RAGGED transform produces and runs a bf16 MMA. The three natural-prompt disagreements are all near-ties — "A year on Earth has approximately 365" (top-1 logprob −0.48 vs −0.71), "A hexagon has" (−0.94 vs −0.86), "The opposite of hot is" (−0.76 vs −0.44) — and on agreeing tokens the logprob moves by 0.09 on average. Random-word prompts have flat next-token distributions, so the same-sized perturbation flips the argmax far more often; they are shown for completeness, not as an accuracy metric. The union path is bit-identical to the per-token path on every prompt of both sets, and the greedy 48-token continuation of a fixed prompt is identical between them too.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel-level numbers are on **real captured GLM-5.1 index sets** at five (batch, seqlen) points, not synthetic indices; times in ms, median of 15, every variant gated at cosine 1.0000 against the fp32 reference. End-to-end numbers are on real model weights except the two 8-layer dummy-weight configs, which are labelled as such; every end-to-end table below is the current revision.

### SM90 — kernel level, vs `flash_mla_sparse_fwd` (padded 8 -> 64 heads, as the backend does)

| capture | tokens | flashmla | ours | +union2 | +union4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bs1 x 2048 | 2048 | 4.516 | 1.209 | **0.850** | 0.940 |
| bs1 x 4096 | 4096 | 8.857 | 3.154 | **2.237** | 2.421 |
| bs1 x 8192 | 8192 | 17.632 | 7.142 | **5.173** | 5.710 |
| bs2 x 4096 | 8192 | 17.629 | 6.217 | **4.348** | 4.642 |
| bs4 x 2048 | 8192 | 17.630 | 4.373 | **3.090** | 3.294 |
| **geomean** | | | **3.12x** | **4.41x** | **4.06x** |

The spread is wide but monotone in the right variable: shorter requests favour this kernel most, because more of their rows are `-1` padding that the per-token early exit skips and the padded dense kernel does not. On real indices `G=2` is the better union setting: the captured selections overlap so tightly that a group of 4 gathers barely fewer rows than a group of 2, while its membership test costs `G*(G-1)` searches instead of 2. On the calibrated synthetic benchmark (SM90, 8 heads) the per-token path takes 1.16 / 3.15 / 7.14 ms at 2048 / 4096 / 8192 tokens and `union=4` 0.96 / 2.26 / 4.88 ms, i.e. up to 1.46x; at 16 heads only `G=2` is legal and it does not pay off there (7.36 -> 8.92 ms), so union is a TP8 setting.

### SM120 — kernel level, this kernel's paths on the same five captures

| capture | tokens | ours | +union2 | +union4 | best vs ours |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| bs1 x 2048 | 2048 | 1.087 | 0.656 | **0.645** | 1.69x |
| bs1 x 4096 | 4096 | 3.288 | 1.845 | **1.735** | 1.90x |
| bs1 x 8192 | 8192 | 7.675 | **4.361** | 4.379 | 1.76x |
| bs2 x 4096 | 8192 | 6.653 | 3.708 | **3.592** | 1.85x |
| bs4 x 2048 | 8192 | 4.583 | 2.705 | **2.586** | 1.77x |

Union pays more on SM120 than on SM90 (1.7-1.9x over the per-token path against 1.3-1.4x) because the gather is a larger share of the kernel on this part. This table deliberately carries no `flashinfer_sparse_mla` column: that kernel takes the packed FP8 pool with its scales, which the real-index harness does not synthesise, so the like-for-like comparison against it is the end-to-end table below rather than a kernel-level number.

### SM120 — end to end, GLM-5.2-NVFP4, real weights, TP8, prefill latency

Launched from this branch with `sglang.launch_server --attention-backend dsa --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --quantization modelopt_fp4 --tp 8`, batch 1, one generated token, median of 5 requests with fresh random prompts so the radix cache never serves the prefix. The baseline is what mainline selects on SM120 by itself (`prefill=flashinfer_sparse_mla, decode=flashinfer_sparse_mla`).

| tokens | baseline | `triton_sparse_mla` | + `--dsa-triton-union 4` | ours | +union4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 556.9 ms | 550.6 ms | 550.4 ms | 1.01x | 1.01x |
| 4096 | 1137.9 ms | 1131.4 ms | **1008.5 ms** | 1.01x | **1.13x** |
| 8192 | 2315.6 ms | 2295.5 ms | **2034.8 ms** | 1.01x | **1.14x** |
| 16384 | 4848.7 ms | 4806.9 ms | **4266.5 ms** | 1.01x | **1.14x** |

Two things this table says plainly. The per-token path alone barely moves the end-to-end number on this deployment: at TP8 with NVFP4 experts the attention kernel is a small share of the prefill, so the per-token path's kernel-level gain shows up as ~1% of the request. Union is where the end-to-end gain is (1.13-1.14x from 4096 tokens up), because it removes most of the gather rather than shaving the MMA. Every run counts invocations of this kernel (`union=0` during CUDA-graph capture, `union=4` on the served requests), so a silent no-op cannot be mistaken for a win, and the greedy continuation of a fixed prompt is identical between the per-token and union paths.

### SM90 — end to end, 8-layer configs, TP8, prefill latency at 4096 tokens

Small configs with `--load-format dummy`, kept because they cover both model generations side by side and are cheap enough to rerun on every revision; these rows are the current code. Two reference runs are shown to make the run-to-run spread visible and the ratios are against their mean. `auto` is what main selects on its own for an FP8 KV cache on SM90 today (`prefill=flashmla_kv`), i.e. the number a user who changes nothing gets.

| model | `auto` (`flashmla_kv`) | `flashmla_sparse` | `triton_sparse_mla` | + union 4 | + union 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| GLM-5.1 | 131.4 ms | 112.3 / 110.6 ms | 80.7 ms (**1.38x**; 1.63x vs auto) | 75.3 ms (1.48x) | 75.3 ms (1.48x) |
| GLM-5.2 | 126.3 ms | 107.4 / 107.5 ms | 77.0 ms (**1.40x**; 1.64x vs auto) | 71.5 ms (1.50x) | 70.3 ms (1.53x) |

For the record, the same launch in July measured `flashmla_sparse` at 128 / 125 ms and this kernel at 82 / 78 ms (1.57x / 1.61x): the reference path has become ~14% faster on main since then while this kernel's time is unchanged, so the ratio on this small config is 1.4x today, not 1.6x.

The same kernel serves both generations unchanged — GLM-5.2 has the same DSA shape (`kv_lora_rank` 512 + `qk_rope_head_dim` 64 = 576, `d_v` 512, topk 2048, 8 heads at TP8) and the same `GlmMoeDsaForCausalLM` architecture. Its layers are not uniform (`indexer_types` mixes `full` and `shared`), so the run counts kernel invocations to confirm coverage rather than infer it: 16 per rank for an 8-layer model over two prefills, i.e. every DSA layer.

### SM90 — end to end, GLM-5.2 (78 layers, real FP8 weights), TP8, prefill latency

Each length is visited twice in-process and the second visit is reported: `bench_one_batch` warms up only at `input_len[0]`, so a plain sweep would charge the first visit to each new shape with Triton JIT and allocator growth, which lands on this backend harder than on a precompiled CUDA kernel. Two independent reference runs agree to within 0.8% at every length. `auto` is main's own pick for an FP8 KV cache on SM90 today (`prefill=flashmla_kv`). Ratios are against the `flashmla_sparse` mean, then against `auto`.

| tokens | `auto` (`flashmla_kv`) | `flashmla_sparse` (x2) | `triton_sparse_mla` | + union 4 | + union 2 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 2048 | 0.211 s | 0.213 / 0.212 s | 0.212 s | 0.213 s (rerun) | 0.214 s |
| 4096 | 1.072 s | 0.888 / 0.888 s | 0.582 s (**1.53x**; 1.84x) | 0.529 s (1.68x; 2.03x) | **0.516 s (1.72x**; 2.08x) |
| 8192 | 2.111 s | 1.891 / 1.892 s | 1.197 s (**1.58x**; 1.76x) | 1.087 s (1.74x; 1.94x) | **1.048 s (1.80x**; 2.01x) |

The kernel is not invoked at 2048 tokens on SM90 (next paragraph), so that row is one code path for every column; the union-4 run's first pass measured 0.285 s there and its rerun 0.213 s, with 0.529 / 1.086 s at the other two lengths (within 0.1% of the first pass), so the 0.285 was a one-off and the rerun is shown. Against the bytemap union this PR replaced (0.521 / 1.065 s at 4096 / 8192 in July), the per-group dedup costs 1.5-2% end to end, the price of removing the three defects. `G=2` is the better setting on real weights as it was on the captured indices: the real selections overlap so tightly that a group of 4 gathers barely fewer rows than a group of 2, while its membership test does six searches per row instead of two.

**Short contexts are unchanged by design, not by accident.** At 2048 tokens the configurations are identical because the kernel is never called: on SM90 and SM100, `dsa_backend.py` routes prefill to a dense MHA one-shot path when `max_kv_len <= SGLANG_DSA_PREFILL_DENSE_ATTN_KV_LEN_THRESHOLD` (default 2048). Counting invocations confirms it — 312 calls per rank across the sweep, i.e. 78 layers x the 4 prefills that exceed the threshold, and zero for the rest.

A benchmark is included at `test/registered/kernels/benchmark/attention/bench_dsa_triton_sparse_mla_prefill.py`. Absolute numbers here are from SM90 and SM120 parts that are not CI runners, so the benchmark is written to make the *relative* comparison reproduce on `1-gpu-large`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to Format code with pre-commit
- [x] Add unit tests according to Run and add unit tests
- [x] Update documentation — `attention_backend.mdx` (DSA sub-backend table) and `server_arguments.mdx` (`--dsa-prefill-backend` choices, `--dsa-triton-union`)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results

title: [diffusion] optimization: accelerate CUDA video output finalization
author: mickqian
body:
## Summary

- encode ordinary video outputs with H.264/AAC in one FFmpeg pass instead of writing a silent video and remuxing it
- use pinned CPU memory for the existing materialization path
- on supported Linux/CUDA MP4 paths, copy directly into a CUDA-registered memfd that FFmpeg consumes, avoiding an intermediate pageable CPU tensor
- reuse one shape-aware registered buffer (capped at 1 GiB), select a bounded x264 thread count, and retain the existing imageio implementation as the compatibility fallback

## Scope and compatibility

The direct path is used only for CUDA tensors on Linux when the request:

- writes MP4
- does not request frame interpolation or upscaling
- does not need decoded frames returned to the caller

Unsupported configurations and runtime failures fall back to the existing materialized/imageio path. Audio remains AAC-encoded and requests without audio retain the existing behavior.

## Performance

For a representative 124-frame 1344x768 H.264/AAC output:

- previous path: 1.591 s median
- registered-memfd path: 0.621 s median
- speedup: 2.56x

The resulting H.264/AAC output was validated by complete decode.

## Validation

- `19 passed` in the output-saving and output-materialization unit suites
- pre-commit passed for both changed files
- public diff is limited to the output helper and its unit tests

title: [Kernel] Fuse KV-cache writes for asymmetric K/V (head_dim != v_head_dim)
author: hnyls2002
body:
MHATokenToKVPool gated the fused store_cache JIT kernel on head_dim == v_head_dim, so models with asymmetric KV (MiMo-V2.5 is 192/128) fell back to two separate index_put_ per layer. This specializes the kernel on (k_row_bytes, v_row_bytes) and gives K and V independent cache strides, so asymmetric K/V takes the fused path as well. Equal-width K/V keeps the existing interleaved two-tensor copy unchanged.

MiMo-V2.5 (310B) TP=4, bs=1 decode: KV-write kernels 102 -> 51 per step, KV-write GPU time -76%, output throughput +2.9%, generated tokens byte-identical.

Also tightens the CPU AMX path, which takes a single row_dim for both tensors and therefore only serves equal-width rows.

title: [Fix] Route asymmetric-KV models to fa4 on SM100 and pin MiMoV2 FP8 MoE to flashinfer_trtllm
author: hnyls2002
body:
MiMo-V2.5 cannot be deployed on SM100/SM103 with default flags (#31243). The SM100 auto-dispatch picks `trtllm_mha`, whose paged-KV kernel requires equal K/V row widths, but MiMoV2 has asymmetric KV (`head_dim` 192, `v_head_dim` 128), so decode CUDA-graph capture aborts with `Check failed: key_cache.size(i) == value_cache.size(i) (37074 vs. 24716)`. The reporter had to fall back to triton with CUDA graphs disabled.

Three changes:

1. `ModelConfig.has_asymmetric_kv` — new property (`head_dim != v_head_dim or swa_head_dim != swa_v_head_dim`). A property rather than an `__init__` field because the MLA special-casing further down still rewrites `v_head_dim`.
2. `_get_default_attn_backend` — on SM100, asymmetric-KV MHA models now resolve to `fa4`, which carries `v_head_dim` through, instead of `trtllm_mha`. This is a capability check, not a model special case; MLA models are asymmetric by construction but resolve through the separate MLA branch and are unaffected.
3. `_mimo_v2_overrides` — on SM100 with an FP8 checkpoint and `moe_runner_backend` still `auto`, pin `flashinfer_trtllm`. Left on `auto` the MoE falls through to the triton fused-MoE runner (`auto` only selects DeepGEMM when the a2a backend is DeepEP / Mooncake / NIXL). Gated on fp8 because the FP4 checkpoints run through `flashinfer_mxfp4` instead.

Also updates the cookbook, whose base-variant Blackwell recipe emitted neither flag while the Pro recipe emitted both.

Measured on MiMo-V2.5 (310B) TP=4, bs=1 decode, `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 --enable-multi-layer-eagle`:

| MoE runner | tok/s | accept_length |
| --- | --- | --- |
| triton (previous `auto` result) | 315.7 | 2.88 |
| flashinfer_trtllm | 353.0 | 2.94 |

+11.8% output throughput (~+9.6% after discounting the 2.1% higher accept length).

Verification: a launch command carrying no backend flags at all now resolves to `attention_backend='fa4'`, `moe_runner_backend='flashinfer_trtllm'`, `page_size=128` and serves correctly, with generated tokens identical to passing both flags explicitly. `test_model_overrides.py` 67 passed.

title: [Quant] Keep the flashinfer_deepgemm FP8 GEMM to 1 <= M < 32
author: zhendonghua
body:
## Motivation

`--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_deepgemm` routes every dense block-FP8 linear through
`flashinfer.gemm.fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90`. That is one Python entry point over **two
different kernels** — profiling kernel names on H200 shows the dispatch flip at M = 32:

| M | kernel actually launched |
| --- | --- |
| M < 32 | `deep_gemm::fp8_gemm_kernel_swapAB` |
| M >= 32 | `deep_gemm::fp8_gemm_kernel` |

Only the swapAB half is worth taking. This PR keeps the backend on `1 <= M < 32` and
hands everything else to DeepGEMM (or triton when DeepGEMM is unavailable), mirroring
vLLM's `FlashInferFp8DeepGEMMDynamicBlockScaledKernel`, which gates the same kernel on
`input.shape[0] < 32`.

The file already carries a guard of this shape: `aiter_w8a8_block_fp8_linear` keeps a
per-shape M bound because `ck_gemm_a8w8_blockscale` returns NaN above it.

## Why M >= 32 should not go there

**Performance — the primary reason, and it holds unconditionally.** Microbenchmark on
H200, per-shape, versus DeepGEMM:

| M | flashinfer vs DeepGEMM |
| --- | --- |
| 16 (decode) | **1.05x faster** |
| 32–64 | **1.42x slower** — flashinfer's worst region, right above the threshold |
| 850 (prefill) | 1.10x slower |

So the split is not a trade-off: below 32 flashinfer wins, above 32 it loses, and the
loss is largest immediately above the boundary.

**Accuracy — a real but checkpoint-dependent second reason.** On Qwen3.6-27B-FP8,
`sglang.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k` drops **3.8 points** with the unguarded backend.
That is not noise: two same-config repeats put the noise floor at 0.15 points. It is
localized to prefill (switching only the prefill backend reproduces it; switching only
decode has zero effect), and the failure mode is specific — extra immediate-EOS empty
generations, all `ntok=1`, while the score on the answered subset is unchanged
(0.8307 -> 0.8307). vLLM reports the same class of regression on DeepSeek-V3.1
(GSM8K 88% vs 95%) as their reason for the same split.

**But this must be stated plainly: the accuracy regression does not reproduce on every
checkpoint.** Running the existing `test_fp8_blockwise_gemm.py` (Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-FP8,
GSM8K 1319 examples, 8-shot) on an H200:

| backend | score |
| --- | --- |
| `deep_gemm` | 0.9016 |
| `flashinfer_deepgemm`, this PR | 0.8955 |
| `flashinfer_deepgemm`, current main (no guard) | 0.8940 |

At n = 1319 the binomial standard error is ~0.83 points, so all three agree within
noise. The defect is checkpoint- and shape-dependent, and **the existing accuracy test
does not catch it** — please read the accuracy argument as a secondary benefit on some
models, not as a universal bug fix. The performance argument is the load-bearing one.

## Why M == 0 must not go there

`fp8_blockscale_gemm_sm90` hard-fails on an empty input. Measured on H200
(N=2560, K=2048, block `[128, 128]`):

| backend | M = 0 |
| --- | --- |
| `deep_gemm` | ok, `(0, 2560)` |
| `triton` | ok, `(0, 2560)` |
| `flashinfer_deepgemm` | `RuntimeError: Check failed: (input_ptr != nullptr) is false: input is null` |

An empty batch is not an edge case here — with DP attention an idle rank runs a
zero-token forward so the collectives stay in sync
(`ScheduleBatch.prepare_for_idle`), so M = 0 is a normal steady-state input.

## What the guard does

Resulting routing, verified on H200 for M in {0, 1, 8, 31, 32, 64} x {DeepGEMM on, off}:

| M | DeepGEMM available | DeepGEMM unavailable |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | `deep_gemm` | `triton` |
| 1 – 31 | **`flashinfer`** | **`flashinfer`** |
| >= 32 | `deep_gemm` | `triton` |

M = 0 and M >= 32 never reach flashinfer in either column. The M check folds into the
existing shape/dtype fallback so there is a single triton exit that keeps the UE8M0
scale unpacking, and DeepGEMM — which has its own triton fallback for shapes it cannot
serve — takes both ends when available.

## Tests

Both suites run on H200 (SM90), which is the only hardware where this code path is
reachable.

- `test/registered/quant/test_fp8_blockwise_gemm.py` — `TestFP8BlockwiseGemmDeepGemm`
  0.9016, `TestFP8BlockwiseGemmFlashinferDeepGemm` 0.8955. `Ran 2 tests, OK`.
- `test/registered/ep/test_deepep_small.py` — `Ran 6 tests, OK (skipped=1)` over the six
  non-MTP classes (scores 0.61–0.665 against a 0.60 threshold). The three MTP classes
  need `lmsys/sglang-ci-dsv3-test-NextN`, which is not publicly accessible, so they were
  not run.
- Routing verified per the table above.
- Condition isolation for the DeepEP interaction described below: nine server-launch arms
  on H200 varying MoE all-to-all backend, DP attention, TP size and GEMM backend.

Worth flagging for reviewers: **CI does not exercise this backend.** The only test that
selects it, `TestFP8BlockwiseGemmFlashinferDeepGemm`, is registered on a `4-gpu-b200`
runner while its own `skipIf(get_device_sm() != 90)` makes it a no-op there. That is why
the M >= 32 behaviour went unnoticed, and it means this path needs manual verification on
Hopper.

## What this PR does not do

**1. Auto mode is untouched; the backend stays opt-in.** An earlier revision of this PR
also made the hybrid the auto-mode default on Hopper. That commit is reverted here — see
point 2.

**2. This backend trips a pre-existing problem in the DeepEP path, and that is not fixed
here.** With `SGLANG_ENABLE_ASYNC_ASSERT=true` (enabled in CI outside `base-a`) the
server fails to start. Isolating the condition on H200, model `lmsys/sglang-ci-dsv3-test`:

| config | fp8 backend | runs | server start |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tp4, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep` | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | 3/3 | **fails** — `NaN detected! sampler: next_token_logits` |
| tp4, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`, `--enable-dp-attention --dp 2` | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | 1/1 | **fails** — same assertion |
| tp4, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep` | `triton` | 1/1 | ok |
| tp4, `--moe-a2a-backend deepep` | `deep_gemm` | 1/1 | ok (this is today's auto default) |
| tp4, `--moe-a2a-backend none` | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | 1/1 | ok |
| tp1, `--moe-a2a-backend none` | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | 1/1 | ok |
| Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507-FP8, tp1 | `flashinfer_deepgemm` | 1/1 | ok (GSM8K 0.8955, above) |

Rows 1 and 5 are a single-variable comparison — same model, same TP, DP attention off in
both — so the trigger is `--moe-a2a-backend deepep`, **not** DP attention and not TP size.
Rows 1, 3 and 4 hold the config fixed and vary only the GEMM backend, so on this config
`flashinfer_deepgemm` is the only one of the three that fails.

The mechanism, as far as I could trace it: some rows entering the block-FP8 linears hold
uninitialized memory. At `forward_mha.py::forward_normal_core -> o_proj` one such row
measured `6.70e16`, `5.09e35`, `1.69e38`, `2.30e38` and `3.10e38` on different calls while
rows 0–6 of the same input stayed in `[0.09, 1.1]` — a different value every call at the
same call site. Whether that becomes NaN depends on the magnitude. Injecting a single
row of a known magnitude into that exact shape (N=2560, K=1024, block `[128, 128]`):

| row magnitude | `deep_gemm` | `triton` | `flashinfer_deepgemm` |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <= 1e35 | clean | clean | clean |
| 1e36 – 3.2e37 | clean | **NaN + Inf** | clean |
| >= 1e38 | clean | clean | **NaN** |

So the uninitialized row is a live hazard for two of the three backends, in different
magnitude windows, and DeepGEMM — the current auto default — is the one that saturates to
a finite value at every magnitude tested. That is why nothing has caught this so far.
`triton` survives the table above in practice only because the magnitudes that actually
occur in this model skip its window.

With the assertion off, the hybrid's `output_ids` are byte-identical to pure DeepGEMM, so
real tokens are unaffected. These rows sit at M < 32, so this guard does not — and
cannot — protect against them.

I could not identify the buffer that produces them. Zeroing the two `dp_attention.py` DP
buffers (at allocation, and with an explicit `buffer.zero_()` outside the
symmetric-memory context) does not fix it, and neither does sanitizing the `o_proj` input.
One further data point I cannot fully attribute: with both CUDA-graph backends disabled
the same config passes, and the garbage magnitudes observed there topped out at `5.09e35`
— below the flashinfer threshold. That run also carried an instrumentation probe, so I
cannot separate "graphs off" from "probe present". The fix belongs upstream of this
backend — initialize the region, or restrict the assertion to valid rows — and is
deliberately not attempted here. I will file it separately.

Consequence for users: **do not combine `--fp8-gemm-backend flashinfer_deepgemm` with
`--moe-a2a-backend deepep` while the async NaN assertion is on.**

**3. One observation I could not explain, recorded rather than omitted.** At the same
call site (M=8, K=2048, N=2560), one run produced NaN in the flashinfer output while all
eight input rows were finite and bounded (`0.097`–`0.473`). An isolated repro of that
shape with clean input produces no NaN, and an isolated repro with one `1.69e38` row
produces NaN only in that row (DeepGEMM and triton stay finite). I have no mechanism for
the clean-input case.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code and run pre-commit hooks
- [x] Add tests / verify existing tests pass on the affected hardware
- [x] Explain the measurements and their limits above

## Motivation I had been working on the torch compile fusion approach for this for a while and am not sure what's gonna happen with it but the kernel gains are significant and can easily be done directly, this builds upon the norm quant kernels added to flashinfer which are faster than the kernels I tried writing for jit kernels (cuz they use clusters) **H100 Gains are in the range of 1.5%~2.5%** **B200 Gains are in the range of 4%~5%** references - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/10549 - https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/2243 To be merged in two parts due to AOT kernel changes - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33469 - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33471 ## B200 Gains

## Modifications Fuse RMSNorm with downstream static per-tensor FP8 activation quantization using FlashInfer's `rmsnorm_quant` and `fused_add_rmsnorm_quant` kernels. The norm can emit an already-quantized FP8 activation, allowing the following FP8 linear layer to skip its activation quantization. On SM90, channelwise CUTLASS FP8 GEMMs now consume the scalar activation scale directly instead of expanding it per token, eliminating the extra copy that reduced the fusion benefit. ### Changes - Add fused RMSNorm + static FP8 quantization, including residual paths and FP16/BF16 output dtype propagation. - Enable compatible FP8 linear layers to consume pre-quantized `(fp8, scale, original_dtype)` inputs. - Support both native FP8 and compressed-tensors W8A8 FP8 linear methods. - Pass downstream projections to Llama and Qwen2 norms so the fused path can be selected. - Add `--enable-flashinfer-rmsnorm-fp8-quant`, disabled by default. - Add native scalar-A/channelwise-B broadcasting to the SM90,SM100,SM120 CUTLASS FP8 GEMM while preserving dynamic per-token and non-SM90,SM100,SM120 behavior. **These changes give a small boost to without fusions also** - Add correctness, dispatch, dtype, scalar-broadcast, and benchmark coverage. In future PR's I hope to expand model support for this fusion ## Accuracy Tests ### GSM8k H100 #### RedHatAI/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-FP8 ```bash # Default Accuracy: 0.514 Invalid: 0.002 Latency: 12.878 s title: [ModelOpt FP4] Support online MoE weight quantization
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

- Add online ModelOpt FP4 quantization for eligible MoE expert weights from BF16, FP16, or FP8 checkpoints.
- Current contract:
  - `modelopt_fp4`:
    - Serialized NVFP4: load packed weights and checkpoint per-tensor FP32 activation scales; missing scales default to `1.0`, and loaded scales overwrite the fallback.
    - BF16/FP16 source: quantize eligible MoE expert weights to NVFP4 at load time; dense and excluded layers keep their source precision.
    - FP8 source: dequantize eligible MoE expert weights to BF16, then quantize them to NVFP4; other layers keep their source quantization.
    - Online conversion uses per-tensor FP32 activation scales. Existing serialized-checkpoint behavior under `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_NVFP4_PER_TOKEN_ACTIVATION=1` is unchanged.
  - `nvfp4_online`:
    - Quantize eligible BF16/FP16/FP8 MoE expert weights at load time with online per-token FP32 activation scales.
    - Support only `flashinfer_trtllm` and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`; per-tensor activation behavior belongs to `modelopt_fp4`.
  - Draft models:
    - For non-serialized sources, `--quantization modelopt_fp4` is inherited by the draft unless overridden; both target and draft use the generic online MoE conversion path.
    - For a serialized target checkpoint whose BF16 MTP experts are excluded, explicit `--speculative-draft-model-quantization modelopt_fp4` opts the draft into online conversion; inherited draft quantization remains checkpoint-driven.
    - Qwen3.5 MTP distinguishes serialized and online `modelopt_fp4`. Existing DeepSeek, GLM, Bailing, and Kimi NextN/EAGLE draft constructors still opt out and remain outside this generic draft path.
  - Scope: MoE expert weights only. Dense, shared, and excluded layers keep their source representation. MXFP8 source requantization is not supported.
- Related work:
  - Initial online NVFP4 implementation:
    - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/26083
  - Corrects the activation contract introduced in:
    - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31382
    - ~~CuTe DSL with FlashInfer A2A or DeepEP used per-tensor activation scaling under `nvfp4_online`.~~ That behavior is now routed through `modelopt_fp4`.
  - Pending CuTe DSL integration for the `nvfp4_online` per-token activation contract:
    - https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28354

## Modifications

- Reuse the `nvfp4_online` weight loader through a thin `modelopt_fp4` adapter instead of duplicating conversion logic.
- Use `DefaultModelLoader` for ordinary online `modelopt_fp4`; preserve explicit ModelOpt restore, save, and export workflows.
- Convert FP8 MoE weights through BF16 before NVFP4 quantization while preserving source quantization for other layers.
- Initialize missing per-tensor FP32 activation scales to `1.0`; checkpoint tensors overwrite the fallback.
- Scope exact FP4 quantization math to load-time conversion.
- Track explicit draft quantization separately from target-inherited defaults and route excluded Qwen3.5 MTP experts accordingly.
- Remove stale `nvfp4_online` backend claims inherited from the per-tensor design and document the two activation contracts.

## Accuracy Tests

- Focused B200 unit tests:
  - Environment: 8x NVIDIA B200, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260801-e4c4faf8`, PyTorch `2.11.0+cu130`, CUDA `13.0`.
  - Result: `27 passed, 15 warnings, 15 subtests passed`.
  - Command:

    ```bash
    python3 -m pytest -q \
      test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_modelopt_nvfp4.py \
      test/registered/unit/model_loader/test_modelopt_loader.py
    ```

- Static checks: `pre-commit run --all-files` passed at the current head.
- Model-output accuracy: not run locally; no model-level result is claimed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- Not run; this PR adds load-time conversion and quantization routing, not a new kernel.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).
