title: [Feat] speculative: Seed rejection-sampling draft proposals for deterministic inference
author: ajit283
body:
## Motivation

Classic EAGLE/NEXTN rejection sampling draws each draft proposal with `fast_sample()`. Although target sampling and verify-side rejection coins support request-local seeds, this proposal draw used the global PyTorch RNG (`exponential_()`), so `--enable-deterministic-inference` still changed outputs with batch shape and CUDA graph replay.

This is the draft-worker follow-up documented in #30822. Before this change, Qwen3.5-9B NEXTN rejection sampling produced 12 unique outputs in 12 changing-batch trials with a fixed sampling seed.

## Modifications

- Add an optional deterministic path to `fast_sample()` keyed by:
  - request sampling seed
  - absolute sequence position
  - draft step / MTP layer
  - vocabulary entry
- Domain-separate draft proposal randomness from target sampling and verify-side rejection coins.
- Convert MurmurHash32 output to open-interval uniforms with midpoint binning, then use exponential-race categorical sampling in float64.
- Preserve the existing RNG-backed fast path when deterministic inference is disabled.
- Plumb request seeds and positions through eager and CUDA-graph EAGLE/NEXTN workers.
- Support both ordinary and multi-layer EAGLE, including the single-CUDA-graph multi-layer draft-extend path.
- Keep deterministic rejection sampling guarded on non-CUDA-compatible devices because this implementation uses a Triton hash kernel.
- Add sampler tests for replay, batch permutation/splitting, seed/position/step separation, hash endpoints, CUDA graph updates, and categorical distribution sanity.
- Add dedicated deterministic E2E smoke tests without changing the existing unseeded rejection-sampling and chain-MTP test configurations.
- Add a reproducible seeded/unseeded sampling microbenchmark.

## Accuracy Tests

### Regular EAGLE/NEXTN

Qwen3.5-9B, TP2, NEXTN, rejection sampling, temperature 1.0, sampling seed 42:

| Version | Changing-batch trials | Unique outputs |
|---|---:|---:|
| Before | 12 | 12 |
| After | 12 | 1 |

The deterministic harness also passed changing batch sizes, prefix batching, bitwise logprob comparison, and radix-cache consistency.

Post-rebase validation on B200:

```text
7 passed, 16 warnings, 2 subtests passed
Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1
OK
```

The unit suite includes 100,000 distinct seeded draws from `[0.1, 0.2, 0.7]` and verifies that observed frequencies are within 0.01 absolute tolerance.

### Multi-layer EAGLE

`stepfun-ai/Step-3.5-Flash`, TP8 on 8x B200, FA4, three MTP layers, single-CUDA-graph draft extend:

```text
Total samples: 6, Unique samples: 1
MULTI_LAYER_EAGLE_REJECTION_SAMPLING_IS_DETERMINISTIC
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B200, vocabulary size 163,840, CUDA-graph replay:

| Batch | Unseeded | Seeded | Slowdown |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 31.9 us | 47.2 us | 1.48x |
| 8 | 38.0 us | 63.5 us | 1.67x |
| 32 | 54.5 us | 131.9 us | 2.42x |
| 128 | 138.9 us | 544.1 us | 3.92x |

Peak allocated memory for batch 128 and vocabulary 163,840:

```text
Input probabilities:       80.00 MiB
Baseline allocated:        80.00 MiB
Peak allocated:           321.25 MiB
Incremental seeded peak:  241.25 MiB
```

The deterministic mode is opt-in. A fused hash/exponential/argmax kernel can be considered separately if end-to-end profiling shows that the materialized hash and score matrices materially affect serving throughput.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and pass Ruff / `git diff --check`.
- [x] Add unit and registered E2E tests.
- [x] Preserve existing unseeded rejection-sampling and chain-MTP coverage.
- [x] Provide accuracy, latency, and peak-memory measurements.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.
- [x] No documentation update is needed; this fixes an existing flag combination without adding user-facing options.

title: Select DeepGEMM standard layouts by memory budget
author: YAMY1234
body:
## Motivation The standard DeepGEMM dispatcher currently selects the masked layout from expert parallelism alone. However, masked workspace grows with the local expert count and padded forward size, so a fixed expert-count threshold can miss safe performance opportunities and can still select shapes that exceed available memory. This follows the layout-selection discussion in [#33128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33128#issuecomment-5162601075). ## Modifications - Add `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_STANDARD_LAYOUT={auto|masked|compact}`. - Add `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_MASKED_MEMORY_BUDGET_FRACTION`, with a default of `0.25`. - Estimate masked peak workspace from the runtime token count, local expert count, model dimensions, activation dtype, and scale layout. - Cache a budget from the minimum free memory across ranks after eager buffers are allocated and before graph capture. Capture paths do not query free memory or synchronize. - Preserve explicit `masked` and `compact` overrides. ## Default Budget Calibration `Captured M` is the aggregate token dimension of a captured prefill bucket, not the ISL of one request. The masked layout allocates a padded M dimension for every local expert, so its workspace grows approximately linearly with both `Captured M` and the local expert count. The policy estimates the largest live stage as: ```text estimated_peak = local_experts * padded_M * max( input + input_scale + gateup_output, gateup_output + down_input + down_scale, down_input + down_scale + final_output, ) masked_budget = capture_start_free_memory * budget_fraction ``` The following matched Qwen3.5-397B serving measurements on GB300 GPUs were used for calibration. All memory values are per GPU. Values marked with `~` are estimated peak workspace; allocation values are taken from the CUDA OOM report. | Captured M | Local experts / topology | Masked memory | Serving result | | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | | 8K | 512 / EP1 | ~34.2 GiB | Pass | | 8K | 256 / EP2 | ~17.1 GiB | Pass | | 8K | 128 / EP4 | ~8.5 GiB | Pass | | 8K | 64 / EP8 | ~4.2 GiB | Pass | | 16K | 512 / EP1 | ~67.3 GiB | CUDA Graph capture OOM | | 32K | 512 / EP1 | 129 GiB allocation | OOM | | 32K | 256 / EP2 | 64.5 GiB allocation | OOM | | 32K | 128 / EP4 | ~33 GiB | Pass | | 32K | 64 / EP8 | ~16 GiB | Pass | | 128K | 64 / EP8 | 64.1 GiB allocation | OOM | Immediately before CUDA Graph capture, the measured free memory was 170.48 GiB per GPU. The default follows from the observed boundaries: 1. The largest successful masked workspace was 34.2 GiB: `34.2 / 170.48 = 20.1%`. 2. The smallest masked workspace that failed was 64.1 GiB: `64.1 / 170.48 = 37.6%`. 3. A calibration value should therefore sit above 20.1% to retain every observed successful case and below 37.6% to reject every observed OOM case. 4. `0.25 * 170.48 = 42.62 GiB`, which is 8.42 GiB above the largest observed success and 21.48 GiB below the smallest observed OOM. It leaves 127.86 GiB, or 75% of capture-start free memory, for other graph pools, temporary activations, and allocator fragmentation. The default is intentionally conservative rather than a universal memory guarantee. `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_MASKED_MEMORY_BUDGET_FRACTION` remains configurable because model dimensions, dtype, capture buckets, and allocator behavior can move these boundaries. ## Auto Policy E2E Verification The memory-aware policy was exercised end to end at this pull request head on 4 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with Qwen3.5-397B FP8, breakable prefill CUDA Graph, and full decode CUDA Graph. Every formal request completed with zero request errors. | Captured M / topology | Estimated masked peak | Measured free / budget | Auto JIT layouts | Result | | --- | ---: | ---: | --- | --- | | 8K / TP4-EP1 | 34.0 GiB | 175.64 / 43.91 GiB | masked only | 48/48, zero errors | | 16K / TP4-EP1 | 67.0 GiB | 170.48 / 42.62 GiB | masked + compact | 12/12, zero errors | | 32K / TP4-EP2 | 66.5 GiB | 174.58 / 43.65 GiB | masked + compact | 192/192, zero errors | | 32K / TP4-EP4 | 33.3 GiB | 175.15 / 43.79 GiB | masked only | 192/192, zero errors | The mixed JIT sets are expected: selection is evaluated from the runtime M, so large prefill buckets fall back to compact while smaller prefill/decode buckets can still use masked. Matched forced-layout controls completed with the same CUDA Graph configuration and zero errors. ## Accuracy Tests This pull request does not change the numerical implementation of either standard DeepGEMM layout. Quantization, scatter, grouped matrix multiplications, activation, down projection, and post-permute are unchanged. It only replaces the previous expert-count selector with the memory-budget gate described above. The underlying standard DeepGEMM path was already validated in [#33128](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33128) at [commit `02d9f2e642`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/commit/02d9f2e642907ceadb60279165a9359a47d436b4). The model-level run used `Qwen/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8` on 16 NVIDIA GB300 GPUs with PP2/TP8/EP1, standard dispatch, the DeepGEMM MoE runner, FP8 weights, BF16 KV and SSM caches, and full decode CUDA Graph through batch size 256. ```bash python -m sglang.test.run_eval \ --base-url http://localhost:8000 \ --eval-name gsm8k \ --num-examples 1319 \ --num-shots 5 \ --num-threads 256 \ --max-tokens 16384 \ --temperature 0 ``` Every scored request completed without request-level errors: **1,288 correct and 26 incorrect, for 0.9802130898 accuracy (1,288/1,314)**. The five-shot harness reserves five records from the 1,319-record GSM8K test file as demonstrations and scores the remaining 1,314 records. The existing Blackwell kernel test also executes the masked and compact layouts explicitly for FP8 and BF16 expert weights and compares their end-to-end outputs. This pull request only adds the focused policy coverage for the new selection boundary. ## Speed Tests and Profiling We compared the standard DeepGEMM masked and compact layouts on NVIDIA GB300 GPUs using Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-FP8 shapes. Apart from the explicit layout override, every matched pair used the same topology, workload, backend, and CUDA Graph settings. Only completed, exact-token, zero-error pairs are included. `M` is the aggregate number of MoE input rows. Across all **50 valid matched comparisons**, masked was faster: - Isolated standard runner: **24/24**, with **+40.4% to +160.7%** equivalent throughput. - Full serving, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024: **12/12**, with **+14.34% to +41.39%** total TPS/GPU. - Prefill, OSL 1: **14/14**, with **+2.69% to +68.25%** total TPS/GPU. The detailed tables are collapsed by default.
Isolated standard runner: 24/24 wins (+40.4% to +160.7%) Masked was faster for every tested M and topology. Values are median eager-mode latency per invocation; lower latency is better, and gain is `compact_latency / masked_latency - 1`. | Topology | Local experts | M | Compact (ms) | Masked (ms) | Masked throughput gain | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 512 | 1.2703 | 0.6926 | +83.4% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 1,024 | 1.2953 | 0.6869 | +88.6% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 2,048 | 1.3436 | 0.6935 | +93.8% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 4,096 | 1.4598 | 0.7132 | +104.7% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 8,192 | 1.4467 | 1.0306 | +40.4% | | TP4/EP1 | 512 | 16,384 | 2.2249 | 1.4313 | +55.4% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 512 | 1.2750 | 0.6135 | +107.8% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 1,024 | 1.2719 | 0.6011 | +111.6% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 2,048 | 1.2780 | 0.5772 | +121.4% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 4,096 | 1.3359 | 0.5575 | +139.6% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 8,192 | 1.4396 | 0.6614 | +117.7% | | TP4/EP2 | 256 | 16,384 | 1.8592 | 0.8383 | +121.8% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 512 | 1.2648 | 0.6296 | +100.9% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 1,024 | 1.2755 | 0.6344 | +101.0% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 2,048 | 1.2120 | 0.6224 | +94.7% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 4,096 | 1.2498 | 0.6044 | +106.8% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 8,192 | 1.3141 | 0.5782 | +127.3% | | TP4/EP4 | 128 | 16,384 | 1.6254 | 0.6372 | +155.1% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 512 | 1.2008 | 0.6072 | +97.7% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 1,024 | 1.1865 | 0.6254 | +89.7% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 2,048 | 1.1970 | 0.6100 | +96.2% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 4,096 | 1.2048 | 0.6009 | +100.5% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 8,192 | 1.2642 | 0.5864 | +115.6% | | TP8/EP8 | 64 | 16,384 | 1.5085 | 0.5785 | +160.7% |

title: [AMD] Support prefill context parallel two batch overlap for DeepSeek V4
author: At1a8
body: ## Motivation DeepSeek V4 prefill context parallelism (CP) distributes long-context prefill across attention CP ranks, but introduces several per-layer CP collectives around attention and MoE. Previously, the DeepSeek V4 two-batch-overlap (TBO) path only supported non-CP DP/EP workflows: - `--enable-prefill-cp` with `--enable-two-batch-overlap` was rejected when DP attention was disabled. - CP batches were explicitly excluded by the runtime TBO gate. - Existing TBO operations only handled DP/EP communication and could not schedule CP all-gather/reduce-scatter operations. This PR enables TBO for the AMD/ROCm DeepSeek V4 DSA prefill CP path. Each eligible prefill batch is split into two sub-batches so that one sub-batch's CP MoE communication can overlap with the other sub-batch's attention and expert computation. Attention-side KV and `kv_score` all-gathers are also launched early and hidden behind projection, indexer, and compressor computation. The goal is to reduce TTFT and improve long-context prefill throughput while preserving CP-only accuracy and leaving existing CUDA and non-CP behavior unchanged. ## Modifications - Add a HIP-only CP-aware TBO forward path for DeepSeek V4: - Split each prefill batch into two independently managed sub-batches. - Rebuild CP metadata and round-robin split `hidden_states`, `positions`, and `input_ids` for each sub-batch. - Restore each sub-batch from CP layout and merge the outputs after overlapped execution. - Add a CP-specific TBO operation schedule: - Overlap one sub-batch's MoE all-gather with the other sub-batch's attention computation. - Overlap one sub-batch's reduce-scatter with the other sub-batch's MoE computation. - Use persistent buffers and stream events to safely manage asynchronous communication. - Add a duplicate `attn_cp_overlap` communicator over the same CP ranks. This allows collectives on the communication stream to execute concurrently with attention collectives on the compute stream without driving the same RCCL communicator from multiple streams, which can deadlock. - Add split-phase CP all-gather helpers: - Launch KV and `kv_score` all-gathers as soon as their inputs become available. - Delay synchronization until immediately before the gathered tensors are consumed. - Keep communication inputs alive until completion to prevent allocator reuse. - Update validation and fallback logic: - Enable CP+TBO only for HIP, DSA prefill CP with round-robin split, CP-v1, non-EP TP-MoE, single-stage PP, and valid sub-batches. - Fall back to the original eager path for unsupported or undersized batches. - Align TBO padding with both TP and CP requirements. - Preserve the existing behavior on NVIDIA/CUDA and non-CP paths. - Add an AMD 8-GPU DeepSeek V4 Pro FP4 nightly test covering CP+TBO startup, high-concurrency GSM8K accuracy, per-sub-batch CP metadata, and concurrent-communicator stability. CP+TBO overlap results ## Server command ``` #!/bin/bash set -uo pipefail ARM=${1:-cptbo} export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 export SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=max export SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0 export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=${SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND:-unified_kv_triton} export SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP=false export SGLANG_ROCM_USE_MULTI_STREAM=false export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 export SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 export SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 export GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MODEL=${MODEL:-/mnt/raid0/pretrained_model/deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro} CHUNK=${CHUNK:-51200} PREFILL_TOKENS=${PREFILL_TOKENS:-${CHUNK}} COMMON=( --model-path "${MODEL}" --trust-remote-code --tp 8 --dp 1 --disable-radix-cache --attention-backend dsv4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --page-size 256 --mem-fraction-static "${MEM_FRAC:-0.9}" --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.15 --disable-shared-experts-fusion --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 --chunked-prefill-size "${CHUNK}" --max-prefill-tokens "${PREFILL_TOKENS}" --max-running-requests 256 --cuda-graph-max-bs 256 ) case "${ARM}" in base | baseline) ARGS=() ;; cp) ARGS=(--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave) ;; cptbo | cp_tbo) ARGS=(--enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave --enable-two-batch-overlap) ;; *) echo "unknown arm: ${ARM} (可选: base | cp | cptbo)" >&2 exit 2 ;; esac echo "[server] arm=${ARM} chunk=${CHUNK} max_prefill_tokens=${PREFILL_TOKENS} args=${ARGS[*]:-}" exec sglang serve "${COMMON[@]}" "${ARGS[@]}" ``` ## Accuracy Tests config | GSM8K 1319 accuracy | -- | -- cp | 0.944 cp+tbo | 0.936 ## Speed Tests and Profiling I/O = 8k/1k~256k/1k, conc=8, np=4*conc TBO's benefit scales with input length, moving from −3.6% throughput at 8k/1k to +7.2% at 256k/1k, with TTFT stabilizing at around −11% once the input reaches 64k. I/O | cp TPUT | cptbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | cptbo TTFT | ΔTTFT | cp TPOT | cptbo TPOT | ΔTPOT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 8k/1k | 3452 | 3327 | −3.6% | 1354 | 1477 | +9.1% | 19.51 | 20.18 | +3.4% 16k/1k | 6059 | 5961 | −1.6% | 2063 | 2055 | −0.4% | 20.39 | 20.77 | +1.9% 32k/1k | 10450 | 10513 | +0.6% | 3557 | 3296 | −7.3% | 21.71 | 21.83 | +0.6% 64k/1k | 16701 | 17198 | +3.0% | 6687 | 5962 | −10.9% | 24.46 | 24.28 | −0.7% 128k/1k | 23684 | 24899 | +5.1% | 13168 | 11624 | −11.7% | 30.42 | 29.83 | −1.9% 256k/1k | 29004 | 31102 | +7.2% | 27542 | 24383 | −11.5% | 43.37 | 41.74 | −3.8% I/O = 128k/1k, conc=2/4/8/16, np=4*conc At a fixed 128k input, TBO gains grow with concurrency (−1.2% → +4.6% throughput from conc 2 to 16), while TTFT improves consistently by 8–11% across all levels. conc | cp TPUT | tbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | tbo TTFT | ΔTTFT | cp TPOT | tbo TPOT | ΔTPOT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 2 | 9536 | 9424 | −1.2% | 4813 | 4417 | −8.2% | 22.25 | 22.97 | +3.2% 4 | 15534 | 15713 | +1.2% | 7663 | 7047 | −8.0% | 25.57 | 25.86 | +1.1% 8 | 22449 | 23349 | +4.0% | 13479 | 12258 | −9.1% | 32.51 | 31.96 | −1.7% 16 | 28333 | 29651 | +4.6% | 25237 | 22501 | −10.8% | 47.65 | 47.11 | −1.1% I/O = 50k/1, prefill only With decode removed, TBO reaches its full prefill-side benefit: 10–14% higher throughput and 8–12% lower TTFT at every concurrency level. conc | cp TPUT | tbo TPUT | ΔTPUT | cp TTFT | tbo TTFT | ΔTTFT -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- 2 | 44133 | 49299 | +11.7% | 2141 | 1941 | −9.3% 4 | 45040 | 49594 | +10.1% | 4042 | 3711 | −8.2% 8 | 45410 | 50311 | +10.8% | 8003 | 7266 | −9.2% 16 | 45536 | 51859 | +13.9% | 15683 | 13823 | −11.9% ## Checklist - title: perf(hisparse): fuse the DSv4 value and scale swap-in copy on ROCm
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
## Motivation

A DeepSeek-V4 C4 token is 584 bytes, but it is **not one contiguous range**. A page row holds 64 values of 576B followed by 64 scales of 8B:

```
/// Paged C4 cache layout:
/// VALUE 0, VALUE 1, ..., VALUE 63,
/// SCALE 0, SCALE 1, ..., SCALE 63,
/// [Padding to align to 576 bytes]
```

So the ROCm swap-in copies a token with two `transfer_item_warp` calls, 576B then 8B. On wave64 that is three wavefront passes — 64 value words, 8 value words, then 1 scale word — and only the first keeps the whole wavefront busy.

The passes also do not overlap. `item_size_bytes` reaches `transfer_item_warp` as a runtime argument, so the compiler keeps the value copy as a rolled loop with the wait inside the body. Disassembling the gfx950 code object:

```
global_load_dwordx2 v[30:31], v[22:23]
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[24:25], v[30:31]
s_cbranch_execnz ...                       <- second value pass
...
global_load_dwordx2 v[22:23], v[22:23]     <- scale
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[24:25], v[22:23]
```

Three serialized host round trips per miss, on the decode critical path: `swap_in_selected_pages` runs once per C4 layer per decode step, on the main stream, between that layer's indexer and its attention.

The CUDA branch does not have this problem — `device::hisparse::transfer_item` already moves the value tail and the scale together. It is unusable on ROCm only because its warp logic is hardcoded to 32 lanes.

## Modifications

Adds `transfer_dsv4_item_warp`, used by the ROCm `IsDsv4Layout` miss copy in place of the two `transfer_item_warp` calls. It walks the token as one 73-word space so the value tail and the scale land in the same pass, and stages every load before any store. The pass count is a compile-time constant, so the copy unrolls and both loads issue before either store:

```
global_load_dwordx2 v[22:23], v[24:25]
global_load_dwordx2 v[20:21], v[18:19]
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[16:17], v[22:23]
s_waitcnt vmcnt(0)
global_store_dwordx2 v[14:15], v[20:21]
```

One exposed round trip instead of three. No API, config, or template change. CUDA behavior untouched; the generic (non-DSv4) path is untouched.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), DSv4 paged-layout swap-in, `miss_rate=0.2`, `hot_buffer_size=4096`, `top_k=2048`.

**Methodology.** Both variants are compiled into a single kernel and selected at runtime, with reps alternating between arms inside one process. This matters here: comparing two separate builds moves identical code paths by up to 14% on this kernel, which is more than the effect being measured. Medians of 15 reps × 5 timed rounds, two independent runs.

| batch | before | after | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 102.4 / 105.7 us | **87.8 / 87.9 us** | -14.2% / -16.9% |
| 10 | 122.8 / 119.8 us | **97.2 / 96.2 us** | -20.9% / -19.8% |
| 24 | 136.9 / 136.1 us | 125.2 / 125.2 us | -8.5% / -8.0% |
| 100 | 468.6 / 467.5 us | 451.7 / 451.5 us | -3.6% / -3.4% |

The copy is worth optimizing: dropping `miss_rate` from 0.2 to 0.001 on the unmodified kernel takes batch 1 from 110.7 to 20.5 us, so **82% of the swap-in is the miss copy**. The gain fades at high batch because the kernel becomes bandwidth-bound rather than latency-bound, and round-trip count stops mattering there.

### A one-pass variant was tried and is worse

576B is exactly 36 × 16B, and both the page stride (37440) and the value stride (576) are multiples of 16, so the value is always 16B-aligned and the whole token fits in a single pass: lanes 0–35 move one 16B vector each, lane 36 moves the scale. Despite needing fewer passes it lost at every batch size, and was slower than the baseline at batch 1:

| batch | two-pass 64-bit | one-pass 128-bit |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | -14.2% / -16.9% | +3.6% / +1.0% |
| 10 | -20.9% / -19.8% | -4.9% / -4.3% |
| 24 | -8.5% / -8.0% | -4.7% / -4.3% |
| 100 | -3.6% / -3.4% | -1.1% / -1.0% |

The two-pass form engages all 64 lanes on its first pass; the one-pass form only 37. For these host reads, full wavefront occupancy at 64-bit beats partial occupancy at 128-bit even when the wider form needs fewer round trips. This is the same effect that gates the widening in #33085.

## Accuracy Tests

Adds `test_load_cache_to_device_buffer_dsv4_fused_copy_multi_miss`: several misses in one launch at varying source and destination page offsets, including the second page, so the value/scale seam does not always fall at the same address. It takes the destinations from the kernel output rather than assuming an eviction order, and checks that slots the kernel never wrote keep their fill.

Suppressing the scale half of the copy fails both the new test and the existing `dsv4_mla_miss_copy_layout` case, so the coverage has teeth.

Full file on MI355X: 10 passed, 2 skipped (the 2 skips are the CUDA-only DSv4 paged cases).

## Checklist

- [x] Format: `black` clean; C++ change confined to the ROCm `#ifdef` branch, <= 120 cols.
- [x] No public API / config / docs surface touched.
- [x] Unit test added for the new code path; full file run before/after on MI355X.

Related: #33085 (widens the generic path; disjoint branch, no overlap with this change).

title: [Model] Support Ling-3.0-flash (BailingMoeV3)
author: JustinTong0323
body:
## Motivation

Day-0 support for [inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash](https://huggingface.co/inclusionAI/Ling-3.0-flash) (`BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM`, `model_type=bailing_hybrid`): a hybrid MoE architecture interleaving KDA linear attention (with a safe-gate lower bound) and MLA, with MTP (NEXTN) and DSPARK speculative decoding support.

## Modifications

- `BailingMoeV3ForCausalLM` model (`bailing_hybrid` config): KDA + MLA hybrid layers, 512-expert MoE, and MTP (NEXTN).
- DSPARK support for the KDA hybrid path: graph-folded draft proposal, fused KDA chain-verify kernel, and DSA token-to-KV pool sizing.
- KDA safe gate propagation through the Triton decode/target-verify kernels and their call sites, matching fused verification.
- `ling3` reasoning and tool-call parsers.
- BF16, FP8, compressed-tensors INT4, and native MXFP4 checkpoint support on Hopper and Blackwell.
- Exactness, fusion-gate, quantization, and parser tests.

## Validation

All serving runs kept decode CUDA Graph enabled and used the default graph sizing. No run used `--disable-cuda-graph` or `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode`.

### Quantized checkpoints

Full GSM8K uses 1,319 questions. Performance uses 80 exact-length random requests at ISL/OSL 8192/1024 with concurrency 1 and 16; throughput includes input and output tokens per second per GPU.

| GPU | format | GSM8K | stop rate | throughput/GPU (c1 / c16) | P50 TTFT ms (c1 / c16) | P50 TPOT ms (c1 / c16) | default graph range |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| H200 | INT4 | 95.30% | 100% | 1,159 / 7,184 | 205.96 / 1,891.74 | 3.68 / 8.16 | through batch 218 |
| H200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 100% | 709 / 5,215 | 305.23 / 2,725.52 | 6.05 / 11.17 | through batch 227 |
| B200 | INT4 | 96.74% | 99.70% | 482 / 1,344 | 641.41 / 6,202.62 | 8.72 / 48.01 | through batch 305 |
| B200 | MXFP4 | 96.29% | 99.62% | 785 / 7,933 | 127.97 / 1,117.16 | 5.60 / 7.98 | through batch 314 |

INT4 selects Marlin on H200 and the graph-compatible Triton WNA16 path on B200. MXFP4 routed experts use the native FlashInfer runner on both GPUs. The B200 MXFP4 checkpoint also contains block-FP8 dense/shared projections, which use the Triton FP8 GEMM backend to avoid an unsupported FlashInfer FP8 tactic without converting the routed experts.

BF16 and FP8 were rerun on H200 and B200 after the quantization changes. All four combinations served with CUDA Graph enabled, completed generation, and passed the 20-example GSM8K regression gate with 100% stop rate.

### Speculative decoding

Ling-3.0-flash BF16, 4x B200 TP4, `temperature=1.0 / top_p=0.95`, thinking on, full GSM8K, `max_tokens=8192`:

| spec decoding | score | stop rate | error rate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DSPARK | 96.66% | 99.77% | 0.00% |
| MTP (NEXTN) | 96.44% | 99.62% | 0.00% |

Non-stop finishes are long reasoning outputs reaching `max_tokens`, not repetition loops.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests and register them in CI.
- [x] Validate serving correctness, stop rate, and accuracy on H200 and B200.
- [x] Publish deployment recipes and benchmark results in #34363.

title: [NPU] [Diffusion] Support MiniMax H3 on Ascend NPU's
author: OrangeRedeng
body: ## Motivation Extend the native MiniMax-H3 pipeline from [#33275](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33275) to Ascend NPU, including packed variable-length attention, NPU-safe runtime paths, media dependencies, documentation, and CI coverage. MiniMax-H3 packs real multimodal tokens together with sequence-parallel alignment padding, so the NPU attention path must keep the real-token and padding segments isolated. The implementation also needs device-generic RNG/autocast/residency handling and safe fallbacks for CUDA/ROCm-specific fused kernels. ## Changes - Add MiniMax-H3 full-loop denoising support on Ascend NPU. - Enable `laser_attn` with packed variable-length handling: compute attention only for real tokens, preserve the padded shape, and zero-fill alignment-padding outputs. - Preserve BF16 activation range around the FP16 Laser kernel by compensating Q/K and value/output scaling. - Use `torch_sdpa` for the Qwen3-VL text encoder when the MiniMax-H3 transformer uses `laser_attn`. - Generalize keyframe RNG forking, decode autocast, and device checks to the active platform; reuse the existing NPU `SiluAndMul` path and generic fallbacks where CUDA/ROCm fused kernels are unavailable. - Install and validate `ffmpeg`/`ffprobe` for MiniMax-H3 media output on Ascend; provide actionable errors/fallbacks for missing runtime dependencies. - Add Ascend cookbook examples and validated TP2+SP4 (8 NPU) / TP2+SP2 (4 NPU) topologies with Cache-DiT. - Add `minimax_h3_t2va_2npu` to Ascend CI with performance and consistency checks, refresh the NPU diffusion baselines, and make baseline generation/diagnostics target the platform-specific baseline file. Related work: [#33827](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33827) adds Cache-DiT support for MiniMax-H3; [#33927](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33927) tracks the FFmpeg-related output issue; [#33366](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/33366) is the related XPU enablement. ## Ascend CI `minimax_h3_t2va_2npu` uses 2 NPUs (TP2 + SP1), `laser_attn`, a resident DiT, layerwise-offloaded text encoder, Cache-DiT, 5-second 1344×768 T2VA generation, 50 inference steps, and seed 1101. Performance and visual consistency checks are enabled against Ascend GT pinned to `ci-data-diffusion@7df858ead07940ff4d9489230fa9f040dd186789`. MiniMax-H3 2-NPU baseline: `e2e=155106.21 ms`, `avg_denoise=2749.56 ms`, `median_denoise=613.17 ms`. _All CI baselines were updated based on the latest results as part of the CI fixing started in https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34855_ ## Accuracy Tests Validated end-to-end 5-second MiniMax-H3 T2VA generation with both Ascend Flash Attention and Laser Attention on 8 Ascend NPUs. Image-conditioned FL2VA was also validated with Laser Attention. The automated 2-NPU NPU CI case runs both performance and visual consistency checks against the pinned Ascend GT revision. title: [AMD] Add Work-Centric (Lean) Attention: a persistent-CTA decode kernel for long-context serving
author: valechen
body:
## Motivation

The standard flash-decode ("SplitK") attention kernel parallelizes decode by splitting each sequence's KV cache into chunks and assigning chunks to GPU compute units (CUs). While effective at short context, it leaves performance on the table in two common serving regimes:

- **Long-context, low-batch** — std's grid is `batch × head-tiles × num_splits` with a fixed split count, so a single (or few) long sequence cannot generate enough KV-split work to fill all CUs: many CUs sit idle while the few launched programs each grind through a long serial KV loop, and decode-step latency grows **roughly linearly** with context, making the workload occupancy-starved, not bandwidth-bound. As context windows reach 64K–128K+, attention dominates the
  decode step here.
- **Ragged batches** — with mixed sequence lengths, SplitK cannot rebalance a long request's work onto the CUs freed by short requests, so a few stragglers set the step latency.

**Work-Centric Attention (WCA / "Lean")** launches a fixed persistent grid sized to the device CU count and derives its KV-tile schedule on-device from `kv_indptr`, cooperatively splitting long sequences across CTAs (work-stealing) so no CU idles. Decode-attention latency stays **nearly flat** as context grows (1.06–1.30× E2E throughput even on uniform batches) and absorbs raggedness for free (up to 1.52× throughput, 3.62× lower ITL). Lean is numerically identical to the standard kernel
and ships behind a conservative auto-gate that enables it only where it wins — including by default under CUDA graphs — so existing workloads are unaffected.

Validated on **AMD MI355X (gfx950)** across GQA (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and MLA (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4, TP=4, fp8 KV). Also re-validated on **AMD MI300X (gfx942)** at the same 1×CU grid across GQA (Qwen2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B) and MLA (proxied with DeepSeek-V2-Lite, fp8 KV, since fp4/MXFP4 GEMM is gfx950-only).

## Modifications

A minimal, mostly-additive change (6 files, ~+1540 lines) on the ROCm/Triton backend. Almost all of it is new code; the only edits to existing paths are the `forward_decode` dispatch hook and the `decode_attention_fwd` signature. The standard decode path is untouched when Lean is inactive.

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py` (+822) | The Lean kernel (`_lean_attention_decode_kernel`) and its launch/dispatch helpers. `decode_attention_fwd` gains an `enable_lean` parameter and early dispatch to Lean. Supports bf16/fp16 and **fp8** KV (fold `k_scale` into `sm_scale`, cast `q → K.dtype` for the fp8×fp8 MMA, dequantize rope-split `kpe`, apply `v_scale`), and both contiguous and **paged** KV (`kv_loc // page_size` / `% page_size` addressing). Auto-gate: `lean_decode_seqlen_gate` (eager) and `lean_capture_policy` (CUDA-graph capture). |
| `test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py` (+440) | CI gating test on the MI35x AMD per-commit suite (`stage-b-test-1-gpu-small-amd-mi35x`): parity vs standard SplitK for bf16 (cos > 0.999), fp8 (cos > 0.99), and paged KV (cos > 0.999), plus gate/policy logic. |
| `python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/triton_backend.py` (+119) | Resolve `enable_lean_attention` in `forward_decode` (explicit override → auto-gate → kill-switch); allocate the Lean scratch buffers (Mp/Lp/Op/locks) for the eager and CUDA-graph paths. |
| `benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py` (+150) | Kernel-level Lean-vs-standard (SplitK) sweep: both GQA head configs × full batch/context grid, per-call latency, speedup, cosine parity, and eager-gate decision; writes a CSV. |
| `python/sglang/srt/server_args.py` (+4) | `--enable-lean-attention` flag (`Optional[bool]`, default `None` = auto-gate). |
| `python/sglang/srt/environ.py` (+11) | Two env vars: `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION` kill-switch (force the standard kernel) and `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT` (persistent-grid size multiplier, default `1.0` = one CTA per CU; a knob for grid A/B without a rebuild). |

**Design:**

- **Persistent grid.** Launches `total_programs = device CU count` CTAs — one CTA per CU (rounded to whole XCDs under the ROCm XCD remap). One CTA per CU maximizes the KV work-tiles handled per CTA, so each CTA's cross-CTA combine/atomic reduction amortizes more useful work; oversubscribing (e.g. 2 CTAs/CU) halves tiles-per-CTA and inflates that reduction, regressing high-batch decode (measured on MI300X/gfx942 and confirmed on MI355X/gfx950). The grid is independent of batch×heads×splits, so it is CUDA-graph capturable and a single captured grid replays across batch sizes.
- **On-device work-stealing.** Each CTA computes its slice of the global KV-tile work list from `kv_indptr`; long sequences are cooperatively split across CTAs. The schedule is derived from `kv_indptr` **at replay**, so a captured graph adapts to the real per-step sequence lengths and raggedness — no host sync, no per-step relaunch.
- **Auto-gate.** The default (`None`) resolves to a concrete decision before launch; explicit `True`/`False` overrides it. Because Lean is a win only in specific regimes, the gate operates in two modes:
  - *Eager decode*, where real `seq_lens` are known: `lean_decode_seqlen_gate` keys a length threshold on query-head parallelism (`tiles = ceil(num_q_heads / min(16, kv_group))`, i.e. how well the standard kernel already fills the CUs), relaxed as batch grows.
  - *CUDA-graph capture*, where per-step lengths are not yet known: `lean_capture_policy` makes the bake decision from capture-time-known signals (`batch`, `tiles`, `is_mla`) — bake GQA/MHA at `batch ≥ 16`, MLA at `batch ≥ 8`, and never for heavy TP shards (`tiles < 4`). Lean's fixed grid then adapts to the actual lengths at replay.
- **Shape/dtype coverage.** MHA, GQA, and MLA (rope-split `qk_head_dim != v_head_dim`); bf16/fp16/fp8 KV; contiguous and paged KV. Falls back to the standard kernel for unimplemented features (logit capping, attention sinks, xAI temperature, score modification), so results are never silently wrong.

**Usage:**
- Default (`None`): auto-gate — Lean turns on automatically where it wins (including by default under CUDA graphs). No flag needed.
- Force on: `--enable-lean-attention` (with `--attention-backend triton`).
- Force off: `--enable-lean-attention=False`, or `SGLANG_DISABLE_LEAN_ATTENTION=1`.

## Accuracy Tests

**Test configuration:**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Hardware** | 1× AMD Instinct MI355X (256 CUs, gfx950, 288 GB HBM3E) |
| **Software** | ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch 2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, Triton 3.7.0 (AMD wheel) |
| **Models (head shapes)** | Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (GQA 28Q/4KV, D=128) · Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct (GQA 32Q/8KV, D=128) |
| **Method** | Isolated decode-attention call; compare Lean vs standard SplitK output over three KV formats — bf16, fp8 (e4m3, per-tensor scales), and paged (4-D buffer, scattered slots) |
| **Metric** | Cosine similarity of the two output tensors |

**Command** (the registered CI gating test):

```bash
python3 -m pytest test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py -v
# Per shape: standard = decode_attention_fwd(..., enable_lean=False)
#            lean     = decode_attention_fwd(..., enable_lean=True, lean_Mp/Lp/Op/locks=...)
#            cos      = F.cosine_similarity(o_lean.flatten().float(), o_std.flatten().float(), dim=0)
```

**Results.** Lean matches the standard kernel across every tested configuration:

| KV format | Configs | Result |
|-----------|:-------:|:-------|
| bf16/fp16 | 59 cells (2 models × 6 batches × 5 contexts, less Llama b32×128K) | **cosine = 1.0000** (bit-identical) |
| fp8 e4m3 (per-tensor scale) | 2 models × {b1,b8} × {8K,32K} | **cosine > 0.99** (fp8 quantization noise only) |
| paged (4-D, scattered slots) | 2 models × page_size {16, 64} | **cosine > 0.999** |

Every measured configuration is bit-identical in bf16 (the one unmeasured cell, Llama batch-32 × 128K, exceeds the microbenchmark's single contiguous KV tensor — it is a harness limit, not a kernel result). The committed CI gating test (`test_lean_attention.py`) reproduces the bf16, fp8, and paged parity checks on the MI35x per-commit suite. Because output is numerically equivalent, downstream generation quality is unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Unless noted otherwise, the tables below are on **1× MI355X** (gfx950); the dedicated **MI300X (gfx942)** subsection re-runs the same suites on that arch. Both: ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, **Triton 3.7.0** (AMD wheel; the production ROCm wheel — the stock rocm7.2 image's Triton 3.5.1 inverts the crossover and must not be used for Lean benchmarking). The **baseline is the Triton backend's own standard decode kernel, not AITER**: both arms use `--attention-backend triton`
and dispatch through the same `decode_attention_fwd`, differing only in the `enable_lean` branch, so this is a clean Lean-vs-standard A/B.

### Kernel-level (isolated decode attention, speedup = standard ÷ lean)

Direct kernel call, fp16, random Q/K/V, `page_size=1`; batch ∈ {1,2,4,8,16,32} × context ∈ {8K,16K,32K,64K,128K}. **Command:** `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT=1.0 python3 benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py`

**Qwen2.5-7B (28Q/4KV):**

| batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K |
|------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:|
|     1 | 0.46× | 0.92× | **1.86×** | **3.30×** | **5.33×** |
|     8 | 0.59× | **1.04×** | **1.28×** | **1.59×** | **1.95×** |
|    32 | **1.78×** | **1.99×** | **2.21×** | **1.74×** | **1.77×** |

**Llama-3.1-8B (32Q/8KV):**

| batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K |
|------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:|
|     1 | 0.79× | **1.47×** | **2.41×** | **3.56×** | **5.92×** |
|     8 | **1.46×** | **1.82×** | **1.97×** | **2.18×** | **1.71×** |
|    32 | **2.13×** | **2.29×** | **1.74×** | **1.73×** | — |

**Bold** = Lean is faster at the kernel level (speedup ≥ 1×). Peak **5.33× (Qwen) / 5.92× (Llama)** at batch=1 / 128K; speedup grows superlinearly with context (SplitK's idle-CU penalty scales with length, Lean's stays flat) and the crossover falls with batch. The production auto-gate turns Lean on around the **end-to-end** break-even (later than the isolated-kernel crossover), so it enables the long-context / larger-batch cells and keeps the standard kernel for short-context low-batch. (The batch-32 × 128K Llama cell exceeds the microbenchmark's single contiguous KV tensor and is not
measured; real serving uses a paged KV pool and is unaffected — see the E2E tables.)

### End-to-end serving — GQA

Full-model serving, closed-loop / fixed-batch (`num-prompts == max-concurrency == reqs`, `--request-rate inf`), CUDA graphs on (`--cuda-graph-bs 1 2 4 8 16 32`), `--seed 42` (both arms see the identical batch). `--random-range-ratio r` samples per-request prompt **and** output lengths in `[r·ctx, ctx]`, so `ratio < 1` = ragged. Rows include batch 1 to show the low-batch long-context win and the auto-gate's enabled region (GQA `batch ≥ 16`); below b16 the standard kernel runs by default.

Columns: **reqs** = concurrent requests; **KV mean / KV range** = mean and min–max prompt (KV) length across the batch; **dec/req** = mean decode (output) tokens per request; **dec iters** = total decode tokens measured; **tps×** = Lean ÷ baseline output throughput; **ITL× / p99×** = baseline ÷ Lean median / p99 inter-token latency (>1 = Lean faster).

| model | B | ratio | reqs | KV mean | KV range | dec/req | dec iters | tps× | ITL× | p99× |
|-------|--:|------:|-----:|--------:|:--------:|--------:|----------:|-----:|-----:|-----:|

| Qwen2.5-7B  | 32 | 1.0 | 32 | 65536 | 65K (uniform) | 512 | 16384 | 1.07 | 1.66 | 1.67 |

| Llama-3.1-8B | 1  | 1.0 | 1  | 65535 | 65K (uniform) | 512 | 512 | 1.24 | 1.59 | 1.59 |

Lean wins across every measured cell — all 26 have `tps× ≥ 1.06`, none regress. The win grows with raggedness (lower ratio) and context: peak **1.52× throughput** (Llama b32/16K r0.1) and **3.62× / 2.91× lower median / p99 ITL** (Llama b32/65K r0.1). **Uniform batches are also faster at every size** (1.06–1.30× throughput, 1.28–1.93× lower ITL) — e.g. b1 uniform 65K: Qwen 1.27× tps / 1.63× ITL, Llama 1.24× / 1.59×; b32 uniform 65K: Qwen 1.07× / 1.66×, Llama 1.16× / 1.93×.

```bash
# Client — per (B, ctx, ratio):
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --model Qwen/Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct \

```

### End-to-end serving — MLA (DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4, TP=4, fp8 KV)

Same closed-loop methodology, `--tp-size 4 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3`. Rows include batch 1 to show the gate boundary and where Lean helps vs regresses. The auto-gate enables MLA at `batch ≥ 8` (below it, the standard kernel runs by default).

| B | ratio | reqs | KV mean | KV range | dec/req | dec iters | tps× | ITL× | p99× |
|--:|------:|-----:|--------:|:--------:|--------:|----------:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 1  | 1.0 | 1  | 65536 | 65K (uniform) | 512 | 512 | 0.83 | 0.60 | 0.60 |
| 8  | 1.0 | 8  | 65536 | 65K (uniform) | 512 | 4096 | 1.06 | 1.33 | 1.42 |
| 8  | 0.1 | 8  | 41112 | 6K–65K | 306 | 2448 | 1.09 | 1.66 | 1.98 |
| 16 | 1.0 | 16 | 65536 | 65K (uniform) | 512 | 8192 | 1.07 | 1.42 | 1.66 |
| 16 | 0.1 | 16 | 38252 | 6K–65K | 332 | 5314 | 1.10 | 1.87 | 2.70 |
| 32 | 1.0 | 32 | 65536 | 65K (uniform) | 512 | 16384 | 1.05 | 1.36 | 1.34 |
| 32 | 0.1 | 32 | 34370 | 6K–65K | 288 | 9226 | **1.13** | **2.41** | **2.47** |

Lean wins at **batch ≥ 8** (the gate threshold): 1.05–1.13× tps, 1.33–2.41× lower ITL, growing with raggedness (peak b32 ragged: 1.13× tps, 2.41× ITL). At **batch 1 it regresses** (0.83× tps, 0.60× ITL), confirming the gate is correct — MLA's splitK is faster at low batch, so the auto-gate keeps it off there.

**Command:**

```bash
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <deepseek-r1-mxfp4> --tp-size 4 \
  --trust-remote-code --attention-backend triton --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --disable-radix-cache --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --context-length 163840 --port 9000
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --model <deepseek-r1-mxfp4> --dataset-name random \
  --random-input-len <ctx> --random-output-len 512 --random-range-ratio <1.0|0.5|0.1> \
  --num-prompts <B> --max-concurrency <B> --seed 42
```

### Default path (auto-gate, no flag)

The tables above are Lean-vs-baseline in the region the auto-gate enables. Confirming the **default** path (no `--enable-lean-attention`) reproduces them under CUDA graphs — 3 arms, Qwen GQA, 64K, ragged `ratio 0.1`, `--seed 42`: `auto` (no flag) tracks `forced` where the capture policy bakes Lean (b≥16) and stays at the standard kernel below the threshold:

| batch | baseline tok/s | auto tok/s | forced tok/s | auto tracks |
|------:|---------------:|-----------:|-------------:|:------------|
| 8  | 79.55 | 79.53 | 88.83 | baseline (Lean off, b<16) |
| 16 | 92.67 | **103.76** | 107.53 | forced (Lean on) |
| 32 | 96.28 | **112.77** | 115.07 | forced (Lean on) |

So the throughput/latency gains are delivered by default, with no configuration change. (At b8 the `forced` arm is already faster than baseline — 88.83 vs 79.55, ITL 1.98× — so the b≥16 GQA capture threshold is deliberately conservative and leaves some b8 headroom on the table; tightening it is future work.)

### MI300X (gfx942, 304 CUs) 

All tests: **1× AMD Instinct MI300X** (304 CUs, gfx942, 192 GB HBM3), ROCm 7.2.0, PyTorch2.9.1+rocm7.2.0, **Triton 3.7.0** (AMD wheel), CUDA graphs on, `--seed 42`, identical harnesses, commands, and auto-gate as above. Parity is arch-independent and passes unchanged (bf16 cos 1.0000, fp8 >0.99, paged >0.999). Results are at the **default 1×CU grid**
(`SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT` default `1.0`, one CTA per CU).

#### Kernel-level (speedup = standard ÷ lean; fp16, `page_size=1`)

**Qwen2.5-7B (28Q/4KV):**

| batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K |
|------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:|
|     1 | 0.53× | 0.66× | **1.38×** | **2.29×** | **3.72×** |
|     8 | 0.53× | **1.03×** | **1.24×** | **1.27×** | **1.25×** |
|    32 | 0.96× | **1.14×** | **1.16×** | **1.34×** | **1.37×** |

**Llama-3.1-8B (32Q/8KV):**

| batch | 8K | 16K | 32K | 64K | 128K |
|------:|---:|----:|----:|----:|-----:|
|     1 | 0.53× | 0.85× | **1.64×** | **2.59×** | **3.34×** |
|     8 | 0.96× | **1.28×** | **1.35×** | **1.38×** | **1.34×** |
|    32 | **1.20×** | **1.23×** | **1.24×** | **1.29×** | — |

Peak **3.72× (Qwen) / 3.34× (Llama)** at batch=1 / 128K; high batch now wins across context. Short-context low-batch stays below 1× and is kept on the standard kernel by the gate.

#### End-to-end serving — GQA (auto-gate enabled region, `batch ≥ 16`)

Same closed-loop methodology and columns as the MI355X table above. **KV mean / KV range / dec-per-req / dec iters are identical to the MI355X rows by construction** (same `--seed 42`, model, `random-input-len`, `random-range-ratio`); only `tps× / ITL× / p99×` are re-measured on MI300X.

| model | B | ratio | reqs | KV mean | KV range | dec/req | dec iters | tps× | ITL× | p99× |
|-------|--:|------:|-----:|--------:|:--------:|--------:|----------:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| Qwen2.5-7B  | 16 | 1.0 | 16 | 16384 | 16K (uniform) | 512 | 8192 | 0.98 | 1.04 | 1.13 |

| Llama-3.1-8B | 32 | 1.0 | 32 | 16383 | 16K (uniform) | 512 | 16384 | 1.05 | 1.13 | 1.09 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 32 | 0.5 | 32 | 12051 | 8K–16K | 391 | 12521 | 1.11 | 1.25 | 1.23 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 32 | 0.1 | 32 | 8795 | 1K–16K | 271 | 8672 | **1.13** | **1.46** | **1.41** |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 16 | 1.0 | 16 | 65535 | 65K (uniform) | 512 | 8192 | 1.08 | 1.17 | 2.81 |
| Llama-3.1-8B | 16 | 0.5 | 16 | 45213 | 32K–65K | 379 | 6060 | 1.12 | 1.38 | 1.36 |

At `1×CU` the enabled region wins across the board on MI300X — including uniform batches (neutral-to-positive throughput, better tail latency). Peak **1.14× throughput** and **2.14× / 1.83× lower median / p99 ITL** (Llama b32×64K ragged). The MI355X auto-gate thresholds transfer unchanged.

#### End-to-end serving — MLA (proxy: DeepSeek-V2-Lite, fp8 KV)

`amd/DeepSeek-R1-MXFP4` **cannot run on MI300X**: fp4/MXFP4 matmul is a CDNA4 (gfx950) feature — gfx942 has no fp4 GEMM (0 `AFP4WFP4` configs; `aiter` marks the OCP fp4 dtypes "gfx950+"). MLA is therefore proxied on MI300X with **DeepSeek-V2-Lite** (16B MoE, MLA, fp8 KV, TP=1), same ragged sweep.
⚠️ V2-Lite has 16 query heads vs R1's 128, so its low-batch CU-saturation differs — this transfers to the R1 MLA gate only *qualitatively*.

| B | ratio | ctx | tps× | ITL× | p99× |
|--:|------:|----:|-----:|-----:|-----:|
| 8  | 1.0 | 65K | 1.04 | 1.12 | 1.12 |
| 8  | 0.5 | 65K | 0.99 | 1.16 | 1.12 |
| 8  | 0.1 | 65K | 0.94 | 1.09 | 0.90 |
| 16 | 1.0 | 65K | 1.07 | 1.29 | 1.28 |
| 16 | 0.5 | 65K | **1.09** | **1.50** | **1.48** |
| 16 | 0.1 | 65K | 1.06 | 1.37 | 1.70 |
| 32 | 1.0 | 65K | 1.08 | 1.36 | 1.36 |
| 32 | 0.5 | 65K | **1.14** | **1.75** | **1.74** |
| 32 | 0.1 | 65K | 1.12 | 1.67 | 1.55 |

b1 loses (0.31–0.42× — Lean's fixed grid is pure overhead at V2-Lite's 16-head batch-1 decode); b8 is borderline (~parity to 1.04×); **b16/b32 win** (up to 1.14× tps, 1.75× ITL). The clean-win region on this proxy is **b ≥ 16** (b8 borderline). Note this differs from R1 on MI355X, where the 128-head decode makes batch 1 a *win* at 1×CU — so the exact `is_mla` batch threshold is a function of head count and should be set from the R1 calibration, not this proxy. (b1 rows omitted from the table.)

## Conclusion

Lean Attention is a flat-latency, work-stealing decode kernel for long-context and ragged serving on ROCm — up to **~5.9× at the kernel level**, **1.52× end-to-end throughput** and up to **3.6× lower median / 2.9× lower p99 ITL** on GQA, and **1.13× tps / 2.41× lower ITL** on MLA at batch ≥ 8 — at zero accuracy cost (bit-identical bf16; fp8/paged parity within quantization noise). It supports MHA/GQA/MLA, bf16/fp16/fp8 KV, and contiguous or paged KV, and runs behind a conservative, CUDA-graph-aware auto-gate that turns it on only where it wins (delivering the gains on the default path) and leaves the standard kernel in place everywhere else — so there is no regression risk.

**Reproduce:** kernel sweep — `SGLANG_FORCE_LEAN_GRID_CU_MULT=1.0 python3 benchmark/lean_kernel_sweep.py`;
CI parity (bf16/fp8/paged) — `pytest test/registered/kernels/test_lean_attention.py`; end-to-end — the  `sglang.launch_server` + `sglang.bench_serving` commands in each subsection above.

title: [AMD] Fuse Kimi-K3 attn-residual aggregation
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
Fuses `_score_kernel`, `_combine_kernel`, the out_norm RMSNorm, the pending residual add (`_aggregate_fused_add`, MLP side) and the bank snapshot copy into one Triton kernel. 7 launches down to 2 per layer.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/kimi_k3/attn_res_hip.py`: 
one Triton kernel, one CTA per token. The bank is loaded as a single register-resident tile so scoring and mixing share one read of it, and the pending residual add, the bank snapshot and the output RMSNorm all fold into the same launch. Holding the tile is the trade — `MAX_REGISTER_TILE` caps the shape, because past that budget it spills and loses to the pipeline it replaces. K3 fits exactly at H=7168, `nvb <= 8`.

`attn_residual.py`: 
`_use_hip_fused()` gates on ROCm plus the kernel's own shape predicate; `_aggregate_hip()` is wired into the three dispatch points. The kernel also accepts `ow=None` (the pre-norm mixture `aggregate_stream()` needs for DSPARK aux capture) and `addend=` (folds the add that `_aggregate_fused_add()` otherwise materializes separately), which the TMA kernel cannot do.

Nothing outside ROCm changes; shapes past the register budget keep the existing pipeline.

## Accuracy Tests

gsm8k 1319: 0.962

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->
5-6% improvement in total throughput, 4-7% improvement in ITL

title: [KDA] Fused-accept state advance for FlashInfer KDA MTP verify
author: yuan-luo
body: ## Motivation KDA MTP verify on the FlashInfer path (`recurrent_kda`, SM100) is two-phase today: the verify kernel writes every draft token's post-state into the speculative `intermediate_ssm` scratch, then `commit_mamba_states_after_verify` scatters the accepted checkpoint back into the persistent pool (`temporal`) across **all** KDA layers, and the next verify re-reads the committed state as its seed. The scatter is a full recurrent-state write per request per round — `num_kda_layers × HV × V × K × 4B` (≈4 MB per layer per request at HV=16, K=V=128 fp32) — plus one kernel launch and its host dispatch, all sitting in the bs=1 MTP inter-phase seam. FlashInfer's `recurrent_kda` already ships the missing half: a `num_accepted_tokens` parameter ("fused speculative decode") that makes the kernel seed itself from `ssm_state_indices[n, nat - 1]` — the checkpoint after the last accepted token of the previous round — instead of slot 0. sglang never passes it. With it, the SSM commit scatter can be skipped entirely: the accepted state is consumed where it already lives. ## Modifications One commit, gated by `SGLANG_OPT_KDA_FUSED_ACCEPT_STATE` (env, default off — zero change to any default path): - **Slot-indexed scratch rows.** In fused mode the verify's `[N, T]` state indices are built from the requests' mamba slots (stable for the request lifetime) instead of batch positions, so last round's checkpoints stay addressable across batch membership changes. Padded CUDA-graph rows carry slot `-1`; every derived index stays negative, which `recurrent_kda` natively treats as inactive — no extra padding plumbing. - **Seeding moves out of the per-verify path.** The per-round committed-pool → scratch slot-0 copy is gone. Fresh requests are staged once at extend time (committed state → `scratch[slot, 0]`, accept length 1); continuing requests seed in-kernel from `slot[nat - 1]`, with `nat` gathered from a persistent per-slot `accept_lens_pool` — all device-side ops, CUDA-graph capture safe. - **Commit shrinks to conv + bookkeeping.** `commit_mamba_states_after_verify` keeps only the conv-window rollback (FlashInfer does not own the conv path) plus a tiny scatter recording this round's accept lengths for the next verify's seed selection. The all-layer SSM state scatter disappears. - **Fail-loud startup gates.** The env requires the FlashInfer KDA decode backend, `--disable-radix-cache` (the committed SSM pool goes stale between verifies; nothing may read it mid-stream), and is mutually exclusive with `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` (both mechanisms own the verify-round SSM state commitment). Bit-exactness by construction: the in-kernel seed value is byte-identical to what the scatter used to commit and the next round re-read (same tensor dtype, pure copy round-trip), so outputs cannot change. Relationship to Kimi-K3: the K3 DSpark verify kernel follows the same read-only-persistent-state contract and still commits via the scatter; extending fused-accept to that path (separate seed-index tensor in the kernel) is planned follow-up and does not affect this PR. ## Accuracy Tests - **Unit tests** `test/registered/attention/unittests/hybrid_linear/test_kda_fused_accept_indices.py` (6 cases). `TestBuildFusedAcceptIndices` pins the padding-negativity invariant of the slot-index arithmetic (a padded slot must yield only negative indices for every step — an arithmetic reorder would silently activate padded rows) and the `accept_lens_pool` gather semantics. `TestFusedAcceptPerForwardCache` guards the per-forward build: what the layers share must equal what each would have built, a different batch must produce different rows, and a fresh `ForwardMetadata` must arrive uncached — a cache outliving its forward would seed the next batch from the *previous* batch's mamba slots, which is a silent wrong-state bug with no shape or index error to catch it. - **GPU parity, SM100** (B200, FlashInfer 0.6.14, real `recurrent_kda`). Two-round legacy-vs-fused (legacy seed-copy + manual commit vs fused staging + `nat` seeding, with deliberately offset slots so slot-indexed rows differ from batch positions): `torch.equal` — not `allclose` — on both rounds' outputs, on the final accepted states, and on the committed pool being untouched by fused. **PASS at B=1/8/32 and T=4/6.** The hoist has its own case: 20 layers sharing one index build vs 20 layers each building their own, bit-identical at B=1 and B=8, so an aliased or stale shared tensor surfaces as a value difference rather than an error. ## Speed Tests and Profiling A/B of the changed path on SM100 (B200, FlashInfer 0.6.14), Kimi-Linear-48B shapes: 20 KDA layers, HV=32, K=V=128, draft window T=4, bf16 state. The 20 per-layer verify calls are captured in a CUDA graph and timed by replay — the mode the real verify path runs in — while the post-verify commit is timed eagerly because it runs after the forward. Min of 5 x 100 iterations. | batch | legacy | fused | saved | |---|---|---|---| | 1 | 393.4 us | 218.5 us | **175.0 us (44.5%)** | | 4 | 720.8 us | 312.3 us | **408.5 us (56.7%)** | | 16 | 1967.8 us | 737.8 us | **1229.9 us (62.5%)** | Breakdown at B=1: the 20 verify kernels are ~212 us; the per-layer committed-pool seed copy fused-accept removes is ~8 us/layer; the per-layer index build the hoist removes is ~9.2 us/layer. The SSM commit scatter this replaces measures 18.3 / 30.9 / 110.8 us at B=1/4/16, against a flat ~5 us accept-length write. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #33247915582](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33247915582) Latest PR Test (Extra): :hourglass_flowing_sand: [Run #33374614240](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33374614240) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 7.2): :x: [Run #33247915571](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33247915571)

title: [3/N] elastic-ep: Recapture decode CUDA graphs after scale-up
author: zackyoray
body:
## Summary

This PR follows [PR #30553](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/30553)
and adds FULL decode CUDA graph recapture after runtime Elastic EP scale-up.
Primary and joiner ranks rebuild their graphs for the expanded topology before
the new EP size is committed.

The existing scale-up API and EPLB lifecycle are unchanged.

## Changes

- Defer initial decode graph capture on joining ranks until they enter the
  expanded world.
- Finish the current sampling step, release the old graph state, and rebuild
  decode graphs with the expanded Mooncake WORLD and NIXL rank mask.
- Require primary and joiner ranks to resolve the same graph mode and capture
  configuration before recapture.
- Reuse SGLang's existing FULL decode graph initializer and synchronize all
  ranks before committing the scale operation.
- Add graph-stable FA3 MLA metadata for the validated DeepSeek path.
- Reject execution modes that do not use the supported decode finalization
  path.

## Configuration

Launch primary and joiner groups with the same resolved graph settings:

```text
--cuda-graph-backend-decode full
--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled
--cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 2 4 8 16
```

The scale request and status API are inherited from the base scale-up PR.

## Known Limitations

- Only FULL decode graph recapture is supported. Prefill and piecewise graph
  recapture are outside this PR.
- Primary and joiner groups must use the same resolved CUDA graph
  configuration and effective capture sizes.
- Recapture is synchronous. Configuring more decode batch sizes increases the
  scale-finalization pause.
- The validated DeepSeek MLA path requires FlashAttention 3.
- Speculative decoding, embedding, diffusion, encoder-only execution, forward
  hooks, and PDMux split-prefill are not supported with Elastic EP recapture.
- The topology, scale-direction, and post-scale recovery limitations of the
  base scale-up PR still apply.
- Recapture releases the old decode graph pool before rebuilding. The deployment
  must still leave enough free GPU memory to capture the configured decode graph
  sizes; the manual tests use `--mem-fraction-static 0.5`.

## Test Plan

The manual Elastic EP tests cover direct, single-rank, mixed-cohort, and
repeated scale-up:

- `TestElasticScaleUp4To5CudaGraph`
- `TestElasticScaleUp4To6CudaGraph`
- `TestElasticScaleUp4To8CudaGraph`
- `TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph`

Each test captures decode batch sizes `1 2 4 8 16` and checks post-scale
generation, routed joiner traffic, input logprobs, and GSM8K correctness.

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3,4,5,6,7 \
python -m pytest -v -s \
  test/manual/ep/test_elastic_scale.py::TestElasticScaleUp4To5To6CudaGraph::test_scale_up_on_demand
```

The repeated 4-to-5-to-6 and direct 4-to-6 validations passed with all five
decode graph sizes captured on every participating rank.

## References

title: [Fix] moe: Fix flashinfer TRT-LLM BF16 expert weight reload on refit
author: Kh4L
body:
## Motivation

BF16 MoE expert weights are converted to the FlashInfer TRT-LLM BlockMajorK
layout on cold load. The inverse restore previously ran only for the routed
backend, although both `flashinfer_trtllm` and `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` use
the transform. A subsequent checkpoint-format copy into a blocked parameter
can therefore fail with:

```
The size of tensor a (64) must match the size of tensor b (2048) at
non-singleton dimension 2
```

A shape-only restore is insufficient: unchanged expert values must also be
returned to checkpoint order before the next pack, or repeated refits can
silently scramble them.

Fixes #27787

## Modifications

1. Gate the inverse on `use_flashinfer_trtllm_moe`, matching the transform for
   both routed and non-routed BF16 backends.
2. Restore both the canonical shape and values in place, preserving parameter
   storage and rejecting non-bijective row permutations or wrong element counts.
3. Implement `restore_weights_before_loading` so `begin_weight_update` restores
   both expert parameters for direct tensor and P2P/RDMA writes that bypass
   model weight loaders. Retain loader-side restoration for disk reloads,
   which do not open a weight-update session.
4. Shape-guard the post-load pack: canonical weights are converted to kernel
   layout, while already-blocked weights remain unchanged. The existing
   `end_weight_update` finalizes once per session, not once per bucket, using
   the existing LoRA-aware model-loader traversal. No new updater/base hook or
   per-bucket `finally` callback is introduced.

Files changed relative to main:
`python/sglang/srt/layers/quantization/unquant.py` and
`test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_flashinfer_trtllm_bf16_moe_reload.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

The CPU-registered unit file contains 10 test methods. It covers exact layout
round trips, bucketed tensor/flattened/distributed updates, mixed
canonical/blocked parameters, unchanged and inactive-backend behavior, invalid
permutations and element counts, LoRA-wrapped traversal, and three successive
loader-free refits through both direct tensor updates and simulated P2P flat
copies. Runtime topology is scoped with `get_parallel().override(tp_rank=0)`.
Loader-free tests assert exact cold-load byte equality and unchanged storage
pointers, while forbidding any call to the model weight loader.

October 5 validation of commit `493fab0f593649c3c22a19302bab1b597a70aada`,
including main `70f0b7351e74b372cc928db533824d3993d65922`: all 10 methods and
5 format subtests pass, plus 22 nearby session/cache-guard methods. Controls
reproduce the three pre-fix TP-rank failures and fail the new loader-free case
in both formats when only the production restore hook is removed. Native XML,
exact source hashes and terminal accounting were independently checked;
all applicable pinned pre-commit hooks pass.
FlashInfer's layout entry points are deterministic, order-changing CPU
stand-ins; this is not on-device kernel accuracy, real RDMA transport, or
end-to-end RL validation.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

No speed benchmark is claimed. Forward kernels are unchanged. Canonical restore
and pack are paid once per weight-update session; disk reloads retain their
existing load/postprocess lifecycle. This fixes representation correctness,
not rollback of partially written weight values.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with the pinned pre-commit configuration.
- [x] Add CPU-registered regression coverage with failure controls.
- [ ] Update external documentation if needed.
- [ ] Provide on-device accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style guidance.

## Review and Merge Process

Required review and green CI remain necessary. Full upstream GPU CI needs a
maintainer to restore the `run-ci` gate; no fresh GPU CI success is claimed.
