title: [AMD] Optimize KIMI-K3 with Triton MLA decode kernel by tuning the stage-1 geometry for gfx950
author: amd-danli103
body: ## Motivation The Triton MLA decode kernel picks its stage-1 geometry -- the number of KV splits and the block size along the KV axis -- from constants tuned on CDNA3. On gfx950 those constants fit badly at the batch sizes that matter for long-context serving. The split count is derived from a fixed workgroup budget, so at small batch a single split covers the whole sequence, while at large batch the budget is treated as a rounding target rather than a ceiling and stage-1 launches more workgroups than the device retires in one wave. What the sweeps below isolate is the timing. The reading behind it -- CU underfill at small batch, one wave too many at large batch -- is the model these values were picked against, not something the A/B separates on its own. ## Modifications All in python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/decode_attention.py. Opt-in via SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE (registered in environ.py, default off). - Stage-1 geometry. One BLOCK_N = 32 for the whole tuned path, where the HIP path otherwise takes 16: at 16 the first dot is a single 16x16 MFMA tile, so the warps only have K=576 to split along and pay a cross-warp reduction every KV step, while 32 gives two of them an N tile each. 64 was timed as well and never came out ahead where the 4-warp bucket applies -- 3-5% behind at batch 1-3, inside noise at 4-5 -- so keeping the tile constant costs nothing. num_warps / num_stages and the workgroup budget come from a batch bucket, since the budget depends on the workgroup size. - The budget is a ceiling, not a rounding target. Overshooting costs a whole wave: batch 24 at 68k context takes 358 us with 21 splits (504 blocks) and 528 us with 22 (528 blocks). Stock round() overshoots at 7 of the 16 captured batch sizes. Below batch 6 the sweep's optimum stops following the budget and the count is capped lower; the reading there is that batch * kv_splits cannot fill 256 CUs and stage-2 merge traffic outweighs the added parallelism, which is analysis rather than something these measurements separate. - The count goes to both stages instead of overwriting the caller's num_kv_splits. Runtime argument in stage-1 -- it only feeds kv_len_per_split, like the stock tl.load(num_kv_splits + cur_batch) -- so the cuda-graph ladder costs no extra compilations; constexpr in stage-2, where it is the loop bound and a dynamic one would stop the unrolling. If the two disagree, stage-2 merges partials stage-1 never wrote, so _mla_launch_plan settles the tuning gate and the count together in the caller that owns both launches, and both launchers default to the stock path. - Determinism. num_warps reorders the fp32 accumulation, so a per-batch geometry would make a request depend on its batch mates. Under --enable-deterministic-inference, or an explicit --triton-attention-split-tile-size, the kernel keeps the scheduler's per-sequence counts and a batch-free geometry. That is batch invariance, not bit-equality with a stock build. Gate, cheapest term first since this runs per layer per decode step -- a CUDA build pays one bool. The env read stays last and uncached so tests can override it: ```python _is_hip and has_mla and head_dim == 576 and is_gfx95_supported() and envs.SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE.get() ``` ## Accuracy Tests | | GSM8K (1319) | |---|---| | tuning off (`SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE=0`) | 0.953 | | tuning on (`SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE=1`) | 0.955 | Repeats of the same configuration land between 0.951 and 0.957, so this says accuracy is unchanged. ## Unit Tests - test_mla_decode_geometry.py (CPU): the split rule at all 16 captured batch sizes, that the budget is never crossed, that it follows the partition size, that stage-1's count is not a constexpr, and that the split-keep decision resolves through the config path a launched server uses (TestKeepSchedulerSplits). 17 passed, 2079 subtests. - test_mla_decode_forced_splits.py (AMD GPU, gfx95 runner): tuned against stock over 12 shapes, that both stages get the same count and stage-1 receives the same gate, and batch invariance with the scheduler's counts kept. Tolerance is two bf16 ULP relative with a 3e-3 floor. 4 passed, 16 subtests. Checked against three mutants -- either stage handed 0, stage-2 one split short -- each of which turns it red. ```bash python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_mla_decode_geometry.py -q python3 -m pytest test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_mla_decode_forced_splits.py -q ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling(baseline data based on 0805 docker image) ### Long context: 68,086 in / 350 out Prefix caching on, 8 shared prefixes, cold prefix per concurrency point. Isolated contribution of this kernel, measured on top of FP8 KV cache + aiter MHA prefill, everything else held fixed, we got 46-73% ITL improvement. ```bash SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE=1 \ # 0 for the baseline arm SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 \ AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path $MODEL \ --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --prefill-attention-backend aiter \ --decode-attention-backend triton \ --page-size 64 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --max-running-requests 32 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 32 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \ --mamba-full-memory-ratio 0.3 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint \ --mamba-track-interval 1024 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \ --enable-cache-report \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT ``` ```bash # aiperf 0.11.0. --warmup-request-count 32, not the default 3, is what gets all 8 # prefixes resident before measurement. aiperf profile \ --model 'moonshotai/Kimi-K3' \ --tokenizer $MODEL --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \ --url "http://localhost:$PORT" \ --endpoint-type chat --streaming --use-server-token-count \ --num-prefix-prompts 8 \ --prompt-prefix-length 63240 \ --synthetic-input-tokens-mean 4760 --synthetic-input-tokens-stddev 0 \ --output-tokens-mean 350 --output-tokens-stddev 0 \ --extra-inputs 'ignore_eos:true' \ --extra-inputs 'min_tokens:350' \ --extra-inputs 'max_tokens:350' \ --warmup-request-count 32 \ --sweep-type zip \ --concurrency 6,12,24,32 \ --request-count 60,72,96,128 \ --random-seed 42 ``` ### Short context: 8192 in / 1024 out MLA attention is 7.5% of the decode step here (2.68 of 35.72 ms at concurrency 32). bf16 KV, `page_size=1`, Triton on both ends, radix off, so this is not the sweep above with a different workload. Both arms ran back to back in one session. With the decode Triton attention kernel optimized, we got 2-12% ITL improvement as well as 2-8% TTT boost. ```bash SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE=1 \ SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 \ AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 AITER_SITUV2_A4W4=0 \ SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_AR_NORM=1 \ python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-path $MODEL \ --served-model-name moonshotai/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --tp-size 8 \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --attention-backend triton \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \ --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT ``` ```bash for C in 2 4 8 16 32; do python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving \ --backend sglang \ --host 127.0.0.1 --port $PORT \ --model $MODEL --tokenizer $MODEL \ --dataset-name random \ --random-input-len 8192 \ --random-output-len 1024 \ --random-range-ratio 1.0 \ --num-prompts $(( C * 8 )) \ --max-concurrency $C \ --warmup-requests $(( C * 2 )) \ --seed 42 done ``` ### Detailed data for MI355X, TP8, on the **0812 image (triton 3.7.0**, torch 2.9.1+rocm7.2) Pasted here. For each workload both arms ran back-to-back in one session and differ only in SGLANG_MLA_DECODE_TUNE. No regression seems to be between Triton 3.6 VS 3.7. ## Checklist - [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). - [ ] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed). - [ ] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance). ## Review and Merge Process 1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process). 2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers. 3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so. - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci` 4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #32007504250](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32007504250) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #32007503937](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/32007503937)

title: [Diffusion][HunyuanVideo] Fuse eager QKV packing and high-quality QKNorm
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Reduce HunyuanVideo eager overhead with three scoped paths:

- a lossless Triton kernel that applies image RoPE while packing image/text Q, K and V into contiguous attention inputs
- a `quality=high` strided QK RMSNorm path that avoids input contiguous copies
- the existing quality-gated fused linear+GELU epilogue for the Hunyuan MLP

The QKV/RoPE pack uses per-signature first-use bit-exact verification. The numerically relaxed RMSNorm and GELU paths are mounted only for `quality=high`. The cleanup keeps mounting all-or-nothing when the public FlashInfer CuTe QK RMSNorm entry point is unavailable, so no partial quality configuration leaks into the model.

## B300 performance

HunyuanVideo, 848x480x65 frames, seed 42, 30 steps, native backend:

| configuration | denoise | e2e | vs latest-main eager |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| latest main eager | 23.7185 s | 26.7040 s | baseline |
| **PR lossless eager** | **22.8496 s** | **25.8321 s** | **+3.66% / +3.26%** |
| **PR `quality=high` eager** | **22.3054 s** | **25.2885 s** | **+5.96% / +5.30%** |
| PR `torch.compile` | 21.6219 s | 23.7775 s | +8.84% / +10.96% |

`quality=high` is 2.38% faster in denoise than the PR's lossless path. It remains 3.16% behind compile in denoise and 6.35% behind end to end; the table intentionally reports that remaining gap rather than implying parity.

The first compile attempt hit the benchmark driver's 180-second warmup limit while compiling the VAE. A retry with the same generated cache and a 900-second limit completed successfully; compilation itself took about 11 minutes, while the displayed measurements exclude warmup.

Measured against main `dbebc1deb42b00befa3d0de67265d7003994c1ad`. The B300 validation tree is identical to this PR's final Git tree.

All videos use the same prompt, seed, resolution, frame count and step count.

title: [Diffusion][GLM-Image] Retune QK head LayerNorm for SM103
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Retune the fused Q/K head LayerNorm launch for B300 / SM103 from 16 rows per program to 32 rows per program, while leaving the independent SM120 and Hopper choices unchanged.

title: [Diffusion][ERNIE] Fuse QKNorm with full-width RoPE
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

Fuse ERNIE-Image Q/K RMSNorm with its full-width rotate-half RoPE cache.

The generic JIT QKNorm+RoPE kernel gains an explicit full-width NeoX cache mode. It remains orthogonal to the Cosmos pack-KV path: full-width caches are rejected for pack-KV, while existing cache layouts retain their behavior.

ERNIE hoists a concatenated full-width cos/sin cache, preserves exact BF16 rounding, and verifies the fused result against the existing split RMSNorm + RoPE path on first use. The cleanup also covers two fallback correctness details:

- the generic API infers the logical half-width RoPE dimension when callers omit `rope_dim` for a full-width cache
- if the first kernel attempt partially mutates Q/K and raises, the reference fallback runs from pristine clones

## B300 performance

ERNIE-Image Turbo, 1024x1024, seed 42, 50 steps, native backend, `quality=lossless`, prompt enhancement disabled for a deterministic text shape:

| configuration | denoise | e2e |
|---|---:|---:|
| latest main eager | 6.5414 s | 6.6666 s |
| **PR eager** | **6.4820 s** | **6.6063 s** |
| PR `torch.compile` | 6.8526 s | 6.9215 s |

The PR's eager path is 0.91% faster than latest-main eager and **5.41% faster than compile in denoise** (4.55% end to end).

Prompt enhancement is intentionally disabled in this comparison because the bundled PE model produced substantially different-length expansions across otherwise identical invocations. Fixing `use_pe=false` makes the actual transformer input, output image and timing comparison deterministic; no timing from the variable-prompt runs is reported.

Measured against main `dbebc1deb42b00befa3d0de67265d7003994c1ad`. The B300 validation tree is identical to this PR's final Git tree.

## Output comparison

The before/after images use the same prompt, seed, resolution, step count and `use_pe=false`. The generated PNGs are pixel-exact and have the same SHA-256 (`3d0eae0ddd90158b8253800cf3db160b2d9514c846e7b97025585126e745531e`).

| latest main eager (before) | PR eager (after) |
|---|---|
| ![ERNIE latest-main output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/b300-pr-visuals/ernie/main-eager-no-pe.png) | ![ERNIE output with PR 34620](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/b300-pr-visuals/ernie/pr-34620-eager-no-pe.png) |

## Validation

- B300 ERNIE + complete generic QKNorm/RoPE + Cosmos pack-KV matrix: `1259 passed`
- includes the ERNIE model-level first-use exact gate, omitted-`rope_dim` full-width API behavior, and partial-mutation exception fallback
- changed-file pre-commit suite passed on the final tree

title: [AMD] Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode (batched bh16bn128).
author: chien-an-chen
body: Enable 12-head MLA aiter fp8 Gluon decode on gfx950 for Kimi-K3 TP8 (12 local heads). If aiter is not updated to the target version, fall back to use the existing zero-pad + mla_decode_fwd. No behavior change on older containers until aiter/Triton are upgraded. below is the dependency: **aiter runtime dependencies** (container/image, not pinned in this repo): - [ROCm/aiter#4480](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4480) (**merged** to `main`, [`fb82bf7`](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/commit/fb82bf7e20adaa9918c9d4bc80e4ff91f000823e)): fp8 Gluon `bh16bn128`, batch>1. - [ROCm/aiter#4555](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4555) (on `main`): decode CUDA graph KV-split budget. - Triton >= 3.7: Gluon `cga_layout` on gfx950. ## Motivation Kimi-K3 at TP8 exposes 12 MLA heads/GPU. The fast aiter persist decode ASM wants head counts divisible by 16 and has no native fp8 12-head path, so fp8 serving had to zero-pad to 16 and go through slower kernels — especially painful at long context under decode CUDA graph. aiter already has a Gluon kernel with a native 12-head masked MFMA tile and an fp8 KV regime (bh16bn128). This PR connects it. ## Modifications - **`aiter_mla_gluon.py`**: thin wrapper + runtime probe (import + Triton `cga_layout` >= 3.7). Logs once at init; returns None → caller falls back. - **`aiter_backend.py`**: h12 head validation (zero-pad mode), decode routing (`_forward_mla_decode`), graph-safe `min_kv_seq_len`, disable slow 16-head persist for h12+fp8, prefill zero-pad Q for h12. - **`forward_mla_rocm.py`**: keep bf16 Q on prefill when fp8 KV (Gluon needs it). - **`test_mla_gluon_h12_fp8.py`**: CPU tests for probe gating and fallback. Scope is **decode only** (`max_q_len==1`, h12, fp8 KV). Prefill unchanged aside from zero-pad Q routing. h=12 KV write is already on main (#34837). ## Accuracy Tests Validated on MI355, Kimi-K3, --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3, --attention-backend aiter, decode CUDA graph enabled (rocm720-mi35x-20260811 image + aiter fb82bf7e2 (aiter PR 4480 merged)): GSM8K: 95.5–95.6% accuracy ## Speed Tests and Profiling ### long-context test(ISL>50K)(radix cache ON) — primary win With this PR, output token/s/gpu has 94%-168% improvement compares to baseline. Baseline: triton attention backend, bf16 kv cache. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260805 This PR stack: fp8 kv cache, Gluon decode, aiter prefill. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260811 ### 8k1k (non-Dspark, disable-radix-cache) With this PR, TTT has 4-10% improvement compares to baseline when c=4/8/16/32. Baseline: triton attention backend, bf16 kv cache. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260805 This PR stack: fp8 kv cache, Gluon decode, aiter prefill. image: rocm720-mi35x-20260811 Compare against 0805 rather than 0811 triton because 0811 image regresses ~10% TTT vs 0805 at high concurrency. | Concurrency | TP | TTT (tok/s) | TTT per GPU (tok/s/gpu) | Output Tput (tok/s) | Median E2EL (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | vs 0805 TTT/gpu | vs 0805 ITL | |------------:|---:|------------:|------------------------:|--------------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|-----------------:|----------------:|----------------:|------------:| | 2 | 8 | 810.2 | 101.3 | 90.0 | 18,738.8 | 537.5 | 18.9 | 18.4 | 0.92× | 0.95× | | 4 | 8 | 1,654.5 | 206.8 | 182.4 | 19,757.5 | 536.5 | 21.1 | 19.6 | 1.04× | 0.95× | | 8 | 8 | 2,652.2 | 331.5 | 291.5 | 23,603.9 | 537.1 | 25.5 | 22.0 | 1.05× | 0.90× | | 16 | 8 | 4,145.6 | 518.2 | 464.8 | 31,279.1 | 541.1 | 32.6 | 25.2 | 1.07× | 0.87× | | 32 | 8 | 5,928.8 | 741.1 | 654.8 | 43,986.3 | 558.4 | 47.2 | 31.5 | **1.10×** | **0.85×** | ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). - title: [AMD] Add concat_and_cast_mha_k_pad_kernel to support 12-head and enable K3 aiter prefill kernel
author: 1am9trash
body:
With this PR, K3 can use the AITER prefill kernel, but must disable FP8 kernel, which does not support 12 heads. Two changes to the server cmd (full cmd in the description above) - `export SGLANG_AITER_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` - `--prefill-attention-backend aiter` ## Motivation The triton `extend_attention_fwd` is much slower than the aiter kernel for MLA prefill. - Triton kernel: `extend_attention_fwd()` in `python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/extend_attention.py` - AITER kernel: `_fmha_fwd_bf16_opus_fwd` in `aiter/ops/mha.py`, calling `gqa_d192_v128_kernel` kernel K3 at TP8 gives 12 heads per GPU, so the existing `concat_and_cast_mha_k_kernel` hits arange's range must be a power of 2. The new kernel handles this by padding the head axis. ## Modifications Add `concat_and_cast_mha_k_pad_kernel` for non-power-of-two head shapes. `concat_and_cast_mha_k_triton` dispatches to it when the head count is not a power of two. title: Apply latest DeepEP branch
author: Fridge003
body:
## Summary

- configure `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` before CUDA DeepEP low-latency buffer initialization
- enforce `max(existing value, 1024, 2 * (num_max_dispatch_tokens_per_rank + 1))`
- preserve larger user-provided values and leave NPU and normal DeepEP paths unchanged
- force reinstall `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7` in CUDA 13 CI and the main CUDA 13 image; CUDA 12 remains unchanged
- bump the runtime dependency to `sgl-deep-ep==0.1.1`

## Motivation

DeepEP v2 requires NCCL Gin from NCCL 2.30.7 and an NVSHMEM QP depth of at least twice the low-latency dispatch capacity plus two. For the DeepSeek V4 configuration with 1024 dispatch tokens per rank, the required QP depth is 2050, which is larger than NVSHMEM default of 1024.

## Validation

- SGLang pre-commit hooks passed for all changed files
- PyPI reports `sgl-deep-ep` 0.1.1 as the latest release with 8 wheel files
- CI dependency script passes shell syntax validation
- mocked CUDA-major checks confirm CUDA 13 installs `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.30.7 --force-reinstall --no-deps` and CUDA 12 skips it
- GB300, four GPUs, with `NVSHMEM_QP_DEPTH` explicitly unset: `TestDSV4FlashFP4B200Balanced` passed all 9 tests in 165.585 seconds

title: [MoE] Add FlashInfer SM90 MXFP4 W4A8 CUTLASS MoE
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Motivation

SGLang currently supports FlashInfer's SM90 MXFP4 W4A16 CUTLASS MoE path, which was introduced in SGLang #24816 on top of FlashInfer [#3084](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3084). FlashInfer [#3738](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738) adds a different Hopper path that dynamically quantizes activations to FP8 and runs MXFP4-weight x FP8-activation MoE GEMMs using Humming-style pre-MMA E8M0 scale fusion.

This PR wires that path into SGLang as an explicit opt-in:

```bash
--moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8
```

The existing `default` and `bf16` behavior is unchanged.

Related work:

- SGLang https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/24816
- FlashInfer https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/3738

### FlashInfer version requirement

This integration intentionally targets the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431, where the FC1 and FC2 residual scales are FP32 tensors in local-expert order with shape `[num_local_experts]`. FlashInfer reuses its internal expert permutation to map those scales to routed rows, including global-to-local expert mapping under EP.

The original #3738 ABI briefly shipped before being reverted from FlashInfer 0.6.17 by #4411. It required downstream runtimes to construct routed-row residual tensors during every forward. SGLang does not support that older ABI.

The new option therefore requires both:

- `flashinfer-python >= 0.6.18`
- `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming`

SGLang currently pins FlashInfer 0.6.17. This PR does not change that global pin. With 0.6.17, selecting `fp8` fails immediately with an actionable error, while all existing FlashInfer paths remain compatible. The dependency, cubin, and JIT-cache pins should be upgraded together in a follow-up change.

GPU validation for this PR used FlashInfer 0.6.18 built from commit `8044d94bf9acc5369857baf88d28906bb32bf264`, which contains the corrected API from FlashInfer #4431.

## Modifications

### Runtime selection and compatibility

- Add `fp8` to `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision`.
- Select the new path only for `flashinfer_mxfp4` on SM90.
- Keep W4A16 as the default SM90 behavior.
- Reject the SM90-specific `fp8` option on SM100 and SM120 to avoid confusing it with their existing MXFP8 activation paths.
- Require the corrected FlashInfer 0.6.18+ API instead of accepting the older routed-row residual ABI.
- Pass `use_wfp4afp8_humming=True` only when the new path is selected. The keyword is omitted completely for FlashInfer 0.6.17 compatibility.

### Weight preprocessing

- Use `preprocess_moe_weights_for_sm90_mixed_gemm_humming` for both FC1 and FC2 during post-load processing.
- Store the folded interleaved weight scales produced by FlashInfer.
- Store `residual * 64` as one FP32 value per local expert for FC1 and FC2.
- Preserve GPT-OSS gate/up layout conversion and its existing padding rules.
- Fill synthetic E8M0 scale padding from an existing scale in the same expert, preventing padding from changing that expert's min/max exponent range.
- Support both the GPT-OSS MXFP4 quantization path and the DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 expert path.

### Kernel invocation

Construct the five Humming quant-scale slots expected by the corrected FlashInfer API:

1. FC1 folded weight block scales
2. FC1 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation
3. Reserved scalar FC2 activation scale
4. FC2 folded weight block scales
5. FC2 per-local-expert residual scale, including the fixed `2^6` compensation

The existing TP/EP topology is forwarded to FlashInfer so it can map global expert IDs to the corresponding local residual scale.

### Tests and benchmark

- Extend the registered SM90 MXFP4 test suite with:
  - GPT-OSS preprocessing checks against the FlashInfer helper
  - five-scale kernel invocation and direct FlashInfer comparison
  - aligned and non-aligned hidden/intermediate dimensions
  - padding invariance for per-expert residual scales
  - EP rank with global expert IDs
  - DeepSeek-V4 preprocessing
  - fail-fast behavior on FlashInfer versions before 0.6.18
- Extend the manual SM90 benchmark to compare:
  - SGLang Marlin W4A16
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A16
  - FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8
- Update the server-argument documentation.

## Accuracy Tests

The registered SM90 MXFP4 suite passed:

```bash
python -m pytest \
  test/registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_mxfp4_sm90_cutlass.py -v
```

```text
18 passed, 1 skipped
```

The DeepSeek-V4 MXFP4 checkpoint was launched with:

```bash
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path /home/models/DeepSeek-V4-Flash \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --tp 4 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_mxfp4 \
  --flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision fp8 \
  --enforce-disable-flashinfer-allreduce-fusion \
  --host 0.0.0.0 \
  --port 30000
```

DeepSeek-V4 accuracy was evaluated using the same 200-example GSM8K setup as SGLang #24816. Both runs used the same TP=4 configuration, dataset, sampling parameters, and server options; only `--flashinfer-mxfp4-moe-precision` changed between `bf16` and `fp8`.

```bash
PYTHONPATH=/sgl-workspace/sglang_dev/python \
python -m sglang.test.run_eval \
  --port 30000 \
  --eval-name gsm8k \
  --num-examples 200 \
  --api chat \
  --max-tokens 1024 \
  --num-threads 32 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --gsm8k-data-path /tmp/gsm8k-test.jsonl
```

| MoE precision | GSM8K score | Total latency | Output throughput |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| W4A16 (`bf16`) | 0.985 | 37.301 s | 611.809 token/s |
| W4A8 (`fp8`) | 0.985 | 32.952 s | 683.574 token/s |

W4A8 preserved the W4A16 GSM8K score while reducing evaluation latency by 11.7% and increasing output throughput by 11.7%. The score also matches the 0.985 W4A16 result reported in SGLang #24816. 

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The downstream benchmark uses the GPT-OSS-like shape from SGLang #24816: hidden size 4096, intermediate size 2048, 256 experts, and top-k 6. Each FlashInfer path was fully autotuned, followed by 5 warmup iterations and 30 timed iterations. The remaining token shapes were run in parallel with one independent shape per H20 GPU; each W4A16/W4A8 pair ran on the same GPU.

The benchmark can be reproduced with FlashInfer 0.6.18+:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python:/path/to/flashinfer \
FLASHINFER_DISABLE_VERSION_CHECK=1 \
python test/manual/layers/moe/bench_mxfp4_sm90_kernels.py
```

Results on NVIDIA H20-3e:

| Tokens | CUTLASS W4A16 median (min) | CUTLASS W4A8 median (min) | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4 | 0.275 ms (0.272 ms) | 0.164 ms (0.162 ms) | 1.68x |
| 16 | 0.842 ms (0.840 ms) | 0.463 ms (0.460 ms) | 1.82x |
| 64 | 1.894 ms (1.892 ms) | 1.037 ms (1.019 ms) | 1.83x |
| 256 | 2.410 ms (2.403 ms) | 1.478 ms (1.383 ms) | 1.63x |
| 1024 | 3.912 ms (3.906 ms) | 2.093 ms (1.999 ms) | 1.87x |
| 2048 | 6.973 ms (6.954 ms) | 3.394 ms (3.384 ms) | 2.05x |
| 4096 | 13.013 ms (12.971 ms) | 6.295 ms (6.210 ms) | 2.07x |
| 8192 | 25.624 ms (25.546 ms) | 12.308 ms (12.293 ms) | 2.08x |

FlashInfer CUTLASS W4A8 was faster at every measured token count, with speedups ranging from 1.63x to 2.08x. The gain reaches approximately 2.0x for token counts of 2048 and above. The GSM8K latency and throughput numbers above provide an end-to-end serving sanity check, but the kernel benchmark is the more controlled performance comparison because generated output lengths are not fixed.

## Scope and Limitations

- The implementation is SM90-only.
- It is opt-in and does not change the default W4A16 path.
- A coordinated FlashInfer 0.6.18 dependency update is required before production enablement.

## Checklist

- [x] Format the code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the repository test conventions.
- [x] Update server-argument documentation.
- [x] Run the registered tests on an SM90 GPU with FlashInfer 0.6.18.
- [x] Add a DeepSeek-V4 end-to-end smoke-test result.
- [ ] Upgrade the FlashInfer Python, cubin, and JIT-cache pins together in a coordinated follow-up change.

title: [AMD] DSv4: fuse the qk-norm-rope pair on the MTP target-verify path
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Summary

On the DeepSeek-V4 unified-KV path, the fused qk-norm-rope kernel is wired to
decode only. MTP **target-verify** falls back to running the same work as two
separate launches per layer — `sglang::fused_q_norm_rope` for q and
`sglang::fused_norm_rope` for kv — which is 122 launches per verify step across
the 61 target layers.

This PR routes target-verify through the same fused kernel, **with the cache
store left off**.

The store half deliberately does not move. Decode is a 1-source consumer: the
ring holds everything, so writing it before attention is required. Target-verify
is **2-source** — attention reads history from the ring and takes the current
chunk as `k`/`v` so the draft tokens stay causally masked against one another.
Writing the current chunk into the ring ahead of attention makes those tokens
indistinguishable from history, and every draft position then attends to all of
them regardless of order. Fusing the store as well drops GSM8K from 0.950 to
0.027 while looking like a ~7% throughput win, because it skips exactly the work
correctness depends on. Only the norm+RoPE half is sound, and that is what this
PR fuses.

## Modifications

- **`python/sglang/srt/models/deepseek_v4.py`** (`MQALayer._forward_prepare`)
  - `do_fused_store` now also admits `is_target_verify()` when the new gate is
    on. The kernel is token-indexed (`q`, `kv` and `positions` are all length M),
    so a verify batch carrying several draft tokens per request is a shape it
    already handles.
  - On that path the kernel is called with `swa_cache`/`swa_loc` left as `None`,
    so it performs q-norm+RoPE and kv-norm+RoPE and stores nothing.
    `get_unified_swa_loc` is not called at all — it exists solely to address a
    store this path no longer performs.
  - `kv` is returned instead of being set to `None`, so the caller's existing
    contract drives the rest unchanged: `attn_k = kv` gives attention the real
    current-chunk source, and `save_kv_cache = kv is not None` makes the backend
    write the ring after attention, exactly as the unfused path did.
  - `kv` is materialised with `.contiguous()` first: it is a strided slice of
    `qkv_a`, and the ring store requires a contiguous buffer. The unfused path
    pays the identical copy inside `_compute_kv_bf16`, so this is parity, not
    added overhead.
- **`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** — new `SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY`
  (default on). Set to 0 to fall back to the unfused chain on the verify path.

Decode, prefill and the non-unified paths are untouched.

### Kernel-level evidence

Per target-verify forward, from graphs-off traces segmented by the 61
`DeepseekV4DecoderLayer` frames (TP8, 8k/1k, conc 16, rank 0). `fused_q_norm_rope`
and `fused_norm_rope` both go to zero and one `_fused_qk_norm_rope_store_kernel`
replaces them; no other kernel is added.

| layer type | launches/fwd (base → patched) | GPU us/fwd excl. collective |
|---|---|---|
| CSA (30 layers) | 1920.0 → 1800.0 | 15779 → 15488 (−1.8%) |
| HCA (31 layers) | 1526.8 → 1410.5 | 12385 → 12014 (−3.0%) |

"excl. collective" is the number to read: `cross_device_reduce` blocks until the
slowest rank arrives, so its duration tracks inter-rank skew rather than work
this change moves.

## Accuracy

Model `deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro`, MI355X (gfx950), TP8. GSM8K, full 1319
questions, 5-shot, greedy.

| run | accuracy | invalid |
|---|---|---|
| baseline (gate 0) | 0.950 | 0.000 |
| patched (gate 1) | 0.949 | 0.000 |
| patched (gate 1, repeat) | 0.945 | 0.000 |

Note this is measured **without** `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN`. The throughput
harness pins acceptance to the golden AL, which fabricates which draft tokens are
accepted — fine for speed, but it would bypass the accept/reject path this change
touches. Acceptance here is whatever the draft model earns.

```bash
export SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton
export SGLANG_ENABLE_UNIFIED_RADIX_TREE=1
export SGLANG_OPT_UNIFIED_CACHE_FREE_OUT_OF_WINDOW_SLOTS=1
export AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0
export SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV4_REASONING_EFFORT=high

# flip this between 0 (baseline) and 1 (patched)
export SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY=1

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --served-model-name deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 31710 --trust-remote-code \
    --tensor-parallel-size 8 \
    --attention-backend dsv4 \
    --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 \
    --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
    --disable-shared-experts-fusion \
    --tool-call-parser deepseekv4 --reasoning-parser deepseek-v4 \
    --chunked-prefill-size 8192 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
    --max-running-requests 32 --cuda-graph-max-bs 32 \
    --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
    --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4

python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py \
    --backend srt --host http://127.0.0.1 --port 31710 \
    --num-questions 1319 --num-shots 5 \
    --max-new-tokens 1024 --temperature 0.0 --parallel 32
```

## Performance

Same model and hardware. 8k input / 1k output, TP8, steady state (10 waves
through a `--max-concurrency` gate). Each cell is the mean of 2 repeats run in
`off, on, on, off` order per concurrency, so a monotonic drift over the block
shifts both arms equally instead of being credited to the patch. Repeated
all-gates-off runs on this node put the noise floor at 0.25% (1σ).

| concurrency | output tok/s (base → patched) | uplift | mean TPOT ms | accept len |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4  | 332.43 → 341.07 | **+2.60%** | 11.37 → 11.06 | 2.499 → 2.498 |
| 8  | 543.73 → 555.57 | **+2.18%** | 13.75 → 13.46 | 2.499 → 2.469 |
| 16 | 839.00 → 857.32 | **+2.18%** | 17.98 → 17.57 | 2.499 → 2.507 |
| 32 | 1167.14 → 1186.66 | **+1.67%** | 25.79 → 25.34 | 2.482 → 2.508 |

Acceptance length is flat across arms, so the uplift is kernel time and not a
shift in speculation behaviour.

```bash
# same server launch as above, with SGLANG_OPT_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE_VERIFY
# flipped 0/1 between arms, plus the throughput harness env:
export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=2.49
export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected
export SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token

# CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32}; --max-running-requests/--cuda-graph-max-bs = 2*CONC
# capped at 32 on both arms (this image cannot capture a decode graph at bs 48).
CONC=16
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang \
    --host 127.0.0.1 --port 31710 --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
    --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
    --random-range-ratio 0.8 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) \
    --max-concurrency $CONC
```

`bench_serving` ignores EOS by default here (it only offers
`--disable-ignore-eos`), so every request runs to exactly 1024 output tokens and
neither arm can win by generating less.

title: [FlashInfer v0.6.18] add FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 W4A16 mode
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Add an opt-in W4A16 compute mode for FlashInfer CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE and dense linear layers: weights remain NVFP4 while activations and outputs stay BF16. Registered tests cover online-quantized Nemotron MoE accuracy, serialized ModelOpt Qwen3 dense+MoE disk-reload invariance, and the existing dense W4A4 numerical path.

Dependency:

- This PR requires the final [FlashInfer v0.6.18](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/v0.6.18) release (`69ff11fc4954396d98326656dc85debd2223f637`), which contains the CuTe DSL NVFP4 MoE W4A16, SiTU, workspace-lifetime, and SM100/SM103 dense W4A16 APIs used here.
- SGLang `main` pins FlashInfer 0.6.18 through merged [#36954](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36954). This integration intentionally has no compatibility fallback for earlier FlashInfer APIs.

## Modifications

- Add `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16` (default `false`).
- Refresh the existing CuTe DSL prefill-dispatch unit fixture after the main merge by declaring its intended `quant_mode="w4a4"`; this follow-up changes no runtime code.
- Select `CuteDslMoEWrapper(quant_mode="w4a16")`, pass raw BF16 activations, and omit GEMM1/GEMM2 activation scales.
- Reuse the existing packed NVFP4 weights and CuTe MMA-layout block scales, but construct weight-only decode alphas for both online-quantized and serialized ModelOpt weights.
- Keep serialized ModelOpt NVFP4 dense layers in the existing `ModelOptFp4LinearMethod`. When the environment variable and `--fp4-gemm-backend flashinfer_cutedsl` are both selected, its registered `fp4_gemm` compiler boundary dispatches to FlashInfer `mm_bf16_fp4`; otherwise the existing W4A4 `mm_fp4` route is unchanged.
- Prepare dense W4A16 weights through `prepare_bf16_fp4_weights`, preserve loader-owned source scales for disk reload, and keep stable prepared scale/alpha bindings for decode CUDA graphs. Reuse the existing NVFP4_AWQ pre-scale operation before BF16 GEMM.
- Recognize prepared W4A16 state in the generic quantized LM-head guard, and keep DeepSeek's W4A4-only GEMM+SwiGLU fusion disabled for W4A16.
- Support the standard CuTe DSL v2 paths with no A2A or FlashInfer A2A on SM100-family GPUs (SM100/SM103). Keep FlashInfer A2A dispatch in BF16 by suppressing automatic NVFP4 dispatch and rejecting an explicit NVFP4-dispatch configuration; the existing DeepEP masked path remains W4A4-only. The registered reload test covers no A2A, while the online accuracy test covers FlashInfer A2A, and the serving benchmark compares no A2A with FlashInfer A2A.
- Preserve the configured finalize mode for ReLU2. For W4A16, honor `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE`; registered tests cover both fused and two-stage finalization.
- Register nightly `4-gpu-b200` end-to-end coverage for `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-FP8` with online NVFP4 expert-weight quantization.
- Add a separate registered TP4/DP4/EP4 case with DP attention and no A2A for serialized `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`: dense and MoE layers use W4A16, and two same-checkpoint disk reloads across weight/CUDA-graph release and resume must preserve deterministic decode text and token IDs exactly, with token logprobs within `1e-4`. This remains alongside the existing per-token NVFP4 CuTe DSL case.

## Accuracy Tests

Post-main-merge regression at `64f0eb711fb78ae2fad82f05329c7efeb8a1dfaa`:

- **Image:** `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260831-bb5e6198` (amd64 image `sha256:3c75c6f7f8e6eaeebdcf92ef47caef818608134252ad5898f4c670b7911768a6`).
- **Hardware:** one C2 bare devbox with 8 NVIDIA B300 GPUs (SM103); the runtime regressions used GPUs 0-3.
- **Runtime:** Python 3.12.3, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA 13.0.
- **FlashInfer:** `flashinfer-python==0.6.18`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.18`, and `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.18+cu130`, force-reinstalled directly from the v0.6.18 release assets with `--no-deps --no-cache-dir`.

The [linked merge-ref CI failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/33354124622/job/99373236375?pr=35120) was test-fixture drift: production CuTe DSL quantization metadata supplies `quant_mode`, while this unit fixture's `SimpleNamespace` did not. Follow-up commit `64f0eb711fb78ae2fad82f05329c7efeb8a1dfaa` declares the fixture's intended W4A4 mode. It adds no runtime fallback and changes no runtime code.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Four-GPU MoE-dispatch comparison at historical head `508aef613`. That head used W4A16 for MoE and W4A4 for dense linear layers, so these results characterize no-A2A versus FlashInfer A2A only; they are not a performance claim for the final combined dense+MoE W4A16 head.

- Model: `nvidia/Qwen3-30B-A3B-NVFP4`
- Common topology: TP4, DP4, DP attention, DP LM head, BF16 model activations, BF16 KV cache
- No-A2A arm: EP1 tensor-parallel MoE
- FlashInfer arm: EP4 with `--moe-a2a-backend flashinfer`
- Workload: 128 simultaneous requests, exactly 8,192 input and 2,048 output tokens each, `request-rate=inf`, concurrency 128, four warmups, cache flush, seed 42
- CUDA graphs: prefill disabled; decode `full` with max batch size 128 in both arms. Each server log contains 208 executed decode batches with `cuda graph: True`.
- This benchmark reused the same persistent compilation cache. Model load, JIT compilation, autotuning, and CUDA-graph capture occur before server readiness and are not included in the serving duration; the client starts timing only after health checks and four warmup requests.

title: Support deepseek v4 and kimi k3 on ssd
author: beyondHJM
body:
# [Feature] Add SSD-backed Expert Pack inference for DeepSeek-V4-Flash and Kimi-K3

## Summary

This PR adds an opt-in SSD-backed inference path for **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** and **Kimi-K3**. It allows these MoE models to run when their complete weights are larger than GPU VRAM and host RAM combined.

Routed expert weights are stored on SSD and loaded only when selected by the router. The implementation uses:

- an expert-major **Expert Pack** layout for efficient random access;
- direct I/O into aligned pinned host buffers;
- asynchronous host-to-device transfers; and
- a byte-budgeted LFU/LRU GPU cache for frequently used experts.

The runtime does not prune, merge, skip, replace, or re-quantize experts, and does not reduce Expert Top-K. The default `auto`, `safetensors`, and `gguf` loading paths remain unchanged; SSD execution is enabled only through the explicit `expert_pack` path.

## Supported Scope

`ExpertPackModelLoader` is selected only with `--load-format expert_pack`. Official checkpoints loaded through the standard `auto` or `safetensors` paths never enter this loader.

The currently validated DeepSeek input is the single-file MXFP4 GGUF used by `frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`. Its routed expert matrices use `MXFP4`; the large non-routed matrices are mostly `Q8_0`, router input weights are `BF16`, and the inventory also contains `F32` and `I32` normalization or auxiliary tensors. The inspected GGUF contains 129 `MXFP4`, 512 `Q8_0`, 43 `BF16`, 641 `F32`, and 3 `I32` tensors. It contains no FP8 tensors.

The other validated input is the text-only 38-shard `KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf`, whose routed experts use Q2_K for gate/up and Q3_K for down. The Kimi launcher extracts the official `text_config` into a flat `KimiLinearConfig`; the complete multimodal Kimi-K3 checkpoint is not supported by this loader. Other GGUF quantization variants have not been validated and are not currently claimed as supported.

## Usage

Install this branch from source before running the examples:

```bash
python3 -m pip install -e "python"
```

### DeepSeek-V4-Flash

The tested MXFP4 GGUF is available as [`frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731:latest`](https://ollama.com/frob/deepseek-v4-flash-0731), which was imported from [`unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/unsloth/DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731-GGUF). The benchmark used the immutable Ollama model blob with SHA-256 `947ac34c08c0e5c5752ac76398f934b3b6b4075cfe915ba43dd5ac754900a4cd`.

```bash
python3 examples/runtime/deepseek_v4/benchmark_deepseek_5090.py \
  --gguf /path/to/deepseek-v4-flash-0731-mxfp4.gguf \
  --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \
  --max-new-tokens 200
```

### Kimi-K3

Download all 38 Q2_K GGUF shards from [`Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED`](https://huggingface.co/Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED). Also place the tokenizer/config files from [`moonshotai/Kimi-K3`](https://huggingface.co/moonshotai/Kimi-K3) in a sibling directory named `kimi-k3-tokenizer`.

```bash
hf download Blackfrost-AI/KIMI-K3-Q2_K-GGUF-ABLITERATED \
  --include "KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-*.gguf" \
  --local-dir /path/to/kimi-k3
```

```bash
python3 examples/runtime/kimi_k3/benchmark_kimi_k3_5090.py \
  --gguf /path/to/kimi-k3/KIMI-K3-MXP4-DERISKED-Q2_K-00001-of-00038.gguf \
  --prompt "Explain why the sky appears blue." \
  --max-new-tokens 200
```

The first shard is only the entrypoint. The launcher automatically discovers and uses all 38 shards in the same directory. Both launchers derive the remaining paths automatically. If the Expert Pack is missing, it is built on the first launch and reused afterward.

| Model | First Expert Pack build | Approximate first-run readiness |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash | Estimated **5-10 minutes** on the benchmark NVMe SSD | **8-15 minutes** |
| Kimi-K3 | **29 minutes 42 seconds measured** | **35-45 minutes** |

The 38 Kimi-K3 source shards and generated Expert Pack occupy approximately 1.814 TiB in total, so a 4 TB SSD is recommended for practical headroom.

## Correctness

- DeepSeek-V4-Flash produced semantically equivalent answers to Ollama across travel planning, science, history, programming, and mathematics prompts.
- Kimi-K3 matched the 200-token SGLang reference output exactly. All 92 routed layers executed Top-16 experts with `fallback_count=0` and `io_errors=0`.

## Performance

The target platform is one RTX 5090 with 32 GB VRAM, 32 GB host RAM, and NVMe SSD storage. The retained measurements were collected on RTX 5090 hosts; host RAM and SSD capacity differed between the two model runs.

### DeepSeek-V4-Flash vs Ollama

Five prompts were measured with 200 generated tokens per prompt.

| Metric | SGLang | Ollama | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 3.265 token/s | 1.457 token/s | **2.24x faster** |
| Decode | 2.020 token/s | 1.354 token/s | **1.49x faster** |

### Kimi-K3 vs llama.cpp

The SGLang run used a 91-token prompt and generated 200 tokens.

| Metric | SGLang | llama.cpp | Result |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Prefill | 0.66412 token/s | 0.11289 token/s | **5.88x faster** |
| Decode | 0.44830 token/s | 0.1810 token/s | **2.48x faster** |

The llama.cpp decode baseline came from an earlier 50-token run, so the 2.48x decode figure is indicative rather than a strict equal-length comparison.

title: [Kernel] Add H200 MoE configs for Qwen3.5 and Qwen3.6
author: vedantjh2
body:
## Summary

Add NVIDIA H200 Triton 3.6 fused-MoE configs for:

- Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8: `E=256,N=512`, block FP8 `[128,128]`, TP1, with separate up/gate and down-projection tables
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8: the cached checkpoint requests the same lookup keys and shares the Qwen3.5 FP8 tables
- Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-BF16: `E=256,N=512`, TP1, with separate up/gate and decode-aware down-projection tables

The unsupported Qwen3.8 MoE entry has been removed. Qwen3.8-27B is a dense hybrid-attention model, so it cannot use these MoE tables. Its H200 packed-GDN and ReplaySSM verification candidates were tuned and validated separately; both were end-to-end neutral and are not included in this change.

## Full-model GSM8K validation

All primary comparisons used one H200, SGLang v0.5.17, the official `benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py`, five shots, temperature 0, a 20-question warmup, ten 200-question repetitions per A/B/A phase, and closed-loop parallelism 64 without a request-rate or TPOT throttle. Changes are against the mean of the A1 and A2 phase medians.

| Model | A1 latency / throughput | Tuned latency / throughput | A2 latency / throughput | Drift-adjusted change | Accuracy A1 / tuned / A2 | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3.5 FP8 | 12.575 s / 3151.08 tok/s | 11.693 s / 3290.12 tok/s | 12.792 s / 3187.02 tok/s | **-7.81% latency, +3.82% throughput** | 0.775 / 0.768 / 0.768 | 0% |
| Qwen3.6 FP8 | 8.793 s / 2965.50 tok/s | 7.999 s / 3128.58 tok/s | 8.403 s / 2879.70 tok/s | **-6.96% latency, +7.05% throughput** | 0.415 / 0.425 / 0.413 | 0% |
| Qwen3.6 BF16 | 14.812 s / 2620.40 tok/s | 14.919 s / 2628.53 tok/s | 14.996 s / 2640.67 tok/s | +0.10% latency, -0.08% throughput | 0.518 / 0.518 / 0.525 | 0% |

Qwen3.6 BF16 was also tested at saturated parallelism 128 using all 1,319 GSM8K questions, with three repetitions per phase:

| Phase | Median latency | Median output throughput | Accuracy | Invalid |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Baseline A1 | 84.680 s | 2906.36 tok/s | 0.600 | 0% |
| Tuned | 85.558 s | 2980.93 tok/s | 0.534 | 0% |
| Baseline A2 | 85.536 s | 2934.67 tok/s | 0.527 | 0% |

The bracket estimate is **+2.07% throughput** and +0.53% latency. A1 had substantial output/accuracy drift; tuned closely matched A2, where it was +1.58% throughput with effectively unchanged latency. This is a saturation-throughput result, not a latency or quality claim.

## Isolated kernel results

### Qwen3.5 FP8 up/gate

| Routed tokens | Baseline | Tuned | Latency reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 256 | 255.43 us | 220.90 us | 13.52% |
| 512 | 265.41 us | 242.75 us | 8.54% |
| 1024 | 284.93 us | 274.94 us | 3.50% |

### Qwen3.5 FP8 down projection

The dedicated down table improves on the previous up-table fallback at every tested serving size.

| Routed tokens | Up-table fallback | Tuned down | Incremental reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 7.75 us | 7.34 us | 5.24% |
| 4 | 11.83 us | 11.26 us | 4.88% |
| 16 | 21.48 us | 20.30 us | 5.48% |
| 32 | 28.33 us | 26.83 us | 5.27% |
| 64 | 35.54 us | 33.43 us | 5.93% |
| 128 | 49.63 us | 46.91 us | 5.47% |
| 256 | 62.99 us | 57.25 us | 9.11% |
| 512 | 85.86 us | 74.59 us | 13.13% |
| 1024 | 107.87 us | 88.59 us | 17.87% |

### Qwen3.6 BF16

| Projection | Routed tokens | Baseline | Tuned | Latency reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Up/gate | 256 | 191.70 us | 181.01 us | 5.58% |
| Up/gate | 512 | 328.60 us | 217.48 us | 33.82% |
| Up/gate | 1024 | 374.91 us | 241.59 us | 35.56% |
| Down | 1 | 8.11 us | 6.96 us | 14.23% |
| Down | 4 | 17.21 us | 15.61 us | 9.25% |
| Down | 16 | 32.50 us | 30.57 us | 5.94% |
| Down | 32 | 42.31 us | 39.10 us | 7.60% |
| Down | 64 | 54.86 us | 51.03 us | 6.98% |
| Down | 128 | 79.94 us | 75.17 us | 5.97% |
| Down | 256 | 105.84 us | 94.32 us | 10.88% |
| Down | 512 | 143.77 us | 115.12 us | 19.92% |
| Down | 1024 | 166.01 us | 131.28 us | 20.92% |

## Qwen3.8-27B dense-kernel evaluation

The public Qwen3.8-27B BF16 checkpoint was tested on the same H200:

- Packed-GDN exact shape `(H,HV,K,V)=(16,48,128,128)`: `BV=16`, 4 stages, 1 warp reduced aggregate B4-B32 kernel time by 5.89% (6.26% gain), with exact output and state matches in 14/14 correctness cases. Full-model A/B/A was neutral: **+0.02% throughput, -0.17% latency**. Rejected.
- ReplaySSM MTP verification exact-shape candidate: 3 stages and `NK=4`, compared against stock ReplaySSM-spec with identical EAGLE 3/1/4 settings. Full-model A/B/A was neutral: **+0.20% throughput, -0.15% latency**. Rejected.
- Operationally, enabling non-speculative ReplaySSM with its required `no_buffer` and overlap-disabled settings raised request capacity from 41 to 69 and measured **+16.06% throughput / -13.72% latency** with unchanged GSM8K accuracy. This is a server-configuration result, not a code change in this PR.

## Reproduce the GSM8K results

Use two source trees built from the same SGLang revision:

- `BASE_SOURCE`: the baseline tree
- `TUNED_SOURCE`: the same tree with this PR's diff applied

Run the commands below three times in order: `BASE_SOURCE` (A1), `TUNED_SOURCE` (B), then `BASE_SOURCE` again (A2). Set `SOURCE` accordingly and use a separate `OUTPUT_DIR` for each phase. Set `MODEL` to one of:

```bash
Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8
Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B-FP8
Qwen/Qwen3.6-35B-A3B
```

Start the server:

```bash
export SOURCE=/path/to/sglang-source
export MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.5-35B-A3B-FP8
export PORT=30000
export DATA=/tmp/gsm8k_test.jsonl
export OUTPUT_DIR=/tmp/gsm8k-qwen
mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"

export PYTHONPATH="$SOURCE/python"
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path "$MODEL" \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --tp-size 1 \
  --trust-remote-code \
  --random-seed 0 \
  >"$OUTPUT_DIR/server.log" 2>&1 &
SERVER_PID=$!

until curl -fsS "http://127.0.0.1:$PORT/health_generate" >/dev/null; do
  sleep 2
done
```

Run the official SGLang GSM8K warmup and ten measured repetitions:

```bash
python "$SOURCE/benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py" \
  --backend srt \
  --host 127.0.0.1 \
  --port "$PORT" \
  --data-path "$DATA" \
  --num-questions 20 \
  --num-shots 5 \
  --parallel 64 \
  --max-new-tokens 512 \
  --temperature 0 \
  --top-p 1 \
  --result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/warmup-result.jsonl" \
  --raw-result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/warmup-raw.jsonl"

for repeat in $(seq -w 1 10); do
  python "$SOURCE/benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py" \
    --backend srt \
    --host 127.0.0.1 \
    --port "$PORT" \
    --data-path "$DATA" \
    --num-questions 200 \
    --num-shots 5 \
    --parallel 64 \
    --max-new-tokens 512 \
    --temperature 0 \
    --top-p 1 \
    --result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/run-$repeat-result.jsonl" \
    --raw-result-file "$OUTPUT_DIR/run-$repeat-raw.jsonl"
done

kill "$SERVER_PID"
wait "$SERVER_PID" || true
```

For the saturated Qwen3.6 BF16 run, change `--parallel 64` to `--parallel 128`, `--num-questions 200` to `--num-questions 1319`, and run three measured repetitions.

For the Qwen3.8-27B operational ReplaySSM comparison, use `MODEL=Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B`. Keep the baseline server command unchanged and add these flags to the optimized server:

```bash
--mamba-radix-cache-strategy no_buffer \
--disable-overlap-schedule \
--enable-linear-replayssm
```

For the isolated ReplaySSM verification-kernel comparison, use the following flags on both baseline and tuned servers:

```bash
--speculative-algorithm EAGLE \
--speculative-num-steps 3 \
--speculative-eagle-topk 1 \
--speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
--enable-linear-replayssm-spec
```

## Environment

- GPU: NVIDIA H200, TP1
- SGLang: v0.5.17 (`29481685462732237d80d86076d6563e1f658102`)
- Torch: `2.11.0+cu130`
- Triton: 3.6.0
- `sgl_kernel`: 0.4.5
- GSM8K: canonical 1,319-example test set

The serving logs confirmed that the tuned H200 files were selected for both up/gate and down projections.

title: [AMD] Improve K3 dspark draft attn kernel perf
author: 1am9trash
body: ## Motivation With DSpark on Kimi-K3, every step runs 5 draft attn layers (qwen-style, non-causal). Draft attn dominates their cost. In a trace study, the 5 draft layers took 2.368 ms, of which the 5 attn kernels alone accounted for 1.244 ms (>50%). The reason is that this falls back to `extend_attention_fwd`. This generic extend kernel is a poor fit for a shared-KV shape. > Note that draft attn is a common path. `--attention-backend` only selects the target-verify kernel. `aiter` is not among the draft worker's supported backends, so on ROCm the draft always falls back to `triton`. Both `--attention-backend triton` and `aiter` therefore reach the kernel this PR changes. ## Modifications Route DSpark draft attn to `verify_shared_kv`, and extend that kernel to cover the two cases it previously rejected. - **Non-causal situation**: The prefix loop never applies a causal mask, so only modify the stage-2 kernel. - **`h_kv > 1`**: Both stages add a KV-head offset (`head // kv_group_num * stride_h`). A `HAS_KV_HEADS` constexpr keeps the single-KV-head (MLA/MQA) path free of that arithmetic, so the existing Kimi-K3 target-verify path compiles exactly as before. Also adds a tuning entry for `head_dim=64` (`BLOCK_N=256`, 4 warps) and `is_dspark_draft()` in `model_config.py` for the gate. ## Accuracy Tests GSM8k, 1319: ``` 100%|███████████| 1319/1319 [02:00<00:00, 10.98it/s] Accuracy: 0.955 Invalid: 0.001 Latency: 120.085 s Output throughput: 1108.066 token/s ``` ## Speed Tests and Profiling Tested with docker image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.17-rocm720-mi35x-20260818`. Since draft attn is a common code path and this change is independent of other work, the numbers are measured directly on `main`, with no other non-merged PRs applied. Perf (isl=8k/16k/32k, cc=4, 32): - On cc=4, ITL improves by 4-12% and TTT by 2-6%. - On cc=32, ITL improves by 1-5% and TTT by 1-2%. The gain grows with input length, from 8k to 32k, in both cases. May be larger with aiter backend, because aiter accelerates target-verify attn, so draft attn takes a larger share of each step. | isl/osl | Concurrency | TP | TTT (tok/s) | Median TPOT (ms) | Median ITL (ms) | acc len | TTT speedup | ITL speedup | | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | | 8k/1k | 4 | 8 | 4994.24 | 5.57 | 4.42 | 4.71 | 1.02x | 1.04x | | | 32 | 8 | 10026.19 | 23.88 | 10.12 | 5.54 | 1.01x | 1.01x | | 16k/1k | 4 | 8 | 7207.37 | 7.53 | 4.65 | 5.60 | 1.04x | 1.07x | | | 32 | 8 | 11215.29 | 39.36 | 11.70 | 5.90 | 1.01x | 1.02x | | 32k/1k | 4 | 8 | 8924.78 | 10.76 | 5.15 | 5.92 | 1.06x | 1.12x | | | 32 | 8 | 11170.47 | 72.99 | 16.30 | 5.98 | 1.02x | 1.05x | Server script: ``` #!/bin/bash export SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 export SGLANG_AITER_K3_OPT=1 export AITER_FLYDSL_FORCE=1 export AITER_SITUV2_A8W4=1 export SGLANG_K3_FLYDSL_AR_NORM=1 sglang serve \ --model-path /models/Kimi-K3 \ --trust-remote-code \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' \ --tp 8 \ --attention-backend triton \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \ --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128 \ --host 127.0.0.1 \ --port 8000 \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --tool-call-parser kimi_k3 \ --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \ --mamba-full-memory-ratio 1.64 \ --mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 \ --enable-int8-mamba-checkpoint \ --mamba-track-interval 1024 \ --chunked-prefill-size 32768 \ --max-prefill-tokens 32768 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --speculative-draft-model-path /models/Kimi-K3-DSpark \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK ``` ## Checklist - title: [ROCm][diffusion] Enable fused qk norm and rope on ROCm
author: gurpreet-dhami
body:
## Motivation

The fused QK-norm + RoPE and fused LayerNorm + modulate kernels were previously gated to CUDA only. This PR enables these fused paths on ROCm, giving FLUX.2 the same eager-mode optimizations on AMD GPUs that already exist on NVIDIA.

Additionally, the single transformer block's packed-QKV unflatten produced strided views that the in-place fused kernel couldn't consume without implicit copies. Instead of forcing `.contiguous()` copies, we plumb `allow_strided_qk=True` so the kernel handles strided views natively.

## Modifications

- **Enable fused QK-norm + RoPE on ROCm**: Gate the fused in-place path on `_is_cuda or _is_rocm` instead of `_is_cuda` alone in `apply_qk_norm` and `apply_qk_norm_rope` (`layernorm.py`).
- **Enable fused LayerNorm + modulate on ROCm**: The `_flux2_norm_modulate` helper (already platform-agnostic via `.is_cuda` tensor check) now runs on ROCm for both double and single transformer blocks (`flux_2.py`).
- **Support strided QKV views**: Add `allow_strided_qk` parameter to `apply_qk_norm_with_optional_rope` and pass `allow_strided_qk=True` in `Flux2ParallelSelfAttention` and `Flux2SingleTransformerBlock`, avoiding unnecessary `.contiguous()` copies.

## Results

Benchmarked on MI350 (ROCm) with FLUX.2 at two resolutions for TP=1, ULLYSSES=8. Times are per-step per-layer GPU kernel time in microseconds. Estimated E2E uplift is extrapolated from per-layer kernel savings; measured E2E is in Accuracy Tests below.

### Kernel microbenchmarks — 1024×1024 (~10% estimated E2E uplift)

| Transformer Component | Q/K Shape | Unfused (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup | Total savings (50 steps, us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Double Stream (Text) | `[1, 64, 48, 128]` | 101.7 | 8.4 | 12.11x | 37,320 |
| Double Stream (Image) | `[1, 512, 48, 128]` | 131.6 | 14.7 | 8.95x | 46,760 |
| Single Stream (Joint) | `[1, 576, 48, 128]` | 153.5 | 15.8 | 9.72x | 330,480 |

### Kernel microbenchmarks — 2048×2048 (~6% estimated E2E uplift)

| Transformer Component | Q/K Shape | Unfused (us) | Fused (us) | Speedup | Total savings (50 steps, us) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Double Stream (Text) | `[1, 64, 48, 128]` | 104.9 | 8.5 | 12.34x | 38,560 |
| Double Stream (Image) | `[1, 2048, 48, 128]` | 257.1 | 40.0 | 6.43x | 86,840 |
| Single Stream (Joint) | `[1, 2112, 48, 128]` | 339.1 | 44.4 | 7.64x | 707,280 |

### Accuracy tests

Verified that the fused ROCm paths (QK-norm + RoPE, LayerNorm + modulate, strided QKV) produce identical accuracy to the unfused baseline on AMD MI350X using SGLang's built-in diffusion consistency test suite (`test_server_1_gpu.py -k flux_2_image_t2i`).

**Setup:** FLUX.2-dev, 1 GPU, 1024×1024, 50 denoising steps, seed=42, prompt: "Doraemon is eating dorayaki"

#### Results

| Build | CLIP Score | SSIM | PSNR | Mean Abs Diff | E2E (ms) | Avg Denoise (ms) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Unfused (baseline) | 0.9837 | 0.7330 | 10.0566 | 33.7260 | 16331.11 | 283.85 |
| Fused (this PR) | 0.9843 | 0.7329 | 10.0570 | 33.7424 | 15179.06 | 248.37 |

- **No accuracy regression.** CLIP score (semantic similarity) is identical or marginally better with fused paths (0.9843 vs 0.9837). All pixel-level metrics (SSIM, PSNR, mean abs diff) are within noise across builds.
- **Performance improvement.** Fused paths reduce average denoise step time from ~284 ms to ~248 ms (**~12.5% faster**), and E2E latency from ~16.3 s to ~15.2 s (**~6% faster**).

> Note: SSIM/PSNR/mean_abs_diff values reflect AMD-vs-H100 ground truth comparison. The relevant comparison is across builds on the same platform, where all metrics are consistent.

title: [NPU] Adapt DFlash2 speculative decoding to Ascend NPUs
author: syd520zy
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->

DFlash2 ([#35371](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/35371)) landed on main as the successor to DFlash. It uses a block-diffusion drafter with local grouped convolutions and a candidate selector.

First-generation DFlash drafts already run on Ascend NPUs ([#23122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23122), [#31739](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/31739)), but DFlash2 checkpoints could not serve on NPU because the target verification path assumed CUDA behavior.

This PR adapts the DFlash2 draft and verification paths for Ascend NPUs while preserving the existing CUDA behavior.

The validated Ascend environment includes `triton-ascend`; this PR assumes Triton is available in the runtime environment.

## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->


- Fix target verification metadata handling on NPU.
  - Non-NPU devices preserve the existing `skip_attn_backend_init=True` behavior because `prepare_for_verify` has already planned the attention metadata.
  - NPU passes `None`, allowing the target forward path to initialize the required attention metadata.
  - This prevents the NPU graph runner from skipping initialization and accessing an uninitialized `raw_num_token`.

- Align DFlash2 selector verification with the existing NPU behavior of EAGLE and first-generation DFlash.
  - On CUDA, selector sampling verification remains unchanged.
  - On NPU, the full-vocabulary selector sampling verification is skipped and target verification uses argmax.
  - The full-vocabulary path scatters a dense `[batch_size, gamma, vocab_size]` draft-probability buffer and performs vocabulary-wide operations whose cost does not shrink with the verification window.
  - This is an NPU-specific performance policy, not a limitation of the selector algorithm itself: the probability-based path can execute in the validated `triton-ascend` environment, but it added about 6 ms of TPOT on the tested 910C setup and is unnecessary for lossless greedy requests.

- Keep draft proposal and target verification consistent on NPU.
  - Selector sampling support is resolved once as a worker-level capability; graph-captured and eager paths consume that semantic state instead of repeatedly checking the device.
  - The capability is disabled on NPU, forcing both selector draft paths to greedy proposal.
  - `_selector_sample` is staged only when selector sampling is enabled, and acceptance dispatches from that staged state rather than rechecking the hardware.
  - This avoids stochastic draft proposals being verified by a greedy target, which would unnecessarily reduce the acceptance length.
  - CUDA and other non-NPU devices continue to use the original request sampling parameters.

- Handle non-greedy requests on NPU explicitly.
  - The request is currently accepted.
  - Both draft proposal and target verification fall back to greedy.
  - A warning is emitted once to state that the requested sampling distribution is not preserved.
  - Lossless behavior on NPU is currently guaranteed only for greedy requests such as `temperature=0` and `top_k=1`.

- Keep DSpark NPU sampling support outside this PR.
  - This PR does not add a torch chain speculative-sampling implementation or a DSpark NPU sampling fallback.
  - The scope is limited to DFlash2 serving and greedy verification on Ascend NPUs.

- Update the Qwen3.8-27B cookbook with the DFlash2 NPU behavior, validated configuration, greedy-only losslessness boundary, and benchmark setup.

### Why the remaining NPU guards are necessary

The runtime changes contain two direct NPU decisions, each representing a separate backend constraint:

1. Selector sampling policy is decided once when the worker is initialized. Ascend currently uses greedy proposal and verification because selector rejection sampling materializes a dense `[batch_size, gamma, vocab_size]` probability buffer and performs full-vocabulary work. All downstream selector paths use the resulting capability state.
2. Target verification metadata is handled differently on Ascend. Non-NPU `prepare_for_verify()` pre-plans graph or attention metadata, while the NPU path must defer planning until DP/EP padding finalizes runtime shapes. Passing `skip_attn_backend_init=True` on NPU would incorrectly mark uninitialized metadata as ready and can make `NPUGraphRunner` access uninitialized state such as `raw_num_token`.

The existing `is_dflash_sampling_verify_available()` helper cannot replace the selector capability decision: it describes a different target-only verification implementation and using it here would change existing behavior on other backends such as HIP.

### Runtime Validation

- Verified DFlash2 on Ascend NPU with greedy decoding (`temperature=0`, `top_k=1`).
- Three repeated requests with the same prompt produced identical output hashes.
- Verified both NPU graph-enabled and eager (`--disable-cuda-graph`) execution paths.
- Non-greedy requests complete successfully and emit the expected one-time warning before falling back to greedy DFlash2 proposal/verification.
- Full deterministic non-greedy validation was not performed because the test image does not include the NPU `batch_invariant_ops` extension required by `--enable-deterministic-inference`.

### Reviewer question: non-greedy requests on Ascend

DFlash2 currently cannot preserve the requested non-greedy sampling distribution on Ascend because selector verification falls back to argmax.

The current implementation keeps the request valid, emits a warning once, and forces both the draft proposal and target verification to greedy so their behavior remains consistent.

Another option is to reject non-greedy requests explicitly instead of allowing this fallback.

Which behavior would be preferred for this PR?

1. Accept the request, warn once, and run both draft proposal and verification greedily.
2. Reject non-greedy requests on Ascend with an explicit error.

## Accuracy Tests

<!-- If this pull request affects model outputs (e.g., changes to the kernel or model forward code), provide accuracy test results. -->

The accuracy setup follows [#23122](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23122) and [#16818](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/16818), except for the hardware and models.

- Hardware: Ascend 910C
- Tensor parallelism: `--tp-size 2`
- Target model: `Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B` with BF16 weights
- Draft model: `z-lab/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2`
- Draft tokens: `--speculative-num-draft-tokens 8`
- Attention backend: `--attention-backend ascend`
- Mamba configuration: `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16 --mamba-scheduler-strategy extra_buffer`
- Dataset: GSM8K, zero-shot
- Sampling: greedy, with `temperature=0.0`, `top_p=1.0`, and `top_k=1`
- Maximum new tokens: `2048`
- Samples: 128 per concurrency level
- RadixCache: disabled for both baseline and DFlash2 to keep the comparison independent of cache warm-up and prefix reuse

### Baseline accuracy

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.828 | 0.820 |

### DFlash2 accuracy

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Accuracy | 0.820 | 0.836 | 0.836 | 0.828 | 0.820 |

### DFlash2 acceptance length

The configured block size is 8. The following values are the windowed mean acceptance lengths reported by scheduler decode logs.

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Mean acceptance length | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 | 5.8 |

The log-reported mean acceptance length was approximately 5.8, with an acceptance rate of approximately 0.68.

End-to-end validation on Ascend 910C confirmed that:

- The target and DFlash2 draft models load successfully.
- The selector draft initializes successfully.
- Both NPU graph captures complete successfully.
- Greedy requests complete successfully.
- Baseline and DFlash2 produced identical aggregate GSM8K accuracy at every tested concurrency level.

Focused unit-test coverage includes:

- Warning once when selector sampling is disabled and a non-greedy request falls back.
- Propagating the worker-level selector sampling capability into the graph sampler.
- Forcing greedy selector draft parameters when sampling is disabled.
- Preserving selector sampling parameters when the capability is enabled.
- Verifying that acceptance uses staged selector state and otherwise takes the greedy fallback.
- Keeping the generic/CUDA Mamba verify-hook ordering test isolated from NPU-specific DSV4 bundle setup.

Local static validation completed:

- `python -m compileall`
- `git diff --check upstream/main`

Focused Python unit tests were executed in the Ascend validation environment and passed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

<!-- If this pull request impacts inference speed, provide benchmarking and profiling results. -->

The throughput benchmark used the same hardware, model configuration, workload, and RadixCache setting as the accuracy test.

### Baseline output throughput

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output tok/s | 33.182 | 60.925 | 109.544 | 176.193 | 247.068 |

### DFlash2 output throughput

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Output tok/s | 101.249 | 162.244 | 259.899 | 329.448 | 431.172 |

### Speedup

| Concurrency | 1 | 2 | 4 | 8 | 16 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash2 / baseline | 3.05x | 2.66x | 2.37x | 1.87x | 1.75x |

The end-to-end speedup decreases from 3.05x at concurrency 1 to 1.75x at concurrency 16 as target-model batching and speculative-decoding overhead become more prominent at higher concurrency.

Local profiling showed:

- Selector top-k costs approximately 0.04 ms per decode step.
- DFlash2 and NEXTN have matching kernel-level draft behavior.
- The target verification step is primarily bounded by the TP2 per-layer all-reduce floor, with approximately 43 collectives per step.
- The original full-vocabulary selector sampling verification added approximately 6 ms of TPOT on the tested setup: about 51 ms with selector sampling verification versus 45 ms with greedy verification.

Further performance work, including acceptance-length tuning and reducing verify-preparation host overhead, is outside the scope of this PR.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

title: [diffusion] Fuse SANA-Video interleaved RoPE
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- add a paired BF16 JIT CUDA kernel for SANA-Video interleaved Q/K RoPE
- preserve the eager fp64 arithmetic and fp64 -> fp32 -> bf16 conversion order for bit-exact output
- guard the fast path with first-sight bit-exact verification and a permanent eager fallback
- register and document the kernel, with CUDA correctness coverage and a representative benchmark

## H200 results

Model: `Efficient-Large-Model/SANA-Video_2B_480p_diffusers`, eager mode, 832x480x17, 12 denoise steps, guidance 6, seed 42.

- paired RoPE microbenchmark: 1.4422 ms eager -> 0.1192 ms JIT (12.1x)
- denoise latency: 0.239-0.245 s/step -> 0.212-0.213 s/step (~11% faster)
- end-to-end median: 3.8675 s -> 3.5492 s (~8.2% faster)
- generated video SHA256 remained exactly `0c1846a9e56c82b285d3b8c7813c81e392c87c04071ac5c517bf09d1f1d6a4ae`
- ptxas: 27 registers, 0 spill stores, 0 spill loads, 0 barriers

## Validation

- `python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_interleaved_rope_fp64.py test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_import_surface.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_sana_video.py` (19 passed)
- `uvx ruff format --check` on changed Python files
- `uvx ruff check` on the new wrapper, kernel test, and benchmark
- `git diff --check`

The full-model runs used a task-scoped model cache; it was removed and verified absent after validation.

title: [diffusion] Fuse LTX-2.5 decoder 3D RoPE
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- cache the compact fp32 temporal/height/width RoPE tables across decoder blocks at the same grid
- add a paired BF16 JIT CUDA kernel that rotates Q and K in one launch while preserving the eager fp32 operation order
- guard the fast path with first-sight bit-exact verification and a permanent eager fallback
- add pointer-alignment and shape guards, CUDA correctness coverage, representative benchmarks, CPU cache/fallback tests, registry entries, and kernel docs

## H200 results

Checked-in paired-RoPE benchmark:

| Shape | Eager | JIT | Speedup |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| stage 0 | 0.9381 ms | 0.0950 ms | 9.87x |
| stage 4 tile | 2.5454 ms | 0.2467 ms | 10.32x |
| stage 5 tile | 9.3790 ms | 0.8643 ms | 10.85x |

Full decoder-component benchmark used the default 960x544x121 geometry, all 24 blocks, tiled decode, and NATTEN `na3d`:

- median latency: 5379.54 ms -> 4463.80 ms (17.0% faster)
- output SHA256 was identical across baseline/candidate runs: `b3a693021e1251d69847903a772e67dca4046425c576c60ce87bfee6689a6a68`
- peak allocated memory was effectively unchanged: 7,422,371,328 -> 7,422,650,880 bytes
- ptxas on sm_90a: 30 registers, 0 spill stores, 0 spill loads, 0 barriers

The LTX-2.5 Hugging Face repo is gated and the benchmark host had no accepted credential, so this draft has not yet run the published checkpoint. The component benchmark instead used deterministically initialized full-size decoder weights; it exercises the production architecture, shapes, tiling, and NATTEN path.

## Validation

- `python -m pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_ltx25_decoder_rope.py test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_import_surface.py python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_ltx2_5_config.py` (55 passed, 5 subtests passed)
