title: [AMD] Fix Qwen3.5 MTP dropping fused shared-expert weights
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

Since #33889, Qwen3.5 MXFP4 with MTP speculative decoding on MI355X lost about 12% throughput. The cause is that the MTP draft model is loaded without its shared-expert weights.

**What fusion does to the weight layout.** When a Qwen3.5 MoE layer fuses its shared expert, it deliberately does not build a separate `shared_expert` module — the shared expert becomes one more routed expert, living in slot `num_experts`. Any loader for such a layer therefore has to route `mlp.shared_expert.*` into that slot. `qwen3_5.py` does exactly that; `qwen3_5_mtp.py` never learned to.

**Why the target model is unaffected.** In this checkpoint the target's routed experts are MXFP4 while its shared expert stays bf16. Fusing them would push a higher-precision tensor through the quantized routed-expert path, so `can_fuse_shared_expert()` refuses. The target therefore always takes the unfused path, keeps its `shared_expert` module, and loads normally — the gap in the MTP loader is invisible from here.

**Why the draft model is affected, and only recently.** The MTP module is excluded from quantization in full: all 1536 `mtp.*` routed-expert tensors and its shared expert alike. The draft is thus uniformly bf16, nothing is mixed-precision, and fusing it is perfectly valid — the gate correctly says yes. It simply never had the chance before. Until #33889, the target's Quark config installed a single process-wide `disable_shared_experts_fusion` override, which switched fusion off for every runner, draft included. #33889 made that decision per-runner, so the draft started fusing for the first time and immediately ran into the loader gap.

**Why nobody noticed.** With fusion on there is no `shared_expert` module to load into, and the expert mapping only covers slots `0 .. num_experts-1`, so each `mlp.shared_expert.{gate,up,down}_proj.weight` matches nothing and ends at `logger.warning_once("Parameter ... not found in params_dict, skip loading")` — three tensors per TP rank, one suppressed log line, no error. The draft then runs with an uninitialized shared expert. Since a speculative draft cannot corrupt verified output, accuracy is unaffected; the damage appears only as a fall in accept rate, from 0.65 to 0.51, and hence in throughput.

This PR teaches the MTP loader to place those weights into the fused slot, so the draft that #33889 legitimately enabled actually receives them.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py`, mirroring `qwen3_5.py`:

- Size the expert mapping as `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so slot `num_experts` has an entry. The fusion count is read from the constructed modules, because `num_fused_shared_experts` is set on `Qwen3_5MoeForConditionalGeneration` and the MTP wraps a `Qwen3_5ForCausalLM`, which does not carry it.
- Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the mapping loops.

Both are keyed on the model's actual fusion state rather than on a platform check. When nothing fuses, `num_fused_shared_experts` is `0`, the mapping size is unchanged and the rewrite never fires, so this is a no-op for every non-fusing configuration.

Not covered: the fused-checkpoint variant (a single `experts.gate_up_proj` tensor). `qwen3_5.py` handles that with a dedicated branch that chunks the tensor into `w1`/`w3`; the MTP loader's `load_fused_expert_weights` indexes per expert id and cannot serve a single shared-expert tensor. Adding that path untested seemed worse than leaving it, since no checkpoint on hand exercises it.

## Accuracy Tests

No accuracy change is expected: only the draft model changes, and a speculative draft cannot alter verified output. The visible effect is the accept rate. Measured over ~100 decode-batch samples per point.

| conc | accept_len before | after | accept_rate before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 2.5278 | 2.9533 | 0.5097 | 0.6509 |
| 8 | 2.5507 | 2.9374 | 0.5168 | 0.6457 |
| 16 | 2.5144 | 2.9508 | 0.5054 | 0.6501 |

Skipped weights during load go from 3 per TP rank to 0.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Summary at conc=4

| Config | Total Throughput | Median E2E (ms) | Median TTFT (ms) | Median TPOT (ms) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| `eda0ddc260d4` (last good) | 5365.74 | 5992.71 | 326.84 | 6.25 |
| `b61a06921e` (#33889) | 4716.15 | 6662.60 | 322.72 | 7.05 |
| `b61a06921e` + PR #35719 | 5429.77 | 5912.64 | 326.93 | 6.11 |

The third row was obtained by switching shared-expert fusion off on `b61a06921e`, which removes the unloaded-shared-expert condition from the draft; this PR removes the same condition by loading the fused weights instead of dropping them.

### Full sweep

MI355X, `amd/Qwen3.5-397B-A17B-MXFP4`, TP=2, EAGLE MTP (3 steps / topk 1 / 4 draft tokens), page-size 16, `fp8_e4m3` KV, `--attention-backend aiter`, ISL=8192 / OSL=1024, `num_prompts = 10 x conc`, server relaunched per concurrency with `--max-running-requests = conc`. Server flags follow `benchmarks/single_node/fixed_seq_len/qwen3.5_fp4_mi355x_mtp.sh`. Before and after were run back to back on the same GPU pair, both at `7f8f030000`.

| conc | Total Throughput before | after | Delta | Median E2E (ms) before | after | Median TTFT (ms) before | after | Median TPOT (ms) before | after |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 4746.11 | 5417.31 | **+14.14%** | 6726.7 | 5969.1 | 333.3 | 336.7 | 7.07 | 6.22 |
| 8 | 6835.64 | 7626.54 | **+11.57%** | 9243.7 | 8370.3 | 336.4 | 335.9 | 9.67 | 8.82 |
| 16 | 9011.82 | 10141.08 | **+12.53%** | 13997.8 | 12840.5 | 346.1 | 361.6 | 14.86 | 13.48 |

The gain is decode-side, as expected from an accept-rate change: TTFT is flat, TPOT improves by 9–12%.

This restores the configuration to its previously published InferenceX level. The last sweep on image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.16-rocm720-mi35x-20260730` recorded 582.84 / 852.30 / 1130.14 output tok/s at conc 4 / 8 / 16; with this patch the same setup measures 602.47 / 857.12 / 1123.38. Bisecting `accept len` over the 759 commits between that image's sglang and `63d783bbe0` lands on #33889, with a clean split (2.84–2.92 before, 2.50–2.57 after, no intermediate values).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [diffusion] Enable LongCat breakable CUDA graphs
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- enable the existing diffusion breakable CUDA graph runner for `meituan-longcat/LongCat-Image`
- keep LongCat's fixed 512-token DiT prompt shape unchanged so the generic BCG buckets do not capture unused expanded signatures
- document the deployment command and refresh the checked-in diffusion performance/profile skills

## Why

LongCat's native eager DiT trace is launch-heavy between attention calls. The existing BCG runner can capture those regions as 31 graph segments, but LongCat was not admitted by the model and pipeline allowlists.

LongCat always sends the full 512-token prompt body to the DiT. A small model-specific pass-through padder therefore preserves one reusable signature for short and long raw prompts instead of applying generic prompt padding.

## Production-shape visual and end-to-end A/B (B300)

Prompt from the checked-in LongCat diffusion benchmark preset: `A red panda reading a book beside a sunlit window.`

Configuration: NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC, native `--backend sglang`, BF16, 1 GPU, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 4.5, seed 42, prompt rewrite disabled, `quality=lossless`, `--performance-mode manual`.

![LongCat main eager versus PR BCG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/35724/main-vs-pr.jpg)

The main and PR PNGs are byte-exact (`sha256=6a44ff30a185993f50d23da660b3cbe42fb8fdf8ac1d0d612d0086f35c723372`).

| Path | Saved-request e2e runs | Mean e2e | Mean denoise stage |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: |
| main, eager | 7.422 / 7.421 / 7.445 s | 7.429 s | 7.109 s |
| this PR, BCG | 7.178 / 7.174 / 7.175 s | 7.175 s | 6.261 s |

That is a **3.42% end-to-end reduction** and an **11.93% denoise-stage reduction** on B300. Request e2e starts immediately before `generate()` and ends after the output file exists and its SHA256 is recorded, so it includes prompt encoding, DiT, VAE decode, materialization, and PNG saving. Model loading, the one-time 16.43 s BCG capture, and one benchmark warmup are excluded. Logs confirm the native backend with no diffusers fallback.

The task-owned B300 LongCat cache was deleted after this model group: 29,316,959,360 bytes removed and zero residual model-cache files verified.

## Validation

- `pre-commit run --files ...` on all changed files
- `python -m pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_diffusion_bcg_padding.py`: 22 passed
- H200, BF16, 1 GPU, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 4.5, prompt rewrite disabled, lossless quality:
  - eager: 177.3 / 177.0 / 177.2 ms per denoise step across three different prompt lengths
  - BCG: 173.1 / 173.3 / 173.1 ms per denoise step (about 2.3% faster)
  - all three BCG outputs were pixel-exact against eager
  - one 31-segment graph was captured and reused for all three prompts
- default BCG text buckets also captured exactly one graph without bucket warnings; the 8-step output remained pixel-exact
- task-owned LongCat cache cleanup: removed 58,644,690,730 bytes and verified zero residual model-weight files

BCG remains opt-in and resolution-specific. The H200 peak was about 33.4 GB with BCG versus 31.7 GB eager.

title: [kernel] Split the custom all-reduce communicator into push/pull planes
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> Generated by Claude.

## Motivation

Every JIT collective in `csrc/distributed` and `csrc/kimi_k3/comm` took one flat `CommunicatorObj` that carried every buffer any of them might want: `2 * world_size` push slots, a pull workspace, per-block semaphores, a rank-local counter, and one of the three multicast addresses. Consequences:

- The other two multicast addresses travelled out of band. `ws_mc_base` was an `int64_t` argument repeated at five call sites, always the same constant; `pull_sem_mc_ptr` went through a per-world-size Python dict populated by `register_comm()`, duplicated in three modules.
- A push-only owner (the fused qk-norm instances in `minimax_m2`) had to allocate a placeholder 1 KB pull buffer plus one semaphore purely to satisfy the constructor.
- Only `custom_all_reduce.cuh` ever read `pull_workspaces` / `pull_bytes` / `pull_mc_workspace`. The K3 pull kernels reduce in place on the caller's own symmetric input and borrow the plane just to barrier on, so half the object was dead weight for most callers.
- `custom_all_reduce.cuh` defined helpers at `namespace sglang` scope and was `#include`d by three K3 files across directories, so renaming anything inside it silently broke downstream kernels.

## What changed

Split the object by lifetime rather than by direction:

| | contents |
|---|---|
| `sgl.distributed.PushPlane` | zero-filled symmetric push slots, rank-local phase counter, multicast base |
| `sgl.distributed.PullPlane` | symmetric pull buffers + per-block semaphores, both multicast bases. Either half may be a 0-element tensor |
| `sgl.distributed.Communicator` | the two planes (either optional) + the pull launch widths; what every kernel takes |

Both *fixed* multicast addresses now live on the planes. That deletes the `ws_mc_base` parameter from five entry points and the `_PULL_SEM_MC_MAP` registry from three modules. The *per-call* multicast address — a slice of the caller's own symmetric buffer, so it changes every call — stays a plain `intptr_t`, which is what it should be.

`PullPlane`'s optional halves replace the placeholder-buffer trick: `minimax_m2` now constructs `Communicator(push=..., pull=None)` and a kernel that needs a missing plane fails with a message instead of reading a dummy buffer.

### Shared vocabulary moved under `include/`

- **`include/sgl_kernel/distributed/ptx.cuh`** collects the inline PTX the collectives share into `sglang::device::ptx`, which `mbarrier.cuh` and the two K3 files reopen. Removed: three identical copies of the multimem flag increment, three copies of the "multicast alias of a semaphore's flag" helper (now `Semaphore::mc_flag`), and the 16B access helpers that were defined at `namespace sglang` scope inside `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. `csrc/kimi_k3/comm/ptx_sys.cuh` is deleted. The five communication kernels now contain zero inline PTX.
- **`Barrier` / `McBarrier`** (unicast fan-out and one-`multimem.red` variants of the same window protocol) and **`LamportTrait`** (the pos-zero marker) live next to the planes, so each protocol has one implementation instead of one per kernel.
- The three `csrc` → `csrc` includes of `custom_all_reduce.cuh` are gone. What they actually used — `reduce_vec`, the marker traits — moved under `include/`.
- `alloc_workspace_tensor` moved to `host::ffi`, so `utils.cuh` no longer depends on `ffi.h`.

`tp_qknorm`'s 8B `ld.volatile` / `st.volatile` pair became `ld_relaxed_8B` / `st_relaxed_8B` at `.sys` scope (PTX defines volatile as relaxed at system scope, and the store is cross-GPU). Load scope measured identical at `.gpu`, so the `.gpu` load variant was dropped and the vocabulary has one scope.

## Verification (8×B200, SM100)

**Correctness — 291 tests, all passing**

| test | |
|---|---|
| `test_custom_all_reduce.py` (8 GPU) | 180 passed |
| `test_ar_fusion.py` (8 GPU) | 58 passed |
| `test_tp_qknorm.py` (8 GPU) | 42 passed |
| `test_collectives.py` (8 GPU) | 5 passed |
| `test_compute.py` | 6 passed |
| `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 4 passed |
| `test_attn_residual.py` | 1 passed |

All 11 affected JIT modules build; `fp8_blockwise_scaled_mm_sm120` verified with a direct SM120 nvcc compile. clangd reports zero diagnostics on every touched file except two pre-existing cutlass include-path gaps in `.clangd`.

**Registers / spills** — `cuobjdump -res-usage`, this branch vs the merge base, kernels paired by hand where the refactor renamed them:

- **No spills anywhere** (`STACK=0`, `LOCAL=0` for every kernel).
- Unchanged or better everywhere except `1shot_push`: bf16 60→63, fp16 61→63, fp32 56→58. That kernel is 2.7–6.2 % *faster* — `LamportTrait`'s 4-byte-atom marker test replaces a per-bf16-half test, cutting its SASS from 512 to 344 instructions.
- `2shot_pull` eager improves (bf16 53→51) and the multicast variants drop one register.

**Performance** — kernel time only, measured by replaying a CUDA graph of 20 chained calls so host dispatch is excluded; three interleaved rounds per arm, per-arm spread under 1 %:

| variant | delta vs merge base |
|---|---|
| `1shot_push` / eager (dispatched ≤ 768 KB) | **−2.7 % … −6.2 %** |
| `2shot_pull` / multicast (dispatched > 768 KB) | −0.03 % … +0.39 % |
| `1shot_pull` eager and multicast | −1.1 % … +0.6 % |
| `2shot_pull` / eager | +0.5 % … +0.9 % |

33 points: median +0.32 %, worst +0.92 %. On the path the tuned SM100/world-8 config actually dispatches: median **−3.30 %**, worst +0.39 %.

One note on how that number was reached. An earlier revision of this branch regressed `2shot_pull` eager by 7–18 %. Bisecting with self-contained reference kernels showed the params layout, the `Barrier` object and the `Impl` abstraction were all innocent — an exact transplant of the old body still regressed. The cause was the address form: folding the shard offset into the eight base pointers as a typed 32-bit vector index keeps the peer table on the uniform datapath (`UIMAD.WIDE` off a constant-bank base), whereas biasing `vid` per access, or using a 64-bit byte offset, makes all eight addresses thread-varying and costs ~12 registers per thread. Also, binding a params array address to a named local that stays live across the kernel breaks the same proof. Both are noted in comments at the point of use, since either one silently costs ~10 %.

title: [AMD] Optimize Kimi-K3 Triton MLA prefill on gfx950
author: clintg6
body:
## Motivation

Kimi-K3 uses two attention representations during prefill at TP8 on MI355X:

- Fresh/zero-prefix MHA: 12 heads with QK/V dimensions 192/128.
- Cached-prefix absorbed MLA: 12 query heads, one KV head, and QK/V
  dimensions 576/512.

Current Triton prefill leaves performance on the table for both shapes:

1. The exact K3 kernels use one pipeline stage and natural-exponential
   online softmax.
2. Absorbed 576/512 prefill processes one full 512-wide value accumulator,
   increasing register pressure.
3. FP8 cached-prefix P·V can underflow small softmax probabilities.
4. Aiter supports native FP8 zero-prefix prefill, but Triton lacks an
   equivalent opt-in path.

## Changes

### K3 prefill tuning

- Use two pipeline stages for exact gfx950 K3 192/128 and N32 576/512
  prefill kernels.
- Fold `log2(e)` into the attention scale and use `exp2` for unmodified K3
  logits.
- Convert stored LSE back to natural-log units.
- Preserve current compact ragged-grid scheduling and the generic
  Triton-3.7 fallback.

### 4×128 absorbed MLA kernel

Add a dedicated split-dimension kernel for cached-prefix K3 MLA:

```text
Q/K latent: 4 × 128
Q/K tail:       64
V/output:   4 × 128
```

The kernel maintains one online-softmax state and four independent FP32
value accumulators before concatenating the normalized 128-wide outputs.

Dispatch is restricted to:

- gfx950;
- 12 query heads and one KV head;
- QK/V dimensions 576/512;
- BF16 current Q/K/V and output;
- BF16 cached prefix with unit scales, or opt-in FP8 cached prefix with
  supported descales;
- causal attention;
- page size 1;
- contiguous last dimensions;
- no custom mask, sliding window, logit cap, XAI temperature, sink, LSE,
  score modifier, auxiliary tensor, or skipped stage.

Unsupported calls immediately use the existing generic kernel.

### FP8 prefill

Add:

```bash
SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=1
```

This is enabled by default. Set `SGLANG_TRITON_FP8_PREFILL_ATTN=0` to disable
native FP8 prefill.

On exact K3 gfx950 shapes:

- Zero-prefix 192/128 Q/K/V are cast from BF16 to FP8 before launch,
  matching Aiter behavior.
- Absorbed 576/512 prefill keeps current-chunk Q/K/V in BF16 while using
  the FP8 cached prefix.
- Softmax probabilities are multiplied by `FP8_MAX` before FP8 P·V and
  the accumulator contribution is divided by the same factor.
- Non-unit cached-prefix K/V descales are supported.

The default-on path achieved 98% GSM8K accuracy in model-level validation.

## Performance

MI355X measurements used a device warmup and HIP-graph replay.

Against unmodified current main:

| K3 prefill case | Current main | This change | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Zero-prefix BF16, 8K | 0.726 ms | 0.415 ms | 1.75× |
| Zero-prefix FP8, 8K, casts included | 0.726 ms | 0.420 ms | 1.73× |
| Absorbed BF16, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 8.658 ms | 4.133 ms | 2.09× |
| Absorbed FP8, 8K prefix + 8K extend | 6.770 ms | 3.687 ms | 1.84× |

FP8 zero-prefix compared with the optimized BF16 path:

| Length | BF16 | FP8, casts included | Result |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 8K | 0.414 ms | 0.421 ms | No difference |
| 16K | 1.500 ms | 1.400 ms | FP8 1.07× faster |
| 32K | 6.255 ms | 5.145 ms | FP8 1.22× faster |

The default-on policy intentionally follows Aiter and enables native FP8 at
every length despite the small 8K crossover loss.

### End-to-end serving

Throughput uplift is computed as the geometric mean of the per-concurrency
ratios at concurrency 2, 4, 8, and 16.

Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 8192/1024:

| Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 874.18 | 879.54 | +0.6% |
| 4 | 1529.69 | 1586.17 | +3.7% |
| 8 | 2554.27 | 2586.82 | +1.3% |
| 16 | 3892.75 | 3940.95 | +1.2% |
| **Geomean** | — | — | **+1.70%** |

Kimi-K3 TP8, ISL/OSL 68K/350:

| Concurrency | Baseline tok/s | This change tok/s | Uplift |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | 6092.96 | 6910.34 | +13.4% |
| 4 | 7060.28 | 8185.23 | +15.9% |
| 8 | 7655.63 | 9017.19 | +17.8% |
| 16 | 7973.53 | 9540.03 | +19.6% |
| **Geomean** | — | — | **+16.67%** |

The long-context gain is predominantly improved prefill/TTFT; median ITL is
effectively unchanged in both comparisons.

## Numerics

- BF16 absorbed split versus current-main generic output:
  relative L2 approximately `9.5e-5`.
- FP8 absorbed split versus the corrected generic FP8 path:
  relative L2 approximately `6.6e-5`.
- Zero-prefix FP8 versus BF16:
  relative L2 approximately 3.4-3.5%.
- Kimi-K3 model-level GSM8K accuracy with FP8 prefill enabled: 98%.

Additional long-context logits and workload validation remain recommended.

## Platform scope

All specialized execution paths require gfx950 and exact K3 shapes.

title: [diffusion] optimization: transfer mapped layers through a courier thread
author: mickqian
body:
A copy whose source is a checkpoint mapping is synchronous however it is requested — the driver stages unpinned memory through its own buffer — and the prefetch hooks run on the compute thread, so every mapped layer stalled the denoise step for its whole transfer. This adds a courier: a worker thread that stages a mapped layer's bytes into one of two pinned slots (a plain memcpy when the page cache holds them) and issues the device copy on its own stream, where it is genuinely asynchronous. Parameters are still rebound on the compute thread at collect time, so module state is never touched concurrently; blocking callers and any courier failure keep the direct synchronous path.

Measured on MiniMax-H3 fl2va, one RTX 4090, 12 GiB allocator cap, 32 GiB host envelope, 864×480 / 124 frames / 20 NFE, interleaved same-window A/B: baseline 538.8 s of denoise (median 25.0 s/step) against 369.1 s (median 18.0) with the courier — 31% faster, and the effect grows with host memory-bandwidth contention, because that contention is exactly what the compute thread stops paying for. Output equivalence was checked at the video level: SSIM against a baseline run equals the baseline's own run-to-run SSIM (0.9941 = 0.9941), and the audio stream is bit-identical.

Stacked with per-layer pinning (#35867) and the VAE staying on its mapping (#35862), the same budget runs the lossless bf16 denoise at a **median of 11.0–12.0 s/step across two interleaved rounds — ahead of ComfyUI's 13.0** measured under the same 32 GiB psutil convention on the same GPU in the same bandwidth window.

Tests cover the ship/collect handshake, release_all draining an in-flight layer, and the fallback when the courier dies mid-flight; the first two fail with the courier disabled.

Merge note: this PR and #35867 touch the same file; whichever lands second rebases (the resolution is mechanical — both sides add independent methods).

title: [diffusion] Flatten Wan VAE RMSNorm row addressing
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- address dense channels-last-3d Wan VAE activations as flat `[pixel, channel]` rows
- remove the per-program `b/t/h/w` div/mod chain and general stride reconstruction
- keep the normalization, dtype boundaries, SiLU path, launch geometry, and output layout unchanged
- add the dense-row guard, unit coverage, a registered benchmark, and kernel documentation

## Why

Nsight Compute on the representative FastWan2.1 shape (`[1, 96, 4, 480, 832]`, BF16 input / FP32 affine) shows 80.58% SM throughput but only 9.14% DRAM throughput and 93.93% achieved occupancy. Source counters attribute 120,771 / 196,793 samples to integer/index instructions. The hottest PCs are the reciprocal-based lowering of the row-to-`b/t/h/w` div/mod chain (`I2F.RP`, `IABS`, and `MUFU.RCP`).

Dense channels-last-3d already stores every pixel as a contiguous channel row, so those coordinates are unnecessary. `stride(C) == 1` is checked explicitly because size-one channel tensors can satisfy the memory-format predicate with channel-first strides.

## Performance

Single NVIDIA H200, cold-L2 registered benchmark:

| Shape | main | PR | Speedup |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| FastWan2.1 BF16 `[1,96,4,480,832]` | 1550.848 us | 972.576 us | 37.29% |
| FastWan2.2 FP32 `[1,256,4,384,576]` | 921.184 us | 553.760 us | 39.89% |

FastWan2.1 end-to-end ABBA, one H200, eager, 832x480x61, 3 steps, no compile, resident DiT:

| Mode | main mean denoise / e2e | PR mean denoise / e2e | e2e change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| lossless | 0.8554 / 2.2129 s | 0.8553 / 2.2151 s | -0.10% (control; kernel is not mounted) |
| quality=high | 0.8513 / 1.9575 s | 0.8533 / 1.8823 s | **+3.84%** |

The quality-high full-stage trace reduces all 415 Wan RMSNorm+SiLU launches from 215.234 ms to 127.128 ms (40.94%). The largest C96 shape falls from 171.438 ms to 101.697 ms over 105 launches. Peak reserved memory stays at 31.402 GiB.

TurboWan2.1 T2V 1.3B provides a second model-level check at 832x480x81, 4 steps, quality=high, and no compile. Its main trace spends 286.083 ms across 545 Wan RMSNorm+SiLU launches (11.84% of GPU time). A clean main/PR/PR/main ABBA measured:

| Model | main mean denoise / e2e | PR mean denoise / e2e | e2e change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| TurboWan2.1 T2V 1.3B | 1.0106 / 2.4235 s | 1.0163 / 2.3325 s | **+3.76%** |

Denoise is 0.57% slower, confirming that the request gain comes from the VAE path rather than timing drift in the DiT. Peak reserved memory remains 30.729 GiB.

The 14B TurboWan checkpoints provide resolution scaling checks with the same 545 launches:

| Model | main mean denoise / e2e | PR mean denoise / e2e | kernel time | e2e change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 14B 480P | 6.6050 / 8.3559 s | 6.6067 / 8.2559 s | 289.647 -> 169.135 ms (-41.61%) | +1.20% |
| 14B 720P | 17.6763 / 21.2482 s | 17.7044 / 21.0438 s | 669.365 -> 389.957 ms (-41.74%) | +0.96% |

Both ABBA brackets are byte-exact across main and PR. These longer DiT-heavy requests dilute the VAE gain, but independently confirm the kernel reduction at both production resolutions.

TurboWan2.2 I2V A14B adds a four-H200 CFG/Ulysses check at 1280x720x81. Main averaged 7.6857 / 12.1847 s and the PR averaged 7.6780 / 12.2241 s. Rank-0 recorded GPU time fell from 12,020.198 to 11,866.292 ms (-1.28%), but synchronized e2e regressed 0.32%, so this checkpoint is validation evidence rather than a claimed request speedup. All five outputs are byte-exact.

## Output comparison

Prompt: `A curious raccoon walks through a sunlit forest.` Seed: `42`.

![main and PR contact sheet](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/contact-sheet.jpg)

[main video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/main.mp4) · [PR video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/pr.mp4) · [side-by-side video](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/pr-media/diffusion-prs/wan-rmsnorm-flat-rows/side-by-side.mp4)

All four FastWan quality-high outputs have the same SHA256: `fcd22372b15c84dca9b7e18848a4642103bbe6f52dc7fbb3314e9d3e81bceb8a`. All four TurboWan ABBA outputs have the same SHA256: `4eaef46a23e5e8c1e5a7a16941ba4c8b9080e2620ec2551848a11e0060270e46`.

## Validation

- `pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_norm.py -k wan_rmsnorm_silu`: 4 passed
- `pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_model_fast_paths.py -k wan_vae_gate`: 1 passed
- pre-commit on all changed files: passed after rebase onto current main
- all FastWan and TurboWan ABBA GPU-process boundaries were empty
- FastWan isolated cache cleanup: 29,228,743,029 bytes / 7 weight files -> 0
- TurboWan isolated cache cleanup: 16,777,680,195 bytes / 5 weight files -> 0
- TurboWan 14B 480P cache cleanup: baseline 42,521,216,678 bytes and ABBA 42,521,168,645 bytes / 7 weight files each -> 0
- TurboWan 14B 720P cache cleanup: baseline 42,519,295,635 bytes and ABBA 42,519,361,308 bytes / 7 weight files each -> 0

title: [diffusion] Fuse LongCat-Image QKNorm and interleaved RoPE

title: [Perf] dsv4: Add native H16 CuTe sparse prefill backend
author: xuqianmamba
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4-Pro has 128 global query heads, so tensor parallelism with TP=8 leaves
16 logical query heads per rank. The existing SM90 FlashMLA sparse-prefill path
operates on an H64-padded query.

This PR adds an explicit, experimental native-H16 CuTe DSL backend:

```bash
--dsv4-prefill-backend cutedsl_h16
```

The backend avoids computing and materializing the 48 padded query heads and
returns a compact `[TQ, 16, 512]` output. The default `auto` behavior is
unchanged.

## Modifications

- Add an SM90 BF16 native-H16 CuTe DSL sparse-prefill kernel using an `m64n16`
  WGMMA decomposition and online softmax.
- Add `cutedsl_h16` to the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-prefill backend selection.
- Validate the supported launch contract:
  - CUDA SM90;
  - BF16 query and sparse workspace;
  - exactly 16 TP-local logical query heads;
  - Q/K/V width 512;
  - combined TOPK aligned to 128 and no greater than 16384.
- Use a configuration-sized aligned C128 TOPK bucket so changing live chunk
  lengths does not introduce a new JIT specialization.
- Cache the padded combined-index representation for reuse across layers.
- Keep decode, speculative, TBO, CP, bounded-tail, non-eager EXTEND, and CUDA
  graph/capture forwards on their existing paths.
- Reject explicit `cutedsl_h16` selection on unsupported HIP/NPU platforms
  instead of silently ignoring it.
- Reuse existing sparse-MLA kernel/backend tests for targeted H16 parity and
  cache coverage, retain dispatch/CLI checks, and document usage.

## Validation after refreshing main (2026-10-29)

Tested executable code: `50f2dbc5ab20561ff45b5c74e268230955fb3a9b`, merging
main `b960aa903aad354fb2e484041e5e33e3eb061e9b`. The subsequent commit
`2e57492ddbf81b94cbee7ef330f02c1e5a1242d1` only bounds the context length in
the documentation launch example. Executable code is unchanged.

The refresh uses the current kernel configuration, typed KV layouts,
compressed gather, and shared dequantization workspace. Native-H16 kernel
math is unchanged from the original PR.

- 17 selected package dispatch/CLI tests passed, with no failures or skips.
- 15 SM90 kernel/numerical tests passed, with no failures or skips.
- Repository-pinned formatting, Ruff selection, codespell, AST, whitespace,
  and test-registration checks passed.
- All 24 serving measurement points passed independent verification:
  864 successful requests with exact input/output lengths and no errors.
- The native-H16 dispatch marker was present on all eight TP ranks.

### End-to-end serving

DeepSeek-V4-Pro on 8x H20-3e, TP=8, context length 49152,
`flashinfer_mxfp4` MoE runner, chunked prefill 4096, max prefill tokens 16384,
max running requests 16, radix cache disabled, prefill CUDA Graph disabled,
decode CUDA Graph enabled, seed 1234, temperature 0. Only the prefill backend
changes between `flashmla_sparse` and `cutedsl_h16`.

Fixed-length token-ID prompts are derived from GSM8K questions using the
same dataset, tokenizer, and seed in both arms. Lengths and deterministic
prompt hashes are checked before model loading. Each case has three
repetitions with two warmup requests per repetition. Compilation, autotuning,
model loading, and request warmup are excluded from the reported times.

Values below are medians of three measurements. Throughput counts input plus
output tokens. The raw three-run ranges and per-request data are preserved.

| Input / output tokens | Concurrency | Requests / repetition | BF16 H64 tok/s | Native H16 tok/s | Throughput gain | Mean TTFT reduction |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4096 / 1 | 8 | 64 | 5286.37 | 5969.72 | 12.93% | 11.45% |
| 16384 / 1 | 8 | 32 | 5028.81 | 5839.60 | 16.12% | 13.87% |
| 32768 / 1 | 4 | 16 | 4875.40 | 5702.65 | 16.97% | 14.49% |
| 4096 / 128 | 16 | 32 | 4224.03 | 4641.04 | 9.87% | 11.64% |

### Accuracy

Legacy `sglang.test.few_shot_gsm8k`: 5 shots, 1314 questions,
512 maximum output tokens, parallelism 32, temperature 0. Answers are
independently regraded from the complete saved state dumps. This legacy
protocol includes its first five in-context examples in the score;
the held-out score below excludes those five.

| Backend | Correct / 1314 | Accuracy | Held-out correct / 1309 | Held-out accuracy | Invalid answers |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| flashmla_sparse | 1253 / 1314 | 95.3577% | 1248 / 1309 | 95.3400% | 0 |
| cutedsl_h16 | 1249 / 1314 | 95.0533% | 1244 / 1309 | 95.0344% | 0 |

The H16 result is 4 fewer correct answers (0.3044 percentage points lower) in this run; this is not a claim of identical full-model accuracy. Paired comparison: 9 questions correct only on the baseline; 5 correct only on H16. Accuracy was evaluated once per backend at temperature zero with identical settings.

### Sparse-prefill operator benchmark

TQ=4096, SKV=49152. Each value is the median of three warmed public-API
CUDA-event p50 measurements, with provider order rotated across repeats.

| TOPK | FlashMLA BF16 H64 (us) | FlashMLA Q8 H64 (us) | CuTe BF16 H16 (us) | vs BF16 | vs Q8 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 690.032 | 534.944 | 236.368 | 2.919x | 2.263x |
| 384 | 1656.816 | 1127.968 | 559.040 | 2.964x | 2.018x |
| 512 | 2140.992 | 1427.264 | 720.272 | 2.972x | 1.982x |
| 640 | 2625.536 | 1726.656 | 882.464 | 2.975x | 1.957x |
| 1152 | 4557.568 | 2915.232 | 1525.600 | 2.987x | 1.911x |

Q8 inputs are prequantized; query casting and KV gather/dequantization/
requantization are excluded. FlashMLA returns H64 plus max/LSE, while
CuTe returns compact H16. These operator timings have different output
contracts and must not be read as end-to-end serving speedups.

Timed shapes pass BF16 parity with maximum absolute error <= 2.44140625e-4
and mean absolute error <= 1.9168e-6.

### Runtime

H20-3e (SM90), CUDA 13.0, driver 580.82.07. The serving environment passes
the complete platform-applicable dependency audit against the merged
`python/pyproject.toml`. Core package versions:

- `torch==2.14.1`
- `triton==3.8.0`
- `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.8.0`
- `sglang-kernel==0.4.10`
- `sgl-flash-mla==1.0.0`
- `sgl-deep-gemm==0.2.3.post2`
- `flashinfer-python==0.7.2`
- `transformers==5.19.0`
- `deepseek-recipe==0.2.0`
- `openai==2.8.0`
- `timm==1.0.25`
- `tml-renderers==0.1.0`

### Integration check

The tested branch can merge cleanly with main
`1ab008f5b090e6595479ba57934e9211ab083565` as checked on 2026-10-29 using
`git merge-tree`. The H20 results above were measured on the explicitly
identified source commits, not on this later main revision.

## Runtime and test simplification (2026-10-30)

Commit `76defc8432d55b68e7520b506f05f21fcca18834` reduces the PR from
2,590 additions / 11 deletions to 1,253 additions / 12 deletions across
11 files. Runtime code shrinks by 183 net lines: remove redundant dispatch
validation and forwarding wrappers, share compilation/execution arguments,
and simplify the cached C128 padding. The 15 device-side computation and
launch functions are AST-identical to the previously validated implementation.

Reuse the existing `test_sparse_mla_q8kv8_prefill_sm90.py` input builder and
FP32 reference, plus the C0/C4/C128 workspace fixtures in
`test_q8kv8_sparse_prefill_backend.py`. Remove the separate 699-line H16
kernel test suite and 195-line benchmark file; retain a 105-line dispatch/cache
test. The reduced tests cover numerical parity, empty/partial rows and invalid
indices, large rebased IDs, H16/H64 storage, output ownership, dynamic TQ/SKV
and stream reuse, eager fallback policy, and C128 cache reuse.

Targeted validation on H20, using the full installed SGLang package:

- 2 dispatch/cache tests, 1 existing CLI test, 6 native-H16 numerical cases,
  and 7 backend/selector cases: **16 passed, no failures or skips**.
- The backend cases include the existing BF16/Q8 workspace regression tests
  and native-H16 parity for C0, C4, and C128.
- Repository-pinned formatting, Ruff selection, codespell, AST, whitespace,
  and registered-test checks passed.

A warmed public-API CUDA-event comparison alternated the previous runtime
(`50f2dbc5ab20561ff45b5c74e268230955fb3a9b`, also unchanged in `9570c09316`)
and this commit for three repetitions on one idle H20. TQ=4096, SKV=49152;
the table gives the median of the three p50 measurements.

| TOPK | Before H16 (us) | Simplified H16 (us) | Change | BF16 H64 (us) | H16 speedup |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 128 | 236.320 | 236.352 | +0.014% | 695.136 | 2.941x |
| 512 | 722.496 | 722.400 | -0.013% | 2160.672 | 2.991x |
| 640 | 886.080 | 885.440 | -0.072% | 2624.544 | 2.964x |

No operator latency regression was observed in these cases. These timings
retain the different H64/H16 output contracts described above. Full-model
serving and GSM8K were not rerun for this refactor; their separately dated
2026-10-29 results remain above.

## Int64 offset fix after review (2026-10-30)

Commit `28471a9ce80d00e9a98d7b4602ad8525eb9b0a47` addresses the
[P1 review](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36059#discussion_r4422602762).
Widen the query position and masked KV row to Int64 before multiplying by
global-memory strides; this covers Q, KV, indices, and output offsets.
The runtime change is two edited lines plus one comment.

Add two parameterized cases to the existing SM90 test, reusing its input
builder and FP32 reference. H64/TQ=65537 crosses the query offset boundary;
H16/TQ=262145/TOPK=8192 also crosses the index and output offset boundaries.
Both cases gather KV rows 4194303 and 4194304, crossing the KV boundary.
Only the two boundary queries have nonempty attention; the remaining outputs
must be zero. Both cases reproduce illegal memory access on `76defc8432d5`
in separate processes and pass with this fix.

H20 validation: **18 passed, no failures or skips** (8 numerical/boundary,
7 backend/selector, 2 dispatch/cache, 1 CLI). Formatting, Ruff, isort,
codespell, whitespace, source hashes, and test-registration checks passed.

Three alternating before/after repetitions on an idle H20, TQ=4096 and
SKV=49152, using warmed public-API CUDA-event timings. Values are medians of
the three p50 measurements; the baseline is `76defc8432d5`.

2026-08-23 09:24:25 UTC (2026-08-23 17:24:25 UTC+08:00).
The following is the original description captured before this update; its
results describe the older source and environment, separately from the

<details>
<summary>Original PR description and historical validation</summary>

## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 has 128 global query heads, so tensor parallelism with TP=8 leaves
16 logical query heads per rank. The existing SM90 FlashMLA sparse-prefill path
operates on an H64-padded query.

This PR adds an explicit, experimental native-H16 CuTe DSL backend:

```bash

```

The backend avoids computing and materializing the 48 padded query heads and
returns a compact `[TQ, 16, 512]` output. The default `auto` behavior is
unchanged.

- Add an SM90 BF16 native-H16 CuTe DSL sparse-prefill kernel using an `m64n16`
  WGMMA decomposition and online softmax.
- Add `cutedsl_h16` to the DeepSeek-V4 sparse-prefill backend selection.
- Validate the supported launch contract:
  - CUDA SM90;
  - BF16 query and sparse workspace;
  - exactly 16 TP-local logical query heads;
  - Q/K/V width 512;
  - combined TOPK aligned to 128 and no greater than 8192.
- Use a configuration-sized aligned C128 TOPK bucket so changing live chunk
  lengths does not introduce a new JIT specialization.
- Cache the padded combined-index representation for reuse across layers.
- Keep decode, speculative, TBO, non-eager EXTEND, and CUDA graph/capture
  forwards on their existing paths.
- Reject explicit `cutedsl_h16` selection on unsupported HIP/NPU platforms
  instead of silently ignoring it.
- Add SM90 kernel tests, independent oracle/parity coverage, dispatch and CLI
  tests, a three-provider CUDA benchmark, and user documentation.

`5d0e688a3ca49bb521be4e20e835d415bb4f72af` on 8x NVIDIA H20-3e (SM90), with

The GPU suite covers dynamic query and KV lengths, TOPK 128 through 8192,

### Full-model accuracy

Both variants used DeepSeek-V4-Pro with TP=8, context length 49,152, random

The candidate server emitted 8

title: [AMD][DSV4] perf: retune decode split-K heuristic for MI355X
author: karverma-amd
body:
## Motivation

`_kv_splits_heuristic` picks how many KV splits DSv4 decode attention launches.
It over-split by exactly one power of two across the whole decode range: at
`H=128`/`block_h=64` it chose 8/4/2 splits for `T=32/64/128` where 4/2/1 measure
faster.

Split-K only pays while the base grid underfills the device. Each extra split
adds a partial-buffer write plus reduce-kernel work, and once per-split K gets
short that overhead is no longer amortized.

## Modification

Two constants in one file: `target_wg_per_cu` 2.0 -> 1.5 and the
`_MAX_KV_SPLITS` cap 64 -> 16. No kernel changes, no new code paths.

Swept `T` in {1..256} x `kv_len` in {128, 512, 1024} at `H=128` on MI355X,
scoring each candidate by distance from the per-shape optimum:

| constants | geomean regret | worst case |
| --------- | -------------- | ---------- |
| (2.0, 64) — current | 33.5% | 119% |
| (1.5, 16) — this PR | **3.7%** | 36% |

The per-shape optimum does depend on per-token K, which is not knowable at
CUDAGraph capture time, so the residual 3.7% is the price of capture-time
safety rather than a tuning gap.

### Kernel level

Decode attention at the production shape (`T=32`, `top-k 1024`, `H=128`):
**55.7 us -> 44.1 us, a 20.8% improvement**. Selection is unchanged, so results
are identical modulo bf16 reassociation of the split reduction.

## Performance

DeepSeek-V4-Pro, MI355X (gfx950), `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x-20260822`,
8192 in / 1024 out, TP8 + DP8 attention + EP8/MoRI + EAGLE MTP. Both arms are the
same image and the same flags; the only difference is the two constants.

| conc | tput base (tok/s) | tput PR (tok/s) | tput | TPOT base (ms) | TPOT PR (ms) | TPOT |
| ---- | ----------------- | --------------- | ------ | -------------- | ------------ | ------ |
| 4    | 860.07            | 873.28          | +1.5%  | 39.79          | 39.11        | -1.7%  |
| 8    | 1508.46           | 1545.51         | +2.5%  | 42.92          | 42.17        | -1.8%  |
| 16   | 2590.30           | 2610.88         | +0.8%  | 50.02          | 49.62        | -0.8%  |
| 32   | 4001.04           | 4073.41         | +1.8%  | 65.30          | 64.24        | -1.6%  |
| 64   | 5539.24           | 5776.29         | +4.3%  | 96.41          | 92.41        | -4.2%  |

Throughput rises and TPOT falls at every concurrency, and the two move together
at each point, which is harder to explain as drift than either alone. The gain
grows with concurrency because more tokens per rank makes decode attention a
larger share of the step.

One run per cell. Note the effect is specific to DP attention: with plain TP8,
the 128 heads sharded to 16 per rank, the same build measures flat (all deltas
under 1%, signs alternating). DP attention keeps all 128 heads resident per rank,
which is the shape the constants were tuned on.

<details>
<summary>Commands</summary>

```
# Server, per arm; $CONC in {4, 8, 16, 32, 64}
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton \
SGLANG_OPT_FUSE_COMPRESS_NORM_ROPE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_NATIVE_BPRESHUFFLE_SCALE=1 \
SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM=1 \
AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 \
SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=1 SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=1 \
SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=1 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=1 \
GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 MORI_SHMEM_MODE=ISOLATION MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=8G \
MORI_EP_LAUNCH_CONFIG_MODE=AUTO \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention \
  --ep-size 8 --moe-a2a-backend mori --deepep-mode normal \
  --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --page-size 256 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 3 \
  --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 4 \
  --context-length 16384 --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.78 \
  --max-running-requests $CONC --cuda-graph-max-bs $CONC

# Perf client, per concurrency
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai \
  --host 127.0.0.1 --port $PORT --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4-Pro \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((CONC * 10)) --max-concurrency $CONC

# Accuracy
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 1319 --parallel 1319
```

Note: under DP attention `--max-running-requests` is divided by `dp_size`, so a
value below the DP degree floors to 0 per rank and trips
`assert max_running_request > 0`. At `$CONC` 4 it was raised to 8; the client's
`--max-concurrency` is what bounds the load either way.

</details>

## Accuracy

GSM8K, 1319 questions, parallel 1319: **0.958** and **0.946** across two runs,
**invalid 0.000** both times.

## Unit test

`_kv_splits_heuristic` had no test. This PR adds
`test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_kv_splits_heuristic.py` (38 cases),
pinning the contract rather than the constants:

- result is always a positive power of two within the cap — the reduce kernel
  indexes partial buffers by pow2 stride, so a bad value corrupts results rather
  than merely running slowly
- splits never rise as token count rises
- no splitting once the base grid saturates the device
- CUDAGraph safety: depends only on capture-time scalars, never reads a tensor

One clearly-marked table pins the six tuned operating points, so retuning for a
future architecture touches that test and nothing else.

```
pytest test/registered/unit/layers/test_dsv4_kv_splits_heuristic.py
```

## Checklist

- [x] Kernel-level and end-to-end benchmarked on MI355X (tables above)
- [x] Accuracy verified, 1319 questions, zero invalid
- [x] Unit test added for a previously untested function
- [x] No new code paths, no monkeypatching; two constants in one file
- [x] CUDA path unaffected — this file is the ROCm-only dsv4 unified_kv backend

title: [diffusion] perf: fuse tanh-GELU into the LongCat-Image DiT FFN up-proj
author: ITerydh
body:
## Motivation
  
The LongCat-Image DiT runs tanh-GELU as a separate op after its FFN up-projection GEMM, in both the dual-stream FFN (`ff` / `ff_context`) and the single-stream block's `proj_mlp`. sglang already ships the AOT cublasLt `linear_gelu_tanh` epilogue that folds bias-add and tanh-GELU into the GEMM (used today by FLUX.1, Qwen-Image, GLM-Image, LTX-2, HunyuanVideo), but LongCat never marked its sites, so the fusion could not engage. These sites execute 4000 times per generation on LongCat-Image-Edit (50 steps x 80 sites), which makes the standalone activation a measurable slice of denoise time.
   
This PR wires LongCat-Image into that existing mechanism.

## Modifications

Single file, `python/sglang/multimodal_gen/runtime/models/dits/longcat_image.py`:
- `_LongCatFFN.__init__`: `mark_fused_gelu_site(self.net[0], "proj")`, covering `ff` and `ff_context` in every dual-stream block. The marked module is the `ModuleDict` that holds `proj` in `_modules`, so `getattr` resolves it for the fusion helper.
- `_LongCatFFN.forward`: take `fused_linear_gelu_tanh` when `fused_gelu_active()` and `can_use_linear_gelu()` both hold; otherwise fall back to the original `proj` + `nn.GELU(approximate="tanh")` chain, unchanged.
- `_SingleTransformerBlock.__init__` / `.forward`: the same treatment for `proj_mlp` / `act_mlp`.
No kernel, gate, or mount code is touched. `mount_fused_linear_gelu` `unmount_fused_linear_gelu` in the denoising stage already discover marked sites at batch boundaries, all-or-nothing per transformer, and `quality` already participates in the dynamic-batch signature.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
Same case (LongCat-Image-Edit, A800, 50 steps, seed 42). The GELU region was measured with temporary instrumentation bracketing "up-proj GEMM + tanh-GELU", removed before submitting:

| Config | GELU region (50-step total) | Per call | vs baseline |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `lossless` (un-fused) | 9638 ms | 2.410 ms | - |
| `high` (fused) | 9044 ms | 2.261 ms | -594 ms / -6.2% |

- 4000 calls per generation (50 steps x 80 sites); two repeats, variance < 0.2%.                                                                                                                                            
- The GELU region itself is 6.2% faster, saving 0.148 ms per call.

End-to-end denoise, 5 runs per config:

| Config | Denoise (mean) | vs baseline |                                                                                                                                                                                   
| --- | --- | --- |
| `lossless` | 45.496 s | - |
| `high` | 44.812 s | -0.68 s / -1.50% |
                       
## Checklist
- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). No new kernel is introduced; the site mechanism is already covered by `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_sites.py`.
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). The mechanism and the `--quality` switch are documented in `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/fused_kernels.mdx`; happy to add a LongCat-Image row to its per-model coverage table if reviewers prefer.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [ROCm][Perf] aiter: page-level KV view for gfx950 fp8 page-64 asm prefill
author: omirosh
body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change for gfx950 fp8 hd256 chunked prefill: at `--page-size 64` it hands aiter's paged-varlen ASM kernel ([ROCm/aiter#4971](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4971)) a page-level view of the KV pool, replacing the gather that main (#36758) runs on every layer to copy the prefix KV into a contiguous buffer, and is worth **+1.1% to +1.9% output tok/s at 60k/600 and +0.9% to +1.6% at 128k/1k**, with TTFT 2% to 7% better, for `amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4` on 8x MI355X, TP8, fp8 KV, measured on two nodes against the released `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x` image at its default `--page-size 1`.

The gather exists because without a page-level table aiter reads a page-64 call as `page_size=1` and this shape falls to CK. It works, but it pays for a copy and a scratch buffer sized by the total KV in the forward, not by the chunk. Reading the pool in place removes both. Per prefill call that is 1.04x to 1.22x faster than the gather (2.8x to 3.7x over CK), and the gap grows with context length and with the number of requests prefilling together. The gather's scratch peaks at 451 MB in the largest case measured, eight prefills over a 111k-token prefix; this path allocates none. At 8k/1k the end-to-end result is flat, -0.1% to +0.9% throughput.

The change is contained. It only engages on gfx95 at `--page-size 64` with fp8 KV, head dim 256, a power-of-two GQA ratio and the plain NHD pool (not the sliding-window or vectorized 5D pool). Everywhere else prefill runs exactly as on main, and `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM=0` restores main's behaviour even there. Page 64 is the only page size aiter's kernel is compiled for, so at `--page-size 16`, where #37465 puts the MTP ASM verify kernel, this path is a no-op. The two cannot both be active on one server until one of them supports the other's page size.

main's `docker/rocm.Dockerfile` pins aiter `acf8fdf` (2026-09-12), which already contains aiter#4971, so no aiter bump is needed.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py`**

- `_build_paged_kv_view()` converts the token-level KV table into `(page_indptr, page_ids, last_page_len)`. The allocator packs each page contiguously, so a slot's page id is `slot // page_size`; the arithmetic runs off `seq_lens_cpu`, so only the gather touches the GPU.
- `ForwardMetadata.paged_kv_view` carries it. It is built once per batch in `init_forward_metadata`, and only where the whole batch can use it: gfx95, page 64, and the plain NHD pool. Off gfx95 there is no kernel for this shape, so the view is never built rather than built and discarded.
- `forward_extend` computes `paged_asm_available` once per layer (view present and power-of-two GQA ratio via `_paged_prefill_asm_supports_gqa()`). The #36758 gather branch requires it to be `False`; the paged branch requires it to be `True`, and then swaps in the 4D K/V views, the page-level indptr/table and `kv_last_page_lens`. One flag read at both sites keeps the two branches mutually exclusive. The guard mirrors aiter's own: there is no CK arm for 4D LINEAR page-64 fp8 hd256, so a call aiter rejects raises `no matching kernel found` instead of falling back.
- `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM` (default on) gates whether the view is built at all.

**`python/sglang/srt/environ.py`** - `SGLANG_AITER_PAGED_PREFILL_ASM = EnvBool(True)`.

**`docs/docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`** - documents the flag, including that it is inert at any page size other than 64.

**`test/manual/test_aiter_paged_kv_view.py`** - CPU-only. `TestAiterPagedKVView` checks the conversion against a shuffled allocation with a ragged last page, since an identity table would pass even if the arithmetic were wrong; `TestPagedPrefillAsmSupportsGqa` covers the GQA guard, including indivisible and zero/negative head counts.

The flag is a plain on/off rather than a context-length heuristic. The paged path wins at 60k and above and is flat at 8k, but the crossover sits inside this host's noise, so a threshold picked from this data would not be defensible. Default on because the long-context win is the larger effect.

## Accuracy Tests

`amd/Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4`, TP8 on MI355X (gfx950), gsm8k 200 questions, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --disable-radix-cache --chunked-prefill-size 512` (reduced from 16384 so gsm8k prompts actually get chunked), `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.18-rocm720-mi35x`. All at `--page-size 64`:

| stock | main (#36758 + #36852) | this PR |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0.985 | 0.990 | **0.995** |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Against the released image, two nodes

Stock `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.19-rocm10-mi35x` at its default `--page-size 1` (#36758 gather) versus the same image with this PR at `--page-size 64`. `--kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --disable-radix-cache`, TP8, everything else identical. Ratios are this PR over stock, ranges span both nodes:

| ISL/OSL | conc | output tok/s | mean TTFT | mean E2E |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 8k/1k | 4 | 0.999 | 1.007 - 1.009 | 1.001 |
| 8k/1k | 8 - 256 | 1.002 - 1.009 | 0.887 - 0.970 | 0.991 - 0.998 |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 1.011 - 1.012 | 0.952 | 0.988 - 0.989 |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 1.014 - 1.015 | 0.933 - 0.935 | 0.985 - 0.986 |
| 60k/600 | 64 | **1.019** | 0.973 - 0.976 | 0.982 |
| 128k/1k | 4 | 1.009 - 1.012 | 0.966 - 0.969 | 0.989 - 0.991 |
| 128k/1k | 16 | 1.014 - 1.016 | 0.955 - 0.966 | 0.984 - 0.986 |

The two nodes agree on throughput to within 0.003 in every cell. Absolute throughput differs between them but the ratio does not, which is what running it twice was for. Per-cell numbers are in [the sweep comment](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/36505#issuecomment-5662364516).

### Against main at the same page size

One node, one day, identical server args at `--page-size 64`; only the aiter build and the patch differ.

- Server: `--attention-backend aiter --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 --tp-size 8 --max-running-requests 256 --mem-fraction-static 0.9 --disable-radix-cache`
- Bench: `bench_serving --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 0.8`

Output throughput, tok/s:

| ISL/OSL | conc | stock | main | this PR | vs main |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1k/1k | 4 | 228.4 | 228.6 | 228.1 | 99.8% |
| 1k/1k | 16 | 668.7 | 672.6 | 671.6 | 99.9% |
| 1k/1k | 64 | 1509.9 | 1515.3 | 1504.7 | 99.3% |
| 8k/1k | 4 | 226.1 | 226.0 | 222.5 | 98.5% |
| 8k/1k | 16 | 576.1 | 576.3 | 567.0 | 98.4% |
| 8k/1k | 64 | 1086.4 | 1093.4 | 1092.4 | 99.9% |
| 60k/600 | 4 | 103.0 | 107.6 | 108.8 | 101.1% |
| 60k/600 | 16 | 145.3 | 157.1 (*) | 158.9 (*) | 101.1% |
| 60k/600 | 64 | 161.8 | 178.1 | 180.8 | 101.5% |
| 128k/1k | 4 | not run | 92.3 | 93.5 | 101.3% |
| 128k/1k | 16 | not run | 123.0 | 125.6 | 102.1% |
| 128k/1k | 64 | not run | 131.2 | 134.0 | 102.1% |
| **geomean, 1k-60k** | | | | | **99.9%** (102.6% vs stock) |
| **geomean, 60k** | | | | | **101.3%** (108.9% vs stock) |
| **geomean, 128k** | | | | | **101.8%** |

At 1k and 8k the two paths are the same code below the branch and land within 1.6%, inside this host's noise floor; the 8k cells here are the ones the two-node sweep resolves as flat. The 128k rows come from a separate sweep on the same node and day, which is why stock was not repeated there. TTFT at 128k: 8.4 s -> 8.1 s at conc 4, 22.6 s -> 21.8 s at conc 16, 239.8 s -> 234.9 s at conc 64.

The 60k trace confirms the swap: prefill attention is `aiter::fmha_fwd_hd256_fp8_causal_paged_varlen_gfx950` (299 calls, 465 ms) where an unpatched run runs `ck_tile::...FmhaBatchPrefillWithPagedKVCacheKernel`.

Moving off `--page-size 1` costs nothing on its own: holding the code fixed and changing only `--page-size`, page 64 over page 1 is 99.9% for stock and 100.1% for main across the nine 1k-60k cells, and 99.1% to 99.6% at 128k.

<details>
<summary>(*) the 60k/16 cell, measurement noise, and two caveats</summary>

This host shows reproducible whole-server stalls: the scheduler stops logging and no requests complete for 13-18 s, roughly every 2-4 minutes, with occasional 30-55 s events. They cost 5-9% of wall time in every run and appear in every arm including unpatched stock, so they are not attributable to any patch. Aligned to each run's first scheduler log line, five runs taken hours apart share one schedule to within 2-3 s, so they are workload-driven and in-process rather than host noise. Per-cell deltas below a few percent are therefore not resolvable from a single run.

60k/16 is where they hit hardest, so it was run three times per arm. main: 155.4, 156.7, 157.1, none carrying a stall. This PR: 158.9 with no stall, 139.3 on a run that lost 47 s to one, and 135.5 on a run that lost 10 s and is not fully explained by it. The table shows each arm's stall-free run. Taking instead each arm's worst run would move the nine-cell geomean to 98.5% and the 60k geomean to 96.9%, so this cell alone spans the whole result.

Two caveats. At 128k conc 64 the KV pool saturates and the scheduler runs only 26-28 requests with 37 queued at 0.94-1.00 token usage, so that cell is capacity-bound rather than prefill-bound; conc 4 and conc 16 are the cleaner read. And the page-1 gather arm ran later on a different node, carrying 8k/16 and 60k/16 as anchors; those came back at 98.6% and 99.1% of the same cells on the original node, so cross-node page-1 comparisons in this table are directional only. The two-node sweep above is the clean version of that comparison.

</details>

### Op-level: why not just gather

Both paths reach the same ASM family, so the choice is measurable on one prefill call. aiter with #4971, page 64, hd256, GQA 8:1, causal, medians of three runs. Wall clock per call, so the gather's copy and index arithmetic are inside the timed region. The budget is held at 16384 new tokens, what `--chunked-prefill-size` caps, and split across the batch:

| prefilling reqs | chunk each | KV prefix | CK | gather + contiguous asm | page view + paged asm | ratio | gather scratch |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 16384 | 0 | 1544 us | 570 us | **549 us** | 1.04x | +8 MB |
| 1 | 16384 | 43,616 | 9213 us | 2892 us | **2595 us** | 1.11x | +30 MB |
| 1 | 16384 | 111,616 | 21310 us | 6577 us | **5685 us** | 1.16x | +64 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 0 | 432 us | 230 us | **203 us** | 1.14x | +8 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 43,616 | 8185 us | 2673 us | **2355 us** | 1.14x | +95 MB |
| 4 | 4096 | 111,616 | 20354 us | 6527 us | **5523 us** | 1.18x | +230 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 0 | 251 us | 176 us | **150 us** | 1.18x | +8 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 43,616 | 8019 us | 2720 us | **2334 us** | 1.17x | +181 MB |
| 8 | 2048 | 111,616 | 22373 us | 6859 us | **5602 us** | 1.22x | +451 MB |

The scratch is the gathered K/V buffer, `2 * total_k * H_kv * D`, allocated and freed per layer, so the column is the transient peak. This path allocates none of it; both paths need the same 128 MB for q and the output.

<details>
<summary>Where the time goes, and two controls</summary>

Timed separately, the index arithmetic costs 74-152 us and the copy 102-514 us, so together they cover about a fifth of the 892 us gap at one request and about half of the 1257 us gap at eight. The rest is the kernel: the contiguous ASM kernel on a gathered buffer is slower on this shape than the paged ASM kernel reading the pool in place, so even with a free gather this path stays ahead. Those splits are upper bounds, since measuring them adds device syncs.

A device-side kernel-time measurement would show none of this - the copy runs as separate `index_select` kernels before the attention call and the index arithmetic is host-side - so wall clock per call is the framing that charges each path for what it does.

Controls: the gather is page-size-insensitive at long context, page 64 landing within 0.3% of page 1 at both 43k and 111k prefix, as it should since `kv_indices` is token-level at either page size; at no prefix page 64 is 8-12% faster, where the scattered page-1 allocation costs the copy its locality. The batch-1 cells reproduce within 4% on a second node.

</details>

- [ ] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).

title: [diffusion][kernel] avoid 4D scale-shift autotuning
author: BBuf
body:
## Summary

- replace request-time Triton autotuning in the 4D causal-video scale/shift path with a capped power-of-two tile heuristic
- add 4D BF16/FP16 correctness coverage and a registered production-shape kernel benchmark
- document the cold-start constraint in the diffusion kernel README and benchmark/profile skill

## Why

LingBot-World invokes this bandwidth-bound kernel once per transformer block. In a full-stage H100 trace, 199 Python calls expanded to 3,820 Triton autotune launches, making tuning dominate the first denoise step. The selected 64/128/256/512 tiles were bit-identical across the tested production shapes; the capped power-of-two choice was fastest or within measurement noise.

## H100 validation

Native SGLang only, CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=2, LingBotWorldCausalDMDPipeline, 832x480x9, 4 steps, lossless, seed 42. ABBA used independent Triton caches so both paths paid their real cold-start cost.

| metric | baseline mean | candidate mean | improvement |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| denoise | 3909.57 ms | 3083.09 ms | 21.14% |
| request E2E | 12416.27 ms | 11467.29 ms | 7.64% |

All four ABBA MP4 files have the same SHA256: fe5c7d6860d5c11432834ef4419c102ab1081f6f4b92897626481151b4483290.

A fresh isolated Triton cache reduced the production [1, 4680, 5120] first call from 1338.47 ms to 714.77 ms. Steady-state H100 speedups from the registered benchmark were 2.36x (Wan), 2.29x (SANA Video), 1.33x (LongLive), and 2.24x (LingBot-World).

LingBot causal DMD does not support breakable CUDA graphs, so this PR makes no BCG performance claim.

The model ABBA ran at c8b56b1f4; the branch was then rebased onto f8cc1f952, whose intervening change is documentation-only, and the focused tests and benchmark were rerun.

## Tests

- pytest -q test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_modulate.py — 993 passed
- pytest -q python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/realtime/test_lingbot_causal_denoising.py — 28 passed
- post-rebase 4D selection — 16 passed
- pre-commit on all changed files — passed

## LingBot-World V2 sibling validation

The independent robbyant/lingbot-world-v2-14b-causal-fast-diffusers checkpoint uses the same native causal pipeline and production shape. A fresh-cache A-B-B-A gives 3882.74 vs 3015.31 ms mean denoise (22.34% faster) and 12953.80 vs 12168.34 ms request E2E (6.06% faster). All four MP4 files are byte-identical with SHA256 ace7fb75f5f3a7837b8e704cddfceef8ff573bc0e126483ad17c3ae6cccca4fb.

The latest-main high-quality lane stays within the repository video gate versus lossless: first/middle/last SSIM 0.98398/0.97955/0.97701 and PSNR 43.86/42.83/42.35 dB. BCG remains statically unsupported for this pipeline.

title: MiniMax-M3: share the sparse index top-k across layers and reuse the decode top-k buffer
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: share the sparse index top-k across layers and reuse the decode top-k buffer

MiniMax-M3's sparse attention runs a lightning-indexer pass in every sparse layer
to choose the top-k KV blocks that the main attention then reads. On the
value-disabled sparse layers that indexer has no output of its own — `idx_o` is
`None` there, only the block selection is consumed — so its result can be
computed once and shared by a run of consecutive layers. This PR adds
`SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ=N` (default 2), which groups every N such
layers: the group's first layer computes and stores the reduced top-k, and the
remaining layers reuse it, skipping both the flash-index attention and the
group-reduce. In decode the selection is written straight into a persistent
per-batch-size `int32` buffer (`topk_out=`) rather than a freshly allocated
tensor per layer, which removes an allocation from every sparse decode layer and
keeps the destination address fixed so CUDA-graph capture never allocates. The
buffer is only useful because of the sharing, so the two changes ship together.

Sharing the selection **changes which KV blocks the skip layers attend to** — see
`## Correctness` below. It is therefore gated: `index_topk_freq` is pinned to `1`
on every non-ROCm platform and whenever two-batch overlap is enabled, and at
freq 1 no buffer is allocated and every new argument is `None`/`False`, so the
default CUDA path is byte-for-byte main's.

Two smaller changes in the same files ride along:

- The layer-invariant prefill seqblock metadata (`cu_seqblocks_q`,
  `max_seqblock_q`, `all_seqblock_q`) is computed once per `ForwardBatch` in the
  backend and passed down, instead of being recomputed inside each sparse layer.
  Same values. The owning `ForwardBatch` is part of the cache key because a
  single metadata init can be followed by more than one `ForwardBatch` reaching
  the layers (two-batch overlap splits into two children with different
  `extend_seq_lens`), so a hit requires the same object, not just a live cache.

title: MiniMax-M3: run the sparse prefill main attention through AITER Gluon paged attention
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: Gluon paged-attention sparse prefill with Triton fallback

MiniMax-M3's sparse prefill runs three steps: a lightning-index attention that
produces per-query block scores, a top-k reduction over those scores, and a
sparse main attention that attends only to the selected KV blocks. Step 3 is
currently a Triton kernel (`flash_prefill_with_gqa_share_sparse`) that walks the
paged KV pool one 128-token block at a time via `req_to_token`. This PR adds a
second implementation of step 3 that calls AITER's Gluon paged attention
(`pa_decode_gluon(..., ps=True)`) instead, selected by
`SGLANG_OPT_USE_GLUON_PREFILL`. The main KV pool layout is unchanged — it stays
NHD `[max_slots, 1, head_dim]` — so each request's context is first gathered
into persistent SHUFFLE 5D scratch pages (`GLUON_PAGE_SIZE = 64`, two pages per
128-token sparse block, `x = 16 // dtype.itemsize`), and the per-query sparse
block table is expanded into a page table plus a per-query effective context
length. Scratch grows in 1024-page steps and is capped at 512 MiB per buffer;
past the cap the entry point raises and the caller falls back. The indexer and
the top-k reduction (steps 1 and 2) are untouched by the dispatch. Two prefill
kernels this path shares also change: a score-only index-attention kernel for
`disable_index_value` layers (it skips the index-value output and, when a sparse
block spans few enough pages, reads one base slot per page instead of one
`req_to_token` entry per token), and CDNA KV sub-tiling (`SUB_K`) in the Triton
sparse kernel so each QK/PV MFMA is right-sized on gfx942/gfx950.

title: MiniMax-M3: allocate the lightning-indexer K cache in fp8 on gfx95
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: allocate the lightning-indexer K cache in fp8 on gfx95

MiniMax-M3's sparse attention keeps a second, much narrower KV cache — the
lightning-indexer K cache — whose only job is to produce the per-block scores
that pick which KV blocks the main attention reads. It is sized over every
sparse layer at `head_num=1, head_dim=sparse_index_dim`, and on ROCm it was
allocated in the model dtype (bf16) while the main K/V follow
`kv_cache_dtype`. This PR allocates it in `fp8_e4m3fn` on gfx95 (MI350/MI355)
behind `SGLANG_OPT_MINIMAX_M3_FP8_INDEX_CACHE`, exactly halving that pool. It
is a widening mode — bf16 q against fp8 k in the score kernels — which is the
same contract `m3_fp8_attn_gemm_enabled` already uses for the SM100 fp8
attn-GEMM path; this change makes the same `index_dtype=fp8` choice reachable
on gfx95 without requiring fp8 main KV. The Triton qk-norm-rope kernel now
stores into the index cache in *that cache's* dtype rather than q's, so the
value is rounded once from fp32 instead of twice through bf16 (a no-op cast
when the two dtypes match).

The change is **selection-only**: `dtype=self.kv_cache_dtype` for the main
attention K/V is untouched, and only `index_dtype` moves.

## Changes

- `KVCacheConfigurator.minimax_sparse_index_dtype()` is the single source of the
  index dtype. Both the pool builder and `pool_configurator`'s per-token cell
  size call it, so the sizing cannot drift from the allocation (same pattern as
  `is_unified_kv_fp8()` for DSV4).
- gfx95 only: OCP `e4m3fn` is only safe where it is native; on gfx94x sglang's
  fp8 is `e4m3fnuz` (max 224), so MI300 keeps the bf16 index cache and the flag
  is a no-op there.
- The flag defaults to `True`, i.e. on for gfx95 MiniMax-M3 sparse serving.
  This is a precision change, not a free fusion — see Accuracy below. Set
  `SGLANG_OPT_MINIMAX_M3_FP8_INDEX_CACHE=0` for a bf16 index cache.

## Behaviour on other platforms

- **CUDA, default config:** no change. The index dtype still resolves to the
  model dtype and the Triton store cast is an identity.
- **CUDA SM100 with fp8 attn-GEMM mode (`m3_fp8_attn_gemm_enabled`):** the index
  cache was already fp8 there, but the cell-size estimate counted it at bf16.
  It now counts the real fp8 size, so this configuration gets slightly more
  `max_total_num_tokens` at the same `mem_fraction_static`. Not measured.
- **MI300 (gfx94x) / NPU:** no change.

## Memory

The index pool is allocated as
`size x page_size x 1 x idx_head_dim x sizeof(index_dtype)` per sparse KV layer,
so bf16 -> `fp8_e4m3fn` is an exact **2x reduction of the index cache** with no
change to the main K/V pool.

Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8,
`--mem-fraction-static 0.80`, one boot per row, identical launch command
throughout (only the flag / the commit under test differs):

| run | index K cache | max_total_num_tokens | available_gpu_mem |
|---|---|---|---|
| baseline (`SGLANG_OPT_MINIMAX_M3_FP8_INDEX_CACHE=0`) | bf16, 43.34 GB | 3189113 | 41.12 GB |
| commit 1 -- fp8 index cache | fp8, 21.67 GB | 3189113 | **62.98 GB** |
| commit 2 -- + cell-size accounting | fp8, 25.05 GB | **3686422** (+15.6%) | 45.22 GB |

Commit 1 halves the index pool exactly (43.34 -> 21.67 GB), but the saving
surfaced as *free GPU memory* rather than capacity: the per-token cell-size
estimate that converts the profiled byte budget into `max_total_num_tokens`
still assumed a bf16 indexer, so the pool was sized as if nothing had been
saved and `max_total_num_tokens` did not move.

Commit 2 makes that estimate use the same dtype the pool is actually built
with. The saving then becomes capacity instead — **+15.6% `max_total_num_tokens`
at the same `mem_fraction_static`** — and free GPU memory returns to roughly the
baseline level, i.e. the freed bytes are spent rather than stranded.
`max_running_requests` is 2048 on all three rows.

Load-tested on the final state at bs44 / 80000 input = 3,520,000 tokens, beyond
the 3,189,113 the first two rows can hold: runs clean, peak token usage 0.95, no
OOM and no retraction.

## Performance
Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.
Two bench reps per boot; the warm (second) rep is reported and the two agreed
within 0.1%. Noise floor is +/-0.4%. Tables are the harness output verbatim,
trimmed to the first five columns. Baseline is `upstream/main`.
**Baseline (`upstream/main`)**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.26 |                     187984 |                       55.35 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.88 |                     191222 |                      108.68 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.39 |                     192965 |                      204.62 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.27 |                     193687 |                      370.13 |
|           16 |       80000 |         22.2  |                     193188 |                      616.28 |
|           32 |       80000 |         33.78 |                     193245 |                      934.92 |
```
**With this PR**

```
Input lens: [80000]. Output lens: [600]. Cache hit rate: 90.0%.
|   batch size |   input len |   latency (s) |   input throughput (tok/s) |   output throughput (tok/s) |
|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.23 |                     191515 |                       55.5  |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.9  |                     196762 |                      108.27 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.11 |                     197873 |                      208.82 |
|            8 |       80000 |         15.69 |                     198566 |                      384.87 |
|           16 |       80000 |         21.13 |                     198257 |                      654.2  |
|           32 |       80000 |         31.54 |                     198355 |                     1030.4  |
```

## Accuracy

same server boot as the perf run.
**Baseline**

== gsm8k ==

* score           =  97.07%

  truncated_rate  =  1.56%  [warn: hitting max_tokens]

## Validation

No unit test is added: the sizing/allocation agreement is enforced by the
shared `minimax_sparse_index_dtype()`, and a dtype-selection test would only
restate its condition. Evidence is end-to-end (memory, perf and gsm8k above).
These numbers were measured before the `kvcache.cuh` change was dropped from

capture) and before the latest merge of `main`; they have not been re-run.

title: MiniMax-M3: Triton split-K router GEMV with in-kernel fixup
author: zcnrex
body:
# MiniMax-M3: Triton split-K router GEMV with in-kernel split-K fixup

The MiniMax-M3 MoE router gate is a skinny GEMV — `[M, K]` bf16 x `[N, K]` bf16 -> `[M, N]` fp32, with `N ~ 128` experts and `M <= 64` at decode — and the vendor BLAS solutions picked for that shape run far off the memory roofline on gfx950 (~0.1 TB/s for a ~1.6MB weight read at `M<=8`, `N=128`). This PR adds `python/sglang/kernels/ops/gemm/router_gemv.py`, a Triton split-K kernel that reads the gate weight once at near-bandwidth, and routes `MiniMaxM3MoE._compute_router_logits` through it when `router_gemv_supported()` says the shape qualifies. Configs are per-M-bucket (`BLOCK_K` 512 throughout, `BLOCK_N` and `SPLIT_K` chosen by batch size, with a dedicated `BLOCK_M == 1` GEMV path that uses `tl.sum` instead of `tl.dot`) covering `M <= 8 / 16 / 32 / 64`. The split-K reduction is done inside the same kernel: the last CTA to finish a `(n-block, row-tile)` pair reduces all `SPLIT_K` partials and resets its counter slot to zero on the way out, so the scratch buffer stays reusable across launches without either a zero-init launch or a separate reduce launch — each extra launch costs ~2us on gfx950, which is a meaningful fraction of the kernel itself at these sizes. Anything the kernel does not cover — wrong dtype, non-contiguous last dim, `N` not divisible by `BLOCK_N`, `K` not divisible by `BLOCK_K`, or `M > 64` — falls through `router_gemv_supported()` to the existing `torch.mm` path unchanged.

## Performance
Measured on 8x MI350X (gfx950), MiniMax-M3-MXFP8, TP8, 80k input / 600 output.
Two bench reps per boot; the warm (second) rep is reported and the two agreed
within 0.1%. Noise floor is +/-0.4%. Tables are the harness output verbatim,
trimmed to the first five columns. Baseline is `upstream/main`.
**Baseline (`upstream/main`)**

|--------------|-------------|---------------|----------------------------|-----------------------------|
|            1 |       80000 |         11.26 |                     187984 |                       55.35 |
|            2 |       80000 |         11.88 |                     191222 |                      108.68 |
|            4 |       80000 |         13.39 |                     192965 |                      204.62 |
|            8 |       80000 |         16.27 |                     193687 |                      370.13 |
|           16 |       80000 |         22.2  |                     193188 |                      616.28 |
