title: [Fix] dsa: Make the fused top-k exact on an overflowing threshold bin
author: xiaofei-zheng
body:
## Motivation

The coarse histogram bin comes from the top bits of the fp16 cast, so one bin spans a quarter-binade. The collect pass stores at most 2048 threshold-bin candidates; when the bin is larger, `handle_tie` ranks whichever arrived first and silently returns a wrong top-k set.

Found while profiling GLM-5.2 decode on MI355X: ~0.04% of rows entered this path across all 8 ranks, with a largest observed bin of 4139 against the 2048 cap and none of those rows bit-identical. #35257 reports the same defect independently from the CUDA side — referenced, not closed.

## Modifications

When the threshold bin overflows, narrow it with three exact-key radix rounds (12 / 12 / 8 bits), then make one final input scan to emit candidates above the selected bucket and re-stage the bucket for the existing tie handler. The refinement histogram overlays the dead arrival-order buffer, so LDS is unchanged.

The cold scan uses a separate reversed-lane load path. This keeps its load-address state out of the fast path's registers and restores most of the CUDA regression reported in review.

Replace the fp16-bin boundary conversion with exact fp32 bounds. In particular, when a bin's high edge is `+0.0`, the boundary advances to the smallest positive subnormal so `-0.0` cannot be misclassified as above the bin.

The ROCm long-row split path from #39931 gets the same refinement: each block publishes its uncapped bin count, and the last block refines the whole row when the bin overflows.

The fast path only adds the overflow comparison. The ROCm `__launch_bounds__` argument also states the physical floor of 4 waves/SIMD; the CUDA spelling is unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

The exactness test covers register, streaming and split (4×65536) shapes with six distributions, including adjacent fp32 values and `-0.0`; on CUDA it skips rows longer than 24576, which can reach the still-unrefined cluster path.

| suite | result before the fix |
|---|---|
| 300 pre-existing cases | 300 passed |
| 10 overflowing non-identical cases | 10 failed |
| 2 `all_equal` controls | 2 passed |

The signed-zero cases also fail on the pre-review refinement and pass with the new boundary conversion. All 330 cases pass on the merged tree; on the split shape, 4 of the 6 distributions failed before the refinement.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

MI355X (gfx950), five paired runs per arm on one GPU, 200 iterations after warmup:

| distribution | shape | main | this PR | |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `randn` (hot path) | 6×8192 | 5.430 µs | 5.338 µs | −1.7% |
| `randn` (hot path) | 4×32768 | 12.270 µs | 12.188 µs | −0.7% |
| `narrow_bin` | 6×8192 | 16.821 µs | 20.937 µs | +24.5% |
| `narrow_bin` | 4×32768 | 29.652 µs | 50.030 µs | +68.7% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 6×8192 | 11.487 µs | 34.862 µs | +203.5% |
| `two_values` (32-bit refinement) | 4×32768 | 36.314 µs | 117.756 µs | +224.3% |

The cold-path delta is the cost of exact work that main skips by returning a wrong answer. It is entered on ~0.04% of rows in the serving traffic above. Against the previous PR implementation, the new scan is 2.6–5.3% faster on `narrow_bin`. On the latest tree, a clean local JIT build is 10.50 s versus 10.02 s on main (+4.8%), rather than the nearly 2× CUDA increase reported before this rewrite.

Without overflow the split path is unchanged (15.5–20.1 µs for batch 1–8, 64K–128K, before and after).

On gfx950: 63 → 71 VGPRs, zero spills, LDS unchanged at 26928 B. We do not have NVIDIA hardware; CUDA register pressure and B200 performance need CI/reviewer measurement.

## Known gap

The CUDA-only `TopKCluster` path still truncates. Refining there needs cluster-wide histogram and emit counters rather than the block-local ones used here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add exactness tests.
- [x] Provide accuracy and performance results.
- [x] Keep documentation and comments synchronized.

title: [diffusion] quantization: ConvRot INT8 online W8A8 for DiTs (sgl-kernel + `convrot_int8_customkernel`)
author: alex0dd
body: ## Motivation DiT inference is dominated by a few large GEMMs, and BF16 weights dominate memory (Qwen-Image's DiT is 38 GiB). The existing online INT8 option, `kitchen_int8`, needs an external package and is slower than BF16 on Hopper and Blackwell. This PR adds `--quantization convrot_int8_customkernel`: online W8A8 INT8 with no calibration data, no extra package and no special checkpoint. Following ConvRot ([arXiv:2512.03673](https://arxiv.org/abs/2512.03673)), a group-wise Hadamard rotation (the regular Hadamard, a Kronecker power of a 4x4 block whose rows all sum to one) is applied before INT8 quantization so that per-row activation and per-channel weight scales stay accurate despite channel outliers and non-zero group means. Rotation, quantization, INT8 GEMM and dequantization run as one fused sgl-kernel op per linear. The method is model-agnostic. On Qwen-Image, Qwen-Image-Edit, Flux it is 1.13x to 1.61x faster (based on setup and model) than BF16, halves the DiT weights, and is about 2x faster than current `kitchen_int8` at the same memory. ## Modifications **sgl-kernel** (`csrc/gemm/convrot_int8_gemm.cu`) - `convrot_rotate_quantize_activation`: regular-Hadamard rotation (4-point stages) + per-row dynamic INT8 quantization in one kernel, optional bit-exact GELU(tanh) on the input; also the offline weight transform. The Sylvester Walsh-Hadamard was rejected: its all-ones row concentrates a group's mean into one coefficient, which sets the INT8 step and adds 1.3x to 1.9x error on GELU outputs. - `convrot_int8_fused_linear[_gelu_input|_out]`: rotate + quantize + CUTLASS INT8 GEMM with the per-row x per-column dequant and bias fused in the epilogue. - `convrot_int8_linear_prequant[_out]`: the same GEMM on an activation quantized once and shared by several linears; bitwise identical to the fused op. - Back ends: WGMMA on CC 9.0, tcgen05 on CC 10.0 (`sm_100a` pass for this file only), and the CUTLASS 2.x mma.sync path of `int8_scaled_mm` (sm89) on CC 12.0 / 12.1. One supported-CC table, exposed as `convrot_int8_supported_sm_versions`. CC 10.3 is refused with a reason (Blackwell Ultra's INT8 rate is a fraction of BF16; use FP8/NVFP4). - CMake: `sm_90a` pass emitted independently of FA3 (Hopper CUTLASS kernels were stubs on aarch64). **sglang-diffusion** - `ConvRotInt8CustomKernelConfig` / `LinearMethod`: quantizes every linear whose input width is a multiple of 256 after loading, honours `--quantization-ignored-layers`, refuses unsupported GPUs with the reason. - Automatic, bit-exact fusions: q/k/v projections sharing an input are rotated once; an FFN down-projection folds its GELU into the rotate kernel. - Qwen-Image dispatch (always on, byte-identical default output): Q/K/V written straight into joint text-image buffers; steps aside under autograd and for LoRA-wrapped layers. - Docs: ConvRot section in `docs/docs/sglang-diffusion/quantization.mdx`. ## Performance Default eager execution (no CUDA graph), n=3 per cell, one host and container per table, idle node, every eligible layer quantized; all tables measured on commit e5af511a87 or its content-identical precursor. Peak memory is the torch allocator peak over load and run. GB200 tables first, then the other GPUs measured with the same harness. **Qwen-Image on GB200 (CC 10.0), 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 4** | configuration | 1 GPU | vs BF16 | 2 GPUs CFG-parallel | vs BF16 | peak memory | DiT weights | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (main) | 7916 ms | 1.00x | 4096 ms | 1.00x | 56.0 GB | 38.0 GiB | | `kitchen_int8` | 18297 ms | 0.43x | 9348 ms | 0.44x | 37.0 GB | 19.0 GiB | | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | 6670 ms | **1.19x** | 3617 ms | **1.13x** | **37.0 GB** | 19.0 GiB | **Qwen-Image on H100 PCIe 80 GB (CC 9.0), 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 4** | configuration | 1 GPU | vs BF16 | 2 GPUs CFG-parallel | vs BF16 | peak memory | DiT weights | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (main) | 22207 ms | 1.00x | 11596 ms | 1.00x | 56.0 GB | 38.0 GiB | | `kitchen_int8` | 22355 ms | 0.99x | 11470 ms | 1.01x | 37.0 GB | 19.0 GiB | | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | 15150 ms | **1.47x** | 7894 ms | **1.47x** | **37.0 GB** | 19.0 GiB | **Qwen-Image on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (CC 12.0, 96 GB), 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 4, 1 GPU** | configuration | time per image | ms/step | vs BF16 | peak memory | DiT weights | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (main) | 24118 ms | 481.9 | 1.00x | 56.0 GB | 38.0 GiB | | `kitchen_int8` | 16995 ms | 339.2 | 1.42x | 37.0 GB | 19.0 GiB | | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | 15011 ms | 299.6 | **1.61x** | **37.0 GB** | 19.0 GiB | **Qwen-Image on DGX Spark (GB10, CC 12.1, 128 GB unified memory), 1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 4, 1 GPU** | configuration | time per image | ms/step | vs BF16 | peak memory | DiT weights | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (main) | 108439 ms | 2166.3 | 1.00x | 56.0 GB | 38.0 GiB | | `kitchen_int8` | 85114 ms | 1699.8 | 1.27x | 37.0 GB | 19.0 GiB | | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | 73876 ms | 1475.1 | **1.47x** | **37.0 GB** | 19.0 GiB | **Qwen-Image-Edit, 1024x1024 input, 50 steps, CFG 4** | configuration | 1 GPU | vs BF16 | 2 GPUs CFG-parallel | vs BF16 | peak memory | DiT weights | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (main) | 21868 ms | 1.00x | 11493 ms | 1.00x | 57.3 GB | 38.0 GiB | | `kitchen_int8` | 40912 ms | 0.53x | not run | - | 38.3 GB | 19.0 GiB | | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | 16571 ms | **1.32x** | 8728 ms | **1.32x** | **38.3 GB** | 19.0 GiB | **FLUX.2-klein-base-4B, 1024x1024, 50 steps, 1 GPU** (guidance embedded, single pass) | configuration | time per image | ms/step | vs BF16 | peak memory | DiT weights | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | BF16 (main) | 3882 ms | 75.5 | 1.00x | 17.4 GB | 6.9 GiB | | `kitchen_int8` | 7098 ms | 140.2 | 0.55x | 14.0 GB | 3.4 GiB | | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | 2961 ms | 57.4 | **1.31x** | **14.0 GB** | 3.4 GiB | Kernel level at the FLUX.2 shapes: ConvRot fused 1.12x geomean vs cuBLAS BF16, `kitchen_int8` 0.29x. On the current main this model renders noise in every configuration, BF16 included, so it is a throughput data point only; the distilled FLUX.2-klein-4B does not load on the current main. Eager Qwen-Image on one GPU is close to launch-bound on GB200, which limits what any GEMM change shows end to end; the edit model, with twice the tokens per pass, is GPU-bound and shows the gain. Kernel level (`bench_kernels.py`, same GPU, fused rotate+quantize+GEMM+dequant vs cuBLAS BF16): geometric mean 1.28x over the Qwen-Image shapes at image-token row counts, 1.69x on the FFN up-projection (3072 to 12288, 8448 rows), 1.18x on the square 3072x3072 projections; `kitchen_int8` 0.38x. Relative L2 error vs BF16: ConvRot 0.009 to 0.012, kitchen 0.010 to 0.013. The ignore-list configuration (`--quantization-ignored-layers img_mod txt_mod txt_mlp.net.2`) keeps the small-row GEMMs in BF16 and saves less memory (45.5 GB peak on Qwen-Image); the default quantizes every eligible layer. ## Accuracy Same seed across arms. On the current main commit neither FLUX.2-klein variant produces usable images regardless of quantization (klein-base renders noise in BF16 too; the distilled klein does not load), so visual comparisons are given for Qwen-Image and Qwen-Image-Edit. **Qwen-Image** (1024x1024, 50 steps, CFG 4) | prompt | BF16 | `kitchen_int8` | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | |---|---|---|---| | A vintage bookstore front with a hand-painted sign reading 'THE PAPER LANTERN', autumn evening | | | | | Portrait of a young woman with freckles and auburn hair, natural window light, shallow depth of field | | | | | Macro photo of a hummingbird hovering at a red trumpet flower, wings frozen mid-beat | | | | **Qwen-Image-Edit** (1024x1024 input, 50 steps, CFG 4) | instruction | input | BF16 | `kitchen_int8` | `convrot_int8_customkernel` (this PR) | |---|---|---|---|---| | Change the sign text to 'OPEN LATE' and make it night time with warm window light | | | | | | Turn the scene into a snowy winter morning, keep the storefront layout | | | | | | Add a bicycle leaning against the wall on the left | | | | | Qwen-Image: equivalent on all three prompts. Qwen-Image-Edit: equivalent on all three edits; on the snowy-storefront edit, PSNR to the BF16 output is 25.2 dB for ConvRot and 24.8 dB for `kitchen_int8`, and a Laplacian grain measure is 15.2 for ConvRot, 17.8 for BF16, 18.3 for kitchen. (An earlier revision of the rotation kernel produced visible grain on this edit, 17.6 dB; that is what motivated the regular-Hadamard rotation.) The bicycle edit is degraded in BF16 itself on the current main and is reported separately. INT8 outputs are not bit-exact to BF16; with quantization off the branch is byte-identical to main. ## Testing ```bash pytest python/sglang/kernels/aot/tests/test_convrot_int8.py # 67 tests: op equalities, Hadamard reference, validation pytest python/sglang/multimodal_gen/test/unit/test_convrot_int8_quant.py python test/registered/unit/models/test_qwen_image_joint_qkv.py python python/sglang/kernels/aot/benchmark/bench_convrot_int8.py # vs cuBLAS BF16 sglang generate --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image --quantization convrot_int8_customkernel \ --prompt "a beautiful sunset" --save-output ``` All suites pass on GB200 (CC 10.0). The same process, tests included, ran on H100 and H200 (CC 9.0), RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (CC 12.0) and DGX Spark (CC 12.1), with the default BF16 path byte-identical to main on each. The Hadamard-reference tests check the kernel's stages against the Kronecker construction at group sizes 64/128/256/512, including partial tiles and rows up to 57856 wide, and the quantization error is checked to be independent of the input statistics (Gaussian, GELU outputs, mean-shifted, per-channel shifted), the case the earlier Sylvester rotation failed. ## Checklist - [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit). - [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci). - [x] Update documentation / docstrings / example tutorials as needed. - [x] Provide throughput / latency benchmark results and accuracy evaluation results as needed. - [ ] For reviewers: If you haven't made any contributions to this PR and are only assisting with merging the main branch, please remove yourself as a co-author when merging. - [ ] Please feel free to join our Slack channel if you have any questions. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #36876971646](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36876971646) Latest PR Test (Extra): :warning: **Not enabled** -- add `run-ci-extra` label to opt in. title: [diffusion] fuse LingBot MoE group-limited top-k index selection
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

The LingBot Video MoE router computes group-limited expert selection with a sequence of small CUDA operations: a per-group top-2 reduction, group top-k, mask construction, masked expert scores, and the final expert top-k. This path is launch-bound for large token counts, so the selection can be fused without changing the selected expert-id set.

The PR is also updated to the latest SGLang `main`, whose diffusion kernels now use a facade + registry layout and consolidated registered tests. The kernel documentation and diffusion benchmark/profile skill need to describe that current layout rather than the pre-refactor file paths.

## Modifications

- Add `sglang/kernels/ops/diffusion/routing/group_limited_topk_triton.py`: one Triton program per token loads the score row once, computes the per-group top-2 sums, selects the allowed groups, and writes the final expert ids.
- Add an explicit `can_use_group_limited_topk` predicate. Supported NVIDIA CUDA inputs use the fused path; unsupported dtype/layout/group configurations retain the eager PyTorch path. Kernel failures are no longer silently swallowed on every router call.
- Register `diffusion.group_limited_topk` in the diffusion kernel registry and export both the predicate and implementation through the public diffusion facade.
- Register the launch as a custom op with a fake implementation, including `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)` coverage.
- Move the correctness test into registered kernel CI as `test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_routing.py`. The matrix now includes LingBot Video's production configuration: 128 experts, 4 groups, 2 selected groups, and top-8 experts.
- Refresh the public fused-kernel inventory and package README. The current registry contains 45 operators / 51 implementations, including the LingBot routing operator and recently registered KDA kernels.
- Refresh the diffusion benchmark/profile skill's fast-path map: add LingBot routing guidance and replace stale pre-refactor kernel/test paths with their current locations.

This is a selection-equivalent, default-on path for supported inputs and is independent of the request quality tier. The output order remains unspecified, matching the reference `torch.topk(..., sorted=False)` contract.

## Reproduction commands

CUDA correctness and compile coverage:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_routing.py -q
```

Facade and registry consistency:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python python3 -m pytest \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_import_surface.py -q
```

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Hardware: one NVIDIA H200. Microbenchmark uses 8,192 tokens and the production LingBot Video routing configuration (128 experts / 4 groups / `topk_group=2` / `top_k=8`), with 100 warmup iterations and 500 measured iterations.

| Measurement | Time | Note |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Reference PyTorch selection chain | 0.2207 ms | multiple small CUDA operations |
| Fused Triton selection | 0.0453 ms | **4.87x faster** |

This is a routing-selection microbenchmark; it does not claim an end-to-end model speedup.

## Accuracy Tests

- 28/28 routing tests pass on H200: six expert/group/top-k configurations across four sequence lengths, uniform ties, repeated nonuniform scores, unsupported-layout rejection, and `torch.compile(fullgraph=True)`.
- 9/9 diffusion facade/registry consistency tests pass.
- The per-row selected expert-id set matches the CUDA reference in every tested case; ordering is ignored because the reference uses `sorted=False`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format and lint the changed files with pre-commit.
- [x] Provide correctness and microbenchmark results.
- [x] Register the kernel and test in the current diffusion layout.
- [x] Update the public kernel documentation and diffusion optimization skill.
- [x] Preserve eager fallbacks for unsupported platforms and inputs.

title: Revert "[kernel] add fused silu mul quant fp8"
author: hnyls2002
body:
Reverts sgl-project/sglang#37376

## Why

#37376 enables a fused silu+mul+FP8-quant kernel on the block-wise FP8 MoE path. It is not numerically equivalent to the two-kernel path it replaces, and the difference is large enough to cost speculative-decoding acceptance on GLM-5.2-FP8 EAGLE MTP.

`test/registered/e2e/models/test_dsa_glm52_tp_mtp.py::test_bs_1_speed` asserts `accept_length > 4.0` and is currently failing on main.

## Bisect

Two `Rerun Test` dispatches of that test on the `8-gpu-h200` pool, at #37376 and its direct parent:

| commit | Acc Length | Tokens | Speed (token/s) | Result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `503511c963` (parent) | **4.727** | 1092 | 323.28 | pass |
| `a8b2f36dee` (#37376) | **3.949** | 778 | 265.40 | fail |

- [run at parent](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34173127970) / [run at #37376](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34173132321)
- 4.727 is the value every scheduled main run produced before #37376 landed; 3.949 reproduces identically across all three attempts in the run.
- Net effect on this recipe: **-16.5% accept length, -18% bs=1 decode speed**.

## Mechanism

- `_can_use_fused_silu_mul_quant_fp8` turns the kernel on from shape/dtype alone. There is no flag or env var to disable it, so an affected model cannot opt out.
- The fused kernel emits the FP8 down-GEMM input directly, skipping the bf16 `intermediate_cache2` round-trip, so its output differs from the two-kernel path.
- The unit test added in #37376 states the tolerance explicitly: `fp8_match > 0.95` (up to 5% of FP8 bytes may differ) and `assert_close(fused_output, fallback_output, rtol=0.02, atol=0.02)`.
- Accuracy-style evals absorb that (`cosine_sim > 0.9999`), but acceptance length is a discrete draft/target token-agreement rate compounded over 5 draft steps, and target and draft share the same MoE, so the perturbation accumulates instead of averaging out.

## Note

Reverting rather than gating because no switch exists today. A reland could keep the kernel behind an opt-in flag, or disable it when speculative decoding is enabled.

title: [Feat] [NPU] DSpark: DeepSeek-V4 support DSpark compact mode
author: randgun
body:
## Motivation

DSpark on the Ascend DSV4 backend currently falls back to a uniform verify window or eager-side post-processing for parts of speculative decoding. This leaves two sources of avoidable overhead:

1. the target model verifies the full draft window even when the SPS policy selects a shorter per-request verify length;
2. accept/finalize and hidden/KV commit remain outside the target verify graph.

This PR enables the compact DSpark path on NPU, adds token-tiered graph replay for ragged target verify, and folds the eligible verify epilogue into the graph.

## Modifications

### 1. DSpark compact verify on NPU

- Build packed/ragged verify windows from per-request verify lengths selected by the DSpark planner.
- Add NPU-safe compact row mapping, verify-ID gathering, cache-location handling, and compact-to-strided scatter.
- Construct DSV4 SWA, sparse-attention, C4/C128 compressor, position, state, and page-table metadata from the live compact layout.
- Preserve eager fallback when the selected attention backend does not support ragged verify graphs.

### 2. Compact target-verify graph

- Advertise ragged verify graph support for the DSV4 Ascend backend.
- Select target-verify graphs by compact token tier while retaining fixed graph-owned buffers.
- Refresh query indptr, sequence lengths, cache/page tables, compressor locations/state, and sparse indices before replay.
- Add an NPU-local bucketed-layout cache so the Ascend and DSV4 metadata consumers reuse the same derived layout.
- Use the safe last-location Triton path for DSV4 NPU allocation metadata.

### 3. Verify epilogue graph

- Add a DSV4 NPU-specific target-verify tail hook that uses the committed/live prefix lengths from DSV4 metadata.
- Fold greedy accept/finalize and eligible hidden/KV commit into the compact target-verify graph.
- Keep sampling, grammar-constrained decoding, logits adjustments, and other ineligible cases on the existing eager epilogue path.
- Keep the adaptation NPU/DSV4-specific so the existing CUDA behavior remains unchanged.

## Accuracy Tests

- GPQA-Diamond accuracy: **0.91** with DSpark on Ascend NPU.
- The compact path preserves the target-model verification result; it changes the number of draft tokens verified and where graph-safe post-processing executes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling
The expected gain comes from reducing target-verify tokens according to the SPS-selected compact lengths and removing eligible verify epilogue launches from the host path.
| Metric | Compact | Static | Delta |
|--------|---------|--------|-------|
| Output throughput (tok/s) | 2027.13 | 1949.98 | Compact +4.0% |
| Mean TPOT (ms) | 20.87 | 26.27 | Compact -20.6% |
| Mean TTFT (ms) | 36563.48 | 38385.26 | Compact -4.7% |

## Validation

- Python syntax compilation passed for all Python files changed by this PR.
- Added scheduler coverage for exact eager token counts when the backend does not support ragged verify graphs.

title: [Fix] sampling: deterministic top-p / top-k renorm when tp_size > 1 (TP rank divergence in DFlash/DSpark)
author: gilfordting
body:
## Summary

flashinfer's default top-p / top-k renorm kernels are non-deterministic (float `atomicAdd`); because of this, TP ranks that renormalize the same logits can produce different results. Every consumer of this output (plain sampler, spec-verify) samples against a deterministic coin and commits the result to per-rank KV/radix state. A coin that lands in between the cross-rank gap causes divergence across ranks, and NCCL collectives hang.

Previous PRs (#33549, #33289; #33614) work around this issue by broadcasting rank 0's decision. This PR addresses the root cause and avoids an extra collective, by routing the renorm through flashinfer's `is_deterministic=True` variants. This is turned on where it matters:

| configuration                         | renorm kernels  | why                                                            |
| ------------------------------------- | --------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------- |
| single rank                           | fast            | nothing to agree with                                          |
| `attn_tp_size > 1`                    | deterministic   | each rank computes the same result; bit-identical across ranks |
| `--enable-deterministic-inference`    | deterministic   | self-explanatory                                               |
| `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1` / `0` | forced on / off | explicit override                                              |

Repro + results are below. With all relevant broadcasts turned off, the fast kernels reproduce the hang on H100 and B200 in every run. The deterministic kernels never diverge, and the end-to-end cost to TPOT is marginal.

## Root cause

- `sgl_kernel.top_p_renorm_prob` and `top_k_renorm_prob` forward to flashinfer.
    - Top-p on rows longer than 2048 uses the AIR radix kernel (>= 0.6.7, flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#2752) whose default histogram is a float atomic.
    - Top-k (`RadixTopKRenormProbMultiCTA`) pools the kept mass with a float atomic.
    - flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#4831 (0.7.x, sglang pins 0.7.2) added a fixed-point `is_deterministic=True` at unchanged latency.
- In non-greedy verification, each rank compares its own `target_probs` (top-p/top-k output) against a shared coin and samples the bonus token from `relu(q - p)`.
    - If ranks differ slightly, the coin might cross the acceptance or bonus thresholds on some ranks and not others; this will cause KV state to drift and a later prefix match will cause NCCL collectives to hang.
- The sampler's `min_p` path calls the same kernels with no broadcast (`SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` is off by default).
- Earlier synthetic repros were clean because they used `top_p=1.0`, which skips the kernel entirely.

## Repro

**Setup**

- Image: current main (nightly `ed8c3139`, flashinfer 0.7.1, sgl_kernel 0.4.10) with this PR applied.
- Model, config, workload: TP=2 DFlash, Llama-3.1-8B + `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat`, `temperature=1.0`, `top_p=0.9`, 32 concurrent multi-turn streams, fp8 KV.
- Broadcast collectives off:
    - Hard-coded broadcast is only on for the EAGLE path. We use DFlash.
    - `SGLANG_SPEC_TP_SYNC=off` turns off #33614's broadcasts.
    - `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` are off by default.
- Deterministic renorm kernels on using a new environment variable, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
- A probe all-gathers per-verify-step fingerprints of `{rng state, prefix_lens, draft_tokens, target_logits, target_probs, accept_len, bonus, commit_lens, out_tokens}` and reports the first field that differs.
    - It also calls `top_p_renorm_prob` twice on the same input on one rank, counting mismatches after.

**Results**

"knob" below refers to the new env-var, `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC=1`.
| broadcast | renorm | runs | requests per run | first cross-rank `target_probs` difference | rank-local mismatches (top-p calls) | outcome |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| off | fast (knob=0, same kernels as main) | 4 x H100, 2 x B200 | 1.4k to 6.5k | 1 to 22 s | 0.4 to 0.9 % | **all 6 hung**, at 190 to 610 s |
| off | deterministic (knob=1) | 3 x H100, 2 x B200 | 22.6k to 35.4k | never | 0 of 276,000 | all 5 clean, full 30 min |
| all (#33614) | fast (knob=0) | 1 x H100 | 25.2k | 14 s | 0.9 % | clean: 436 `target_probs` divergences, none reaches a token |
| all (#33614) | deterministic (knob=1) | 1 x H100 | 24.4k | never | 0 of 46,000 | clean, 0 divergences |

Every fast-kernel run with the broadcast off hung, with the same recorded chain each time:

- `target_probs` differs between ranks while logits, `prefix_lens` and RNG are identical.
- `bonus` / `out_tokens` differ on one rank.
- Next step's `draft_tokens` differ.
- Hang.

Toggling only the knob to 1 on the same image, model, load and probe consistently results in zero divergences, zero rank-local mismatches, and no hang.

## Kernel measurements

We perform 99 repeated calls on byte-identical input. Settings: flashinfer 0.7.1, vocab 128256, H100. B200 and B300 give the same results.

`nondet` refers to calls that differ from call 0.

| rows | input distribution | kernel | current default        | `is_deterministic=True` |
| ---- | ------------------ | ------ | ---------------------- | ----------------------- |
| 32   | flat               | top-p  | 0.136 ms, nondet 99/99 | 0.169 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-p  | 0.127 ms, 0/99         | 0.149 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | flat               | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 99/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 32   | peaky              | top-k  | 0.042 ms, 77/99        | 0.042 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-p  | 0.603 ms, 98/99        | 0.815 ms, 0/99          |
| 256  | flat               | top-k  | 0.288 ms, 99/99        | 0.289 ms, 0/99          |

We observe the following:

- Top-k performs near-identical between both fast and deterministic arms.
- Top-p adds 20 to 45% to a 0.1 to 0.8 ms kernel. We measure how much this matters in the next section.
- The deterministic wrapper adds no host sync and no `cudaMalloc`, so there is no overhead.

## End-to-end speed

**Setup**

- Workload: `sglang.bench_serving`, random 512-in / 256-out, 400 prompts, concurrency 32.
- Model, config: Llama-3.1-8B, fp8 KV, triton attention, H100.
- One container boots four servers in sequence with the knob 1 / 0 / 1 / 0, two trials each, so both arms share a host and an image.
- We look at TPOT, since this code change is exercised during decode. The first trial (warmup) is dropped, and we calculate mean TPOT. We see that differences are on the order of 0.01 ms.

| config                                                                           | knob=1   | knob=0   | delta  | accept len    |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | -------- | -------- | ------ | ------------- |
| plain TP2 `min_p=0.05` (the path the default policy makes deterministic), host A | 4.974 ms | 4.976 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| same, host B, order 0 / 1 / 0 / 1                                                | 5.058 ms | 5.062 ms | -0.1 % |               |
| plain TP1 `min_p=0.05`                                                           | 8.065 ms | 8.067 ms | -0.0 % |               |
| DFlash TP2 `top_p=0.9` (knob=1 forces the verify path deterministic too)         | 3.992 ms | 3.983 ms | +0.2 % | 4.563 / 4.564 |
| EAGLE3 TP2 `top_p=0.9`                                                           | 7.191 ms | 7.175 ms | +0.2 % | 1.929 / 1.930 |

Thus, we see that there is no measureable end-to-end cost, including the forced-deterministic verify path; the accept length is also unchanged.

The renorm kernel runs once per step over `batch_size` rows (sampler) or `batch_size x draft_tokens` rows (verify), so deterministic top-p adds ~0.03 ms at 32 rows and ~0.2 ms at 256 rows, which is small compared to a step of several ms.

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/sampling_renorm.py` (new):
    - `renorm_deterministic(ranks_agree)` policy.
    - `top_p_renorm_prob` / `top_k_renorm_prob` for the sampler and `spec_top_p_renorm_prob` / `spec_top_k_renorm_prob` for verify, calling flashinfer with `is_deterministic=True` when appropriate (`sgl_kernel` as before otherwise).
    - The flag's presence is checked once at import (`inspect.signature`), so an older flashinfer degrades to the fast kernel rather than failing on the first sampled request.
    - Without flashinfer (MUSA, XPU) `sgl_kernel`'s own single-CTA kernel is already deterministic; no int32-sensitive code is added there.
- `layers/sampler.py`, `speculative/dflash_utils.py`, `speculative/eagle_utils.py` are the only renorm call sites, and now they import from the module above.
    - The `_sync_token_ids_across_tp` and `spec_tp_sync.py` comments name the renorm kernels as a known source of nondeterminism and point at the knob.
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_RENORM_DETERMINISTIC` next to the other determinism knobs.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/sampling/test_renorm.py`: existing correctness tests run through the new module; regression tests call each deterministic renorm 30 times on a flat 256 x 128256 input and assert bit-identical output (the default kernels fail this 30 of 30); scoped runtime-context fixture.
- `test/registered/unit/sampling/test_renorm_policy.py` (CPU): single rank fast; TP=2 sampler deterministic and verify fast; `--enable-deterministic-inference` forces on; env overrides both ways.

The fix lives in `sglang` rather than the `sgl_kernel` wrappers, because `sglang-kernel` ships as a pinned prebuilt wheel. A wrapper change there is not testable in CI, and is not delivered until the next kernel release.

This fix is Complementary to #33614: the broadcast keeps replicated state safe against any future non-deterministic operator. This removes the one we found, so rank 0's own output and every other consumer of `target_probs` (logprobs, sampling masks) become reproducible too.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Diffusion] Optimize Qwen-Image-Edit attention on Hopper
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Qwen-Image-Edit's Hopper profile contains repeated QK normalization/RoPE and joint-QKV concatenations in the DiT, plus 96 separate SDPA window calls per window-attention layer in the vision encoder. Reuse the existing Qwen QKV epilogue on Hopper and process packed vision windows through PyTorch's public varlen attention API.

On one H200 with main's PyTorch 2.13 dependencies, lossless eager engine E2E falls from **32.8171 s to 32.3141 s (1.533%)**. All saved before/after images are byte-identical within each quality mode. This is a modest combined full-model gain; the much larger microbenchmark ratios do not represent E2E speedups.

## Modifications

- Enable the existing BF16, batch-one, head-dimension-128 QKV epilogue for eligible unquantized SM90 Qwen attention. Support independent image/text token strides; retain mask, shard/padding, layout and alignment fallbacks and the existing environment opt-out.
- Vectorize adjacent RoPE-cache loads and paired V-head copies, and move Q/K/V dispatch into the grid's second dimension. Explicit `fmaf`/`fmul` preserves the original RoPE contraction and intermediate rounding. Odd head counts retain a smaller final copy.
- Use public `torch.nn.attention.varlen.varlen_attn` for eligible Hopper Flash SDPA inference with packed windows. No token reordering or padding. CPU/HIP/MPS, other SDPA subclasses, compilation, gradients, dropout, missing API, and unsupported inputs retain the existing path. The new SDPA dispatch is SM90-only; the shared QKV kernel also serves the existing SM100 path, whose B200 regression now passes CI (14 QKV epilogue tests).
- Update the kernel inventory's SM90 capability and extend the existing kernel, model-path and registry tests.

## Accuracy Tests

Rehashed **16 formal PNGs**: four A-B-B-A runs × two quality modes × two Torch versions. Within each mode, A/A, B/B and A/B are byte-identical, with SSIM 1 and maximum pixel error 0. Actual output resolution is 1024×1024.

The contact sheet shows baseline and candidate in columns, lossless and high in rows:

![Actual Qwen-Image-Edit before and after outputs](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/comparison.png)

| Quality | Actual baseline PNG | Actual candidate PNG |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Lossless | [Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/lossless-baseline.png) | [After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/lossless-candidate.png) |
| High | [Before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/high-baseline.png) | [After](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/high-candidate.png) |

**Use lossless for this recipe.** High already changes this input visibly: high versus lossless has SSIM **0.830311**, PSNR 17.3808 dB and maximum difference 255/255, identically for baseline and candidate. The high timing below documents compatibility with that existing mode; it is not a lossless-equivalent result or a new quality optimization.

[Torch 2.13 image comparisons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-image-quality.json), [Torch 2.11 comparisons](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-image-quality.json), [all formal hashes, source checks and selected-GPU samples](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/artifact-gpu-audit.json).

- **35 H200 tests passed on each of Torch 2.11.0+cu130 and 2.13.0+cu130**. Coverage includes QKV exactness, separate and packed strides, odd head counts, misaligned cache/token-stride fallbacks, masked attention, packed SDPA BF16/FP16, causal/ragged/empty/single windows, strided V, and training/dropout/missing-API fallbacks.
- **28 CPU registry tests passed** at the final PR head. All nine changed files passed pre-commit and `git diff --check`.
- Production microbenchmarks check six QKV cases and fourteen SDPA cases exactly. The existing B200 CI lane passes all 14 QKV epilogue tests, including the production 8,152/1,365-token shape, odd heads, and mask/shard/alignment guards. A Hopper lane is added.

[Final checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/final-checks.json), [2.11 test log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-tests.log), [2.13 test log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-tests.log), [registry test log](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/registry-tests.log).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Native `QwenImageEditPipeline`, `Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit@ac7f9318f633fc4b5778c59367c8128225f1e3de`; one H200, BF16, 1024×1024, 50 steps, guidance 4, embedded guidance 6, seed 42, official Qwen Edit input, prompt `Make the cat wear a red hat.` Automatic residency in both arms, including the existing text/image encoder layerwise offload. Eager only, no torch.compile. Native BCG probes were disabled for both qualities, so no BCG fallback timings are counted.

A is main `482e9f257bb9d9ac57c2245c93768a96ec70edbe`. Lossless measurements and microbenchmarks use candidate `60def09d35c8912db76144e7ca6691dca554bc94`; final head `7df1e941ca7782d9a964a98a9720d4ddd1cd7fa4` adds only registry capability metadata, README and CPU tests. The four runtime files are byte-identical ([audit](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/runtime-equivalence.json)). Primary high and paired profiles measured the actual final head. Runtime import paths and perf-dump commits were verified.

Each row uses fresh processes in A-B-B-A order on the same selected GPU. No rows were discarded. Primary environment: PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130, sglang-kernel 0.4.6.post1, driver 595.71.05. It was installed in a private venv; the separate legacy 2.11 environment was unchanged.

| Primary Torch 2.13 eager | A1 / A2 engine E2E | B1 / B2 engine E2E | Mean A → B | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Lossless | 32.805944 / 32.828280 s | 32.300505 / 32.327791 s | 32.817112 → 32.314148 s | **1.533%** |
| High, existing quality tradeoff | 32.290089 / 32.280895 s | 31.610836 / 31.596315 s | 32.285492 → 31.603576 s | **2.112%** |

| Environment / quality | Mean denoising A → B | Denoising reduction | Mean engine E2E A → B | E2E reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Torch 2.13 lossless | 31.821445 → 31.486249 s | 1.053% | 32.817112 → 32.314148 s | 1.533% |
| Torch 2.13 high | 31.296227 → 30.783327 s | 1.639% | 32.285492 → 31.603576 s | 2.112% |
| Torch 2.11 lossless | 31.936158 → 31.592483 s | 1.076% | 32.930535 → 32.441389 s | 1.485% |
| Torch 2.11 high | 31.378467 → 30.879241 s | 1.591% | 32.385151 → 31.710122 s | 2.084% |

The legacy lossless result is below the campaign's 1.5% acceptance threshold; it is not rounded up or pooled with 2.13. Only one input/seed and two measurements per arm are reported, so this does not establish a universal 1.5% improvement across Qwen models or inputs.

Engine E2E is synchronized stage `total_duration_ms`, excluding model loading, request warmup and PNG saving. Profile-export wall times are excluded. In unprofiled primary lossless runs, image encoding is 792.848 → 632.484 ms and denoising saves 335.196 ms. Selected GPUs were idle at every cell entry. Ten-second samples, including two legacy NVML query timeouts, are preserved; they do not prove continuous host exclusivity.

[Primary lossless ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-lossless-abba.json), [primary high ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch213-high-abba.json), [legacy lossless ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-lossless-abba.json), [legacy high ABBA](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/torch211-high-abba.json).

### Kernel and profile evidence

The initial trace identified actual DiT shapes of 8,152 image tokens and 1,365/1,358 text tokens, 24 heads, head dimension 128. Vision attention has 5,400 tokens over 96 ragged windows, 16 heads, dimension 80. Measurements below are cumulative GPU kernel durations from separate tiny Torch 2.11 traces, excluding CPU launch gaps; they are not full request timings.

| Production operation | Baseline kernels / device time | Candidate kernels / device time |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| QK norm + RoPE + joint QKV, 8,152 + 1,365 tokens | 7 / 179.617 µs | 1 / 109.023 µs |
| Packed vision SDPA, 5,400 tokens / 96 windows | 96 / 517.984 µs | 2 / 38.240 µs |

The two SDPA kernels are FlashAttention and an auxiliary zero-RNG fill; dropout is zero and no random numbers are consumed. Copy events are separate from kernel counts. QKV input restoration is outside the timed interval; the reference's packed-input materialization cost is conservatively excluded.

NCU localized 7,309,056 excess L2 sectors to four stride-two scalar RoPE-cache loads. Vector loads remove those sectors, but alone do not improve duration (121.248 → 121.760 µs). Paired V-head copies alone regress to 131.840 µs; hoisting dispatch/index work into `grid.y` reduces it to **112.544 µs**, with 63,691,368 executed instructions and 93.204% occupancy. Explicit FMA operations are necessary to retain bit-exact arithmetic. These are NCU diagnostics with clock/cache control disabled, not E2E measurements.

The final matched Torch 2.13 full-stage captures contain two denoising steps each. Overlapping image-encoding GPU annotations are unioned before counting each kernel once; no boundary-crossing kernels were found.

| Rank-0 stage, two-step request | A kernels → B kernels | A cumulative GPU time → B |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Denoising | 7,113 → 5,673 | 1,233.223 → 1,221.776 ms |
| Image encoding | 11,042 → 5,778 | 190.449 → 164.337 ms |

Other stage kernel counts are unchanged. The vision reduction is 56 window-attention invocations × (96 − 2) = 5,264 launches. These short instrumented requests establish the changed paths; the full 50-step unprofiled ABBA establishes E2E.

[QKV microbenchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/qkv-microbenchmark.json), [SDPA microbenchmark](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/sdpa-microbenchmark.json), [NCU iterations](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/ncu-comparison.json), [paired profile and trace hashes](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/profile-comparison.json), [profile aggregation script](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/summarize_qwen_attention_profile.py).

### Reproduce

Run the same command on the stated baseline and candidate, in A-B-B-A order, with the same idle H200 and environment:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 sglang generate \
  --backend sglang --model-path Qwen/Qwen-Image-Edit \
  --revision ac7f9318f633fc4b5778c59367c8128225f1e3de \
  --num-gpus 1 --performance-mode auto --enable-torch-compile false \
  --quality lossless --warmup-mode request --width 1024 --height 1024 \
  --num-inference-steps 50 --guidance-scale 4 \
  --seed 42 --prompt 'Make the cat wear a red hat.' \
  --image-path https://github.com/lm-sys/lm-sys.github.io/releases/download/test/TI2I_Qwen_Image_Edit_Input.jpg \
  --save-output --output-path outputs/qwen-edit --perf-dump-path qwen-edit.perf.json
```

For high, change only `--quality high` in both arms and retain its quality caveat. Capture full stages in separate diagnostic requests with two inference steps, `--profile` and `--profile-all-stages`; exclude their wall times. Exact executed [QKV harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/bench_qwen_qkv_hopper_production.py) and [SDPA harness](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/bench_native_varlen_final.py) are included; their output directory and commit assertions record the original experiment.

Task-owned checkpoint caches on both H200 hosts were deleted after model validation: 57,722,203,391 and 57,722,164,005 logical bytes before cleanup, zero files/weights/bytes afterward. These are logical cache counts, not unique physical storage freed. [First ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/ion9-cache-cleanup.jsonl), [second ledger](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/ion8-cache-cleanup.jsonl), [independent zero-residual check](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/cleanup-verification.json), [media manifest](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/pr-media/diffusion-prs/qwen-edit-attention-h200/manifest.json).

## Checklist

- [x] Format code and pass pre-commit.
- [x] Extend registered tests and run focused H200/CPU checks.
- [x] Update kernel inventory documentation.
- [x] Provide accuracy, kernel, profile, E2E and actual output comparisons.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.
- [x] Existing [B200 kernel regression CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34296369242/job/102293942926): all 14 QKV epilogue tests pass on `b200-cirrascale1-0123`. [B200 diffusion CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/34296369242/job/102293942990) also passes.

title: [AMD] Load fused shared experts for Qwen4-Exp and Qwen3.5 MTP
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

`Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` loads with its shared experts uninitialized whenever shared-expert fusion is active. There are two independent instances of this, one in the main model and one in the MTP draft.

**Main model.** When fusion is enabled the model has no separate `mlp.shared_expert.*` parameters — the shared expert lives in routed slot `num_experts` of the fused MoE. The checkpoint still ships the tensors separately, and `Qwen4ExpForConditionalGeneration.load_weights` has no mapping for them, so every one is dropped with only a warning:

```
Parameter model.layers.18.mlp.shared_expert.down_proj.weight not found while loading Qwen4-Exp VL weights
```

144 warnings per TP rank (3 projections x 48 layers), 1152 across TP8. There is no error and no failed assertion: the server starts, reports ready, and generates fluent text with 48 layers of garbage shared-expert contribution.

**MTP draft.** `qwen3_5_mtp.py` rebinds `expert_params_mapping` to `fused_expert_params_mapping` permanently on the first fused tensor it sees, inside the stacked-params loop. This checkpoint interleaves the two forms — 49 fused `experts.gate_up_proj` tensors and 196 separate `mlp.shared_expert.*` tensors, with no per-expert `experts.N.gate_proj` — so every shared-expert tensor that follows a fused one looks up the wrong mapping and falls through:

```
Parameter model.layers.0.mlp.experts.512.gate_proj.weight not found in params_dict
```

ROCm images set `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` by default, so fusion is on out of the box and every ROCm run of this model hits both.

## Modifications

Both changes are the minimum needed to load the weights. Each was verified necessary by reverting it in isolation on an 8x MI355X host and re-measuring — see Accuracy Tests.

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen4_exp.py` (+26/-2)

- Discover `num_fused_shared_experts` from the built modules, and build `expert_params_mapping` with `num_experts + num_fused_shared_experts` so the mapping covers routed slot `num_experts`.
- Rewrite `mlp.shared_expert.` to `mlp.experts.{num_experts}.` before the stacked/expert loops, so the existing per-expert loader handles the tensor.

This reuses the idiom `qwen3_5.py` already applies to the identical problem rather than adding a second mechanism. `FusedMoE.make_expert_params_mapping(num_experts=513)` already emits exactly the entries needed:

```
('experts.w13_', 'experts.512.gate_proj.', 512, 'w1')
('experts.w2_',  'experts.512.down_proj.', 512, 'w2')
('experts.w13_', 'experts.512.up_proj.',   512, 'w3')
```

`qwen4_exp.py` already computed `is_fused_expert` per weight, so a rewritten `experts.512.gate_proj` name correctly selects the per-expert mapping rather than the fused one.

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_5_mtp.py` (+13/-8)

- Compute `is_fused_expert` per weight and select `current_expert_params_mapping` from it, instead of rebinding the shared `expert_params_mapping` local inside the stacked-params loop. Selecting a mapping for one weight no longer affects the next.

### Scope: both loaders gate on `_use_aiter`

Both shared-expert paths are gated on `_use_aiter` (`SGLANG_USE_AITER and is_hip()`), matching the gate `qwen3_5_mtp.py` already used. That keeps this PR provably free of CUDA impact: nothing today enables shared-expert fusion for Qwen3.5 / Qwen4-Exp on CUDA, since `enable_cuda_shared_expert_fusion` defaults to `False` in `qwen2_moe.py` and only `qwen3_next.py` passes `True`. On ROCm the gate is always true because the images ship `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`.

To be explicit about the tradeoff: `_use_aiter` is a proxy, and the precise predicate is `num_fused_shared_experts > 0` (derived from the built module), which is what `qwen2_moe.py` actually branches on. If someone later wires `enable_cuda_shared_expert_fusion=True` for these models the way `qwen3_next.py` does, both gates here will need to drop. That change belongs with whoever can validate the CUDA fusion path; this PR has no way to test it, so it keeps the blast radius at zero rather than making an unverifiable claim.

Measured both ways on the hardware below — gated and ungated are equivalent on ROCm (accept length 3.164 vs 3.157, inside run-to-run noise), so the gate costs nothing here.

## Accuracy Tests

8x MI355X (gfx950), released BF16 `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next` checkpoint, `--tp-size 8 --attention-backend aiter --page-size 32 --chunked-prefill-size 16384`, EAGLE MTP (3 steps, topk 1, 4 draft tokens), `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1` (the ROCm image default, so fusion is on). GSM8K, 200 examples.

Each row reverts one part of this PR and leaves the rest applied:

| Variant | Missing-weight warnings | GSM8K | Accept length |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| This PR | 0 | 0.980 | 3.164 |
| Revert the `qwen3_5_mtp.py` change | 24 (`experts.512.*` in the draft) | 0.975 | 3.067 |
| Revert both (main today) | 1152 (`mlp.shared_expert.*`) + 24 | not meaningful | not meaningful |

The MTP row is why that change is included: with the draft's shared experts dropped, accept length falls 3.1% (3.164 to 3.067) while GSM8K is unchanged. That is the expected signature — EAGLE verification against the target model keeps the output distribution correct no matter how bad the draft is, so a broken draft costs throughput, not accuracy. Nothing in an accuracy gate would catch it.

The last row cannot be scored meaningfully: dropped shared experts in the main model do not raise, they quietly degrade it, so 0 remaining warnings is the direct signal that the tensors now reach a parameter.

An 18k-token prompt retrieval check passes and the server stays healthy through the full eval.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Weight loading only, run once at startup, so there is no steady-state cost. The measurable effect is the MTP accept-length recovery in the table above (3.164 vs 3.067, +3.1%), which is a throughput gain in proportion. This PR measures 1608 tok/s output throughput on the GSM8K run; the reverted variant's throughput was not captured, so only the accept-length delta is quoted as evidence.

## Checklist

- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). Validated end to end against a served model, including the per-part ablations above. A CPU unit test over the name rewrite and mapping selection would be straightforward — happy to add one if reviewers want it.
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Feat] dcp: Support breakable prefill CUDA graphs under decode context parallelism
author: klshuster
body:
## Motivation

`--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` with `--dcp-size > 1` crashes during capture: the dummy extend batch has no `attn_dcp_metadata`, and the MLA extend path dereferences it in `all_gather_kv_cache_for_mla_extend`. The auto-disable rule only covers the default backend, so an explicit selection (as in the documented Kimi-K3 recipe) fails to boot, and DCP deployments have had to run prefill eagerly.

## Modifications

Breakable-graph break functions are replayed with their capture-time arguments, so per-batch state has to come from somewhere stable rather than the batch object passed at capture.

- `forward_mla.py`: the DCP extend KV assembly becomes an `eager_on_graph` break, `bcg_dcp_extend_kv_gather`. It reads the live batch from the forward context, like the attention break. With no cached prefix there is nothing to gather from other ranks, so it copies the local `k_nope` / `k_pe` into the gather buffer and skips the collective; prefix hits keep the existing all-gather.
- `prefill_cuda_graph_runner.py`: capture plans DCP metadata for its zero-prefix batch and keeps that bucket-sized gather buffer per shape. Replay plans the live batch's indices eagerly and points them at the captured buffer.
- Under DCP only fresh prefills replay. Prefix-hit extends, including chunked-prefill continuations, fall back to eager via `can_replay_locally`. Replaying prefix hits is a follow-up.
- The auto-disable rule is unchanged; the feature is reached by selecting `breakable` explicitly.

Tests: `test_prefill_cuda_graph_dcp.py` covers the admission gate, the replay buffer contract and the live-batch gather (all fail on `main`). The Kimi-Linear cutedsl + DCP e2e test gains a breakable-prefill variant, which could not boot before.

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3, `cutedsl_mla`, `--dcp-size 8`, 2 nodes, against the same server with prefill graphs disabled. Graph replay is deterministic (repeated fresh prefills are bitwise identical), graph-vs-eager logprob differences are no larger than the eager server's own batch-composition variation, and standard accuracy evals plus a paired agentic coding benchmark match the disabled baseline. Every fresh prefill replayed and every prefix hit went eager in the logs. Also checked with draft-model speculative decoding and at a 1M-token context.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Prefill TTFT, sequential, one output token, median ms:

| prompt tokens | 22 | 301 | 1142 | 1996 | 4437 (above largest bucket) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| disabled | 404 | 454 | 461 | 486 | 460 |
| breakable | 133 | 155 | 171 | 177 | 460 |

Short-prompt rolling benchmark: TPOT 38.0 -> 33.6 ms, output throughput +14%, decode throughput unchanged. Capture: 42 buckets in ~70 s, 3.6–4.8 GB per GPU.

## Summary

Update HiCache KV offloading defaults and quick-reduce quantization for the Qwen3.5-397B-A17B MXFP4 MI355X deployment, and bump the MI355X Docker image.

Supersedes #35879 (closed due to branch recreation during conflict resolution).

Aligned with:

title: Add triton autotune on the Mamba2 SSD kernels
author: elvischenv
body: ## Motivation The Mamba2 SSD Triton kernels were adapted from vLLM without their `@triton.autotune` decorators: sglang's original import (#10988) carried them commented out, and #10909 deleted the commented blocks while re-syncing the ops. The launchers still size their grids from `META["BLOCK_SIZE_*"]`, so every kernel silently ran at its signature default of `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` -- a 10x+ loss on the prefill kernels. Upstream vLLM has these decorators live today. ## Modifications - Restore `@triton.autotune` on `ssd_bmm`, `ssd_chunk_scan`, `ssd_chunk_state` and `ssd_state_passing`. The config lists and keys are verbatim from current `vllm/model_executor/layers/mamba/ops/`, so these blocks stay diffable on the next upstream sync. - `_chunk_state_varlen_kernel` is sglang-only -- vLLM replaced it with `gather_initial_states.py` driven by `cu_chunk_seqlens` -- so it reuses the `_chunk_state_fwd_kernel` list (same tile-shape family). - Add `**autotune_cache_kwargs` (the existing sglang FLA idiom, `kernels/ops/attention/fla/utils.py`) so a tuning result survives process restarts instead of being re-measured on every server launch. - Add `prune_configs_by` / `prune_oversized_tiles`, which caps each `BLOCK_SIZE_*` at `next_power_of_2` of the dimension it tiles. A tile wider than its dimension computes a fully masked remainder over the same grid, so it is dominated. This is the fix for the `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` CI timeout -- see below. - Fix `bench_one_batch` on Mamba models: `selective_state_update` dispatches through a process-global backend that only the Scheduler installs, so every Mamba model died during decode CUDA-graph capture inside `load_model`. It is now initialized from a helper shared by `latency_test` and `correctness_test`, so `--correctness-test` is covered too. ## CI cost The 30-minute timeout on the previous run was real and caused by this PR. Autotuning is per distinct key, and `test_mamba_ssm_ssd.py` spans many: `_chunk_scan_fwd_kernel` alone sees ~22 keys over the CI-reduced matrix (Triton folds the tensor dtypes into the key on top of `chunk_size`/`hdim`/`dstate`), at 23 configs each -- ~500 compile+bench cycles for one kernel, and ~4x that across all six. A persistent cache does not help here, since the cold pytest process never gets a hit. The prune collapses the small CI shapes to a handful of configs each (`hdim=5, dstate=5, chunk_size=16` -> 1 config; `hdim=32, dstate=32, chunk_size=8` -> 1), without touching the test matrix. ## Accuracy Tests Autotuning selects `BLOCK_SIZE_K`, which sets the K-split of the fp32 `tl.dot` accumulation, so output is **not** bit-identical to the `BLOCK_SIZE_* = 16` defaults. `lm_eval` GSM8K (5-shot), Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4, TP4: | | main | + autotune | | --- | ---: | ---: | | flexible-extract | 0.9401 ± 0.0065 | 0.9409 ± 0.0065 | | strict-match | 0.9378 ± 0.0067 | 0.9393 ± 0.0066 | ## Speed Tests and Profiling **End-to-end serving**, Nemotron-3-Ultra-550B-A55B-NVFP4 on GB300 TP4, ISL 8192 / OSL 1024: | Concurrency | Total tok/s (main) | Total tok/s (+autotune) | Speedup | tok/s/user (main) | tok/s/user (+autotune) | Speedup | | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 16 | 10,981 | 13,264 | **1.21x** | 104.9 | 110.2 | **1.05x** | | 32 | 15,728 | 17,751 | **1.13x** | 78.0 | 85.4 | **1.10x** | | 64 | 20,772 | 23,662 | **1.14x** | 53.0 | 59.5 | **1.12x** | | 128 | 24,877 | 29,892 | **1.20x** | 33.9 | 39.0 | **1.15x** | | 256 | 28,190 | 35,747 | **1.27x** | 20.0 | 24.3 | **1.22x** | | 512 | 29,558 | 37,776 | **1.28x** | 16.8 | 20.5 | **1.22x** | ## Checklist - title: [AMD] [GLM-5.3-Flash] Enable FP8 and MXFP4 serving on gfx950
author: hdt98
body:
## Motivation Serve the official GLM-5.3-Flash FP8 checkpoint and [`OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4`](https://huggingface.co/OneNexus/GLM-5.3-Flash-MXFP4) on MI355X (gfx950) at full speed and correct output. The target stack is zero-RoPE sparse attention, FP8 KV cache, and graph-enabled EAGLE 5/1/6. `main` now includes all ten Day-0 enablement PRs (#38545, #38546, #38547, #39317, #39338, #39339, #39340, #39341, #39778, #39779). This PR adds the remaining correctness fixes and optimizations for serving Flash on gfx950. On the same four MI355X GPUs and AgentX replay, it measures **+14.3%** geomean output throughput over `main` at c1–c32, with higher P90 interactivity at every rung. At c48, `main` falls off the frontier, while this PR holds it. The four CI and test-hygiene fixes that used to be here now live in #40721. ## What changed Runtime paths are relative to `python/sglang/`; tests are excluded. | Area | Kind | Change | Files | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | K-pool top-k | Correctness (CUDA and HIP) | A threshold bin holding more than 4,096 candidates is rescanned with unique score/index keys, so ties or late higher scores are never clipped. The ordinary fast path is unchanged. HIP sets the dynamic shared-memory attribute. | `kernels/jit/csrc/dsa/kpool_topk_transform.cuh` | | K-pool scoring memory | Correctness · HIP | The logits row budget counts AITER's 256-column row padding, so a chunk cannot exceed AITER's 2 GiB limit, and page indices are promoted to int64 before offsetting. | `srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_indexer_kpool.py`
`srt/layers/attention/dsa/kpool_fp8_index.py` | | Unfused top-k memory | Correctness · all backends | Ragged batches above 4,096 rows run in 4,096-row chunks (`_TOPK_ROW_CHUNK`). Each row's top-k depends only on that row, so results are identical on every backend; only the scratch peak changes. | `srt/layers/attention/dsa/dsa_topk_backend.py` | | Graph variants | Correctness / capture cost | K-pool has no dense-skip path, so it is captured once instead of as a dense/sparse pair. Without a host length mirror, sparse is chosen without a device sync. | `srt/layers/attention/graph_variants.py` | | Attention backend lookup | Correctness | GLM-5.3-Flash wraps DSA inside the hybrid KDA backend, so on `main` the FP8 MHA prefix read takes the outer backend and fails with `forward_metadata is None` on the first image request (reproduced on MI355X). `resolve_attn_backend` now unwraps to the full-attention child. AITER extend also prefers the per-batch `qo_indptr`. | `srt/models/deepseek_common/attention_forward_methods/forward_mha.py`
`srt/layers/attention/aiter_backend.py` | | Visible-prefix / Mamba ownership | Correctness | A verify step can commit past the stop token; only client-visible tokens are cached. The other ping-pong slot's length is tracked, so a shorter key donates the state that actually matches it. Freed rows can no longer scatter into a reused slot. | `srt/managers/schedule_batch.py`
`srt/managers/scheduler_components/batch_result_processor.py`
`srt/mem_cache/{base_prefix_cache,common,memory_pool}.py`
`srt/mem_cache/unified_cache/components/mamba.py` | | Mamba chunk fill | Correctness | Exact chunk fill is disabled for Mamba caches, because checkpoints only land on page-aligned chunk ends. | `srt/managers/schedule_policy.py` | | Graph read fences | Correctness | Without an in-graph marker (HIP), the read-done event is published after replay rather than before. Draft extend follows the backend's declared read end. | `srt/model_executor/runner/decode_cuda_graph_runner.py`
`srt/speculative/eagle_draft_extend_cuda_graph_runner.py` | | EAGLE draft on ROCm | Optimization · measured | ROCm enables rejection sampling (#37134), but verify takes argmax for all-greedy batches and never reads the draft distribution. The draft now skips the full-vocab softmax, Gumbel sample and probs stack for those batches and captures a matching greedy graph variant. | `srt/speculative/eagle_worker_v2.py`
`srt/speculative/eagle_draft_cuda_graph_runner.py` | | KDA fused verify | Correctness + optimization · HIP only | On top of #39524: separately rounded conv products (bit-exact with the reference on gfx950), a one-wave default, and BV16 for measured GLM shapes. The HIP gate keys on gfx950, bf16 QKV, fp32 conv weights, T ∈ {6, 8}, and batch 1–16. | `kernels/ops/attention/fla/fused_kda_conv_recurrent_verify.py`
`srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py` | | Chat serving | Optimization / correctness | Send the token ids already rendered instead of re-tokenizing long text-only prompts. Apply the GLM47 full-assistant grammar only when tools are present, since its terminal state ends requests even under `ignore_eos`. | `srt/entrypoints/openai/serving_chat.py` | | Quark loading | Correctness | Block-FP8 is claimed only when the activation grouping matches the weight block. `ignore` is materialized once. Quark `weight_scale` maps to `weight_scale_inv` only when the name is missing. | `srt/layers/quantization/quark/{quark,utils}.py`
`srt/models/glm5_next.py` | | Vision downsample | Optimization · measured | The non-overlapping 2×2 merge uses `Conv2dLayer`'s unfold + linear path, which avoids the MIOpen search. | `srt/models/glm5_next.py` | | Small ROCm fixes | Correctness | `tree_speculative_sampling_target_only` accepts any GPU device (`kDLGPU`), and a comment in the AITER MoE runner is corrected. | `kernels/jit/csrc/speculative/sampling.cuh`
`srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/aiter.py` | | MI355X cookbook | Docs | FP8 and MXFP4 on the GLM-5.3-Flash selector, with TP4/EP4 commands and the ROCm runtime environment used for the measurements below. | `docs/cookbook/autoregressive/GLM/GLM-5.3-Flash.mdx`
`docs/src/snippets/configs/zai-org/glm-5.3-flash.jsx`
`docs/src/snippets/_playground.jsx` | Footprint against `main`: 26 production files (+361 / −80), 14 test files (+563 / −21), 3 docs files (+179 / −26). ## Serving performance Setup: four MI355X VFs, TP4/EP4, FP8 E4M3 KV, EAGLE 5/1/6, 393-entry AgentX corpus, 900 s per rung, image `lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260918`. The client and server are pinned to the same NUMA placement, and `main` and this PR ran back to back on the same GPUs.

The single fused kernel with BV4 tiles is slower (**41.7 μs**), because it repeats the Q/K convolution across 32 value tiles. title: [dsv4.1] Exact bf16 consumer top-k adapted from DeepSelect
author: DarkSharpness
body:
## Motivation

The DeepSeek-V4.1 two-level sparse indexer's consumer step picks the top-512 of up to 16384 bf16 sparse logits per row and writes them through the per-row physical block table (`topk_transform_bf16_small`). The kernel behind it was a placeholder: a single 13-bit fp16-derived histogram (approximate at the selection boundary), 1024 threads x 16 elements, and untuned.

## Modifications

Replace it with an exact selection **adapted from [DeepSelect](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/DeepSelect)**. DeepSelect's kernel starts by selecting the top-k of a 32 KiB "init window" that lives entirely in registers; our consumer rows (<= 16384 bf16) are exactly that window, so our kernel agent took that part of the algorithm, dropped the TMA/streaming machinery around it, rewrote it in plain SIMT and specialised it for 16384-wide rows at k = 512. The result was then reviewed and wired into the existing host API here.

What is kept from DeepSelect:
- two radix passes on the raw bf16 bytes: a 256-bin histogram of the high byte, then of the low byte among the elements sharing the pivot's high byte, which locates the k-th largest value exactly;
- the "distorted" value order (`x ^ (x < 0 ? 0xFFFF : 0x8000)`: negatives reversed and below positives, -0 below +0), applied once per lane while walking the histogram instead of once per element;
- the packed hit test: `__hgt2_mask` / `__heq2_mask` on bf16x2, `prmt` + `dp4a` to turn the flags into one bit per element, one warp prefix plus one shared atomic per warp for the block-wide (gt, eq) prefix, and an equal quota so exactly k elements are taken.

What is specific to this port:
- one CTA of 512 threads per row, each thread keeping a contiguous slice of up to 32 scores (4 x 16 B vectors) in registers for the whole kernel; 40 registers per thread, 3 CTAs per SM, no spills;
- the negative half of the high-byte histogram is offset by 16 words so that +x and -x with the same exponent (the common case for centred scores) do not hit the same smem bank on every atomic;
- the partial last vector of a row is padded with a negative NaN, which sits below -inf in the distorted order and fails every ordered compare, so it is never counted nor selected;
- a -0 pivot is handled separately (the float census sees +0 == -0 while the histogram ranked them apart);
- the selected indices are staged in shared memory (a union with the histograms, 9 KiB in total) and written with one coalesced page-transformed copy.

The host API is unchanged: per-row `seq_lens` (prefetched ahead of the PDL wait, like the streaming top-k), the fused page-table transform, `-1` past `min(k, seq_len)`. `k` is now at most 2048 (was 4096). NaN scores are never selected (no ordered compare matches them): a row with n positive NaNs yields its top (k - n) real scores and `-1` in the remaining slots, derived from the census totals so nothing reads stale shared memory; a negative NaN orders below `-inf` and is simply never picked.

## Accuracy

`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_topk_bf16.py` (100 cases): the existing configurations plus odd row widths (partial last vector), heavy ties / constant / all `-inf` rows, signed zeros around the pivot, denormals and full-range bf16 bit patterns, and rows with positive / negative NaNs below and above k. Every case checks the selected values as a multiset against `torch.topk` (elements of equal value may swap) and the page transform through the inverse table. `test/registered/attention/unittests/dsv4/test_dsv41_sparse_indexer.py` passes.

## Performance

B200, `marker.do_bench` (CUDA graph, L2-rotated inputs), k = 512, page transform included, random bf16 scores, permuted block table. Old kernel -> this PR, in us:

| valid len | rows = 1 | rows = 32 | rows = 128 | rows = 512 |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 16384 | 5.24 -> 4.93 | 5.51 -> 5.18 | 7.09 -> 6.58 | 15.94 -> 12.38 |
| 9000 | 4.36 -> 4.06 | 4.71 -> 4.36 | 5.08 -> 5.07 | 13.03 -> 9.03 |
| 4096 | 3.97 -> 3.49 | 4.32 -> 3.81 | 4.74 -> 4.32 | 10.83 -> 7.36 |

Beyond ~450 rows the GPU is saturated (3 CTAs/SM) and time is linear in rows: 36 us at 2048 rows and 134 us at 8192 rows for full-width rows.

k = 2048 stays supported but is not the target shape: it is 10-15% slower than the old kernel at small batch (the epilogue runs on 512 threads instead of 1024) and 10% faster at 512 rows.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Code Formatting with Pre-Commit](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-formatting-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests as outlined in the [Running Unit Tests](https://docs.sglang.ai/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#running-unit-tests-adding-to-ci).
- [x] Update documentation / docstrings as needed.
