title: [Kernel] Coalesce the KDA CuTe DSL decode state transpose: ~3x faster, bit-identical
author: yekerr
body:
## Motivation

The CuTe DSL KDA decode kernels (`kda_kernel_small_batch`, `kda_kernel_small_batch_varlen`,
`kda_kernel_large_batch`, `kda_kernel_large_batch_varlen` in
`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/cutedsl_kda.py`) stage the recurrent state through shared
memory with a `global (V, K) <-> shared (K, V)` transpose, once to load the state and once to write it
back. The thread -> element mapping for that transpose uses **V as the fast-varying index**:

```python
k_load = flat_idx // TILE_V
v_load = flat_idx % TILE_V
```

But the state tensor is `(pool_size, HV, V, K)` with **K contiguous** and V strided by
`K * sizeof(fp32) = 512 B`. So the 32 lanes of a warp hit 32 *different* 32-byte sectors and use
4 bytes out of each one — roughly 28 sectors per request where ~4 is the ideal for 32 x 4 B. The
same strided pattern is repeated on the write-back. Since the decode step is state-bandwidth-bound
(every token reads and writes the full fp32 `[HV, V, K]` state), this dominates kernel time.

## Modifications

Swap the two index expressions in each of the 8 transpose sites (one load pair + one write-back pair
per kernel variant) so that **K is the fast-varying index**:

```diff
-                    k_load = flat_idx // TILE_V
-                    v_load = flat_idx % TILE_V
+                    k_load = flat_idx % TILE_K
+                    v_load = flat_idx // TILE_K
```

(`TILE_V_SMALL` -> `TILE_K` in the two small-batch kernels, `TILE_V` -> `TILE_K` in the two
large-batch kernels; the `k_write` / `v_write` pairs change identically.)

`flat_idx` ranges over exactly `[0, TILE_K * TILE_V)` in every loop, so both the old and the new
expression are bijections onto the same `(k, v)` tile: the same elements land in the same shared-memory
slots, the existing `if k_load < TILE_K` guards and `v_global < v.shape[3]` bounds checks are
untouched, and no barrier, loop trip count or arithmetic order changes. Consequently the kernel's
**output tensor and the in-place fp32 state update are bit-identical** before and after (verified
below). Nothing else in the file is modified (16 lines, 8 two-line pairs).

Now a warp's 32 lanes read/write 32 consecutive fp32 along K = 128 contiguous bytes = 4 sectors.

### Known tradeoff (shared memory)

The new mapping trades a global-memory win for a shared-memory regression in the transpose itself.
`TILE_V_PADDED = 36` was chosen so the *compute* loop is bank-conflict-free: there a warp covers
`8 k x 4 v` (`k_local = in_warp_tid // V_PER_WARP`, `v_local = in_warp_tid % V_PER_WARP`), and
bank `(36*k + v) % 32 = (4*k + v) % 32` hits 32 distinct banks. In the transpose, however, the new
mapping walks 32 consecutive `k` at fixed `v`, and `(4*k + v) % 32` takes only 8 distinct values —
a 4-way bank conflict on the staging loads/stores. Nsight Compute confirms it (b=32, large-batch
kernel): shared-load bank conflicts 29.6 K -> 4.74 M, shared-store 5.7 K -> 4.74 M, LSU shared
wavefronts 10.9 M -> 15.6 M (ld) and 3.3 M -> 8.0 M (st). The kernel is still ~3x faster end to end,
which bounds the cost of the shared side.

No single padding constant fixes both patterns: the transpose wants `gcd(P, 32) = 1` (odd `P`), the
compute loop wants `P == 4 (mod 32)`. The remaining lever is a swizzled shared-memory layout or a
128-bit vectorized load of 4 consecutive `k` per thread — not a padding tweak. Left as a follow-up to
keep this PR a pure, bit-identical index swap.

## Accuracy Tests

Because the change is a permutation of the thread -> element assignment with no arithmetic change,
the expected result is bit-exactness, and that is what is observed.

A standalone check ran `cutedsl_fused_sigmoid_gating_kda_update` on the stock and patched kernel
across 9 cases covering all four kernel variants, three input classes, and the `pool_idx < 0` pad
path, hashing (sha256) the raw bytes of the bf16 output and of the updated fp32 state, and also
comparing both arms to an independent from-scratch fp32 PyTorch reference of the recurrent step
(`H=HV=96`, `K=128`, non-zero initial state so the load half of the transpose is exercised):

| case | kernel variant | inputs | out sha256 equal | state sha256 equal | rel err vs fp32 ref (out / state) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| b=32,  dv=128 | dense large-batch | randn | yes | yes | 3.1e-3 / 6.6e-4 |
| b=128, dv=128 | dense large-batch | randn | yes | yes | 2.9e-3 / 6.3e-4 |
| b=32,  dv=256 | dense large-batch | randn | yes | yes | 2.3e-3 / 6.7e-4 |
| b=16,  dv=128 | dense small-batch | randn | yes | yes | 3.8e-3 / 6.3e-4 |
| b=64,  dv=128 | varlen large-batch | randn | yes | yes | 2.9e-3 / 6.6e-4 |
| b=8,   dv=128 | varlen small-batch | randn | yes | yes | 2.3e-3 / 6.7e-4 |
| b=32,  dv=128 | dense large-batch | all zeros | yes | yes | 0 / 1.0e-3 |
| b=32,  dv=128 | dense large-batch | range stress (q, k magnitude ~64; v ~256; g from -1e-6 to -40; beta from 1e-6 to 1-1e-6) | yes | yes | 3.2e-3 / 1.6e-6 |
| b=32,  dv=128 | dense large-batch | randn + every 7th `pool_idx = -1` | yes | yes | 2.8e-3 / 5.9e-4 |

All 9 cases: output **and** state bit-identical stock vs patched; reference errors are identical on
both arms (bf16 output rounding), all values finite.

Existing CI coverage of this kernel is thinner than the file name suggests — no registered test calls
`cutedsl_fused_sigmoid_gating_kda_update`:

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_fused_decode.py` exercises the Triton `fla.fused_recurrent` decode path, not this kernel;
- `test/registered/attention/test_kda_prefill_cutedsl.py` covers the CuTe DSL *prefill* kernel (4-gpu-b200 suite);
- the GDN sibling `test_cutedsl_gdn.py` currently has its precision test skipped.

I have not run the sglang test suite locally. If maintainers want in-tree coverage for the decode kernel, I can add
`test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_cutedsl_kda.py` (CuTe DSL decode vs. the Triton `fused_sigmoid_gating_recurrent`
reference, modeled on `test_cutedsl_gdn.py`) to this PR or as a follow-up.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel-only timing via CUPTI (10 warmup + 10 timed launches per config), bf16, `dqk = dv = 128`,
`qo_len = 1`, recurrent decode step, single-GPU. `h = 96` (Kimi-K3). All rows are within-box A/B comparisons with **unlocked SM clocks**; the A/B/A protocol
(stock -> patched -> stock) bounds the clock/thermal noise (A-vs-A drift <= 0.03 % on every row,
orders of magnitude below the effect).

The numbers come from a standalone CUPTI harness rather than the in-tree
`benchmark/bench_linear_attention/bench_cutedsl_kda_decode.py` (#21203, Triton vs. CuTe DSL); I can append
that script's stock-vs-patched output on request.

### NVIDIA B200 PCIe

`h = 96`, `dv = 128`; median of 3 per phase.

| batch | stock (us) | patched (us) | delta | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 32  | 476.5  | 152.0  | -68.1 % | 3.14x |
| 128 | 1817.7 | 584.5  | -67.9 % | 3.11x |
| 512 | 7171.1 | 2309.5 | -67.8 % | 3.11x |

A wider sweep on the same B200 (`b in {1, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 512} x dv in {128, 256, 512}`, both
dense kernel variants) showed a consistent ~-67.8 %.

Only the two **dense** variants are exercised by these shapes (b >= 32 -> `kda_kernel_large_batch`;
the b=16 accuracy case -> `kda_kernel_small_batch`). The two **varlen** variants are covered by the
bit-exactness check above but were not timed; the same 8-lane swap applies to them and the access
pattern is identical.

### Mechanism (Nsight Compute)

B200, `b = 32`, `h = 96`, `kda_kernel_large_batch`, one profiled launch, `--cache-control all`.

| metric | stock | patched |
|---|---|---|
| global load sectors / request (`l1tex__average_t_sectors_per_request_pipe_lsu_mem_global_op_ld`) | 28.39 | 3.68 |
| global store sectors / request (`..._op_st`) | 30.18 | 3.82 |
| L1TEX sectors total (`l1tex__t_sectors.sum`) | 101.0 M | 12.9 M (7.8x fewer) |
| L1TEX throughput (% peak) | 83.75 | 65.79 |
| long-scoreboard stalls / issue | 17.48 | 4.10 |
| DRAM bytes read (`dram__bytes_read.sum`) | 204,564,736 | 204,542,208 (unchanged) |
| DRAM throughput (% peak) | 9.54 | 29.83 |
| registers / thread | 128 | 124 |
| kernel duration | 480.9 us | 151.7 us |

DRAM traffic is unchanged: the kernel already moved exactly the bytes the state-update model
predicts, it was just delivering them through ~8x more L1 sectors than necessary. The predicted
mechanism (sectors/request collapse, L1TEX pressure drops, DRAM bytes flat, DRAM utilization rises
toward the bandwidth roof) is what moved.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit). (`ruff format --check`, `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037`, `isort --check-only` and `codespell` at the pre-commit-pinned versions (ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, codespell 2.4.1) report no changes; `git diff --check` clean.)
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests). (No new test in this revision; see Accuracy Tests for the current coverage gap of the CuTe DSL decode kernel. I can add `test_cutedsl_kda.py` on request.)
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). (N/A — kernel-internal change.)
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: Skip fully-masked KV tiles in sliding-window extend attention
author: jiaqiang-dot-liu
body:
## Motivation

On a sliding-window layer, the stage-2 loop in `_fwd_kernel` sweeps the extend KV from 0:

```python
for start_n in range(0, extend_end, BLOCK_N):
```

The window mask inside that loop keeps `(q, kv)` only when `q <= kv + SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE`, so every tile lying entirely below `cur_block_m * BLOCK_M - SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE` is fully masked and contributes nothing.

Those tiles do not read K/V and do not run the dot — `SKIP_TILE` already guards that. What they still pay, once per tile, is the cost of establishing that they contribute nothing: building `final_mask` (the causal compare, the window compare, the `&`), and then the `[BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N]` cross-wave `tl.max` reduction that computes `SKIP_TILE` itself.

On a long extend with a small window that is the majority of the loop. At `extend_len = 8192` and `W = 127`, the last M block's floor sits at roughly `8192 - 127`, so almost every iteration is spent proving that the tile is empty.

### Where this kernel runs by default

The Triton backend is the default attention backend, without any flag, for:

- **Gemma 4** (`Gemma4ForConditionalGeneration`): its model override selects `triton` whenever `--attention-backend` is unset, on ROCm and on CUDA other than SM100 (which gets `trtllm_mha`). The server logs `Use triton as default attention backend for Gemma4`. 25 of the 30 layers of `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it` are sliding-window layers (`W = 1024`, `head_dim = 256`).
- **OLMo 3** (served as `Olmo2ForCausalLM`) and **EXAONE 4.0** checkpoints with a sliding-window pattern (e.g. `EXAONE-4.0-32B`): `triton` by default on ROCm and on CUDA below SM80.

It also runs for any sliding-window model served with `--attention-backend triton`.

## Modifications

Start the loop at the `BLOCK_N`-aligned tile that contains the window floor:

```python
extend_start = 0
if SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE > 0:
    extend_start = (
        tl.maximum(cur_block_m * BLOCK_M - SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE, 0) // BLOCK_N
    ) * BLOCK_N
for start_n in range(extend_start, extend_end, BLOCK_N):
```

The bound is derived from the mask predicate rather than estimated. The kernel returns early when `cur_block_m * BLOCK_M >= cur_seq_len_extend`, so `offs_m = 0` is always a live row and the smallest query index in the block is exactly `m0 = cur_block_m * BLOCK_M`. A skipped tile satisfies `start_n + BLOCK_N <= floor_aligned <= m0 - W`, hence its largest key index `start_n + BLOCK_N - 1 < m0 - W`, so the window mask is false for every one of its elements.

It is also tight at tile granularity: the preceding tile would need `floor_aligned >= m0 - W + 1` to hold a surviving element, which contradicts `floor_aligned <= m0 - W`. Nothing that can contribute is skipped, for any `BLOCK_M`/`BLOCK_N`.

`SLIDING_WINDOW_SIZE` is a `tl.constexpr`, so a full-attention layer loses the branch at trace time and its loop is unchanged. `extend_start` is a multiple of `BLOCK_N`, so `tl.multiple_of(start_n, BLOCK_N)` stays valid. A custom mask or the non-causal path only adds conjuncts, which narrow the mask further, so the bound remains sound there. Under the HIP compact grid `cur_block_m` is still the per-sequence tile index, so the derivation is unaffected.

`test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/test_triton.py` gains three cases with extend lengths above `BLOCK_M` and windows below it — no prefix; a prefix with a window that is not a tile multiple; a window landing exactly on a tile boundary — so some query tile starts past the window and the bound takes effect. Every pre-existing SWA extend case keeps the extend length under `BLOCK_M`, where the loop always starts at tile 0.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X (gfx950, 256 CU), ROCm 7.2.0, torch 2.9.1, Triton 3.7.0. sglang `main` @ `7ff3a11284` with `sglang-kernel` 0.4.9 built from the same tree and transformers 5.19.0.

**Unit tests.** `test/registered/attention/unittests/swa/test_triton.py` and `.../dense/test_triton.py`: 15 passed, 2 skipped, 58 subtests passed.

**Kernel output is bitwise identical.** 21 configurations (12 sliding-window, 4 full-attention, 5 where the bound never fires) at `B=32, H_Q=64, H_KV=8, D=128`, bf16, causal. Each run hashes its inputs as well as `o_extend`, so the output comparison is only accepted when the inputs provably matched: **21/21 inputs identical, 21/21 outputs bitwise identical.**

**End to end, `gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, default server args** (no `--attention-backend`; the server resolves `triton`):

- Greedy parity: 32 chat requests sent one at a time to a `main` server and a server with this PR, prompts of 3,968–18,164 tokens (all longer than the 1024-token window, so the bound fires), 128 output tokens, temperature 0. **Outputs identical: 32/32.**
- GSM8K, `python -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k` (chat API, 5-shot, greedy), all 1319 questions, two runs per server:

| | Run 1 | Run 2 |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 0.960 | 0.959 |
| This PR | 0.954 | 0.956 |

The per-question standard deviation is 0.20, so the standard error of one run is about 0.0055 and the gap is within run-to-run noise. Concurrent batches change the numerics of other kernels between runs; the parity check above runs one request at a time and shows identical outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Kernel

`triton.testing.do_bench(warmup=100ms, rep=500ms, return_mode="median")`, minimum over 7 repetitions, one idle GPU. Inputs come from `_build_batch` in `benchmark/kernels/sliding_window_attention_triton/bench_triton_swa_kernel.py`; `extend_attention_fwd` is called the way `triton_backend` calls it, including `extend_seq_lens_cpu`, so the HIP compact ragged grid is exercised. (That file's own `_run_triton` predates the `k_scale`/`v_scale` parameters, and `sglang.benchmark.bench_utils` imports `flashinfer`, which has no ROCm build.) The baseline was measured before and after this PR; **maximum run-to-run drift was 0.30%**.

| N_CTX | window | `main` (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 | 127 | 16.8079 | 10.2546 | **−39.0%** |
| 8192 | 256 | 17.8121 | 11.8463 | **−33.5%** |
| 8192 | 512 | 19.8016 | 14.9416 | **−24.5%** |
| 4096 | 127 | 6.0625 | 4.4068 | −27.3% |
| 4096 | 256 | 6.5597 | 5.1879 | −20.9% |
| 4096 | 512 | 7.6096 | 6.6472 | −12.6% |
| 2048 | 127 | 2.0704 | 1.7548 | −15.2% |
| 2048 | 256 | 2.3996 | 2.1685 | −9.6% |
| 2048 | 512 | 2.9883 | 2.8848 | −3.5% |
| 1024 | 127 | 0.7139 | 0.6697 | −6.2% |
| 1024 | 256 | 0.8551 | 0.8332 | −2.6% |
| 1024 | 512 | 1.0639 | 1.0535 | −1.0% |

The gain tracks the fraction of the loop below the floor: it grows with sequence length and shrinks with the window.

**Full-attention control.** At `sliding_window_size = -1` the branch is constexpr-eliminated:

| N_CTX | `main` (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 0.6606 | 0.6597 | −0.1% |
| 2048 | 2.4420 | 2.4376 | −0.2% |
| 4096 | 8.1296 | 8.1287 | −0.0% |
| 8192 | 22.9057 | 22.9425 | +0.2% |

All within drift. Full-attention models and the global-attention layers of hybrid models are unaffected.

**Where the bound never fires.** A sliding-window layer whose every M block satisfies `m0 <= W`: `extend_start` evaluates to 0, the trip count is unchanged, and the computation still runs. `_build_batch` draws extend lengths from `randint(1, N_CTX // 2)`, so `W >= N_CTX / 2` makes the bound inert (`max_len_extend <= W` checked per configuration). Drift 0.47%.

| N_CTX | window | max_len_extend | `main` (ms) | This PR (ms) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1024 | 1024 | 466 | 1.1159 | 1.1043 | −1.0% |
| 1024 | 2048 | 466 | 1.1189 | 1.1059 | −1.2% |
| 2048 | 2048 | 913 | 4.3393 | 4.2786 | −1.4% |
| 4096 | 4096 | 1884 | 14.9175 | 14.6701 | −1.7% |
| 8192 | 8192 | 4072 | 42.4523 | 41.9583 | −1.2% |

No configuration regresses. The small consistent gain is above drift, but I do not have an explanation for it, so I am reporting it rather than claiming it.

**Register pressure.** Compiled AMDGCN at `N_CTX=8192, W=127`:

```
sgpr_count:        106 -> 106
vgpr_count:        204 -> 204
sgpr_spill_count:   76 ->  80
vgpr_spill_count:    0 ->   0
shared:          16384 -> 16384
```

Four more SGPR spills. They do not show up in any measurement here, but I would rather flag them than assert the bound is free.

### End to end: prefill latency

`gemma-4-26B-A4B-it`, `python -m sglang.bench_one_batch` with default server args (the attention backend resolves to `triton`), `--output-len 4`, one MI355X. Minimum of 4 alternating runs per arm.

| Batch | Input len | `main` (s) | This PR (s) | Delta |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2048 | 0.0505 | 0.0496 | −1.7% |
| 1 | 8192 | 0.2064 | 0.1952 | −5.4% |
| 1 | 16384 | 0.5389 | 0.4952 | **−8.1%** |
| 1 | 32768 | 1.5027 | 1.3333 | **−11.3%** |
| 4 | 2048 | 0.1584 | 0.1571 | −0.8% |
| 4 | 8192 | 0.7822 | 0.7470 | −4.5% |
| 4 | 16384 | 1.9825 | 1.8370 | **−7.3%** |

This is whole-model prefill, MoE included, so the attention-only share of the gain is larger. The 2048 rows are small because the sliding layers have `head_dim = 256`, so `BLOCK_M = 128` here, and against a 1024 window the bound only starts skipping tiles at `cur_block_m >= 9`, i.e. for query tiles from token 1152 on.

### End to end: serving

Same model and default server args (`chunked_prefill_size = 16384`). `python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random-ids --random-range-ratio 1.0 --random-output-len 16`, 16 prompts at concurrency 1 and 32 at concurrency 4, prefix cache flushed before each run. The `main` and PR servers ran on two separate MI355X GPUs; the run was repeated with the GPU assignment swapped, and the table reports the mean of the two rounds.

| Input len | Concurrency | Median TTFT `main` (ms) | Median TTFT this PR (ms) | Delta | Input throughput |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8192 | 1 | 237.2 | 226.1 | −4.7% | +1.7% |
| 8192 | 4 | 897.9 | 841.6 | −6.3% | +6.6% |
| 16384 | 1 | 604.5 | 559.3 | −7.5% | +6.0% |
| 16384 | 4 | 1947.0 | 1890.9 | −2.9% | +7.8% |
| 32768 | 1 | 1378.3 | 1293.2 | −6.2% | +5.4% |
| 32768 | 4 | 4153.0 | 3872.2 | −6.8% | +6.9% |

A 32k prompt is prefilled in two 16k chunks here, so its gain is smaller than the single 32k extend in `bench_one_batch`. At concurrency 4 the median TTFT includes queueing and varies between rounds (−6.9% and +1.2% at 16k); input throughput is the steadier measure there.

### Reproduce

```bash
MODEL=google/gemma-4-26B-A4B-it

# prefill latency
python -m sglang.bench_one_batch --model-path $MODEL \
  --batch-size 1 4 --input-len 2048 8192 16384 --output-len 4

# serving
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path $MODEL --port 30000
python -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang --port 30000 --model $MODEL \
  --dataset-name random-ids --random-input-len 16384 --random-output-len 16 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts 16 --max-concurrency 1

# accuracy
python -m sglang.test.run_eval --port 30000 --eval-name gsm8k --num-examples 1319
```

Only MI355X was measured. The change is not ROCm-specific, so CUDA runs of the Triton backend take the same bound; their correctness is covered by the unit tests above in CI.

title: [NPU] Fuse MXFP4 W4A8 MoE gmm1 + swiglu + requant into one kernel
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

The unfused MXFP4 W4A8 MoE chain runs three kernels per MoE layer for the gate/up projection: gmm1, a separate swiglu activation kernel, and a dynamic MX requant. NPU A5 already provides `npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2`, which folds all three into a single aclnn kernel.

## Modifications

- `NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod` gains `apply_fused_gmm1_swiglu`, mirroring `NPUMXFP8MoEMethod`: same fused-kernel call shape, with the FP4 weight dtype and e8m0 weight/x scale dtypes. `pertoken_scale` handling matches the class's existing unfused `apply()` (quantize on the DeepEP bf16 path; pair-reshape when a scale is handed over).
- The Ascend MoE runner replaces the `NPUMXFP8MoEMethod` isinstance check with a `_uses_fused_gmm1(kernel)` probe, so both MXFP8 and MXFP4 W4A8 skip the separate activation step; the fail-loudly semantics of  `self.activation = None` are preserved.

## Accuracy Tests

```
echo performance | tee /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor
sysctl -w vm.swappiness=0
sysctl -w kernel.numa_balancing=0
sysctl -w kernel.sched_migration_cost_ns=50000

export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=lo
export HCCL_HOST_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=auto
export SGLANG_ALLOW_OVERWRITE_LONGER_CONTEXT_LEN=1

sglang serve \
        --model-path $MODEL_PATH \
        --served-model-name $MODEL_PATH \
        --trust-remote-code \
```

title: [ROCm] topk v2: split one long row across blocks, the CDNA cluster-path equivalent
author: EricKing626
body: ## Motivation By default, top-k v2 launches one block per row, so a long row is scanned by a single block **while most CUs sit idle**. On NVIDIA Hopper+, rows above a length threshold are split across a block cluster that shares DSMEM. CDNA has no clusters or DSMEM, so ROCm do not support top-k v2's cluster path. This happens often in reasoning-model decode: small batch, long context. This PR adds a row split to top-k v2 for ROCm. It uses two launches: one to build the histogram, one to select the top-k from it, and global memory takes the place of DSMEM. - **When it engages:** small batch, long context: `batch_size <= 64` and rows longer than a batch-dependent floor (40K at small batch). Everything else runs the existing path unchanged. - **Kernel speedup:** 1.8–3.0x at batch 1–8 with 128K+ context; 1.56x geomean across all gated shapes. - **End to end (GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4, MI355X):** - Single request: - TP4, batch 1 and 120K context, the decode top-k kernel is 2.07x faster and median ITL drops 3.8%. - TP4, batch 1 and 600K context, the decode top-k kernel is 6.42x faster and median ITL drops **18.7%**. - Agentic replay: compared with the packed-only top-k v2 baseline, adding row split improves: - P90 interactivity by **+11.3%** at TP8 and +3.5% at TP4. - Token TPUT per chip by +1.9% at TP8 and **+5.9%** at TP4. - Each figure is a geomean over c1/c4 for TP8 and over c4/c8/c12 for TP4. ## Modifications Originally, one block handles one row, so batch 8 over 128K uses only 8 blocks on a 256-CU GPU. CUDA splits a row across a cluster; CDNA has no clusters or DSMEM, so on ROCm this shape runs narrow. With this PR, each row is split across 8 blocks, so the same shape uses 64 blocks **Row length L**: how many KV positions each query token picks its top-k from, i.e. its context length. **Score rows R**: how many query tokens one top-k launch handles, one row each: - decode without MTP: **batch size** - decode with MTP: batch size × draft tokens, since the verify pass scores every draft token A long row is split across several blocks so a small R no longer leaves most CUs idle. Two launches, with the kernel boundary as the sync (no spinning): 1. `topk_split_hist`: each block builds the histogram of its slice of the row. 2. `topk_split_select`: each block finds the threshold from the merged histogram and writes its candidates; the last block resolves ties and applies the page-table transform. Each row is split `clamp(64 / R, 4, 32)` ways, aiming at about 64 blocks per launch: more than that and the cross-block cost, which grows with `R * split`, outweighs the shorter scan. The split turns on only when: - `R <= CU count / 4` (64 on MI355X), since past that even a 4-way split oversubscribes the GPU, and - L is long enough to pay for the extra launch: from 40K at small R, higher as R grows. ```math \mathrm{TopK}_k(s)=\lbrace i: b(s_i)>b^{\ast}\rbrace \cup \mathrm{Tie}_{k-n_{>}}\lbrace i: b(s_i)=b^{\ast}\rbrace,\quad b^{\ast}=\max\Big\lbrace b:\sum_{r=1}^{S}\sum_{i\in C_r}\mathbf{1}[b(s_i)\ge b]\ge k\Big\rbrace,\quad S=\mathrm{clamp}\big(\lfloor 64/R\rfloor,4,32\big)\ \text{when}\ R\le N_{\mathrm{CU}}/4 \wedge L>F(R) ``` where - $s_i$: score of KV position $i$, $i=1..L$; $k$ = 2048 for GLM-5.2. - $b(s_i)$: the score's top 12 bits, i.e. its histogram bin. - $S$: blocks per row; $C_r$: the slice of the row block $r$ scans. - $n_{>}$: elements strictly above the threshold bin $b^{\ast}$; $\mathrm{Tie}_m$: the exact top $m$ inside that bin. - $F(R)$: shortest row worth splitting: ```math F(R)=\begin{cases}40960 & R\le 8\\ 49152 & R\le 16\\ 65536 & R\le 32\\ 114688 & R>32\end{cases} ``` ## Scope - CUDA untouched: preprocessed TU is byte-identical to baseline without `USE_ROCM`. - Decode only. Prefill / ragged / packed do not reach the new path. - One file (topk_v2.cuh‎) plus its test. ## Correctness - `test_topk_v2.py` on gfx950: **294 passed** (288 existing + 6 new). - Output matches `torch.topk` exactly, ties included. New `test_topk_v2_split_duplicate_scores` covers heavy ties at the threshold, which the existing suite didn't. - 12-bit histogram, same as the `TopKStreaming` path it replaces on ROCm. ## Performance **Baseline:** `topk_v2` at this PR's parent commit — the kernel this PR edits, and the one GLM uses on ROCm since #36851 made it the default. The other ROCm implementation, the native `topk.hip` cooperative kernel from [#37591](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37591), sits behind `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2=0` and is not touched. MI355X, `k=2048`, `page_size=64`, vs. `topk_v2` at the parent commit. All 71 gated points are >= 1.00x: worst 1.06x, best 3.03x, geomean 1.56x. | B | L | before (us) | after (us) | speedup | |---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 128K | 33.50 | 16.70 | **2.01x** | | 8 | 128K | 33.78 | 18.94 | **1.78x** | | 32 | 128K | 33.95 | 25.29 | 1.34x | | 64 | 128K | 35.94 | 33.89 | 1.06x | | 4 | 256K | 53.71 | 19.07 | **2.82x** | | 128 | 128K | 38.11 | 38.08 | 1.00x (outside gate) | ## GLM-5.2 results GLM-5.2-MXFP4, TP4 on MI355X **End to end (median ITL):** | config | baseline (ms) | split (ms) | change | |---|---|---|---| | ISL 8K / OSL 1024, conc 8 (below floor) | 12.31 | 12.27 | -0.3% | | ISL 70K / OSL 300, conc 4 | 11.21 | 11.00 | -1.9% | | ISL 70K / OSL 300, conc 8 | 12.89 | 12.67 | -1.7% | | ISL 120K / OSL 300, conc 4 | 11.54 | 11.13 | -3.6% | | **ISL 120K / OSL 2000, conc 1** | 10.29 | 9.90 | **-3.8%** | | **ISL 200K / OSL 1000, conc 4** | 11.77 | 11.07 | **-6.0%** | | **ISL 300K / OSL 1000, conc 2** | 11.58 | 10.42 | **-10.0%** | | **ISL 400K / OSL 1000, conc 1** | 11.16 | 9.84 | **-11.8%** | | **ISL 600K / OSL 1000, conc 1** | 12.32 | 10.02 | **-18.7%** | No config is slower. TTFT is unchanged, so prefill is unaffected. **Accuracy (TP4)**: GSM8k 0.933 → 0.936, baseline → split (1200 questions). **Accuracy (TP8)**: GSM8k 0.934 → 0.933, baseline → split (1200 questions). ## Checklist - [x] `pre-commit` on changed files - [x] gfx950 correctness — 294 passed, incl. new duplicate-score test - [x] gfx950 kernel benchmarks - [x] CUDA compile check — preprocessed TU byte-identical; real `nvcc` run still needs CI - [x] GLM-5.2 A/B — 1.41x kernel, -1.7% to -3.8% median ITL, none slower, GSM8k within noise --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :white_check_mark: [Run #36693493288](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36693493288) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #36693492711](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36693492711) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #36693493355](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/36693493355)

title: [Feat] [NPU] DSpark: Support dsv4 dspark on ascend 950
author: randgun
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

Enable DeepSeek V4 DSpark speculative decoding on NPU Ascend 950 (arch35). The existing DSpark implementation only supported CUDA and older NPU (arch22). Arch35 hardware requires different sparse-attention operators, weight-loading strategies, and numerical compatibility workarounds. Several follow-up fixes address a regression where DSpark's unquantized `wo_a` path conflicted with the arch35 MXFP8 detection logic, plus NPU-specific numerical gaps.

## Modifications

- **arch35 DSpark sparse attention**: Added arch35-specific v2 sparse attention operators via a new `TorchOpLoader` extension; loaded during TP worker and DSpark draft worker initialization.
- **`wo_a` quantization fix**: `use_npu_arch35_mxfp8_wo_a()` now accepts a `wo_a_keeps_quant_config` parameter and returns `False` when DSpark explicitly disables `wo_a` quantization. This fixes a regression introduced by a previous commit that changed the assertion condition from `if fp8:` to `if quantize_wo_a:`, which caused an incorrect assertion on arch35 because DSpark's `wo_a` was not quantized. The model also caches this value instead of recomputing it at each call site.
- **DSpark stage configuration**: Added `_dspark_stage_config()` to apply draft-specific expert counts to draft stages and disable vision layers for text-only stages. Arch35 now falls back to standard vocabulary/fusion behavior instead of the arch31-specific path.
- **Weight loading**: Moved the NPU `weight_packed` → `weight` rename before stacked parameter mapping, eliminating duplicated branch logic.

## Accuracy Tests

| Model | Dataset | Metric | Subset | Num | Score |
|---|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash-0731 | GPQA-Diamond | Accuracy ↑ | gpqa_diamond | 198 | 89.9% |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

|---|-----|------|---------|---------|---------|----------|------|-----|
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash| GPQA-Diamond | 198 | 149.111 s | 1943.3 ms | 14.3 ms | 67 tok/s | 344 | 9991 |

title: [MoE] Disable FlashInfer fused finalize by default for numerical accuracy
author: zianglih
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

@humansand

Default to unfused FlashInfer MoE finalize for better numerical accuracy. Users can opt in to fused atomic finalize with `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE=1` when they prefer more aggressive performance.

- **History:** [#28354](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28354) introduced this environment variable with `EnvBool(True)` and made deterministic inference force it to `0`.
- **Prior behavior:** immediately before #28354, the [CUTLASS calls](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutlass.py#L221-L238) and [CuTe DSL v2 wrapper](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/flashinfer_cutedsl.py#L287-L302) omitted `use_fused_finalize`. SGLang [pinned FlashInfer 0.6.17](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/c4271c3fe1262fc2adbd162c33b25de5255251c5/python/pyproject.toml#L36), whose [CUTLASS API](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/a0a6b019b9b27d49d209f85d028a1ae5a9b347d7/flashinfer/fused_moe/core.py#L943) and [CuTe DSL wrapper](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/a0a6b019b9b27d49d209f85d028a1ae5a9b347d7/flashinfer/fused_moe/cute_dsl/fused_moe.py#L464) both defaulted to `True`. Thus #28354 exposed the existing fused-finalize default as a SGLang setting; this PR changes that default to `False` for the callers that honor it. The separate CuTe DSL v1 DeepEP masked path is outside this flag's scope.

## Modifications

- **Default:** change `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE` from `EnvBool(True)` to `EnvBool(False)`.
- **Documentation:** update the default and explain the performance opt-in.
- **Existing paths:** CUTLASS and CuTe DSL callers continue to read the same flag; deterministic inference continues to force it off. No kernel changes or new tests.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Static validation:** changed-file pre-commit checks and `git diff --check` passed at `e3bcc8f7b4337565baea1d2b44fd4f0f838b1953` (base: `6e1d9c14647e3e16f2a103b89dead95f1400ea48`).
- **Environment:** macOS 26.4.1, arm64, Python 3.14.6, pre-commit 4.6.1; local CPU checks only, no container or GPUs used.
- **Not run:** model accuracy tests; no tests added for this default-only runtime change. Mintlify build/link checks were not run because `mint` is unavailable locally.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

- **Result:** Disabling fused finalize has a measurable W4A4 cost in this EP8 sweep. CuTe W4A4 per-tensor latency increases **21.75% at 1 token**. At **16,384 tokens**, latency changes by **+7.82% for CUTLASS**, **+12.55% for CuTe W4A4 per-tensor**, **+10.70% for CuTe W4A4 per-token**, and **-9.20% for CuTe W4A16**. These single sweeps do not support a blanket claim of negligible regression. Users can retain `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MOE_FUSED_FINALIZE=1` when this performance tradeoff matters.
- **Scope:** [`benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/blob/8bc3b578027791336c6ae87db5c9d76f82cef8bc/benchmarks/bench_moe_deepseek.py) at official release [`v0.6.18.post1`](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/releases/tag/v0.6.18.post1), commit `8bc3b578027791336c6ae87db5c9d76f82cef8bc`. All four configurations were measured with simulated EP=8 using the benchmark-only patch below: forward the existing finalize option to CUTLASS and add a W4A4-only selector. No FlashInfer runtime/kernel changes. This directly compares the FlashInfer flag used by SGLang PR head `e3bcc8f7b4337565baea1d2b44fd4f0f838b1953`.
- **Hardware/image:** 1× NVIDIA B300 SXM6 AC (SM103; GPU 0 of an allocated 8-GPU node), 275,040 MiB reported memory, 1,100 W power limit, driver `590.48.01`. Image `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20260918-20518d85`, runtime digest `sha256:d46a59f4b98658f728a1e006c003ad5ee0628e999fd8b2bef71ac1bb61b814da`. Run date: 2026-09-18 UTC.
- **Software:** Python `3.12.3`, PyTorch `2.13.0+cu130`, CUDA toolkit `13.0.88`, `flashinfer-python==0.6.18.post1`, `flashinfer-cubin==0.6.18.post1`, `flashinfer-jit-cache==0.6.18.post1+cu130`, `nvidia-cutlass-dsl==4.6.2`, `apache-tvm-ffi==0.1.11`, `cupti-python==13.4.0` (`nvidia-cuda-cupti==13.4.92`). The image shipped FlashInfer 0.6.18; all three FlashInfer packages were updated to the matched official post1 release before measurement.
- **Workload:** DeepSeek-V3 MoE: hidden 7,168, intermediate 2,048, 256 experts, top-8, 8 routing groups/top-4 groups, routed scale 2.5, random seed 42, routing bias scale 0.01; simulated EP=8, TP=1: rank 0 holds experts 0–31 of 256. The token count is the global input batch routed across all 256 experts; this single-GPU benchmark computes the local expert contribution. Powers of two from 1 through 16,384 tokens. CUTLASS uses NVFP4 W4A4 per-tensor activation scaling. CuTe DSL covers NVFP4 W4A4 per-tensor, NVFP4 W4A4 per-token, and NVFP4 W4A16 with BF16 input, using its wrapper API.
- **Timing:** one complete flag-True sweep followed by one flag-False sweep for each configuration; no repeated or reverse-order sweeps. Independent autotuning caches per backend/activation/finalize mode; 10 warmups, 100 measured iterations per case, native median GPU latency, CUDA graphs and CUPTI with cold-L2 flushing. Routing, input activation quantization (`--include-activation-quant`, for W4A4), both expert GEMMs, and finalize are included. Weight preparation, compilation, and autotuning are excluded. W4A16 consumes BF16 input directly. All six commands exited 0, yielding all 120 requested latency rows with no CUPTI fallback warnings.
- **Build/provenance:** all EP8 runs used the same physical GPU (UUID `GPU-aa4e94df-96de-22b9-87c2-9960d6b27cb8`), image, and package versions. JIT was left enabled. The release wheel provides `fused_moe_103.so` and `fp4_quantization_103.so` for CUTLASS MoE and FP4 quantization; no CUTLASS build was needed.
- **Limits:** single sweeps provide no repeat/order-variation statistics. This covers local MoE only: no inter-GPU communication, other EP/TP layouts, model accuracy checks, or end-to-end serving. No numerical-error reduction is measured here.

**Speedup = latency with `use_fused_finalize=True` (old default) / latency with `False` (proposed default); greater than 1 means disabling fused finalize is faster.** CUTLASS `True` permits eligible fused-finalize tactics; autotuning can still choose an unfused tactic.

title: [XPU] Enable fused QK-norm + RoPE for Qwen3-MoE
author: mehersai07
body:
## Motivation

Qwen3-MoE already has a fused QK-norm + RoPE path, but the gate in `Qwen3MoeAttention.__init__` requires `_is_cuda`. On XPU this falls back to two RMSNorm launches plus a separate RoPE launch per layer, even though `sgl-kernel-xpu` already has the kernel AOT as `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope` which uses the cos/sin cache from rotary embedding.

This enables that kernel on XPU, cutting the q/k-norm + RoPE stage from 3 launches per layer to 1.

## Modifications

The device dispatch lives in the kernel wrapper, so the model keeps a single code path and other callers get XPU support for free.

`python/sglang/srt/models/qwen3_moe.py`:

- New branch on XPU using the `fused_inplace_qknorm_rope`.

Kept opt-in behind the existing flag `--enable-fused-qk-norm-rope` to match CUDA.

## Accuracy Tests

The new `test/registered/xpu/test_fused_inplace_qknorm_rope_xpu.py` added to `nightly-xpu-1-gpu` nightly suite to cover the kernel beyond this model: the packed-qkv strided views this branch passes, a case against the model's unfused `apply_qk_norm` + `RotaryEmbedding` path with the fused call fed from `rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache` as this branch does (default and YaRN `rope_scaling`, `theta=1e6`).

**End-to-end**, GSM8K 1319 examples (1314 scored), greedy, Qwen3-30B-A3B, TP=4.
Both arms verified via `/get_server_info` to have actually resolved
`enable_fused_qk_norm_rope` as intended before running:

| | baseline | fused |
|---|---|---|
| GSM8K | 94.14 | 94.6 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**q/k-norm + RoPE stage**, rank 0 over 40 profiled decode steps, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP=4 on 4x Intel Arc Pro B60, launches / device ms:

| component | baseline | fused |
|---|---|---|
| q/k RMSNorm (`FusedNormKernelFunctor`, 3 instantiations) | 3,858 / 79.6 ms | 18 / 0.52 ms |
| RoPE (`FusedRopeCacheKernel`) | 1,920 / 23.07 ms | 0 / 0.00 ms |
| `FusedQKNormRopeCacheKernel` | 0 / 0.00 ms | 1,920 / 40.80 ms |
| **stage total** | **5,778 / 102.67 ms** | **1,938 / 41.32 ms** |

**−66% launches, −60% device ms.**.  The kernel reads cos/sin from the existing `rotary_emb.cos_sin_cache` and takes the model's int64 positions directly, so no per-layer cast is needed. Total device time on rank 0 drops 5,672 → 5,495 ms (−3.1%).

**End-to-end**, `bench_serving`, input 1024 / output 256, one run per arm (baseline run-to-run spread ~1%):

| conc | baseline | fused | delta | TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 21.4 tok/s | 22.9 tok/s | +7.0% | 46.5 → 43.5 ms |
| 8 | 158.4 tok/s | 168.4 tok/s | +6.3% | 49.0 → 46.0 ms |
| 32 | 557.6 tok/s | 583.9 tok/s | +4.7% | 54.7 → 52.1 ms |

**+4.7-7.0% output throughput** with TPOT down 4.6-6.6%.

cc: @rahulvijayaraghavan @rbabukv

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

title: [Diffusion] Fuse lossless SenseNova RoPE for 5% faster H200 inference
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

SenseNova-U1.5 eagerly applies three-axis RoPE using separate multiply, negate, concatenate and add kernels. Reusing the existing lossless bf16 rotate-half kernel reduces native 2048×2048/50-step **worker request E2E by 5.17% on one H200**, with byte-identical PNGs. Client E2E, including PNG save, improves 5.13% in the repeated isolated comparison.

## Modifications

- Route eligible bf16 CUDA Q/K tensors through the existing `fused_rope_rotate_half_bitexact`; preserve the original bf16 rounding after each product. Materialize the spatial head slices in BSHD layout, then return BHSD views to the existing attention path.
- Keep eager fallback for short prefixes, unsupported shapes/dtypes/table broadcasting, gradients and compilation. No normalization reduction, RoPE table computation, weights or attention backend changes.
- Forward the standard profiling/perf fields through SenseNova's sampling whitelist. Previously `--profile` was silently dropped, and stage timings were absent. Both benchmark arms contain this instrumentation-only fix.

This follows the shared-kernel reuse/rounding approach in #34004 and #38530. It is independent of the open RoPE-table reuse (#38927), RMSNorm dispatch (#39705), and host-sync (#38905) changes.

## Benchmark

Native `sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT`, revision `9feeeab8a2792514d109cd34589342a2cc1d4ab2`; bf16, `quality=lossless`, 2048×2048, 50 steps, CFG 4, seed 42, one H200, request warmup at the same resolution, eager, no torch.compile. Prompt: “A curious raccoon peers through a vibrant field of yellow sunflowers, its eyes wide with interest.” Model and components stay GPU-resident.

Baseline `e8d68ce11f1bc1e880112da35606e8b1fd93db99` = main `993d1fccba` plus the profiling-control fix. Benchmarked candidate: `853522eff16a7294d9a4d2de21658dc260a9d2b6`. Follow-up commit `c48ce29976` adds only the registered test script entry point; runtime code is identical to the benchmarked candidate. Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, driver 595.71.05. Fresh main `9e5a62a767` has unchanged SenseNova and reused RoPE sources.

Same idle GPU, A–B–B–A, separate warmed native CLI runs. Primary repeat, seconds:

| Run | Worker request E2E | Generation stage | Client E2E incl. save |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| A1 | 20.3587 | 20.3252 | 20.83 |
| B1 | 19.3331 | 19.2968 | 19.78 |
| B2 | 19.3743 | 19.3380 | 19.82 |
| A2 | 20.4572 | 20.4244 | 20.91 |

| Mean | Baseline | Candidate | Reduction |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Worker request E2E | 20.4079 | 19.3537 | 5.17% |
| Generation stage | 20.3748 | 19.3174 | 5.19% |
| Client request, including PNG save | 20.8700 | 19.8000 | 5.13% |

Peak reserved memory remains **35.6836 GiB**. Worker E2E is the native perf-dump `total_duration_ms`, ending before `SAVE_OUTPUTS`; model loading and warmup are excluded. `SenseNovaU1GenerationStage` includes prefix processing, denoising and pixel denormalization. Client E2E is the native generation timer around the scheduler call and output save, logged to 0.01s precision.

The first ABBA independently measured 20.3565→19.3780s worker E2E (−4.81%). Its first baseline client request had higher non-worker overhead, so the primary repeat ran after all CPU trace analysis and GPU microbench jobs completed. [All eight raw results, logs and timings](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/final-evidence.json) are retained. Profile/export latency is excluded from every speed row.

BCG is disabled by the current native SenseNova pipeline; its actual fallback probe was rejected. [Probe log](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/bcg-disabled.log). There is no BCG speed claim.

## Profile and operator benchmark

Paired native full-stage traces, sliced between matching completed host synchronizations in the third denoising cycle: 252 RoPE calls per slice, zero boundary-crossing kernels. The application chain changes from **2,520→840 launches** and **28.9995→5.6673ms cumulative GPU time**. Candidate totals include 504 fused kernels and 336 spatial-layout copies. The removal of about 23.3ms of device work per cycle is consistent with the unprofiled request improvement. Profile CPU/window time includes instrumentation overhead and is not a speed measurement.

[Baseline trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/baseline-denoise-step2.trace.json.gz) · [Candidate trace](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/candidate-denoise-step2.trace.json.gz) · [Baseline attribution](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/baseline-profile-evidence.json) · [Candidate attribution](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/candidate-profile-evidence.json). Full-trace SHA256 manifests and the extraction script are included with the artifacts.

Exact committed-function microbenchmark: B=1, 4096 tokens, Q/K heads 32/8, bf16; means in µs, including guards, transposes and materialization. A–B–B–A; each cell uses 100ms warmup and 300ms measurement.

| Axis | Rotary width | Eager | Candidate |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| t | 64 | 165.90 | 31.59 |
| h | 32 | 99.05 | 50.18 |
| w | 32 | 99.05 | 51.93 |

[Raw microbenchmarks and source SHAs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/rope-committed-microbench.json) · [Harness](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/scripts/bench-sensenova-rope-heads.py).

## Output comparison

All eight unprofiled outputs and both profiled outputs are **byte-identical**, with identical decoded 2048×2048 pixels (max difference 0, SSIM 1, PSNR ∞). Before/after originals were visually inspected.

| Baseline | Candidate |
| --- | --- |
| ![Baseline SenseNova output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/baseline.png) | ![Optimized SenseNova output](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/candidate.png) |

PNG SHA256: `db4ed33a284477a5d9f5f6ac7d53f959799c2c1844150fcf753164f431c5aafc`. [Per-output file and decoded hashes](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/final-evidence.json).

## Validation and reproduction

**Validation scope:** The test counts, logs and GPU measurements below are historical results from the recorded benchmark revisions, before test cleanup. The current diff retains the profiling-argument forwarding regression in the existing model test file; the dedicated RoPE test file has been removed. This cleanup does not change runtime code or claim a new GPU measurement.

- **98 tests passed**: 17 new CUDA cases for the real strided t/h/w heads, batches/odd lengths, full-attention output equality, non-mutation, and fallback/gradient behavior; 81 existing SenseNova tests. [Test log](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/tests.log).
- Pre-commit passed for all four changed files; source tree clean at benchmark head. The CI entry-point follow-up also passed registry collection and all 17 CUDA cases via `python test/registered/kernels/ops/diffusion/test_sensenova_rope.py -f` on H200.
- Campaign-owned SenseNova checkpoint cache deleted after validation: **zero residual files, weights or bytes**. Shared caches untouched. [Cleanup audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/70bef5daba348bf82fe17bef9b4cc119002d36ae/diffusion-prs/sensenova-rope-h200/cache-cleanup.json).

Run on each revision with the same pinned checkpoint/cache:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1 \
sglang generate \
  --model-path sensenova/SenseNova-U1.5-8B-MoT \
  --revision 9feeeab8a2792514d109cd34589342a2cc1d4ab2 \
```

title: [Diffusion] Accelerate Cosmos3 Edge on Hopper with lossless fusions
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Cosmos3 Edge's single-image path still uses separate Q/K normalization, RoPE and KV concatenation on Hopper. Its dense MLP also materializes ReLU before a separate square. Native profiles identify both chains in all 28 generation blocks, with separate positive and negative CFG passes.

This enables the existing rounded QK norm/RoPE/KV packing for the validated Edge shape and reuses the unary ReLU² kernel with fast math disabled. On **one H200**, two native A–B–B–A groups reduce **image worker E2E by 29.61–32.23%** and **saved-image client E2E by 26.92–30.59%**. Video worker E2E improves about **2.2%**. All generated images and all 81 video frames remain exact.

## Modifications

- Admit the 2048-wide dense Edge T=1 shape to the existing Hopper TP1/SP1 QK norm/RoPE/KV-pack path. Preserve the rounded BF16 cache and Edge's separately normalized UND keys. Larger dense, parallel and compiled configurations retain the previous gate.
- Expose the existing activation compiler's `fast_math` option through the unary wrapper, defaulting to the existing behavior. Cosmos contiguous BF16 CUDA inference uses `fast_math=False` for ReLU²; other model paths retain Torch.
- Add finite-domain, production-shape, storage-ownership, changed-input CUDA-graph replay and fallback tests, plus a registered marker benchmark. No CUDA arithmetic implementation or checkpoint change.

The first fast-math experiment flushed 511 BF16 subnormal products to zero and was rejected before native combined benchmarks. Disabling fast math preserves all **65,280 finite BF16 encodings**, including signed zero and subnormal results. [Rejected experiment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/rejected-fast-math-experiment), [source review](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/source-review.md).

This builds on the actual rounded Cosmos T1 and Hopper Nano implementations in #34932 and #36571, following the lossless fusion approach in #38530. Edge's architecture comes from #31590. Closed #34618 does not provide a usable BCG path in the current custom denoising stage.

## Benchmark

`nvidia/Cosmos3-Edge@344d602b128d1bbdacb43b08d0a3626f46343e29`, **1× H200**, TP1/SP1, BF16, native eager, `quality=lossless`, manual performance mode, GPU-resident components, no torch.compile. Native same-shape request warmup, two warmup steps; fixed sampling in both arms:

| Workload | Output | Steps / CFG / seed | Prompt |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| T2I | 640×640, 1 frame | 35 / 7 / 0 | A warehouse robot folds a blue cloth on a clean workbench. |
| T2V | 832×480, 81 frames, 24 fps (3.375 s) | 35 / 5 / 42 | A warehouse robot carefully places a blue box on a shelf. |

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; candidate `18f1417a8b189fcb80b38d6ca3b487ecca89f39d`. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05. [Environment](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/environment.json). Both arms use the existing native helper's Cosmos guardrail setting; the checkpoint already disables its safety checker.

Fresh native CLI processes, same idle GPU, two A–B–B–A groups per workload. Profile and microbenchmark runs are excluded. Seconds, with reduction from each group's arithmetic means:

| Workload / repeat | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E including saved output |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T2I-R1 | 0.9986 → 0.6768 (32.23%) | 0.9653 → 0.6435 (33.33%) | 1.095 → 0.760 (30.59%) |
| T2I-R2 | 0.9588 → 0.6749 (29.61%) | 0.9253 → 0.6414 (30.68%) | 1.040 → 0.760 (26.92%) |
| T2V-R1 | 6.2802 → 6.1386 (2.25%) | 4.5535 → 4.4176 (2.98%) | 6.625 → 6.475 (2.26%) |
| T2V-R2 | 6.2865 → 6.1464 (2.23%) | 4.5580 → 4.4190 (3.05%) | 7.550 → 6.490 (14.04%) |

T2V-R2 contains a baseline client-only outlier (A1 **8.47 s**, worker **6.2879 s**). All rows are retained; its inflated client percentage is not treated as a repeatable benefit. T2V-R1 saved-client reduction is about 2.3%; both video groups have consistent worker reductions. The image result independently exceeds 1.5% in both worker and saved-client E2E in both groups.

<details><summary>All 16 unprofiled native measurements</summary>

| Group | Arm | Worker E2E | Denoise | Client E2E incl. save |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T2I-R1 | A1 | 1.0380 | 1.0044 | 1.15 |
| T2I-R1 | B1 | 0.6858 | 0.6522 | 0.77 |
| T2I-R1 | B2 | 0.6677 | 0.6349 | 0.75 |
| T2I-R1 | A2 | 0.9591 | 0.9261 | 1.04 |
| T2I-R2 | A1 | 0.9567 | 0.9235 | 1.04 |
| T2I-R2 | B1 | 0.6775 | 0.6439 | 0.76 |
| T2I-R2 | B2 | 0.6722 | 0.6389 | 0.76 |
| T2I-R2 | A2 | 0.9609 | 0.9270 | 1.04 |
| T2V-R1 | A1 | 6.2796 | 4.5538 | 6.62 |
| T2V-R1 | B1 | 6.1399 | 4.4225 | 6.48 |
| T2V-R1 | B2 | 6.1374 | 4.4128 | 6.47 |
| T2V-R1 | A2 | 6.2807 | 4.5532 | 6.63 |
| T2V-R2 | A1 | 6.2879 | 4.5580 | 8.47 |
| T2V-R2 | B1 | 6.1471 | 4.4184 | 6.49 |
| T2V-R2 | B2 | 6.1458 | 4.4196 | 6.49 |
| T2V-R2 | A2 | 6.2851 | 4.5580 | 6.63 |

</details>

Worker E2E is perf-dump stage duration before saving, excluding loading and warmup. Client E2E is the native scheduler-request/output-save timer, logged to 0.01 s. Peak reserved memory is unchanged: **8.9258 GiB T2I / 13.2598 GiB T2V**. [Raw perf dumps, source SHAs, configs and native logs](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/raw), [complete timing audit](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/final-evidence.json).

The current PR head `1430010b7b20f9d56d6d6d4caeebee1980e28c73` adds only a test coverage correction after the measured head: the newly enabled Hopper split-path parity checks are registered on the Hopper CI lane and skipped on other architectures. B200 continues to run all four ReLU² tests, which passed in the first CI run. That run exposed three failures from applying the Hopper split-path bitwise contract to the unchanged Blackwell QK path. Runtime files and all benchmark measurements are unchanged.

The corrected seven-test file passed on H200 (14.27 s). In the next CI run, the H100, B200 and BCG jobs were skipped by fast-fail after the unrelated [CPU fixture failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35475607241/job/105984387058): `test_auxiliary_output.py` supplies a mock batch without `split_index`, which the existing scheduler reads. Those skipped GPU jobs are not recorded as passing validation.

The T1-only ablation also has exact images: worker mean **0.9589 → 0.6666 s**, client **1.040 → 0.765 s**. This is a separate exploratory group at `8d329ce689`; the headline uses the final combined head and its repeated groups.

## Profile and operator benchmark

Each slice is one complete second CFG iteration, covering both positive and negative passes. CPU model-call boundaries are joined to GPU execution through CUDA launch correlations; all five retained slices have **zero boundary-crossing GPU kernels**. The baseline video path already uses the QK fusion; its gain comes from ReLU².

| Workload | All kernels, before → after | Eager ReLU + square calls / ms | Fused ReLU² calls / ms | Candidate fused QK/RoPE calls / ms |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| T2I | 1996 → 708 | 112 / 0.4350 | 56 / 0.2138 | 56 / 0.2485 |
| T2V | 708 → 652 | 112 / 8.2427 | 56 / 3.8970 | 56 / 3.7125 |

T1-only reduces complete-iteration kernels from **1996 → 764**. Final ReLU² fusion removes another 56 launches. T2I is sensitive to launch overhead; T2V is largely GPU busy. Cumulative profile device times explain the changed operators and are not E2E measurements. [Original and complete-iteration traces, attribution and three-table triage](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/profiles).

Committed-wrapper marker benchmark, rotating inputs, median **microseconds**, including dispatch and normal output allocation:

| Operation / shape | Eager | Fused |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| QK norm + RoPE + KV pack, S400, Q16/KV8, D128 | 64.9402 | 4.7117 |
| QK norm + RoPE + KV pack, S1024, Q16/KV8, D128 | 85.8332 | 8.9444 |
| ReLU², [1, 400, 9216] | 8.6710 | 4.0407 |
| ReLU², [1, 8190, 9216] | 146.1616 | 71.6109 |

[Raw marker output](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/cosmos3-edge-combined-marker-retry1.log). Mutable Q/K views belong to the current forward; V and cached UND K/V remain unchanged, as tested.

## Output comparison

The audit covers **39 output records**: **33 valid eager requests**, plus six explicitly unsupported BCG requests. Every valid image/video, including separate lossless/high checks and profiled requests, is byte-identical within its workload. All videos independently decode to **81/81 identical frames**, SSIM1, PSNR∞, no audio stream. Before/after image and video contact sheets were visually inspected. The T2I native result contains a blue cloth/workbench but no visible robot in either arm; this comparison establishes output preservation.

![Baseline and optimized image](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/output-comparison/image-comparison.png)

[Original baseline PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/baseline.png) · [Original optimized PNG](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/candidate.png)

![Baseline and optimized video: frames 0, 26, 53, 80](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/output-comparison/video-comparison.jpg)

[Original baseline MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/baseline.mp4) · [Original optimized MP4](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/BBuf/sglang/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/candidate.mp4) · [Per-frame hashes](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/output-comparison)

PNG SHA256: `5a3849ada21e0799fefa4c571cdf9cf005eab33b013eeb074c2f6c0782e67b23`. MP4 SHA256: `6d7403a334c8a4f7487ee13e13e7c707898aecd5eb2529f34408a76b26f64350`.

BCG was actually attempted for T2I/T2V and in the lossless/high T2I matrix. Every attempt reports `[diffusion bcg] disabled` with no capture, so fallback outputs are retained only as applicability evidence. **No Cosmos BCG speedup is claimed.** High eager T2I/T2V checks are exact, with no separate high-mode performance claim.

## Validation and reproduction

- **145 Cosmos/kernel tests and 46 subtests passed**, including the new CUDA tests and existing model tests. [Log](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/2ca713c21ccf1bc613a6f18ef6c7115b8b49f1fb/diffusion-prs/cosmos3-edge-hopper-fusions/cosmos3-edge-combined-tests-retry1.log).

title: [Diffusion] Fuse lossless Wan VAE post-ops for LongLive 2 I2V
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

LongLive 2's lossless Wan VAE decoder executes five separate FP32 pointwise passes after normalization. In the native I2V profile, the 464 norm/SiLU scopes take **690.82 ms across 3248 kernels**. Keeping Torch's reduction and fusing only the exact post-ops reduces that to **275.26 ms / 1834 kernels**, including first-sight reference checks and fallback calls.

On **one H200**, final-source I2V A–B–B–A groups reduce worker E2E by **5.53–5.88%**. The representative final group reduces client E2E including video save from **5.980 to 5.665 s (5.27%)**. All lossless before/after videos are byte-identical. T2V worker latency improves, but retained client outliers prevent a T2V client E2E speed claim.

## Modifications

- Keep native autocast-aware L2 normalization and epsilon clamp, then fuse divide, scale, affine multiplication, bias addition and SiLU into one JIT CUDA kernel. Inputs/gamma may be BF16, while the normalized intermediates and output remain FP32.
- Use explicit FP32 round-to-nearest operations and `expf`, with FMA contraction disabled and no fast math. Support dense NCDHW and channels-last-3D layouts through the existing JIT utilities.
- Integrate through the shared Wan VAE wrapper with per-signature integer-bit verification and permanent fallback on mismatch. Unsupported dtype/layout, gradient-enabled, compiled and unverified-capture calls retain the native path. Unsupported post-op inputs reuse the already-computed denominator.
- Preserve the existing high-quality full RMSNorm+SiLU dispatch. Keep three focused tests for autocast/layout/affine behavior, numerical boundaries and graph replay, and update fusion-coverage documentation.

The existing Wan full-norm fusion (#33546, #35981) and the open conv-bias/full-norm tiling work in #38650 are distinct from this lossless post-only path. The shared wrapper also serves other Wan/Qwen VAEs; this PR's native model evidence covers LongLive 2 T2V and I2V. Other model families are protected by the first-sight exactness gate but are not claimed as benchmarked here.

[Source review and execution flow](https://github.com/BBuf/sglang/blob/5af31ea3b6b434c21b2014ea2834876317818058/diffusion-prs/longlive2-wan-norm-post-h200/source-review.md). Native SiLU arithmetic was checked against the [installed Torch source](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pytorch/pytorch/cf30153c4c131c8164ee7798e5022d810682e2cb/aten/src/ATen/native/cuda/ActivationSiluKernel.cu).

## Benchmark

Model `Rabinovich/LongLive-2.0-5B-Diffusers@37664a64cfc38cdc5fabe88576961ef10646e4f1`. Native SGLang eager, 1×H200 / TP1, unquantized BF16 DiT, native VAE/autocast precision, all components resident. Automatic performance mode resolves CPU/layerwise offload to false in both arms. No torch.compile or approximate cache. Four steps, CFG1, flow shift5, seed42, 61 frames at24fps (2.5417s), no audio.

- I2V: native helper requests960×928; the input-image aspect handling produces **1152×768** in all24 accepted I2V videos. The helper's supported-resolution advisory is retained. Prompt: `The cat starts walking slowly towards the camera.`
- T2V: requested and actual832×480. Prompt: `A curious raccoon`.
- Both modes use the same native helper warmup in every arm: **960×928×29 frames, two of four steps**. Warmup is excluded from request timing; the requested warmup flags do not override that helper's synthetic request geometry.

Baseline `993d1fccbaafe3e79d91567d2fc1d665cc94fa50`; final measured/PR candidate `be05e7e6c24252db11458621f2d06f3969be08d1`. Earlier r1/r2 use `a98b0875c4`; final r3/r4 include the reviewed fallback fix and unique custom-op name. The CUDA device implementation and marker/NCU harness are unchanged. Torch2.13.0+cu130, Triton3.7.1, CUDA13.0, driver595.71.05.

title: [NPU] Skip fused gmm1+swiglu for swiglu_limit (SiLU-with-clamp) checkpoints
author: iridiumine
body:
## Motivation

Follow-up to #39881. The fused gmm1 kernel ( npu_grouped_matmul_swiglu_quant_v2 ) applies plain SiLU with no clamp , but _uses_fused_gmm1 selected it for W4A8 MXFP4 MoE based only on the kernel type and use_fused_gmm1 — it never looked at the activation configuration.

Checkpoints whose MoE activation is SiLU-with-clamp ( swiglu_limit , e.g. DSV4) therefore lost the clamp when the fused kernel was selected, producing incorrect numerics. This silently bypassed the clamp path ( NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant ) that #38420 had just added for exactly this case.

## Modifications

Single-file change in python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/moe_runner/ascend.py :

- _uses_fused_gmm1(kernel, config) now takes the runner config and returns False when config.swiglu_limit is set and > 0 :
  - W4A8 MXFP4 + swiglu_limit (DSV4): falls back to the unfused path — w13 gmm + NPUSwigluMxfp8Quant(config.swiglu_limit) , which applies the clamp. This restores the pre-#39881 behavior
  - MXFP8 + swiglu_limit : raises NotImplementedError at init — this method has no unfused gmm1 path, so failing loudly beats silently serving wrong numerics (no known checkpoint hits this combination today)
  - Plain-SiLU models ( swiglu_limit unset or 0 ): keep the fused kernel, unchanged
- Both call sites ( __init__ and run() ) now pass the same config, so the activation selection and the fused/unfused branch decision can never disagree

## Accuracy Tests

- Dispatch logic verified locally with mocked kernels for all combinations: W4A8 ± swiglu_limit, MXFP8 ± swiglu_limit, use_fused_gmm1=False , and non-fused kernels — all resolve as intended
- DSV4 on NPU (fp4 experts → NPUW4A8MXFP4MoEMethod , swiglu_limit from HF config) now resolves to the unfused clamp path, bit-identical to the pre-#39881 serving path

## Speed Tests and Profiling

None — this PR intentionally trades the #39881 fusion gain back for correctness on clamp checkpoints. Plain-SiLU models (e.g. Kimi-K3 MXFP4) keep the full fused-path benefit (~15% per-layer MoE latency reduction from #39881). Recovering the fusion gain for clamp checkpoints would require adding a limit parameter to the fused kernel, which is kernel-side work out of scope here.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.

4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: fix(cuda-graph): remove unnecessary CP batch alignment
author: AMD-yanfeiwang
body:
### Summary

Decode CUDA graph capture aligned batch sizes to `attn_cp_size`, even though prefill CP is inactive for `DECODE` and `TARGET_VERIFY`. DCP and `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` partition KV/head dimensions rather than token rows, so they do not require CP-width batch alignment.

Remove the CP factor while retaining the existing TBO and gathered-buffer attention-TP alignment.

## AgentX performance

This result requires the combined [#34200](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/34200), [#39950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39950), and [#40543](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40543) stack: HIP CP-v2 support, correct AITER B-preshuffled slicing, and removal of unnecessary CP decode-graph alignment.

Single-node DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813 on 8×MI355X, TP8, DSpark gamma 6, static verify, 3,600 seconds per point. C4/C16 use GPU KV; C32/C48/C64 use HiCache. `PCP8 + DTP` enables `--enable-prefill-cp --attn-cp-size 8 --enable-cp-decode-attn-tp`.

Values are `TP8 → PCP8 + DTP`; latency is lower-is-better and throughput is higher-is-better. Deltas are relative to TP8.

| C | TTFT avg | TTFT p90 | TPOT avg | TPOT p90 | Total tok/s/GPU | Output tok/s/GPU |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 4 | 1.074 → 0.929 s (-13.5%) | 1.957 → 1.687 s (-13.8%) | 4.86 → 5.36 ms (+10.3%) | 6.09 → 6.07 ms (-0.3%) | 3,139 → 3,266 (+4.1%) | 23.62 → 24.52 (+3.8%) |
| 16 | 1.206 → 1.019 s (-15.5%) | 2.314 → 1.948 s (-15.8%) | 7.20 → 7.39 ms (+2.6%) | 10.56 → 10.21 ms (-3.3%) | 11,299 → 11,252 (-0.4%) | 78.59 → 78.49 (-0.1%) |
| 32 | 2.176 → 1.711 s (-21.4%) | 4.263 → 3.155 s (-26.0%) | 11.26 → 10.31 ms (-8.4%) | 16.93 → 14.38 ms (-15.1%) | 20,608 → 21,506 (+4.4%) | 130.79 → 136.27 (+4.2%) |
| 48 | 3.715 → 2.802 s (-24.6%) | 8.027 → 5.821 s (-27.5%) | 15.67 → 13.49 ms (-13.9%) | 21.03 → 17.52 ms (-16.7%) | 24,786 → 26,911 (+8.6%) | 172.36 → 187.30 (+8.7%) |
| 64 | — → 7.745 s | — → 18.477 s | — → 18.34 ms | — → 23.08 ms | — → 28,413 | — → 222.15 |

At C32/C48, PCP8 + DTP reduces average/P90 TTFT by 21–27%, reduces average/P90 TPOT by 8–17%, and improves per-GPU throughput by 4–9%. C64 reaches 28,413 total tok/s/GPU. All five PCP8 + DTP points completed with zero profiled request errors; C64 has no TP8 reference point.

title: [Kimi K3] Fix CUDA graph stream explosion
author: kpham-sgl
body: ## Motivation Kimi K3 target CUDA graph replay expands to 96 streams on B300. Repeated attention forks move subsequent layers onto new replay streams. Record the main attention branches before their auxiliary kernels to fix this stream explosion: the same workload now uses 4 target streams on all eight TP ranks. ## Modifications - Record the KDA main projection before the side-stream gate GEMVs. - Fork the MLA output gate before attention, then record its kernel at the output-projection boundary after the attention core. Keep the original fork/join dependencies so the GPU work can still overlap, and close skipped gate branches. - Extend changed-input CUDA graph correctness coverage. ## Accuracy Tests `python test/registered/unit/models/test_kimi_k3_bfa_overlap.py`: **5 tests passed on B300**. [Overlap unit CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662649445) and [B300 end-to-end CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662661359) also passed on the current PR head; both Kimi K3 B300 end-to-end files passed two tests each. KDA bitwise parity covers token counts 1, 4, and 12, both `defer_f_b` settings, and three changed-input replays. MLA checks an in-graph input producer and changed-input parity, including eager and breakable-graph fallback selection. Full-model traces retain identical kernel-name/count multisets: 1,950 target kernels per replay on every rank. ## Speed Tests and Profiling In TP8/DCP1 traces, target replay streams fall from **96 to 4 on all eight TP ranks**, with stable assignments across 16 profiled replays and identical kernel-name/count multisets. This is reproduced with both real and dummy weights. Separate **N=5 unprofiled runs per variant and batch size**, using dummy MXFP4 target and dummy draft weights: 8× B300, CUDA 13.0, TP8, 60k input / 1k output, DSpark block 7, simulated acceptance 5.5, FP8 E4M3 KV, FP32 SSM, CuTe DSL MLA, FlashInfer MXFP4 MoE, connections=8. **TP8/DCP1:** | Batch size | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change in mean | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 493.06 ± 2.41 | 498.12 ± 2.14 | +1.03% | | 16 | 3139.65 ± 252.29 | 3249.41 ± 15.07 | +3.50% | BS1 improves in all five matched pairs (+0.77% to +1.14%). **The BS16 mean is distorted by one slow baseline sample (2689.09 tok/s), retained in the results.** The other four matched pairs differ by −0.10% to −0.15%; these results do not establish a BS16 speedup. Full-batch steady-state throughput gives the same interpretation. Order: baseline (3 samples), patched (3), patched (2), baseline (2), each with a fresh server and a full-shape warmup pair excluded in advance. Client/server seeds are 42; actual acceptance lengths match in every corresponding pair. All requests generated the requested tokens. Measurements share two server launches per variant, so N=5 is limited evidence. Dummy weights and simulated acceptance do not test model accuracy. **TP8/DCP8**, same N=5 design and workload, with `fi_a2a` and replicated Q projection: | Batch size | Before, tok/s (mean ± SD) | After, tok/s (mean ± SD) | Change in mean | | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | | 1 | 470.94 ± 2.23 | 474.87 ± 2.26 | +0.83% | | 16 | 3060.60 ± 14.24 | 3060.26 ± 13.92 | −0.01% | Every BS1 matched pair improves (+0.72% to +0.88%); BS16 decode is unchanged (paired changes −0.028% to +0.001%). Acceptance matches in every pair. All samples are retained and all requests complete their requested output length with a valid full-batch decode window. BS16 mean total latency is 44.845 → 45.105 s (+0.58%), driven by last-TTFT/prefill time (39.617 → 39.876 s), including one slower patched prefill sample. N=5 does not establish whether the small prefill difference is noise; the flat decode result is not a claim about all end-to-end timings. The DCP benchmark uses `--skip-token-capacity-check` because the client guard reads physical capacity while DCP exposes eight times the logical capacity; server memory settings are unchanged. Both repeated comparisons use baseline `0f6761b54` with the PR patch applied for the patched runs. DCP8 was not profiled in this timing experiment. ## Profile **Before** **After** ## Checklist - [x] Pre-commit checks pass for all changed files. - [x] Registered CUDA unit tests extended and run. - [x] Correctness and full-model profiling results provided above. --- ### CI States Latest PR Test (Base): :x: [Run #35662490950](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662490950) Latest PR Test (Extra): :x: [Run #35662490698](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662490698) Latest PR Test (AMD ROCm 10): :x: [Run #35662491074](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/35662491074)
