title: [PD] Add opt-in prefill-complete decode KV allocation
author: ekrim
body:
## Motivation

In PD serving, decode can reserve a request's destination KV slots while its
prefill is still running. Long prefills can therefore occupy decode capacity
that other requests could use.

Add `--disaggregation-decode-allocation-policy prefill_complete` to delay
per-request destination KV reservation until the accepted final prefill result
is ready. Global KV pool creation and size are unchanged. The policy is opt-in;
`early` remains the default.

This policy targets workloads where decode KV capacity is constrained and
prefill completion times vary—for example, concurrent short and long prompts.
Early reservation lets unfinished long prefills occupy decode slots before they
can generate tokens, potentially delaying other requests that are ready.
Deferring reservation makes that capacity available until prefill finishes; it does
not make allocation itself or decode kernels faster.

## Modifications

- Add a Mooncake readiness control protocol with request ownership/nonces,
  subscription retry backoff, bounded waits, failure propagation, and
  pre-allocation cancellation.
- Signal readiness after accepting the final prefill result and preparing its
  output/logprob/speculative sidecars. Gate decode admission on that signal.
- Preserve the existing destination-metadata handshake and abort/drain protocol
  after destination pointers have been published.
- Keep exhausted optimistic retries eligible for prefill, and dispatch true
  retraction/rebootstrap recomputation before waiting for source readiness.
- Validate matching policies and supported configurations; add registered CPU
  regressions, a two-GPU lifecycle suite, and documentation.

Initial support is Mooncake (including TCP), the Python bootstrap registry, and
attention TP1/CP1/PP1 per rank, including attention DP. Prefill HiCache support is
limited to L2 `write_back` without storage. Decode radix/HiCache, staging,
runtime role switching, PD multiplexing, encoder disaggregation, decoupled
speculation, HiSparse, and non-DSA auxiliary state pools are excluded.

Enable the option on **both roles**. Upgrade all communicating workers with
`early` still enabled before switching policies; old decode workers cannot
enforce the new policy-mismatch check. Prefill resolves zero optimistic attempts
to one; model/cache configurations that disable optimistic prefill are rejected.

## Accuracy Tests

- Previous revision: **99 CPU tests and 27 subtests passed**, one
  Mori-dependent test skipped, across six files on Linux ARM64.
- All applicable pinned pre-commit hooks passed on the submitted files.
- **Pending:** CPU/GPU regression execution on the latest rebase. The local CPU
  attempt could not collect tests because `torchvision` is missing. GPU and
  performance results below predate both rebases.

The registered two-GPU suite,
`test/registered/e2e/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete_allocation.py`, covers
multi-chunk prefill, prefix reuse, concurrency, cancellation before/after
transfer, retract/resume, optimistic retry exhaustion, and timeout cleanup.

<details>
<summary>Validation commands, environment, and revision details</summary>

CPU command:

```bash
python -m pytest -q -ra \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_complete_integration.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_prefill_abort_result_cleanup.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_register_to_bootstrap.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_pd_role_switch.py \
  test/registered/unit/disaggregation/test_admission_abort_not_enqueued.py
```

The run at `4f5fa4d7` had zero failures/errors and 14 warnings. Mori was
unavailable. No custom import shims or weakened assertions were used. Torch was
2.15 development rather than the source's 2.13 pin, so dependency-lock parity
remains unvalidated.

The earlier submitted commit `86d123ec` differs only in one test's line wrapping:
production code is byte-identical and all changed Python files are AST-identical.

Current HEAD `f7b24085` rebases that change onto `771c9d78`, retaining upstream's
new EFA allocator validation before our readiness initialization. All added and
removed feature lines are unchanged. Pre-commit passed again. The local attempt
also included `test_mooncake_efa_allocator.py`: seven collection errors from
missing `torchvision`, zero tests executed.

Before the rebase, the original candidate passed all eight registered GPU
lifecycle tests, additional attention-DP checks, and six TCP/prefill-HiCache
checks. In the isolated GLM comparison, all 1,280 measured requests completed at
exact lengths without client errors, and timed texts matched across all four
arms. Untimed probes had identical output tokens and finite logprobs, with a
maximum logprob difference of 0.002925. These are functional parity checks, not
a model-quality benchmark.

</details>

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Historical GLM-5.2-NVFP4 ABBA comparison: real MTP3, 12 Rubin GPUs, two prefill
replicas and one decode replica, each TP4/DP4/EP4, with FP8 KV and Mooncake.
Only the allocation policy differed; optimistic prefill was 1 in both policies.
Decode KV was deliberately capped at 163,840 tokens/rank to test capacity
pressure, rather than a production-default configuration.

| Mixed-workload metric | Early, two runs | Prefill-complete, two runs | Change in mean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Output tokens/s, system | 458.88 / 435.98 | 616.39 / 518.39 | +26.81% |
| TTFT p95, seconds | 71.22 / 79.97 | 36.03 / 41.27 | -48.87% |
| Mean TPOT, ms | 4.108 / 3.869 | 4.204 / 3.943 | +2.13% |
| ITL p99, ms | 34.40 / 12.03 | 46.40 / 43.10 | +92.77% |

Changes compare arithmetic means of the two per-run metrics, including
percentiles, not pooled percentiles or confidence intervals.

The throughput/TTFT gain comes with a worse ITL tail. Delayed allocation also
retains source KV longer and removes overlap between chunked prefill and KV
transfer. A separate Qwen3-8B policy-only comparison showed approximately 1%
throughput differences within run variation, without a clear mixed-workload
short-request tail improvement. These workload-dependent tradeoffs are why the
policy remains opt-in.

<details>
<summary>Historical benchmark protocol and provenance</summary>

Candidate `bd4b80dd`, based on `e4a6b090`, ran on identical hosts in
`early / prefill_complete / prefill_complete / early` order, with DP attention
enabled. Workers restarted between arms.

Each arm included 64 short requests (ISL 4,096, OSL 256, concurrency 8), followed
by 256 mixed requests (64 at ISL 131,072 and 192 at ISL 4,096; OSL 256,
concurrency 64). The table reports the mixed workload.

A separate larger-workload campaign did not pass its final provenance audit;
its apparent gains are not used as validated performance evidence here.

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Run applicable pinned pre-commit hooks on the PR files.
- [x] Add registered unit and lifecycle tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [ ] Complete CPU/GPU regression and performance validation on the latest HEAD.
- [x] Review changes against the SGLang code-style guidance.

AI assistance was used for implementation/review and test preparation.
Maintainer help enabling the appropriate upstream CPU and GPU CI would be
appreciated.

title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen3.5: Route 512-expert softmax MoE routing through aiter topk_gating
author: omirosh
body:
## Motivation

This is a ROCm performance change: it routes Qwen3.8's 512-expert softmax MoE router through aiter's `topk_gating` instead of the vendored `vllm::moe::topkGatingSoftmax` launcher it reaches today. Against its merge-base on the aiter pin that SGLang ships (`285579b62`, since #45498, with [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334)), it gives **+1.27%** output tok/s without MTP on 8x MI355X, TP8, geomean over 12 serving shapes. On v0.5.19 with NEXTN MTP it gave **+2.22%**.

On SGLang v0.5.20 at the default page size the gain is +1.03% without MTP and +0.40% with MTP; see https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/40708#issuecomment-5933064541. 

Qwen3.8 picks 10 experts out of 512 on every one of its 92 layers. On ROCm that pick is 0.878 ms per decode step, 4.8% of decode kernel time, against 0.440 ms/step on B300. `aiter.fused_moe.fused_topk` only hands off to its ASM router for `(experts, topk)` in `(128,4), (128,6), (128,8), (256,6), (256,8), (384,8), (640,8)`, and Qwen3.8 is `(512, 10)`. Qwen3.8-Flash-Next has the same `(512, 10)` softmax router at hidden size 2560 and takes the same path.

[#28399](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28399) tried the same wiring in August and got nothing for it (ITL +3.7%, throughput -1.9% on Qwen3.5 TP2). aiter has since gained the E=512 kernel and learned to honour `need_renorm` for softmax ([Rocm/aiter4460](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/4460)).

## Modifications

- `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: `_use_aiter_topk_gating_softmax()` decides, and the `_use_aiter` softmax branch calls `topk_gating` when it says yes. Every other shape keeps `aiter_fused_topk`.
- `python/sglang/srt/environ.py`: `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_AITER_TOPK_GATING`, default off. Set it to 1 to fall back to `fused_topk`.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen38_moe_softmax_topk_gating.py`: agreement with the legacy launcher at 4, 128, 1024, 1025, 2048 and 4096 rows at hidden sizes 8192 and 2560, so both aiter kernels are covered up to the ceiling, plus every envelope boundary.

The dispatch: gfx95, AITER on, hidden size 8192 (Qwen3.8) or 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next), BF16 hidden states, BF16 contiguous gating output, 512 experts, at most 4096 rows, no correction bias, no fused shared slots, no packed output.

## Accuracy Tests

MI355X node, TP8, SGLang v0.5.19. GSM8K is 5-shot, 1314 items, thinking on. NIAH is `niah_single_2` at 65,536 / 131,072.

| Arm | GSM8K | NIAH 65k / 131k |
| --- | --- | --- |
| MTP baseline | 0.978 | 0.998 / 1.000 |
| MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.990 / 1.00 |
| non-MTP baseline | 0.979 | 0.998 / 0.998 |
| non-MTP this PR | 0.978 | 0.998 / 0.994 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B-Quark-MXFP4, `chunked-prefill-size 16384, page-size 64`. 12 cells per arm: 8k/1k at concurrency 4 through 256, 60k/600 at 4, 16 and 64, 128k/1k at 4 and 16. Geomeans of output tok/s. 

The four arms ran on the same node and differ only in which kernel the softmax router call reaches:

- **baseline**: v0.5.19 as released. Every router call goes through `aiter_fused_topk`, which for `(512, 10)` lands on the vendored `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling**: this PR without the 4096-row limit. Every router call, including the 16384-token prefill chunks, goes to `topk_gating`. Above 1024 rows `topk_gating` switches from the E=512 kernel to a shared-memory kernel, which loses to `topkGatingSoftmax` above 4096 rows (see the microbenchmark below).
- **this PR**: `topk_gating` up to 4096 rows, which covers decode, verify, draft-extend and short prefill chunks. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.
- **#39986 Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024**: [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) sends 512-expert softmax routing to a Triton kernel, but only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and at most 128 rows, so on main it never fires for Qwen3.8. For this arm its gate was widened to hidden size 8192 and at most 1024 rows, enough for every decode and verify step in this sweep. Larger calls stay on `topkGatingSoftmax`.

Non-MTP:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline, `topkGatingSoftmax` | 1.0000 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0142 | 0.9872 |
| **this PR** | **1.0148** | 0.9859 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0160 | 0.9891 |

NEXTN MTP, 3 steps / eagle-topk 1 / 4 draft tokens:

| Arm | out tok/s geomean | accept length | TTFT geomean |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 1.0000 | ~4.00 | 1.0000 |
| aiter `topk_gating`, no ceiling | 1.0211 | ~4.00 | 0.9906 |
| **this PR** | **1.0222** | ~4.00 | 1.0009 |
| [#39986](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39986) Triton router, ceiling raised to 1024 | 1.0199 | ~4.00 | 0.9966 |

On v0.5.19 at page size 64, MTP gains more because verify and draft-extend add router launches per accepted token. On v0.5.20 at the default page size it gains less. Decode, verify and draft run in CUDA graphs; prefill runs eager (`prefill.backend='disabled'` in the server log, confirmed in the traces).

The #39986 Triton arm lands within 0.25% of this PR in both modes (0.12% above without MTP, 0.23% below with MTP), inside run-to-run spread, so end to end the two routers tie on Qwen3.8. The microbenchmark below shows where each kernel is faster and why this PR uses `topk_gating`.

End to end, the ceiling is worth 0.06% without MTP and 0.11% with it, inside run-to-run spread, so the case for it rests on the kernel census. Concurrency 4, TP0 trace, router launches (one per layer per forward):

| Arm | Cell | `topkGatingSoftmax` | E=512 kernel | aiter smem | Total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 8k/100 | 9476 | 0 | 0 | 9476 |
| baseline | 60k/100 | 10580 | 0 | 0 | 10580 |
| no ceiling | 8k/100 | 0 | 9200 | 276 | 9476 |
| no ceiling | 60k/100 | 0 | 9202 | 1380 | 10582 |
| **with ceiling** | 8k/100 | 276 | 9200 | 0 | 9476 |
| **with ceiling** | 60k/100 | 1380 | 9201 | 0 | 10581 |

Without a ceiling the prefill chunks (3 x 92 at 8k, 15 x 92 at 60k) land on aiter's slower shared-memory kernel; with it they go back to the legacy launcher and decode keeps the E=512 kernel.

Microbenchmark, gfx950, E=512, topk=10, softmax, bf16, median of 3 runs of 200 iters, us. Graph times 20 calls replayed from a CUDA graph, which is what decode sees. Triton is #39986's router.

| rows | eager: legacy | eager: `topk_gating` | eager: Triton | graph: legacy | graph: `topk_gating` | graph: Triton |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | 14.70 | **11.47** | 20.50 | 9.26 | 4.74 | **4.20** |
| 1024 | 15.56 | **12.28** | 21.18 | 9.42 | 5.50 | **4.75** |
| 2048 | 15.57 | **11.98** | 21.18 | 9.44 | 9.73 | **6.57** |
| 4096 | 15.53 | **12.00** | 21.61 | 11.50 | 11.63 | **10.78** |
| 5120 | 14.86 | **12.53** | 20.66 | **11.51** | 12.92 | 12.66 |
| 6144 | 15.02 | **13.68** | 20.82 | **11.58** | 14.10 | 14.55 |
| 7168 | **14.88** | 15.16 | 20.84 | **11.58** | 15.18 | 15.95 |
| 8192 | **14.89** | 16.55 | 20.85 | **11.64** | 16.51 | 17.93 |
| 16384 | **18.74** | 28.20 | 32.30 | **18.56** | 28.58 | 32.60 |

Graph times approximate kernel GPU time; eager times include launch overhead. On GPU time `topk_gating` leads through 1024 rows, is within 0.3 us of legacy at 2048 and 4096, and falls clearly behind from 5120 (12.92 vs 11.51 us, 28.58 vs 18.56 at 16384). Eager it stays ahead through 6144. The ceiling is 4096, the largest size where it is within noise on GPU time and still ahead eager.

Why `topk_gating` rather than extending #39986 to Qwen3.8. Under CUDA graphs the Triton kernel is the fastest of the three, 0.5-0.75 us per call up to 1024 rows. Decode, verify and draft replay from graphs, so that lead is real, but it is small next to a decode step: in the TP0 traces Triton saves 9-20 us per graph replay of 7.7-14.2 ms, 0.1-0.15% of GPU time, which is why the end-to-end numbers above tie.

Where they differ is eager. Triton is the slowest of the three there (about 21 us per call, against 12 us for `topk_gating` and 15 us for `topkGatingSoftmax`), but those times are mostly launch overhead, so this matters only for prefills short enough to be launch-bound, which this sweep did not measure.

The two PRs don't conflict. #39986 fires only at hidden size 4096 (Qwen3.5) and this PR only at 8192 (Qwen3.8) and 2560 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next). 

Without [Rocm/aiter5334](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5334), `topk_gating` falls back to a generic kernel at 8.0-9.2 us in graphs through 1024 rows, barely ahead of legacy.

Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, measured by @amd-nprotaso in review: output tok/s +2.17%, median TPOT 7.71 -> 7.54 ms (-2.25%). Accept length came out 0.7% higher on the patch side, so per decode step the gain is -1.4% (17.84 -> 17.59 ms). 

Not measured: other 512-expert models, which keep their current dispatch; short-prompt prefill (chunks <= 4096 rows) end to end; gfx942; anything outside TP8/EP1.

title: [JIT] Fuse FP8 KV-cache quantization into the prefix-valid commit kernel
author: JiaFengYu
body:
## Motivation

  MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid commits accepted-prefix KV rows after DFLASH verification. With --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 and checkpoint KV scales, the existing path performs:

  1. In-place scale division for K
  2. In-place scale division for V
  3. K cast to FP8
  4. V cast to FP8
  5. Triton byte-copy/scatter

  This is five GPU kernel launches per layer and introduces full HBM round-trips for the intermediate scaled tensors. Without explicit scales, the path still requires two casts plus the scatter kernel.

  This PR fuses source-dtype scaling, FP8 conversion, and prefix-valid scatter into one Triton kernel.

  ## Modifications

  - Added set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled_fp8 in cache_move.py.
      - Preserves the existing (batch, row, tile) structure, commit_lens early exit, and loc_2d indirection.
      - Uses element-based offsets and strides rather than byte-based addressing.
      - Receives typed source and FP8 destination pointers.
      - Divides in FP32 registers, rounds back to the source dtype to reproduce eager div_ semantics, then casts directly to the destination FP8 type.
      - Supports BF16, FP16, and FP32 sources.
      - Performs no intermediate allocation, source-tensor write, or HBM round-trip.

  - Added _set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_impl_fp8 in memory_pool.py.
      - Mirrors the original empty-input and contiguity guards.
      - Computes its grid, strides, and tile sizes in elements.
      - Passes zero-copy FP8 views of SGLang’s uint8-backed KV buffers so Triton infers correctly typed destination pointers.

  - Added narrow dispatch in MHATokenToKVPool.set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid.
      - Fused path requires an E4M3 KV cache and safely resolved K/V scales.
      - Python scalars and CPU scalar tensors are accepted directly.
      - GPU layer scale parameters use their existing k_scale_float/v_scale_float shadows without host synchronization.
      - Unsupported tensor scales, missing scales, non-FP8 caches, CPU execution, and asymmetric K/V rows retain the existing fallback.
      - The eager fallback continues using the original scale objects, including GPU tensors.

  - Threaded the draft model’s resolved quant_config into DFlashAttention’s RadixAttention.
      - This enables the existing Fp8KVCacheMethod for online-FP8 DFLASH drafts.
      - It initializes the KV scale parameters and float shadows required by the fused dispatch.
      - No new scale-loading mechanism or global configuration mutation was added.

  - Unlike the eager div_ path, the fused path does not mutate the input K/V tensors. Intermediate scaled values remain in registers and only the final FP8 cache is written.

  ## Accuracy Tests

  Added test_prefix_valid_fp8.py with coverage for:

  - Exact FP8 byte parity against the eager div_ → FP8 reference for BF16, FP16, and FP32 inputs.
  - Every tile-size branch and masked epilogue rows using row dimensions 63, 2048, and 4097.
  - Mixed per-request commit_lens.
  - Noncontiguous source tensors.
  - Separate K/V scales.
  - Representable FP8 limits, NaN, and signed zero.
  - Untouched destination slots.
  - GPU scale parameters with float shadows.
  - GPU tensor scales without float shadows taking the eager fallback.
  - Missing-scale fallback.
  - Non-FP8 cache fallback.
  - Input non-mutation on the fused path.

  Local CUDA validation:

  NVIDIA B200
  PyTorch 2.13.0+cu130
  Triton 3.7.1
  7 tests passed

  ROCm coverage is registered in jit-kernel-unit-test-amd but has not yet been run locally.

  ## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Test configuration

- **GPU:** NVIDIA B200
- **CUDA:** CUDA 13
- **Target model:** `NousResearch/Meta-Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct`
- **Draft model:** `z-lab/LLaMA3.1-8B-Instruct-DFlash-UltraChat`
- **KV-cache dtype:** `fp8_e4m3`
- **Draft quantization:** `fp8`
- **Attention backends:** Triton target and draft
- **Batch size:** 4
- **Output length:** 48 tokens per request
- **Acceptance length:** fixed at 4 to deterministically exercise prefix commits
- **CUDA graphs:** enabled

The benchmark-only baseline retained the same DFLASH quantization configuration and scales, but forced `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid` through the existing eager fallback.

### Kernel engagement

The profiler recorded 65 prefix commits in both variants:

| Variant | Legacy `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled` | Fused `set_kv_buffer_prefix_valid_tiled_fp8` |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Eager fallback | 65 | 0 |
| Fused | 0 | 65 |

This confirms that the A/B comparison exercised the intended implementations without mixing the legacy and fused commit paths.

### Prefix-commit GPU time

| Variant | Kernel sequence | Median GPU time per layer |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| Eager fallback | K division + V division + K FP8 cast + V FP8 cast + byte-copy store | 14.528 us |
| Fused | Required source-layout copy + fused FP8 quantize/store | 4.864 us |
| **Speedup** |  | **2.99x** |

The fused Triton kernel alone measured 1.951 us per layer. The 4.864 us result above includes the preceding source-layout copy and is therefore the fair implementation-level comparison.

This establishes a **2.99x improvement in the prefix-valid FP8 commit GPU cluster for this fixed-shape B200 workload**. It is not a claim of a 2.99x end-to-end request speedup.

### End-to-end A/B

A separate process-level benchmark ran 10 alternating A/B pairs. Each variant received 10 warmup batches followed by 100 measured batch-4 requests per pair.

The mean paired request-p50 saving was 0.25 ms, with a 95% bootstrap confidence interval of `[-0.96, +1.11]` ms. Because the confidence interval crosses zero, no statistically significant end-to-end latency improvement is claimed.



  ## Validation State

  - Focused GPU tests: passed
  - B200 live DFLASH server startup: passed
  - Batched request with deterministic prefix commits: passed
  - Fused-kernel trace engagement: confirmed
  - CUDA fallback preservation: passed
  - ROCm execution: pending CI
  - Controlled latency benchmark: not run
  - Rebase onto latest upstream main: pending

  ## Checklist

  - [x] Format code according to the Format code with pre-commit (https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
  - [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests (https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
  - [ ] Update documentation according to Write documentations (https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
  - [ ] Provide controlled speed benchmark results according to Benchmark the speed (https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
  - [x] Follow the SGLang code-style guidance (https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Feat] [NPU] kimi-k3: Support DCP with shared compact communication
author: qybnb
body:
## Motivation Enable decode context parallelism (DCP) for Kimi-K3 on Ascend NPU, including DSPARK speculative decoding. Sharding the target model's MLA KV cache across DCP ranks reduces per-rank KV storage for a given logical context capacity. ## Implementation - **KV layout:** distribute target MLA latent and RoPE buffers by physical page. Localize cache-write locations to the owning rank, while keeping draft KV replicated. - **Prefill/extend:** all-gather the cached target prefix and restore token order before the existing MLA attention computation. Replicated draft workers read their complete local cache. - **Decode/target verify:** reuse the common Q all-gather, compute attention over each rank's local KV pages, and merge partial results through compact AllToAll with BF16/FP16 outputs and FP32 LSE. Eager target verification with no real queries returns zero partial outputs and `-inf` LSE for collective participation. - **Eager and graph execution:** derive rank-local KV lengths, block tables, and per-query visibility from page ownership. Graph replay uses the backend's prepared local CPU lengths and pads graph-only request rows with zero; the FIA CPU length mirror is required. - **P/D transfer:** support prefill DCP=1 to decode DCP=N with Ascend page transfers. Hybrid MLA uses the common layer-ID pairing helper across PP stages and selects local target pages and global replicated draft pages directly in `AscendKVManager.send_kvcache_dcp()` using `num_draft_entries`. DSA retains its per-entry pool layout metadata; KDA state uses its existing state-transfer path. Shared pool and prefill files are unchanged. ## Validation - 17 CPU regression tests pass with production imports in an isolated CANN 9.2 overlay. Coverage includes 20 hybrid PP/draft/buffer-width transfer combinations that reject layout-helper calls, DSA index-buffer transfer addresses, and invalid metadata/draft-count rejection. - CPU prefix-reconstruction checks pass across 450 configurations and 2,104 rank outputs, covering DCP2/4/8, token/page interleaving, partial pages, mixed and empty prefixes, and 128K/512K contexts. - Syntax, repository-selected Ruff rules, Ruff formatting, isort, and diff checks pass for the tested files. Two existing E402 findings remain in `npu_graph_runner.py`. These CPU checks do not validate native NPU kernels or full-model serving. Full-model accuracy, throughput/latency, and P/D end-to-end validation for the current head remain pending. The model results below are reference measurements and have not been reproduced on this head. ## Run Four-node DSPARK example. Replace the paths, node addresses, distributed initialization address, and network interface with the deployment values. Ascend DCP requires `ASCEND_USE_FIA=1`; this example uses `--dcp-comm-backend a2a`.
Launch script ```bash #!/usr/bin/env bash set -eo pipefail CODE_PATH=XXX MODEL_PATH=XXX DRAFT_MODEL_PATH=XXX cd "$CODE_PATH" mkdir -p logs/manual_dcp unset http_proxy https_proxy HTTP_PROXY HTTPS_PROXY ALL_PROXY all_proxy export NO_PROXY=XXX export no_proxy="$NO_PROXY" unset PYTHONPATH unset ASCEND_CUSTOM_OPP_PATH source /usr/local/Ascend/ascend-toolkit/set_env.sh source /usr/local/Ascend/nnal/atb/set_env.sh export PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 export SGLANG_SET_CPU_AFFINITY=1 export SGLANG_ONE_VISIBLE_DEVICE_PER_PROCESS=1 export SGLANG_NPU_USE_TRITON_PREFIX_KV_CACHE_STORE=1 export SGLANG_K3_SHARED_EXPERTS_ATTN_TP=1 export SGLANG_K3_DENSE_MLP_ATTN_TP=1 export SGLANG_ENABLE_OVERLAP_PLAN_STREAM=1 export SGLANG_RAGGED_VERIFY_MODE=static export SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_PROPOSAL=0 export SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=0 export SGLANG_DSPARK_STACKED_CTX_KV=0 export SGLANG_DSPARK_EMBED_IN_GRAPH=0 export ASCEND_USE_FIA=1 export SGLANG_USE_FIA_NZ=0 export SGLANG_NPU_USE_FIAS_V2_BSND=0 export PYTORCH_NPU_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True export HCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp196s0f0 export GLOO_SOCKET_IFNAME=enp196s0f0 export HCCL_IF_BASE_PORT=18000 export HCCL_NPU_SOCKET_PORT_RANGE=18000-18100 export HCCL_BUFFSIZE=200 export DEEPEP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE=1800 export HCCL_OP_EXPANSION_MODE=AIV export STREAMS_PER_DEVICE=32 export DEEP_NORMAL_MODE_USE_INT8_QUANT=1 export SGLANG_DEEPEP_NUM_MAX_DISPATCH_TOKENS_PER_RANK=128 export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_ROUND=64 export DEEPEP_NORMAL_LONG_SEQ_PER_ROUND_TOKENS=512 unset DEEP_USE_MODE DEEPEP_MC2_COMM_ALG DCP_HCCL_BUFFSIZE unset MOE_ENABLE_TOPK_NEG_ONE SGLANG_NPU_FUSED_MOE_MODE unset ENABLE_PROFILING SGLANG_NPU_PROFILING unset SGLANG_K3_TRACE_STATE_FILE SGLANG_K3_TRACE_HIDDEN_FILE unset ASCEND_RT_VISIBLE_DEVICES ASCEND_LAUNCH_BLOCKING unset SGLANG_ENABLE_CP_V2 SGLANG_ENABLE_SPEC_V2 unset SGLANG_MAMBA_SSM_DTYPE SGLANG_MAMBA_CONV_DTYPE NODE_IPS=(XXX) LOCAL_IPS=" $(hostname -I) " NODE_RANK=-1 for i in "${!NODE_IPS[@]}"; do if [[ "$LOCAL_IPS" == *" ${NODE_IPS[$i]} "* ]]; then NODE_RANK="$i" break fi done if [[ "$NODE_RANK" == "-1" ]]; then echo "ERROR: 无法识别节点，hostname -I: $LOCAL_IPS" >&2 exit 1 fi LOG_FILE="$PWD/logs/manual_dcp/rank${NODE_RANK}_$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ).log" echo "node_rank=$NODE_RANK log=$LOG_FILE" python3 -m sglang.launch_server \ --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true}' \ --dist-init-addr XXX \ --nnodes 4 \ --node-rank "$NODE_RANK" \ --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --tokenizer-path "$MODEL_PATH" \ --trust-remote-code \ --attention-backend ascend \ --device npu \ --quantization modelslim \ --dtype bfloat16 \ --tp-size 64 \ --enable-dp-attention \ --dp-size 4 \ --enable-dp-lm-head \ --enable-shared-experts-attn-tp \ --enable-dense-mlp-attn-tp \ --dcp-size 2 \ --dcp-comm-backend a2a \ --mem-fraction-static 0.72 \ --chunked-prefill-size 8192 \ --max-running-requests 64 \ --cuda-graph-bs-decode 1 4 16 \ --disable-radix-cache \ --disable-custom-all-reduce \ --enable-metrics \ --reasoning-parser kimi_k3 \ --moe-a2a-backend deepep \ --deepep-mode auto \ --expert-balancedness-report-mode off \ --speculative-algorithm DSPARK \ --speculative-draft-model-path "$DRAFT_MODEL_PATH" \ --speculative-draft-model-quantization unquant \ --speculative-dspark-block-size 7 \ --speculative-attention-mode decode \ --speculative-draft-attention-backend ascend \ --linear-attn-verify-backend triton \ --speculative-eagle-topk 1 \ --watchdog-timeout 9000 \ --host 0.0.0.0 \ --port 15010 \ 2>&1 | tee "$LOG_FILE" ```

title: [AMD][DSV4] moe: enable shared-expert fusion on the grouped-topk path (megamoe)
author: karverma-amd
body:
> Stacked on top of the Aiter MegaMoEv2 integration, **sgl-project/sglang#35619** — that PR adds the FlyDSL MegaMoEv2 backend but requires `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` on ROCm because of the bug below. This change removes that restriction. Base is the `20260922` image commit; #35619 is bind-mounted on top for the megamoe path.

## Motivation

`select_experts` already computes `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate` — `0` on the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path, because the shared expert is appended afterwards by `_post_process_topk_ids` — and uses it at the **non-grouped** gate call sites. But the two **grouped** call sites (`grouped_topk` / `biased_grouped_topk`) still pass the raw `num_fused_shared_experts`, so on the per-rank fused shared-slot path the gate double-emits the shared marker:

- a routed expert is dropped — the gate is asked for `K_routed = top_k - num_fused_shared_experts` and spends one of those slots on its own marker (top-6 → top-5); and
- that marker lands at id `num_experts`, which the DeepEP per-rank remap shifts one past the end of the expert space (`384 → 392` on EP8, valid ids `0..391`).

DeepSeek-V4 routes through grouped `biased_grouped_topk`, so it hits this path. On the FlyDSL MegaMoEv2 backend (#35619) the out-of-range id faults the dispatch with `HSA_STATUS_ERROR_EXCEPTION 0x1016` — which is exactly why #35619 has to run with `--disable-shared-experts-fusion`, forcing the shared expert to run as a separate per-layer GEMM instead of being fused into the megamoe dispatch/combine chain.

## What changed

* `python/sglang/srt/layers/moe/topk.py`: pass `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate` (not `num_fused_shared_experts`) to `grouped_topk` and `biased_grouped_topk` in `select_experts`.

Two lines. No-op off the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path (there `num_fused_shared_experts_for_gate == num_fused_shared_experts`). No behavior change on CUDA / non-fused-shared-slot paths.

## Validation (MI355X gfx950, DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813, TP8 / DP8 attention / EP8, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`)

With the fix, `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` boots and serves — no `0x1016`; the dispatch/combine runs at `topk=7, local_experts=49` (48 routed + 1 fused shared per rank), confirming the shared expert is fused into the megamoe chain rather than run as a separate GEMM.

**Accuracy** — 5-shot GSM8K:

| arm | accuracy | invalid |
| --- | -------- | ------- |
| shared-off (`--disable-shared-experts-fusion`) | 0.940 | 0.000 |
| shared-on (`--enforce-shared-experts-fusion`) | **0.970** | 0.000 |

Same fp4-MoE run-to-run band, no regression (200 questions; the gap is within noise).

**Throughput / interactivity A/B** (`random`, ISL/OSL 8192/1024, `num-prompts = 4 × conc`), shared-off vs shared-on:

| conc | out tok/s off → on | Mean TPOT off → on | Δ TPOT |
| ---- | ------------------ | ------------------ | ------ |
| 256  | 2814.5 → 2775.9    | 74.2 → **67.9 ms** | **−8.4%** |
| 512  | 3974.6 → 3873.3    | 90.8 → 90.1 ms     |  (flat) |

Fusing the shared expert removes a separate per-layer GEMM from the decode critical path: a **−8% mean-TPOT (decode interactivity) win at conc256** and +5.5% per-rank decode throughput; flat at conc512 (workload-dependent). Aggregate output tok/s is within noise at ISL 8192 (prefill/TTFT-dominated).

## Commands

Server (shared-on arm; drop `SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE` etc. and swap `--enforce-` for `--disable-shared-experts-fusion` for the off arm):

```bash
# image: lmsysorg/sglang-rocm:v0.5.20-rocm724-mi35x-20260922  (+ #35619 srt + this patch)
SGLANG_USE_AITER=1 SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE=1 \
SGLANG_AMD_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE_MTPR=8192 SGLANG_AMD_FLYDSL_MEGA_QUANT=a8w4 \
MORI_SHMEM_HEAP_SIZE=17179869184 MORI_EP_LAUNCH_CONFIG_MODE=AUTO \
SGLANG_SHARED_EXPERT_TP1=0 SGLANG_DP_SHARED_EXPERT_LOCAL=0 \
SGLANG_DP_USE_GATHERV=0 SGLANG_DP_USE_REDUCE_SCATTER=0 GPU_MAX_HW_QUEUES=5 \
SGLANG_HACK_FLASHMLA_BACKEND=unified_kv_triton AITER_BF16_FP8_MOE_BOUND=0 \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path <DeepSeek-V4-Pro-0813> --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --ep-size 8 \
  --enable-dp-lm-head --enable-dp-attention-local-control-broadcast \
  --moe-a2a-backend megamoe --moe-dense-tp-size 1 --enforce-shared-experts-fusion \
  --attention-backend dsv4 --enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer \
  --page-size 256 --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.10 --kv-cache-dtype fp8_e4m3 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 65536 --mem-fraction-static 0.85 \
  --max-running-requests 512 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 128
```

Throughput A/B:

```bash
python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang-oai --model <served-name> \
  --dataset-name random --random-input-len 8192 --random-output-len 1024 \
  --random-range-ratio 1.0 --num-prompts $((4*CONC)) --max-concurrency CONC --disable-tqdm
```

Accuracy:

```bash
python3 benchmark/gsm8k/bench_sglang.py --num-questions 200 --parallel 64 --num-shots 5 --port <port>
```

## Checklist

- [x] Two-line change; no-op off the per-rank fused shared-slot / aiter path
- [x] Enables `--enforce-shared-experts-fusion` on FlyDSL MegaMoEv2 (no `0x1016`; `topk=7`)
- [x] GSM8K accuracy preserved (0.970 vs 0.940 baseline band)
- [x] Decode-interactivity A/B measured (conc 256/512), −8% TPOT at conc256
- [x] Stacked on #35619

Co-authored-by: Cursor <cursoragent@cursor.com>

title: dsv4.1-amd: gfx950 MXFP8 matmul kernels and fp8-grid producers
author: kevin-mii
body:
> This PR was "stack 1/4" of the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD series (#41018 to #41021). It now follows the CUDA dsv4.1 layout (#39646, #39652, #39653, #39656, #39664, then #38798): kernel PRs by domain, each on `main` with no callers, then one integration PR. This is the first kernel PR.

## Summary
- Native MXFP8 dense route for 32x32-block ue8m0 fp8 checkpoints on gfx950 (`ops/quantization/mxfp8_native_amd_gfx95.py`, `csrc/deepseek_v4/mxfp8_gemv_gfx95.cuh`): the weight is reordered once at load into the scaled-MFMA lane order and stays fp8, with K zero-padded to a multiple of 128 and the activation tail masked. M <= 32 runs a HIP GEMV on `v_mfma_scale_f32_16x16x128_f8f6f4`, larger M a Triton `tl.dot_scaled` GEMM. The input is bf16, bf16 on the fp8 grid, or fp8 + ue8m0 scales, and all three give the same bits.
- Tile tables (`mxfp8_gemv_gfx95_configs.json`) tuned at DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's TP4 shapes, fastest config per M bucket; `benchmark/kernels/quantization/tuning_mxfp8_native_gfx95.py` regenerates a shape's rows.
- fp8-grid helpers in `mxfp8_amd_gfx95.py`: `fake_quant_fp8_activation` / `fp8_grid_quantize` with the ue8m0 rule of CUDA's `per_token_group_quant`, the bf16-dequant linear for shapes the native kernels cannot tile, and the `Fp8GridActivation` / `Mxfp8Activation` wrappers that let a consumer skip its own quant.
- Fused producers of those wrappers: RMSNorm (+ residual) + quant (`rmsnorm_fake_quant_amd_gfx95.py`), clamped SiLU-mul + quant (`silu_and_mul_clamp_hip.py`), and the wo_a batched GEMM with the quant in its epilogue (`gfx95_batched_gemm_bf16_fp8_grid.py`, fixed-order split-K up to 64 rows).
- Model call sites are in the integration PR of this stack.

## Changes to existing kernels
- `mxfp8_amd_gfx95.py`: new code appended; existing functions and callers unchanged. Every other file is new and HIP-only, and the `.cuh` refuses to build for any target but gfx950.

## Verification
- MI350X (ROCm 10.0.0, torch 2.11, triton 3.8, aiter at the Dockerfile pin): `test_mxfp8_amd_gfx95.py` and `test_fp8_grid_producers_gfx95.py` pass (fp64 references, bitwise agreement of the three input encodings including non-finite activations, bitwise match to aiter `batched_gemm_bf16`), and so does the existing `test_minimax_m3_mxfp8.py`.
- With the integration PR's callers, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at TP4 loads every dense block-FP8 linear on the native route. Tuned tiles are up to 2.2x faster than the defaults; the native K tail takes 0.63-0.93x the time of the bf16-dequant route at (5120, 576) up to M 4096.
- Not executed on this branch alone: end-to-end serving and accuracy.

title: [Feat] hicache: Support MLA DCP with HiCache L3(file/mooncake)
author: ByronHsu
body:
## Why?

1. HiCache L3 rejects DCP.
2. This stack adds MLA + DCP + L3 support:
   - #41187 (this PR): file storage.
   - #41265: Mooncake storage.
   - #41591: hybrid MLA/KDA storage.

## What?

1. Allow file L3 with DCP for one materialized MLA host pool using `layer_first`, `page_first`, or `page_first_direct`. Keep existing validation; split buffers, separate scale buffers, and additional pools remain unsupported.
2. Pass `is_storage_owner` to file eviction instead of deriving ownership from `is_mla_model`. Select one writer per distinct MLA shard, avoiding duplicate writes and eviction accounting:

```text
TP=4 / DCP=2:
rank 0 writes shard 0 -> ranks 0,2 read
rank 1 writes shard 1 -> ranks 1,3 read
2 files per logical page
```

3. Translate logical page positions into physical rows and count only complete logical pages:

```text
64 physical tokens/shard x 2 = 128 logical tokens
logical start 256 -> physical start 128 on each rank

Both shards present -> complete page hit
Either shard missing -> stop before that page
```

KV-format/layout key separation remains deferred with a TODO; engines sharing files must use compatible formats and layouts.

## Tests?

- Six focused CPU tests added to existing CI-registered file-backend and host-pool tests. No new test files.
- CPU regressions: **62 tests and 40 subtests passed**, covering DCP keys/ownership, page mapping, file eviction, attachment, and prefetch.
- **Previously validated manually on H200**, DeepSeek-V2-Lite-Chat, BF16, TP=4/DCP=2, `page_first`, write-through, complete-prefetch waiting: **1 passed in 149.48 s**.

```text
Cold writer:  1,025 input tokens -> 16 files, zero cache hits
Fresh reader: 1,024 L3 tokens    -> identical output IDs
Missing shard in page 2:        -> 128 L3 tokens, identical output IDs
```

- Ruff, import ordering, registered-test validation, and whitespace checks passed. The history rewrite preserves the cleaned Git tree exactly. CI status is tracked below.

title: [Perf] Mamba2 selective_state_update up to 2x faster on B200 via 8x1 launch config for dstate 128 (+7.5% Nemotron-3-Super serving)
author: TarzanZhao
body:
## Summary

The Mamba2 decode kernel `selective_state_update` is memory bound: each step it reads and writes every request's fp32 SSM state. For 64 < dstate <= 128 it launches with `BLOCK_SIZE_M=4, num_warps=4`, so each thread handles only 4 elements. That is too few loads in flight to fill HBM, and on B200 the kernel stays near 3.1 TB/s.

This PR changes that one entry to `BLOCK_SIZE_M=8, num_warps=1`, 32 elements per thread. On one B200 the kernel is **1.19x, 1.86x and 2.02x faster at batch 8, 128 and 512** (3.1 -> 6.3 TB/s at batch 512), with bitwise-identical outputs. Nemotron-3-Super on 8x B200 serves **+7.5%** output tokens/s. H200 numbers are in the comment below.

### Speedup Result

**Kernel alone**, one B200, CUDA graph timing with cold L2 (headdim 64, dstate 128, fp32 state, bf16 inputs, 16 heads per GPU as in Nemotron-3-Super TP8):

| batch | baseline, us | this PR, us | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| 8 | 4.77 | 4.02 | 1.19x |
| 128 | 44.7 | 24.1 | 1.86x |
| 512 | 173.5 | 85.7 | 2.02x |

Other launch configs at the same batches, all bitwise identical to the baseline. Of the 20 configs I tried, `(8, 1)` is the fastest at batch 128 and 512, and 4% behind the fastest, `(8, 4)`, at batch 8.

| (BLOCK_SIZE_M, num_warps) | batch 8, us | batch 128, us | batch 512, us |
|---|---|---|---|
| (4, 4), baseline | 4.77 | 44.7 | 173.5 |
| (4, 1) | 4.26 | 36.6 | 138.1 |
| **(8, 1), this PR** | 4.02 | 24.1 | 85.7 |
| (16, 1) | 4.04 | 24.2 | 86.1 |
| (16, 4) | 3.96 | 25.6 | 94.7 |

**End to end**, 8x B200 (TP8), `sglang.bench_serving`, ShareGPT, 1000 prompts, request rate inf:

| | baseline (`567d5925fe`) | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| output token throughput, mean of 3 | 10,505 tok/s (10,499 / 10,516 / 10,499) | 11,289 tok/s (11,283 / 11,262 / 11,321) | **+7.5%** |
| peak GPU memory per GPU, max of 3 | 164.2 GB | 163.9 GB | |

## Correctness Verification

I ran the baseline and this branch as servers and compared greedy completions for the same requests: the token id and logprob of every generated token. I also ran the kernel alone with both configs from the same inputs and initial state, and compared its output and updated state bit for bit. I set the tolerance before the runs: exact equality, because the baseline server reproduces its outputs bit for bit across restarts. The scripts are not part of this PR, and I can share them.

Every compared value is identical.

| recorded | baseline vs this PR | tolerance |
|---|---|---|
| greedy token ids and logprobs, 64 ShareGPT prompts x 128 tokens, 3 server runs | identical | exact |
| same, 8 prompts of 3.2k to 3.5k tokens x 128 tokens, 3 server runs | identical | exact |
| kernel output and updated state, 5 head counts x 184 batch sizes (920 points) | bitwise identical | exact |

## Checklist

- [x] Format: `ruff format` and `ruff check --select=F401,F821,UP037` (the pre-commit rules) pass on the changed file.
- [ ] Unit tests: no new test. `test/registered/layers/mamba/test_mamba_ssm.py` covers this path and passes, 340 passed on B200.
- [ ] Documentation: none needed. The change is internal to a kernel launcher.
- [x] Accuracy and speed results: above.
- [x] Code style: one-value change inside the existing table, no new comments.

Scope: this affects every model that runs Mamba2 decode through the default Triton `selective_state_update` with 64 < dstate <= 128, on any GPU. I measured only B200. For the same shape, vLLM's tuned configs for H100 and H200 mostly pick 1 or 2 warps rather than 4x4, which points the same way but is not a measurement.

<details>
<summary>Details: hardware, model, full command, traces</summary>

**Hardware.** 8x NVIDIA B200 (183 GB, sm_100), driver 580.126.20, CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0+cu130, triton 3.7.1, flashinfer 0.6.18, sglang at `567d5925fe`.

**Model.** `nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16`, TP8. 88 layers: 40 Mamba2, 40 MoE, 8 attention. Per rank the Mamba2 layers have 16 heads, headdim 64, dstate 128, and an fp32 SSM cache (`mamba_ssm_cache_dtype` in the checkpoint config).

**Kernel measurement.**
- Shapes follow the model: state pool `[pool, H, 64, 128]` fp32 with random `state_batch_indices`; x `[bs, H, 64]` and B/C `[bs, 1, 128]` are strided views of one tensor; dt, A, D and dt_bias are stride-0 broadcasts.
- Timing: max(20, K) calls captured in one CUDA graph, 20 replays timed with CUDA events, median of 5 repeats. Call i reads state slot set (i mod K); the K sets are disjoint and together hold at least 3x the 126.5 MiB L2, so every call reads state from HBM, as in real decode where each layer's state is touched once per step. Without this rotation, batches whose state fits in L2 looked up to 2.6x faster than they are.
- Speed tables: 16 heads, batch 8, 128, 512, 20 launch configs. Bitwise check (Correctness table): heads 8, 16, 32, 64, 128; batch 1 to 64, then every 8 up to 1024.
- The config is switched through a temporary override in the launcher, so both configs run the same compiled kernel code.

**End-to-end measurement.**
- Measured on base `567d5925fe` with only this one-line change applied. The branch is rebased onto `ec070ec8c8`; `mamba_ssm.py` is identical at both, and `test_mamba_ssm.py` passes on the rebased branch.
- Both versions run the same server command, including `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1024`. That flag is not part of this PR; without it, decode batches above 512 run without CUDA graphs on this workload, which hides kernel differences.
- 3 interleaved runs per version on one node, warm caches, ShareGPT 1000 prompts, seed 42.
- Throughput is measured over the `Benchmark duration` window of `bench_serving`: first request sent to last response, excluding server startup, dataset loading and warmup.

**Server**, both versions:
```
python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path nvidia/NVIDIA-Nemotron-3-Super-120B-A12B-BF16 \
  --tp 8 --trust-remote-code --disable-radix-cache \
  --model-loader-extra-config '{"enable_multithread_load": true, "num_threads": 50}' \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 1024
```

**Client:**
```
python -m sglang.bench_serving --dataset-name sharegpt --num-prompts 1000 --seed 42 --request-rate inf --flush-cache
```

**Settings tried and rejected.**
- `--mamba-backend flashinfer`: similar end-to-end speed, but greedy outputs are not bitwise identical to the Triton kernel.

title: [diffusion] Run an all-valid attention mask on the backend's unmasked kernel
author: mickqian
body:
## Problem

On sm100 the default attention backend resolves to `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA`, but `USPAttention`'s masked local path opens its varlen fast path only for `backend == FA`. Every other backend gets a dense additive mask for `torch.nn.functional.scaled_dot_product_attention`, and any mask moves SDPA off flash and cuDNN onto PyTorch's `fmha_cutlassF_*_sm80` kernel, even when the mask masks nothing.

Ideogram4 passes such a mask on both guidance branches at batch 1: its text is never padded at batch 1, so `segment_ids > 0` is all true. Every attention call on B200 therefore took the cutlassF path:

- torch profile of the denoising loop: attention = **54% of GPU time on 1×B200, 47% at TP2**, all in `fmha_cutlassF_bf16_aligned_32x128_gmem_sm80`
- per call (`[1, 18, 4126, 256]` bf16): **2.19 ms with the mask, 0.81 ms without**

It is also consistent with Ideogram4 measuring only ~9% faster on B200 than on H200, against 1.7-2.6× for the other models: on Hopper the default backend is FA, whose varlen path already treats an all-valid mask as dense.

## Fix

When `attn_mask_meta` shows every key valid (its index count equals the mask's element count, known on the host, no device sync), the masked local path runs the backend's own unmasked kernel. Segmented-prefix inputs (Qwen-Image) are concatenated first, so the prefix is kept. Masks with real padding, and meta without indices (padding-gap meta), keep the masked path. The FA backend is untouched (its varlen branch returns before this point), and so are the sequence-parallel paths.

## Validation (4×B200)

- Unit: the new `test/unit/test_usp_all_valid_key_mask.py` drives `USPAttention.forward` through the masked local branch with real varlen meta. An all-valid mask runs the backend kernel once and matches unmasked attention; a real padding mask, and padding-gap meta without indices, keep the masked path; a segmented prefix is concatenated before dispatch. The two backend-kernel tests fail on `main`. The neighbouring attention/mask unit tests (ring tail-pad, K/V gather, varlen meta, replicated prefix, Ideogram4, BCG padding) pass.

- Ideogram4 serving, default B200 command (`--tp-size 2`), warmup then 5 measured requests, interleaved main/PR/main/PR on the same node:

  | | round 1 | round 2 |
  |---|---:|---:|
  | `main` | 3.424 s | 3.427 s |
  | this PR | **2.192 s** | **2.205 s** |

- Steady denoising step (single `sglang generate`, no warmup): 1 GPU 277.0 → 158.2 ms, TP2 160.8 → 126.1 ms.
- Kernels (torch profile, TP2): attention 78.0 → 8.7 ms per step. cuDNN 9.20 (bundled with torch 2.13) has no head_dim-256 kernel on sm100, so `DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA` takes its FA4 fallback (`sm100_hd256_2cta_fmha_forward`, 128 µs per call against 1104 µs for cutlassF).
- Output: PR vs `main` PSNR 26.2 dB at TP2 and 26.5 dB on 1 GPU, against 22.7 dB between TP2 and 1 GPU on `main` itself. Ideogram4's guidance amplifies FP reordering; the all-valid additive mask is exactly zero, so the math is unchanged.

- Qwen-Image-2512 and Z-Image-Turbo, which also pass masks with varlen meta, produce bitwise-identical images before and after: at batch 1 they do not reach this branch.
- The second commit logs the cuDNN → FlashAttention fallback once per process. Routing these calls to the backend kernel made Ideogram4 log it once per attention layer, 68 times per start.

title: [VLM] Introduce FA4 into ViT for SM100/SM103
author: yuan-luo
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

This PR is to fill gaps in FA4 path on Blackwell:
1. **The softmax row max ignores an sm_103 instruction.** Blackwell Ultra adds `tcgen05.ld.red`, a TMEM load that also returns a per-thread reduction of the loaded values. We can use it to get each row's max for free while reading S out of TMEM. Currently SGLang FA4 forward does not: on B300 every softmax step still reduces 128 values per row with FMNMX3.
2. **ViT attention on B300 falls back to Triton.** #25570 switched the default multimodal attention backend on SM103 from `fa4` to `triton_attn` because "FA4 is not yet validated on B300". Measured on B300, FA4's kernel is 2–20x faster than the Triton kernel on ViT shapes (head dims 64/72/80/128) and matches it numerically, so B300 ViTs pay a large, avoidable cost.
3. **The ViT CUDA graph runners do not support `fa4`.** `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` only handles `triton_attn` and `fa3`; with `fa4` (already the default on SM100) the server dies at startup with `AssertionError: cu_seqlens must be a torch.Tensor`. Changing the SM103 default without fixing this would break every B300 deployment that turned the ViT graph on. The graph is also what removes FA4's per-call host overhead for small images (see Speed Tests).


## Modifications

- `flash_fwd_sm100.py`: on sm_103, build a second TMEM copy with `tcgen05.LdRed32x32bOp(redOp=MAX)`. In `softmax_step`, tiles that need no masking (`mask_fn is None`) in kernels without `score_mod`/bias load S with it — one `cute.copy_atom_call` per 32-column chunk, each also returning that chunk's max — and pass the reduced max to the softmax. Masked tiles keep the plain load and the software max, because the hardware max is taken over the raw S. On the tiles where it is used the hardware max equals the software reduction exactly, so **outputs are bit-identical** to the current kernel. The first-iteration tile is always masked (`mask_seqlen=True`), so only steady-state tiles change.
- `softmax.py`: `SoftmaxSm100.update_row_max` accepts an optional precomputed `tile_row_max`; everything after the max (fast `exp2`, rescale threshold) is unchanged.
- `interface.py`: `SGLANG_FA4_TMEM_LOAD_RED_MAX` (default `1`; `0` restores the FMNMX reduction). It is part of the compile key, so both variants can coexist in one process. The flag is ignored on non-sm_103 GPUs.
- `vision.py`: the platform default multimodal attention backend is `fa4` for all compute capability 10.x (SM100 and SM103). Explicit `--mm-attention-backend` and per-model overrides (e.g. Kimi-K3-VL's own SM103 heuristic) are unchanged.
- `vision.py` (`VisionFlash4Attention`): accepts the graph runners' `[cu_seqlens, max_seqlen]` list. Unlike the fa3/triton wrappers it keys off the argument type, not the env var, so models without a graph runner keep passing tensors when `SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1` is set globally.
- `vit_cuda_graph_runner.py`, `internvl_vit_cuda_graph_runner.py`: pass `fa4` the same layout as `fa3`. FA4 JIT-compiles a kernel variant the first time it sees a configuration, which must not happen inside stream capture; for windowed ViTs (Qwen2.5-VL) the generic runner therefore warms up both the windowed and the full-attention layout before capturing (it previously warmed up only block 0's layout). The InternVL runner already warms up every layer eagerly.
- `test_vision_backend_selection.py`: covers the CUDA default per compute capability (9.0→fa3, 10.0→fa4, 10.3→fa4, 12.0→triton_attn) and `VisionFlash4Attention` with list-form and tensor seqlens, with the graph env var on and off.

## Accuracy Tests

All on 8x B300 (sm_103, 148 SMs), CUDA 13.0, torch 2.13.0, nvidia-cutlass-dsl 4.6.2.

**FA4 kernel, bit-exactness.** 16 configurations run on the unpatched tree and on this branch with the flag on; outputs and LSE are identical in every case (`torch.equal`): causal / non-causal, varlen, chunked prefill (q < k), GQA and `pack_gqa`, head dims 64 / 96 / 128 / (192,128) (incl. the 2-CTA path), sliding window, learnable sink, softcap (reducing load disabled there), split-KV, paged KV (page 128 TMA and page 64 cp.async), and fp8 e4m3 with descales. The compiled PTX (`.target sm_103a`) contains 4 `tcgen05.ld.red` instructions with the flag on and none with it off.

**FA4 unit tests.** `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_flash_attention_4.py`: 330 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed.

**ViT attention, FA4 vs Triton.** sglang's own `VisionFlash4Attention` and `VisionTritonAttention` on the same inputs: max abs difference 5e-4 – 1.6e-2 in bf16 across GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V4.1 shapes (d=64) and Qwen2.5-VL shapes (d=80, windowed and full attention), consistent with bf16 rounding.

**End to end, MMMU validation (900 questions)** Two servers from the same base commit, one per GPU:

| model (serving config) | ViT | `triton_attn` (current B300 default) | `fa4` (this PR) | same final answer | same-config baseline |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (1 GPU) | eager | 51.7% | 51.8% | 871 / 900 (96.8%) | eager vs graph, same backend: 887–891 / 900 |
| Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct (1 GPU) | CUDA graph | 52.0% | 51.6% | 875 / 900 (97.2%) | (same as above) |
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (TP4 + EP4, cookbook flags, chat mode; 32-layer d=64 ViT) | eager | 67.8% / 66.9% / 67.2% (3 runs) | 68.0% | 830 / 900 (92.2%) | two identical `triton_attn` servers: 834 / 900 (92.7%) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

All on B300 (sm_103, 148 SMs, 1 GPU per measurement unless noted). Kernel numbers are CUDA-graph timed unless marked eager; "eager" includes the Python wrapper, as an un-graphed ViT sees it.

**`tcgen05.ld.red.max` in the FA4 forward, ViT shapes**

Command: `python benchmark/kernels/attention/bench_flash_attention_tmem_red_max.py`. It calls FA4 the way `VisionFlash4Attention` does (varlen, non-causal, no LSE, 16 heads, bf16).

Each of 10 rounds times the flag off and on back to back, alternating which goes first. "off" and "on" are the best round of each. "paired" is the median of the per-round off/on ratios, and "wins" counts the rounds where on was faster. Outputs are bit-identical for every shape.

| input | head dim | off | on | paired speedup | wins |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 80 (Qwen2.5-VL) | 648.8 us | 588.0 us | **1.075x** | 10/10 |
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 72 (Qwen3-VL) | 703.9 us | 681.6 us | 1.039x | 10/10 |
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 64 (InternViT, GLM / DeepSeek-V4 ViT) | 527.4 us | 518.2 us | 1.023x | 8/10 |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 80 | 438.2 us | 415.7 us | 1.048x | 10/10 |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 64 | 360.5 us | 356.8 us | 1.010x | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 80 | 4861.1 us | 4572.3 us | **1.058x** | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 72 | 5217.1 us | 5070.5 us | 1.030x | 10/10 |
| 1 image x 32768 tokens | 64 | 3974.7 us | 3887.8 us | 1.022x | 10/10 |

**ViT attention kernel, `fa4` vs `triton_attn`** (the kernels behind the default switch):

Head-dim sweep, 16 heads, non-causal varlen, speedup of `fa4` over `triton_attn` (FA4 from the base commit, i.e. without item 1; the two wrapper tables below are on this branch):

| layout | d=64 | d=72 | d=80 | d=128 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 8 images x 4096 tokens | 5.4x | 20.5x | 7.9x | 6.6x |
| 1 image x 16384 tokens | 5.4x | 19.3x | 7.8x | 6.4x |
| 64 images x 1024 tokens | 4.2x | 16.2x | 6.1x | 5.4x |

GLM-5.3 / DeepSeek-V4.1 ViT shapes (16 heads, d=64), sglang's `VisionFlash4Attention` / `VisionTritonAttention`, per call:

| input | fa4 eager | triton eager | eager ratio | fa4 graph | triton graph | graph ratio |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 image 224² (256 tok) | 62.4 us | 38.4 us | 0.62x | 7.0 us | 14.4 us | 2.05x |
| 1 image 448² (1024 tok) | 61.5 us | 49.3 us | 0.80x | 13.1 us | 44.4 us | 3.38x |
| 4 images 448² | 62.0 us | 98.3 us | 1.59x | 25.5 us | 93.5 us | 3.67x |
| 16 images 448² | 94.2 us | 370.2 us | 3.93x | 90.7 us | 364.8 us | 4.02x |
| 64 images 448² | 361.2 us | 1522.1 us | 4.21x | 357.0 us | 1516.7 us | 4.25x |
| 1 image 896² (4096 tok) | 75.9 us | 357.7 us | 4.71x | 72.5 us | 352.8 us | 4.87x |
| 4 images 896² | 258.4 us | 1351.9 us | 5.23x | 254.6 us | 1347.1 us | 5.29x |
| 1 image 1792² (16384 tok) | 904.4 us | 5200.8 us | 5.75x | 944.3 us | 5187.9 us | 5.49x |
| 8 mixed-size images (11136 tok) | 124.9 us | 610.0 us | 4.88x | 120.6 us | 606.1 us | 5.03x |
| video, 32 frames x 256 tok | 61.2 us | 62.1 us | 1.01x | 28.7 us | 57.8 us | 2.01x |

Qwen2.5-VL-7B ViT (16 heads, d=80; windows of 64 patches, 28 windowed + 4 full-attention blocks), per layer and per image:

| image | windowed layer fa4 / triton (eager) | full layer fa4 / triton (eager) | per image, eager: fa4 / triton | per image, ViT graph: fa4 / triton |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 448x448 (16 windows) | 62.6 / 37.2 us | 61.2 / 42.3 us | 2.00 / 1.21 ms | **0.38 / 0.55 ms** |
| 720p (84 windows) | 62.3 / 64.9 us | 138.5 / 783.8 us | 2.30 / 4.95 ms | 2.11 / 4.81 ms |
| 1080p (180 windows) | 147.5 / 150.6 us | 478.0 / 3725.6 us | 6.04 / 19.12 ms | 5.98 / 18.79 ms |
| 4K (700 windows) | 977.7 / 561.5 us | 7399.8 / 60559.9 us | 57.0 / 258.0 ms | 57.6 / 257.7 ms |

Where `fa4` loses: (a) eager calls on tiny inputs (a single image of ≤1024 tokens), where its ~60 us per-call host overhead exceeds the kernel time; the ViT CUDA graph removes it (448x448: 0.38 ms vs 0.55 ms per image), and SM100 already carries this trade-off with `fa4` as its default. (b) Very many 64-token windows (Qwen2.5-VL at 4K, 700 windows): the windowed layer is 1.7x slower than Triton because FA4's 128-row tiles are half empty; the full-attention layers more than make up for it (4.5x per image). A smaller Q tile for short segments would be a follow-up, not part of this PR.

**End to end, eager ViT** (Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, 1 GPU per server, c=1, `bench_serving --dataset-name image`, fresh images per run):

| request | triton_attn median TTFT | fa4 median TTFT |
|---|---|---|
| 1 image 4K (2 runs) | 943 / 1021 ms | 752 / 868 ms (−15–20%) |
| 1 image 1080p (3 interleaved runs) | 235 / 169 / 211 ms | 194 / 171 / 159 ms |

At 1080p the per-image attention saving (~13 ms) is below the run-to-run noise of host-side image preprocessing (medians of the same server swing by ~60 ms), so it is not claimed from this table. GLM-5.3-Flash (TP4, 24-layer d=64 ViT) is neutral end to end within noise. Concurrent image benchmarks (c=16/32) were dominated by host-side image preprocessing (the same configuration varied 1.8x between runs) and are not used.

**End to end with the ViT CUDA graph** (`SGLANG_VIT_ENABLE_CUDA_GRAPH=1`, Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct, c=1, fresh images per run). Preprocessing noise only ever adds latency, so the per-request p25 (2 interleaved runs of 40 / 20 requests) tracks the floor better than the median:

| request | triton_attn + graph, p25 TTFT | fa4 + graph, p25 TTFT | difference | attention-only prediction (item 2) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 image 448x448 | 38.3 / 38.6 ms | 38.9 / 38.3 ms | none | −0.2 ms |
| 1 image 1080p | 181.9 / 182.3 ms | 168.7 / 166.7 ms | −13 to −16 ms | −13 ms |
| 1 image 4K | 866.7 / 901.7 ms | 673.9 / 747.5 ms | −150 to −190 ms | −200 ms |

title: feat(kda): integrate FlashInfer prefill checkpoints
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

[FlashInfer #5021](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5021) (0.7.0) adds indexed, floor-aligned checkpoints to CuTe DSL KDA prefill, which SGLang needs for radix prefix caching.

## Modifications

- Opt-in `--linear-attn-prefill-backend flashinfer` for BF16, 128-dim safe-gate KDA on SM100/SM103.
- Map FlashInfer checkpoints to radix-cache track rows (FP32 state pools, padded gate/beta); write only radix-tracked checkpoints.
- KDA models pass raw beta logits in every phase. Kernel adapters own activation, without backend-dependent model flags or model mutation during backend construction. FlashInfer tensor validation runs during warmup.
- Call `flashinfer.kda.recurrent_kda(..., backend="cute-dsl")` directly. FlashInfer owns scheduling and workspace allocation; SGLang maps radix-cache checkpoint destinations once per tracked batch. Invalid scheduler/checkpoint metadata raises an assertion.
- Reject incompatible checkpoint intervals, TBO, and full prefill CUDA graphs at setup. FlashInfer validates safe gates during warmup. BCG keeps linear attention eager; verify uses its separately configured backend.
- Retain Triton fallback for a packed prefill containing only one token, which FlashInfer's current packed-prefill API excludes.

This PR leaves dependency pins unchanged; the current tree already pins FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1.

## Accuracy Tests

Historical default-selection experiment (reverted by `c0d8467478`; FlashInfer remains opt-in): pre-commit passed. The [registered CPU rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37808499136) passed all 10 tests on `a231d574ae`, after correcting the policy fixture to publish a resolved CUDA graph config. The [B200 rerun](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/37715933478) passed FlashInfer KDA kernel tests and GLM-5.3-Flash low-latency GSM8K on `70b968ef19`: score 0.932 over 500 questions. The server log confirms `decode=triton, prefill=flashinfer, verify=nv_cutedsl`. The follow-up commit changes only the unit fixture.

Previously reported on 8xGB300, FlashInfer 0.7.0: the original five KDA prefill cases, existing KDA decode/verify (11), and CuTe DSL KDA + GDN checkpoint smoke (2) passed.

The current GPU test file contains six checkpoint/layout cases and two numerical backend cases (tracked prefill and single-token fallback). The direct-call cleanup passes pre-commit and focused CPU checks: eight checked-in test methods, 22 raw-beta contract checks, six checkpoint harness cases exercising the production adapter with a substituted numerical kernel, and six metadata-hook cases. GPU imports and numerical kernels were isolated for these local CPU checks. The eight GPU cases passed on pre-rebase head `ae9847e073` on B300 (SM103), FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 and CUDA 13.0, in 207.87 seconds. The exact rebased-head rerun is reported below.

### Exact rebased-head GLM-5.3-Flash checks

Reran both prefix-cache methods on the **exact rebased head `706048f3fd`** (before the default-selection change), with the full upstream fix and no diagnostic patch: real `zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash` weights (revision `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`), **4xB300 / TP4**, BF16 KV and SSM caches, TileLang DSA, Triton decode, 16K prefill chunks, eager execution, and `--mamba-track-interval 256`. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1 (Python TreeCore), Transformers 5.17.0. Both arms use `SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE=0` to compile the exercised GEMM shapes on demand; the initial exhaustive startup compilation was stopped before probe requests.

**Kernel/configuration checks:** 23 tests passed, including all eight FlashInfer KDA numerical/layout cases, in 229.46 seconds. Pre-commit and focused CPU contract/metadata checks also passed.

**Cold versus cached continuation:** score the same fixed 167-token continuation after 32,769 / 36K / 72K context tokens. All target scores are finite; inputs are identical between backends.

| KDA prefill | Context | Cold/cached absolute logprob difference mean / p90 / max | Warm/repeat mean | Cached tokens warm / repeat |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| triton | 32769 | 0.022187 / 0.000521 / 2.914499 | 0.017015 | 32768 / 32768 |
| triton | 36000 | 0.006804 / 0.000954 / 0.562500 | 0.003408 | 35840 / 35840 |
| triton | 72000 | 0.005175 / 0.000746 / 0.500000 | 0.003549 | 71936 / 71936 |
| flashinfer | 32769 | 0.009283 / 0.000480 / 1.046875 | 0.003289 | 32768 / 32768 |
| flashinfer | 36000 | 0.003019 / 0.000722 / 0.312500 | 0.003292 | 35840 / 35840 |
| flashinfer | 72000 | 0.003710 / 0.000662 / 0.346874 | 0.002871 | 71936 / 71936 |

**Branching corruption check from #42178:** cache an 8,320-token prefix; score copying a 167-token span from branch A before and after an unrelated branch B extends the shared prefix. Three different spans/seeds per backend.

| KDA prefill | Copy mean logprob before | After competing request | Second request cache hit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| triton | -0.015645 | -0.016829 | 8192 |
| flashinfer | -0.015597 | -0.016357 | 8192 |

The pre-rebase controls dropped from approximately -0.02 to -1.35 after the competing request. The rebased runs retain high copy scores with both KDA prefill backends and resume at 8,192, keeping the pooled index group private. This reproducer no longer shows the large branching collapse.

Warm repeats and the aligned-boundary control are **not bit-exact** on GLM. The Triton aligned control has a 2.9145 maximum cold/cached difference and a 2.0505 maximum warm/repeat difference despite a small p90; these outliers preclude claiming exact cache parity. These measurements do not isolate the residual drift to a specific operator. HiCache host restore and current-head speed were not tested.

### GLM-5.3-Flash checks before rebase

2026-10-07, head `ae9847e073`, real GLM-5.3-Flash weights, 4xB300 TP4, BF16 KV/SSM caches, TileLang DSA, 16K prefill chunks, eager execution, Triton decode. FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.14.1 (Python TreeCore), Transformers 5.17.0. Model revision `eb9eb208eb0d988989d07a6a12d0fdeb5f52574a`.

Cold versus cached scoring uses identical contexts and a fixed 167-token continuation. Values are absolute logprob difference mean / p90 / max.

| Layout / prefill | 36K | 72K |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| PR head, Triton | 0.0044 / 0.0006 / 0.312 | 0.0023 / 0.0004 / 0.178 |
| PR head, FlashInfer | 0.0081 / 0.0009 / 0.550 | 0.0043 / 0.0007 / 0.344 |
| Device fix, Triton | 0.0089 / 0.0004 / 0.595 | 0.0040 / 0.0008 / 0.314 |
| Device fix, FlashInfer | 0.0045 / 0.0007 / 0.312 | 0.0054 / 0.0005 / 0.500 |

The branching check warms a prefix ending inside a 256-token index group, scores copying a span from the first suffix, then rescoring follows a competing request with unrelated text. Values below average three different 167-token copy spans.

| Layout / prefill | Copy mean logprob before | After competing request | Second request cache hit |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| PR head, Triton | -0.0189 | -1.3455 | 8320 |
| PR head, FlashInfer | -0.0169 | -1.3452 | 8320 |
| Device fix, Triton | -0.0158 | -0.0147 | 8192 |
| Device fix, FlashInfer | -0.0145 | -0.0159 | 8192 |

Before rebase, head `ae9847e073` lacked #42178. Both backends reproduced its pooled-index branching corruption; the device-cache portion of that fix, ported only into the isolated test checkout, removed the collapse. The PR has now been rebased onto main `7760d5264a`, which contains the full merged #42178 fix. The earlier diagnostic measurements below retain their original source provenance.

Warm repeats and the 32,768-token aligned-resume control are not bit-exact on GLM; residual small drift is not isolated to KDA. At 72K on the old layout, warm/repeat cache depths also differ (65,536 / 71,936). Fixed-layout arms use the required 256-token decode tracking interval; old-layout arms use 64. Probe requests generate zero tokens, and prefill tracking follows page/chunk geometry. HiCache host restore and latest-head speed were not tested.

### Historical Kimi K3 measurements

The following Kimi K3 results predate the current direct-call cleanup.

Kimi K3 real weights, 8xGB300, BF16 KV, DSpark: cold vs prefix-cache-resume logprobs over a fixed 167-token continuation (|Δlogprob| mean / p90 / max). Warm vs warm is bit-exact in all cases.

| Config | 36k ctx | 72k ctx |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| DCP8, Triton prefill | 0.044 / 0.149 / 0.69 | 0.050 / 0.174 / 1.04 |
| DCP8, FlashInfer prefill | 0.043 / 0.147 / 0.55 | 0.055 / 0.215 / 0.61 |
| TP8, Triton prefill | 0.051 / 0.190 / 0.69 | 0.059 / 0.213 / 0.86 |

FlashInfer matches Triton. The drift is from chunk layout, not state restore: a resume on a cold chunk boundary (32768) is bit-exact.

## Speed Tests

These are historical measurements from the wrapper-based integration. The current direct API can read packed sequence offsets on the host to size its workspace and allocates that workspace within each call; performance and D2H behavior need remeasurement on the latest head.

Kimi K3 NVFP4 dummy weights, 8xGB300 TP8/DCP8, bs1, 131k in / 1k out, 95% prefix hit, A/B/A x10:

| Metric | Triton | FlashInfer |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Normal TTFT, median | 0.429 s | 0.411 s |
| Output throughput, median | 406.5 tok/s | 407.4 tok/s |
| KDA GPU time per layer (EXTEND trace) | 421 µs | 219 µs |
| KDA-associated D2H copies | 0 | 0 |

An intermittent ~6.7 s TTFT stall appears with both backends and is not attributed to KDA.

Kernel-only KDA prefill (checkpoints off), K3 shape on one TP8 rank (12 heads x 128), single GB300, bf16 in / fp32 state, median of 5 (ms). Backends that fall back to Triton at these lengths are omitted: `nvidia_kda` (needs >1 sequence), `flashkda` (caps at 2048 tokens/seq).

| Case | Triton | FlashInfer | ptx_kda | cutedsl |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 16k | 1.18 | 0.87 | 0.72 | 1.51 |
| 32k | 2.09 | 1.37 | 1.13 | 2.67 |
| 64k | 3.95 | 2.38 | 1.94 | 4.94 |
| 128k, one sequence | 7.76 | 4.36 | 3.65 | 9.61 |
| 128k as 8x16k chunks | 3.82 | 1.18 | 2.66 | 7.52 |

FlashInfer is 1.3-1.8x Triton on a single sequence and 3.2x on the 8x16k shape chunked prefill actually issues, where it batches the sequences into one kernel. `ptx_kda` is ~20% faster on a single sequence but 2.3x slower on that chunked shape; it is also not measured here with checkpoints on, which its own fallback note says routes tracked batches to Triton. `cutedsl` cannot serve K3 at all (no safe gate, no interior checkpoints).

- [x] Add registered tests

title: [KDA] Enable the ptx_kda prefill backend on SM100 (B200 / GB200)
author: yuan-luo
body:
## Motivation

`--linear-attn-prefill-backend ptx_kda` only runs on SM103 (B300 / GB300) today: the extension is built with `-gencode arch=compute_103a,code=sm_103a` and `PtxKDAKernel.supports_prefill` checks for compute capability (10, 3). On B200 / GB200 the backend silently falls back to Triton.

Nothing in the kernel needs SM103:
- All of its inline PTX is available on sm_100a:
  - tcgen05 `cta_group::1`: alloc, ld, st, mma (`kind::f16` and `kind::tf32`), commit, wait and fence.
  - TMA (`cp.async.bulk.tensor`), mbarrier, `mma.sync`, `ldmatrix`, `cp.async`, `prefetch`.
- There is no `ld.red` or other sm_103-only instruction.
- The route and piece-budget cost model reads `multiProcessorCount` at runtime.

On B200 the kernel gives the same speedup over the default Triton path as it does on B300.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/attention/linear/kda_ptx_prefill/__init__.py`:
  - Add `SM_ARCHS = {(10, 0): "100a", (10, 3): "103a"}`.
  - Build for the running device's arch. Arch-specific cubins do not run across the two.
  - Name the JIT extension per arch (`kda_prefill_ptx_sm100a` / `kda_prefill_ptx_sm103a`), so a shared `TORCH_EXTENSIONS_DIR` can keep both.
- `srt/layers/attention/linear/kernels/kda_ptx.py`: `supports_prefill` is true on SM100 and SM103.
- `srt/layers/attention/linear/kda_backend.py`: update the fallback and error messages.
- `kernels/jit/csrc/attention/kda_prefill.cu`: update the build comment only. The kernel code is unchanged.
- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill.py`:
  - The two ptx cases now also run on SM100.
  - The B200 runner now JIT-builds the extension, so its `est_time` goes from 180 to 300 s. The measured time on B200 is 146 s, including the build.

The default KDA prefill backend is unchanged (`triton`). `ptx_kda` stays opt-in.

## Accuracy Tests

B200 (SM100), this branch:

```
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_nvidia_prefill PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_padded_raw_beta PASSED
test_kda_prefill.py::TestKdaPrefill::test_ptx_prefill PASSED
3 passed in 146.12s
```

The ptx cases compare both the output and the final state with Triton. The raw-beta case also exercises the wrapper's padding path.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

- Hardware: B200 (148 SMs), torch 2.13 + cu130, triton 3.7.1.
- Method: `PtxKDAKernel.extend` against `TritonKDAKernel.extend`, called the way `KDAAttnBackend.extend` calls them.
- Inputs:
  - q, k, v and the raw gate are bf16 with shape `[1, B·T, H, 128]`.
  - beta is raw (the kernel applies the sigmoid).
  - `A_log` and `dt_bias` follow the Mamba/KDA init.
  - The state pool is fp32.
- Timing: CUDA events including wrapper overhead, median of 10 runs. Latency is in µs.
- "Max diff" is the maximum absolute difference from the Triton output.

With `lower_bound = -5` (safe gate, as in Kimi-K3):

| B × T × H | triton | ptx_kda | speedup | max diff |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 × 8192 × 32 | 968 | 761 | 1.27× | 3e-2 |
| 1 × 32768 × 32 | 3442 | 2498 | 1.38× | 3e-2 |
| 1 × 32768 × 8 | 1835 | 766 | 2.40× | 3e-2 |
| 1 × 32768 × 4 | 1583 | 510 | 3.10× | 3e-2 |
| 4 × 8192 × 32 | 2884 | 1677 | 1.72× | 3e-2 |
| 16 × 2048 × 32 | 2675 | 1798 | 1.49× | 3e-2 |
| 4 × 8192 × 8 | 965 | 808 | 1.19× | 3e-2 |

For comparison, B300 with the same script gives 1.09–2.98×. The absolute ptx_kda times on B200 and B300 are within ±6% of each other.

Without `lower_bound` (plain softplus gate, as in Kimi-Linear), ptx_kda is 1.34–3.21× faster than triton on the same shapes. One shape produces NaN, see Notes.

The biggest gains are at few heads per GPU (TP-sharded) with long prompts. There the Triton `chunk_h` recurrence is latency-bound, taking about 2.3–2.4 µs per 64-token chunk on B200 whether H = 32 or H = 4. ptx_kda splits the sequence into pieces and composes their affine state maps.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the pre-commit hooks (isort 7.0.0, ruff 0.15.1 check and format are clean on the changed Python files).
- [x] Add unit tests (existing ptx cases now run on SM100).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
