title: [Fix] sampling: Make top-k/top-p filtering consistent across sampling paths
author: alvion427
body:
Supersedes #36173 and addresses its final review findings.

## Motivation

SGLang normally computes the top-p cutoff from the original probability distribution and intersects that support with top-k. Some sampling paths instead applied top-k, renormalized the remaining probabilities, and then applied top-p. That applies top-p to whatever probability mass happens to remain after top-k, making its effect unpredictable and inconsistent with other sampling paths using the same parameters.

The affected paths are the FlashInfer min-p path, the shared EAGLE-family/standalone/n-gram verifier, and the target-distribution builder shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO. UNO's separate compact top-k path also needed the same fix; its behavior could otherwise depend on other requests in the batch.

## Modifications

- Apply top-p before top-k in the FlashInfer min-p path.
- Apply the same ordering in the shared EAGLE-family, standalone, and n-gram verifier.
- Correct dense/sparse target distributions shared by DFlash, DSpark, and UNO.
- Preserve the sparse top-k path by translating the top-p cutoff into the renormalized top-k distribution using the top-k support's original probability mass.
- Apply the same correction to UNO's separate compact top-k path.
- Fuse CUDA unseeded top-p rescaling by reusing the retained top-k maximum, avoiding a full-vocabulary maximum reduction and exponential intermediate.
- Preserve logsumexp for seeded/non-CUDA callers; UNO rejects deterministic inference.
- Document that fused FP32 rounding can change cutoff membership, without promising bitwise identity or trainer alignment.
- Reject `min_p > 0` for built-in speculative decoding, where it is not currently applied.
- Add focused CUDA regression tests for each corrected implementation.

## Accuracy Tests

The regressions use probabilities `[0.35, 0.25, 0.20, 0.05, 0.03, ...]`, `top_k=4`, and `top_p=0.82`. The FlashInfer min-p case also uses `min_p=0.1`.

The original top-p nucleus includes token 3 because the probability mass before it is `0.80`. Applying and renormalizing top-k first changes that mass to `0.80 / 0.85`, causing token 3 to be incorrectly removed.

Validated rebased commit `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f` on an NVIDIA H200 with Python 3.12.3, CUDA 13.0, PyTorch 2.13.0, FlashInfer 0.6.18, and Triton 3.7.1.

`TestSamplingMaskCapture` and `test_speculative_sampling.py`: **18 passed, 6 subtests passed**, no failures/errors/skips.

Each regression passed with the fix and failed with pre-fix filtering:

| Path | With fix | Before fix |
| --- | --- | --- |
| FlashInfer min-p | Pass | Support length 3 instead of 4 |
| EAGLE, using the production FlashInfer kernels | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, dense | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| Shared target builder, sparse | Pass | Token-3 probability mismatch |
| UNO compact | Pass | Compact support probability mismatch |

The same tests exercised pre-fix filtering from public base `d2a436446cca3d955358e7b4a5bf6881ea8591cd`; EAGLE retained the extracted helper signature for testability.

Ruff 0.15.1, isort 7.0.0, syntax, whitespace, and registry checks passed. The H200 results above apply to `50e6ca6b73cc49214b5e9e28068b187ac3d7de2f`, not current-head CI.

[Base CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/39500026515) passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03`; Extra/AMD had failures. CI States below tracks newer runs.

<!-- lint: profile=evidence-heavy -->

### Historical HTTP validation at `f0c0a64`

All 10 HTTP checks passed at `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` on H200 using `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` revision `7ae557604adf67be50417f59c2c2f167def9a775`, Transformers 5.19.0, and the runtime below.

NGRAM accepted `min_p=0`. With `min_p=0.1`, non-streaming requests returned HTTP 400; streaming requests emitted `abort`, embedded status 400, and `[DONE]`. Each rejection mode ran twice; all four following valid requests succeeded. Ordinary sampling accepted `min_p=0.1`. Both servers remained healthy before teardown. Other speculative modes and PD deployment were not exercised. Source Rust extensions used `SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE=auto`.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

These measurements predate fusion in `b94a95d5e805e0ee214c6d355a3a6cc79dd5e073`; see the [fused-helper validation summary](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41916#issuecomment-6328764169) for results and limitations.

Historical head `f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03` versus base `f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38`:

| Setup | Value |
| --- | --- |
| Hardware/runtime | H200; driver 595.71.05; Python 3.12.15; PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130; FlashInfer 0.7.2; Triton 3.8.0 |
| Functions | Production head functions and exact base definitions with unchanged dependencies; UNO retains `torch.compile(dynamic=True)` |
| Inputs | Seed 41916; FP32 normal logits, std=2; temperature=0.8; top-k=50; top-p=0.9; draft width=6 |
| Timing | Median microseconds/call; five alternating base/head samples; 200 CUDA Graph replays/sample; compilation and warmup excluded |
| Shape order | Vocabulary 32,768 then 128,256; batch 1, 16, 64 for each |

Outputs were finite and normalized; base/head sampling semantics intentionally differ.

| Path | Batch | Vocabulary | Base (us) | Head (us) | Added (us) |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| DFlash sparse | 1 | 32,768 | 79.85 | 99.50 | 19.65 |
| UNO compact | 1 | 32,768 | 28.75 | 38.01 | 9.26 |
| DFlash sparse | 16 | 32,768 | 130.29 | 158.38 | 28.09 |
| UNO compact | 16 | 32,768 | 30.45 | 48.85 | 18.40 |
| DFlash sparse | 64 | 32,768 | 373.87 | 437.04 | 63.17 |
| UNO compact | 64 | 32,768 | 61.63 | 119.92 | 58.30 |
| DFlash sparse | 1 | 128,256 | 101.42 | 139.81 | 38.40 |
| UNO compact | 1 | 128,256 | 49.55 | 70.68 | 21.13 |
| DFlash sparse | 16 | 128,256 | 320.54 | 442.95 | 122.41 |
| UNO compact | 16 | 128,256 | 59.51 | 116.82 | 57.31 |
| DFlash sparse | 64 | 128,256 | 896.05 | 1211.86 | 315.81 |
| UNO compact | 64 | 128,256 | 163.58 | 369.16 | 205.58 |

With top-p disabled at batch=16, vocabulary=128,256, DFlash measured 300.17 -> 300.31 us; UNO measured 57.71 -> 56.90 us. Costs increased 17-38% for DFlash and 32-126% for UNO in this sweep. End-to-end serving throughput and latency remain unmeasured.

`torch.profiler` CPU/CUDA traces used ten graph replays and three ordinary calls, after warmup. At batch=64, vocabulary=128,256:

| Path | Additional full-vocabulary work | Profile attribution |
| --- | --- | --- |
| DFlash sparse | Eager `logsumexp`: max, subtract, exp, sum, final normalization | 9 kernels, ~350 us; ~188 MiB temporary tensor. Total kernel count: 30 -> 52. Unprofiled rerun: 886 -> 1199 us. |
| UNO compact | Compiled full-vocabulary max and exp-sum reductions | 4 kernels, ~206 us; two scans dominate. Total kernel count: 6 -> 10. Unprofiled rerun: 163 -> 369 us. |

DFlash's top-p kernel fell from ~53 to 5 us; kernel durations attribute costs but do not replace unprofiled timings.

UNO depends on shape warmup order. Starting with vocabulary=128,256 and batch 1 then 64 generated a single full-vocabulary reduction kernel (~113 us), with unprofiled timings 161 -> 275 us. Repeating the sweep restored 163 -> 369 us; the percentage is not universal.

import ast
import gc
import hashlib
import importlib.metadata
import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import statistics
import subprocess
import time
from types import SimpleNamespace

import torch

from sglang.srt.speculative import dflash_utils as dflash
from sglang.srt.speculative import uno_utils as uno

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
OUT = ROOT / 'benchmark-results.json'


def source_node(path, name):
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    node = next(n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name == name)
    return source, node


def load_base(path, names, module):
    namespace = dict(vars(module))
    source = Path(path).read_text()
    nodes = [n for n in ast.parse(source).body if isinstance(n, ast.FunctionDef) and n.name in names]
    assert len(nodes) == len(names)
    exec(compile(ast.Module(body=nodes, type_ignores=[]), str(path), 'exec'), namespace)
    return namespace


def capture(fn):
    # Compilation and allocator warmup are outside the measured region.
    for _ in range(4):
        fn()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        output = fn()
    for _ in range(10):
        graph.replay()
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    tensors = output if isinstance(output, tuple) else (output,)
    assert all(torch.isfinite(t).all().item() for t in tensors)
    probs = tensors[-1]
    assert torch.allclose(probs.sum(-1), torch.ones_like(probs.sum(-1)), atol=2e-5, rtol=2e-5)
    return graph, output


def measure(graph, repetitions=200):
    start, end = torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True), torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True)
    start.record()
    for _ in range(repetitions):
        graph.replay()
    end.record()
    end.synchronize()
    return start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / repetitions


def main():
    base_dflash = load_base(ROOT / 'base_dflash_utils.py', {'build_speculative_verify_target_probs'}, dflash)
    base_uno = load_base(ROOT / 'base_uno_utils.py', {'_normalize_sparse_topk_probs', '_build_sparse_target_support_tensors'}, uno)
    for helper in ('_dflash_top_p_renorm_prob', '_dflash_top_k_renorm_prob'):
        _, before = source_node(ROOT / 'base_dflash_utils.py', helper)
        _, after = source_node(dflash.__file__, helper)
        assert ast.dump(before) == ast.dump(after), f'Dependency changed: {helper}'
    metadata = {
        'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03',
        'base': 'f0b65907227480afc376a66db62931b7e9c46c38',
        'torch': torch.__version__, 'cuda': torch.version.cuda,
        'gpu': torch.cuda.get_device_name(),
        'driver': subprocess.check_output(['nvidia-smi', '--query-gpu=driver_version', '--format=csv,noheader'], text=True).strip(),
        'packages': {p: importlib.metadata.version(p) for p in ('flashinfer-python', 'triton', 'transformers')},
        'method': 'Production head functions, exact base function ASTs with unchanged production dependencies; UNO torch.compile(dynamic=True) retained. CUDA Graph replay, warmup and compilation excluded, 5 paired samples alternating order, 200 replays/sample. Synthetic fixed-seed float32 logits, std=2; temperature=.8; top_k=50; draft_width=6.',
        'scope': 'Sampling function microbenchmark only. No model inference or end-to-end latency claim. Base/head intentionally implement different distributions.',
        'source_sha256': {str(p.name): hashlib.sha256(p.read_bytes()).hexdigest() for p in (ROOT/'base_dflash_utils.py', ROOT/'base_uno_utils.py', Path(dflash.__file__), Path(uno.__file__), Path(__file__))},
    }
    results = []
    cases = [(b, v, True) for v in (32768, 128256) for b in (1, 16, 64)] + [(16, 128256, False)]
    for bs, vocab, enabled in cases:
        torch.manual_seed(41916)
        width, k = 6, 50
        logits = torch.randn(bs * width, vocab, device='cuda', dtype=torch.float32) * 2
        temperatures = torch.full((bs, 1), .8, device='cuda')
        top_ks = torch.full((bs,), k, device='cuda', dtype=torch.int32)
        top_ps = torch.full((bs,), .9 if enabled else 1.0, device='cuda')
        info = SimpleNamespace(temperatures=temperatures, top_ks=top_ks, top_ps=top_ps, need_top_k_sampling=True, need_top_p_sampling=enabled)
        for path in ('dflash_sparse', 'uno_compact'):
            print(json.dumps({'starting': path, 'batch': bs, 'vocab': vocab, 'top_p_enabled': enabled}), flush=True)
            if path == 'dflash_sparse':
                args = dict(next_token_logits=logits, sampling_info=info, draft_token_num=width, bs=bs, max_top_k=k, uniform_top_k_value=k, use_sparse_topk=True)
                before = lambda: base_dflash['build_speculative_verify_target_probs'](**args)
                after = lambda: dflash.build_speculative_verify_target_probs(**args)
            else:
                args = (logits, temperatures, top_ks, top_ps, bs, width, k)
                before = lambda: base_uno['_build_sparse_target_support_tensors'](*args)
                after = lambda: uno._build_sparse_target_support_tensors(logits, temperatures, top_ks, top_ps if enabled else None, bs, width, k)
            bg, bo = capture(before)
            hg, ho = capture(after)
            samples = {'base': [], 'head': []}
            for round_id in range(5):
                pairs = [('base', bg), ('head', hg)] if round_id % 2 == 0 else [('head', hg), ('base', bg)]
                for label, graph in pairs:
                    samples[label].append(measure(graph))
            bm, hm = statistics.median(samples['base']), statistics.median(samples['head'])
            row = dict(path=path, batch=bs, vocab=vocab, top_p_enabled=enabled, base_us=bm, head_us=hm, delta_us=hm-bm, ratio=hm/bm, samples_us=samples)
            results.append(row)
            OUT.write_text(json.dumps({'metadata': metadata, 'results': results}, indent=2)+'\n')
            print(json.dumps(row), flush=True)
            del bg, bo, hg, ho, before, after
            gc.collect()
            torch.cuda.empty_cache()
    print('BENCHMARK_COMPLETE', flush=True)


if __name__ == '__main__':
    main()

import json
import os
from pathlib import Path
import signal
import subprocess
import sys
import time

import psutil
import requests

ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent
BASE_URL = 'http://127.0.0.1:31916'
RESULT = {'head': 'f0c0a64ad1b70d9a72f9d741b9eaa2b51d088c03', 'model': json.loads((ROOT/'model.json').read_text()), 'checks': [], 'launches': []}


def save():
    (ROOT/'http-results.json').write_text(json.dumps(RESULT, indent=2)+'\n')


def request(min_p, stream, expected_rejection, label):
    payload = {'text': 'The capital of France is', 'sampling_params': {'temperature': .7, 'top_k': 50, 'top_p': .9, 'min_p': min_p, 'max_new_tokens': 8}, 'stream': stream}
    start = time.monotonic()
    response = requests.post(BASE_URL+'/generate', json=payload, timeout=(10, 60))
    duration = time.monotonic()-start
    body = response.text
    if expected_rejection:
        assert 'min_p is not supported with NGRAM speculative decoding' in body, (response.status_code, body)
        assert response.status_code in (200, 400, 422), response.status_code
        if stream:
            assert 'data:' in body or response.status_code != 200, body
    else:
        assert response.status_code == 200, (response.status_code, body)
        parsed = response.json()
        assert isinstance(parsed.get('text'), str), parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['completion_tokens'] > 0, parsed
        assert parsed['meta_info']['finish_reason']['type'] != 'abort', parsed
    RESULT['checks'].append({'label': label, 'request': payload, 'status_code': response.status_code, 'elapsed_seconds': duration, 'response': body, 'passed': True})
    save()
    print(json.dumps({'label':label, 'status':response.status_code, 'seconds':duration, 'passed':True}), flush=True)


def stop_server(process):
    try:
        children = psutil.Process(process.pid).children(recursive=True)
    except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
        children = []
    try:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGTERM)
    except ProcessLookupError:
        pass
    try:
        process.wait(timeout=45)
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        os.killpg(process.pid, signal.SIGKILL)
        process.wait(timeout=15)
    for child in children:
        try:
            if child.is_running(): child.terminate()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess:
            pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(children, timeout=15)
    for child in alive:
        try: child.kill()
        except psutil.NoSuchProcess: pass
    _, alive = psutil.wait_procs(alive, timeout=15)
    assert not [p.pid for p in alive if p.status() != psutil.STATUS_ZOMBIE], 'server children survived'


def run_server(speculative):
    label = 'ngram' if speculative else 'ordinary'
    cmd = [sys.executable, '-m', 'sglang.launch_server', '--model-path', str(ROOT/'model'), '--host', '127.0.0.1', '--port', '31916', '--attention-backend', 'flashinfer', '--dtype', 'bfloat16', '--mem-fraction-static', '.5', '--max-running-requests', '8', '--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode', '8', '--context-length', '2048']
    if speculative:
        cmd += ['--speculative-algorithm', 'NGRAM', '--speculative-num-draft-tokens', '16']
    env = dict(os.environ, PYTHONPATH=str(ROOT/'source/python'), HF_HOME=str(ROOT/'hf'), HF_HUB_CACHE=str(ROOT/'hf/hub'), TORCHINDUCTOR_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'inductor'), TRITON_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'triton'), SGLANG_JIT_DEEPGEMM_PRECOMPILE='0', SGLANG_RUST_BUILD_MODE='auto', SGLANG_CACHE_DIR=str(ROOT/'sglang-cache'))
    with open(ROOT/f'server-{label}.log', 'w') as log:
        process = subprocess.Popen(cmd, env=env, cwd=ROOT/'source', stdout=log, stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, start_new_session=True)
        RESULT['launches'].append({'mode':label, 'command':cmd, 'pid':process.pid})
        save()
        try:
            deadline = time.monotonic()+600
            while time.monotonic()<deadline:
                if process.poll() is not None:
                    raise RuntimeError(f'{label} server exited: {process.returncode}; see server-{label}.log')
                try:
                    if requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=2).status_code == 200:
                        break
                except requests.RequestException:
                    pass
                time.sleep(2)
            else:
                raise TimeoutError(f'{label} server startup exceeded 600 seconds')
            print(f'SERVER_READY {label}',flush=True)
            if speculative:
                request(0, False, False, 'ngram valid initial control')
                for iteration in range(2):
                    for stream in (False, True):
                        request(.1, stream, True, f'ngram reject min_p=.1 stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
                        request(0, False, False, f'ngram valid after rejection stream={stream} repeat={iteration}')
            else:
                request(.1, False, False, 'ordinary accepts min_p=.1')
            assert requests.get(BASE_URL+'/health',timeout=10).status_code == 200
            assert process.poll() is None
        finally:
            stop_server(process)
            RESULT['launches'][-1]['stopped'] = True
            save()


try:
    run_server(True)
    run_server(False)
    RESULT['complete'] = True
    print('HTTP_CHECK_COMPLETE',flush=True)
except Exception as exc:
    RESULT['error'] = repr(exc)
    raise
finally:
    save()

title: [AMD][V4.1][*/N] Route low-ratio indexer and candidate-block top-k through top-k v2
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
On ROCm, the DSV4.1 low-ratio indexer still uses the older AOT kernels for its top-k. On MI355X, v2 is 1.4-2.6x faster at decode shapes and selects exactly the same indices.

Two AOT kernels are replaced:
- `deepseek_v4_topk_transform_512`, which picks the top 512 positions, both over the full row and inside the candidate blocks;
- `fast_topk`, which picks the top 2048 candidate blocks.

The AOT top-512 kernel also sorts each row by position. This sort is not needed, because the attention kernels that read the selection do not care about its order:
- decode attention reads the first `lengths[t]` entries and skips -1;
- prefill (`combine_topk_swa_indices`) only requires unused entries to be -1.

The CUDA path already passes the selection through unsorted, so this PR drops the sort as well.

title: [perf] [multi-lora] remove empty CTAs from fused LoRA expand and add split-K to shrink
author: kailash109
body:
## Summary

CSGMV launches empty tiles for smaller packed QKV expand slices and leaves parallelism unused in rank-32 shrink operations. Compact the expand grid using existing CPU slice offsets, and add opt-in split-K shrink with FP32 partials and a separate reduction.

## Changes

- Calls without CPU slice offsets retain the rectangular expand path with early returns for empty tiles.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_LORA_CSGMV_SPLIT_K=1` enables the existing BF16 rank-32 dispatch policy; it remains off by default. Deterministic inference retains the original shrink accumulation order because split-K changes rounding.
- Treat the partial-buffer row stride as a runtime parameter so different token counts reuse compiled split-K kernels.
- Use `split_k=None` for automatic dispatch, preserve explicit positive values, and reject invalid values before deterministic fallback.
- Keep one kernel benchmark and consolidate regressions into the existing CUDA-graph test script.

## Validation

Validated on H200 at `a7deef700821501c37fd1de266d4f1f42848d23a`:

- Existing CI entry point `python test/registered/kernels/ops/lora/test_chunked_sgmv_cuda_graph.py -f`: **8 tests passed**. Coverage includes FP32 partials, ragged and empty slices, output stride, mixed ranks, CUDA-graph metadata replay, explicit split factors, and deterministic fallback.
- The extended dispatch regression fails on the old argument logic when explicit split 4 is overwritten by 8.
- Eager token counts 7, 8, 9, and 17 pass the FP32 numerical oracle and reuse one compiled producer and reducer each.
- Full `pre-commit run --all-files` passed before both fix commits.

## Performance

The contributor's [corrected serving results](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41951#issuecomment-5925662323) report approximately 9.5–11.6% throughput improvement. These measurements predate the cleanup commits; no new serving or performance measurements are claimed for this head.

title: [AMD][V4.1][*/N] OPUS sparse prefill on gfx950 through layout conversion
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation
In gfx950, DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill attention runs on the aiter_sparse decode kernel, the only aiter kernel that reads V4.1's radix KV cache as stored. aiter's OPUS sparse prefill kernel (`pa_sparse_prefill_opus`) is 1.4-1.7x faster over a 16384-token chunk, but it expects a different layout:
| | V4.1 radix cache | OPUS input |
|---|---|---|
| KV rows | fp8 nope + scales + bf16 rope packed into 584 B per token, in 256-token pages; SWA and compressed history in separate pools | contiguous bf16 rows of 512, one buffer per source |
| Index lists | fixed width per query, -1 padded | CSR (indices + indptr), every entry a valid row |

This PR converts V4.1's layout into OPUS's on the fly: it dequantizes the rows a chunk reads into bf16 workspaces and turns the index lists into CSR. V4.1 layers share their compressed KV and top-k with a few source layers, so most of this conversion runs once per source layer rather than once per layer, and it costs under 5% of the attention time. 
It is opt-in with `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_OPUS_SPARSE_PREFILL=1`.


## Modifications

<!-- Detail the changes made in this pull request. -->
- Add an OPUS prefill path for DSV4.1 on gfx950, behind `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_OPUS_SPARSE_PREFILL` (default off). It converts the radix cache layout for the kernel: fp8 rows to bf16, -1 padded index lists to CSR. Layers that share a source layer's KV / top-k reuse its conversion.
- Fall back to the decode kernel for drafts, batches under 1024 tokens, context parallel, SWA bounded replay, or very long compressed history.
- Fill the raw top-k buffers with -1, so OPUS never reads a stale index.
- Add `test_dsv41_opus_sparse_prefill_hip.py`.

## Accuracy Tests

title: [XPU] Use the shared fused decode-metadata kernel in the intel_xpu ba…
author: xinchen9
body:
<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`XPUAttentionBackend.init_forward_metadata_out_graph()` built the decode page
table with separate PyTorch ops each step: strided gather from `req_to_token`,
floor-divide by `page_size`, cast to `int32`, copy into the preallocated
`page_table`, zero the trailing columns; plus separate ops for
`cache_seqlens_int32` and `cu_seqlens_k`, and a separate SWA page-table copy.

The NVIDIA FlashAttention backend already does all of this with one fused Triton
kernel, `normal_decode_set_metadata()` in
`python/sglang/kernels/ops/attention/metadata.py`. The kernel is plain Triton
with no CUDA-specific intrinsics and runs unchanged on Triton's XPU backend,
but the XPU backend did not use it.

This change calls that existing kernel from the XPU backend. No new kernel is
introduced; the Intel attention kernels, the graph runner and the KV-cache
allocator are untouched.

## Modifications

**`python/sglang/srt/layers/attention/xpu_backend.py`** (modified)

- Import `normal_decode_set_metadata` alongside the other helpers already
  imported from `flashattention_backend`.
- New private method `_set_decode_page_metadata()` issues one fused launch for
  `cache_seqlens_int32`, `cu_seqlens_k`, `page_table` and, for hybrid-SWA
  models, `swa_page_table`. It forwards `seq_len_delta` (= `kv_len_offset`) so
  target-verify and draft-decode keep their KV extension, and passes the tight
  bound `max_seq_pages = cdiv(max_seq_len_k, page_size)`.
- `init_forward_metadata_out_graph()` calls it for the ordinary
  (non-encoder-decoder) branch. The encoder-decoder branch keeps its original
  PyTorch implementation; the seq-len cast and cumsum moved into that branch.
- The separate SWA page-table gather/translate/copy block is removed. The fused
  kernel writes `swa_page_table` through `full_to_swa_index_mapping`, which is
  what `SWAKVPool.translate_loc_from_full_to_swa()` does.
- Net ~ -30 / +40 lines; one Triton launch replaces 6-8 PyTorch ops per decode step.

**`test/registered/attention/test_normal_decode_set_metadata.py`** (modified)

- Existing kernel test now runs on XPU as well as CUDA/ROCm (device from
  `get_device()`, skip only if neither is available).
- Registered for XPU CI: `register_xpu_ci(est_time=15, suite="stage-b-test-1-gpu-xpu")`.

**`benchmark/kernels/bench_xpu_decode_metadata.py`** (new)

- Standalone correctness + latency comparison of the previous PyTorch block vs
  the fused kernel on XPU. Loads the kernel from the repo file, so it needs only
  torch and triton. Exits non-zero if any live entry differs.

**Behavioral note: page-table tail columns.** The previous XPU block zeroed
columns past the batch-wide max page count every step. The fused kernel writes
only each request's live prefix (`cdiv(seq_len + delta, page_size)` pages) and
leaves the rest untouched. This is the kernel's documented contract and what the
FlashAttention backend already relies on: attention kernels bound their reads by
`cache_seqlens_int32`, and stale tail entries are always in-range page ids from
earlier steps (or zero from allocation), so whole-table gathers in the
chunked-attention path stay in bounds. Validated end to end below.

**Reproduction notes for XPU.** The decode graph is opt-in on XPU
(`--cuda-graph-backend-decode full`); without it decode runs eagerly through
`init_forward_metadata()` and this change is not exercised. The `intel_xpu`
backend accepts `--page-size` 64 or 128 only; other values are coerced to 128.

## Accuracy Tests

Environment: 1x Intel Arc Pro B70, torch 2.13.0+xpu, Triton 3.7.2,
sglang-kernel-xpu 0.3.0, image built from `docker/xpu.Dockerfile`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `python3 -m pytest test/registered/attention/test_normal_decode_set_metadata.py` on XPU | 16 passed, 8 subtests passed |
| `benchmark/kernels/bench_xpu_decode_metadata.py`: `cache_seqlens`, `cu_seqlens_k`, all live `page_table` entries vs previous PyTorch block | exact match, 36 configs (bs 1-32, ctx 1K-8K, page 1/16/64) |
| GSM8K 5-shot, 200 questions, temperature 0, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct BF16, `--page-size 64 --cuda-graph-backend-decode full`, fused path | accuracy 0.625, 0 invalid |

Server log confirmed the decode graph captured (3.4 s) and every decode batch
ran through it, so the fused path was exercised on each decode step.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Metadata preparation, standalone** (host-inclusive latency per call,
`python3 benchmark/kernels/bench_xpu_decode_metadata.py --markdown`):

| bs | ctx | page | pytorch (us) | pytorch + .item() sync (us) | fused (us) | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 8192 | 64 | 97.4 | 124.3 | 31.5 | 3.1x to 3.9x |
| 4 | 8192 | 64 | 103.8 | 130.6 | 31.3 | 3.3x to 4.2x |
| 16 | 8192 | 64 | 104.0 | 131.5 | 32.5 | 3.2x to 4.0x |
| 32 | 1024 | 64 | 103.5 | 130.8 | 32.3 | 3.2x to 4.0x |
| 32 | 8192 | 64 | 104.8 | 131.6 | 32.5 | 3.2x to 4.0x |

Latency is flat in batch size and context on both sides: the cost is launch
overhead, not bandwidth. Absolute microseconds vary with GPU clock state; the
ratios are stable.

**End-to-end serving** (`python3 -m sglang.bench_serving --backend sglang
--num-prompts 300 --max-concurrency {1,32}`, Qwen2.5-1.5B-Instruct BF16,
`--attention-backend intel_xpu --page-size 64 --cuda-graph-backend-decode full
--mem-fraction-static 0.8`; only `xpu_backend.py` differs between the servers;
one run per cell):

| Concurrency | Metric | Before | After | Change |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Median ITL | 6.33 ms | 6.31 ms | -0.3% |
| 1 | Median TPOT | 6.32 ms | 6.30 ms | -0.3% |
| 1 | Output throughput | 155.1 tok/s | 155.4 tok/s | +0.2% |
| 32 | Output throughput | 2494 tok/s | 2724 tok/s | +9.2% (*) |
| 32 | Median TPOT | 10.88 ms | 9.95 ms | -8.5% (*) |
| 32 | Median ITL | 8.27 ms | 8.29 ms | 0 |

(*) The baseline run at concurrency 32 contained a ~1 s stall (max ITL 886 ms
vs 133 ms after), so these cells are single-run observations, not a claimed gain.

Interpretation: at concurrency 1 the end-to-end effect is neutral, as expected.
With the overlap scheduler the host-side metadata work runs while the device
executes the previous step, so removing ~70-100 us of host time does not
shorten a 6.3 ms step; the ~20 us that does show up matches replacing several
tiny device kernels with one. The value of this change is 3-5x faster metadata
preparation, 5-7 fewer launches per decode step, and the XPU backend sharing
the fused path with the FlashAttention backend instead of maintaining its own
PyTorch version.

title: [Performance] Optimize Qwen3.8-Flash-Next BF16 decode on Blackwell
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

Single-token BF16 Qwen3.8-Flash-Next decode launches separate HC combine/norm and MoE shared-gate/finalize/collective work, while the packed GDN value tile leaves substantial register pressure at this shape. On four B200 GPUs, this patch raises the measured 8k-input/1k-output decode rate from fresh stock **242.443** to **270.982–271.759 token/s**, preserving the sampled stock accuracy in four native runs.

## Modifications

- Overlap the HC gate with block computation, fuse HC apply with grouped Gemma RMSNorm, and pass the prepared norm tensors explicitly across layers. PLE and PP boundaries retain the normal handoff.
- Extend the existing collective with an FP32 shared gate, preserving routed BF16 rounding before the shared-expert FMA. Defer BF16 MoE finalize and overlap the shared branch through a guarded single-token TP4/EP1 path with its own communication buffer.
- Use the smaller GDN value tile for the packed single-token BF16/FP32-state Blackwell shape, preserving the one-warp reduction order. Existing dispatch remains for unsupported shapes.

The MoE specialization requires hidden size 2560, 512 experts/top-10, BF16, SM10, TP4/EP1, attention DP1, with LoRA, speculative decoding and two-batch overlap disabled. No extra command-line switch enables the kernels. The benchmark selects the existing faster custom-all-reduce deployment option for both stock and candidate.

## Accuracy Tests

Stock and all four native candidate runs score **126/128 GSM8K, zero invalid answers, zero truncations**. These use identical frozen tokenized prompts, normal EOS and the same 2,048-token cap. All 128 per-question correctness and finish-reason verdicts match the fresh stock run.

Historical GPU validation before the standalone test cleanup: 6 HC unit configurations; 12 independent torch-reference GDN configurations; 6 collective configurations on each of 4 ranks, including the original ungated API; 90 trained HC-chain comparisons; 324 changed-input trained collective graph comparisons; 192 seeded GDN output/state bit comparisons. Isolated HC memcheck: zero errors. Full-stack communicator checks have the same handled PyTorch FABRIC capability API errors in stock and candidate, so they are not claimed as clean full-stack sanitizer runs. Pre-commit passes.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

title: [Speculative] Add opt-in block verification
author: maocheng23
body:
## Motivation

Add the block verifier from [Block Verification Accelerates Speculative Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2403.10444), Algorithm 2. Standard rejection sampling stops at the first rejected draft token. Block verification selects the longest accepted prefix and can accept a longer prefix after an earlier rejection, with a scaled correction distribution that preserves target sampling.

## Modifications

- Add opt-in `--speculative-use-block-verification`; this flag automatically enables the required proposal sampling and draft-probability storage. `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling` alone selects token-wise rejection sampling, and passing both flags remains supported. Support the existing linear EAGLE/EAGLE3/NEXTN proposal path (`--speculative-eagle-topk 1`) on CUDA/ROCm, with startup validation for unsupported configurations.
- Extend the existing Triton chain sampler with a compile-time branch. Compute `r_i = min(1, r_(i-1) * p(x_i) / q(x_i))` forward, then test prefixes longest-first and stop at the first acceptance. The original per-prefix random samples are retained, so skipped shorter-prefix tests cannot change the selected prefix. Commit that prefix once and sample correction from normalized `(r_tau * p - q)+`; full acceptance samples the bonus token from the target.
- Skip a prefix's vocabulary reduction when its coin is already at least `r_i`, using `h_i <= r_i` for normalized distributions. Reuse the selected prefix's residual mass for correction normalization. Use a separate reduction tile capped at 32768 with 8 warps for large vocabularies; keep the final CDF tile at 4096. Token verification retains its original acceptance loop and 4-warps launch.
- Add a reproducible sampler benchmark with optional comparison against a saved baseline kernel.
- Reuse proposal buffers, output indices, TP synchronization, and the greedy verification path. No scheduler or KV-cache changes; the existing verification defaults remain unchanged.
- Document the option and add focused kernel and configuration tests.

## Accuracy Tests

The optimized sampler at `42d866ccd5` was validated on one NVIDIA GB300 (Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1):

```bash
PYTHONPATH=python CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_block_verification.py \
  test/registered/unit/spec/test_block_verification_args.py
```

**25 passed, 12 configuration subtests passed.** Coverage includes both token/block paths against a reference, accepting past an earlier rejection, longest-prefix selection for every accepted length, strict acceptance-threshold boundaries (including `h_i == r_i`), scaled residuals, zero/unit probabilities, zero/one/multiple drafts, strided tensors, vocabulary tails up to 131073, and global output-index mapping. Statistical tests use 65,536 samples each to check the paper's expected acceptance lengths and the complete output joint distribution, including context-dependent targets with two and five drafts.

Compute Sanitizer memcheck passed all **17 non-statistical kernel cases with 0 errors**. An additional **4800 per-sequence comparisons** against the pre-optimization kernel covered three seeds, 0/1/3/5/8 drafts, five vocabulary sizes through 131073, and both verification modes: accepted lengths, output indices, and all valid output tokens matched exactly in these cases. This is observed parity, not a general bitwise guarantee for block verification after changing floating-point reduction order.

Independent exact rational enumeration reproduced the paper's `10/9` versus `11/9` accepted-draft example and target joint distributions for context-dependent binary models with draft lengths 1–5. A separate 42,252-case rational check validates longest-first selection and the `h_i <= r_i` shortcut across draft lengths 0–6.

Local configuration tests and CLI parsing passed. All pre-commit hooks applicable to the changed files passed; `git diff --check` passed. The full-model results below were obtained before this sampler optimization and have not been rerun on the optimized kernel. ROCm execution is not yet validated.

The subsequent CLI change (`25fca89325`) passed **17 CPU tests and 23 subtests** across block-verification configuration, EAGLE gate routing / ROCm defaults, and CLI metadata. A block-only CLI smoke test also verified that the published scheduler configuration enables both required sampler settings while preserving raw user arguments. The kernel is unchanged; GPU benchmarks were not repeated for this CLI change. Mintlify validation could not run locally because its CLI is unavailable.

The CI follow-up (`3e5cd56c29`) fixes the custom-algorithm and bootstrap-registration test fixtures. The random sampler reference now uses FP64 arithmetic and checks the final token's CDF interval with a `1e-6` probability tolerance; accepted lengths, draft tokens, and output indices remain exact. This handles FP32 boundary rounding without tolerating arbitrary token-ID differences. Validation: **57 CPU tests and 21 subtests passed**, plus **all 23 sampler tests on GB300** (Torch 2.13.0 / Triton 3.7.1). No production code changed in this follow-up; the original H100 job will be checked by the CI rerun.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

### Qwen3.8-27B / AIME25 end-to-end

These are historical measurements at `b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74`, before the sampler optimization.

| Metric | Token-wise | Block | Change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Acceptance length (includes bonus) | 2.9802 | 3.0063 | +0.88% |
| Output throughput (tokens/s) | 988.43 | 995.36 | +0.70% |
| Boxed score over entire response | 76/90 (84.44%) | 77/90 (85.56%) | +1.11 pp |
| Boxed score after `</think>` | 70/90 (77.78%) | 65/90 (72.22%) | -5.56 pp |
| Responses hitting the 32,768-token cap | 20/90 | 22/90 | |

AL increased in all three seed pairs. The pooled throughput increase is small (+0.70%); per-seed changes were +2.71%, +0.41%, and -0.99%, so this does not establish a consistent throughput speedup. The original entire-response score counts boxes inside reasoning, including 6 token-wise and 12 block responses that hit the cap. The added post-`</think>` score uses only the answer text after that marker and counts missing answers as incorrect. The 32k cap and three sampled runs limit quality comparisons; neither score difference establishes a quality change. All 23 responses without a parsed integer hit the token cap.

One NVIDIA GB300, TP1, Qwen/Qwen3.8-27B BF16 revision `1d4bf0f2ff6012fd82039f2fa52739d0dd7c60c0`, native MTP, three proposed tokens (`EAGLE`, steps=3, topk=1, draft-tokens=4). BF16 KV cache, FP32 recurrent state, FlashInfer attention and Triton GDN, CUDA graphs enabled, concurrency 8. Thinking enabled, xhigh template setting, temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, maximum 32,768 new tokens. All 30 MathArena/aime_2025 questions for each of three seeds; 90 attempts per arm, 180 total.

Both arms use commit `b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74` and `--speculative-use-rejection-sampling`. The block arm adds only `--speculative-use-block-verification`. Each run warms eight slots and flushes the cache before timing. Arm order alternates by seed. Startup and warmup are excluded. Incremental native streaming avoids repeatedly transferring the entire output prefix.

Acceptance length is total completion tokens / total verification steps, including the bonus token. Throughput is total output tokens / total measured wall time, including prefill and the final partially occupied batches. Both answer scores use the last boxed integer in their specified text region; cap hits are retained in the denominator. These are stochastic runs at one concurrency and draft length.

Torch 2.13.0+cu130, Triton 3.7.1, sglang-kernel 0.4.8, FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, Transformers 5.17.0, NVIDIA driver 590.48.01.

| Seed | Token AL | Block AL | Token tok/s | Block tok/s | Token entire-response correct | Block entire-response correct |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 980406 | 2.9725 | 3.0225 | 959.37 | 985.39 | 26/30 | 25/30 |
| 981406 | 2.9736 | 2.9890 | 995.39 | 999.45 | 25/30 | 25/30 |
| 982406 | 2.9947 | 3.0069 | 1011.64 | 1001.61 | 25/30 | 27/30 |

### Sampler microbenchmark

Paired sampler-only measurements of the pre-optimization kernel (`b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74`) and optimized kernel on the same GB300, Torch 2.13.0+cu130 / Triton 3.7.1. FP32, five drafts, vocabulary 131072, `q = 0.7*p + 0.3*softmax(random logits)`, seed 2026. Each cell is the median of three `triton.testing.do_bench` runs with 100 ms warmup and 500 ms measurement; implementation order alternates between repetitions.

| Batch | Token before | Token after | Block before | Block after | Block latency reduction |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | 62.08 µs | 61.97 µs | 159.69 µs | 58.07 µs | 63.6% |
| 16 | 104.81 µs | 105.12 µs | 207.87 µs | 132.83 µs | 36.1% |
| 128 | 133.91 µs | 133.39 µs | 250.78 µs | 146.25 µs | 41.7% |

Additional paired block-sampler measurements (before → after):

| Drafts | Vocabulary | Batch 1 | Batch 16 | Batch 128 |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 131072 | 127.61 → 57.32 µs | 163.45 → 113.39 µs | 184.65 → 131.07 µs |
| 5 | 131073 | 233.53 → 79.08 µs | 334.14 → 166.65 µs | 334.20 → 166.38 µs |

Reproduce the primary comparison:

```bash
git show b40ee2c99a17341d35ff1e47684bc8a471797d74:python/sglang/kernels/ops/speculative/reject_sampling.py > /tmp/reject_sampling_before.py
PYTHONPATH=python python benchmark/kernels/bench_block_verification.py \
  --baseline-file /tmp/reject_sampling_before.py
```

The final CDF sampling still scans vocabulary tiles; block verification additionally reduces vocabulary rows only for unresolved candidate prefixes. Longest-first selection eliminates those extra reductions when the full block is accepted. The remaining cost depends on the sampled proposals and prefix acceptance, so these results do not establish that block verification is always faster than token verification. They measure sampler cost only; the historical end-to-end results above have not been rerun after this optimization.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered unit tests.
- [x] Update documentation.
- [x] Provide output-distribution checks and sampler speed measurements.
- [x] Follow SGLang code style.

title: [diffusion] CI: fix qwen cache-dit step 10/49 perf baselines
author: niehen6174
body:
## Motivation

`qwen_image_t2i_cache_dit_enabled` fails its H100 per-step perf check at random. From 09-30 to 10-04, 71% of attempts went over the step-49 limit. Every final 1-GPU failure in that window came from this case.

The cause, found in the debug runs in #42546, is how the step time is measured. It is not a regression.

- Steps 10 and 49 are the first cached step after a full step.
- Per-step times are host wall times with no device sync.
- The cache-dit residual check in that step is the first point where the host blocks, so that step absorbs the previous full step's queued GPU work.

Debug run on CI H100, 3 launches per arm, times in ms:

| Arm | Full step | Steps 10 / 49 | Other cached steps | E2E |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Fused QK-norm/RoPE epilogue on, unsynced (CI today) | 178 | 64 / 66 | 6.3 | 4310 |
| Fused off, unsynced | 196 | 55 / 56 | 6.5 | 4455 |
| Fused on, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_SYNC_STAGE_PROFILING=1` | 238 | 7.0 / 7.1 | 6.3 | — |
| Fused off, synced | 245 | 7.2 / 7.1 | 6.5 | — |

With synced timing, steps 10 and 49 take about 7 ms, like every other cached step. #38584 enabled the fused epilogue on Hopper, which cut host launches from 3031 to 2007 per profiled window. The real GPU time got about 3% faster. But the host now enqueues faster too, so more GPU work spills into steps 10 and 49.

## Modifications

`perf_baselines/h100.json`: steps 10 and 49 of `qwen_image_t2i_cache_dit_enabled` are set to their CI medians, 64.58 / 66.38 ms (previously 48.7 / 45.11). The medians come from 328 H100 CI measurements between 09-30 and 10-04. They are the unsynced host wall times this check measures. No other baseline or tolerance changes.

The `ltx_2_5_diffusion_decoder_2gpus` timing tolerance from earlier commits is dropped. Its host-bound slowdown will be handled in a separate PR.

## Validation

PR CI on fe3b48d passed with the same qwen baselines.

title: [Feat] paged-experts: Serve MoE models whose weights do not fit VRAM
author: N3mezis
body:
# [Feature] Paged Experts: serve MoE models whose weights do not fit in VRAM

<!-- Successor to #29971 (closed), cut down to a reviewable first step. -->

This is a smaller, first-iteration version of #29971. That PR tried to make the feature fast and complete at once (pinned windows, a disk tier, breakable decode graphs, NVFP4, six new flags; ~7k lines). This one ships only the core: **page experts between host RAM and the GPU, keep the computation on the GPU, change no results.** Everything else is a follow-up that plugs into the seams added here.

## Motivation

A lot of laptops and gaming PCs typically pair 4–16 GB of VRAM with 32–64 GB of RAM. MoE models are increasingly the default open-weight architecture (Qwen3/3.5 MoE, DeepSeek, GLM, gpt-oss, Mixtral), and their expert weights are most of the parameters. For example, Qwen3-30B-A3B in int4 has ~15 GB of expert weights, which is all of the usable VRAM on a 16 GB card. Currently, SGLang either does not load such a model on these machines, or loads it with `--cpu-offload-gb`, which streams *every* offloaded weight to the GPU on every forward pass, whatever the routing.

llama.cpp and Ollama keep the experts of some MoE layers in system RAM and **compute them on the CPU** (`--n-cpu-moe N`, or `--cpu-moe` for all of them).

**What this PR does instead.** Each token is routed to only `top_k` of the `E` experts per layer, and consecutive tokens reuse most of them. Paged Experts keeps **K of the E experts per layer in a K-slot table on the GPU**, holds all E in pinned host memory, and copies in only the experts a step needs that are not resident. The layer's own fused-MoE kernel then runs on the GPU as usual. It is the HiCache idea applied to expert weights: the GPU holds the working set, host RAM the rest.

**It is a memory knob as much as a speed feature.** K trades directly against the KV cache, so a deployment can choose more context or concurrency (smaller K, more paging) or more speed (larger K). Models that already fit can give up some resident experts for longer context, or to share the GPU with another model.

## Where it helps, and where it does not

Measured against each alternative at its best setting (methodology and full numbers in [Speed Tests](#speed-tests-and-profiling)):

- **Against SGLang today** (`--cpu-offload-gb`): paging moves only the experts a step routes to and does not have, instead of every offloaded weight. 12× (int4) and 30× (FP8) faster single-stream decode on the 16 GB card, 27× on the 8 GB laptop.
- **Against llama.cpp tuned** (`--n-cpu-moe` at the best fitting value, byte-matched `IQ4_XS` / `Q8_0`):
  - when most of the model fits (a 16 GB int4 model on a 16 GB card), or the host link is slow (int4 on an 8 GB laptop over PCIe 4.0 x8), the two are **close**: 205.7 vs 194.4 tok/s single-stream decode and 379 vs 312 tok/s with 4 requests on the 16 GB card; 30.6–32.9 vs 23.0–32.4 tok/s single-stream decode on the laptop;
  - when a large share of the experts must live in host RAM and the host link is fast (FP8 on a 16 GB card over PCIe 5.0 x16), paging **decodes faster**: 87.7 vs 45.2 tok/s;
  - **llama.cpp has the lower time-to-first-token on short prompts.** A prefill touches nearly every expert, so it pages in all non-resident experts once (≈4 GB for Qwen3-30B int4 at K=92, ≈80 ms over PCIe 5), while llama.cpp computes its few CPU-side layers in place. For long prompts paging wins, since its transfer is a fixed cost and the GPU computes the tokens faster: 2,048-token prompt 267 vs 344 ms (int4, 16 GB), 443 vs 984 ms (FP8, 16 GB), 1,441–1,538 vs 2,396 ms (laptop); short prompts 89–90 vs 68 ms, 284–285 vs 226 ms, 872–953 vs 620 ms;
  - **with several concurrent requests and a small K/E**, each step routes to more experts than fit, and paging can fall behind: 11–12 vs 41 tok/s with 4 requests on the laptop (K = 26 of 128); FP8 on the 16 GB card gives 84 tok/s at K = 40 but 31 at K = 24 (llama.cpp: 55).

Note: #29971 compared only against llama.cpp `--cpu-moe` (all experts on the CPU), which overstated the advantage. The numbers here compare against llama.cpp's tuned offloading.

## Scope

**In this PR**
- Unquantized (bf16/fp16), block-quantized FP8 (triton runner) and GPTQ int4/int8 (Marlin runner) experts.
- A single GPU.
- Works with SGLang's default CUDA graphs: decode is captured (full graph) up to `K // top_k` concurrent requests, and in breakable prefill graphs the paged MoE layer runs as an eager break. CUDA graphs can also be off entirely.
- K is sized automatically from the memory budget, or set with `--paged-experts-num-resident`.
- **Results are unchanged.** Bit-identical logprobs for bf16 and FP8 versus the unpaged model, eager and with CUDA graphs; GPTQ stays within Marlin's own batch-to-batch noise.

**Not in this PR** (each is a follow-up on the seams below)
- Stores larger than pinnable RAM (pinned window, pageable or disk cold tier).
- Capturing decode beyond `K // top_k` requests (breakable decode graphs fail on these models upstream, with or without paging, so they are rejected for now).
- Computing a short prefill's non-resident experts on the CPU instead of paging them (the short-prompt TTFT gap above).
- More formats: NVFP4 (via Marlin W4A16 for exact results), AWQ, MXFP4.
- Tensor or expert parallelism.

Two new server flags: `--enable-paged-experts` and `--paged-experts-num-resident`.

## Modifications

**New package `srt/layers/moe/paged_experts/`** (~1,150 lines). It wraps a layer's existing fused-MoE method and splits paging into replaceable parts:

| Module | Responsibility |
|---|---|
| `method.py` | `PagedExpertsMoEMethod`. Creates the layer's expert tensors with K rows and redirects their weight loaders into a host store, so checkpoints load through SGLang's **native** per-expert loader (sharding, gate/up order, scale layout). Also holds the startup guard and the capture-size cap. |
| `formats.py` | One `ExpertFormat` per quantization method: which tensors are loaded and paged, and what happens after loading. GPTQ's Marlin repack runs over the host store K experts at a time; a check rejects post-load transforms the store would not replicate. **Adding a quantization is one subclass.** |
| `runners.py` | One `RunnerContract` per runner backend (triton, Marlin). The runner returns router-weighted per-(token, expert) outputs (`no_combine`), and the contract performs the same top-k sum the runner would. That is what makes multi-wave steps bit-identical. |
| `store.py` | The pinned host store: `page_in` for host-planned steps, `gather` for device-planned steps. |
| `residency.py` | LRU slot assignment and wave planning on the host, plus `DeviceResidency`, the same LRU state on the GPU. |
| `executor.py` | `EagerExecutor`: host-planned waves, any step; inside a breakable prefill graph it runs as an eager break. `DeviceExecutor`: one wave decided and paged on the GPU with no host sync, so the decode graph captures it. |
| `sizing.py` | Auto-K from exact checkpoint bytes (safetensors headers), `--mem-fraction-static`, and a KV reserve. |

**New JIT kernel** `kernels/jit/csrc/moe/paged_experts.cuh` with wrapper `kernels/ops/moe/paged_experts.py` (~290 lines; no sgl-kernel change):
- an on-device LRU decide that writes the page-in plan to GPU buffers;
- one gather launch that copies every paged tensor from the pinned host store through its UVA address, reading the count on the device.

**Upstream touches** (82 lines):
- `MoeRunnerConfig.no_combine_keep_router_weight`;
- the triton fused-MoE tail factored into `moe_combine_topk`;
- `fused_marlin_moe(no_combine=)`;
- `FusedMoE.weight_load_method` and the paged-experts hook in `FusedMoE.__init__`;
- the two server flags.

**Docs:** `docs/advanced_features/paged_experts.mdx` and the server-argument entries.

## Accuracy Tests

Logprobs against the unpaged server, prompt plus 16 greedy tokens, 3 prompts. Settings: `--enable-deterministic-inference --attention-backend triton`, K = 8, so every prompt runs in several waves and every decode step pages. "With CUDA graphs" means full decode plus breakable prefill.

| Model | Experts | Eager | With CUDA graphs |
|---|---|---|---|
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct | bf16 (triton) | **bit-identical** | **bit-identical** |
| OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, FP8 block 128×128 | fp8 (triton) | **bit-identical** | **bit-identical** |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-GPTQ-Int4 | int4 (Marlin) | within tolerance (max 0.1, mean 0.01) ‡ | within tolerance ‡ |

‡ Marlin's stream-K split depends on the batch shape, so the unpaged kernel is not batch-invariant either.

GSM8K, the same `sgl-eval` chat evaluation for both engines (thinking off), on models that cannot run unpaged on these cards:

| Model | this PR | llama.cpp (byte-matched GGUF) |
|---|---|---|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B int4, 16 GB card (200 q) | 0.955 | 0.965 (`IQ4_XS`) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B FP8, 16 GB card (200 q) | 0.945 | 0.955 (`Q8_0`) |
| Qwen3-30B-A3B int4, 8 GB laptop (100 q) | 0.98 | 0.98 (`IQ4_XS`) |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

**Machines:** an RTX 4070 Laptop (8 GB, PCIe 4.0 x8, 54 GB RAM under WSL2) and an RTX 5070 Ti desktop (16 GB, PCIe 5.0 x16, 62 GB RAM, native Linux).

**Methodology** (each engine at its best setting, identical workload):
- Real prompts (ShareGPT, 256 output tokens) as the headline workload: paging speed depends on how consecutive tokens route, so synthetic prompts mis-measure it. One 2,048-token prompt phase for long-prompt TTFT.
- Fixed prompt set per phase (a seed each, identical across engines and runs, never repeated across phases); prefix caching off in both engines; warm-up before measuring.
- Same KV capacity for both (10,240 tokens, 4 slots); byte-matched quantization (GPTQ int4 vs `IQ4_XS`, FP8 vs `Q8_0`).
- llama.cpp at its best: `--n-cpu-moe` searched in steps of 1 and counted only when its own memory projection fits physical VRAM, thread count swept per machine, `--load-mode none` and mmap both tried; `--fit on` and `--cpu-moe` reported too.
- Each headline cell measured twice.

Metrics: TTFT p50/p99 and ITL p50/p99 at bs=1, decode tok/s (`1000 / median TPOT`) at bs=1, output tok/s at bs=4, TTFT for a 2,048-token prompt, peak VRAM, time to ready.

### Results

Qwen3-30B-A3B. Runs separated by `/`; — in "time to ready": the cell includes the search for the best setting.

**16 GB card, int4** (GPTQ g128 vs `IQ4_XS`)

| config | decode tok/s | TTFT p50 / p99 | ITL p50 / p99 | 4 requests: out tok/s | TTFT, 2k prompt | peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **this PR** (auto K = 92 of 128) | **205.6 / 205.8 / 205.9** | 89 / 150 ms | 4.8 / 6.3 ms | **387 / 374 / 376** | **267 ms** | 14.7 GB |
| SGLang `--cpu-offload-gb 3` | 16.6 | 147 / 176 ms | 60.1 / 60.3 ms | 62 | 317 ms | 14.9 GB |
| llama.cpp `--n-cpu-moe 4` | 192.6 / 193.8 | 76 / 107 ms | 5.2 / 6.8 ms | 295 / 296 | 360 ms | 15.3 GB |
| llama.cpp `--n-cpu-moe 3`, q8 KV | 194.4 | **68 / 101 ms** | 5.1 / 6.8 ms | 312 | 344 ms | 15.2 GB |
| llama.cpp `--fit on` | 169.5 | 76 / 115 ms | 5.8 / 7.6 ms | 240 | 369 ms | 14.5 GB |
| llama.cpp `--cpu-moe` | 50.6 | 208 / 303 ms | 19.7 / 21.4 ms | 61 | 896 ms | 2.2 GB |


**16 GB card, FP8** (block FP8 vs `Q8_0`)

| config | decode tok/s | TTFT p50 / p99 | ITL p50 / p99 | 4 requests: out tok/s | TTFT, 2k prompt | peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **this PR** (auto K = 40 of 128) | **87.7 / 87.6** | 284 / 397 ms | 10.5 / 22.3 ms | **84 / 84** | **443 ms** | 13.4 GB |
| SGLang `--cpu-offload-gb 18` | 2.9 | 705 / 720 ms | 341 / 342 ms | 11 | 800 ms | 14.6 GB |
| llama.cpp `--n-cpu-moe 27` | 45.2 / 45.2 | 235 / 335 ms | 22.1 / 23.9 ms | 55 / 55 | 984 ms | 15.4 GB |
| llama.cpp `--n-cpu-moe 27`, q8 KV | 44.5 | 231 / 335 ms | 22.4 / 24.4 ms | 55 | 984 ms | 15.0 GB |
| llama.cpp `--fit on` | 43.1 | **226 / 343 ms** | 23.2 / 24.9 ms | 52 | 996 ms | 14.4 GB |
| llama.cpp `--cpu-moe` | 28.1 | 351 / 521 ms | 35.5 / 37.2 ms | 34 | 1,481 ms | 2.9 GB |


**8 GB laptop, int4** (GPTQ g128 vs `IQ4_XS`)

| config | decode tok/s | TTFT p50 / p99 | ITL p50 / p99 | 4 requests: out tok/s | TTFT, 2k prompt | peak VRAM |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **this PR** (auto K = 26 of 128) | 32.6 / 32.9 / 30.6 | 928 / 1,393 ms | 28.2 / 61.0 ms | 12 / 11 / 11 | **1,441 / 1,506 / 1,538 ms** | 7.5 GB |
| SGLang `--cpu-offload-gb 10` (bs=1 only) | 1.2 | 1,749 / 2,064 ms | 833 / 896 ms | — | — | 7.5 GB |
| llama.cpp `--n-cpu-moe 32` | 32.4 / 23.0 | 719 / 981 ms | 30.4 / 56.2 ms | **41 / 32** | 2,586 ms | 6.8 GB |
| llama.cpp `--n-cpu-moe 30`, q8 KV | 32.8 | **620 / 911 ms** | 29.0 / 55.0 ms | 40 | 2,396 ms | 7.0 GB |
| llama.cpp `--fit on` | 28.2 | 818 / 1,064 ms | 34.1 / 75.2 ms | 36 | 2,745 ms | 6.0 GB |
| llama.cpp `--cpu-moe` | 22.0 | 999 / 1,372 ms | 44.6 / 86.8 ms | 27 | 3,488 ms | 2.0 GB |


## Tests

- **Unit** (CPU): paged forward against unpaged over 1, 2 and 64 tokens and several steps; padding; LRU and waves; host-loader layout and tags; the K-at-a-time repack; device↔host residency round trip; sizing.
- **Kernel** (CUDA): decide against a Python reference over 200 random steps; the multi-tensor gather; decide + gather across 20 CUDA-graph replays with changing routing; rejection of more than K entries.
- **e2e** (`test/registered/e2e/moe/`): bf16, FP8 and GPTQ, each eager and with CUDA graphs (full decode, breakable prefill) against unpaged.

Run on RTX 5070 Ti (SM120) and RTX 4070 (SM89), with an image whose torch / sgl-kernel / FlashInfer predate this branch's upstream base (`SGLANG_SKIP_SGL_KERNEL_VERSION_CHECK=1`); CI on the current image may differ slightly.

## Known limitations

- **Startup is long for GPTQ.** The Marlin repack runs over the host store K experts at a time (slower at small K), and on the first start without a warm JIT cache, compiling upstream's `gptq_marlin` kernel takes minutes on a laptop CPU. With CUDA graphs off, that compile happens on the first request and can exceed the scheduler watchdog; this is upstream behaviour, not specific to paging.
- **The host store is pinned**, so the whole store must fit pinnable memory (WSL2 caps it at about half of system RAM).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [AMD] MiniMax-M3 indexer CP: packed scoring for EAGLE verify rows
author: kevin-mii
body:
## Motivation

With #41488 merged, MiniMax-M3 indexer context partitioning serves EAGLE chain verify: the ROCm verify
funnel hands the indexer each request's `ndt` draft rows as ordinary decode queries. The CP scorer then
scores them one row at a time. Its 16-row tile holds `WORLD`=4 live rows per program (one head per lane),
so it runs 25% occupied and reads every index-K block once per draft row -- four times per request at
the default 4 draft tokens.

## Modifications

1. **Packed scorer** (`kernels/ops/attention/minimax_sparse/decode/indexer_cp.py`). `score_local_blocks`
   takes `packed_queries`; when a request's rows fit the tile it launches `_score_shard_packed`, which maps
   tile row `i` to (draft row `i // WORLD`, head `i % WORLD`). That fills the tile and reads each K block
   once per request. Rows in a group can straddle a block boundary, so the K-read branch uses the group's
   longest row, while masking and the forced init/local blocks use each row's own length. A pack that does
   not fit the tile falls back to the existing kernel. Like `_score_shard`, it skips the K read for a slot
   past the request table (graph padding).
2. **Wiring** (10 lines). `minimax_sparse_decode` and `MiniMaxIndexerCP` pass `packed_queries` through;
   the backend passes the draft-token count for target-verify batches and 1 otherwise. Only the CP branch
   reads it, and CP already serves score-only layers alone, so no other path changes.

The packed kernel stays separate from `_score_shard`. Folding the plain path in as `PACK=1` reproduces it
exactly, but the vector row addressing measured 3.6% slower on ordinary decode (30/30 shapes).

## Accuracy Tests

Selection is exact, not approximate: the packed kernel must pick the same block IDs the native selector
picks for each row.

- `test_packed_verify_rows_match_the_native_selector` (registered AMD, 1 GPU) builds verify rows the way
  the funnel lays them out -- 4 requests x 4 draft rows -- ending at 32767..32770, so one tile mixes
  256- and 257-block rows with different local windows. bf16 and fp8: exact ID equality on every head.
  Each of these injected bugs fails it: the group's block count in place of each row's, sizing the group
  by its shortest row (fails only because the rows straddle a block boundary), dropping the forced local
  window, a wrong score-row index, and dropping the fp8-to-bf16 cast (fp8 subtest only).
- The shared `_inputs` now gives each request a permuted, gapped slot that never equals its row or group
  index. A packed kernel that addresses K by group index instead of through the slot table now fails (2
  subtests); before this change it passed. `test_minimax_indexer_cp.py` on gfx950 (MI355X): 2 passed,
  6 subtests.
- The test moves to the MI35x suite and skips off gfx950: its reference kernel needs more shared memory
  than MI300 has, and the CP path is gfx950-only.
- GSM8K-500, 5-shot: 0.896 packed vs 0.892 unpacked (same A/B as below). On the main A/B below:
  0.864 / 0.866 packed vs 0.884 / 0.886 unpacked; this raw few-shot gate moves about +-3.5 points between
  server instances of the same build, so read it as no change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiniMax-M3 MXFP4 (`amd/MiniMax-M3-MXFP4`), TP4 on MI350X, EAGLE3 (`Inferact/MiniMax-M3-EAGLE3-GQA`,
3 steps / 4 draft tokens, real acceptance), `SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEXER_CP=1`,
`SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_INDEX_TOPK_FREQ=1`. AgentX agentic traces (SemiAnalysis AIPerf, seed 42), 900 s per
point, both arms side by side on the node's two GPU halves with identical flags. The unpacked arm forces
`pack = 1` -- the scorer main runs today. Total tok/s per GPU:

| | unpacked (main today) | packed (this PR) | change | ITL p50 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| c=24 | 26,576 | **28,380** | **+6.8%** | 12.4 -> 10.2 ms |
| c=32 | 32,294 | **34,282** | **+6.2%** | 17.1 -> 12.7 ms |

Measured on a development branch whose CP kernel is identical to this PR and whose verify wiring is
equivalent (packing applies only to CP's score-only layers).

**On main.** A-B-B-A on one TP4 replica (MI350X, hostcall-capable node, `sgl_kernel` built from main),
main `44a2558d40` vs main + this PR, same flags as above, c=24, 900 s per arm:

| arm | total tok/s/GPU | ITL p50 |
|---|---:|---:|
| main | 16,912 / 16,983 | 30.8 / 31.0 ms |
| main + this PR | **17,728 / 17,731** | **28.5 / 28.0 ms** |

+4.6% throughput, -8.6% ITL p50; repeated arms agree within 0.4%. A 20-step decode profile of the PR arm
shows only `_score_shard_packed` (57 launches per rank per step, one per sparse layer) and no `_score_shard`.
Both arms ran with `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled`, because main crashes on its first M3 prefill
with breakable prefill graphs (fixed by #41845); the decode/verify path this PR changes is unaffected.
The gain on main is smaller than on the development branch because main's other per-step costs are larger.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add unit tests according to the Run and add unit tests.
- [ ] Update documentation -- not applicable; no user-facing interface change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results.
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style guidance.

title: [Perf] moe: Enable deferred finalize for NVFP4 on the routed TRT-LLM runner
author: vincentzed
body:
## Motivation

This PR covers the NVFP4 case of #39299.

- Deferred finalize means the MoE kernel skips its last step, the weighted sum over the selected experts. A later fused kernel then does that step together with the shared-expert add.
- Today NVFP4 experts on the `flashinfer_trtllm_routed` runner can never use it. The hybrid FP8 + NVFP4 DeepSeek V4 / V4.1 checkpoints always use this runner, because the routing options built into the kernel (`RoutingMethodType`) cannot describe their routing.
- The routed FlashInfer op already accepts `do_finalize=False`, and the MXFP4 method uses it (#38798). The NVFP4 routed path was never connected to it. Three places block it:

1. `FusedMoE.supports_deferred_finalize` requires `is_flashinfer_trtllm()`, which is false for the routed backend.
2. `DeepseekV2MoE` only defers when the top-k output format is `BYPASSED`. The routed runner receives regular top-k ids and weights.
3. `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp4` only set `defer_finalize` when `use_routed_topk` was false, and the routed call always passed `do_finalize=True`. #44666 has since changed this on main, so the routed call can now defer. Blockers 1 and 2 remain on main.

wenchen76 is working in the same direction in wenchen76/sglang#1.

## Modifications

- `FusedMoE`: new flag `supports_routed_deferred_finalize`. It is true for `ModelOptNvFp4FusedMoEMethod` on `flashinfer_trtllm_routed`, when there is no A2A backend and the routed scaling factor is already folded into the top-k weights. `supports_deferred_finalize` is not changed, so the CuTe DSL layer-boundary fusion, Kimi and Qwen paths behave as before.
- `DeepseekV2MoE`: picks which flag to check from the top-k output format. `BYPASSED` top-k checks the old flag. Regular top-k checks the new one.
- `fused_experts_none_to_flashinfer_trtllm_fp4`: #44666 (merged 2026-10-18) now makes the routed call defer on main, and this PR uses that code. This PR only adds the workaround below to it.
- Workaround: the deferred routed call still passes a `[T, hidden]` output buffer, although the kernel does not write to it in deferred mode. FlashInfer's autotune cache key includes the output shape. With `output=None` the lookup misses the tuned entry and the expert GEMMs run with a fallback tactic. On FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1 each call was 9 to 14% slower. I filed this as flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6077 with a standalone repro. The lookup still misses on 0.7.2 (see below). The buffer can be removed once that is fixed.
- `SGLANG_ENABLE_MOE_DEFERRED_FINALIZE=0` turns the new behavior off.
- `test_deepseek_v4_amd_tp4.py`: the MoE stub gets the new attribute.

Since #42245, the V4 block asks the MoE for deferred output whenever the fused mHC kernel can be used. With this PR the NVFP4 routed runner can return it. So NVFP4 now uses the single fused kernel that does the finalize, the shared-expert add and the all-reduce, and no other condition has to change.

## Accuracy Tests
