### Accuracy

**By design this PR does not affect accuracy: it only changes which tile configuration (tactic) of the same MoE GEMM runs**, so the GEMM computes the same values, at most with a different summation order (with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's MoE shape, one call at 8192–32768 tokens is bit-identical to the fallback tactic). **Measured: GSM8K stays within sampling noise on all seven models (−0.83 to +0.15 points) and in the DeepSeek-V4-Flash CI test (+1.5).**

| Test | main | this PR | difference, percentage points (95% noise range) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| GSM8K, all 1,319 test questions, 20-shot, temperature 0: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash | 91.43% | 90.60% | −0.83 (±2.2) |
| Same: Nemotron-3.5-Lightning | 87.64% | 87.79% | +0.15 (±2.5) |
| Same: Ling-3.0-flash | 86.28% | 86.05% | −0.23 (±2.6) |
| Same: gpt-oss-20b | 80.14% | 79.38% | −0.76 (±3.1) |
| Same, through the chat API (up to 4096 output tokens): GLM-5.3-Flash | 97.35% | 96.82% | −0.53 (±1.3) |
| Same, chat API: MiniMax-M3 | 97.19% | 97.27% | +0.08 (±1.3) |
| Same, chat API: Gemma-4-26B-A4B-it | 96.36% | 96.06% | −0.30 (±1.5) |
| CI `TestDSV4FlashFP4H200FlashInferCutlass.test_gsm8k` (DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4 + EAGLE, 200 questions; threshold 93%) | 96.0% | 97.5% | +1.5 (±3.5) |

The noise range is 1.96 standard errors of the difference between two scores over that many questions (an independent-sample approximation, conservative here because both versions answer the same questions). GPQA and long-context evals were not run.

<details>
<summary>GSM8K command</summary>

The 20 shots are the first 20 training examples, so no test question appears in the prompt.

```bash
{ curl -sL $D/train.jsonl | head -n 20; curl -sL $D/test.jsonl; } > gsm8k_k20.jsonl
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --eval-name gsm8k --num-shots 20 --num-examples 1319 \
  --num-threads 32 --api completion --gsm8k-data-path gsm8k_k20.jsonl
# GLM-5.3-Flash, MiniMax-M3, Gemma-4: --api chat --max-tokens 4096 instead of --api completion
```

</details>

## CI

**No file fails only with this PR, and the new CPU test passes all 80 sub-cases (60 fail on main).** Local CI on 8×H200 with the commands CI uses: every CPU and GPU suite this machine can run (1,427 files) with this PR, and on its parent main every CPU suite in full plus every file that failed with this PR. SM100, SM110 and SM120 cannot run here; the CI tests that reach the changed call there (`test_mxfp4_sm120_cutlass.py` on the RTX 5090 runner, `test_nvfp4_moe_backends.py::test_flashinfer_cutlass` on B200) are in upstream CI; this command runs them with the other changed test files and the DeepSeek-V4-Flash H200 test: `/rerun-test -c registered/unit/layers/quantization/test_nvfp4_moe_backends.py registered/e2e/models/test_deepseek_v4_flash_fp4_h200.py::TestDSV4FlashFP4H200FlashInferCutlass`.

<summary>Results per test and per suite, and why the other files fail</summary>

| `TestDSV4FlashFP4H200FlashInferCutlass` (TP4 + EAGLE) | 8 of 9 pass (`test_bs_1_speed`: accept length 2.790, threshold 2.8; borderline and unrelated to MoE tactics) | 9 of 9 pass |

- They fail on main at this PR's base for their own reasons: `kernels/ops/attention/test_dsa_metadata_replay.py` (fixed on main by #42750 after this PR's base); `pp/test_pp_gemma4.py` (accuracy 0.498, threshold 0.65); `core/test_basic_sanity_eagle3.py` (`fwd_occupancy` 97.7, threshold 98); `core/test_basic_sanity_dspark.py`; `prefill_only/test_embedding_models.py`; `prefill_only/test_pooled_hidden_states.py`; `unit/mem_cache/test_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`; `unit/mem_cache/test_rust_unified_radix_cache_unittest.py`; and in `base-a-test-cpu`, `test_disagg_idle_step_counters.py`, `test_page_interleave_shard.py`, `test_vit_npu_graph_runner.py`, `test_numa_utils.py`.

## Related work

- #42693 (merged): autotunes GLM-5.3-Flash's TRT-LLM MoE kernels at prefill sizes through a model-specific startup pass. This PR does the same for FlashInfer's CUTLASS MoE kernel, for every model that uses it, without an extra pass.

The two are complementary, touch different files and can land in either order; with #42736 and flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5631 both landed, they would together cover this PR's prefill gain (from the code; not measured).

title: [diffusion] perf: pipeline MiniMax-H3's Ulysses exchange against cuDNN SDPA on Blackwell
author: mickqian
body:
Stacked on #43361 (#43164 is merged). Merge #43361 first; this PR's own change is the cuDNN gate in `minimax_h3.py` and one cookbook line.

## Motivation

On Blackwell, MiniMax-H3's dense attention runs on cuDNN SDPA through `DynamicCudnnSDPAImpl`. The pipelined Ulysses exchange from #43164 only accepted the FlashAttention backend, so B200/B300 kept the sequential exchange and got none of it.

## Modifications

- The pipeline also accepts `AttentionBackendEnum.DYNAMIC_CUDNN_SDPA`. Attention still runs through the backend's `forward_varlen`, one head group at a time.
- The skip-softmax check only exists on the FlashAttention impl, so it is now optional.
- Cookbook: the configuration note says the pipeline runs against FlashAttention on Hopper and cuDNN SDPA on Blackwell.

## Accuracy Tests

- **Per head group, cuDNN SDPA gives the same bytes as those heads inside the full call.** Checked with `torch.equal` on 4×B300 at H3's per-rank attention shapes:
  - 49652 tokens × 28 heads in groups of 4 (Ref2VA, Ulysses 2);
  - 37742 tokens × 28 heads in groups of 4 (T2VA, Ulysses 2);
  - 37744 tokens × 14 heads in groups of 2 (T2VA, Ulysses 4).

  It holds on both torch 2.14.1 with cuDNN 9.24 and torch 2.13 with cuDNN 9.20.
- End to end on 4×B300, the MP4 md5 is the same for the sequential exchange and for 7, 4 and 2 groups, in every cell.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Client end-to-end latency, 4×B300, 50 steps, default quality, one run per arm. The base is this stack (#43164 + #43361) with #43327 and #43337, and `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_ULYSSES_PIPELINE_GROUPS` selects the sequential exchange (0) or a group count:

| Case | sequential | 7 groups (default) | 4 groups | 2 groups |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| T2VA 5 s, Ulysses 2 | 65.83 s | 63.24 s (−3.9%) | 63.40 s (−3.7%) | 63.48 s (−3.6%) |
| T2VA 5 s, Ulysses 4 | 34.20 s | 32.75 s (−4.3%) | — | 32.90 s (−3.8%) |
| Ref2VA 5 s, Ulysses 2 | 102.68 s | 99.24 s (−3.4%) | 98.70 s (−3.9%) | 98.89 s (−3.7%) |

- Blackwell gains more than Hopper (2–3%) because its exchange is a larger share of a faster step.
- Splitting heads costs cuDNN some efficiency, which FlashAttention 3 does not pay. On B300, 7 group calls over the Ref2VA shape take 3.5% longer than one call over all heads, and over the Ulysses 4 shape (2 heads per call) 5.4% longer. That is why 4 groups edge out 7 for Ref2VA in this single-run pass.
- A paired ABBA of 7 against 4 groups on B300 puts 4 ahead by only 0.1–0.2%, within run-to-run noise: Ref2VA 98.70 → 98.51 s, T2VA 63.74 → 63.68 s. So the automatic count stays at 7 for both backends.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] fp8_fa_sm120: Use the block-scaled MMA encoding
author: emre570
body:
## Motivation

`fp8_fa_sm120` computes QK and PV with the plain FP8 `mma.sync` (E4M3 x E4M3, FP32
accumulate). On GeForce SM120 this instruction runs at half rate. I measured the raw MMA
peak on an RTX 5080 with back-to-back chains and no memory traffic:

| instruction | SASS | TFLOP/s |
|---|---|---:|
| plain FP8, FP32 accumulate | `QMMA.16832.F32.E4M3.E4M3` | 246 |
| block-scaled FP8, FP32 accumulate | `QMMA.SF.16832.F32.E4M3.E4M3.E8` | 488 |

The block-scaled encoding (`kind::mxf8f6f4.block_scale`) multiplies each operand by a
UE8M0 scale, one byte per 32 k elements. With every scale byte set to 0x7F (2^0) the math
is the same product. On random finite E4M3 inputs, 0 of 704 M accumulator registers differ
between the two instructions.

So the kernel was limited by the instruction encoding, not by its design.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/attention/fp8_fa_sm120/kernel.py`
  - The MMA atom is `warp.MmaMXF8Op` when the compile target has it (sm_120a/f,
    sm_121a/f), `warp.MmaFP8Op` otherwise.
  - Four scale fragments (for Q, K, P, V) hold the constant byte 0x7F. They live in
    registers: no shared memory, no extra loads.
  - The two `cute.gemm` calls pass `[operand, scale]` pairs.
- `kernels/ops/attention/fp8_fa_sm120/plan.py`: the public `fp8_attention()` signature is
  unchanged. An internal compile-time parameter selects the encoding. It is not a user
  option, because the output is bit-equal and there is no speed against accuracy choice.
- One unit test runs both encodings on the same inputs and requires equal bits.

Operand layouts, shared memory, the softmax, the P pack and the prep do not change.
Register count goes from 244 to 250, no stack.

## Accuracy Tests

The output is bit-identical to `main`. Same inputs (seed 42), SHA-256 over the O and LSE
bytes, `main` against this branch:

| H | S | equal |
|---:|---:|---|
| 8 | 1052 (key mask path) | yes |
| 56 | 20440 | yes |
| 56 | 30272 | yes |

Unit tests: 10/10, including the new bit-equality test.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

RTX 5080, H=56, D=128, median of 5 runs, same process and inputs.

| S | prep (ms) | kernel `main` (ms) | kernel this PR (ms) | full call `main` (ms) | full call this PR (ms) |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 20440 | 2.60 | 56.34 | 37.66 | 58.91 | 40.27 |
| 30272 | 3.84 | 123.60 | 83.28 | 127.26 | 86.29 |

The full call is 1.47x faster at both lengths. Against cuDNN SDPA BF16 on the same card
(226 ms at S=30272) the backend is now 2.6x faster, was 1.8x.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations). No user-facing change.
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Fix] Account for captured inputs in DeepGEMM masked workspace budget
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

DeepGEMM's automatic standard-layout policy can select a masked workspace that OOMs during prefill CUDA Graph capture. The estimate assumes the runner input is released after the gate/up GEMM, but capture makes `dispose_tensor` a no-op: the input and its scales remain live during activation and the down GEMM.

Reproduced on H200 with the default memory fraction, prefill chunk size, and graph settings:

| Model | TP | Failing prefill shape | Masked budget | Failing `down_output` allocation |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 | 1 | 4608 | 3.15 GiB | 2.38 GiB, with 1.20 GiB free |
| Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 | 2 | 3072 | 5.37 GiB | 4.88 GiB, with 1.89 GiB free |

The 30B failure reproduces with a warm compilation cache. Minimal 30B reproduction: `python -m sglang.launch_server --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-FP8 --tp-size 1 --moe-runner-backend deep_gemm`.

## Modifications

Include the retained input and scales in the activation/down-GEMM peak estimate. Use the same conservative bound during warmup and capture so layout selection stays consistent. Extend the existing layout-policy test with the two failing geometries and packed/unpacked scales; no new test files.

Explicit layout overrides and the budget fraction are unchanged. Automatic selection can switch to compact earlier on other models too: the existing 397B-shaped fixture now selects compact at 8K under its 42.5 GiB budget, while 4K remains masked. That can change performance near the selection boundary.

## Accuracy Tests

- Existing `test/registered/kernels/ops/moe/test_minimax_quant_scatter.py`: **53 passed** on GB300. The six parameterized policy cases fail against the original estimator.
- Both affected models complete startup, graph capture, serving benchmarks, and GSM8K with the fix on H200. Validation base: `e35f60b9`.
- GSM8K: 1,314 held-out cases, greedy, 2,048-token cap, identical case IDs/prompt hashes. Qwen3-30B fixed-auto scored **1215 / 1217** across two runs; forced-compact controls scored **1223 / 1221**. All requests stopped normally, with no errors. The reverse pair loses 13 and gains 9 cases; these results do not establish numerical equivalence.
- Qwen3.5-122B fixed-auto scored **1275**, versus **1277** with the default Triton MoE runner. Both have the same two length-capped cases, retained in scoring, and no request errors. Original DeepGEMM auto cannot supply an accuracy baseline because startup fails.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Qwen3-30B, one H200, 320 requests, nominal 8K input / 1K output, concurrency 64. Saved prompts and actual token counts match across all four runs. Repeated in reverse order:

| Configuration | Output token/s, runs 1 / 2 | Median TPOT ms, runs 1 / 2 |
|---|---:|---:|
| Forced compact | 1852.52 / 1853.72 | 30.608 / 30.596 |
| Fixed auto | 2083.69 / 2083.45 | 26.780 / 26.779 |

Fixed auto retains masked decode while using compact for large prefills: about **12.4%** faster than the forced-compact workaround, with median TTFT around 4.04 seconds in both configurations. The default Triton runner remains faster at 2140.95 token/s; this fixes capture reliability rather than establishing a generally faster backend. Qwen3.5-122B also remains slower with DeepGEMM than with its default Triton runner.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit and `git diff --check` passed.
- [x] Extended an existing test file; GPU suite passed.
- [x] GPU startup, accuracy, and serving comparisons completed.
- [x] No public API or launch-option changes requiring documentation.

title: [Perf] Compact GDN causal-conv grids for skewed prefill batches
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

GDN's prefill convolution launches a rectangular grid sized by the longest sequence. With an 8K prefill chunk and 127 decode rows, this schedules about 3.1 million CTAs, most of which immediately return. The same overhead is repeated across 36 GDN layers in Qwen3.5-122B-A10B.

## Modifications

Build a compact `(sequence, chunk)` table once per forward and reuse the existing causal-conv kernel's `block_table` path across layers. This reduces the example above to 27,264 CTAs without changing convolution arithmetic or state updates.

Enable this for CUDA EXTEND/MIXED batches only when the rectangular grid has more than four times as many sequence/chunk blocks as the compact grid. Uniform and mildly ragged batches keep the existing launch to avoid table-construction overhead. MIS, TBO, speculative modes, non-CUDA paths, and unavailable or mismatched host lengths retain the existing behavior.

This is narrower than the prefill/decode split in #36065: it only compacts the convolution grid and does not change GDN attention dispatch.

## Accuracy Tests

- Extended three existing test files; no new test files. On both H200 and GB300, all 29 tests and 55 subtests pass:
  ```bash
  python -m pytest -q \
    test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_gdn_prefill_backend_policy.py \
    test/registered/unit/layers/attention/test_mamba_track_state_dtype.py \
    test/registered/attention/test_gdn_prefill_layout.py
  ```
- CUDA tests compare convolution output and the entire state cache bitwise, including strided QKV, ragged/empty rows, initial state, permuted cache indices, and a padded cache slot. A separate microbenchmark also checks bitwise output/state at the model's actual convolution dimension of 6,144.
- Full held-out GSM8K validation uses 1,314 cases, five separate few-shot examples, temperature 0, seed 42, concurrency 64, and a 2,048-token limit. Case IDs and prompt hashes match; all runs have zero request errors. The first and reverse-order pairs give:

  | Run | Correct / 1314 | Token-limit case IDs |
  | --- | ---: | --- |
  | Baseline A | 1270 | 119, 423, 641, 1176, 1183 |
  | Compact A | 1273 | 119, 711 |
  | Compact B | 1273 | 119, 304, 423 |
  | Baseline B | 1276 | 119, 423, 1176 |

  The first pair has three losses/six gains; the reverse pair has five losses/two gains. Case 711 is correct on the candidate repeat; case 304 is newly capped there. No case is correct in both baseline runs and incorrect in both candidate runs. Baseline answers also vary across repeats. These measurements do not establish identical full-model outputs or statistical non-inferiority.

- Default cached-path regression check (mixed chunk disabled): C128 throughput 2693.96 -> 2699.97 output tok/s, median TTFT 12.886 -> 12.913 s, TPOT 34.90 -> 34.86 ms, and p99 E2E 48.87 -> 48.72 s. Exact requests/token counts match. GSM8K is 1277/1314 in both runs, with three losses and three gains and zero errors; token-limit finishes increase from two to four (new cases 87 and 157). This is a completed regression check with the per-case differences disclosed, not a claim of identical model outputs.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same 2x H200, TP2, Qwen3.5-122B-A10B-FP8 revision `a099dee70ccfcd8d5dda56aaa0b60cb8ecadabc9`; baseline `e35f60b9`, candidate adds only this patch. Nominal 8192-token inputs and fixed 1024-token outputs, seed 42, 320/640 requests at C64/C128. Exact request records and actual token counts match. Timings exclude profiling and follow warmup/cache flush.

Both versions use FlashInfer full attention, Triton GDN prefill, BF16 Mamba state, `--enable-mixed-chunk`, and `--disable-radix-cache`. These numbers isolate the convolution change; they do not validate enabling mixed chunk with the default prefix-cache path.

| Concurrency | Version | Output tok/s | Median TTFT (s) | Median TPOT (ms) | p99 E2E (s) |
| --- | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 64 | Baseline | 2126.54 | 1.120 | 28.94 | 42.68 |
| 64 | Compact grid | 2204.10 | 1.024 | 27.85 | 40.95 |
| 128 | Baseline | 2470.12 | 1.205 | 50.92 | 79.48 |
| 128 | Compact grid | 2686.89 | 1.073 | 46.36 | 72.63 |
| 128 | Compact grid, repeat | 2698.68 | 1.068 | 46.09 | 72.21 |
| 128 | Baseline, reverse repeat | 2475.35 | 1.273 | 50.62 | 78.95 |

C64 output throughput improves by 3.6%. C128 improves by 8.8% in the first pair and 9.0% in the reverse-order pair (A-B-B-A), with matching request records and actual token counts. Median TPOT and p99 E2E also improve in both C128 pairs.

A second full pair using `--prefill-attention-backend fa3` also improves C64 from 2193.74 to 2275.06 output tok/s and C128 from 2564.33 to 2797.15 (+9.1%). At C128, median TTFT changes from 1.205 to 1.000 s, TPOT from 48.94 to 44.55 ms, and p99 E2E from 75.45 to 68.98 s. Inputs and actual token counts match. GSM8K is 1272/1314 in both versions, with three losses and three gains, zero request errors, and three token-limit finishes each (candidate case 425 is newly capped). This separately checks the FA3 prefill backend; the repeated same-configuration results above isolate the convolution patch.

For `[8065] + [1] * 127`, dimension 6144 and width 4, isolated convolution time changes from 1873.5 to 104.0 us on H200 and 1568.4 to 86.7 us on GB300. Host table construction plus transfer takes about 280 us once per forward, amortized across layers. The approximately 18x kernel speedup is not an end-to-end model speedup.

A separate TP2 trace with 127 active decode requests confirms the actual dispatch: across eight mixed steps and 288 convolution launches, per-rank convolution GPU time drops from 525.87 to 29.26 ms on rank 0 and 525.88 to 29.79 ms on rank 1. Decode progress differs between those profiling probes, so their total wall times are not treated as matched end-to-end measurements.

## Checklist

- [x] Pre-commit checks pass.
- [x] Existing CPU/CUDA tests extended and run on H200 and GB300.
- [x] First full-model timing and accuracy pair completed.
- [x] Default cached-path C128 timing and full GSM8K regression check (results and per-case differences above).
- [x] Reverse-order C128 timing and full GSM8K confirmation, including per-case and token-limit comparisons.

title: [DSpark] Add `MarkovSampleStep`, one op for a markov draft step's add and token pick
author: hnyls2002
body:
Stacks on #43620.

- `MarkovSampleStep` adds a step's bias to the base logits, rounds the sum to the head's step dtype, and picks one token per row: the argmax at temperature 0, a Gumbel-max sample otherwise. Triton and torch implementations.
- The noise is Philox4x32-10 computed in the kernel, keyed by the server seed and countered by (global token id, row, step, a per-block offset). It needs no noise tensor, does not touch the torch generator, and every TP rank draws the same values from the same inputs.
- TP-sharded vocab: without kept logits each rank reduces its shard to one (value, index) pair per block and only those pairs are all-gathered; with kept logits the step logits are gathered once and every rank picks from the full vocab. Either way a step takes one collective.
- A greedy-only variant (no temperature read, no noise code) compiles when no row samples.
- Replaces `sharded_greedy.py`; the DeepSeek-V4.1 greedy graph tail now calls the op.
- Tests: Triton against the torch reference, the greedy-only variant against the mixed one, NaN and inf, ties across blocks, strided rows, the tempered-softmax distribution, noise keying, and sharded against full vocab in both gather modes.

No behavior change: greedy picks are the same argmax with the same lowest-index tie rule.

## Verification

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/speculative/test_dspark_markov_sample.py`: 9 passed on GB300 (torch 2.14.1, Triton 3.8.0).
- Per launch, against the kernels it replaces: the greedy-only variant is no slower than the old sharded greedy step, and sampling rows run 2.0-2.3x faster than the old sampling path. 1024-wide blocks cut a one-row sampled step over a 129280-token vocab from 5.6 to 2.4 us.

title: [Perf] Enable native MXFP4 routing and CuTeDSL fusion for MiMo
author: leonardHONG
body:
## Motivation

MiMo MXFP4 currently computes routing separately and finalizes the MoE output before communication. Use FlashInfer native routing and deferred finalization with the existing CuTeDSL layer-boundary fusion to reduce this overhead.

## Modifications

- Add native grouped routing and deferred finalization for supported MiMo MXFP4 configurations.
- Support CuTeDSL layer-boundary fusion without shared experts.
- Automatically select CuTeDSL for supported configurations, preserving explicit backend choices.
- Keep standard routing for expert capture, distribution recording, simulated routing and expert remapping. Exclude PDMux from automatic selection.

RoPE/KV-store fusion remains in #43106.

## Accuracy Tests

The same 128 frozen GSM8K questions, normal EOS and generation settings were used for both versions. Exact numerical-answer scoring changes from 123/128 to 124/128, with two gains and one loss. Strict answer-string scoring is 119/128 and 120/128, respectively.

Fixed-prefix full-vocabulary log-probabilities were compared on 24 cases. Exact argmax matches in 22 cases; one additional mismatch falls within the baseline's tied top-1 set, while one changes the top-1 choice outside that set. Mean total variation distance is 3.15%, with a maximum of 14.10%.

FlashInfer native routing returns BF16 expert weights, while the precomputed route retains FP32 weights. Generated outputs and DFlash acceptance trajectories are not identical. These checks do not establish numerical equivalence or general quality equivalence.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MiMo-V2.6-Pro-RL revision `73875d00b30a`, 8×B300, TP8, concurrency one, FA4, page size 128, KV capacity 32768 and prefix caching disabled.

Baseline: `6e7beace143964386ce2e4418401b7369f0dabd0`.
Candidate: `d7b192133f73ef2068debc349eda85a1d0dce218`.

Each comparison uses one fresh server per revision, three warmups and 96 frozen random-topic essay requests with 8,000 input tokens and 1,024 output tokens. EOS is ignored only for timing. Both versions use the same model, dependencies and requests; DFlash comparisons also use the same draft checkpoint.

Decode throughput uses tokens emitted after the first emission divided by the first-to-last emission interval. E2E throughput and TTFT are reported separately. Timing excludes profiling and log-probability collection.

| Mode | Decode tok/s | E2E tok/s | TTFT ms |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| DFlash, baseline | 302.44 | 285.44 | 204.75 |
| DFlash, candidate | 338.01 | 315.72 | 216.63 |
| Without DFlash, baseline | 176.54 | 170.75 | 202.17 |
| Without DFlash, candidate | 186.58 | 179.74 | 214.21 |

With DFlash, decode throughput improves by 11.76% and E2E throughput by 10.61%. All 96 requests have partial rejection; acceptance changes from 21.38% to 21.61%, so the measured gain includes verification-workload differences.

Without DFlash, decode throughput improves by 5.69% and E2E throughput by 5.26%. Mean TTFT increases by approximately 12 ms in both modes.

These results cover the measured single-concurrency workload and are single fresh-server pairs, not multi-run confidence estimates.

<!-- pr-states:start -->

title: [DCP] Decode context parallelism for DSA (GLM-5.2 / GLM-5.3) with MTP
author: kpham-sgl
body:
## Motivation

`--dcp-size > 1` does not work for the RoPE DSA models (GLM-5.2, GLM-5.3, DeepSeek-V3.2): the sparse backend returns no LSE, the index-K cache and the MTP draft pool are sized per rank while the allocator hands out widened slots, and the TRT-LLM buffers are sized for one rank's heads. Builds on the approach of #42536 (co-authored with @vincentzed) and the Flash stack #40433 / #40434.

## Modifications

- **Target KV** stays striped by position (unchanged `main` layout). The **index-K cache is replicated** and addressed by the widened allocator slot, so every rank scores the whole sequence and selects the global top-k.
- **Attention**: one Triton kernel keeps the top-k slots this rank owns, maps them to local rows and compacts them; the TRT-LLM sparse kernel runs on the DCP group's gathered query heads with `return_lse`, and the existing MLA DCP merge combines the partials. Decode, target verify and extend all take this path (no prefix-KV gather). Shared-top-k layers reuse the localized table (21 remaps per step instead of 78).
- **MTP draft (nextn)**: the pool is replicated over the widened slots (`dcp_replicated`, kernel page stays 64) and the draft attends without the DCP group (`is_nextn` / `is_draft_worker`, as the Qwen3.5 draft does), so MTP index share feeds the draft directly.
- **Accounting**: index keys and the draft pool are charged `dcp_size` times per physical token on every platform (the NPU-only guards are dropped).
- **Launch validation**: the generic DCP hook now rejects prefill CP with `--dcp-size > 1`; the DSA override rejects HiSparse, HiCache, PD disaggregation and tree drafting, and defaults the DSA backends to `trtllm` (`index_kpool > 1` was already rejected on `main`).
- **Fast follows** (rejected at launch for now): HiCache and PD disaggregation need the replicated index-K cache's widened page geometry in the host pool and the transfer page-id lists; other DSA backends need to return the LSE under DCP.
- Kept from #42536: the LSE combine keeps all-empty padding rows at zero. Not kept: the head folding to at most 32 heads per trtllm call. Vincent's reproducer (comment below) does fail on B300 with FlashInfer 0.7.0.post1, for exactly 64 heads with short KV at >= 1024 rows per call (16, 32 and 128 heads are clean up to 65535 rows), so this is a kernel bug that only DCP8 extend can hit. It will be filed with FlashInfer once the cause is narrowed down; the gathered heads go to the kernel in one call.

Design notes with permalinks: `dsa-dcp-design.md` (shared separately).

## Accuracy Tests

`zai-org/GLM-5.3` (FP8), 8xB300, `--tp 8 --mem-fraction-static 0.88 --max-running-requests 64`, branch at `28bb3d6074`. MTP = `--speculative-algorithm EAGLE --speculative-num-steps 5 --speculative-eagle-topk 1 --speculative-num-draft-tokens 6`. GSM8K: `few_shot_gsm8k`, 8-shot, 1319 questions. AIME26: `sgl-eval run aime26 --n-repeats 4` with the GLM-5.2-FP8 preset (200k max tokens).

| Config | GSM8K acc | AIME26 pass@1 (avg of 4) | AIME26 pass@4 | AIME26 gen tok/s | MTP accept len |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP8 | 0.912 | 99.17% | 100% | 1140 | - |
| TP8 + DCP2 | 0.917 | 99.17% | 100% | 1041 | - |
| TP8 + DCP2 + MTP | 0.919 | 95.83% | 100% | 1876 | 3.51 |
| TP8 + DCP8 | 0.914 | 95.00% | 100% | 838 | - |
| TP8 + DCP8 + MTP | 0.919 | 95.00% | 100% | 1784 | 3.62 |

Spot checks (GSM8K, 300-400 questions): `--dcp-comm-backend ag_rs` DCP2 + MTP 0.907; an 8192-token-per-rank pool so the last allocator page is in use, DCP2 0.903 and DCP2 + MTP 0.907; without head folding, DCP8 0.943 and DCP8 + MTP 0.913 (the 64-head case).

AIME26 pass@1 spread is sampling noise: every run loses problem 14 to the 200k cap (including TP8), and the remaining misses are either a correct final line without `\boxed{}` (3 in DCP2 + MTP, 2 in DCP8) or single-sample arithmetic slips; no run shows degenerate output. The DCP2 + MTP run surfaced one bug, fixed in `28bb3d6074`: the DSA draft's one-shot MHA prefill keyed its prefix all-gather on the global DCP flag instead of the layer's `dcp_size`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit.
- [x] GPU kernel test (localize kernel, merged shards vs the unsharded kernel at 64 heads) and a registered 4-GPU GLM-5.3 TP4 + DCP2 + MTP GSM8K test.
- [x] Update `docs/docs/advanced_features/dcp.mdx`.
- [x] Accuracy results (above).

title: [DeepSeek-V4.1] Run decoder SWA bounded replay inside the breakable prefill CUDA graph
author: jyizheng
body:
## Motivation

`--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` refuses every prefill CUDA graph backend, so DeepSeek-V4.1 prefill runs eager whenever bounded replay is on. On GB300 the eager prefill step is host-launch-bound (~2.5k launches per request per rank, ~10 ms of GPU work inside a ~230 ms step), so this is the dominant TTFT cost at low and medium concurrency.

This is the same gap #42078, #42909, #43440 and #43534 address. The variant here keeps the late layers on their bounded-replay tail **inside the same breakable prefill graph** instead of capturing separate late-layer graphs or running the captured late layers on full rows; the measurements below are why.

## Modifications

- The late layers (after the last KV source layer) run over a per-shape tail block inside the captured graph: `tail_rows = min(max_running_requests x 128, shape tokens)`. The tail's extend/positions/scatter indices and SWA write locations live in persistent, block-sized buffers (padding rows point at slot 0), so the graph replays with no reallocation; one tail metadata per block size is built the prefill-graph way (`use_prefill_cuda_graph=True`) and refreshed in place on every replay (`_prefill_graph_tail_metadata`, `prefill_graph_enter/exit_late_layer_tail`).
- `DeepseekV4Model.forward` switches to the tail at the `enter`/`exit` eager breaks and scatters the tail rows back (`_scatter_tail_rows` graph branch); the outer forward slices logits by `hidden_states_token_indices`, which the runner's `_trim_logits_output` now carries so the DSpark injector sees the right rows.
- `init_forward_metadata_in_graph` clears `tail_forward_metadata` on the decode/target-verify graph paths: the prefill graph capture/replay leaves it set, and the decode graph capture that follows otherwise slices a decode publish in `_publish_candidate_metadata` (`NotImplementedError: _SparseTable is not a prefill publish`).
- `validate_deepseek_v41_features` admits `Backend.BREAKABLE` with decoder bounded replay (encoder replay still eager).

With this, `--enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay` and `--cuda-graph-backend-prefill breakable` work together; the capture width (`--cuda-graph-max-seq-len-prefill`, default 16k) is unchanged. #43733 builds on this to replay the graph at any context length.

## Accuracy Tests

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 1P1D on GB300 (prefill TP4 + decode TP4, DSpark PD, FlashMLA): capture of 74 shapes; needle prompts at 4.5k / 11k / 40k and greedy 24k / 40k / 86k-token prompts return the expected key with text matching the eager run (divergence within eager run-to-run noise); six-rung real-trace replay (300 s per rung) 100% success at every rung. Validated on the Sep-24 nightly series and on the Oct-8 nightly (7760d526) stack; the rebase onto current `main` applies cleanly and is compile- and lint-checked. A GPU run on `main` itself is still owed.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Same deployment, real DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash production trace (ISL median 6.7k / p90 127k), three arms that differ only in the late-layer handling: eager + bounded replay (today), breakable graph with the late layers on full rows (bounded replay off inside the graph), and this PR (late layers on the tail inside the graph). All graph arms capture at 16k.

| conc | TTFT p50 eager / full rows / tail | TTFT p90 | output tok/min per chip | TPOT |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 272 / 179 / **152** ms | 1,071 / 1,162 / **1,026** | 2,292 / 2,268 / **2,375** | 2.67 / 2.75 / 2.64 |
| 4 | 496 / 362 / **327** | 1,903 / 1,900 / 1,940 | 7,687 / 7,618 / **7,989** | 2.87 / 2.97 / 2.87 |
| 8 | 748 / **519** / 545 | 2,498 / 2,561 / **2,149** | 12,790 / 12,813 / **13,870** | 3.11 / 3.24 / 3.11 |
| 16 | 1,215 / 1,397 / **1,226** | 6,419 / 10,017 / **6,512** | 17,123 / 16,270 / **17,340** | 3.64 / 3.73 / 3.70 |
| 32 | 3,304 / 3,667 / **3,415** | 17,899 / 19,676 / **17,841** | 20,115 / 19,833 / 20,073 | 4.12 / 4.12 / 4.15 |

Idle-worker floor: an 11-token request 258-302 ms -> 59-60 ms end to end, an 11k cached-prefix request 298-320 ms -> 65-72 ms. Full rows inside the graph wins the floor but returns the bounded-replay saving once the batch fills (at 16 concurrent it is behind eager on p50 and p90); the tail inside the graph keeps eager-level p90 and adds 5-8% output per chip at 4-16. Graph pool at 16k capture is ~39 GB on GB300 (prefill `mem_fraction_static` 0.78 -> 0.70 in our deployment).

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4: Fuse inverse RoPE into wo_a FP8 quantization
author: Phoenix3334
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4 applies inverse RoPE to attention output before the `wo_a` projection. The CUDA UE8M0 FP8 path currently launches inverse RoPE separately, writes rotated BF16 values to memory, and reloads them for activation quantization.

This PR folds inverse RoPE into the `wo_a` quantization kernel, keeping rotated values in registers and preserving the intermediate BF16 rounding boundary. It complements [#39957](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39957), which fuses inverse RoPE with a small-batch BF16 wo_a projection. This PR instead quantizes the activation before the FP8 wo_a DeepGEMM path.

[#37658](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37658) introduced the analogous inverse-RoPE + FP8 input-quantization optimization on ROCm/aiter and the existing `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_FUSED_INVROPE` flag. This PR extends that flag to the CUDA UE8M0 path. The BF16 and FP8 wo_a gates are mutually exclusive, so their reported speedups are not additive.

## Modifications

- Fuse inverse RoPE into the CUDA wo_a activation quantization kernel, rotating the last 64 dimensions of each 512-dimensional head.
- Preserve BF16 rounding before quantization, native packed-int32 UE8M0 scale storage and PDL dependencies.
- Issue position/frequency loads early and vectorize frequency loads; keep the selected launch configuration.
- Share the quantization / packed-scale epilogue and host tensor validation between fused and unfused kernels; reuse Python output allocation.
- Cache configuration-derived eligibility in `MQALayer.__init__`; check graph state, pre-applied inverse RoPE and current tensor properties at execution time.
- Reuse `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_FUSED_INVROPE`, off by default, with existing fallbacks.
- Add only two focused GPU tests to the existing test file: production numerical equivalence and CUDA Graph replay with updated inputs. An existing CPU fixture that bypasses initialization receives the new attribute's default.

## Accuracy Tests

### Current-head upstream kernel validation (2026-11-02)

PR head: `fb4e80ea8474e8fdb7aab692119202f4834a424c`. CI checked out merge `5da168b82470b256b49f494dc27ceb991c4399c1`, combining this head with upstream main `1599b166ac856f4fd192feb2c16304fae7860a72`.

The [B200 kernel job](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41413851551/job/125186911527) executed `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fp8_wo_a.py`: **all 7 tests passed**.

```text
[CI Test Method] TestDeepSeekV4FP8WoA.test_fused_inverse_rope_quant_cuda_graph
[CI Test Method] TestDeepSeekV4FP8WoA.test_fused_inverse_rope_quant_matches_production
.......
Ran 7 tests in 12.830s
OK
```

The runner summary also records this file as `"passed": true` (`elapsed: 23` seconds for the file subprocess, distinct from unittest's 12.830 seconds). This covers both new tests—production-path numerical equivalence for FP8 codes and packed scales, and CUDA Graph capture/replay with updated inputs—alongside the existing quantization-path tests. [Hosted Lint](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41413851247/job/125172847972) also passed on this head.

These are kernel correctness and graph-replay results for the current head. They do not establish full-model serving accuracy, bitwise-equal serving logits, or post-refactor performance gains. Full-model serving and performance validation after the refactor remain pending.

### Historical local GPU validation (B300, aiopt v0.5.21)

**Local GPU validation uses aiopt v0.5.21 on 8×B300.** It shares upstream's packed-int32 UE8M0 contract. On that backport:
- Both new tests passed: strided BF16 inputs, T ∈ {0,1,32,100,777,2047,8192,8193}, G ∈ {2,16}, FP8 codes, packed scales and strides; graph capture/replay with updated input.
- Serving startup completed decode CUDA Graph capture.
- Five greedy prompts, up to 64 generated tokens each: two additional independent baseline startups matched each other and the fused run on all returned texts.
- The first baseline startup differed on one prompt. Subsequent comparisons matched; the cause remains unresolved. Returned-text equality does not establish bitwise-equal logits or internal serving tensors.

These local GPU results **predate cleanup commit `7c5d3eb7ce`**. That commit shares the quantization code and caches eligibility. Subsequent main-based B200 kernel validation is documented below; full-model serving validation after the refactor remains pending. No full model accuracy evaluation is claimed.

Local checks on the cleanup: Python syntax, Ruff, isort and clang-format passed. An exhaustive static eligibility comparison matched the previous predicate for configurations with attention output width equal to the configured head dimension.

### Source preparation and current head (2026-11-02)

The branch was originally rebased onto main `c757c4bb7c55d1eb69fdb2bdc6e6fb8507acb7a0` and subsequently updated by merging main. The current head is `fb4e80ea8474e8fdb7aab692119202f4834a424c`, with upstream main `1599b166ac856f4fd192feb2c16304fae7860a72` incorporated.

The quantization helper and kernel tests follow upstream's `ops/quantization` paths, with imports updated accordingly. The shared host validation retains upstream's `kDLGPU` device definition. Repository-pinned pre-commit checks on the six changed files, Python syntax checks and `git diff --check` passed during the earlier rebase preparation. Current-head hosted Lint and B200 kernel results are documented above. Full-model serving and performance validation after the cleanup/rebase remain pending; the historical performance results below are not measurements of this current head.

### Upstream CI and DCP fixture correction (2026-11-01)

At `38c39bddb75b4b53fdcc1fd2d791307f4f973fdc` (via CI merge `769fc5fcce14`), [B200 CI](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41303149108/job/124869681626) executed `test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fp8_wo_a.py`: **7 tests passed** (`Ran 7 tests in 11.821s; OK`). This includes production-path numerical equivalence, CUDA Graph replay, and the existing quantization-path tests. These are main-based kernel correctness results; they do not revalidate the historical performance gains or full-model serving behavior.

That run's [CPU failure](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41303149108/job/124869681607) was the independent DCP replay fixture missing `skips_prefill_metadata_on_idle_dp_rank`. The test file was identical in the PR head and its main base (Git blob `ef5beb976949ec8fb56be440812c166c5e2b2177`).

Follow-up commit [`289c324`](https://github.com/Phoenix3334/sglang/commit/289c324cf5d64108e73a52580172913ec6bc7b4d) carries the **one-line test-fixture correction from mickqian's [#47736](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47736)** (source commit `be43d568ca8115e173bd4b9f5d106a3060ae1f8b`): set `skips_prefill_metadata_on_idle_dp_rank=False` on the mocked backend. The corrected file matches that source exactly. No production kernel/model code or B200 tests changed after the passing run. The subsequent CI run was stopped by the independent decode-queue fixture failure described below.

### Decode-queue scheduler fixture correction (2026-11-01)

The next [CPU run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41316331423/job/124877244394) stopped in `test_decode_queue_cleanup.py::TestHeldDestinationPublication::test_publishes_while_retracted_requests_wait`: its mocked scheduler lacks `tree_cache`, which `process_decode_queue` now reads even with HiCache disabled. Both the failing test and `disaggregation/decode.py` are identical between that CI merge (`632c7f4`) and its actual upstream main parent (`e298298`), so this is a second independent baseline fixture issue. That shard stopped before executing its scheduled DCP test.

Commit [`fddd180`](https://github.com/Phoenix3334/sglang/commit/fddd18005f0a6f91469390132141660bf3553612) carries the one-line correction from **DarkSharpness's [#47758](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47758)** (source `44b1e4b35608c8e388b1d16dc86ceec34514bcc3`): `tree_cache=SimpleNamespace(linker=None)`. It models the no-linker-offload case while preserving the existing metadata-publication assertion. No test is skipped and no assertion is removed.

The corrected file matches #47758 exactly. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed locally on that file. The source PR's [targeted CPU run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41311097837/job/124861547391) passed **12 tests** at its own source head; this is separate from validation of our updated head. [CI on the earlier head `fddd180`](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41317407949) was triggered but stopped at the per-user 120-minute cooldown gate before tests executed. The logged previous accepted trigger is 2026-11-01 14:28:02 UTC, so the earliest retry under that cooldown is 16:28:02 UTC / 2026-11-02 00:28:02 UTC+8. Production code and B200 tests remain unchanged from the previous passing B200 run. After the cooldown expired, empty commit `ddcabbe` triggered [another historical CI run](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/actions/runs/41376972480) on 2026-11-02. It has since been superseded by the main merges leading to `fb4e80e`; see the current-head validation above.

### Non-main adaptation

The backport omits `and inv_rope is None` because v0.5.21 lacks that local variable. Main defines it, so this PR retains the guard to avoid double rotation. Local full-model serving validation is on the available aiopt build; the current main-based head has the hosted B200 kernel coverage documented above. Full-model serving validation on that head remains pending.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

B300 ×8, DeepSeek-V4-Pro, aiopt v0.5.21, TP8/DP8, MegaMoE, 60k input / 1 output, C16, N160, seeds 1/2/3. Radix cache disabled; prefill-delayer enabled. aiakperf uses random token IDs through the `sglang` runner, so this benchmark does not measure real-text tokenization throughput.

| Arm | Mean input tok/s | Mean of per-run median TTFT (s) |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Baseline | ~101,710 | ~9.600 |
| Fused | ~103,349 | ~9.452 |
| Change | ~+1.61% | ~-1.54% |

Each arm used one fresh server startup and three seed runs; fused preceded baseline. These are not three independent paired startups. Fused per-seed throughput: 103,476.7 / 103,283.0 / 103,287.0 tok/s; TTFT: 9.4312 / 9.4523 / 9.4514 s. Baseline raw per-run values and exact dependency/image identifiers are not included in this summary.

These measurements predate the cleanup commit and remain evidence for the preceding implementation; performance after the refactor needs confirmation. Cross-build absolute throughput is not attributed to fusion. No v0.5.21 multi-shape sweep is claimed.

<summary>Prior v0.5.17-derived B300 evidence</summary>

| Input | Concurrency | Baseline input tok/s | Fused input tok/s | Throughput Δ | Median TTFT Δ |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 60k | 1 | 13,645.6 | 14,008.5 | +2.66% | -2.46% |

Its numerical tests reported identical FP8 codes and scales, and its greedy decode comparison produced identical tokens. <details>
<summary>Reproduction: tests, server, greedy probe and benchmark</summary>

Apply the PR changes to the build, with the non-main `inv_rope` adaptation above. Use the same model weights, dependencies and launch parameters for both arms. The fusion flag is fixed for each server startup. Run the three seeds on one server per arm, then restart with the other flag. The recorded run order was fused first, baseline second.

### Kernel tests

```bash
python3 -m pytest -s test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fp8_wo_a.py \
    -k "fused_inverse_rope"
```

The numerical test covers T ∈ {0, 1, 32, 100, 777, 2047, 8192, 8193}, G ∈ {2, 16}, BF16 strided inputs, FP8 codes, packed scales and output strides. The graph test captures and replays with updated inputs.

### Server launch

Set `MODEL_PATH` to the local DeepSeek-V4-Pro weights. Run separately with `FLAG=1` (fused) and `FLAG=0` (baseline).

```bash
MODEL_PATH=/path/to/DeepSeek-V4-Pro
FLAG=1
export SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_FUSED_INVROPE="$FLAG"
export SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=8320

python3 -m sglang.launch_server \
    --trust-remote-code \
    --model-path "$MODEL_PATH" \
    --tp-size 8 --dp 8 --enable-dp-attention --enable-dp-lm-head \
    --load-balance-method round_robin --moe-a2a-backend megamoe \
    --disable-radix-cache --mem-fraction-static 0.835 \
    --swa-full-tokens-ratio 0.075 --chunked-prefill-size 65536 \
    --tokenizer-worker-num 32 --detokenizer-worker-num 32 \
    --enable-prefill-delayer --dist-init-addr 127.0.0.1:9500 \
    --host 0.0.0.0 --port 30000
```

Wait for inference readiness before sending probes. Stop all workers belonging to this server and verify its ports/GPU allocations have been released before starting the next arm.

### Greedy serving probe

Run once per startup, setting a distinct `ACC_OUT` filename; compare the returned texts across saved files.

```bash
ACC_OUT=acc_fused.json python3 - <<'PY'
import json
import os
import urllib.request

prompts = [
    "Explain in detail how a transformer neural network works, step by step.",
    "Write a Python function that returns the n-th Fibonacci number and explain it.",
    "What are the main causes of the French Revolution? Give a structured answer.",
    "Describe the process of photosynthesis and why it matters for life on Earth.",
    "Summarize the plot of Romeo and Juliet and its central themes.",
]
outputs = {}
for i, prompt in enumerate(prompts):
    payload = json.dumps({
        "text": prompt,
        "sampling_params": {"max_new_tokens": 64, "temperature": 0.0},
    }).encode()
    request = urllib.request.Request(
        "http://127.0.0.1:30000/generate",
        data=payload,
        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
    )
    with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=600) as response:
        outputs[str(i)] = json.loads(response.read())["text"]
with open(os.environ["ACC_OUT"], "w") as output:
    json.dump(outputs, output, ensure_ascii=False, indent=2)
PY
```

### Prefill benchmark

Use the same `MODEL_PATH` and `FLAG` as the running server. For SEED=1, 2, 3, run the following warmup then formal commands, ensuring no warmup requests remain in flight before the formal measurement. Use separate output directories per arm/seed.

```bash
SEED=1  # repeat with 2 and 3
OUT="logs/flag${FLAG}_seed${SEED}"

aiakperf -a http://127.0.0.1:30000 -r sglang \
    -m "$MODEL_PATH" -M "$MODEL_PATH" \
    -d random -if 60000 -of 1 -n 16 -w 16 \
    -seed "$((SEED + 10000))" -igr true -o "$OUT/warmup"

aiakperf -a http://127.0.0.1:30000 -r sglang \
    -m "$MODEL_PATH" -M "$MODEL_PATH" \
    -d random -if 60000 -of 1 -n 160 -w 16 \
    -seed "$SEED" -igr true -o "$OUT/formal"
```

After applying the cleanup commit, also run the existing full kernel test file to cover the shared unfused quantization path and the existing CPU fixture:

```bash
python3 test/registered/kernels/ops/quantization/test_fp8_wo_a.py
python3 test/registered/unit/models/test_deepseek_v4_unified_fp8_q_pair.py
```

title: [Perf] DeepSeek-V4.1: Run the small-batch decode fusions at TP2
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash small-batch decode fusions (fused all-reduce + mHC epilogues, the fused inverse-RoPE + WO-A + MXFP8 kernel, and SM100 swap-AB decode attention) were gated to TP4 shapes (tp_size == 4, 2 local o_groups, 16 local heads). TP2 decode therefore ran the unfused path at every batch size, although TP2 is the better latency/throughput point for this model on GB300 at mid concurrency.

## Modifications

- Fused all-reduce + mHC: admit tp_size 2 (the all-reduce kernels are already templated on world size).
- Fused WO-A: take the local group count (2 at TP4, 4 at TP2) as a template parameter.
- Swap-AB decode attention: run TP2's 32 local heads as two 16-head groups on the partial kernel's grid z axis.
- Tests: WO-A fused test parametrized over 2 and 4 groups; swap-AB test covers 32 heads.

The gates check shapes (16 or 32 local heads, 2 or 4 local o_groups, tp_size 2 or 4), not TP size alone, so any deployment with those local shapes takes these paths; only DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP2 and TP4 have been validated.

## Setup

Both arms use the same image, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261012-e6072935`, on GB300 with 2 GPUs. "main" is the image as shipped. "this PR" overlays this branch's changed files onto the same image. Both arms use identical server flags.

Server launch, shown with the c32 flags:

```bash
SGLANG_DEFAULT_THINKING=1 SGLANG_DSV41_REASONING_EFFORT=high \
SGLANG_DSPARK_FOLDED_SAMPLING=2 SGLANG_DSPARK_OPT_MARKOV_W2_BF16=True \
SGLANG_ENABLE_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE=1 SGLANG_DSV41_ENGRAM_HOST_TABLE_LAYOUT=per_rank \
PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF=expandable_segments:True \
python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --trust-remote-code \
  --tensor-parallel-size 2 --expert-parallel-size 2 \
  --speculative-algorithm DSPARK --speculative-dspark-block-size 5 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.8 --chunked-prefill-size 16384 --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --max-running-requests 64 --prefill-decode-interval 48 \
  --swa-prefix-tails 2048 --enable-decoder-swa-bounded-replay --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --schedule-policy fcfs --tokenizer-worker-num 4 \
  --reasoning-parser auto --tool-call-parser auto --enable-metrics --watchdog-timeout 3600
```

Per-concurrency overrides (all other flags as above):

| conc | max-running-requests | prefill-decode-interval | expert-parallel-size | swa-prefix-tails | bounded replay / prefill graph off / fcfs / 4 tokenizer workers |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 2 | 16 | 2 | default | no |
| 2 | 4 | 16 | 2 | 128 | no |
| 4 | 8 | 96 | 1 | 256 | no |
| 16 | 32 | 96 | 2 | 1024 | yes, but no fcfs |
| 32 | 64 | 48 | 2 | 2048 | yes |

c4 and c16 also set `SGLANG_NUMA_BIND_V2=0`; c1–c4 do not set `PYTORCH_CUDA_ALLOC_CONF`.

## Accuracy Tests

GSM8K, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash TP2 on GB300. All 1319 test questions, 5-shot, `max_tokens` 16384, real MTP verification (no simulated acceptance):

```bash
python3 -m sglang.test.run_eval --base-url http://localhost:30000 --eval-name gsm8k \
  --num-examples 1319 --num-shots 5 --max-tokens 16384 --num-threads <1|64>
```

`--num-threads` is the number of concurrent client requests:
- **1 thread** runs against the c1 server flags.
- **64 threads** runs against the c32 server flags (`max-running-requests` 64).

| setting | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| 1 thread | 0.968 | 0.967 |
| 64 threads | 0.970 | 0.973 |

## Speed Tests and Profiling

The speed tests use AgentX trace replay from InferenceX (`inferencex-e2e/benchmarks/srt_agentic.sh`, which wraps `aiperf profile --scenario agentx`). The replay:
- uses the `semianalysisai/cc-traces-weka-062126` multi-turn agentic coding traces;
- runs `--concurrency <conc>` concurrent sessions for `--benchmark-duration 3600` (1 h per point), after the scenario's cache-primer warmup;
- uses the chat template and streaming.

```bash
aiperf profile --scenario agentx --url http://localhost:30000 \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash --tokenizer-trust-remote-code \
  --concurrency <conc> --benchmark-duration 3600 --warmup-grace-period 1800 \
  --public-dataset semianalysis_cc_traces_weka_062126 --apply-chat-template
```

As in InferenceX throughput runs, MTP acceptance is pinned to the golden length on both arms with these server environment variables:

```bash
SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51 SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_METHOD=match-expected SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_TOKEN_MODE=real-draft-token
```

The metrics are computed over requests in the profiling phase:
- **P90 tok/s/user:** the 10th percentile, which is the slow tail, of per-request `1 / TPOT`, where `TPOT = (E2E latency − TTFT) / (output tokens − 1)`.
- **tok/s/GPU:** total input plus output tokens of all requests, divided by the wall-clock span and by 2 GPUs.

Results are P90 tok/s/user @ tok/s/GPU:

| conc | main | this PR | P90 | tput/GPU |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 431.7 @ 12,443 | 517.7 @ 13,423 | +19.9% | +7.9% |
| 2 | 392.6 @ 12,689 | 439.6 @ 13,865 | +12.0% | +9.3% |
| 4 | 383.5 @ 18,119 | 417.5 @ 18,495 | +8.9% | +2.1% |
| 16 | 264.6 @ 55,560 | 292.6 @ 56,590 | +10.6% | +1.9% |
| 32 | 183.1 @ 113,613 | 189.0 @ 115,634 | +3.2% | +1.8% |

Unit tests on GB300: test_wo_a_fused.py and test_swapab_attention.py pass.

Co-authored-by: @nbommi19

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] [AMD] qwen3_5: Quantize the BF16 GDN projections to MXFP4 online
author: omirosh
body:
## Motivation

This ROCm performance change quantizes the BF16 GDN `in_proj_qkvz` and `out_proj` of Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 to MXFP4 once after load and runs them on AITER MXFP4 GEMMs instead of BF16 hipBLASLt, because the Quark MXFP4 checkpoints keep both projections in BF16, and cuts median TPOT by **5.1% with NEXTN MTP and 4.0% without MTP** for Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B MXFP4 on 8x MI355X, TP8, geomean over 12 serving shapes on the SGLang main nightly with only this PR added. Output tok/s goes up by 5.9% and 4.2%. The change is on by default on gfx95x with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`. `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4=0` turns it off.

At TP8, `in_proj_qkvz` is a 4608x8192 weight per GPU and the largest dense weight that every decode and verify step reads. A retuned BF16 GEMM table for these shapes gave no end-to-end gain (99.8% of the current table), and no BF16 kernel we tried beat hipBLASLt on 4608x8192. An MXFP4 weight with its scales is about a quarter of the bytes. At 16 rows, the MXFP4 `in_proj_qkvz` and the BF16 `in_proj_ba` take 8.1 + 7.9 us, and the packed BF16 GEMM of both takes 23.1 us.

## Modifications

- `environ.py` adds the boolean `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4`. The default is true. `0` keeps the BF16 projections.
- `quark_w4a4_mxfp4.py` adds `AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod`. A model sets it on a BF16 linear layer after `create_weights`. The loader then calls `process_weights_after_loading()`, which quantizes the loaded BF16 weight with the existing `dynamic_mxfp4_quant`, preshuffles the weight (16x16) and the E8M0 scales, and records whether AITER has a tuned preshuffled config for (N, K). A second call does nothing. `apply()` quantizes the activation with `per_1x32_f4_quant_hip`. Up to 64 rows with a tuned config, it runs the Triton `gemm_afp4wfp4_preshuffle`. All other batches run the ASM `gemm_a4w4(bpreshuffle=True)`.
- `qwen3_5.py` reads the variable at import. It has an effect only on gfx95x with `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`, and only for the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 model types (`qwen3_5_text`, `qwen3_5_moe_text`). There, each GDN layer sets `AiterMxfp4OnlineLinearMethod` on `in_proj_qkvz` and `out_proj` in `__init__`, so the model loader quantizes them in `load_model`, before SGLang sizes the KV cache and captures the CUDA graphs. It skips projections that the checkpoint already quantized, and projections with N or K not a multiple of 256. Models that reuse `Qwen3_5GatedDeltaNet`, such as `qwen4_exp` and `interns2_mobius`, keep BF16. An MXFP4 `in_proj_qkvz` is no longer an `UnquantizedLinearMethod`, so `finalize_fused_in_proj()` in `prepare_before_cuda_graph_capture` does not build the packed BF16 qkvz+ba GEMM, and `in_proj_ba` (N=32) runs alone in BF16.
- `test/registered/amd/test_qwen35_gdn_online_mxfp4.py` checks both TP8 shapes at 1, 4, 16, 31, 32, 64, 65 and 256 rows against a dequantized FP32 reference. The rows cover both sides of the 32-row scale-layout split and of the 64-row kernel cut. `register_amd_ci` puts it in the MI35x suite, because it skips on anything other than gfx95x.
- `environment_variables.mdx` adds one row for the new variable.

With `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4=0`, nothing changes. No layer is quantized, and `finalize_fused_in_proj()` builds the packed BF16 path as before. With the default, only the GDN projections of Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 on gfx95x with AITER change. Other platforms and other models do not change. The MI35x nightly accuracy tests of Qwen3.5-397B (BF16 and MXFP4) and Qwen3.8 MXFP4 now run the MXFP4 projections.

The Triton path for `in_proj_qkvz` needs the tuned config from [Rocm/aiter5998](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/5998) (merged). The AITER pin on main, `2bb549102b` (#44379), includes it. With an older AITER, such as `e7d2453f`, `in_proj_qkvz` takes the ASM path at every row count. The output is still correct there, but we did not measure the speed.

The MXFP4 projections do not support online weight updates, because quantization changes the weight shape and dtype at load. Set `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4=0` on servers that receive weight updates. The memory that the BF16 weights free (about 5.5 GB per GPU on Qwen3.8 TP8) goes to the KV cache, because quantization runs before SGLang sizes the pool. The pool grows by 6.4%, from 6.65M to 7.07M tokens with NEXTN and from 7.39M to 7.86M without MTP. The speed tests below ran on the first commit, which quantized after the pool was sized. There, both servers of each pair have the same KV pool, and peak usage was 63% and 56%. The speedup does not come from memory.

## Accuracy Tests

The unit test passes on MI355X, with a relative error below 1e-2 for every shape and row count. It also checks that a second `process_weights_after_loading()` call does not quantize the MXFP4 weight again. It ran in the benchmark job before the servers started.

The end-to-end evals ran on the same servers as "Speed Tests and Profiling" below. BF16 is the same image with the variable off.

| Eval | NEXTN BF16 | NEXTN MXFP4 | No MTP BF16 | No MTP MXFP4 |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| GSM8K 5-shot, chat, thinking, flexible-extract (1319) | 0.9765 | 0.9742 | 0.9788 | 0.9818 |
| GPQA Diamond (198, thinking, temperature 1.0) | 0.9343 | 0.9091 | 0.9343 | 0.9242 |
| RULER niah_single_2, 64k | 0.996 | 0.994 | 0.996 | 0.996 |
| RULER niah_single_2, 128k | 0.994 | 0.990 | 0.998 | 0.996 |

With plain MXFP4 on these projections, the model thinks for longer. We repeated the thinking-length check of [vllm#62750](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/62750) without MTP: thinking-on GSM8K, temperature 1.0, 8 reps of 1319 questions per arm. The MXFP4 answers are 10.7% longer than BF16 (95% CI 6.1% to 15.7%), and the accuracy goes from 0.9641 to 0.9597 (McNemar p = 0.0017). Where long reasoning matters more than the per-token speed, set `SGLANG_ROCM_GDN_ONLINE_MXFP4=0`. A Hadamard-32 rotation in the MXFP4 activation quant removes most of the increase ([Rocm/aiter6734](https://github.com/ROCm/aiter/pull/6734), open). It is a follow-up PR after the AITER pin moves.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI355X, TP8, one node, all four servers in one job. The image is `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm10-mi35x-20261016` (SGLang main `34c4ba14c8`, AITER `2bb549102b`) plus the first commit of this PR, `ad94c3c8f2`, and no other change. The later commits make the variable a boolean that is on by default, limit it to the Qwen3.5 / Qwen3.8 model types and to shapes with N and K multiples of 256, change the CI suite and comments, and move the quantization into the load path. "Load path check" below compares the load path with the first commit. Page size 16, `SGLANG_USE_AITER_UNIFIED_ATTN=1`, fp8 KV cache, `--mamba-ssm-dtype bfloat16`, chunked prefill 16384, radix cache off, at most 256 running requests. NEXTN runs use 3 steps, top-k 1, 4 draft tokens, `--enable-linear-replayssm-spec` and `--speculative-draft-model-path` set to the model path. `bench_serve` random dataset, range ratio 0.8, one run per cell.

NEXTN MTP:

| ISL / OSL | Concurrency | TPOT BF16 (ms) | TPOT MXFP4 (ms) | TPOT change | Output tok/s change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8k / 1k | 4 | 6.11 | 6.01 | -1.6% | +3.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 8 | 8.14 | 7.96 | -2.2% | +2.8% |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 11.70 | 11.28 | -3.6% | +3.6% |
| 8k / 1k | 32 | 18.12 | 17.25 | -4.8% | +5.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 29.21 | 27.46 | -6.0% | +6.6% |
| 8k / 1k | 128 | 48.70 | 45.86 | -5.8% | +6.6% |
| 8k / 1k | 256 | 92.06 | 85.36 | -7.3% | +8.0% |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 16.05 | 15.84 | -1.3% | +6.4% |
| 60k / 600 | 16 | 61.08 | 55.69 | -8.8% | +7.0% |
| 60k / 600 | 64 | 245.92 | 228.60 | -7.0% | +7.8% |
| 128k / 1k | 4 | 20.06 | 18.91 | -5.7% | +6.3% |
| 128k / 1k | 16 | 82.98 | 77.75 | -6.3% | +7.1% |
| Geomean | | | | **-5.1%** | **+5.9%** |

No MTP:

| ISL / OSL | Concurrency | TPOT BF16 (ms) | TPOT MXFP4 (ms) | TPOT change | Output tok/s change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 8k / 1k | 4 | 13.64 | 13.47 | -1.2% | +1.4% |
| 8k / 1k | 8 | 17.13 | 16.32 | -4.7% | +5.0% |
| 8k / 1k | 16 | 23.36 | 22.44 | -3.9% | +4.1% |
| 8k / 1k | 32 | 32.26 | 31.50 | -2.4% | +2.5% |
| 8k / 1k | 64 | 46.25 | 45.08 | -2.5% | +2.7% |
| 8k / 1k | 128 | 71.55 | 68.90 | -3.7% | +4.0% |
| 8k / 1k | 256 | 119.80 | 113.40 | -5.3% | +5.6% |
| 60k / 600 | 4 | 24.71 | 23.87 | -3.4% | +4.0% |
| 60k / 600 | 16 | 77.35 | 73.17 | -5.4% | +5.8% |
| 60k / 600 | 64 | 268.45 | 252.45 | -6.0% | +6.1% |
| 128k / 1k | 4 | 28.21 | 27.14 | -3.8% | +4.2% |
| 128k / 1k | 16 | 96.83 | 91.48 | -5.5% | +5.5% |
| Geomean | | | | **-4.0%** | **+4.2%** |

Median TTFT is lower in every cell too, by 8.6% (geomean) with NEXTN and 6.5% without MTP. The NEXTN accept length does not drop. `bench_serve` reports a lifetime average per server, and at the end of the run it was 3.14 for BF16 and 3.18 for MXFP4.

The MXFP4 projections run the Triton kernel up to 64 rows and the ASM kernel above that. Prefill always runs ASM. A NEXTN verify step has 4 rows per request, so NEXTN decode runs ASM from concurrency 32 up, and decode without MTP from concurrency 128 up.

Per-call time on one MI355X GPU in the same image, CUDA-graph replays, in us. The MXFP4 times include the activation quant. The BF16 `in_proj` column is what main runs: one packed qkvz+ba GEMM up to 64 rows, and separate qkvz and ba GEMMs above 64 rows. With MXFP4, `in_proj_ba` stays BF16 and runs alone.

| Rows | MXFP4 kernel | BF16 in_proj (qkvz+ba) | MXFP4 qkvz + BF16 ba | BF16 out_proj | MXFP4 out_proj |
| ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1 | Triton | 16.3 | 10.1 | 6.0 | 4.3 |
| 4 | Triton | 16.7 | 12.8 | 7.0 | 4.9 |
| 16 | Triton | 23.1 | 16.0 | 5.8 | 5.1 |
| 64 | Triton | 22.0 | 20.0 | 7.8 | 6.9 |

The servers ran on one node in the order capture, load, load, capture, with and without NEXTN. 8k / 1k, one `bench_serve` run per cell and round. The table gives the mean of the two median TPOTs.

title: [Perf] hicache: Parallel THP-backed host pool allocation (opt-in)
author: whybeyoung
body:
## Motivation

HiCache host pools are allocated by `alloc_mmap` as one `MAP_SHARED | MAP_ANONYMOUS` mapping prefaulted with `MAP_POPULATE` from a single thread, then pinned with `cudaHostRegister`. An anonymous shared mapping is shmem: every page fault takes the backing shmem file's locks, so the prefault runs at ~1.5–2 GB/s single-threaded and plateaus at ~2–4.5 GB/s with 32–64 threads (ablation below), and shmem THP is disabled by default (`shmem_enabled=never`), so every page is 4 KB.

With large host pools this becomes a significant part of engine startup. On a single node with 4x B300 and a ~306 GB host pool per rank, allocating and pinning the host pools takes ~185 s of every start.

## Modifications

Opt-in via `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_PARALLEL_ALLOC_THREADS=<n>` (default `0` = off; with it unset the code path is unchanged):

- `mmap_allocator.py`: new `_mmap_private_parallel_prefaulted(alloc_bytes, num_threads)`:
  - maps the pool `MAP_PRIVATE | MAP_ANONYMOUS` (regular anonymous memory, no shmem lock contention);
  - `madvise(MADV_HUGEPAGE)` so it is backed by 2 MB transparent huge pages under the common `enabled=madvise` policy (best effort; still correct on 4 KB pages);
  - `madvise(MADV_DONTFORK)`: this is what makes `MAP_PRIVATE` safe to pin. The reason the existing path uses `MAP_SHARED` is that a private page goes copy-on-write in a forked child and a parent write after `fork()` would move the parent off the page `cudaHostRegister` pinned. With `MADV_DONTFORK` the mapping is not inherited at all, so there is no COW to race with — the same treatment the CUDA driver gives `cudaHostAlloc` memory. Consequence: a `fork()`ed (not spawned) child cannot see this buffer;
  - prefaults the whole range before returning (as `cudaHostRegister` requires) with a THP-aligned chunked `memset` from `n` threads (32 in the runs below). ctypes releases the GIL around the libc call, so the threads fault in parallel. (`MADV_POPULATE_WRITE` per chunk was measured to be noticeably slower than `memset` with the same thread count.)
- `alloc_mmap`: when `n > 0`, the plain (non-hugetlb) path uses the function above; any `OSError` logs and falls back to the existing shared prefaulted mapping. The explicit hugetlb path (`SGLANG_HUGEPAGE_SIZE`) is untouched.
- `environ.py`: `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_PARALLEL_ALLOC_THREADS` (`EnvInt(0)`), documented in `docs/references/environment_variables.mdx`.
- Tests (`test/registered/unit/mem_cache/test_mmap_allocator.py`, CPU CI):
  - the mapping is fully resident and zero-filled for 1 / 4 / 64 threads with a ragged, non-THP-aligned size;
  - a forked child touching the buffer gets `SIGSEGV` (i.e. `MADV_DONTFORK` is in effect; mutation-checked — removing the `madvise` makes this test fail);
  - with the flag on, `alloc_mmap` does not take the shared path, and an `OSError` on the new path falls back to it;
  - with the flag unset (default), the new path is never taken.

Note: `alloc_mmap` is also used by `utils/weight_checker.py` for its snapshot arena, which therefore follows the same flag.

## Accuracy Tests

N/A — host memory allocation only; the pool contents are zero-filled exactly as before and no model-output code is touched.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

End to end, one B300 node, 4 ranks allocating concurrently, 306 GB host pool per rank, real `alloc_mmap` + `_cuda_host_register` path, two runs (per rank):

| | allocation + prefault | `cudaHostRegister` | total (slowest rank) |
|---|---|---|---|
| default (`MAP_SHARED`, single-thread `MAP_POPULATE`) | 115–172 s | 13–47 s | 185–189 s |
| `SGLANG_HICACHE_HOST_PARALLEL_ALLOC_THREADS=32` | 4–27 s | 12–29 s | 46 s |

~4x faster overall (~140 s saved per start); with 4 concurrent ranks, allocation is bound by memory bandwidth / page allocator rather than threads.

Ablation, 64 GB prefault, one B300 node (256 cores, kernel 6.8, THP `enabled=madvise`, `shmem_enabled=never`), chunked `memset`, two runs:

| mapping | 1 thread | 8 threads | 32 threads | 64 threads |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| default: shared + `MAP_POPULATE` | 1.4–1.8 GB/s | – | – | – |
| shared (4 KB; `MADV_HUGEPAGE` has no effect on shmem here) | 1.1–1.4 | 1.7–3.8 | 1.7–4.5 | 1.9–4.6 |
| private, 4 KB (`MADV_NOHUGEPAGE`) | 1.2 | 4.1–5.4 | 7.6–8.9 | 8.4–14.4 |
| private + THP (100% 2 MB pages) | 2.2–2.3 | 10.2–10.4 | 30–43 | 47–48 |

So multithreading alone on the shared mapping gives at most ~2x and is noisy; going private gives most of the scaling, and THP another ~4x on top.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).

title: [Feat] FlashInfer: Add NVFP4 W4A16 and SiTU support to MegaMoE
author: zianglih
body:
## Motivation

@humansand

Add opt-in NVFP4 W4A16 to FlashInfer MegaMoE for serialized ModelOpt checkpoints
and `nvfp4_online`, reusing `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1`. The default
NVFP4 MegaMoE path remains W4A4.

This is the remaining integration from [#39210](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39210)
on top of merged [#43789](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/43789).
Startup autotuning, cache ownership, native workspace pooling and DP token-count
synchronization are already upstream and are not changed here. The original PR's
branch and history are preserved.

**Dependency:** the existing FlashInfer 0.7.1 pin includes
[FlashInfer #5019](https://github.com/flashinfer-ai/flashinfer/pull/5019).
No Dockerfile or dependency changes.

## Modifications

- **Precision and preparation:** extend the existing MegaMoE adapter with the
  native W4A16 config/preprocessing. Keep packed NVFP4 weights/block scales,
  per-expert FP32 weight scales, BF16 activations/EP transport/combine and
  post-FC2 routing. Neutralize serialized checkpoint activation scales and
  bypass activation quantization for online W4A16. Retain the existing source
  precision and excluded-layer behavior for online weight conversion.
- **Activation and model wiring:** support gated SiLU/SwiGLU and SiTU for NVFP4
  W4A4/W4A16. Kimi K3 uses standard TopK and local EP/shared-expert handling;
  its GEMM1 alpha/clamp fields map to SiTU beta/linear-beta, separately from
  SwiGLU clamps. MXFP8/DeepGEMM reject unwired SiTU. Nemotron ReLU-squared is
  unsupported. Requirements remain SM100/SM103 and attention-DP=TP=EP;
  W4A16 additionally requires BF16 model dtype and combine.
- **Reload:** restore canonical loading views over the four prepared
  weight/block-scale allocations, then copy newly prepared data into those
  allocations. Share this loader/preparation lifecycle between W4A4 and W4A16. Keep the live
  MegaMoE layer, tuned profiles and workspace owner so CUDA graph pointers remain
  stable; per-expert runtime scales are staged on each forward. FlashInfer 0.7.1
  captures W4A4 input normalization as a scalar: reloading a different input
  scale is rejected and requires a server restart. Weight, weight-scale and
  per-expert FC1-output scale updates remain supported. The registered
  W4A16 serialized reload test covers both cache-flush modes; the existing
  storage regression covers both precisions.
- **Dummy weights:** initialize FP4 global `weight_scale_2` tensors to one,
  preserving ordinary random-weight initialization. Retain the simple
  neutral-scale regression test.
- **FC2 reduction:** default `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=0`
  uses external FP32 accumulation. Setting it to `1` permits nondeterministic
  BF16 atomic candidates; tuning can still select external reduction.
- **Current upstream contracts:** preserve the default non-MegaMoE draft runner
  and A2A behavior. An unset draft A2A backend now resolves to `none` for a
  FlashInfer MegaMoE target, and the NVSHMEM guard accounts for that default.
- **Tests:** extend the existing adapter/storage and architecture cases, plus
  the registered online NVFP4 GSM8K and serialized weight-reload classes.
  No full Kimi K3 E2E or dedicated NVSHMEM environment tests are added.

### Single-node NVSHMEM defaults

For single-node FlashInfer MegaMoE, with no speculative decoding or a default/
explicit `none` draft A2A backend, set these defaults before initialization:

```bash
NVSHMEM_REMOTE_TRANSPORT=none
NVSHMEM_IB_ENABLE_IBGDA=0
NVSHMEM_DISABLE_LOCAL_ONLY_PROXY=1
```

Explicit environment settings are preserved. These defaults apply to all
supported FlashInfer MegaMoE formats and select direct peer memory access,
avoiding the uninitialized proxy global-exit state fixed by
[NVIDIA/nvshmem commit `af9e2391a849`](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvshmem/commit/af9e2391a849d1a36b4be09c3f6f20d622dada1b).
The closed [NVIDIA/nvshmem#110](https://github.com/NVIDIA/nvshmem/pull/110) has
additional background. Remote IB/UCX transport and proxy-based global-exit/
timeout polling are disabled; bootstrap networking is unaffected. All EP GPUs
must support peer memory access. Multi-node jobs and explicit other draft A2A
backends receive no automatic defaults.

### Example server command

Four Blackwell GPUs, FlashInfer 0.7.1, online expert-weight conversion:

```bash
CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0,1,2,3 \
SGLANG_FLASHINFER_CUTEDSL_NVFP4_W4A16=1 \
SGLANG_FLASHINFER_MEGAMOE_IN_KERNEL_FC2_REDUCE=0 \
SGLANG_FP4_IGNORED_LAYERS='' \
SGLANG_ENABLE_JIT_DEEPGEMM=False \
python -m sglang.launch_server \
  --model-path Qwen/Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507-FP8 \
  --quantization nvfp4_online --dtype bfloat16 \
  --moe-runner-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --moe-a2a-backend flashinfer_megamoe \
  --tp-size 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --ep-size 4 \
  --enable-dp-lm-head \
  --cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 64 \
  --cuda-graph-backend-prefill disabled \
  --max-running-requests 64 \
  --chunked-prefill-size 16384 \
  --mem-fraction-static 0.7
```

Convert every routed expert for this example; excluded FP8 expert layers cannot
use the NVFP4 MegaMoE runner. With attention DP4, the 16384-token configured
prefill chunk resolves to 4096 tokens per rank. The existing startup autotuner
therefore prepares a 4096-token per-rank prefill profile.

## Accuracy Tests

**Current source:** `7337b0c6aa709132170b4128eb83b8db8c4fb3be`, based on
upstream main `12dc62310288926b0f38e33ff2d466dee2bf6bb9`. This includes the
CI-required ancestor `ff8d964cf5b6c463966bca5016018d2fa0836326`.
All six feature commits are patch-identical after rebase; the scope remains 15 files.

**Current-head checks:** pre-commit and diff checks passed. The focused CPU
adapter harness passed 29 tests; autotune/cache checks passed 15 tests with one
CUDA-only skip; the neutral-scale regression and accessor source check each
passed. These harnesses use real CPU Torch tensors with serving/GPU imports
stubbed or exact-source AST loading; they do not establish CUDA correctness.
The title also passes the exact upstream title-validation script.

```text
29 passed, 1 warning in 1.35s
Ran 16 tests in 3.115s — OK (skipped=1)
Neutral-scale regression: Ran 1 test in 0.001s — OK
Accessor source check: Ran 1 test in 20.960s — OK
```

**C2 evidence scope:** the GPU results below predate this rebase. Units, native,
dummy and online cases ran at `7b173e5261ac63ab5a1d6617a1d2ed626ab4aec1`;
serialized reload cases ran at `562fe4e70f48de798c9260c71af821b8bad10b5f`.
Those two tested revisions have identical production Python trees and retained
tests; only documentation and removal of the extra W4A4 test class differ.
The integration patches are unchanged by the rebase, but surrounding upstream
runtime code changed. GPU validation has not been rerun on the current head.

**Environment:** eight B300 SXM6 AC GPUs, 275040 MiB each, driver 590.48.01;
four GPUs per model/native case. Image
`lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261013-7224fce1`, amd64 digest
`sha256:009eafc447f47fc595ea5f9820a9d7a07a9d144f3c8b90ab8ef568f4124475a7`.
Python 3.12.15, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130 (CUDA 13.0), CuTe DSL 4.8.0,
