title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] deepseek-v4.1: Default aggregated servers to MegaAttention only when each rank holds 64 query heads
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

Since #43922, `--dsv4-attn-backend auto` resolves to `flashmla_mega` for DeepSeek-V4.1 on SM100/SM103 with an `fp8_e4m3` KV cache, whatever the attention TP width. MegaAttention always runs a 64-head tile (`kernel_num_heads = 64 if n_local_heads <= 64 else 128`), and `pack_query` zero-fills the missing heads. DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has 64 query heads, so TP2 (32 heads per rank) runs 2x and TP4 (16 heads per rank) runs 4x the attention work it needs. The `flashmla` path has a small-batch SM100 kernel specialized for 16 and 32 heads (`can_use_swapab_attention`), so it wins at these widths.

At TP4 the target-verify graph of one decode step gains the MegaAttention kernel (~1.45 ms over 40 layers) and the fp8 `wo_a` GEMM it feeds (~0.29 ms). It drops the FlashMLA partial/combine, fused `wo_a`, Q-norm-RoPE and quant kernels (~0.85 ms), so each step is ~1.1 ms slower.

## Modifications

- For an aggregated server (`--disaggregation-mode null`), `_default_dsv4_attention_backend` returns `flashmla` when attention is tensor-parallel across ranks (`attn_tp_size > 1`). This mirrors `_kernel_num_heads`, which pads to the 64-head tile exactly when `attn_tp_size > 1`.
  - TP1, DP attention at attention TP 1 and prefill CP are not sharded, so they still resolve to `flashmla_mega`.
  - Prefill CP counts as attention TP 1 directly, because `validate_deepseek_v4_cp` sets `attn_cp_size` only after this default runs.
  - An explicit `--dsv4-attn-backend` is unchanged.
- PD roles keep today's default (#45075): `flashmla_mega` on both prefill and decode, whatever their attention TP size.
  - The two backends do not store the same KV layout. `SGLANG_DSV4_KV_LAYOUT` defaults to `v4`, so `flashmla` stores V4, while `flashmla_mega` forces V4.1.
  - Gating PD roles by head count would let a TP prefill and a DP-attention decode resolve differently. They would then fail the KV-layout handshake: on GB300 such a pair failed its first request with `KV layout mismatch: prefill server has kv_layout=v4,c1:v4,c2:v4, but decode server has kv_layout=v41,c1:v41_fp4,c2:v41_fp4`.
- The `--dsv4-attn-backend` help text describes the new default. The cookbook PD note now says both roles run MegaAttention whatever their attention TP size; it previously said "as a single server does".

## Accuracy Tests

The change selects an existing backend; no kernel or model code changes. Paired runs:
- Aggregated TP4 EP1 server, same image as below, DSpark with real acceptance.
- `sgl-eval` 0.1.3, GSM8K, all 1319 examples, `--load-preset-from-model-id deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash` (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95, thinking, reasoning effort high), 128 threads.
- The two servers differ only in the attention backend.

| backend | GSM8K 1319 | errors / truncated | mean output tokens |
|---|---|---|---|
| `auto` with this PR (resolves to `flashmla`) | **96.82%** | 0 / 0 | 266.7 |
| explicit `flashmla_mega` (main's `auto` here) | 96.59% | 0 / 0 | 270.5 |

The 0.23-point gap is 3 of 1319 questions, inside one standard error (about 0.5 points at this score).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4 on GB300, `lmsysorg/sglang:nightly-dev-cu13-20261021-c1c287a4`. Aggregated serving behind the Dynamo frontend, DSpark (MTP), agentic multi-turn coding trace replay, full warmup, then a 60-minute measurement window. One server per row, with the same recipe except `--dsv4-attn-backend`. `auto` resolved to `flashmla_mega` on this image.

| Point | Backend | Requests / errors | Total tok/s/GPU | Interactivity P50 / P90 (tok/s/user) | TTFT P90 | Clean decode step, 1 / 4 running |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP4, conc 4 | `auto` (mega) | 751 / 0 | 9,881 | 537.6 / 465.8 | 0.288 s | 6.41 ms / - |
| TP4, conc 4 | `flashmla` | 741 / 0 | 9,736 | **683.7 / 590.8** | 0.254 s | **5.05 / 6.72 ms** |
| TP4, conc 16 | `auto` (mega) | 2671 / 0 | 29,051 | 473.8 / 403.7 | 1.888 s | 6.40 / 7.85 ms |
| TP4, conc 16 | `flashmla` | 2714 / 0 | 29,371 | **593.2 / 468.6** | 1.401 s | **5.06 / 6.84 ms** |
| TP2 EP2, conc 16 | `auto` (mega) | 2662 / 0 | 57,766 | 376.2 / 309.0 | 1.310 s | 7.19 / 9.67 ms |
| TP2 EP2, conc 16 | `flashmla` | 2675 / 0 | 57,999 | **414.8 / 315.4** | 1.176 s | **6.07 / 9.22 ms** |

The decode step is taken from scheduler log intervals with no prefill batch: `running x accept length / generation throughput`. P90 interactivity rises 27% (TP4 c4), 16% (TP4 c16) and 2% (TP2 c16, P50 +10%), at matching throughput.

Resolution checked with `ServerArgs.resolve_once` on a GB300 node, the image above with this change's two files in place:

| Arguments | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `--tp 4` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla` |
| `--tp 2 --ep 2` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla` |
| `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 2` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla` |
| `--tp 1` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --enable-prefill-cp --cp-strategy interleave` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| `--tp 4 --dsv4-attn-backend flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| PD prefill: `--tp 4`, `--tp 2`, `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --ep 4`, `--tp 2 --attn-dp-size 2 --ep 2` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |
| PD decode: `--tp 4`, `--tp 4 --attn-dp-size 4 --ep 4`, legacy `--dp-size 4 --enable-dp-attention --ep 4` | `flashmla_mega` | `flashmla_mega` |

Larger batches, same setup. TP2 c32 uses `--max-running-requests 64`. TP4 c64 uses `--max-running-requests 256` and `--prefill-decode-interval 24`. With DSpark block size 5, every bucket of 9 or more running requests is above the swap-AB row cap, so `flashmla` pads to 64 heads there too:

| Point | Backend | Requests / errors | Total tok/s/GPU | Interactivity P50 / P90 | TTFT P90 | Clean decode step by running requests |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP2 EP2, conc 32 | `auto` (mega) | 4792 / 0 | 120,870 | 282.4 / 220.5 | 1.978 s | 1-8: 9.06 ms, 9-16: 12.82 ms |
| TP2 EP2, conc 32 | `flashmla` | 4817 / 0 | 122,250 | **291.5 / 227.4** | 1.780 s | 1-8: **8.31** ms, 9-16: **12.46** ms |
| TP4, conc 64 | `auto` (mega) | 11501 / 0 | 116,866 | 210.9 / 176.0 | 2.000 s | 1-16: 9.38 ms, 17-32: 12.13 ms |
| TP4, conc 64 | `flashmla` | 11604 / 0 | 118,577 | **220.9 / 184.8** | 1.754 s | 1-16: **8.40** ms, 17-32: **11.57** ms |

The TP4 margin narrows as the batch grows: -10% at 1-16 running, -5% at 17-32, and -4% at 33-48 (steps with prefill, 23.44 vs 22.58 ms).

Fixed batches at TP4 EP1, to cover the high-throughput regime the trace does not reach:
- `bench_serving --dataset-name random-ids`, 4096 input / 1024 output tokens, C requests sent at once, two rounds per C.
- DSpark, simulated acceptance 3.51, `--max-running-requests 256`, `--cuda-graph-max-bs-decode 256`.
- Clean decode step from scheduler log intervals at that running count:

| running requests | `flashmla` | `flashmla_mega` | delta |
|---|---|---|---|
| 57-64 | **17.50 ms** | 18.25 ms | -4.1% |
| 121-128 | **26.48 ms** | 26.98 ms | -1.9% |
| 241-256 | **42.64 ms** | 43.58 ms | -2.2% |

`flashmla` decodes faster at every batch size up to 256. MegaAttention prefills slightly faster (median TTFT at C=128: 4.54 s vs 5.22 s), which leaves end-to-end bench throughput within 1.7% at C=128/256.

Side effects on aggregated TP2/TP4 servers:
- **KV layout:** they now store the V4 KV layout instead of V4.1. The swap-AB kernel reads V4. The KV pool at `--mem-fraction-static 0.8` was 66.86M vs 67.19M tokens (-0.5%) in the fixed-batch runs.
- **Shared HiCache stores:** a HiCache storage backend shared with a V4.1-layout server (a DEP server or a PD role on `auto`) would see a different layout. The store key does not include the layout.

Not measured:
- `--enable-cp-decode-attn-tp` (opt-in), which splits heads across CP ranks at decode. It still resolves to `flashmla_mega`, as on main.

The GB300 TP2 CI suites with `--attn-dp-size 1` now run `flashmla` instead of padded `flashmla_mega`.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [ ] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [x] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] [AMD] deterministic: Use a fixed-order two-stage all-reduce for large inputs
author: aarnetalman
body:
## Motivation

In deterministic mode on ROCm every custom all-reduce runs the 1-stage kernel: each GPU reads every peer's whole input and sums the ranks in the order 0..n-1. That order is what makes the result independent of the input size, but each GPU reads n times the data, so at TP4/TP8 the all-reduce takes a large share of the step: on MI350X, Qwen3-8B deterministic decode/prefill spends 48% of GPU time in it at TP4 and 63% at TP8 (8k-token inputs), and deterministic throughput at TP8 was about half of normal mode. The 2-stage kernel (reduce-scatter + all-gather) reads far less, but it cannot be used as is: each owner starts its sum at its own rank, so an element's result depends on which rank owns it, which changes with the input size. This PR adds a fixed-order option to the 2-stage kernel that sums the ranks in the same order as the 1-stage kernel, so the two give the same bits for every element at every size, and uses it for large inputs at 4 and 8 ranks. Results do not change; on MI350X deterministic throughput rises 16-24% at TP4 and 29-57% at TP8 on Qwen3-8B, and 28-54% at TP8 on Qwen3.8-27B, with every determinism check passing.

## Modifications

- `custom_all_reduce_hip.cuh`: `cross_device_reduce_2stage` gets a template parameter `kFixedOrder` (default `false`, so normal mode is unchanged). With it, stage 1 reads the ranks in the order 0..n-1 instead of starting at its own rank; stage 2 (the gather) is unchanged.
- `deterministic_all_reduce.hip`: one templated launcher instead of three copies per dtype. Inputs copied into the registered buffer (`deterministic_all_reduce_unreg`, which every deterministic call of `CustomAllreduce` uses for inputs that fit the buffer, including in CUDA graphs and the pieces of larger inputs) take the fixed-order 2-stage kernel with 32 blocks at or above 512 KiB at 4 ranks and 256 KiB at 8 ranks (the thresholds `CustomAllreduce::allreduce` uses); everything else keeps the 1-stage kernel with 16 blocks: smaller inputs, 2 and 6 ranks, and `deterministic_all_reduce_reg` (its inputs can be larger than the IPC buffer that the 2-stage kernel stages 1/n of the input in).
- New test `test/registered/kernels/ops/communication/test_amd_deterministic_allreduce_fixed_order.py` (`stage-c-test-large-8-gpu-amd-mi35x`): at 4 and 8 ranks, bf16 and fp16, sizes on both sides of the thresholds, eager and CUDA graphs, the all-reduce output must equal, bit for bit, the sum of the ranks' inputs computed in torch in the order 0..n-1 (float32 accumulation). The data is chosen so its float32 sum depends on the order of the ranks.

## Accuracy Tests

MI350X, ROCm 7.2.4, `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x-20261021`.

Kernel level (bf16, hidden 4096 and 7168, 1-2,040 rows eager and 1-512 rows in CUDA graphs, order-sensitive data, 2/4/8 ranks): the fixed-order 2-stage kernel's output equals the current 1-stage kernel's output bit for bit at every size, is identical on every rank, and a row's result does not depend on the number of rows. Control: the current (unordered) 2-stage kernel differs from the 1-stage kernel at 42-44 of 42-44 sizes at 4 and 8 ranks.

End to end, deterministic mode (`--enable-deterministic-inference`, Triton prefill and AITER decode attention, together with the other open MI350X deterministic-mode PRs), `python3 -m sglang.test.test_deterministic` (`single`, `prefix`, `prefix --return-logprob`, `radix_cache`, 50 trials) plus a bitwise batch-size check (the same prompt in batches of 1 to 50, 1,275 responses, token IDs and logprobs compared exactly with the batch-size-1 response): every check passes (`single` 1 output, `prefix` 1/1/1/1, prefix logprobs identical, radix cache consistent, bitwise 1,275 / 1,275). With this branch's build (sgl-kernel rebuilt for gfx950):

- the new test passes at 4 and 8 ranks, and the existing 2-rank deterministic all-reduce test passes;
- every check above passes on Qwen3-8B TP2, TP4 and TP8, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4, Qwen3.8-27B TP4 and Qwen3.8-27B TP8, and again on fresh servers: Qwen3-8B TP8 4 / 4, Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 3 / 3, Qwen3.8-27B TP4 2 / 2;
- GSM8K (sgl-eval 0.1.2, temperature 0, 1,319 questions) is unchanged: Qwen3-8B 93.40% / 93.25% / 93.48% at TP2 / TP4 / TP8 (93.48% at TP8 before), Qwen3.8-27B 96.21% at TP4 and 96.13% at TP8.

Through the experiment-only switch (same kernel and selection) the checks also passed on Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 with GSM8K 95.15% (95.15% before).

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Kernel time per all-reduce (bf16, hidden 4096, CUDA graph of 50 calls, median of 7), current 1-stage kernel vs this PR:

| input | 8 ranks: current | 8 ranks: this PR | 4 ranks: current | 4 ranks: this PR |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 MiB (128 rows) | 23.9 us | 15.4 us (1.55x) | 22.2 us | 16.2 us (1.37x) |
| 4 MiB (512 rows) | 77.8 us | 31.4 us (2.47x) | 74.8 us | 43.1 us (1.74x) |
| 8 MiB (1,024 rows) | 149.2 us | 50.7 us (2.94x) | 144.5 us | 77.8 us (1.86x) |
| 16 MiB (2,040 rows) | 291.5 us | 88.1 us (3.31x) | 283.1 us | 146.0 us (1.94x) |

Below the thresholds (decode-size inputs) the 1-stage kernel is faster and is kept; at 2 ranks the two kernels are equally fast and the 1-stage kernel is kept.

End to end, deterministic mode, `python3 -m sglang.benchmark.serving --backend sglang --dataset-name random --random-range-ratio 1.0 --request-rate inf`, output throughput, current vs this branch's build (same server arguments, interleaved):

| model, TP | 1k in / 1k out | 8k in / 1k out | 32k in / 256 out | long context |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Qwen3-8B, 2 | 10,135 -> 10,145 (+0.1%) | 2,623 -> 2,624 (0.0%) | 207.2 -> 207.3 (0.0%) | |
| Qwen3-8B, 4 | 15,543 -> 18,129 (+16.6%) | 3,946 -> 4,755 (+20.5%) | 303.4 -> 377.5 (+24.4%) | 64k / 120k: 125.2 -> 149.3 (+19.2%) / 30.8 -> 36.2 (+17.5%) |
| Qwen3-8B, 8 | 20,147 -> 26,751 (+32.8%) | 5,044 -> 7,409 (+46.9%) | 383.3 -> 600.6 (+56.7%) | 64k / 120k: 160.1 -> 233.9 (+46.1%) / 41.7 -> 60.0 (+43.9%) |
| Qwen3.8-27B, 8 | 7,635 -> 9,803 (+28.4%) | 2,191 -> 3,196 (+45.9%) | 165.2 -> 254.9 (+54.3%) | |

(tok/s; 256 / 256 / 64 prompts; long context 64k in / 256 out and 120k in / 128 out, Qwen3-8B with YaRN.) Qwen3-8B TP8 is the mean of two rounds: the current kernel gave the same throughput in both (20,136 / 20,158 at 1k in / 1k out), this PR 27,503 and 25,999 (+36.6% and +29.0%); at 8k and 32k the two rounds agree within 0.3%. TP2 is unchanged because the 1-stage kernel is kept at 2 ranks. Time to first token falls 19-47% at TP4 and TP8 (Qwen3.8-27B TP8: 5.6 -> 3.3 s, 22.9 -> 13.3 s, 13.5 -> 8.2 s). Normal mode is unchanged.

Through the experiment-only switch running the same kernel and selection, before the build: Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 15,024 -> 16,431 (+9.4%) / 4,435 -> 5,089 (+14.7%) / 334.6 -> 393.1 (+17.5%); Qwen3.8-27B TP4 5,517 -> 6,245 (+13.2%) / 1,776 -> 2,160 (+21.6%) / 131.8 -> 164.2 (+24.6%), 64k / 128k +21.8% / +22.8%.

Related: #34543 (merged) reduces deterministic inputs larger than the buffer piece by piece through `deterministic_all_reduce_unreg`, so those pieces also take the faster kernel. The measurements above include it in both columns, and this branch merges cleanly on current main.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

## Review and Merge Process

1. Ping Merge Oncalls to start the process. See the [PR Merge Process](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/MAINTAINER.md#pull-request-merge-process).
2. Get approvals from [CODEOWNERS](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/main/.github/CODEOWNERS) and other reviewers.
3. Trigger CI tests with [comments](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#how-to-trigger-ci-tests) or contact authorized users to do so.
   - Common commands include `/tag-and-rerun-ci`, `/tag-run-ci-label`, `/rerun-failed-ci`
4. After green CI and required approvals, ask Merge Oncalls or people with Write permission to merge the PR.

title: [Fix] dspark: Draw the simulated-acceptance bonus at the simulated row
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

With `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN` set, DSpark replaces the accepted length with the simulated value `c`. The bonus token, however, stays the one the real accept computed for its own length: the target argmax at the real first-mismatch row, or the rejection-sampled token at the real reject row. That token is committed after `drafts[:c]`, at a position the target never predicted it for. It is also the anchor of the next draft block. The committed text degenerates as a result, and verify batches route to fewer experts than at the same acceptance length under real verification. Simulated-acceptance throughput is therefore overstated.

The only configuration that was correct is `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` with temperature-only requests, which has been opt-in since #45433. EAGLE/MTP and DFlash already take the bonus from the target at the forced row.

## Modifications

Under simulation, the bonus is the target's token at verify row `c`, drawn with the request's sampling law.

- `dspark_worker_v2.py`: every sampled batch now passes its sampling info as `simulate_bonus_sampling_info`. Before, only `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_GREEDY=1` with temperature-only batches did. The flag now only selects the greedy draft/accept, under the same eligibility checks as before.
- Sampling-accept region graph (`SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH`): it stays eligible under simulation for the same batches as in real serving (all-sampled, temperature-only, no logit adjustments or grammar), so a simulated run keeps the graph that real serving uses.
  - Before the region runs, the worker stages the step's temperatures and seed with `begin_sim_bonus`.
  - Inside the region, the bonus is drawn at row `c` with the epilogue's graph-safe sampler (`sim_bonus`, renamed from `_sim_bonus`), the same kernel `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD` uses.
  - The region's rejection accept still runs, as it does in real serving; under simulation only its length and bonus are replaced.
- `build_accept_outs`: when no sampled bonus is supplied, the bonus is the argmax of row `c`. This covers greedy batches on the eager accept and on the folded greedy accept (`DsparkVerifyEpilogue._accept` without `SGLANG_DSPARK_SIMULATE_FOLD`).
- `sample_simulated_bonus`: top-k/top-p batches sample row `c` from `build_speculative_verify_target_probs`, the target distribution the sampling accept uses. Greedy requests in a mixed batch have top_k=1, so they stay argmax. Temperature-only batches keep the existing Gumbel kernel.
- `static_accept_tail` (Triton kernel and torch reference): the argmax-id bonus is read at the committed length rather than the matched length.
- A sampled simulated bonus is broadcast on the `DSPARK_ACCEPT_SAMPLE` TP sync site, so the `rng` preset keeps ranks consistent.
- `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py`: the sampling-info stand-in gains `need_top_k_sampling` / `need_top_p_sampling`.

Scope of the sampling law under simulation:
- Temperature and top-k/top-p are applied by the bonus sampler.
- Logit adjustments (penalties, logit bias) and grammar masks are honoured only because they are already in the verify logits when the bonus is drawn: `run_non_compact` / `run_compact` apply the adjustments and the worker applies the grammar mask. The sampler itself does neither.
- Batches with adjustments or grammar never use the region graph.
- min-p is not applied. The non-simulated sampling accept does not apply it either.

Simulated acceptance is a benchmark-only mode.

TP: a sampled bonus is broadcast from rank 0 when the `DSPARK_ACCEPT_SAMPLE` site is enabled. Without it, ranks draw from identical seeds, the same assumption the simulated-length draw and the non-simulated rejection sampler already make.

Non-simulated paths are unchanged. Every new branch is behind `simulated_correct_len is not None`, and the tail kernel's non-simulated length is still `num_correct`.

## Accuracy / correctness

Unit-level checks on GB300 run the real kernels, with drafts rejected at row 0 and simulated `c = 3`:

| path | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| eager accept, greedy batch | bonus = row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| folded greedy accept, eager call and inside a CUDA graph | row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| fused static accept tail (Triton) | row-0 argmax | row-3 argmax |
| top-p bonus distribution (T=0.8, p=0.7), max abs diff vs. the renormalized target, 200k draws | 0.21 | 0.0016 |
| non-simulated fused tail | unchanged | unchanged |
| sampling-accept region under simulation, bs 1/1, 3/3, 3/4 (padded); eager warm-up, capture, replays at fixed seeds | rejection bonus at the real row | equals the eager row-`c` draw; drafts at `[:c]`, bonus at `[c]` |
| region bonus distribution, 6,000 replays (T=0.8), max abs diff vs. softmax(row `c` / T) | 0.65 | 0.0099 |

Existing tests, before and after: `test_dspark_accept_tail.py`, `test_dspark_sampling_accept_graph.py` and `test_dspark_sim_draw_ahead.py` pass. `test_dspark_simulated_bonus.py::test_bf16_full_vocab_low_temperature` fails identically with and without this change on NVIDIA. It is registered for AMD CI only.

End to end: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash FP4, DSpark block 5, TP2 EP2, GB300, AgentX-style agentic traces at 32 concurrent, temperature 1, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51` (match-expected). The committed text is re-tokenized; about 1,500 turns are shared across runs.

| | real acceptance | simulated, before | simulated, after |
|---|---|---|---|
| token equal to one of the previous 6 | 0.070 | 0.375 | 0.145 |
| 4-gram already seen in the response | 0.282 | 0.387 | 0.197 |
| share of the most frequent token | 0.042 | 0.170 | 0.083 |
| distinct experts per MoE layer, B=4 / 5 / 8 / 10 | 75.0 / 84.9 / 116.2 / 123.9 | 53.9 / 62.7 / 85.0 / 94.9 | 71.8 / 85.3 / 108.3 / 121.9 |

After the fix, the remaining difference from real acceptance is in the drafted tokens. Simulation accepts them unconditionally, so repeats 2-3 tokens apart rise from 0.027 to 0.096 of tokens. Immediate repeats (0.0008 vs 0.0024) and repeats 4-6 tokens apart match real acceptance. An independent simulated-acceptance implementation that commits the target's token at the forced position measures the same statistics on this workload (0.148 / 0.182 / 0.087).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

The size of the change depends on the point: it is largest where MoE is a big share of the step and the degenerate text cut the distinct experts the most.

**TP2 EP2, 32 concurrent** (the end-to-end setup above), 3600 s:

| | total tok/s/GPU | output tok/s/GPU | ITL p50 / p90 (ms) | interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s, 1000/ITL) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| simulated, before | 122.2K | 697 | 3.43 / 4.40 | 291.5 / 227.3 |
| simulated, after | 118.9K | 683 | 3.85 / 4.92 | 259.7 / 203.3 |

Both runs measure AL 3.51. The "after" run is 2.7% lower in total throughput and 11% lower in p90 interactivity (11% higher p90 ITL). This is expected: the "before" run's degenerate text made MoE about 1 ms/step cheaper at B=4-10. Each number is a single run, on different nodes. These two runs applied the same change to an earlier nightly and use the eager accept (no sampling-accept graph).

**TP4 EP1, 1 concurrent, NVIDIA megakernel**, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_SAMPLING_ACCEPT_GRAPH=1`, `SGLANG_SIMULATE_ACC_LEN=3.51`, same traces, 1800 s, AL 3.51 in every run. At batch 1 with the experts sharded across four GPUs, MoE is a small share of the step, so the change costs about 1%. This table also shows why the sampling-accept region change is needed:

| | region graph replays | interactivity p50 / p90 (tok/s, 1000/ITL) |
|---|---|---|
| this PR | ~110k per rank | 976 / 949 |
| this PR without the region change (sampled simulated steps fall back to the eager accept) | 0 | 939 / 863 |
| before this PR (region graph with the misplaced bonus), 3600 s | captured | 987 / 954 |

Keeping the region in the graph is worth 4% / 10% at p50 / p90. The remaining ~1% to "before" is within what the text change and the shorter run can explain.

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Existing unit tests updated; no new test file (verified on GPU as above).

title: [Perf] diffusion: HunyuanImage-3 prefix K/V cache, opt-in FA3 attention and think-prompt support
author: OnePunchMonk
body:
## Motivation

Depends on #46600 (the CUDA MoE noise fix, which fixes #46461). This PR will be rebased on it once it lands, so the fix commit below will drop out of the diff.

Changes for HunyuanImage-3 (the prefix K/V cache is the main one; the opt-in FA3 attention and the `cot_text` fix are described under Modifications):

1. **Fix: generation on CUDA produced a noise texture** (on main too). The MoE block ran the routed experts before the shared MLP. On CUDA the Triton `FusedMoE` path runs in place (`inplace=True` by default) and overwrites `hidden_states` with the expert output, so the shared MLP read the expert output instead of the layer input and every MoE layer was wrong. The NPU path (AscendTPDispatcher) is not in place, which is likely why the original NPU validation in #36311 did not see it; the cookbook also marks the CUDA recipe as unverified. srt's own Hunyuan model already runs the shared MLP first.
2. **Perf: cache the text prefix K/V across denoising steps.** HunyuanImage-3 recomputes the whole text prefix through every layer (attention and MoE) on every step, even though that prefix never changes. The proposal this implements:

> **P1. Prefix KV cache** (`hunyuan_image3.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager`, `forward_block`)
> The text prefix is causal and step-invariant. At `first_step`, keep the per-layer prefix K/V; on later steps feed only the image tokens as queries and attend to [cached prefix K/V, image K/V]. Replace the dense 4-D bool-mask SDPA with FA varlen (prefix causal + image full) or flex.
> Removes L_text/(L_text+L_img) of the MoE compute per step. Large for long or "think" prompts; also recovers FlashAttention.

This PR does the prefix K/V cache with the dense SDPA as the default, plus the FA varlen part as an opt-in (`--attention-backend fa3`), since FA3 is not bitwise equal to SDPA. The official model does the same caching at inference (later steps feed only the timestep and image tokens against a static KV cache).

## Modifications

**Fix (commit 2)**
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `HunYuanSparseMoeBlock.forward` runs the shared MLP before the in-place experts.
- `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: match the official `FlowMatchDiscreteScheduler` schedule, `shift(linspace(1, 0, N + 1))[:-1]` (`use_uniform_sigmas=True`). The old setup shifted the training-sigma range a second time; for 10 steps the last timestep was 8.93 instead of 250.

**Prefix K/V cache (commit 1)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `ImageKVCacheManager` stores each layer's prefix K/V on step 0, keyed by a cache slot, and on later steps prepends it to the suffix K/V. Adds `split_suffix_inputs` and `pad_prefix_rows`.
- `hunyuan_image3.py`: `forward_block` takes `prefix_len` and `cache_slot`. Step 0 runs the full sequence; later steps run only the suffix rows and pad the output back to full length, so callers see the same shape.
- `ar_stage.py`: computes the prefix once as the rows before the first noisy-image or timestep token, and returns no prefix (full compute) when a clean image block straddles that boundary. `first_step` is now `step_idx == 0` (it was always `True`, and nothing read it). CFG cond and uncond use separate cache slots, since they run as two backbone calls on the same modules.
- Falls back to the current path when CLA is on, when the cache-dit adapter drives the blocks, or when no safe prefix exists.

Why the cache is exact: the mask is causal, so every row before the first varying token only sees prompt and clean conditioning tokens. Clean conditioning images before the noisy block are cached too, so the saving is a bit larger than L_text/(L_text+L_img).

Memory cost of the cache: `bs x P x kv_heads x head_dim x 4 bytes` per layer per CFG slot. Measured 156 MB per GPU for a 1,248-token prefix with both CFG slots (exactly the formula); the reported peak is unchanged.

**Opt-in FA3 segment attention (`--attention-backend fa3`)**
- `hunyuan_image3_utils.py`: `build_attention_segments` splits the mask (causal text, bidirectional image blocks) into `(start, end, causal)` segments; `segmented_attention` runs one FA3 varlen call per segment with bottom-right causal alignment, for both full and cached-suffix steps. GQA is native, so no `repeat_kv`. Hopper only; elsewhere the masked SDPA path is kept.
- `ar_stage.py` / `pipelines/hunyuan_image3.py`: segments are built only when `attention_backend == "fa"` (what `fa3`/`fa4` resolve to). The default path is unchanged and still bitwise identical to main + fix.
- 2x H200: 22.6 s vs 26.8 s for the default path (1.55x vs main + fix). Not bitwise: PSNR 21-24 dB vs SDPA, same composition. On GPU the segments reproduce the attention mask exactly over 384 calls and FA3 vs SDPA differs by at most one bf16 ulp per call, so the drift is kernel rounding compounding over layers and steps. Details and images: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422227024

**Fix: `cot_text` from the image API**
- `configs/sample/hunyuan_image3.py`: declare `bot_task`, `system_prompt` and `cot_text` in `image_request_extra_fields`. The image endpoint only forwards declared fields, so think/recaption text was silently dropped. With it, think prompts are 1.32x to 1.50x faster than main + fix (the reasoning text lands in the cached prefix), outputs identical: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/46454#issuecomment-6422648092

## How the noise bug was found

On 2x H200 TP2 with debug-only instrumentation (not in this PR):
- Checked the port line by line against the official `modeling_hunyuan_image_3.py` and `hunyuan_image_3_pipeline.py` shipped with the checkpoint. 2D RoPE, QKV split, QK norm order, SwiGLU half order, residual flow, UNetDown/UNetUp, timestep embedders, CFG, Euler step and VAE decode all match.
- Compared real decoder layers at step 0 against an fp32 reference transcribed from the official layer, with weights read straight from the checkpoint shards:

| layer | attention cos / rel err | MoE cos / rel err |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0.99999 / 0.004 | 0.738 / 0.94 |
| 1 | 0.99999 / 0.005 | 0.608 / 0.80 |
| 31 | 0.99999 / 0.003 | 0.166 / 1.02 |

- Inside the MoE everything feeding the kernel was correct: router logits matched exactly, top-k ids agreed 100%, and every expert `w13`/`w2` shard and the shared MLP weights matched the checkpoint slices. That left execution order, and `FusedMoE` turned out to be in place.

## Accuracy Tests

CPU unit tests in `test_hunyuan_image3_tp_broadcast.py`, all 11 in the file pass:
- Fix regressions: the shared MLP sees the layer input when the experts run in place; timesteps follow the official schedule. With only the two fixed source files reverted, exactly these two fail.
- Prefix cache: a cached suffix-only step matches full recompute; CFG slots do not overwrite each other; the prefix ends at the first varying token and is `None` when a clean image block straddles it.
- FA3 segments: segment attention equals masked SDPA for full and suffix-only steps; overlapping blocks fall back.
- Image API: `cot_text` and `bot_task` reach the sampling params.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

main + the fix vs this PR (prefix cache + fix), 2x H200 TP2 per the cookbook recipe, 1024x1024, 50 steps, guidance 2.5, seed 42. One warmup then one timed request per prompt.

| | main + fix | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| short prompt, request | 34.97 s | 27.42 s | -21.6% (1.28x) |
| short prompt, AR/denoise stage | 34.19 s | 26.68 s | -22.0% |
| long prompt, request | 35.84 s | 27.49 s | -23.3% (1.30x) |
| long prompt, AR/denoise stage | 35.04 s | 26.75 s | -23.7% |
| peak memory (server log) | 106,318 MB | 106,318 MB | no change |
| output vs main + fix | | byte-identical on both prompts | PSNR inf |

Images and notes are in the results comment. Earlier numbers and the noise-texture images in older comments were taken before the fix and should be ignored.

## Checklist

- [x] Format with pre-commit hooks (ruff F401/F821/F823/UP037, ruff-format)
- [x] Unit tests added (fix regressions + prefix cache)
- [x] GPU time / memory / parity on the fixed code
- [ ] Docs / cookbook update (the CUDA recipe could move from unverified once the numbers are in)

title: [Feat] [AMD] minimax: gfx950 sparse attention, NVFP4 KV and DSpark verify kernels
author: kevin-mii
body:
> Part of the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash AMD series that replaces #45936 (closed with its base branch `minimax-m3.1-flash`): kernel PRs #46690 (attention), #46691 (MoE / GEMM) and #46692 (quick all-reduce), each on `main`; then #46693 with the M3.1 call sites and #46694 (indexer CP). It follows the DeepSeek-V4.1 AMD layout (#41018-#41021, then #41308).

## Summary
- **NVFP4 KV (MSA-v1 layout).** `minimax_sparse/common/nvfp4.py` reads the packed rows for the Triton kernels and `nvfp4_gfx950.py` dequantizes them in Gluon. The kernel tests build their packed caches with a torch quantizer in `NVFP4KVQuantizeUtil`'s layout (`nvfp4_kv_quantize` in `sglang/test/quant_ref_utils.py`).
- **Sparse decode.** `decode/nvfp4_decode_gfx950.py` runs sparse decode over the packed NVFP4 K/V in Gluon (one program per row, top-k chunk and KV head; per-warp online softmax). `topk_sparse.py` dispatches an `Nvfp4Cache` to it, and the NVFP4 verify scorer sits beside the bf16 one in `decode/verify_topk_idx.py`.
- **Verify indexer.** `decode/verify_topk_idx.py` scores a linear draft chain against one shared prefix; `decode/verify_topk_gfx950.py` fuses the per-block max score with a streaming top-k on MFMA tiles.
- **Prefill.** `prefill/index_topk_gfx950.py` is the fused prefill indexer; `prefill/gluon_prefill_pair_gfx950.py` runs two queries per program over the union of their top-k blocks; `prefill/nvfp4_prefill.py` gathers the NVFP4 cache into the Gluon prefill's paged layout; `prefill/gluon_prefill.py` and `prefill/flash_with_topk_idx.py` take the new cache.
- **fp8 O epilogue.** `common/out_quant_gfx950.py` is shared by the Gluon decode and pair prefill: they can write O directly as the fp8 o_proj input, with the same bytes and scales as aiter's separate per-token or 1x128 quant.
- **QK-norm + RoPE.** `minimax_m3_qk_norm_rope.py` adds the gfx950 fused Gemma Q/K RMSNorm + partial RoPE + KV-cache write.
- **HiCache.** The NVFP4 page-row copy takes its CTA quota as a template argument: 32 on HIP (MI350X needs 16+ to saturate PCIe), 2 on CUDA as before.
- **Windowed verify.** `verify_mla_window.py` lets the gfx950 grouped-head split-KV verify serve the DSpark draft's sliding window (its non-causal draft block, window 4095) with a one-pass combine, as a `VerifyMLA` subclass; `num_stages=2` was 13-26% faster for that window. The shared `verify_mla.py` only gains the stage-1 window mask (a constexpr, compiled out without a window), the caller's opt-in in `can_handle`, and the two class hooks the subclass sets; Qwen3.5 and Kimi-K3 verify outputs are bitwise unchanged.
- The M3.1 call sites (NVFP4 pool, verify indexer, fp8 O for `o_proj`, windowed draft verify) are in the integration PR.

## Serving gain of each kernel
Measured in the integration PR at TP4 on MI350X (NVFP4 KV, DSpark acceptance simulated at 3 tokens per step, 32K-token contexts), each change turned off alone; the share decode TPOT or prefill latency grows without it, mean of two GPU sets:
- Windowed draft verify (`verify_mla_window`): decode TPOT +20.6% at 1 request, +8.2-9.6% at 8-64.
- Two-queries-per-program Gluon prefill (`gluon_prefill_pair_gfx950`): 32K-token prefill +10.3%, decode +4.2-5.4% at 8-64.
- Gluon prefill over an FP8 KV pool (`SGLANG_MINIMAX_M3_AMD_KV_FORMAT=fp8`): prefill +11.7% (32K tokens) and +12.4% (eight 8K requests).
- NVFP4 KV itself (kernel level, CUDA-graph replay, per layer): the verify indexer at 110K context takes 0.75-0.84x FP8's time from 8 requests and sparse decode 0.42-0.68x, with 1.78x the tokens per GB of KV.

## Changes to existing kernels
On CUDA nothing changes: `topk_sparse` only dispatches the new `Nvfp4Cache` type, the decode top-k only moves into `select_decode_topk`, and the page-row quota stays 2.

On gfx950, main's MiniMax-M3 layers switch kernels when this merges, with no new call site:
- QK-norm + RoPE + cache store (`sparse_qk_index_gemma_rmsnorm_rope_cache`) runs the tiled kernel for M3's 128-wide head with 64-dim neox RoPE; its bf16 outputs equal the per-head kernel's bit for bit.
- The Gluon sparse prefill pairs two queries per program for bf16 batches from 2048 tokens (16 query heads), and now also serves an fp8 KV pool at its per-tensor k/v scales, which `minimax_sparse_prefill` now passes on; before, an fp8 pool stayed on Triton. Both match the Triton kernel up to bf16 rounding.
- The prefill indexer uses the fused gfx950 index top-k for score-only max layers at unit scales and 128-aligned pages; on these bf16 / fp8 index caches it emits the Triton two-pass indexer's block ids exactly. It keeps Triton when Gluon's CDNA4 module is missing.

On other ROCm GPUs, the per-head QK-norm kernel, which serves them (and gfx950 heads other than M3's), no longer writes main K/V to slot 0, the reserved CUDA-graph padding slot. The unfused `store_cache` already skips it, and no real token is stored there.

## Verification
- MI350X (ROCm 7.2 image `rocm/sgl-dev:v0.5.20-rocm720-mi35x-20260926`, AITER `acf8fdf93`, `SGLANG_USE_AITER=1`), this branch alone on `main`: `test_minimax_gfx950_prefill` 35 passed, `test_minimax_m3_qk_norm_rope` 55, `test_minimax_nvfp4_sparse_decode` 13, `test_minimax_verify_topk_idx` 68 (the kernel cases; the integration PR adds 8 more), `test_verify_shared_kv` 10. pre-commit clean; main's callers of every modified kernel module import.
- Not executed on this branch alone: CUDA (shared files keep main's behavior there), end-to-end serving.

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Optimize the Wan VAE decode for gfx1250
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What**
Cut the Wan VAE decode on gfx1250 (MI450) from 22.5 s to 8.5 s for Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 720p / 193 frames. The changes: run the ROCm batched-Conv2D replacement in NHWC, install the existing Wan VAE fast path (fused RMSNorm+SiLU, DupUp3D+add) on gfx1250, and drop the slow `where` from the gfx1250 math-SDPA VAE attention.

It also keeps that fast path under multi-GPU: with `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel`, Wan's `auto` VAE parallel-decode mode no longer picks spatial-shard decode on gfx1250, and only the main rank decodes. TP2 VAE decode goes from 28.5 s to 9.0 s.

**Why**
A torch profile of the decode showed only ~9 s of the ~20 s of GPU time was convolution. The rest was unfused fp32 elementwise work plus one attention fixup:

- `RocmPlatform.optimize_vae` never installed `wan_vae_cuda_opt`, so every `WanRMS_norm -> SiLU` ran as `linalg_vector_norm` + `div` + `mul` + `silu` (div 4.8 s, mul 3.0 s, silu 2.7 s per decode).
- The fused norm needs a channels_last_3d input, but the ROCm batched-Conv2D replacement produced `[N, T, C, H, W]` memory. Simply making the conv2d channels_last does not help: PyTorch runs MIOpen convs in NHWC only when `PYTORCH_MIOPEN_SUGGEST_NHWC=1` (read on every call). Without it, a channels_last conv2d is transposed to NCHW and back. With it, the VAE convs run 1.4-2.9x faster (34.97 -> 11.89 ms at 96 ch, 720x1280). The conv output then folds back to channels_last_3d without a copy, so the fused norm applies.
- gfx1250 pins VAE attention to the math SDPA backend (AOTriton fails above head_dim 256). 121 of its 131 ms per call is the `where` in `_safe_softmax` that zeroes fully masked rows. There is no mask here, so computing the same ops explicitly (`q*s @ (k*s)^T`, softmax, `@ v`) is bit-identical and skips it.
- Multi-GPU: `WanVAEConfig.auto_parallel_decode_prefers_spatial_shard()` returns True, so with more than one rank the decoder is built for spatial-shard decode, and `_maybe_optimize_wan_family_vae` then skips the fast path (`Wan VAE: spatial-parallel decode; skipping fast path.`). The sharded decode on the slow path takes 28.5 s on 2 ranks, slower than one rank on the fast path. Once `auto` stops sharding there, `AutoencoderKLWan.use_parallel_decode` was still the raw config flag (always True), so `DecodingStage` stayed `REPLICATED` under cfg-parallel and both ranks decoded the same full video (10.0 s).

## Modifications

- `platforms/rocm.py`:
  - On gfx1250, `optimize_vae` installs `maybe_optimize_wan_vae` / `maybe_optimize_qwen_image_vae`.
  - `_replace_conv3d_with_conv2d` keeps a channels_last BF16 2-D weight when the 3-D weight is channels_last_3d, and sets `PYTORCH_MIOPEN_SUGGEST_NHWC=1` with `setdefault` (an explicit user value wins).
  - `_conv3d_as_batched_conv2d` gets an NHWC branch: one copy gathers the Kt frames and casts to BF16 into `[N*T_out, H, W, Kt*C_in]`, and the output reshapes back to channels_last_3d.
- `models/vaes/wanvae.py`:
  - Import the Triton VAE helpers on gfx1250 too.
  - Keep the fused cat+pad away from convs patched by the Conv2D replacement (it would call the unpatched epilogue).
  - Use explicit math attention when `_sgl_math_sdpa` is set and inputs are fp32.
  - `AutoencoderKLWan.use_parallel_decode` is the config flag, except in `auto` mode where it is True only when spatial-shard decode is chosen, so a single-rank decode runs on the main rank alone under cfg-parallel. Explicit modes keep the config flag.
- `configs/models/vaes/wanvae.py`: `WanVAEConfig.auto_parallel_decode_prefers_spatial_shard()` returns `not is_gfx1250_supported()`. An explicit `parallel_decode_mode=spatial_shard` still shards.
- `models/vaes/wan_vae_cuda_opt.py`: allow the exact-tier post-op fusion on HIP. It keeps its first-use `torch.equal` verification and falls back to aten on any mismatch. On ROCm it is only reachable through the gfx1250 install above.
- Scope: all new behavior is gated on `is_gfx1250_supported()`. NVIDIA, MI300, and MI355 paths are unchanged (one extra `hasattr`/`getattr` that evaluates false).
- Tests (`test_rocm_conv3d_patch.py`):
  - The NHWC conv matches the original `WanCausalConv3d` (with `residual=` / `skip_bias=`) and returns channels_last_3d.
  - Explicit math attention is `torch.equal` to the math SDPA backend.
- Tests (`test_vae_spatial_parallel_decode.py`): `auto` does not shard on gfx1250 while explicit `spatial_shard` does; `use_parallel_decode` is False only for `auto` on gfx1250 (`spatial_shard`, `patch`, and non-gfx1250 `auto` are unchanged). The existing Wan assertion runs with gfx1250 patched off.

## Accuracy Tests

Wan2.2-T2V-A14B, 720x1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42, fp32 VAE decode, single MI450 (gfx1250) partition. The video is compared against main with the same flags, per frame:

| comparison | PSNR mean | PSNR min | last frame |
|---|---|---|---|
| this PR vs main, full 8-step video | 38.45 dB | 35.64 dB | 38.34 dB |
| VAE attention change only vs main | bit-identical | bit-identical | bit-identical |

The difference comes from the NHWC conv algorithm (the BF16 compute was already there) and the fused norm's rounding order (`quality="lossless"`, the default request tier). Against an fp32 `conv3d` reference, the NHWC and NCHW batched-conv2d paths have the same relative error (3.20e-3 / 3.05e-3 / 3.00e-3 at the three decoder resolutions). Frames were checked visually, including the last frame.

Multi-GPU (TP2, `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel`), same prompt and seed, decoded video compared over all frames:

| comparison | PSNR |
|---|---|
| single-rank fast-path decode vs spatial-shard decode (before) | 38.7 dB |
| main-rank-only decode vs both ranks decoding | inf (identical) |

Spatial-shard and single-rank decode were never bit-identical; per-frame PSNR is flat (37.7-38.9 dB), with no shard seams.

## Benchmarking and Profiling

`sglang generate` with the flags of the Wan2.2 cookbook debug script: `--num-gpus 1 --vae-decode-precision fp32 --attention-backend aiter --enable-torch-compile false`, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_VAE_CONV2D_BF16=1`, `SGLANG_DIFFUSION_VAE_CHANNELS_LAST_3D=1`, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_FLYDSL=1`, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0`. One gfx1250 partition (DPX), single request:

| | denoise (s) | VAE decode (s) | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| main `3dce594de3` | 199.3 | 22.5 | 223.3 |
| this PR | 198.9 | **8.5** | **208.9** |

VAE decode kernels (torch profiler, one decode):

| op | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `aten::div` (F.normalize) | 4.83 s | fused |
| `aten::mul` | 3.03 s | fused |
| unary (SiLU) | 2.75 s | fused |
| math SDPA (25 calls) | 3.28 s | ~0.2 s |
| convolution | ~5.3 s + transposes | NHWC, 1.4-2.9x faster per conv |

Multi-GPU. TP2 is `--num-gpus 2 --enable-cfg-parallel` on the two halves of one gfx1250 package, same flags otherwise. These runs were on a later branch that also has #46723, with the dashboard shape (90000 DiT tokens), so absolute times are not comparable with the TP1 table above:

| run | text encode (s) | denoise (s) | VAE decode (s) | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| TP1 (reference) | 1.05 | 161.3 | 8.7 | 171.4 |
| TP2 before the multi-GPU change | 1.97 | 93.8 | 28.5 | 124.7 |
| TP2 with this PR | 1.96 | 93.6 | **9.0** | **105.0** |

TP2 e2e is 1.19x faster, and TP2 vs TP1 goes from 1.37x to 1.63x. The remaining denoise gap to 2x is the package power limit (both halves pin the 1600 W socket cap, gfx clock ~1840 -> ~1360 MHz), not this code path.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] [AMD] diffusion: Replace the gfx1250 bf16 scale-shift torch fallback with a bit-exact Triton kernel
author: yichiche
body:
## Motivation

**What**
On gfx1250, replace the torch fallback behind `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` for bf16 `x` with an fp32 scale by a dedicated Triton kernel. The kernel is bit-identical to that fallback and 6.4x faster, and covers Wan's `MulAdd` residual gate (`x * (k + scale) + shift`).

**Why**
#42859 routes every bf16 `fuse_scale_shift_kernel` call on gfx1250 to `fuse_scale_shift_kernel_native`, because the existing Triton kernels miscompile there (the identity term is dropped). With an fp32 scale, that fallback promotes to fp32 and returns fp32, so Wan's `mlp_residual(...).to(orig_dtype)` costs three passes over a [90000, 5120] tensor: an fp32 broadcast mul, an fp32 add, and a bf16 cast. That is 2.18 ms per block, 40 blocks per forward.

When the scale is fp32, every intermediate in the fallback is fp32. A kernel that does the same fp32 ops, with FMA contraction disabled (`enable_fp_fusion=False`) and a single rounding to `x.dtype`, therefore produces exactly the fallback's result cast to bf16. That cast is the next thing every caller does, and it matches the `empty_like(x)` contract of the CUDA kernel. Any other case (bf16 scale, per-frame 4-D scale, non-3-D `x`) still takes the fallback.

## Modifications

- `kernels/ops/diffusion/modulate/scale_shift_triton.py`: add `_scale_shift_fp32_rows_kernel` (16x256 row tiles, int64 row offsets, shift that is per-token or broadcast) and `_fuse_scale_shift_fp32_gfx1250`. The guard checks shapes, dtypes, and unit stride on C, and returns `None` for anything else. The kernel is tried first inside the existing `is_gfx1250_supported() and x.dtype is torch.bfloat16` branch.
- `test_modulate.py`: add a gfx1250-only test asserting `torch.equal` with `fuse_scale_shift_kernel_native(...).to(bf16)` for k in {0, 1}, full and broadcast shift, bf16 and fp32 shift.
- Scope: gfx1250 with bf16 inputs only. Other platforms never enter the branch.

Note: `test_scale_shift_3d_tiling_is_bit_exact` (added by #46147) already fails 8/8 on gfx1250 on main, because its reference is the Triton `blc_opt` kernel that #42859 routes around. With this PR, 3/8 pass. The remaining cases compare against that miscompiled reference.

## Accuracy Tests

Bit-exact by construction and by test: `torch.equal` against the fallback in 8 parametrized cases, plus 24 shape/dtype cases at L = 777 / 90000 / 176400, C = 5120.

End to end, Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 720p, 193 frames, 8 steps, seed 42 on gfx1250: the output video is **bit-identical** to main (per-frame PSNR = inf, max abs diff 0).

## Benchmarking and Profiling

Kernel, gfx1250, [1, 90000, 5120] bf16 `x`, fp32 scale, bf16 shift:

| path | time |
|---|---|
| torch fallback + `.to(bf16)` (main) | 2.176 ms |
| this PR | **0.341 ms** (6.4x) |

End to end, `sglang generate` Wan2.2-T2V-A14B 720x1280, 193 frames, 8 steps, CFG, `--num-gpus 1 --attention-backend aiter`, `SGLANG_USE_ROCM_FLYDSL=1`, `HIP_FORCE_DEV_KERNARG=0`, one gfx1250 partition, single request:

| | denoise (s) | e2e (s) |
|---|---|---|
| main `3dce594de3` | 199.3 | 223.3 |
| this PR | **197.3** | **221.5** |

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] muse-spark-open: Fuse MoE finalize with the 2shot_push all-reduce
author: wookjeHan
body:
## Motivation Muse Spark fuses its MoE finalize with the custom all-reduce. Today the fused kernel only implements `1shot_push`, and it runs only where the standalone all-reduce would pick `1shot_push`. Above that size the MoE output falls back to a separate finalize kernel plus a standalone all-reduce launch. This PR adds a `2shot_push` exchange to the fused kernel. The fused path now follows the standalone all-reduce's choice: fused 1-shot where it picks `1shot_push`, and fused 2-shot where it picks `2shot_push`. Independent of #46197; the fused 2-shot path runs wherever the all-reduce table picks `2shot_push` (main's table on GB300; on SM107 from #46197). SM107 numbers below are measured on top of #46197, GB300 numbers on main. ## Modifications **Kernel** (`muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce_cutedsl.py`) - The 2-shot exchange follows the `2shot_push` protocol of `custom_all_reduce.cuh`. - The output is bitwise equal to the fused 1-shot path. - It reuses the communicator's push slots and epoch controllers, so there are no new allocations. - When M exceeds the controller count, a block finalizes two tokens, one row of threads each, with per-row named barriers. This applies to 2-shot and unicast 1-shot; multicast 1-shot measured slower. - One-row fused blocks reduce four experts per barrier pair (`group_width` 4, as the cluster path already does). - Refactor: the 1-shot `push_token` / `reduce_token` and the new 2-shot functions share small helpers: copy atoms, `_vec_at`, `_epoch_base`, `_remap_sentinel`, `_poll_arrived` and `_sum_ranks`. **Dispatch** (`muse_spark_finalize_workspace.py`, `muse_spark_moe_finalize_all_reduce.py`) - `two_shot_max_tokens = slot_bytes * world / (4H)` (2048 tokens at TP4 with the default 8 MB slot). It is 0 unless `H % (8 * world) == 0`, so every rank owns whole 8-column vectors. - `uses_two_shot_push(M)` is true exactly where the standalone all-reduce picks `2shot_push`, including under `override_algo`. - `can_fuse` takes the fused 1-shot or the fused 2-shot path. The separate `override_algo` check is gone, because both predicates already go through the communicator's own override handling. - No standalone all-reduce thresholds or buffer allocations change. ## Accuracy Tests **E2E** Muse Spark Open, DFlash (8 draft tokens, real acceptance), sgl-eval with T=1.0, top_p=1.0, top_k=64 and xhigh reasoning. On SM107 fused 2-shot serves every decode batch above 128 tokens (c ≥ 17). | GPU, config | GSM8K | AIME26 pass@1 (x16) | AIME26 pass@16 | |---|---|---|---| | SM107 TP4/EP4, #46197 + this PR | 97.35% | 96.46% ± 2.57 (SEM 0.64) | 100% | | SM107 TP8/EP8 (2 nodes), #46197 + this PR | 97.35% | 97.08% ± 2.06 (SEM 0.52) | 100% | | GB300 TP4/EP4, main + this PR | 97.57% | 95.83% ± 3.10 (SEM 0.78) | 100% | | GB300 TP8/EP8 (2 trays), main + this PR | 97.65% | 95.62% ± 3.15 (SEM 0.79) | 100% | On SM107 the acceptance length was 4.84 / 3.85 (GSM8K / AIME26) on main (earlier run) and 4.94 / 3.85 with #46197 + this PR.
Kernel correctness (bitwise vs fused 1-shot, interleaving with standalone all-reduce, stress) Kernel correctness was checked with a multi-GPU harness, each check in eager mode and under CUDA-graph replay with fresh inputs, with unicast and multicast pushes: - Fused 2-shot vs fused 1-shot, bitwise (only +0 -> -0 differs) for M = 8 to 1024, both router-weight dtypes and both `weight_first` modes. - Two-rows-per-block and persistent layouts vs the same tokens launched in chunks of at most `controller_count` tokens (one row per block), bitwise, for 1-shot and 2-shot. - Fused (1-shot / 2-shot) and standalone `CustomAllReduceV2` (`1shot_push` / `2shot_push`) launches interleaved at changing sizes: they share the push slots and epoch controllers but lay out phase two differently. Standalone results match the exact sum, fused results match fused 1-shot bitwise, and every push slot is empty again after each round. | GPU | world | result | |---|---|---| | SM107 | 2, 4 | 80 / 80 checks passed | | SM107 | 8 (2 nodes, MNNVL) | 80 / 80 checks passed | | GB300 | 4 | 38 / 38 checks passed (earlier harness revision) | | GB300 | 8 (2 trays) | 38 / 38 checks passed on both trays (earlier harness revision) | Stress runs, all bitwise PASS: - SM107: 20 rounds of the interleaved sequence (worlds 2 and 4, unicast and multicast, eager and graph); no slot words left behind, no wrong output. - GB300, 2-shot: 4,000 pipelined calls with random per-rank delays and interleaved standalone all-reduces, then 4 graphs x 1,000 replays with one slow rank each: 496 / 496 at TP4, 992 / 992 at TP8, with no +0 / -0 pairs. - GB300, 1-shot with two rows per block: the same, 496 / 496 at TP4 and 992 / 992 at TP8. Fused 2-shot output equals fused 1-shot output bit for bit. It differs from main only at M where main runs the finalize and the standalone all-reduce separately: there the reduction order and rounding point differ.
## Speed Tests and Profiling ### Kernel Finalize + all-reduce for one Muse Spark MoE layer: H = 4096, top-8, M = 8 x c (DFlash verify), µs per call. "separate" is finalize followed by the standalone `2shot_push` all-reduce. **SM107** (#46197 vs #46197 + this PR; one CUDA graph of 100 calls, median of 9 replays, slowest rank, mean of 2 rounds; TP8 is 2 nodes over MNNVL with multicast) | c | M | TP4 before (path) | TP4 this PR (path) | TP4 speedup | TP8 before (path) | TP8 this PR (path) | TP8 speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 8 | 5.4 (fused 1shot) | 5.4 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | 4.5 (fused 1shot) | 4.5 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | | 4 | 32 | 5.4 (fused 1shot) | 5.4 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | 5.8 (fused 1shot) | 5.8 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | | 8 | 64 | 6.3 (fused 1shot) | 6.3 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | 9.2 (separate) | 7.3 (fused 2shot) | 1.26x | | 16 | 128 | 7.7 (fused 1shot) | 7.7 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | 9.9 (separate) | 7.9 (fused 2shot) | 1.25x | | 24 | 192 | 11.7 (separate) | 8.4 (fused 2shot) | 1.40x | 11.5 (separate) | 8.4 (fused 2shot) | 1.37x | | 32 | 256 | 13.0 (separate) | 10.2 (fused 2shot) | 1.27x | 12.7 (separate) | 9.6 (fused 2shot) | 1.32x | | 48 | 384 | 14.1 (separate) | 10.6 (fused 2shot) | 1.34x | 14.2 (separate) | 10.8 (fused 2shot) | 1.32x | | 64 | 512 | 15.3 (separate) | 14.8 (fused 2shot) | 1.04x | 15.8 (separate) | 14.1 (fused 2shot) | 1.12x | | 96 | 768 | 18.7 (separate) | 16.0 (fused 2shot) | 1.17x | 19.0 (separate) | 15.3 (fused 2shot) | 1.24x | | 128 | 1024 | 22.8 (separate) | 19.1 (fused 2shot) | 1.20x | 23.9 (separate) | 19.1 (fused 2shot) | 1.25x | On SM107 the path this PR serves is also the fastest of fused 1-shot, fused 2-shot and separate finalize + `1shot_push` / `2shot_push` at every measured point. **GB300** (main vs main + this PR, as serving runs each tree: production communicator with 8 MiB push slots and 152 controllers; one CUDA graph of 32 calls, median of 100 replays, slowest rank, mean of 3 interleaved rounds) | c | M | TP4 main (path) | TP4 this PR (path) | TP4 speedup | TP8 main (path) | TP8 this PR (path) | TP8 speedup | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | 1 | 8 | 4.73 (fused 1shot) | 4.76 (fused 1shot) | 0.99x | 9.59 (fused 1shot) | 9.09 (fused 1shot) | 1.06x | | 4 | 32 | 5.17 (fused 1shot) | 5.18 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | 10.81 (fused 1shot) | 10.74 (fused 1shot) | 1.01x | | 8 | 64 | 6.55 (fused 1shot) | 6.56 (fused 1shot) | 1.00x | 13.63 (separate) | 11.48 (fused 2shot) | 1.19x | | 10 | 80 | 7.65 (fused 1shot) | 7.24 (fused 1shot) | 1.06x | 13.50 (separate) | 11.74 (fused 2shot) | 1.15x | | 11 | 88 | 9.12 (separate) | 7.15 (fused 2shot) | 1.28x | 14.24 (separate) | 11.74 (fused 2shot) | 1.21x | | 16 | 128 | 9.78 (separate) | 7.54 (fused 2shot) | 1.30x | 14.37 (separate) | 11.47 (fused 2shot) | 1.25x | | 24 | 192 | 13.28 (separate) | 9.83 (fused 2shot) | 1.35x | 17.79 (separate) | 13.14 (fused 2shot) | 1.35x | | 32 | 256 | 13.81 (separate) | 9.95 (fused 2shot) | 1.39x | 18.19 (separate) | 14.02 (fused 2shot) | 1.30x | | 48 | 384 | 16.29 (separate) | 13.56 (fused 2shot) | 1.20x | 21.10 (separate) | 17.28 (fused 2shot) | 1.22x | | 64 | 512 | 19.20 (separate) | 15.25 (fused 2shot) | 1.26x | 24.40 (separate) | 19.55 (fused 2shot) | 1.25x | | 96 | 768 | 24.40 (separate) | 20.73 (fused 2shot) | 1.18x | 31.12 (separate) | 24.26 (fused 2shot) | 1.28x | | 128 | 1024 | 31.16 (separate) | 25.74 (fused 2shot) | 1.21x | 36.86 (separate) | 30.25 (fused 2shot) | 1.22x | On GB300 the three rounds agree within 1-3% at TP4; across two trays the per-round spread reaches about 25%, so TP8 points with the same path on both sides (c <= 4) move within noise. At TP4 c = 10 the path is unchanged and the four-experts-per-barrier change makes fused 1-shot 5% faster. title: [Perf] kda: Write convolution output directly into contiguous QKV planes
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

KDA already computes packed Q/K/V convolution in one call. Its token-major output leaves the three channel slices non-contiguous, so the FlashInfer prefill path materializes three copies before consuming them. At the GLM-5.3-Flash TP4 16K-token shape, those copies cost more than the convolution itself.

## Modifications

Add an optional split-output layout to the existing Triton convolution. The convolution stores directly into contiguous Q/K/V planes in one allocation, using the runtime total-token count as the plane pitch. Arithmetic and convolution-state updates are unchanged.

Both eager KDA prefill and captured KDA prefill enable it only for FlashInfer with equal Q/K/V widths. Other backends and unequal widths retain the original layout. There are no server-argument, graph-size, precision, MoE or memory-budget changes, and no dependency on the separate empty-view fix #46737 or community PRs #45369/#45583.

Related work: #32474 packs convolution with a separate output-layout kernel; #34299 integrates a native checkpoint backend; #45992 handles copies in the Triton KDA normalization path. This patch changes the existing convolution producer's store for the existing FlashInfer path, including graph execution.

## Accuracy Tests

Rebased and tested independently on main `def8f93212bd997ec19b1395e0d892b442374552`, B300, PyTorch 2.14.1+cu130, FlashInfer 0.7.2, Triton 3.8.0:

```bash
python -m pytest -q \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/mamba/test_causal_conv1d_split_output.py \
  test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_kda_prefill_graph.py::TestFlashInferKDAPrefillGraph
```

**5 tests and 12 subtests passed.** The new operator regression checks bit-exact output and state, unequal request lengths, strided input, padded block-table rows and changed-input graph replay. Existing KDA graph tests use their existing numerical tolerances; they are not described as bit-exact. A separate five-case microbench also passes bit-exact output/state/replay checks, including FP32 convolution weights at model dimensions. Pre-commit and `git diff --check` pass.

**Validation limitation:** isolated model-level accuracy remains pending. An earlier `d1bbcbdc` GLM-5.3-Flash experiment combining this change with the separate empty-view fix scored 1281/1319 on GSM8K versus baseline 1286/1319; both had four truncations and passed 12/12 long-context retrieval probes. Thirty-two fixed short-input teacher-forcing probes matched exactly, while long-input probes also varied between unchanged-baseline repeats. This does not establish the cause or an accuracy pass for this individual patch.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

Single B300, BF16 input, FP32 width-4 weights, no bias, local Q/K/V width 2048 each, input row stride 6416. CUDA-event medians of nine samples, alternating baseline/candidate order; each sample includes 100 invocations through CUDA-graph replay. Both arms use the same patched operator: the original output mode plus three contiguous copies versus the new split-output mode.

| Total tokens | Original convolution + Q/K/V copies | Split-output convolution | Speedup |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 1024 | 24.945 us | 10.272 us | 2.43x |
| 8192 | 180.952 us | 68.585 us | 2.64x |
| 16384 | 347.838 us | 130.748 us | 2.66x |

These new-main measurements cover this local path, not full-model latency or request throughput. The convolution-only kernel is not claimed to be 2.66x faster; eliminating the three layout copies supplies the improvement. No combined serving-throughput result is attributed to this PR.

<details>
<summary>Reproduce the 16K local timing</summary>

Run from this PR checkout with SGLang installed and one idle GPU:

```python
import statistics
import torch
from sglang.kernels.ops.mamba.causal_conv1d_triton import causal_conv1d_fn

torch.manual_seed(44)
lengths, h = [8192, 8192], 2048
m, dim = sum(lengths), 3 * h
x = torch.randn(m, dim + 272, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)[:, :dim]
w = torch.randn(dim, 4, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32) * 0.1
seed = torch.randn(4, 3, dim, device="cuda", dtype=torch.bfloat16)
states = [seed.clone().transpose(-1, -2) for _ in range(2)]
cu = torch.tensor([0, 8192, 16384], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int64)
slots = torch.tensor([2, 1], device="cuda", dtype=torch.int32)
initial = torch.tensor([False, True], device="cuda")

def run(split):
    out = causal_conv1d_fn(
        x.T, w, None, states[int(split)], cu, lengths, slots, initial,
        output_split_size=h if split else 0,
    )
    return tuple(out.unbind(0)) if split else tuple(
        t.contiguous() for t in out.T.chunk(3, dim=-1)
    )

before, after = run(False), run(True)
for a, b in zip(before, after):
    torch.testing.assert_close(a, b, rtol=0, atol=0)
torch.testing.assert_close(states[0], states[1], rtol=0, atol=0)
graphs = []
for split in (False, True):
    for _ in range(5):
        run(split)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    graph = torch.cuda.CUDAGraph()
    with torch.cuda.graph(graph):
        for _ in range(10):
            run(split)
    graphs.append(graph)
samples = [[], []]
for repeat in range(9):
    for index in ([0, 1] if repeat % 2 == 0 else [1, 0]):
        start, end = (torch.cuda.Event(enable_timing=True) for _ in range(2))
        start.record()
        for _ in range(10):
            graphs[index].replay()
        end.record()
        end.synchronize()
        samples[index].append(start.elapsed_time(end) * 1000 / 100)
print("baseline_us, split_us:", *map(statistics.median, samples))
```

</details>

## Checklist

- [x] Format code with pre-commit.
- [x] Add registered operator correctness tests.
- [x] Run existing FlashInfer KDA graph tests.
- [x] Provide scoped microbenchmarks and reproduction.
- [ ] Complete isolated model-level validation.

## Cleanup validation (2026-10-29)

Cleanup at `f5495a66`: clarified convolution-output naming and fixed the CPU hook fixture to initialize the KDA dispatcher and check the Q/K/V tuple contract. The fixture covers GDN, Triton KDA, equal-width FlashInfer planes, and unequal-width fallback. The old fixture reproduced `AttributeError: kernel_dispatcher`; the updated CPU file passed **5 tests and 11 subtests**. On RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell (SM120), split-output convolution and Triton graph tests passed **4 tests and 8 subtests**; the existing **4 FlashInfer graph tests were skipped because they require SM100/SM103**, not counted as passes. Production dispatch, convolution arithmetic, and kernel source are unchanged; changed-file pre-commit checks pass. Earlier B300 results above were not rerun.

title: [Perf] dsv41: Use the Engram all-to-all lookup for decode and CUDA graphs
author: hnyls2002
body:
Follow-up to #46917 and #46925.

- `auto` now uses the Engram `all_to_all` lookup for decode batches and inside CUDA graphs too, not only for eager prefill. Only a prefill batch of uneven per-rank counts captured in a CUDA graph keeps the earlier collective.
- Equal per-rank counts (MAX_LEN batches, CUDA graphs) take the fixed-size collectives, which a graph can capture: `all_gatherv` already reduces to an all-gather for them, and the exchange uses `reduce_scatter_tensor` or `all_to_all_single`; uneven counts keep the variable-size ones.
- `auto` is resolved in one place, `resolve_engram_config` in `engram.py`: once per process at model construction, when the parallel layout is final, and recorded in `engram_config` (log: `Engram lookup auto -> ...`). The layers run the resolved lookup, and the per-step `_dp_exchange` choice is gone; server-argument resolution only validates explicit values.
- The DP lookup is one method per exchange: `_dp_reduce_scatter_lookup` and `_dp_all_to_all_lookup` beside `_dp_global_buffer_lookup`.
- An explicit `reduce_scatter` or `all_to_all` now applies to decode as well; `all_reduce` keeps the collectives used before `auto`.
- Docs: `auto` and its decode measurements.

Behavior change: DP-attention decode on CUDA with columns that divide over the TP group moves from the reduce-scatter to the all-to-all; the output is bitwise the same.

## Measurements

GB300, one host-table Engram layer, rank 1, us per layer:

| DP | Tokens per rank | `all_reduce` (us) | `reduce_scatter` (us) | `all_to_all` (us) | `auto` (us) |
|---:|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2 | prefill 32K | 3,479.0 | 2,645.6 | 2,478.2 | 2,475.1 |
| 2 | decode 16 | 31.4 | 28.2 | 37.3 | 35.2 |
| 2 | decode 400 | 72.3 | 68.5 | 65.3 | 65.2 |
| 2 | decode 1,280 | 135.0 | 130.7 | 123.7 | 124.3 |
| 4 | prefill 32K | 5,861.4 | 3,819.1 | 2,463.2 | 2,460.4 |
| 4 | decode 16 | 49.6 | 33.7 | 42.1 | 41.6 |
| 4 | decode 400 | 105.5 | 101.2 | 69.2 | 70.1 |
| 4 | decode 1,280 | 193.3 | 187.1 | 130.5 | 131.2 |

Before this PR, decode used the reduce-scatter. In a decode microbenchmark under CUDA graphs on GB300, B300 and H200 (DP 2-8, 16 to 1,280 tokens per rank), `all_to_all` was faster in 35 of 48 shapes: from DP 4 it was up to 48% faster and at most 12 us behind at 64 tokens per rank or fewer; at DP 2 it was at most 20 us behind and up to 53 us ahead.

## Verification

- Bitwise check of the `EngramEmbedding` DP lookup on GB300 at DP 2 and 4, every `lookup` choice against `all_reduce`: prefill (uniform, skewed, one empty rank) and decode captured in a CUDA graph and replayed with new ids. All equal.
- `test_deepseek_v41_flash_gb300_dp2ep2.py` on GB300: passed, GSM8K 0.98, MMMU-Pro 0.79.
- The same recipe at attention DP 4 / EP 4, GSM8K: 0.985.

body:

## Motivation

<!-- Describe the purpose and goals of this pull request. -->
AITER varlen routed every varlen call on gfx942 to AITER's Triton kernel, working around a hang on MiniMax-H3's packed sequences reported in #33275. The condition was architecture alone, with no shape, length or head-count qualifier, so MI300X/MI325X never reached the FAv3 kernel for any model or any shape.

The hang does not reproduce. 
Across every varlen shape H3 submits, all four Ulysses degrees, 28K to 104K rows, including the zero-length second segment that occurs whenever the used length is a multiple of 64, the FAv3 kernel completes and is 6.6-27% faster (median 15.1%), matching the Triton output to bf16 accumulation noise. 

Also enables RTZ rounding mode for varlen as well, similar to how it's enabled for non-varlen. Affects only gfx942 and gives a boost in perf like in #28650. Safe to enable for non-gfx942 systems as well - it's just ignored.

| H3 | A length threshold | Ruled out | Clean at 1024–104448 |
| H4 | Odd head count (Ulysses8 leaves 7) | Ruled out | Clean at 1, 7, 8, 14, 28, 56 heads |
| H5 | Workaround is stale | Consistent with all of the above | — |

| `[0, 16384, 16384]` | 16384 | 0 | OK |

| `[0, 16384]` | 16384 | — | OK |
| `[0, 65536]` | 65536 | — | OK |

### Head sweep @ 65536 rows, `[0, N, N]`

| heads | ASM |
|---|---|
| 1 | OK |
| 7 | OK |
| 8 | OK |
| 14 | OK |
| 28 | OK |
| 56 | OK |

| workload | rows | tail | u1 (56h) | u2 (28h) | u4 (14h) | u8 (7h) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

## Motivation

On the owned DSA DCP route from [#44322](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/44322), every MLA layer all-gathers the full-head query (`[T, H, 576]`) before attention, in decode and in every DSA extend, and the a2a merge ships each head's partial at `kv_lora_rank` (512) wide. This PR removes the query all-gather and halves the a2a payload, without changing what attention computes:

- **Q replication**: every rank holds the whole DCP group's `q_b_proj` and `w_kc`, so it projects all query heads locally. `--dcp-replicate-q-proj` (already on by default for DeepSeek-family models on the a2a backend) now also covers DSA extend on HIP, not just decode.
- **Project before merge**: the LSE merge is linear in the partial output, so every partial is V-projected first and the a2a carries `v_head_dim` (256) instead of `kv_lora_rank` (512) per head.

## Correctness

MI355X, `amd/GLM-5.2-MXFP4`, TP4/EP4 + DCP4, FP8 KV, MTP (EAGLE, 5 steps, 6 draft tokens), real draft acceptance. Both columns were measured on the same day with the same scripts.

| check | #44322 (b8a0a1ac70) | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| passkey 8K / 34K / 96K (3 depths each) | 3/3, 3/3, 3/3 | 3/3, 3/3, 3/3 |
| GSM8K (400 questions, few-shot) | 0.953 | 0.945 / 0.940 (two runs) |
| GSM8K (1319 questions, few-shot) | 0.935 | 0.933 |
| MTP accept length (4 prompts x 400 tokens, greedy) | 3.23 | 3.26 |
| NLL, last 2K tokens of a 48K prompt | 1.232 | 1.236 / 1.227 (two runs) |
| KV capacity (tokens) | 8.89M | 8.89M |

Two values are two runs on the same server: GSM8K 400 moves by up to ±0.02 between runs, NLL by about ±0.01.

Kernel tests (`test_dcp_qrep_hip.py`): `head_bmm` matches `torch.bmm` for the absorb and V-projection shapes, and project-then-merge matches merge-then-project.

## Performance

**Fixed-length probes** on a 131K cached prefix, simulated AL 3.61:

| probe | #44322 | this PR | change |
|---|---|---|---|
| extend 2K (TTFT) | 331 ms | 287 ms | −13% |
| extend 4.6K | 584 ms | 485 ms | −17% |
| extend 12K | 1267 ms | 1007 ms | −21% |
| extend 32K | 3509 ms | 2844 ms | −19% |
| fresh 131K prefill | 12.87 s | 10.30 s | −20% |
| decode, 16 users (tok/s/user) | 84.7 | 87.1 | +2.8% |
| decode, 24 users (tok/s/user) | 70.0 | 72.4 | +3.4% |

**InferenceX agentic replay**, TP4/EP4 + DCP4 with MTP (simulated AL 3.61), 1 h per point, same server arguments as the #44322 table. The #44322 rows are its "after" numbers.

#44322: 10/28/2026 commit b8a0a1ac70
This PR: 10/28/2026 commit e25d76df7b
| Conc | Config | P90 Interactivity (tok/s/user) | TPUT per Chip (tok/s/GPU) | Chip Cache Hit Rate | CPU Cache Hit Rate | Theoretical Cache Hit Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 16 | #44322 | 41.19 | 17,196 | 96.7% | — | 97.0% |
| 16 | this PR | **51.38** | **18,125** | 96.6% | — | 96.9% |
| 24 | #44322 | 31.32 | 23,416 | 96.8% | — | 97.3% |
| 24 | this PR | **36.05** | **25,151** | 96.9% | — | 97.3% |
| 40 | #44322 | 16.79 | 24,740 | 95.5% | — | 97.0% |
| 40 | this PR | **19.70** | **26,583** | 95.0% | — | 97.0% |
| 48 | #44322 | 2.56 | 10,774 | 82.6% | — | 96.1% |
| 48 | this PR | **3.18** | **12,819** | 81.9% | — | 96.4% |

- P90 interactivity is 1.15–1.25x of #44322 at every point, and throughput per GPU 1.05–1.07x at c16–c40.
- The gain comes mostly from prefill (extend 13–21% faster above), which shortens the decode stalls behind each prefill batch. Decode itself is about 3% faster.
- At c48 the DCP pool is still full (chip hit rate 82%), so P90 stays low; throughput per GPU is 1.19x because each recomputed prefix costs less.

## Modifications

- **Replicate `q_b_proj` / `w_kc` across the DCP group** (`model_runner.py`, `forward_mla.py`)
    - The model runner all-gathers `q_b_proj` and `w_kc` once before graph capture. The local `q_b_proj` weight then aliases its own slice of the replica, so replication adds `(W-1)/W` of the weight instead of doubling it.
    - GLM keeps `w_kc` / `w_vc` as per-tensor FP8 on gfx95; they are dequantized to bf16 before the gather instead of skipping the layer.
    - `is_dcp_q_replicate_phase` also returns true for DSA extend on HIP, so prefill skips the Q all-gather too.
- **Project before merge** (`forward_mla_rocm.py`, `deepseek_v2.py`)
    - With the a2a backend and an unquantized `o_proj`, each rank V-projects the partials of every group head with the replicated `w_vc` before the a2a, and the merged result goes straight to `o_proj`.
- **Token-major absorb** (`forward_mla_rocm.py`, `dcp_kernels.py`)
    - The absorb bmm writes `[T, H, kv_lora_rank]` directly instead of transposing a head-major result. A small Triton per-head bmm (`head_bmm`) serves batches up to 288 tokens; larger ones use `torch.bmm` on transposed views.

Scope: Without `--dcp-size > 1` nothing changes. The new extend path is gated on `is_hip()` and DSA; CUDA keeps the decode-only behavior. `--no-dcp-replicate-q-proj` restores the old route. No new environment variables.

## Checklist

- [x] `pre-commit`
- [x] Kernel tests (`test_dcp_qrep_hip.py`), and the existing DCP kernel/unit tests
- [x] GLM-5.2 DCP4 end-to-end sanity (passkey up to 96K, NLL)
- [x] GSM8K, this PR vs. #44322
- [x] Agentic replay at c16 / c24 / c40 / c48
