body:
[Feat] [AMD] custom-all-reduce: Run the JIT custom all-reduce v2 on ROCm

<!-- Thank you for your contribution! Please follow these guidelines to enhance your pull request. If anything is unclear, submit your PR and reach out to maintainers for assistance. Join our Slack community at https://slack.sglang.io to discuss further. -->

## Motivation

`CustomAllReduceV2` (the JIT custom all-reduce, "carv2") only runs on NVIDIA today. On AMD the custom all-reduce is AITER's (or the legacy AOT one), so ROCm gets neither carv2's Lamport push algorithms nor the push/pull communicator planes the fused collectives are built on.

The push algorithms matter most for decode-sized all-reduces: on 8x MI350X, carv2 `1shot_push` is 20-37% faster than AITER at 4-64 KB, and carv2 matches or beats AITER up to 4 MB (table below).

This PR makes carv2 build and run correctly on ROCm (gfx950) and tunes its launch geometry for MI350X. It does **not** change ROCm dispatch: `dispatch_custom_allreduce` still selects AITER on AMD, so serving behavior is unchanged until a follow-up enables v2 there with tuned thresholds. CUDA behavior is unchanged.

## Modifications

Two commits: the ROCm port, then the MI350X block/thread tuning.

**Symmetric workspace over HIP VMM + POSIX fds** (`srt/utils/hip_vmm_utils.py`, new)
- `HipSymmetricBuffer`: one `hipMemCreate` allocation per rank (`hipMemAllocationTypeUncached`, POSIX-fd handle type), exported as an fd, exchanged with the existing `exchange_posix_fds` (`SCM_RIGHTS`), imported and mapped into every peer, and exposed as per-rank uint8 tensors on the local device. It replaces torch symmetric memory on ROCm and needs no FABRIC handle and no multicast.
- Chunked fallback: some amdgpu/KFD drivers reject a VA-less VRAM allocation whose `[0, size)` overlaps an SVM range, which RCCL init can leave in Python's low brk heap (dmesg: `Address: 0x0 already allocated by SVM`); every later large allocation then fails as out of memory with the GPU nearly empty. On that failure the buffer is built from smaller handles mapped back to back, and the handled error is cleared from `hipGetLastError` so torch does not report it later.
- All ranks agree on allocation success before the fd exchange, so a failure raises everywhere instead of hanging peers.

**JIT kernels under hipcc** (`ptx.cuh`, `custom_all_reduce.cuh`, `utils.cuh`)
- HIP implementations of the `ptx::` vocabulary behind `#ifdef USE_ROCM` (the CUDA PTX is untouched): system-scope `__builtin_amdgcn_global_{load,store}_b128` for peer-visible 16B accesses, `__hip_atomic_*` for flag traffic, `__builtin_amdgcn_fence` for fences, and traps for multimem (no multicast on ROCm).
- The local Lamport poll uses agent scope (`sc1`). The uncached workspace is still L2-cached by its owner, with peer writes over XGMI invalidating the line by probe. A single-thread signal fence keeps the poll in the loop: without it LLVM treats the b128 builtin as a pure read and deletes the spin loop.
- `2shot_pull`: every wave issues a system-scope release before the block barrier. On gfx950 `s_barrier` does not drain a wave's outstanding stores and the signalling thread's release only covers its own wave; without this, graph replays rarely read stale reduced shards (1 bad replay in 200 at TP6).
- `utils.cuh`: add the missing `cudaMemcpyDeviceToDevice` / `cudaGetDevice` HIP aliases.

**`CustomAllReduceV2` on ROCm** (`custom_all_reduce_v2.py`, `configs/custom_all_reduce_v2.py`)
- `_allocate_symmetric_memory` returns `(owner, per-rank views, multicast VA)` and uses `HipSymmetricBuffer` on ROCm; `has_multicast` is False there.
- No graph zero-copy input registration on ROCm (the 2-shot graph path would store into peers' cached input buffers, which XGMI does not keep coherent); captured all-reduces stage through the workspace. `IPCManager` is only built when graph registration can happen.
- ROCm gets its own tuning table instead of falling into the SM90 table because gfx950 reports capability 9.5.
- Gate: on ROCm, `can_use_custom_all_reduce_v2` disables v2 with a warning when the loaded HIP runtime (`hipRuntimeGetVersion` on the `libamdhip64` torch loaded) is older than `MIN_HIP_VERSION = (7, 2)`, the oldest validated. ROCm 10.x ships HIP 7.16+.

**MI350X launch geometry** (second commit). Swept grid size x threads per block x message size at TP2/4/6/8, two runs per point (median run-to-run spread 1.3%):
- `num_pull_blocks = 32` in the ROCm table instead of one block per CU. Each pull block runs its own cross-GPU barrier, so 256 blocks spend most of a pull all-reduce on flag traffic; 32 blocks make `2shot_pull` 39-65% and `1shot_pull` 35-51% (from 1 MB) faster at TP8, and are within a few % of the best grid at TP2/4/6. The existing thread rule stays within ~3% of the best block size at this grid.
- `1shot_push` launches 1024 threads per block from 128 KB on ROCm (TP8 -7 to -11% at 128-256 KB, -8% at 1 MB; TP4/6 -4 to -8%; neutral below 128 KB).
- The push grid stays at one block per CU: `2shot_push`, which covers the mid range, is best or within ~2% there at every world size, and the push grid is bound to the counter array.
- Size thresholds are unchanged (follow-up).

**Tests**
- `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py`: the HIP runtime gate (7.0/7.1 rejected before topology checks, 7.2/7.17 admitted).
- `test_custom_all_reduce.py`: graph capture uses `capture_error_mode="thread_local"`; the reference NCCL group's watchdog thread queries events during capture, which fails under global capture mode on ROCm.

## Accuracy Tests

Kernel-level, bit-exact against RCCL (`atol=0, rtol=0`) on 8x MI350X, ROCm 7.2 (HIP 7.2.26015), image `lmsysorg/sglang:v0.5.22-rocm724-mi35x`, on the final branch:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `test_custom_all_reduce.py --num-gpu 2,4,6,8` with `SGLANG_JIT_KERNEL_RUN_FULL_TESTS=1` (4 algos x eager/graph x fp16/bf16/fp32 x 16 B-8 MB) | 310 passed per world size |
| `test_custom_all_reduce_v2_capability.py` | 13 passed |
| Back-to-back stress, no host sync, random algo/size interleaving (eager), and CUDA-graph replay, each also with RCCL initialized before carv2 (exercises the chunked VMM path) | 0 mismatches at TP8 (also TP2/4/6 before the tuning commit) |

No model-level accuracy run: ROCm dispatch does not select v2 in this PR, so model outputs are unchanged.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

8x MI350X, TP8, bf16, CUDA-graph mode (16 all-reduces per graph), us per all-reduce (max over ranks), median of 3 runs; every column from the same runs. Bold is the fastest custom all-reduce (AITER or carv2).

| Size | RCCL | AITER | carv2 1shot_push | carv2 2shot_push | carv2 1shot_pull | carv2 2shot_pull | best carv2 vs AITER |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 KB | 14.5 | 5.3 | **4.2** | 6.7 | 6.9 | 10.0 | -20% |
| 16 KB | 14.4 | 5.6 | **4.4** | 7.0 | 7.2 | 11.0 | -23% |
| 64 KB | 14.3 | 8.7 | **5.5** | 7.3 | 7.9 | 11.2 | -37% |
| 128 KB | 14.1 | 7.3 | **7.1** | 7.5 | 9.4 | 11.4 | -3% |
| 256 KB | 16.7 | **7.6** | 10.6 | 7.8 | 11.9 | 12.1 | +3% |
| 512 KB | 21.7 | **8.7** | 16.4 | 8.7 | 16.8 | 13.1 | +0% |
| 1 MB | 25.0 | 11.3 | 28.0 | **10.3** | 26.0 | 16.4 | -9% |
| 2 MB | 31.2 | 16.7 | 49.2 | **16.4** | 44.0 | 23.2 | -2% |
| 4 MB | 48.5 | 25.8 | 90.6 | **25.3** | 83.8 | 36.6 | -2% |
| 8 MB | 73.1 | **44.5** | 172.3 | 49.0 | 158.7 | 64.5 | +10% |
| 16 MB | 112.0 | **82.6** | 333.5 | 90.8 | 306.8 | 122.1 | +10% |

carv2 is faster than RCCL at every size. Against AITER, `1shot_push` wins up to 128 KB (20-37% up to 64 KB), `2shot_push` ties at 256-512 KB, leads at 1 MB (-9%) and ties at 2-4 MB, and carv2 trails by ~10% at 8 MB and up.

Effect of the MI350X tuning commit (same setup; before = first commit, push medians of 3 runs, pull 1 run):

| Size | 1shot_push | 2shot_push | 1shot_pull | 2shot_pull |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 4 KB | 4.1 -> 4.2 (+2%) | 6.9 -> 6.7 (-3%) | 6.8 -> 6.9 (+1%) | 19.8 -> 10.0 (-50%) |
| 64 KB | 5.6 -> 5.5 (-2%) | 7.3 -> 7.3 (-0%) | 8.2 -> 7.9 (-3%) | 21.7 -> 11.2 (-48%) |
| 128 KB | 7.7 -> 7.1 (-7%) | 7.6 -> 7.5 (-1%) | 9.8 -> 9.4 (-4%) | 22.0 -> 11.4 (-48%) |
| 256 KB | 12.0 -> 10.6 (-11%) | 7.8 -> 7.8 (+0%) | 12.6 -> 11.9 (-5%) | 28.9 -> 12.1 (-58%) |
| 1 MB | 30.5 -> 28.0 (-8%) | 10.4 -> 10.3 (-1%) | 40.1 -> 26.0 (-35%) | 46.1 -> 16.4 (-65%) |
| 4 MB | 92.4 -> 90.6 (-2%) | 25.3 -> 25.3 (-0%) | 170.0 -> 83.8 (-51%) | 60.2 -> 36.6 (-39%) |
| 16 MB | 337.2 -> 333.5 (-1%) | 90.8 -> 90.8 (+0%) | 568.7 -> 306.8 (-46%) | 212.2 -> 122.1 (-42%) |

Even tuned, the pull algorithms trail `2shot_push` (1 MB: 16.4 vs 10.3 us), so the ROCm thresholds should route 1-16 MB to `2shot_push` rather than `2shot_pull`. Retuning the thresholds and enabling v2 in ROCm dispatch are follow-ups.

## Checklist

- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Localize DeepGEMM Mega MoE weights across locality domains
author: zcnrex
body:
## Motivation

On GPUs with two locality domains, DeepGEMM's Mega MoE gives rows `[d * N / 2, (d + 1) * N / 2)` of every expert to domain `d`'s SMs. With `deep_gemm.localize`, those rows also live in domain `d`'s memory, so weight reads stay local. DeepGEMM takes localized weights since sgl-project/DeepGEMM#119 (native CUDA 13.4 locality domains); this PR wires it into SGLang behind an opt-in env var.

`deep_gemm.localize` returns `(domains, experts, N / domains, K)` tensors, but the expert parameters are also read in two places outside Mega MoE:
- The deep-ep path above `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK` (`DeepseekV2MoE.forward` falls through when `should_use_mega_moe` is false).
- EPLB, which slices every routed-expert parameter by expert. A domain-major tensor fails `filter_moe_weight_param_global_expert`'s `shape[0] == num_local_experts`, so EPLB would silently move the scales but not the weights.

This PR keeps EPLB working and makes the token cap explicit.

## Modifications

- `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_LOCALIZE` (default off), applied on compute capability 10.7 only.
- `build_mega_moe_experts_weights`: localizes the interleaved L1 and the L2 weights. The kernel gets the domain-major tensors (`mega_l1_weights` / `mega_l2_weights`); `w13_weight` / `w2_weight` hold the expert-major `(experts, domains, N / domains, K)` view of the same memory, so every `get_moe_weights` keeps slicing by expert. No second copy of the weights.
- `build_mega_moe_shared_weights`: localizes the fused shared expert's L1 / L2 (DeepGEMM requires shared and routed weights to agree).
- `update_expert_weights_single_layer`: P2P needs each expert's slice dense, and a localized expert's halves live in different domains. Such a tensor is sent from a contiguous staging copy (one message per expert, like every other tensor) and received into a contiguous temp buffer; its weight, temp buffer and staging copy are viewed as int64 once when all three allow it. Every other tensor is moved exactly as before.
- `should_use_mega_moe`: with localized weights there is no non-mega fallback, so tokens above the cap assert with the same message pattern as Kimi K3.
- `test/manual/test_expert_location_updater.py`: the exchanged weights include an expert-major view of padded domain-major storage, so staged sends go through P2P. Passes with gloo (8 and 32 ranks) and NCCL (4 GPUs); with the previous updater NCCL rejects it (`Tensors for P2P must be non-overlapping and dense`).

Setting the env var requires sgl-deep-gemm >= 0.2.4 built with CUDA >= 13.4 (the cu134 image builds it from source).

## Accuracy and speed

DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, one node, DP-attention 4 / EP 4, `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe`, DSPARK, main e152f531d9 + this PR, sgl-deep-gemm v0.2.5.post3 built with CUDA 13.4, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_NUM_MAX_TOKENS_PER_RANK=16384`.

GSM8K (200 questions):

| Localize | EPLB | First commit | Head |
|---|---|---|---|
| off | off | 0.990 | 0.990 |
| on | off | 0.995 | 0.990 |
| off | on, 32 redundant experts, rebalance every 100 iterations | 0.995 | 0.980 |
| on | on, same; 5 rebalances during the eval, `SGLANG_EXPERT_LOCATION_UPDATER_CANARY=1` | 0.995 | 0.995 |

Decode, 128K-token context, output throughput (sum of per-DP medians), interleaved off / on / on / off:

| Batch | On vs off |
|---|---|
| 128 | +2.6% |
| 224 | +0.9% |

Both "on" runs beat both "off" runs at each batch size.

EPLB weight update, one layer on 4 GPUs (104 physical experts per rank, shuffled placement, `update_expert_weights_single_layer`, median of 36): localized weights take +3.5% vs plain weights, and plain weights are unchanged from main. Moving each domain's slice as its own message instead cost +22%: the update is dominated by per-message overhead, not bytes. In the server, a rebalance took 13.5% longer localized than plain (mean of 5 each, same run). Transient memory during a rebalance grows by the staging copy of the localized tensors (about 2% of weight memory at 104 experts per rank).

Memory: the routed experts keep one copy (the localized one). Weight memory reads 1.7% higher and KV capacity 1.47% lower: the original routed weights are freed from PyTorch segments shared with other weights, and those holes cannot be returned to the driver. The fused shared expert's L2 is held twice, as the original stays for the shared-expert linear.

`test_waterfill_eplb.py` passes.

## Not covered

- Prefill throughput (Mega MoE prefill showed no gain in earlier kernel measurements; not re-measured).
- Elastic EP's reload of missing experts from disk and `update_weights_from_disk` into localized parameters.
- Multi-node EPLB (only single-node P2P was exercised).

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] moe: Re-land the JIT moe_finalize_fuse_shared with the shared row read after the PDL wait
author: DarkSharpness
body:
> (auto generated by Claude)
> (auto generated by MyGO (Make your GPU-kernel Optimal) agent)

## What

Re-lands #47784 (the JIT `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`, reverted by #47994) with one fix: the shared-expert row is now read after `PDLWaitPrimary`. The routing tensors still load before the wait when `routing_ready=True`. It also drops the device guard #47784 added around the launch.

cc @hnyls2002 @BBuf

## Why the revert happened

#47994 suspected the early `shared_output` load, and that is the cause. `shared_output` is written by the shared expert on `alt_stream` and joined with `wait_stream` before the finalize. In a CUDA graph, that cross-stream join into a PDL launch is a programmatic edge as well, so a shared expert that triggers its dependents early lets the finalize start before the row is written. Only the PDL wait orders it.

Reproduced on B300 with a shared-expert stand-in on a side stream that triggers at entry and spins 300 us before writing, joined with `wait_stream`, followed by the PDL finalize:

| kernel | eager | CUDA graph | eager, PDL writer | CUDA graph, PDL writer |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #47784 | 0/20 wrong | 0/20 | 0/20 | 20/20 wrong |
| this PR | 0/20 | 0/20 | 0/20 | 0/20 |

The reproduction needs a purpose-built early-triggering writer kernel, so it is not added as a registered test.

## Performance

B300, hidden 7168, top-k 8, bf16 with fp32 weights, CUDA graph behind a real PDL producer that triggers before its final stores. Finalize cost = pair time minus producer-only time, medians of 2 x 15 replays.

| | this PR vs #47784 | this PR vs the pre-#47784 kernel on main |
|---|---|---|
| warm (the shared row was just written, in L2) | within +-0.04 us at 1-8192 tokens | 1 token -0.65 us, 32-128 tokens -1.5 to -2.9 us, 4096-8192 tokens equal |
| cold (rotated buffers) | +0.12 / +0.23 us at 64 / 128 tokens, about 0 elsewhere | 32-128 tokens -2.6 to -6.5 us |
| without PDL | about 0 | |

Issuing the shared load right after the wait is as fast as or faster than issuing it in use order (after the gathers): for one-wave grids ptxas places it after the gathers either way, and the persistent kernel is up to 0.6 us faster with the early issue.

## Tests

`test_moe_finalize_fuse_shared.py` on B300: 132 passed, 6 skipped (unchanged from #47784). SASS: the shared `LDG.E.128` is after the grid-dependency wait; no stack or spills in any instance.

Needs before merge: `/rerun-test` of the nightly `test_dsa_glm52_hisparse.py` on 8-gpu-b200, which caught the regression and is not part of the per-PR runs.

title: [Refactor] env: Dispatch on the GPU architecture instead of env vars that restate it
author: BBuf
body:
## Motivation

SGLang declares about 910 environment variables (819 in `srt/environ.py`, 91 in `multimodal_gen/envs.py`) and reads about 115 more raw. Many of them only restate the hardware: a path that is valid on one GPU and must be switched on by hand there, or a kill switch for a path that is already gated by architecture. This PR deletes those and decides at the read site from the GPU itself (`sglang.kernels.arch.current_arch()` / the platform helpers).

Rules used for every variable:

- **Selector that restates the hardware**: deleted; the read site checks the architecture.
- **Kill switch of a default-on, architecture-gated path**: deleted; the path keeps its existing gate. Kept when a doc tells users to set it, or a CI test uses it as the A/B control (listed below).
- **Default-off fast path for one architecture**: only the five with the strongest evidence are turned on: the cookbook already sets them on exactly that hardware, and GSM8K was checked wherever a checkpoint was available. The rest stay opt-in.

Wrong architecture gates and env bugs found during the audit are fixed here too.

**41 variables deleted** (33 declared, 8 read raw); 4 are now declared or read under their documented name.

## Behavior changes (please review these first)

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4 on gfx950 | `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM`, `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_FUSED_INVROPE`, `SGLANG_HIP_DSV4_C4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP` (and `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_FLYDSL_MXFP8` for V4.1) had to be set; every MI355X cookbook cell set them | On by default on gfx95 / gfx950 when the kernel is available. `FUSED_INVROPE` stays an opt-in on CUDA |
| DSA `flashmla_sparse_q8` (SM90) | Per-row top-k length behind `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_TOPK_LENGTH` | Always on (bit-exact by construction: skipped blocks hold only `-1` pads) |
| MiniMax-H3 VAE | The fused residual-add + RMSNorm ran at every quality level, including `exact`, though it is not bit-exact | Runs only at `lossless` / `high`; `exact` output now equals the unfused path byte for byte |
| `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_TENSOR_CORE` | Compared to `"true"`, so `=1` turned tensor cores **off** | Parsed as a boolean; unset keeps the heuristic |
| `SGLANG_FORCE_SHUTDOWN`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP` | Documented under these names, read as `SGL_FORCE_SHUTDOWN` / `SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP`, so the documented name did nothing | Read through `envs`; the old names still work as deprecated aliases |
| `SGLANG_USE_DEEPGEMM_BMM` | `not DEEPGEMM_BLACKWELL` let SM120/121 into DeepGEMM's SM90 masked/einsum kernels; dots3 had no gate | Requires SM90 (MUSA keeps its path) |
| MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 native stack | `is_blackwell` (majors 10-12) selected MSA-v1 kernels that build for SM10x only | SM10x only |
| DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer | `major >= 10` sent SM120 into the DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4` path, which raised at build time | SM100 family only; SM120 gets the torch / Triton paths |
| DSA backend | TRT-LLM workspace allocated on SM120, where the kernel raises "Unsupported architecture" | Allocated on SM10x only |
| DeepSeek-V4 model hooks | The ROCm block overwrote 9 variables unconditionally; `SGLANG_OPT_USE_TOPK_V2` on SM120 and `SGLANG_OPT_FLASHMLA_SPARSE_PREFILL` on ROCm overwrote user values | Values the user set are kept; sets equal to the default, or for variables nothing reads on that platform, are removed |
| MegaMoE on ROCm | `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` without `SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE=1` ran DeepGEMM, which has no ROCm kernels | megamoe on ROCm is aiter MegaMoEv2 |
| DSpark on NPU | Needed `SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL=0` | Chosen by platform |
| smallm router, smallm FP8 block-scale GEMM | Admitted any `gfx95*` | `gfx950` exactly, like the other smallm kernels |
| gfx1250 MXFP4 MoE | Every recipe and test had to set `AITER_FORCE_A8W4=1` | SGLang's own decisions key on gfx1250, and startup sets the variable for aiter on gfx1250 when unset |
| DGX Spark DeepSeek-V4 recipe | Selected the `b12x` FlashMLA backend, which main does not have | Removed from the recipe |

## Deleted variables

**Restate the hardware (decided at the read site)**

| Variable | Now |
|---|---|
| `SGLANG_DEEPGEMM_ON_H20` | SM90 with 78 SMs (H20 / H20-3e) |
| `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_INDEXER` | `is_hip()` |
| `SGLANG_AMD_USE_FLYDSL_MEGA_MOE` | ROCm + `--moe-a2a-backend megamoe` |
| `SGLANG_DSPARK_FAST_KERNEL` | `not is_npu()` |
| `SGLANG_DSPARK_SHARDED_ACCEPT` | `is_hip()` |
| `SGLANG_OPT_USE_AITER_BATCHED_GEMM`, `SGLANG_OPT_HIP_FLYDSL_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_HIP_DSV4_C4_INDEXER_ROWGROUP`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_DSA_Q8KV8_TOPK_LENGTH` | On for their architecture (table above) |

**Kill switches of default-on, architecture-gated paths (path and gate kept)**

- NVIDIA: `SGLANG_FA4_TMEM_LOAD_RED_MAX`, `SGLANG_HICACHE_TMA_TRANSFER`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_BF16_SPLITK_GEMM`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_MUSE_SPARK_FINALIZE_AR`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA_V1_Q8KV4`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_FP8_GEMM_CONFIG_TUNE`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_MINIMAX_FP8_Q_EPILOGUE`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_LFM_FUSED_CONV`, `SGLANG_OPT_DSV41_FAST_DECODE_INDEXER`, `SGLANG_DSV41_FUSED_WO_A`, `SGLANG_OPT_DEEPGEMM_MEGA_MOE_FUSE_SHARED_EXPERTS`, `SGLANG_EXPERIMENTAL_DSA_KPOOL_METADATA_FUSION`
- ROCm: `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX115_WEIGHT_PADDING`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_SPLITKV_VERIFY`, `SGLANG_TRITON_DENSE_PREFILL_ATTN`, `SGLANG_EXACT_CHUNK_FILL`, `SGLANG_ENABLE_QUARK_MXFP4_MOE_W4A16`, `SGLANG_GFX1250_W4A8_MOE`, `SGLANG_MOE_SHUFFLE_GFX1250`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_PROJ`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_ROUTER`, `SGLANG_ROCM_KDA_HIP_PREFILL`, `SGLANG_ASM_VERIFY_ATTN`, `SGLANG_DP_MASK_PAD_ROWS`, `SGLANG_HIP_SHARED_ACT_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_HIP_WO_A_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_HIP_FFN_NORM_MXFP8`, `SGLANG_OPT_USE_FUSED_QK_NORM_ROPE`

Tests that flipped one of these now patch the gate instead (for example the FA4 sm_103 test builds the FMNMX kernel with `tmem_load_red_max=False`), so no comparison was lost.

**Nothing read them:** `SGLANG_NGRAM_FORCE_GREEDY_VERIFY`, `SGLANG_DATA_PARALLEL_BUDGET_INTERVAL`, `SGLANG_USE_BREAKABLE_CUDA_GRAPH` (written by `--debug-cuda-graph`, never read; the BCG doc now points at `--cuda-graph-backend-decode breakable`).

**Diffusion:** `MINIMAX_H3_VAE_DECODER_FUSED_NORM` (now the quality gate).

## Kept on purpose

- Documented escape hatches / CI A/B controls: `SGLANG_DISABLE_MSA`, `SGLANG_K3_SP_COLLECTIVE`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_FUSED_AR_QUANT`, `SGLANG_AITER_GFX942_BLOCKSCALE_USE_CK`, `SGLANG_DISABLE_GFX1250_FP8_GEMM`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_MOE`, `SGLANG_ROCM_DISABLE_AITER_TOPK_GATING`, `SGLANG_ROCM_SMALLM_FP8_BS` (now also gated on gfx950).
- `SGLANG_AITER_CAPTURE_COPY_IN` stays off. #43077 moved it from on to off on purpose and scoped it to the DeepSeek-V4.1 MI355X DP-attention recipe. It is now declared, and its comment no longer says the opposite of the default. On Qwen3-30B-A3B TP4 / DP4 DP-attention on MI350X, turning it on costs about 2.7% output throughput with the same GSM8K.
- The other default-off candidates stay opt-in. The closest to ready are `SGLANG_OPT_SM120_MTP_ROUTER_TOP22` (bit-exact, needs a re-benchmark) and `SGLANG_ENABLE_FP8_BLOCK_GEMV` (needs an H200 accuracy run).

## For the owners (not changed here)

- The DGX Spark DeepSeek-V4 cells are still `verified: true`, but they use the preview image and `--moe-runner-backend b12x`, which main does not have.
- MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 still keys on `is_blackwell` in `model_overrides/minimax_m3.py` and `quantization/minimax_m3_nvfp4.py`, so SM12x end to end is unsupported. This PR only stops SM12x from selecting MSA-v1.
- `single_batch_overlap.py` uses `not is_blackwell()` for the Hopper paths; switching to `is_sm(9)` would change HIP / MUSA with SBO, so it is left alone.
- The gfx950 V4.1 multi-stream branch from #41308 has never run in a server: the ROCm hook already turned `SGLANG_OPT_USE_MULTI_STREAM_OVERLAP` off. It stays off by default, and setting it to 1 now works.
- DeepGEMM `fp8_fp4_mqa_logits` also runs on SM120; the V4.1 prefill indexer could re-admit SM120 there.
- With `SGLANG_FA4_TMEM_LOAD_RED_MAX` gone there is no runtime switch back to FMNMX. Two benchmark rounds on GB300 showed `ld.red` about 5-7% slower on d64 ViT shapes and 3-10% faster on d72 / d80.

## Validation

Every changed read site was tested on base (`27aedf7f93`) and on this branch, on the hardware it runs on.

**Full sweep.** All 1,561 files under `test/registered/unit` and `multimodal_gen/test/unit`, plus the kernel tests this PR touches. Each file ran in its own process on both trees, and every failure seen only on the branch was rerun serially on both.

| Hardware | Failing only on the branch | Import / collect |
|---|---|---|
| H200 (sm_90) | 0 | identical |
| GB300 (sm_103) | 0 (3 port-in-use failures in the parallel run pass serially) | identical (+2 tests) |
| RTX 5090 (sm_120) | 0 | identical |
| MI350X (gfx950, ROCm 7.2) | 0 (13 port-in-use failures in the parallel run pass serially) | identical |

**Accuracy** (sgl-eval 0.1.3, GSM8K). DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4, 200 questions, temperature 0.6, top-p 0.95, max tokens 8192. Base runs the recipe with the deleted variables set; the branch runs it without them:

| Setup | Base | Branch | New default path seen |
|---|---|---|---|
| GB300, cookbook FP4 low-latency | 98.0% | 97.5% | same command |
| MI350X, MI355X FP4 low-latency | 97.5% | 97.0% | `aiter::inverse_rope_group_quant_kernel` in the trace |
| MI350X, plus `--enable-deepseek-v4-fp4-indexer` | 97.0% | 98.0% | row-group FP4 MQA logits kernel logged on every rank |
| MI350X, `SGLANG_OPT_FP8_WO_A_GEMM=false` (the CI setting) | 98.0% | 98.5% | `_batched_gemm_bf16_kernel` in the trace |

Qwen3-30B-A3B-Instruct-2507 on MI350X (TP4, DP4 DP-attention, TP MoE; all 1,319 questions, temperature 0.7): 0.9598 / 0.9545 with `SGLANG_USE_ROCM700A=0` and 0.9591 / 0.9598 with the image default (base / branch). Output throughput is within 1%.

**Targeted checks**
- MiniMax-H3 VAE on H200 with real weights: `exact` is now byte-identical to the unfused path (base differed by up to 1.36e-2), and `lossless` / `high` are byte-identical to base.
- FA4 on sm_103: `test_flash_attention_4_sm103.py` still checks FMNMX against `ld.red` bit-exactly (62 passed).
- FlyDSL MXFP8 GEMM on gfx950, now the default on the V4.1 route: matches an fp32 reference within bf16 rounding for M = 2048-8192. No V4.1 checkpoint was available for an end-to-end run.
- Probes: `SGLANG_FORCE_SHUTDOWN=1`, `SGLANG_SYNC_TOKEN_IDS_ACROSS_TP=true` and `SGLANG_FLASHINFER_USE_TENSOR_CORE=1` take effect only on the branch, and the old names still work. The changed arch gates were probed on H200, GB300, 5090 and MI350X, and mocked as gfx942 / gfx1151 / gfx1250 / gfx115x.
- `cargo clippy -p sglang-server -- -D warnings` passes on Linux; the Rust changes are doc comments only.

After merging main (`77c3bcbe`), the DSA metadata tests and main's new `test_dsa_kernel_metadata_hook.py` were rerun on H200 and pass.

**Not run on hardware:** H20 (the 78-SM rule), gfx1250 / gfx1151 / gfx115x (arch-mocked unit tests only), MegaMoE EP8 on ROCm, DGX Spark, MuseSpark finalize-AR, and MiniMax-M3 NVFP4 end to end.

This PR and #48366 touch 19 of the same files but delete different variables; whichever lands second will be rebased.

title: [Perf] [AMD] dsa: Split-K HIP sparse MLA for decode/verify
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
Generated by SkyOpt (Berkeley SkyDiscover)

## Motivation

On MI355X (gfx950), when Kimi-K3.1 runs TP8 speculative decoding, the target-verify batches go through the Triton split-K kernel in `triton_sparse_mla_fwd`. Each request contributes bs × 6 rows (DFLASH MLA5 draft, 5 draft tokens), so a batch is 16–512 query rows. In a TP8 bs48 decode step, sparse MLA takes about 18% of the step time. The gfx950 HIP sparse MLA prefill kernel is already in the tree, but it runs one CTA per row, which can't fill the GPU at these row counts.

## Modifications

- **`sparse_mla_prefill_gfx950.cuh` / `.py`**: add a split-K mode (`run_split` / `sparse_mla_split_gfx950`). Each row's top-k is split across `splits` CTAs, and the partial results are merged with an fp32 log-sum-exp combine, so the merge adds no extra rounding. `sparse_mla_decode_splits(rows)` picks the split count from the row count (16 / 8 / 4 / 2, from per-shape microbenchmarks; numbers in the docstring).
- **`triton_sparse_mla.py`**: in `triton_sparse_mla_fwd`, batches of 16–512 rows (H ≤ 16, shapes supported by `supports_sparse_mla_prefill_gfx950`) go to the HIP split-K kernel. Smaller batches (6 / 12 rows) stay on the Triton split-K path, which is faster there. Batches above 512 rows keep the existing single-CTA HIP path. Non-DCP only.
- **`environ.py`**: new switch `SGLANG_ROCM_SPARSE_MLA_DECODE_HIP`, on by default; set it to `0` to fall back to Triton.

Kernel time (MI355X, 12 heads, top-2048):

| Rows | Triton split-K (µs) | HIP split-K (µs) |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 24 | 28.6 | 20.5 |
| 96 | 89.5 | 31.2 |
| 192 | 239 | 46.3 |
| 288 | 103 (single-CTA HIP) | 70.8 |

## Accuracy Tests

Kimi-K3.1 on MI355X, compared against the same tree with this change off:
- GSM8K (DCP8 c48, TP8 c4): unchanged
- Real accept length: unchanged

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Kimi-K3.1, InferenceX fixed-seq 8k/1k, simulated accept length 3.69, paired against the same tree with this change off. Throughput per GPU:

| Concurrency | Change |
|---:|---:|
| 4 | +1.3% |
| 16 | +4.0% |
| 32 | +6.9% |

The sparse MLA decode step itself runs about 6× faster.

title: [Perf] [AMD] moe: Run the small-batch sort + stage-1 quant up to 1024 pairs on Kimi-K3
author: RolaoDenthu
body:
Generated by SkyOpt (Berkeley SkyDiscover)

## Motivation

In Kimi-K3's MoE (E = 896, top-16, block_m 32), small batches go through a patched sort kernel that also quantizes the stage-1 input to MXFP8. Until now it covered at most 256 (token, expert) pairs, i.e. 16 tokens at top-16; larger batches fell back to aiter's opus sort + quant.

On MI355X the patched sort is **31–46% faster** than aiter's sort + quant up to 960 pairs, and only ties from 1152 pairs, where its bitonic sort width doubles past 1024. The 256-pair limit therefore left decode/verify batches of 17–64 tokens on the slower path.

## Modifications

`python/sglang/kernels/ops/moe/moe_sorting_small.py`:

- Raise the limit from 256 to 1024 (token, expert) pairs (64 tokens at top-16).
- Rename `_EMIT_MAX_PAIRS` to `_SMALL_SORT_MAX_PAIRS`, and use this one constant both for picking the patched sort and for its stage-1 quant, which previously had separate hard-coded `256` checks.

Batches above 1024 pairs still use aiter's sort + quant.

## Accuracy Tests

The patched sort's outputs (sorted ids, weights, expert ids, and the quantized stage-1 input) are **byte-identical** to aiter's at 384–1024 pairs, so model outputs do not change.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

MI355X, Kimi-K3.1, InferenceX fixed-seq 8k/1k, throughput per GPU:

| Concurrency | Change |
|---:|---:|
| 4 (TP8) | +2.3% |
| 8 (DCP8) | +1.1% |

title: [Chore] [NVIDIA] deps: Bump FlashInfer to 0.7.3 and migrate the NVLink one-sided all-to-all to flashinfer.moe_ep
author: leejnau
body:
## Motivation

This PR bumps FlashInfer to 0.7.3. It also brings in @trevor-m's migration of the NVLink one-sided all-to-all to `flashinfer.moe_ep` from #46885, because neither change can land without the other:

- **The bump needs the migration.** FlashInfer 0.7.3 removes `flashinfer.comm.MoeAlltoAll` and `moe_a2a_get_workspace_size_per_rank`, which the current `FlashinferDispatcher` uses (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6047, #6621).
- **The migration needs the bump.** #46885 passes `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank` to `flashinfer.moe_ep`, and that argument only exists from 0.7.3. In 0.7.2 it is `max_tokens_per_rank`.

#46926 (0.7.2.post1) stays open for now as a fallback.

## Depends on

- #48467 (DeepSeek-V4 trtllm counter buffer), now merged. Main's `deepseek_v4_trtllm_backend.py` patches `flashinfer.mla._core._get_trtllm_gen_multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`. 0.7.3 no longer has that name, so `--dsv4-attn-backend trtllm` fails at init. #48467 works on 0.7.2 and 0.7.3, so it can merge first.

## Modifications

- Commits from #46885, cherry-picked with @trevor-m as author:
  - Switch `NVLinkOneSidedAllToAll` to the `flashinfer.moe_ep` API.
  - Lint fix.
  - Pass `runtime_max_tokens_per_rank` in dispatch.
- Pass the new `last_valid_index` argument to `flashinfer::sampling::DeviceSamplingFromProb` in SGLang's JIT tree speculative-sampling kernel (`sgl_kernel/speculative/sampling.cuh`). flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#5352 (in 0.7.3) added that parameter. Without this change the kernel fails to compile, and the first EAGLE verify step crashes the scheduler. The change mirrors FlashInfer's own chain speculative-sampling kernel, and it only compiles against 0.7.3 headers, so it has to land with the bump.
- Pass the new `fixed_uniform_q_len` argument in the FlashInfer backend's `fast_prefill_plan`. FlashInfer 0.7.3's FA2 paged-prefill `plan()` takes 21 arguments instead of 20. The fast plan also clears `_eagle_verify_fp8kv_sm90_state`, as FlashInfer's own `plan()` now does on every call.
- MiniMax-M3.1's fused NVFP4 KV store now zeroes the payload when a block's scale underflows to zero, to match FlashInfer 0.7.3's quantizer (flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6996 changed its guard from `amax != 0` to `sf != 0`).
- **Temporary workaround for flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#8831.** FlashInfer 0.7.2.post1 and 0.7.3 include flashinfer-ai/flashinfer#6546, which adds a small-batch MoE finalize kernel for 4 < top-k <= 64. That kernel adds the top-k expert outputs in a different order from the large-batch kernel, so a token's MoE output depends on its batch size, and prefill and decode logprobs stop matching. With `--enable-deterministic-inference`, the pre-routed NVFP4 trtllm MoE path now calls FlashInfer with `do_finalize=False` and sums the outputs with SGLang's `moe_finalize_fuse_shared`, which uses one order at every batch size. `moe_finalize_fuse_shared` gains an `out=` argument so the sum lands in the usual output buffer. Nothing changes outside deterministic mode. Remove this once #8831 is fixed in a FlashInfer release.
- Bump FlashInfer from 0.7.2 to 0.7.3 in `docker/Dockerfile`, `docker/Dockerfile.cu134`, `python/pyproject.toml` and the `engine.py` version check.

0.7.3 requires `nvidia-cutlass-dsl[cu13]>=4.8.0`, and SGLang already pins 4.8.0.

## Tests

- CI. The first run is expected to hit the cold SGLang JIT cache in the jit-kernel suite, as on earlier FlashInfer bumps.

title: [Perf] [NVIDIA] dsv41: Index-Q RoPE + fp4 pack runs one thread per fp4 block for prefill-sized calls
author: dmtri35
body:
## Motivation

`index_q_rope_pack_weights` (`index_q_kernel` in `fp4_indexer_rope.cuh`) applies RoPE and two-stage fp4 packing to the DeepSeek-V4.1 indexer query and also writes the head weights. It gives each (token, head) row of 128 bf16 to one warp, which per row means:
- 4-byte loads;
- four 16-lane max reductions and two shuffles;
- two 1-byte payload stores per lane;
- 4-warp CTAs.

That shape was chosen from decode measurements and suits decode. At prefill sizes it runs far from memory bandwidth. On VR200 a 32768-token chunk with 32 index heads (1M rows, ~340 MB of traffic, ~26 us at HBM speed) took 251 us per indexer layer.

## Modifications

- `index_q_block_kernel` gives each 32-element fp4 block to one thread: four threads per row, 256-thread CTAs of 64 rows. Warps 0-3 take the head blocks and warps 4-7 the RoPE blocks, so the RoPE branch is warp-uniform. Each thread does:
  - all of its loads before any math: the input block, plus its `freqs_cis` slice for the RoPE half, as `kMaxVecBytes` vectors (32 bytes on Blackwell);
  - the RoPE of its tail pairs;
  - both block absmaxes as trees seeded with 0;
  - the fake quant up to the e2m1 grid value, then the packer's exponent read from the grid amax's biased exponent (no division) and the e2m1 codes, with the two power-of-two scales folded into one multiply;
  - one 16-byte payload store and one byte of the row's little-endian scale word.

  The row's first thread writes the head weight. The current version of the kernel is @zcnrex's from review (about 10-23% faster than the first version, same bytes).
- **Bitwise:** every fp4 stage of `index_rope_quant_pack` works per element except the block absmax, and a max is exact in any order, so the bytes match the warp kernel's. Both kernels write the RoPE products with `__fmaf_rn` / `__fmul_rn` as `fma(x, fx, -(y * fy))` and `fma(x, fy, y * fx)`, so they match by construction. For `index_rope_quant_pack` (warp kernel and index-K) that is the contraction nvcc already chose, so its bits are unchanged. Left to nvcc, the block kernel contracted the imaginary part the other way and differed in rare last bits.
- **Dispatch:** `IndexQKernel::launch` takes the block kernel for calls of at least 8192 (token, head) rows on SM100-family GPUs (CC 10.x). The gate counts rows, so decode reaches it too: with 4-token speculative verify and 32 index heads, 64 requests per rank make 8,192 rows, and decode graphs at bs >= 64 capture the block kernel (it is also faster at that size). Smaller batches, other GPUs and ROCm keep `index_q_kernel` unchanged. The PDL wait placement is the same as in the warp kernel.
- **Alignment:** on the block-kernel path, `launch` checks 32-byte alignment of `input` and `freqs_cis` and 16-byte alignment of `payload`, so a misaligned view raises a clear error instead of a misaligned-address fault.

## Accuracy Tests

The change is bitwise, so no model-level accuracy run is needed. The new test `test_index_q_rope_pack_prefill_matches_decode_kernel` covers this. It runs 4100 tokens x 32 heads as one call (131,200 rows, block kernel) and as 128-token calls (4,096 rows each, warp kernel), and requires payload, scale words and head weights to be equal. The inputs cover seven families: normal, per-row scales of exp(6 N(0,1)), sparse with signed zeros, below both fp4 amax floors, values on e2m1 rounding ties, per-row scales of 2^U(-150, 126), and 0.3% each of inf / -inf / nan. It runs with int32 and int64 positions, and skips unless the GPU is CC 10.x (elsewhere both calls take the warp kernel). It passed 14/14 on VR200 with this branch.

The updated kernel was also compared directly with the first block kernel of this PR on VR200: payload, scale words and head weights of both Q kernels, plus the index-K slot bytes, on the seven families x 9 shapes (128 / 255 / 256 / 257 / 4100 / 32768 tokens x 32 heads, 2731 x 3, 8193 x 1) x int32 / int64 positions, are identical in all 126 cases.

## Speed Tests and Profiling

VR200 (SM107), one GPU, 32 heads x 128, bf16 head weights. CUDA graph of 20 calls, us per call:

| tokens | rows | `main` | first version | this PR |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 128 | 4,096 | 1.9 | 1.9 | 1.9 (warp kernel, unchanged) |
| 255 | 8,160 | 2.5 | 2.5 | 2.5 (warp kernel, unchanged) |
| 256 | 8,192 | 2.5 | 2.1-2.2 | 1.6-1.7 |
| 1,024 | 32,768 | 6.4 | 3.6 | 2.7 |
| 8,192 | 262,144 | 52.2 | 16.2 | 13.7 |
| 32,768 | 1,048,576 | 251.1 | 60.3-60.4 | 55.4 (4.5x) |

The first-version and current columns are three alternating rounds each in one job; the `main` column is from an earlier job. B300 numbers for both versions are in the review thread.

End to end on 4x VR200 (DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, DEP4 prefill with 32K-token chunks per rank), the first version of this kernel together with two DeepGEMM MQA-logits epilogue changes (sgl-project/DeepGEMM #138 and #140) gave +1.0% prefill throughput. The index-Q part alone saves about 0.6 ms per 192 ms forward: three indexer layers, ~190 us each.

## Testing

- `test/registered/kernels/ops/attention/test_fp4_indexer.py::test_index_q_rope_pack_prefill_matches_decode_kernel`: 14 passed on VR200 against this branch's JIT build. It skips outside CC 10.x, where both calls take the warp kernel, so it needs a Blackwell runner (`/rerun-test`).
- Whole `test_fp4_indexer.py` on VR200: 108 passed, 2 skipped, 6 failed. The 6 failures are `test_fp4_paged_logits_replay` cases whose `topk_v2` JIT module fails to build in my VR200 environment; they fail the same way on the previous head of this PR. On B300 the file passes (110 passed, 2 skipped, per the review thread).
- The pre-commit hooks pass, including clang-format.

## Limitations

- Measured on VR200 here, and on B300 in review. The gate covers the whole SM100 family because the cost being removed (per-row shuffles and byte stores of a warp-per-row layout) does not depend on the SM variant. B200 and GB300 timings would be welcome, and the gate can be narrowed if either regresses.

## Checklist

- [x] Format your code according to the [Format code with pre-commit](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#format-code-with-pre-commit).
- [x] Add unit tests according to the [Run and add unit tests](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#run-and-add-unit-tests).
- [ ] Update documentation according to [Write documentations](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#write-documentations).
- [x] Provide accuracy and speed benchmark results according to [Test the accuracy](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#test-the-accuracy) and [Benchmark the speed](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#benchmark-the-speed).
- [x] Follow the SGLang code style [guidance](https://docs.sglang.io/developer_guide/contribution_guide.html#code-style-guidance).

title: [Perf] eplb: Vectorize the static per-rank dispatch map
author: weireweire
body:
## Motivation

With `ep_dispatch_algorithm=static`, every EPLB rebalance rebuilds the per-rank dispatch map in `compute_logical_to_rank_dispatch_physical_map`. It calls `_find_nearest_expert` in Python once per (layer, logical expert, rank). For DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at DEP32 that is 40 x 384 x 32 calls, which take 250-290 ms on every rank on each rebalance while the whole DP group waits.

## Modifications

- `_compact_candidates`: move each row's valid physical ids to the front, keeping their original order.
- `_nearest_expert_dispatch`: pick the same-GPU replica, otherwise the same-node replica when it narrows the candidate set, using tensor ops over the replica slots. Rows with a single replica broadcast it. This is the same rule as `_find_nearest_expert`, which still serves the startup collapse in `_compute_logical_to_all_physical_map`.
- Only the (layer, expert, rank) entries left unresolved still go through `_fair_choices` with the seeded `random.Random`, in the same row-major order. The output is therefore bitwise identical to the previous implementation.
- Scratch tensors are created on the input map's device, and `_logical_to_all_physical_raw`, which lost its last caller, is removed.

## Accuracy

Placement is unchanged. Bitwise comparisons against the previous function, all equal:

- 96 cases: 12 layouts x 2 shapes x 4 ranks, scattered -1 padding, with and without the node topology.
- 17,430 random layouts x ranks: ep 1-16, 1-8 nodes, scattered -1 padding, duplicate ids, int32/int64.
- 12,910 random layouts x ranks at the head: ep 1-32, 1-8 nodes, shuffled candidate order (so first-match order is exercised, not just smallest id), scattered -1 padding, duplicate ids, int32/int64, node preference on and off.

## Performance

Time per call:

| shape | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| 40 layers x 384 logical / 416 physical, ep 32 | 255 ms | 39 ms |
| 3 layers x 128 logical / 160 physical | 5.6 ms | 9.1 ms |

The small shape gets a few ms slower from tensor-op overhead; the large one, where the time matters, is 6.5x faster.

End to end, DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash disaggregated serving on GB300 (DEP32 decode, 8 nodes), EPLB every 15000 iterations, AgentX 3600 s at concurrency 3018, one same-day run per arm:

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| rebalance pause p50 | 0.734 s | 0.467 s |
| total token throughput per GPU | 458.7k | 466.6k (+1.7%) |
| interactivity mean (tok/s/user) | 346.2 | 354.4 (+2.4%) |
| interactivity p90 (tok/s/user) | 326.7 | 339.8 (+4.0%) |
| TTFT p95 | 9.33 s | 7.81 s |

The rebalance pause shrinks by 0.27 s, in line with the per-call saving; that is the effect of this change. At one rebalance per 15000 iterations the pause is a small share of the run's wall time, so the throughput, interactivity, and TTFT deltas, from a single run per arm, are larger than the removed pause alone accounts for and should not be read as its effect. The gain grows with rebalance frequency and EP size.

## Related

#45282 (non-blocking EPLB rebalance) moves the rebalance off the forward thread but keeps calling this function, so the two are complementary; it adds a `device` argument to the same function, which is a small conflict.
